declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorensteinLocalRing_stalk_iff_of_essFiniteType_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C03.** Gorensteinness of local rings is unchanged after a finitely
generated extension of the ground field of a locally Noetherian scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinLocalRing_stalk_iff_of_essFiniteType_fieldExtension
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X)
    (x' : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hx' : (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base x' = x) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian
        (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}) :=
      (AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_baseChange_iff k K X f).mp inferInstance
    Dualizing.IsGorensteinLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) ↔
      Dualizing.IsGorensteinLocalRing
        ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk
          x')
declarations.comment: finitely generated field extension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorensteinLocalRing_stalk_iff_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C03.** Gorensteinness of local rings is unchanged after an arbitrary
extension of the ground field when the scheme is locally of finite type over that field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinLocalRing_stalk_iff_of_locallyOfFiniteType
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X)
    (x' : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hx' : (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base x' = x) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    Dualizing.IsGorensteinLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) ↔
      Dualizing.IsGorensteinLocalRing
        ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk
          x')
declarations.comment: arbitrary field extension for a locally finite type scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsGorensteinAt
declarations.doc:
A scheme morphism with locally Noetherian fibres is Gorenstein at `x` if it
is flat at `x` and the local ring of the fibre over `f x` is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsGorensteinAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) (x : X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsGorenstein
declarations.doc:
A scheme morphism with locally Noetherian fibres is Gorenstein when it is
Gorenstein at every point of the source.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsGorenstein {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes with locally Noetherian fibres is Gorenstein if and only if it is flat
and all of its fibres are Gorenstein schemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) :
    IsGorenstein f hf ↔ Flat f ∧ ∀ y : Y, AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein (f.fiber y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isCohenMacaulay_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0C06.** A Gorenstein morphism is Cohen--Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulay_of_isGorenstein
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) (h : IsGorenstein f hf) :
    IsCohenMacaulay f hf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C07 (1).** Gorensteinness at a point is preserved under a base change
locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinAt_pullback {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) (x' : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}))
    (h : IsGorensteinAt f hf ((pullback.fst f g).base x')) :
    IsGorensteinAt (pullback.snd f g)
      (fun y' => isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_pullback f g hf y') x'
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_of_pullback_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C07 (2).** Gorensteinness descends from a base change locally of
finite type when the original morphism is flat at the point in question.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinAt_of_pullback_of_flat {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) (x' : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}))
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom ((pullback.fst f g).base x'))
    (h : IsGorensteinAt (pullback.snd f g)
      (fun y' => isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_pullback f g hf y') x') :
    IsGorensteinAt f hf ((pullback.fst f g).base x')
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_of_pullback_of_flat_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C07 (3).** Gorensteinness descends from a base change locally of
finite type that is flat at the image of the point in the new base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinAt_of_pullback_of_flat_base {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) (x' : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u}))
    (hflat : IsFlatAt g.toLRSHom.toShHom ((pullback.snd f g).base x'))
    (h : IsGorensteinAt (pullback.snd f g)
      (fun y' => isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_pullback f g hf y') x') :
    IsGorensteinAt f hf ((pullback.fst f g).base x')
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isGorensteinAt_iff_isGorensteinFiberStalkAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C08**, the first equivalence of its proof. A flat morphism with
locally Noetherian fibres is Gorenstein at a point exactly when the local ring of its fibre
through that point is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinAt_iff_isGorensteinFiberStalkAt (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) [Flat f] (x : X) :
    f.IsGorensteinAt hf x ↔ IsGorensteinFiberStalkAt f hf x
declarations.comment: proof chain (1) ↔ (2); (2)↔…↔(6) needs 0A9Y, 0BZZ, 0BFQ invertibility

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isGorensteinAt_iff_exists_isInvertible_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Y` a flat morphism of `FTS S` and `x ∈ X`. Then `f` is
Gorenstein at `x` if and only if `f^!𝒪_Y` is isomorphic to an invertible object in a
neighbourhood of `x`. In particular the set of points where `f` is Gorenstein is open in `X`.
Here `f^!` is computed at any compactification `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinAt_iff_exists_isInvertible_upperShriek [Flat f.left] :
    (∀ x : X.left, f.left.IsGorensteinAt (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f) x ↔
      ∃ W : X.left.Opens, x ∈ W ∧
        letI := Scheme.Modules.derivedMonoidal W.toScheme
        MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible
          ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor W.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj
            (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j))) ∧
      IsOpen {x : X.left | f.left.IsGorensteinAt (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f) x}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinAt_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (x : X) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    List.TFAE [
      f.IsGorensteinAt (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation f) x,
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (g : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) S)
          (hg : g ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) S ↘ S) = U.ι ≫ f),
        (LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite g) ∧
          g.IsGorensteinAt (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_comp_eq hg) ⟨x, hx⟩,
      ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : x ∈ U) (g : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) S)
          (hg : g ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) S ↘ S) = U.ι ≫ f),
        (LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite g) ∧
          g.IsGorenstein (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_comp_eq hg),
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (g : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) S)
          (hg : g ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) S ↘ S) = U.ι ≫ f),
        AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt g ⟨x, hx⟩ →
          g.IsGorensteinAt (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_comp_eq hg) ⟨x, hx⟩]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1), (2), (3) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isOpen_setOf_isGorensteinAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C09, last assertion.** For a flat morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S`
locally of finite presentation, the set of points of `X` at which `f` is Gorenstein is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_isGorensteinAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    IsOpen {x : X | IsGorensteinAt f
      (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation f) x}
declarations.comment: the set of points where f is Gorenstein is open in X

declarations.name: RingHom.Smooth.exists_baseChange_smooth_of_colimitPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness spreads out in a filtered colimit of base rings.** Let `A` be the colimit of a
filtered diagram of `R`-algebras `Aᵢ`, computed on underlying sets, and let `φ : B →ₐ[R] C` be of
finite presentation. If the base change `1 ⊗ φ : A ⊗[R] B → A ⊗[R] C` is smooth, then
`1 ⊗ φ : Aᵢ ⊗[R] B → Aᵢ ⊗[R] C` is smooth for some `i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_baseChange_smooth_of_colimitPresentation
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {J : Type w} [Category.{t} J] [IsFiltered J]
    {A : CommAlgCat.{v} R} (pres : ColimitPresentation J A)
    [PreservesColimit (pres.diag ⋙ forget₂ (CommAlgCat.{v} R) CommRingCat.{v})
      (forget CommRingCat)]
    {B C : Type*} [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R C] (φ : B →ₐ[R] C)
    (hφ : φ.toRingHom.FinitePresentation)
    (hA : (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R ↥A) φ).toRingHom.Smooth) :
    ∃ i : J, (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R ↥(pres.diag.obj i)) φ).toRingHom.Smooth
declarations.comment:
The source's `A_0` is the base ring `R` and its index set restricted to `i ≥ 0`,
which is cofinal, is the diagram; `A = colim A_i` is `Limits.ColimitPresentation J A` in
`CommAlgCat R` over a filtered `J` whose colimit is computed on underlying sets, and the base
change of `φ` is Mathlib's `Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R _) φ`. Smooth is
`RingHom.Smooth`, the source's notion by Proposition 00TN. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_smooth_baseChange_of_smooth_limitBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0C.** If a locally finitely presented morphism over a stage of a
cofiltered inverse system becomes smooth over the limit, it becomes smooth at some later
stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_baseChange_of_smooth_limitBaseChange
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [IsCofiltered I]
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    (hc : IsLimit c)
    [Smooth ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀),
      Smooth ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_isProper_over_dvr_of_isReduced_specialFiber

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedHomCompIso
declarations.doc:
For ring maps `A → B → C`, the composite `RHom_B(C, -) ∘ RHom_A(B, -)` is naturally
isomorphic to `RHom_A(C, -)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHomCompIso (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C) :
    Nonempty
      (derivedHom.{u, v} f ⋙ derivedHom.{u, v} g ≅
        derivedHom.{u, v} (g.comp f))

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedHom_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0G for a finite `φ`.**  Let `φ : R →+* A` be a finite homomorphism
and let `p` be any polynomial presentation of `φ`.  Then the algebraic upper
shriek functor of `p` is the derived coextension-of-scalars functor

`φ^! ≅ RHom_R(A, -) : D(R) ⥤ D(A)`

of [Stacks, Tag 0A70].

`φ` factors as `R → C → A` through a monic quotient
`C = R[T₀, …, Tₙ₋₁]/(f₀(T₀), …, fₙ₋₁(Tₙ₋₁))` by a surjection
(`Dualizing.exists_monicIdeal_quotient_surjection`).  The bottom map is
`Dualizing.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedHom_monicIdeal`, whose inputs — the weak
regularity of `f₀(T₀), …, fₙ₋₁(Tₙ₋₁)` and the finiteness, freeness and self-duality of `C` — are
`MvPolynomial.isWeaklyRegular_ofFn_aeval_X_of_monic` and
`Dualizing.finite_free_selfDual_monicIdeal`.  The surjection is Tag 0C0G at an arbitrary
presentation, `Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedHom_of_surjective`, and the two halves are
put together by [Stacks, Tag 0BZT] for a surjective second map
(`Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_comp_of_surjective`) and [Stacks, Tag 0C0F]
(`Dualizing.derivedHomCompIso`).

The module universe is the ring universe here, unlike in the surjective case: the computation of
`ω_{C/R}` and the tensor formula of [Stacks, Tag 0E4B] it is fed to are both stated at module
universe equal to the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedHom_of_finite (φ : R →+* A) (hφ : φ.Finite)
    (p : PolynomialPresentation φ) :
    Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, u} ≅ derivedHom.{u, u, u} φ)
declarations.comment: for a finite φ of Noetherian rings, at an arbitrary polynomial presentation, at module universe equal to the ring universe

declarations.name: Dualizing.upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_away_and_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C0H].**  Let `R` be a ring.

1. For `f ∈ R` and `φ : R → R_f` the localization away from `f`, the algebraic upper shriek
   functor `φ^!`, read at any polynomial presentation of `φ`, is isomorphic to `- ⊗_R^L R_f`.
2. More generally, if `φ : R → R'` is a ring map such that `Spec(R') → Spec(R)` is an open
   immersion, then `φ` admits a polynomial presentation, and `φ^!` read at any of them is
   isomorphic to `- ⊗_R^L R'`.

Both hold at an arbitrary module universe.  `- ⊗_R^L R'` is derived tensor product over `R` with
`R'` in degree zero, `Dualizing.derivedTensorProductOver`; `R_f` is any localization of `R` away
from `f`.  The source assumes `R` Noetherian, which neither clause needs.  The first clause is
`Dualizing.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_away`, computed from
[Stacks, Tag 0BZH] at `R[x] → R[x]/(fx - 1)` as in the source; the second is
`Dualizing.nonempty_upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_of_isOpenImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriekFunctor_iso_derivedTensorProduct_away_and_of_isOpenImmersion
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] :
    (∀ (f : R) (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization.Away f S]
        (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap R S)),
        Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ≅
          derivedTensorProductOver.{u, v} (algebraMap R S) (Stacks0BZE.unitObject.{u, v} S))) ∧
      ∀ (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] (φ : R →+* R'),
        IsOpenImmersion (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) →
          Nonempty (PolynomialPresentation φ) ∧
            ∀ p : PolynomialPresentation φ, Nonempty (p.upperShriekFunctor.{u, v} ≅
              derivedTensorProductOver.{u, v} φ (Stacks0BZE.unitObject.{u, v} R'))

declarations.name: Dualizing.nonempty_dualizingModule_linearEquiv_homologyZero_relativeDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0I.**  Let `A → B` be a quasi-finite homomorphism of Noetherian rings
and let `ω•_{B/A}` be its algebraic relative dualizing complex.  Then the relative dualizing
module `ω_{B/A} = Hom_A(B', A) ⊗_{B'} B` of a finite-open factorization `A → B' → B` is
isomorphic to `H⁰(ω•_{B/A})` as a `B`-module.

The source's isomorphism is *nonunique*, so the conclusion is the existence of a `B`-linear
equivalence rather than the invertibility of a named map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_dualizingModule_linearEquiv_homologyZero_relativeDualizingComplex
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B]
    (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} A B)
    (p : PolynomialPresentation (algebraMap A B)) :
    Nonempty (dualizingModule F ≃ₗ[B]
      ↥((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} B) 0).obj
        p.relativeDualizingComplex))
declarations.comment: ω_{B/A} = H⁰(ω•_{B/A}), the source's isomorphism being nonunique

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_properFlat
declarations.doc:
**The homotopy sequence of a proper flat family is exact.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a flat proper
morphism of finite presentation whose geometric fibres are connected and reduced, let `S` be
connected, let `s` be a geometric point of `S` and let `z` be a geometric point of the geometric
fibre `X_s`. Then

```
π₁(X_s, z) ⟶ π₁(X, z ∘ p) ⟶ π₁(S, z ∘ p ∘ f) ⟶ 1
```

is exact: the second map is surjective, the composite of the two is trivial, and the kernel of
the second map is the smallest closed normal subgroup containing the image of the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem isExactSequence_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_properFlat {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f) [GeometricallyConnected f]
    [GeometricallyReduced f] [ConnectedSpace ↥S] (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (z : GeometricPoint (pullback f s.hom)) :
    letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f := hfp.1
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥X := GeometricallyConnected.connectedSpace f f.isOpenMap
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f s.hom) :=
      connectedSpace_pullback_geometricPoint_of_geometricallyConnected f s
    IsExactSequence (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (pullback.fst f s.hom) z)
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f (z.map (pullback.fst f s.hom)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_properFlat
declarations.doc:
For a flat proper morphism of finite presentation with geometrically connected and
geometrically reduced fibres over a connected base, the fundamental group of the total space maps
onto the fundamental group of the base, at the base points coming from a geometric point of a
geometric fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_of_properFlat {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f) [GeometricallyConnected f]
    [GeometricallyReduced f] [ConnectedSpace ↥S] (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (z : GeometricPoint (pullback f s.hom)) :
    letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f := hfp.1
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥X := GeometricallyConnected.connectedSpace f f.isOpenMap
    Function.Surjective (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f (z.map (pullback.fst f s.hom)))
declarations.comment: surjectivity of `π₁(X) → π₁(S)`, the assertion `→ 1` of the homotopy sequence; triviality of the composite and exactness at `π₁(X)` are separate

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupMap_comp_eq_one_of_properFlat
declarations.doc:
For a flat proper morphism of finite presentation with geometrically connected and
geometrically reduced fibres over a connected base, the composite of the maps on fundamental
groups from a geometric fibre to the total space and from there to the base is trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFundamentalGroupMap_comp_eq_one_of_properFlat {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f) [GeometricallyConnected f]
    [GeometricallyReduced f] [ConnectedSpace ↥S] (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (z : GeometricPoint (pullback f s.hom)) :
    letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f := hfp.1
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥X := GeometricallyConnected.connectedSpace f f.isOpenMap
    letI : ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f s.hom) :=
      connectedSpace_pullback_geometricPoint_of_geometricallyConnected f s
    (etaleFundamentalGroupMap f (z.map (pullback.fst f s.hom))).toMonoidHom.comp
        (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (pullback.fst f s.hom) z).toMonoidHom = 1
declarations.comment: triviality of the composite `π₁(X_s) → π₁(X) → π₁(S)`, the complex condition of the homotopy sequence; surjectivity and exactness at `π₁(X)` are separate

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSpecializationMap_of_square
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0K.** Consider a commutative square of schemes with `a : Y ⟶ X` on
top, `g : Y ⟶ T` and `f : X ⟶ S` vertical and `b : T ⟶ S` on the bottom, where `f` and `g` are
proper with geometrically connected fibres. Let `t'` and `t` be geometric points of `T` and let
`sp : π₁(Y_{t'}) → π₁(Y_t)` be a specialization map. Then there is a specialization map
`π₁(X_{s'}) → π₁(X_s)`, where `s'` and `s` are the images of `t'` and `t` in `S`, making the
square of maps induced by the morphisms `Y_{t'} ⟶ X_{s'}` and `Y_t ⟶ X_s` of geometric fibres
commute.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSpecializationMap_of_square (a : Y ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ S) (b : T ⟶ S)
    (hab : a ≫ f = g ≫ b) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f] [IsProper g]
    [GeometricallyConnected g] (t' t : GeometricPoint T)
    (y' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t'))
    (y : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t') y' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t) y)
    (hsp : IsSpecializationMap g t' t y' y sp)
    (hclosedFibre : ∀ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : HenselianLocalRing C),
      ∀ (_ : IsSepClosed (ResidueField C)) (r : Spec (.of C) ⟶ S)
        (p : (t.map b).source ⟶ Spec (.of C)) (hp : p ≫ r = (t.map b).hom),
      p (closedPoint (t.map b).residueField) = closedPoint C →
      (finiteEtaleBaseChange
        (fiberOverGeometricPointMap f (t.map b) r p hp)).IsEquivalence) :
    ∃ sp' : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f (t'.map b))
          (y'.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t')) →ₜ*
        EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f (t.map b))
          (y.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t)),
      IsSpecializationMap f (t'.map b) (t.map b)
          (y'.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t'))
          (y.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t)) sp' ∧
        ∀ γ, etaleFundamentalGroupMap
              (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t) y (sp γ)
          = sp' (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
              (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t') y' γ)
declarations.comment: the whole statement — the specialization map on the bottom row and the commutativity of the square of fundamental groups — granted the one input this library cannot prove, carried as the hypothesis `hclosedFibre`: that base change along the inclusion of the closed geometric fibre `X_s ⟶ X ×_S Spec C` is an equivalence on finite étale covers, for a strictly henselian local ring `C` over `S` through whose closed point `s` factors. That is Stacks 0A48 with 0A49 and 0BTW; `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FundamentalGroup.ClosedGeometricFibre` reduces it to the essential-surjectivity half of Stacks 0GS2, left open by `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FundamentalGroup.FiniteEtaleProperEquivalence`. It is an input to the construction of a specialization map (Stacks 0BUP) — the same datum for the upper row is part of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSpecializationMap` — and it restricts nothing about `a`, `b`, the specialization `t' ⤳ t` or the schemes. Everything else is proved here: the strict henselization `A` of the stalk at the image of `t`, the ring map `A → B` of Stacks 04GU, the factorizations of the two geometric points of `S` through `Spec A`, connectedness of `X_A`, and the base-point bookkeeping.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSpecializationMap_comm_square
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0K.** Consider a commutative square of schemes with `a : Y ⟶ X` on
top, `g : Y ⟶ T` and `f : X ⟶ S` vertical and `b : T ⟶ S` on the bottom, where `f` and `g` are
proper with geometrically connected fibres. Let `t'` and `t` be geometric points of `T` and let
`sp : π₁(Y_{t'}) → π₁(Y_t)` be a specialization map. Then there is a specialization map
`sp' : π₁(X_{s'}) → π₁(X_s)`, where `s'` and `s` are the images of `t'` and `t` in `S`, such that
the square formed by `sp`, `sp'` and the maps induced by the morphisms `Y_{t'} ⟶ X_{s'}` and
`Y_t ⟶ X_s` of geometric fibres commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSpecializationMap_comm_square (a : Y ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ S)
    (b : T ⟶ S) (hab : a ≫ f = g ≫ b) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f] [IsProper g]
    [GeometricallyConnected g] (t' t : GeometricPoint T)
    (y' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t'))
    (y : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t') y' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint g t) y)
    (hsp : IsSpecializationMap g t' t y' y sp) :
    ∃ sp' : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f (t'.map b))
          (y'.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t')) →ₜ*
        EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f (t.map b))
          (y.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t)),
      IsSpecializationMap f (t'.map b) (t.map b)
          (y'.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t'))
          (y.map (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t)) sp' ∧
        ∀ γ, etaleFundamentalGroupMap
              (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t) y (sp γ)
          = sp' (etaleFundamentalGroupMap
              (fiberOverGeometricPointSquareMap a g f b hab t') y' γ)
declarations.comment: The whole statement, under the source's hypotheses only.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSpecializationMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0L.** For a proper morphism with geometrically connected fibres and
specializations `s'' ⇝ s' ⇝ s`, the composite of a specialization map
`π₁(X_{s̄''}) → π₁(X_{s̄'})` with a specialization map `π₁(X_{s̄'}) → π₁(X_{s̄})` is again a
specialization map `π₁(X_{s̄''}) → π₁(X_{s̄})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSpecializationMap_comp (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f]
    (s'' s' s : GeometricPoint S)
    (x'' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s''))
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s))
    (h₁ : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'') x'' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x')
    (h₂ : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x)
    (hs₁ : IsSpecializationMap f s'' s' x'' x' h₁)
    (hs₂ : IsSpecializationMap f s' s x' x h₂) :
    IsSpecializationMap f s'' s x'' x (h₂.comp h₁)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_strictlyHenselianValuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0M.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism with geometrically
connected fibres, let `s'` and `s` be geometric points of `S` and let
`sp : π₁(X_{s̄'}) → π₁(X_{s̄})` be a specialization map. Then there are a strictly henselian
valuation ring `R` with algebraically closed fraction field (and algebraically closed residue
field) and a morphism `r : Spec R ⟶ S` sending the generic point `η` of `Spec R` to the image of
`s'` and its closed point `o` to the image of `s`, such that `sp` is isomorphic to the
specialization map `sp_R : π₁((X_R)_η) → π₁((X_R)_o)` of the base change `X_R ⟶ Spec R`: there
are isomorphisms of topological groups `π₁(X_{s̄'}) ≅ π₁((X_R)_η)` and `π₁(X_{s̄}) ≅ π₁((X_R)_o)`
intertwining `sp` and `sp_R`.

The geometric points `η` and `o` of `Spec R` are the generic and closed points themselves: the
field of `η` is a fraction field of `R`, and `R` maps onto the field of `o`. This is
`exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_valuationRing` with its input Tag 0A48 supplied by
`properHenselianFiniteEtaleEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_strictlyHenselianValuationRing
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f]
    (s' s : GeometricPoint S)
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x)
    (hsp : IsSpecializationMap f s' s x' x sp) :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R) (_ : ValuationRing R)
      (_ : StrictlyHenselianLocalRing R) (_ : IsAlgClosed (FractionRing R))
      (_ : IsAlgClosed (ResidueField R))
      (r : Spec (.of R) ⟶ S) (η o : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of R)))
      (yη : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η))
      (yo : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o))
      (spR : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η) yη →ₜ*
        EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o) yo),
      η.hom default = genericPoint (Spec (.of R)) ∧
      o.hom default = closedPoint R ∧
      @IsFractionRing R _ η.residueField _ (Spec.preimage η.hom).hom.toAlgebra ∧
      Function.Surjective (Spec.preimage o.hom).hom ∧
      r (η.hom default) = s'.hom default ∧
      r (o.hom default) = s.hom default ∧
      IsSpecializationMap (pullback.snd f r) η o yη yo spR ∧
      ∃ (eη : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' ≃ₜ*
            EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η) yη)
        (eo : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x ≃ₜ*
            EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o) yo),
        ∀ γ, eo (sp γ) = spR (eη γ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_valuationSubring_strictlyHenselian_of_specializes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0M**, the existence of the valuation ring. Let `φ : Spec K ⟶ S` be a
geometric point of a scheme `S`, with `K` algebraically closed, and let the image of `φ`
specialize to `s`. Then there is a strictly henselian valuation subring `A` of `K` — so a
valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field `K` and, as it happens, algebraically
closed residue field — together with a morphism `r : Spec A ⟶ S` over which `φ` is the generic
point and which carries the closed point of `Spec A` to `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_valuationSubring_strictlyHenselian_of_specializes
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (φ : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S) {s : S}
    (h : φ (closedPoint K) ⤳ s) :
    ∃ A : ValuationSubring K, StrictlyHenselianLocalRing A ∧
      IsAlgClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) ∧
      ∃ r : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S,
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K)) ≫ r = φ ∧ r (closedPoint A) = s
declarations.comment: the existence of the strictly henselian valuation ring `R` over `S` with algebraically closed fraction field realizing the specialization, which is the only step the Stacks proof argues; the comparison `sp ≅ sp_R` of specialization maps of fundamental groups is not formalized, because the specialization map `sp` cannot be constructed in this library: its construction (Stacks 0BUP) is the composite of the functoriality map with the identifications of Stacks 0A48, 0BTW and 0A49, and none of those three is available here — 0BTW is proper base change over a henselian local ring, i.e. Stacks 0GS2, whose essential-surjectivity half is open (see `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FundamentalGroup.FiniteEtaleProperEquivalence`)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_isDiscreteValuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0N.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism with geometrically
connected fibres over a Noetherian scheme, let `s'` and `s` be geometric points of `S`, and let
`sp : π₁(X_{s'}) → π₁(X_s)` be a specialization map. Then there are a complete — in particular
strictly henselian — discrete valuation ring `R` with algebraically closed residue field, a
morphism `r : Spec R ⟶ S` carrying the generic point of `Spec R` to the image of `s'` and its
closed point to the image of `s`, and a specialization map
`sp_R : π₁((X_R)_{η̄}) → π₁((X_R)_{ō})` of the base change `X_R ⟶ Spec R` from the generic to the
closed point, such that `sp` and `sp_R` are intertwined by isomorphisms of topological groups on
the source and on the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_isDiscreteValuationRing
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f] [IsNoetherian S]
    (s' s : GeometricPoint S)
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x)
    (hsp : IsSpecializationMap f s' s x' x sp)
    (h0A48 : ProperHenselianFiniteEtaleEquivalence.{u}) :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R)
      (_ : HenselianLocalRing R) (_ : IsAlgClosed (ResidueField R))
      (r : Spec (.of R) ⟶ S) (η o : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of R)))
      (yη : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η))
      (yo : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o))
      (spR : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η) yη →ₜ*
        EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o) yo),
      η.hom default = genericPoint (Spec (.of R)) ∧
      o.hom default = closedPoint R ∧
      r (η.hom default) = s'.hom default ∧
      r (o.hom default) = s.hom default ∧
      IsSpecializationMap (pullback.snd f r) η o yη yo spR ∧
      ∃ (eη : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' ≃ₜ*
            EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η) yη)
        (eo : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x ≃ₜ*
            EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o) yo),
        ∀ γ, eo (sp γ) = spR (eη γ)
declarations.comment: the whole statement, with the same one input this library cannot prove carried as the hypothesis `h0A48`: `ProperHenselianFiniteEtaleEquivalence`, Tag 0A48 for a proper — not merely finite — scheme over a henselian local ring, whose remaining content is Grothendieck existence together with Artin approximation (see `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FundamentalGroup.FiniteEtaleAlgClosedExtension`). It is used exactly twice, for Tag 0A49 through `isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_specMap_algebraMap_of_properHenselian_of_isAlgClosed` and for the closed geometric fibre of `X_R ⟶ Spec R`; it is the same datum that is already part of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSpecializationMap`, so it constrains none of the data quantified over. Everything else is proved here: the discrete valuation ring (Tags 00PH, 0ARL and 0AP1), that the strict henselization of the stalk is Noetherian, the two factorizations of the geometric points, and the base-point bookkeeping. `sp_R` is produced as a specialization map in the sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsSpecializationMap`, and `R` is strictly henselian in the strong sense that its residue field is algebraically closed.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_strictlyHenselianDVR
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0N.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism with geometrically
connected fibres over a Noetherian scheme `S`, let `s'` and `s` be geometric points of `S` and let
`sp : π₁(X_{s̄'}) → π₁(X_{s̄})` be a specialization map. Then there are a strictly henselian
discrete valuation ring `R` (whose residue field is even algebraically closed) and a morphism
`r : Spec R ⟶ S` sending the generic point `η` of `Spec R` to the image of `s'` and its closed
point `o` to the image of `s`, such that `sp` is isomorphic to the specialization map
`sp_R : π₁((X_R)_{η̄}) → π₁((X_R)_{ō})` of the base change `X_R ⟶ Spec R`: there are isomorphisms
of topological groups `π₁(X_{s̄'}) ≅ π₁((X_R)_{η̄})` and `π₁(X_{s̄}) ≅ π₁((X_R)_{ō})` intertwining
`sp` and `sp_R`.

This is `exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_isDiscreteValuationRing` with its input
Tag 0A48 supplied by `properHenselianFiniteEtaleEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSpecializationMap_isomorphic_over_strictlyHenselianDVR
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f] [IsNoetherian S]
    (s' s : GeometricPoint S)
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x)
    (hsp : IsSpecializationMap f s' s x' x sp) :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R)
      (_ : StrictlyHenselianLocalRing R) (_ : IsAlgClosed (ResidueField R))
      (r : Spec (.of R) ⟶ S) (η o : GeometricPoint (Spec (.of R)))
      (yη : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η))
      (yo : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o))
      (spR : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η) yη →ₜ*
        EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o) yo),
      η.hom default = genericPoint (Spec (.of R)) ∧
      o.hom default = closedPoint R ∧
      r (η.hom default) = s'.hom default ∧
      r (o.hom default) = s.hom default ∧
      IsSpecializationMap (pullback.snd f r) η o yη yo spR ∧
      ∃ (eη : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' ≃ₜ*
            EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) η) yη)
        (eo : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x ≃ₜ*
            EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint (pullback.snd f r) o) yo),
        ∀ γ, eo (sp γ) = spR (eη γ)
declarations.comment: The full statement under the source's hypotheses; nothing is granted or assumed.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_specializationMap_of_isProper_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0P.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a flat proper morphism with geometrically
connected fibres and let `s' ⇝ s` be a specialization of points of `S`, realized as in the
construction of the specialization map: `A` is a strict henselization of `𝒪_{S,s}` relative to a
separable closure of `κ(s)`, and the two geometric points are factored through `Spec A`, the
special one over the closed point. Let

```
sp : π₁(X_{s̄'}) ⟶ π₁(X_{s̄})
```

be the resulting specialization map, that is, a continuous homomorphism satisfying the equation
defining it against the canonical maps to `π₁(X_A)`. If the fibre `X_s` is geometrically reduced,
then `sp` is surjective.

No finiteness hypothesis beyond properness is needed. Every specialization map is isomorphic to a
specialization map over a strictly henselian valuation ring `R`, for the base change
`X_R ⟶ Spec R` along a morphism `Spec R ⟶ S` carrying the generic point of `Spec R` to the image
of `s̄'` and the closed point to the image of `s̄`. That base change is flat and proper with
geometrically connected fibres, its closed fibre is geometrically reduced because `X_s` is, and
over a valuation ring a flat morphism of finite type is automatically of finite presentation. So
the geometrically reduced fibre locus of `X_R ⟶ Spec R` is open and contains the closed point of
the local scheme `Spec R`, hence is all of it; the homotopy sequence of `X_R ⟶ Spec R` together
with the triviality of `π₁(Spec R)` makes the specialization map over `R` surjective, and
surjectivity transports back to `sp`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_specializationMap_of_properFlat` is the same conclusion for a
morphism which is moreover assumed to be of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_specializationMap_of_isProper_of_flat {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] [GeometricallyConnected f] (s' s : GeometricPoint S)
    (hred : GeometricallyReduced
      (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField))))
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [Algebra (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField))) A]
    (hA : Stacks.StrictHenselization.IsStrictHenselization
      (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))
      (SeparableClosure
        (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)))).ResidueField) A)
    (p' : s'.source ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (hp' : p' ≫ specStalkAlgebraHom S (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)) A = s'.hom)
    (p : s.source ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    (hp : p ≫ specStalkAlgebraHom S (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)) A = s.hom)
    (hclosed : p (closedPoint s.residueField) = closedPoint A)
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x) :
    letI : ConnectedSpace
        ↥(pullback f (specStalkAlgebraHom S (s.hom (closedPoint s.residueField)) A)) :=
      connectedSpace_pullback_spec_of_isProper f A _
    ∀ t : finiteEtaleFiberFunctor (x'.map (fiberOverGeometricPointMap f s' _ p' hp')) ≅
        finiteEtaleFiberFunctor (x.map (fiberOverGeometricPointMap f s _ p hp)),
      (∀ γ, etaleFundamentalGroupMap (fiberOverGeometricPointMap f s _ p hp) x (sp γ)
          = etaleFundamentalGroupMulEquiv t
            (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (fiberOverGeometricPointMap f s' _ p' hp') x' γ)) →
        Function.Surjective sp
declarations.comment: the whole statement, under the source's hypotheses only.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_isSpecializationMap_of_ringChar_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C0Q].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a smooth proper morphism with geometrically
connected fibres, let `s' ⇝ s` be a specialization of points of `S` realized by a specialization
map `sp : π₁(X_{s̄'}) ⟶ π₁(X_{s̄})`, and suppose the residue characteristic of `s` is zero. Then
`sp` is bijective, i.e. an isomorphism of topological groups.

Surjectivity is [Stacks, Tag 0C0P]. Injectivity is reduced, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_isSpecializationMap_of_ringChar_zero_of_forall_essImage_isGalois`, to
the descent of the Galois covers of a geometric generic fibre over a strictly henselian discrete
valuation ring of residue characteristic zero, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_model_of_isGalois_geometricGenericFibre`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_isSpecializationMap_of_ringChar_zero {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsProper f] [Smooth f] [GeometricallyConnected f] (s' s : GeometricPoint S)
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x)
    (hsp : IsSpecializationMap f s' s x' x sp)
    (hchar : ringChar (S.residueField (s.hom default)) = 0) :
    Function.Bijective sp
declarations.comment: the whole statement, under the source's hypotheses only: `f` smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres (`IsProper f`, `Smooth f`, `GeometricallyConnected f`), a specialization of points of `S` realized by a specialization map `sp` (`hsp`), and `κ(s)` of characteristic zero (`hchar`). The conclusion `Function.Bijective sp` is the source's conclusion that `sp` is an isomorphism: `sp` is a continuous homomorphism of profinite groups, so bijectivity is invertibility. Both halves are proved -- surjectivity through Tag 0C0P and injectivity through the descent of the Galois covers of a geometric generic fibre over a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic zero.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_and_exists_continuousMulEquiv_primeToP
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C0R].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a smooth proper morphism with geometrically
connected fibres, let `s' ⇝ s` be a specialization of points of `S` realized by a specialization
map `sp : π₁(X_{s̄'}) ⟶ π₁(X_{s̄})`, and let `p` be the characteristic of `κ(s)`. Then `sp` is
surjective and induces an isomorphism `π'₁(X_{s̄'}) ≅ π'₁(X_{s̄})` of the maximal prime-to-`p`
quotients, commuting with the projections.

Surjectivity is [Stacks, Tag 0C0P]. The isomorphism of the maximal prime-to-`p` quotients is
reduced by
`surjective_and_exists_continuousMulEquiv_primeToP_of_forall_isDiscreteValuationRing`
to the descent of the Galois covers of order prime to `p` of a geometric generic fibre over a
strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with algebraically closed residue field of
characteristic `p`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_model_of_isGalois_geometricGenericFibre_of_not_dvd`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_and_exists_continuousMulEquiv_primeToP {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Smooth f] [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f] (s' s : GeometricPoint S) (p : ℕ)
    (x' : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s))
    (sp : EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x' →ₜ*
      EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x)
    (hsp : IsSpecializationMap f s' s x' x sp)
    (hchar : ringChar (S.residueField (s.hom default)) = p) :
    Function.Surjective sp ∧
      ∃ e : PrimeToP p (EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s') x') ≃ₜ*
          PrimeToP p (EtaleFundamentalGroup (fiberOverGeometricPoint f s) x),
        ∀ g, e (primeToPMk p _ g) = primeToPMk p _ (sp g)
declarations.comment: the whole statement, under the source's hypotheses only: `f` smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres (`IsProper f`, `Smooth f`, `GeometricallyConnected f`), a specialization of points of `S` realized by a specialization map `sp` (`hsp`), and `p` the characteristic of `κ(s)` (`hchar`). Both of the source's conclusions are stated and proved: `sp` is surjective, and the induced map of the maximal prime-to-`p` quotients is an isomorphism of topological groups commuting with the projections, which is the source's isomorphism `π'₁(X_{s̄'}) ≅ π'₁(X_{s̄})`.

declarations.name: IsRegularLocalRing.nonempty_ringEquiv_and_algEquiv_mvPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian complete local ring which is regular, and let `d` be its
embedding dimension `dim_{R/𝔪} 𝔪/𝔪²`, which equals `dim R`.
1. If `R` contains a field — equivalently `𝐅_p` or `𝐐` — then `R` is isomorphic to the power
   series ring in `d` variables over its residue field.
2. If `k` is a field and `k → R` is a ring map inducing an isomorphism `k → R/𝔪`, then `R` is
   isomorphic as a `k`-algebra to the power series ring in `d` variables over `k`.
(Stacks 0C0S)
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularLocalRing.nonempty_ringEquiv_and_algEquiv_mvPowerSeries (R : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = d) :
    (∀ (F : Type v) [Field F] [Algebra F R],
        Nonempty (R ≃+* MvPowerSeries (Fin d) (ResidueField R))) ∧
      (∀ (k : Type w) [Field k] [Algebra k R],
        Function.Bijective ((residue R).comp (algebraMap k R)) →
          Nonempty (R ≃ₐ[k] MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k))
declarations.comment: The source's Noetherian complete local regular ring is `IsRegularLocalRing R` with `IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R`. `R` contains `𝐅_p` or `𝐐` iff it contains a field, which is how the first part is hypothesized; the number of variables is pinned to the embedding dimension, the `d` of the source's proof. The two parts are the two conjuncts, each guarded by its own hypothesis. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.PicFinite.exists_isInvertible_modulePullback_iso
declarations.doc:
**An invertible module descends along a finite morphism that is an isomorphism away
from a discrete closed subset.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_modulePullback_iso
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite f]
    (V : Y.Opens) [IsIso (f ∣_ V)] [DiscreteTopology (Vᶜ : Set Y)]
    (L : X.Modules)
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
      ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).mp X.IsSheaf) L) :
    ∃ M : Y.Modules,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
          ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ Y.presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).mp Y.IsSheaf) M ∧
        Nonempty ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M ≅ L)

declarations.name: Stacks.PicFinite.exists_isInvertible_modulePullback_iso_of_isClosedImmersion_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0U.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes with `Y` of
Noetherian underlying space and dimension at most one, and suppose `f` is a closed immersion
over a dense open subset `V` of `Y`. Then every invertible `𝒪_X`-module is the pullback of an
invertible `𝒪_Y`-module.

The morphism factors as `f.toImage ≫ f.imageι` through its scheme-theoretic image `Z`. Over
`U := f.imageι ⁻¹ᵁ V` the first factor is a closed immersion with trivial kernel ideal sheaf,
hence an isomorphism, and the part of `Z` outside `U` is discrete, so Tag 0C0T descends the
module to `Z`; Tag 09NY then lifts it across the closed immersion `f.imageι` to `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_modulePullback_iso_of_isClosedImmersion_restrict
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] [NoetherianSpace Y]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ 1) (V : Y.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set Y))
    [IsClosedImmersion (f ∣_ V)]
    (L : X.Modules)
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
      ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ X.presheaf
        (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).mp X.IsSheaf) L) :
    ∃ M : Y.Modules,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
          ((Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_comp _ Y.presheaf
            (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).mp Y.IsSheaf) M ∧
        Nonempty ((AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj M ≅ L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPullback_hasTorAmplitudeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C0V (1).** For a cartesian square of schemes whose two morphisms to the base are
Tor independent, derived pullback preserves Tor amplitude over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedPullback_hasTorAmplitudeOver
    {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S')
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (htor : TorIndependent f g) (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (a b : ℤ)
    (hE : HasTorAmplitudeOver f E a b) :
    HasTorAmplitudeOver f'
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) a b
declarations.comment: preservation of Tor amplitude over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPullbackComparison_isIso_of_isFlatOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C0V (2).** For a Tor-independent cartesian square of schemes and an `𝒪_X`-module
`G` flat over `S`, the canonical comparison from the derived pullback of `G` along `g'` to its
ordinary pullback is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedPullbackComparison_isIso_of_isFlatOver
    {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}} (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S')
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (htor : TorIndependent f g) (G : X.Modules) (hG : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom G) :
    IsIso ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullbackComparison
      g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).app
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G)))
declarations.comment: derived pullback of a module flat over the base is the ordinary pullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulayAt_comp
declarations.doc:
The composite of morphisms Cohen–Macaulay at the relevant points is Cohen–Macaulay at the
point of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulayAt_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hgf : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z)) (x : X)
    (hfx : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt f hf x)
    (hgy : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt g hg (f x)) :
    Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt (f ≫ g) hgf x
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_comp
declarations.doc: The composite of Cohen–Macaulay morphisms is Cohen–Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulay_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hgf : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z))
    (hfm : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay f hf)
    (hgm : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay g hg) :
    Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay (f ≫ g) hgf
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulayAt_left_of_comp_of_flatAt
declarations.doc:
If the composite is Cohen–Macaulay at `x` and `f` is flat at `x`, then `f` is Cohen–Macaulay
at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulayAt_left_of_comp_of_flatAt {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hgf : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z)) (x : X)
    (hcomp : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt (f ≫ g) hgf x)
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt f hf x
declarations.comment: part (3), first conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulayAt_right_of_comp_of_flatAt
declarations.doc:
If the composite is Cohen–Macaulay at `x` and `f` is flat at `x`, then `g` is Cohen–Macaulay
at `f x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulayAt_right_of_comp_of_flatAt {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hgf : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z)) (x : X)
    (hcomp : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt (f ≫ g) hgf x)
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt g hg (f x)
declarations.comment: part (3), second conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_left_of_comp_of_flat
declarations.doc: If the composite is Cohen–Macaulay and `f` is flat, then `f` is Cohen–Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulay_left_of_comp_of_flat {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))

    (hcomp : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay (f ≫ g) hgf)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulayAt_right_of_comp_of_flat
declarations.doc:
If the composite is Cohen–Macaulay and `f` is flat, then `g` is Cohen–Macaulay at every
point in the image of `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulayAt_right_of_comp_of_flat {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))

    (hcomp : Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulay (f ≫ g) hgf)
    (hflat : Flat f) (x : X) :
    Scheme.Hom.IsCohenMacaulayAt g hg (f x)
declarations.comment: part (4), second conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_of_isCohenMacaulay_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0X.** A flat morphism of locally Noetherian schemes whose source is
Cohen–Macaulay is a Cohen–Macaulay morphism.

    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Flat f]

    f.IsCohenMacaulay (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_targetStalk_of_isCohenMacaulay_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C0X.** For a flat morphism of locally Noetherian schemes whose source

    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Flat f]

    IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))
declarations.comment: the target local rings are Cohen-Macaulay

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.cardinalMk_fiber_multiplication_by_char_le
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0` and `A` an abelian variety of dimension `g` over
`k`. The fibre of `[p] : A → A` over the identity has at most `p ^ g` distinct points. The fibre is
the pullback of `[p]` along the identity section, and its points are counted by the cardinality of
its underlying space.
declarations.statement:
theorem cardinalMk_fiber_multiplication_by_char_le {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj A] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelianVariety k A] (p : ℕ)
    [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) :
    Cardinal.mk
      (pullback (η[A]).left (((𝟙 A : A ⟶ A) ^ (p : ℤ)).left) : Scheme.{u}) ≤
      p ^ abelianVarietyDimension A

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isCohenMacaulayAt_iff_exists_unique_nonzero_homology_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Y` a flat morphism of `FTS S` and `x ∈ X`. Then `f` is
Cohen–Macaulay at `x` if and only if `f^!𝒪_Y` has a unique nonzero cohomology sheaf in a
neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulayAt_iff_exists_unique_nonzero_homology_upperShriek [Flat f.left]
    (x : X.left) :
    f.left.IsCohenMacaulayAt (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f) x ↔
      ∃ W : X.left.Opens, x ∈ W ∧ ∃ n : ℤ,
        ¬ IsZero ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor W.ι).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules n).obj
            (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j))) ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ n → IsZero ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor W.ι).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
            (relativeDualizingComplexObj f j)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.nonempty_iso_pullback_tensor_shift_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C10], last sentence, the complexes.** Let `S` be Noetherian with a dualizing
complex `ω_S^•` and `f : X ⟶ Y` a separated Cohen–Macaulay morphism of relative dimension `d`
between schemes of finite type over `S`, not necessarily separated over `S`. For dualizing
complexes `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` normalized relative to `ω_S^•` and `ω_{X/Y} = H^{-d}(f^! 𝒪_Y)`,
`ω_X^• ≅ Lf^* ω_Y^• ⊗ᴸ ω_{X/Y}[d]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_pullback_tensor_shift_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) (hf : IsShriekable f)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS)
    (hCM : haveI := hf.target_noetherian
      (ftsHomOf f hf.separatedFiniteType (isSeparatedFiniteType_id Y)
        (Category.comp_id f)).left.IsCohenMacaulay (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left _))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ∀ x : X, topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) =
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    haveI := hf.target_noetherian
    Nonempty (𝒦X.complex.obj ≅ ((quasiCoherentDerivedTensor X).obj
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' f).obj 𝒦Y.complex.obj)).obj
          (relativeDualizingSheafShift (ftsHomOf f hf.separatedFiniteType
            (isSeparatedFiniteType_id Y) (Category.comp_id f)) (nagataCompactification f hf)
            hCM d hd))
declarations.comment: Similar results hold for X and Y of finite type over S, not necessarily separated, with complexes normalized relative to omega_S: omega_X = Lf^* omega_Y (x) omega_{X/Y}[d]

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.exists_homology_iso_pullback_tensor_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C10], last sentence, the dualizing modules.** In the situation of
`nonempty_iso_pullback_tensor_shift_nagata`, if moreover `Y` is connected and Cohen–Macaulay, the
normalized complexes `ω_Y^•` and `ω_X^•` are concentrated in single degrees `m` and `m - d`, and
their cohomology sheaves `ω_Y`, `ω_X` there satisfy `ω_X ≅ f^* ω_Y ⊗ ω_{X/Y}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homology_iso_pullback_tensor_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) (hf : IsShriekable f)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS)
    (hCM : haveI := hf.target_noetherian
      (ftsHomOf f hf.separatedFiniteType (isSeparatedFiniteType_id Y)
        (Category.comp_id f)).left.IsCohenMacaulay (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left _))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ∀ x : X, topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) =
      (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    [ConnectedSpace Y] (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay Y) :
    haveI := hf.target_noetherian
    ∃ m : ℤ,
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ m → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.Modules i).obj
        𝒦Y.complex.obj.obj)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ m - d → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj
        𝒦X.complex.obj.obj)) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules (m - d)).obj 𝒦X.complex.obj.obj ≅
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.sheaf).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.Modules m).obj 𝒦Y.complex.obj.obj))).obj
          (relativeDualizingSheaf (ftsHomOf f hf.separatedFiniteType
            (isSeparatedFiniteType_id Y) (Category.comp_id f)) (nagataCompactification f hf)
            d))
declarations.comment: Similar results hold for X and Y of finite type over S, not necessarily separated, with complexes normalized relative to omega_S: omega_X = f^* omega_Y (x) omega_{X/Y} for connected Cohen-Macaulay schemes

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_upperShriek_iso_pullback_tensor_shift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C10, the canonical isomorphism.** For a Cohen–Macaulay morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of `FTS S` of relative dimension `d` and `K ∈ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`,
`f^!K ≅ Lf^*K ⊗ᴸ ω_{X/Y}[d]`, through `μ_{f,K}` of Tag 0B6U.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriek_iso_pullback_tensor_shift
    (hCM : f.left.IsCohenMacaulay (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ x : X.left,
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.left.fiber (f.left x)) (f.left.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left) (hK : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj) :
    Nonempty ((upperShriek f j).obj K ≅
      ((quasiCoherentDerivedTensor X.left).obj
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' f.left).obj K)).obj
          (relativeDualizingSheafShift f j hCM d hd))
declarations.comment: f^!K = Lf^*K (x) omega_{X/Y}[d] for K in D^+_QCoh

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_upperShriek_comp_iso_pullback_tensor_shift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C10, "in particular".** For `πY : Y ⟶ T`, `πX = f ≫ πY` and
`ω_T ∈ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_T)` (for instance a dualizing complex), with `ω_Y = πY^!ω_T` and
`ω_X = πX^!ω_T`: `ω_X ≅ Lf^*ω_Y ⊗ᴸ ω_{X/Y}[d]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriek_comp_iso_pullback_tensor_shift
    (hCM : f.left.IsCohenMacaulay (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ x : X.left,
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.left.fiber (f.left x)) (f.left.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {T : FTS S} (πY : Y ⟶ T) (πX : X ⟶ T) (hπ : f ≫ πY = πX)
    (jY : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πY.left)) (jX : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πX.left))
    (ωT : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory T.left) (hωT : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow ωT.obj) :
    Nonempty ((upperShriek πX jX).obj ωT ≅
      ((quasiCoherentDerivedTensor X.left).obj
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' f.left).obj ((upperShriek πY jY).obj ωT))).obj
          (relativeDualizingSheafShift f j hCM d hd))
declarations.comment: omega_X = Lf^* omega_Y (x) omega_{X/Y}[d]

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_homology_upperShriek_comp_iso_pullback_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C10, the dualizing modules.** If moreover `ω_T` is a dualizing
complex and `Y` is connected and Cohen–Macaulay, then `ω_Y^•` and `ω_X^•` are concentrated in
single degrees `m` and `m - d`, and their cohomology sheaves `ω_Y`, `ω_X` there satisfy
`ω_X ≅ f^*ω_Y ⊗ ω_{X/Y}`. (Connectedness and Cohen–Macaulayness of `X` are not needed.)
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homology_upperShriek_comp_iso_pullback_tensor
    (hCM : f.left.IsCohenMacaulay (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ x : X.left,
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.left.fiber (f.left x)) (f.left.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    {T : FTS S} (πY : Y ⟶ T) (πX : X ⟶ T) (hπ : f ≫ πY = πX)
    (jY : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πY.left)) (jX : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πX.left))
    (ωT : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory T.left) (hωT : IsDualizingComplex ωT.obj)
    [ConnectedSpace Y.left] (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay Y.left) :
    ∃ m : ℤ,
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ m → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.left.Modules i).obj
        ((upperShriek πY jY).obj ωT).obj)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ m - d → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
        ((upperShriek πX jX).obj ωT).obj)) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules (m - d)).obj
          ((upperShriek πX jX).obj ωT).obj ≅
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.left.sheaf).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f.left).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.left.Modules m).obj
              ((upperShriek πY jY).obj ωT).obj))).obj (relativeDualizingSheaf f j d))
declarations.comment: omega_X = f^* omega_Y (x) omega_{X/Y} for connected Cohen-Macaulay schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_comp
declarations.doc: Gorensteinness at a point is preserved by composition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinAt_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hfg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z)) (x : X)
    (hfx : IsGorensteinAt f hf x) (hgy : IsGorensteinAt g hg (f x)) :
    IsGorensteinAt (f ≫ g) hfg x
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_comp
declarations.doc: The composite of Gorenstein morphisms is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hfg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z))
    (hF : IsGorenstein f hf) (hG : IsGorenstein g hg) :
    IsGorenstein (f ≫ g) hfg
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_left_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If a composite is Gorenstein at a point and the first map is flat there, then the first map is
Gorenstein at that point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinAt_left_of_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hfg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z)) (x : X)
    (hcomp : IsGorensteinAt (f ≫ g) hfg x)
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    IsGorensteinAt f hf x
declarations.comment: part (3), first morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_right_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If a composite is Gorenstein at a point and the first map is flat there, then the second map is
Gorenstein at the image point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinAt_right_of_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hfg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z)) (x : X)
    (hcomp : IsGorensteinAt (f ≫ g) hfg x)
    (hflat : IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom x) :
    IsGorensteinAt g hg (f x)
declarations.comment: part (3), second morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_left_of_comp
declarations.doc: If the composite is Gorenstein and the first map is flat, the first map is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_left_of_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hfg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z))
    (hcomp : IsGorenstein (f ≫ g) hfg) (hflat : Flat f) :
    IsGorenstein f hf
declarations.comment: part (4), first morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isGorensteinAt_image_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If the composite is Gorenstein and the first map is flat, the second map is Gorenstein at each
point in the image of the first.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorensteinAt_image_of_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y))
    (hg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian (g.fiber z))
    (hfg : ∀ z : Z, IsLocallyNoetherian ((f ≫ g).fiber z))
    (hcomp : IsGorenstein (f ≫ g) hfg) (hflat : Flat f) (x : X) :
    IsGorensteinAt g hg (f x)
declarations.comment: part (4), second morphism on the image

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isGorensteinLocalRing_stalk_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C12.** The local ring of the base at any point in the image of a flat
morphism of locally Noetherian schemes with Gorenstein source is Gorenstein.

The map of local rings `𝒪_{Y, f x} → 𝒪_{X, x}` induced by a flat morphism is a flat local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, so `isGorensteinLocalRing_of_flat` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinLocalRing_stalk_of_flat {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Flat f] (x : X) :
    Dualizing.IsGorensteinLocalRing (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))
declarations.comment: Gorenstein local rings of the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isGorenstein_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C12.** A flat morphism of locally Noetherian schemes with Gorenstein
source is a Gorenstein morphism.

The local Noetherianity of the fibres that `Scheme.Hom.IsGorenstein` requires is supplied here
rather than assumed: it follows from local Noetherianity of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorenstein_of_flat {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Flat f] :
    ∃ hf : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y),
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsGorenstein f hf
declarations.comment: Gorenstein morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.trace_ne_zero_iff_isTraceElement_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C13, (1) ⟺ (2).** For a finite algebra `A` over a field `k`, the
algebra trace `Tr_{A/k}` is nonzero exactly when a trace element of the relative dualizing module
is nonzero.

The trace element is given by the predicate `Stacks.Discriminant.IsTraceElement` rather than
chosen; by uniqueness (Tag 0BT7) this is a statement about a single determined element.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_ne_zero_iff_isTraceElement_ne_zero (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] (F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, v, w} k A)
    (τ : dualizingModule F) :
    letI : IsNoetherianRing A := IsNoetherianRing.of_finite k A
    IsTraceElement.{u, v, w, u, max u v, max u v} F τ → (Algebra.trace k A ≠ 0 ↔ τ ≠ 0)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.trace_ne_zero_iff_isSeparable_and_length_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C13, (1) ⟺ (3).** For a finite local algebra `A` over a field `k`, the
algebra trace `Tr_{A/k}` is nonzero exactly when the residue field of `A` is separable over `k`
and the length of `A` is prime to the characteristic of `k`.

"Prime to the characteristic" is the nonvanishing in `k` of the natural number `length_A(A)`, a
condition that also covers characteristic zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_ne_zero_iff_isSeparable_and_length_ne_zero (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsLocalRing A] [Module.Finite k A] :
    Algebra.trace k A ≠ 0 ↔
      Algebra.IsSeparable k (ResidueField A) ∧ ((Module.length A A).toNat : k) ≠ 0
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorenstein_of_syntomic
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0C15.** A syntomic morphism of schemes is a Gorenstein morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_of_syntomic {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hf : Syntomic f) :
    f.IsGorenstein (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_syntomic hf)
declarations.comment: a syntomic morphism is Gorenstein

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorenstein_of_flat_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C15.** A flat local complete intersection morphism of schemes is a Gorenstein
morphism; this is the second formulation of the lemma, equivalent to the first by Stacks
069K.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_of_flat_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (hflat : Flat f) (hlci : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f) :
    f.IsGorenstein (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_syntomic
      (syntomic_of_flat_of_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism hflat hlci))
declarations.comment: a flat local complete intersection morphism is Gorenstein

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.syntomic_le_gorensteinWithLocallyNoetherianFibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C15.** A syntomic morphism of schemes is a Gorenstein morphism: the syntomic
morphisms are contained in the morphism property of having locally Noetherian fibres and being
Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem syntomic_le_gorensteinWithLocallyNoetherianFibers :
    (@Syntomic : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ≤ gorensteinWithLocallyNoetherianFibers
declarations.comment: a syntomic morphism is Gorenstein, as an inclusion of morphism properties

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_inf_lci_le_gorensteinWithLocallyNoetherianFibers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C15.** A flat local complete intersection morphism of schemes is a Gorenstein
morphism: the meet of flatness and being a local complete intersection morphism is contained in
the morphism property of having locally Noetherian fibres and being Gorenstein. This is the second
formulation of the lemma, equivalent to the first by Stacks 069K.
declarations.comment: a flat lci morphism is Gorenstein, as an inclusion of morphism properties

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isInvertible_of_isGorenstein_fiber
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C16], (2) implies (3).** For a quasi-finite flat morphism of Noetherian
schemes whose fibres are Gorenstein schemes, the relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` is an
invertible `𝒪_Y`-module.

Invertibility is the chartwise condition (4) of the same tag, and on a chart it is the fibrewise
condition of [Stacks, Tag 0DWK]; the fibre ring of a chart is the ring of sections of the
scheme-theoretic fibre over an affine open, hence Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isGorenstein_fiber [Flat f] (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (hG : ∀ x : X, AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein (f.fiber x)) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace).property ω.sheaf
declarations.comment: (2) implies (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isInvertible_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C16], (1) implies (3).** The relative dualizing module of a quasi-finite
Gorenstein morphism of Noetherian schemes is an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module.

Gorensteinness of the morphism is flatness together with Gorensteinness of the fibres, by
[Stacks, Tag 0C05].
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_of_isGorenstein (hF : ∀ x : X, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber x))
    (hGor : Scheme.Hom.IsGorenstein f hF) (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) :
    letI : Flat f := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f hF).mp hGor).1
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace).property ω.sheaf
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isGorenstein_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorenstein_tfae :
    List.TFAE [
      Scheme.Hom.IsGorenstein f (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_of_locallyOfFiniteType f),
      Flat f ∧ ∀ x : X, AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein (f.fiber x),
      Flat f ∧ Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace).property (relativeDualizingModuleData f).sheaf,
      ∀ y : Y, ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1), y ∈ V.1 ∧
        letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
        Module.Flat Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) ∧
          ∀ F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1),
            Module.Invertible Γ(Y, V.1) (dualizingModule F)]

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isInvertible_iff_exists_chart_dualizingModule_invertible
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C16], conditions (3) and (4).** For a quasi-finite morphism of locally
Noetherian schemes with relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}`, the module `ω_{Y/X}` is an
invertible `𝒪_Y`-module exactly when every point of `Y` has an affine open neighbourhood
`V = Spec B` lying over an affine open `U = Spec A` of `X` for which the algebraic relative
dualizing module `ω_{B/A}` is an invertible `B`-module.

Both conditions of the source also ask that `f` be flat; flatness plays no role in the
equivalence of the two readings of invertibility, so it is not assumed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_iff_exists_chart_dualizingModule_invertible
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing
          Y.toRingedSpace).property ω.sheaf ↔
      ∀ y : Y, ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens) (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1), y ∈ V.1 ∧
        letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
        ∀ F : FiniteOpenFactorization.{u, u, u} Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1),
          Module.Invertible Γ(Y, V.1) (dualizingModule F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.exists_affineOpens_different_isPrincipal_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C17 (1)].** The different of a quasi-finite Gorenstein morphism of Noetherian
schemes is a locally principal ideal: every point of `Y` has an affine open neighbourhood
`V = Spec B` on which the ideal of sections of `𝔇_f` is generated by a single element of `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpens_different_isPrincipal_of_isGorenstein
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) :
    letI : Flat f := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f _).mp hGor).1
    ∀ (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) (y : Y),
      ∃ V : Y.affineOpens, y ∈ (V : Set Y) ∧
