        (show Ideal Γ(Y, V.1) from (different ω τ).toSubmodule.obj (op V.1)).IsPrincipal

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isLocallyPrincipal_differentIdealSheaf_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C17 (2)].** The closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the different of a
quasi-finite Gorenstein morphism of Noetherian schemes is a locally principal closed
subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyPrincipal_differentIdealSheaf_of_isGorenstein
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) :
    letI : Flat f := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f _).mp hGor).1
    ∀ τ : RelativeTraceSection ω,
      Stacks.Divisors.IsLocallyPrincipal (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.different_sections_eq_noetherDifferent_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C17 (3)].** On affine opens `V = Spec B ⊆ Y` and `U = Spec A ⊆ X` with
`f(V) ⊆ U`, the different of a quasi-finite Gorenstein morphism of Noetherian schemes is the
Noether different of `B` over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem different_sections_eq_noetherDifferent_of_isGorenstein
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens)
    (hVU : V.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) :
    letI : Flat f := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f _).mp hGor).1
    letI : Algebra Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) := (f.appLE U V hVU).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, U.1) := IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian U
    letI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(Y, V.1) := IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian V
    letI : Module.Flat Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) :=
      RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff.mp (f.flat_appLE U.2 V.2 hVU)
    letI : Algebra.QuasiFinite Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1) :=
      RingHom.quasiFinite_algebraMap.mp (LocallyQuasiFinite.quasiFinite_appLE U.2 V.2 hVU)
    ∀ τ : RelativeTraceSection ω,
      (show Ideal Γ(Y, V.1) from (different ω τ).toSubmodule.obj (op V.1)) =
        noetherDifferent Γ(X, U.1) Γ(Y, V.1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_and_invertibleSheafIso_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C17 (6)].** If a quasi-finite Gorenstein morphism of Noetherian schemes is
étale at the associated points of `Y`, then the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the different
is an effective Cartier divisor, and there is exactly one isomorphism `𝒪_Y(R) ≅ ω_{Y/X}` carrying
the canonical section `1_R` to the trace element `τ_{Y/X}`.

Gorensteinness makes `f` flat and `ω_{Y/X}` invertible, which is the situation of
[Stacks, Tag 0BWA (3)].
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_and_invertibleSheafIso_of_isGorenstein
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f)
    (hét : ∀ y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.schemeAssociatedPoints Y, EtaleAt f y) :
    letI : Flat f := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f _).mp hGor).1
    ∀ τ : RelativeTraceSection ω,
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (differentIdealSheaf ω τ) ∧
        ∃! e : Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (differentIdealSheaf ω τ) ≅ ω.sheaf,
          Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom ⊤
            ((Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection' (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)).eval (op ⊤)) =
              τ.sect

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.discriminantIdeal_eq_normIdealSheaf_differentIdealSheaf_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C17 (5)].** If a finite Gorenstein morphism of Noetherian schemes has
relative dualizing module `ω_{Y/X}` and trace element `τ_{Y/X}`, then the norm of the closed
subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the different is the discriminant `D_f`: as ideal sheaves on `X`,
`Norm_f(𝔇_f)` is the discriminant ideal sheaf.

Gorensteinness makes `f` flat and `ω_{Y/X}` invertible, which is the situation of
[Stacks, Tag 0BWA (2)].
declarations.statement:
theorem discriminantIdeal_eq_normIdealSheaf_differentIdealSheaf_of_isGorenstein
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) :
    letI : Flat f := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f _).mp hGor).1
    letI : Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f :=
      (Stacks.Morphisms.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff_isFinite_flat_of_isLocallyNoetherian f).mpr
        ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩
    ∀ τ : RelativeTraceSection ω,
      discriminantIdeal f = Stacks.Norm.normIdealSheaf f (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Discriminant.isIso_different_baseChange_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C17 (4)].** Formation of the closed subscheme `R ⊆ Y` cut out by the
different of a quasi-finite Gorenstein morphism of Noetherian schemes commutes with base change
along an arbitrary morphism `g : X' ⟶ X`: the closed immersion `R' ⟶ R ×_Y Y'` induced by
`Y' ⟶ Y` is an isomorphism.

Gorensteinness makes `ω_{Y/X}` invertible, which is the case of [Stacks, Tag 0BW7] in which the
inverse image of the different is the different of the base change with no flatness hypothesis
on `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_different_baseChange_of_isGorenstein {R R' : Scheme.{u}}
    (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f) (i : R ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    letI : Flat f := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f _).mp hGor).1
    ∀ (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω) (ω' : RelativeDualizingModuleData (pullback.snd f g))
      (τ' : RelativeTraceSection ω') (i' : R' ⟶ pullback f g) [IsClosedImmersion i'],
      i.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω τ → i'.ker = differentIdealSheaf ω' τ' →
      ∀ (k : R' ⟶ R) (hk : k ≫ i = i' ≫ pullback.fst f g), IsIso (pullback.lift k i' hk)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_invertibleSheafIso_upperShriekDualSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C18, the finite case.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite Gorenstein
morphism of schemes separated and of finite type over a Noetherian base, with `X` Cohen–Macaulay
and `f` étale at the generic points of `X`, and let `R ⊆ X` be cut out by the different of the
relative dualizing module `ω_{X/Y} = H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)` of Tag 0BUL. Then the isomorphism
`𝒪_X(R) ≅ ω_{X/Y}` of Tag 0C17 is the unique one sending the canonical section `1_R` to the
section `τ_{X/Y}` of `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)` corresponding under duality to `Trace_f : f_*𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Y`
(Tag 0BVI).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_invertibleSheafIso_upperShriekDualSection [IsFinite f.left]
    (hGor : f.left.IsGorenstein (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f))
    (hX : IsCohenMacaulay X.left) (hét : ∀ x ∈ genericPoints X.left, EtaleAt f.left x)
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) :
    letI : Flat f.left := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f.left
      (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)).mp hGor).1
    ∃! e : Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (differentIdealSheaf
        (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j)
        (relativeTraceSectionData (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j))) ≅
        (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j).sheaf,
      Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom ⊤
          ((Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection' (differentIdealSheaf
            (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j)
            (relativeTraceSectionData (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j)))).eval
              (op ⊤)) =
        upperShriekDualSection f (pushforwardTrace f.left) j
declarations.comment: if f is finite: O_X(R) = omega_{X/Y} comes from tau_{X/Y}, dual to Trace_f

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_homology_upperShriek_iso_pullback_tensor_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C18.** Let `S` be Noetherian, `f : X ⟶ Y` a quasi-finite Gorenstein
morphism of `FTS S` étale at the generic points of `X`, with `X` Cohen–Macaulay, and let
`ω_Y^• = π_Y^!ω_T`, `ω_X^• = π_X^!ω_T` for `π_X = f ≫ π_Y` and `ω_T` bounded below (for instance
a dualizing complex on the base). Let `ω_{X/Y}` be any relative dualizing module (Tag 0BVG; by
Tag 0BUL it is `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)`), `τ` its trace element and `R` the closed subscheme cut out by the
different. Then in every degree `i`
`Hⁱ(ω_X^•) ≅ f^*Hⁱ(ω_Y^•) ⊗ ω_{X/Y} ≅ f^*Hⁱ(ω_Y^•) ⊗ 𝒪_X(R)`.
When `X` and `Y` are Cohen–Macaulay and `ω_T` is dualizing, `ω_X^•` and `ω_Y^•` have a single
nonzero cohomology sheaf on each connected component, in the same degree; `ω_X` and `ω_Y` are
these sheaves, and the displayed isomorphisms are `ω_X = f^*ω_Y ⊗ ω_{X/Y} = f^*ω_Y ⊗ 𝒪_X(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_homology_upperShriek_iso_pullback_tensor_of_isGorenstein
    (hGor : f.left.IsGorenstein (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f))
    (hX : IsCohenMacaulay X.left) (hét : ∀ x ∈ genericPoints X.left, EtaleAt f.left x)
    {T : FTS S} (πY : Y ⟶ T) (πX : X ⟶ T) (hπ : f ≫ πY = πX)
    (jY : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πY.left)) (jX : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πX.left))
    (ωT : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory T.left) (hωT : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow ωT.obj)
    (i : ℤ) :
    letI : Flat f.left := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f.left
      (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)).mp hGor).1
    ∀ (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f.left) (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω),
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
          ((upperShriek πX jX).obj ωT).obj ≅
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.left.sheaf).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f.left).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.left.Modules i).obj
              ((upperShriek πY jY).obj ωT).obj))).obj ω.sheaf) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
          ((upperShriek πX jX).obj ωT).obj ≅
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.left.sheaf).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f.left).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.left.Modules i).obj
              ((upperShriek πY jY).obj ωT).obj))).obj
          (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)))
declarations.comment: omega_X = f^* omega_Y (x) omega_{X/Y} = f^* omega_Y (x) O_X(R)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriek_quasiFinite_isGorenstein_dualizing_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C18**, the whole remark. Let `S` be Noetherian and `f : X ⟶ Y` a
quasi-finite Gorenstein morphism of schemes separated and of finite type over `S`, with `X`
Cohen–Macaulay and `f` étale at the generic points of `X`. Let `ω_Y^• = π_Y^!ω_T` and
`ω_X^• = π_X^!ω_T` for `π_X = f ≫ π_Y` and a bounded below `ω_T` (for instance `T = S` with its
dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, which gives the normalized dualizing complexes). Then:

1. for every relative dualizing module `ω_{X/Y}` (Tag 0BVG; by Tag 0BUL it is `H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)`),
   with trace element `τ` and `R` the closed subscheme cut out by the different, in every degree
   `i` one has `Hⁱ(ω_X^•) ≅ f^*Hⁱ(ω_Y^•) ⊗ ω_{X/Y} ≅ f^*Hⁱ(ω_Y^•) ⊗ 𝒪_X(R)`; in the degree of the
   dualizing modules this is `ω_X = f^*ω_Y ⊗ ω_{X/Y} = f^*ω_Y ⊗ 𝒪_X(R)`;
2. if moreover `f` is finite, the isomorphism `𝒪_X(R) ≅ ω_{X/Y} = H⁰(f^!𝒪_Y)` is the unique one
   sending the canonical section `1_R` to the section `τ_{X/Y}` which corresponds under duality to
   `Trace_f : f_*𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_Y` (Tag 0BVI).
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriek_quasiFinite_isGorenstein_dualizing_iso
    (hGor : f.left.IsGorenstein (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f))
    (hX : IsCohenMacaulay X.left) (hét : ∀ x ∈ genericPoints X.left, EtaleAt f.left x)
    {T : FTS S} (πY : Y ⟶ T) (πX : X ⟶ T) (hπ : f ≫ πY = πX)
    (jY : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πY.left)) (jX : CompactificationOf (Over.mk πX.left))
    (ωT : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory T.left) (hωT : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow ωT.obj) :
    letI : Flat f.left := ((Scheme.Hom.isGorenstein_iff_flat_and_isGorenstein_fiber f.left
      (isLocallyNoetherian_fiber_left f)).mp hGor).1
    (∀ (i : ℤ) (ω : RelativeDualizingModuleData f.left) (τ : RelativeTraceSection ω),
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
          ((upperShriek πX jX).obj ωT).obj ≅
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.left.sheaf).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f.left).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.left.Modules i).obj
              ((upperShriek πY jY).obj ωT).obj))).obj ω.sheaf) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.left.Modules i).obj
          ((upperShriek πX jX).obj ωT).obj ≅
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.left.sheaf).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f.left).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.left.Modules i).obj
              ((upperShriek πY jY).obj ωT).obj))).obj
          (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (differentIdealSheaf ω τ)))) ∧
    ∀ [IsFinite f.left] (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)),
      ∃! e : Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (differentIdealSheaf
          (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j)
          (relativeTraceSectionData (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j))) ≅
          (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j).sheaf,
        Scheme.Modules.Hom.app e.hom ⊤
            ((Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSection' (differentIdealSheaf
              (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j)
              (relativeTraceSectionData (upperShriekRelativeDualizingModuleData f j)))).eval
                (op ⊤)) =
          upperShriekDualSection f (pushforwardTrace f.left) j
declarations.comment: the whole remark: omega_X = f^* omega_Y (x) omega_{X/Y} = f^* omega_Y (x) O_X(R), and for f finite O_X(R) = omega_{X/Y} comes from tau_{X/Y}, dual to Trace_f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_dualizingSheafOverField
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k` of dimension one with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`. If `X` is
Gorenstein, then `deg(ω_X) = 2g - 2`, where `g` is the genus of `X` and `ω_X` is the dualizing
sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 0BS2].
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleCurveDegree_dualizingSheafOverField (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)]
    [IsGorenstein X] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    letI := connectedSpace_of_isIso_globalSections k f
    letI := isInvertible_dualizingSheafOverField_of_connectedSpace k f hdim
    invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim.le (Stacks.Duality.dualizingSheafOverField f) =
      2 * (genus f : ℤ) - 2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree_relativeDifferentials_eq_two_mul_genus_sub_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1A, second equality.** Let `X` be a smooth proper curve over a field
`k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, of genus `g`. Then `deg(Ω_{X/k}) = 2g - 2`: `Ω_{X/k} ≅ ω_X` by
Tag 0BS2 (6), and `deg(ω_X) = 2g - 2` (Tag 0C19 for the Gorenstein curve `X`).
declarations.statement:
theorem invertibleCurveDegree_relativeDifferentials_eq_two_mul_genus_sub_two :
    invertibleCurveDegree k f (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)))
        (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) = 2 * genus f - 2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_relativeDifferentials_eq_genus_and_curveDegree
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C1A]**: for a smooth proper curve `X` over a field `k` with
`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and genus `g`, `dim_k H⁰(X, Ω_{X/k}) = g` and `deg(Ω_{X/k}) = 2g - 2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_relativeDifferentials_eq_genus_and_curveDegree
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pX.appTop)] :
    Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k pX (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials pX) 0) =
        genus pX ∧
      letI := smoothOfRelativeDimension_one_of_isCurve k pX
      letI := Scheme.Hom.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_one_relativeDifferentials pX
      curveDegree k pX (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := pX)))
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials pX) 1 = 2 * (genus pX : ℤ) - 2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genericallyEtale_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1C.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of smooth curves over a field `k`
the following are equivalent: the differential `f^*Ω_{Y/k} ⟶ Ω_{X/k}` is nonzero; the sheaf
`Ω_{X/Y}` is supported on a proper closed subset of `X`; `f` is unramified on a nonempty open;
`f` is étale on a nonempty open; `f` is dominant and the extension of function fields it induces
is finite separable.
declarations.statement:
theorem genericallyEtale_tfae
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [Smooth pX] [Smooth pY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) :
    List.TFAE [
      Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsMap f pY pX (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
        (by simpa using hf) ≠ 0,
      ∃ Z : Set X, IsClosed Z ∧ Z ≠ Set.univ ∧
        SheafOfModules.supp (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f) ⊆ Z,
      ∃ U : X.Opens, Nonempty U ∧ Unramified (U.ι ≫ f),
      ∃ U : X.Opens, Nonempty U ∧ Etale (U.ι ≫ f),
      IsDominant f ∧
        (letI : Algebra (Y.residueField (f (genericPoint X)))
            (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) :=
          (f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint X)).hom.toAlgebra
         Module.Finite (Y.residueField (f (genericPoint X)))
            (X.residueField (genericPoint X)) ∧
         Algebra.IsSeparableExtension (Y.residueField (f (genericPoint X)))
            (X.residueField (genericPoint X)))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.two_mul_genus_sub_two_eq_degreeOver_mul_add_of_exists_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1D (Riemann–Hurwitz).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of smooth
proper curves over a field `k` satisfying the equivalent conditions of Tag 0C1C (here (4): `f` is
étale on a nonempty open), with `k = H⁰(Y, 𝒪_Y) = H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)`, and let `X`, `Y` have genus
`g_X`, `g_Y`. Then

`2g_X - 2 = (2g_Y - 2) deg(f) + deg(R)`,

where `R ⊆ X` is the effective Cartier divisor cut out by the different of `f`, of degree
`dim_k Γ(R, 𝒪_R)`, and `deg(f) = [k(X) : k(Y)]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem two_mul_genus_sub_two_eq_degreeOver_mul_add_of_exists_etale (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    (hgen : ∃ U : X.Opens, Nonempty U ∧ Etale (U.ι ≫ f)) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k pX pY f hf
    letI : IsDominant f := isDominant_of_exists_etale_comp_ι pX pY f hf hgen
    letI : Algebra k Γ((Stacks.Discriminant.kaehlerDifferent f).subscheme, ⊤) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫
        ((Stacks.Discriminant.kaehlerDifferent f).subschemeι ≫ pX).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    2 * (genus pX : ℤ) - 2 =
      (2 * (genus pY : ℤ) - 2) * (degreeOver f : ℤ) +
        (Module.finrank k Γ((Stacks.Discriminant.kaehlerDifferent f).subscheme, ⊤) : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.two_mul_genus_sub_two_eq_degreeOver_mul_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1D (Riemann–Hurwitz).** Let `f : X → Y` be a morphism of smooth
proper curves over a field `k` whose differential `f^*Ω_{Y/k} → Ω_{X/k}` is nonzero (condition (1)
of [Stacks, Tag 0C1C]), with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k = H⁰(Y, 𝒪_Y)`, and let `R ⊆ X` be the closed
subscheme cut out by the different of `f`. Then `2g_X - 2 = (2g_Y - 2) deg(f) + deg(R)`, where
`deg(R) = dim_k Γ(R, 𝒪_R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem two_mul_genus_sub_two_eq_degreeOver_mul_add [IsProper pY]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pX.appTop)]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pY.appTop)]
    (hdf : Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsMap f pY pX (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
      (by simpa using hf) ≠ 0) :
    letI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k pX pY f hf
    letI : IsDominant f := isDominant_of_relativeDifferentialsMap_ne_zero pX pY f hf hdf
    letI : Algebra k Γ((kaehlerDifferent f).subscheme, ⊤) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ ((kaehlerDifferent f).subschemeι ≫ pX).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    2 * (genus pX : ℤ) - 2 =
      (2 * (genus pY : ℤ) - 2) * (degreeOver f : ℤ) +
        Module.finrank k Γ((kaehlerDifferent f).subscheme, ⊤)
declarations.comment: the different is the Kähler different, which is the different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG; the conditions of Tag 0C1C are stated as its condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.differential_uniformizer_basis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1E.** At a closed point of a scheme over a field, smooth there of
relative dimension one and with separable residue field, the differential of any uniformizer
freely generates the stalk of relative differentials.
declarations.statement:
theorem differential_uniformizer_basis
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (hsm : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = 1)
    (hsep :
      letI : Algebra k (X.residueField x) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation x).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsSeparable k (X.residueField x))
    (s : X.presheaf.stalk x)
    (hs : maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x) = Ideal.span {s})
    (U : X.Opens) (hxU : x ∈ U) (a : X.presheaf.obj (op U))
    (hsa : ((X.presheaf.germ U x hxU).hom a) = s) :
    letI := relativeDifferentialStalkModule f x
    ∃ e : X.presheaf.stalk x ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x] relativeDifferentialStalk f x,
      e 1 =
        (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
            (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).val.presheaf U x hxU)
          ((Scheme.Hom.universalRelativeDerivation f).d a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.two_mul_genus_sub_two_eq_degreeOver_mul_add_finsum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1F, the formula.** Under the assumptions of [Stacks, Tag 0C1D],
`2g_X - 2 = (2g_Y - 2) deg(f) + ∑_x d_x [κ(x) : k]`, the sum over the closed points `x` of `X`,
where `d_x = length_{𝒪_{X,x}}(𝒪_{X,x} / 𝓘_{R,x})` is the multiplicity of `x` in the closed
subscheme `R` cut out by the different of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem two_mul_genus_sub_two_eq_degreeOver_mul_add_finsum [IsProper pY]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pX.appTop)]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pY.appTop)]
    (hdf : Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialsMap f pY pX (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))
      (by simpa using hf) ≠ 0) :
    letI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k pX pY f hf
    letI : IsDominant f := isDominant_of_relativeDifferentialsMap_ne_zero pX pY f hf hdf
    2 * (genus pX : ℤ) - 2 =
      (2 * (genus pY : ℤ) - 2) * (degreeOver f : ℤ) +
        ((∑ᶠ x : {x : X // IsClosed ({x} : Set X)},
          letI : Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x.1) :=
            ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pX.appTop ≫
              X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x.1 (by simp)).hom.toAlgebra
          (Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk x.1)
              (X.presheaf.stalk x.1 ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (kaehlerDifferent f) x.1)).toNat *
            Module.finrank k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x.1)) : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the formula 2g_X - 2 = (2g_Y - 2) deg(f) + Σ d_x [κ(x) : k] over the closed points x; the different is the Kähler different, which is the different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.multiplicity_kaehlerDifferent_eq_length_stalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1F, part (1).** Let `f : X → Y` be a dominant morphism of smooth
curves over a field and `x ∈ X` a closed point. The multiplicity `d_x = length_{𝒪_{X,x}} 𝒪_{R,x}`
of `x` in the closed subscheme `R` cut out by the different of `f` is the length of the stalk
`Ω_{X/Y,x}` of the sheaf of relative differentials.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicity_kaehlerDifferent_eq_length_stalk (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    letI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k pX pY f hf
    letI : DecidableEq (OrderDual (TopologicalSpace.OpenNhds x)) := Classical.decEq _
    Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (X.presheaf.stalk x ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (kaehlerDifferent f) x) =
      Module.length (ToType (X.sheaf.presheaf.stalk x))
        (ToType (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f).val.presheaf x))
declarations.comment:
(1): `d_x = length_{𝒪_{X,x}}(Ω_{X/Y,x})`, for a dominant morphism of smooth curves;
the different is the Kähler different, which is the different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ramificationIdx_sub_one_le_multiplicity_kaehlerDifferent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1F, part (2).** Let `f : X → Y` be a dominant morphism of smooth
curves over a field and `x ∈ X` a closed point with image `y`. The multiplicity `d_x` of `x` in
the closed subscheme cut out by the different of `f` is at least `e_x - 1`, where `e_x` is the
ramification index of `𝒪_{X,x}` over `𝒪_{Y,y}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ramificationIdx_sub_one_le_multiplicity_kaehlerDifferent (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    letI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k pX pY f hf
    letI := (f.stalkMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    ((ramificationIdx (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤
      Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (X.presheaf.stalk x ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (kaehlerDifferent f) x)
declarations.comment:
(2): `d_x ≥ e_x - 1`, for a dominant morphism of smooth curves; the different is the
Kähler different, which is the different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.multiplicity_kaehlerDifferent_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1F, part (3).** Let `f : X → Y` be a dominant morphism of smooth
curves over a field and `x ∈ X` a closed point with image `y`. The multiplicity `d_x` of `x` in
the closed subscheme cut out by the different of `f` equals `e_x - 1` if and only if `𝒪_{X,x}` is
tamely ramified over `𝒪_{Y,y}`: the residue field extension `κ(x) / κ(y)` is separable and the
characteristic of `κ(y)` does not divide `e_x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicity_kaehlerDifferent_eq_iff (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    letI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k pX pY f hf
    letI := (f.stalkMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (X.presheaf.stalk x ⧸ IdealSheafData.stalk (kaehlerDifferent f) x) =
        ((ramificationIdx (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ↔
      (letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra;
        Algebra.IsSeparable (Y.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) ∧
        ¬ ringChar (Y.residueField (f x)) ∣
          ramificationIdx (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment:
(3): `d_x = e_x - 1` if and only if `𝒪_{X,x}` is tamely ramified over `𝒪_{Y,y}`,
for a dominant morphism of smooth curves; the different is the Kähler different, which is the
different of Tag 0BW4 by Tag 0BWG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ramificationIdx_baseChange_algClosure_eq_finInsepDegree
declarations.doc:
The ramification index at a closed point of a smooth curve after extension to an algebraic
closure is the inseparable degree of the original residue field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ramificationIdx_baseChange_algClosure_eq_finInsepDegree
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsAlgClosure k K]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f]
    (xbar : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hxbar : IsClosed ({xbar} : Set
      (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}))) :
    let p := pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))
    let x := p xbar
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) :
          Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk xbar) :=
      (p.stalkMap xbar).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra k (X.residueField x) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation x).hom.toAlgebra
    Stacks.DiscreteValuationRing.Ramification.ramificationIdx (X.presheaf.stalk x)
      ((pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) :
        Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk xbar) =
      Field.finInsepDegree k (X.residueField x)

declarations.name: Algebra.algEquiv_prod_or_dualNumber_of_natCard_subalgebra_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1I.** An algebra over an algebraically closed field with exactly
two subalgebras is isomorphic, as an algebra, either to the product algebra or to the dual
numbers.
declarations.statement:
theorem algEquiv_prod_or_dualNumber_of_natCard_subalgebra_eq_two
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (h : Nat.card (Subalgebra k A) = 2) :
    Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[k] k × k) ∨ Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[k] DualNumber k)

declarations.name: Algebra.algEquiv_prod_or_dualNumber_of_no_intermediateSubalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1I.** An algebra over an algebraically closed field with no proper
intermediate subalgebra is either the product algebra or the algebra of dual numbers.
declarations.statement:
theorem algEquiv_prod_or_dualNumber_of_no_intermediateSubalgebra
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (h_ne : (⊥ : Subalgebra k A) ≠ ⊤)
    (h : ∀ B : Subalgebra k A, B = ⊥ ∨ B = ⊤) :
    Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[k] k × k) ∨ Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[k] DualNumber k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic `k`-schemes glues the distinct rational points `a` and `b` if
they have the same image, the morphism is finite and is an isomorphism off that image, and
the additive difference of evaluation at `a` and `b` gives the skyscraper quotient of its
pushforward structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def IsGlueingTwoPoints {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X') : Prop
declarations.comment: glueing_two_points

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishUnits.isShortExact_units_of_isGlueingTwoPoints
declarations.doc:
**The short exact sequence of sheaves of units of a glueing of two rational points.**
If `f : X' ⟶ X` glues the distinct rational points `a` and `b` of `X'` to the point
`x = f(a) = f(b)` of `X`, then

`1 ⟶ 𝒪_X^* ⟶ f_*𝒪_{X'}^* ⟶ (k^*)_x ⟶ 1`

is a short exact sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on `X`, the first map being pullback of
units along `f` and the second the ratio `h ↦ h(a) h(b)⁻¹` of the two values of a unit. Both
maps are pinned down on sections, so the sequence is the one of [Stacks, Tag 0C1J] and not
merely some exact sequence with those terms.

This is the input from which [Stacks, Tag 0C1M] obtains the exact sequence
`k^* ⟶ Pic(X) ⟶ Pic(X') ⟶ 0`: the five-term low-degree cohomology sequence over `U = ⊤`,
`Stacks.Cohomology.AbelianColimit.H'longExactSequence_exact`, gives
`H⁰(X, f_*𝒪_{X'}^*) ⟶ k^* ⟶ H¹(X, 𝒪_X^*) ⟶ H¹(X, f_*𝒪_{X'}^*)`, and
`Stacks.Cohomology.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup` identifies the first cohomology of a
units sheaf with the Picard group.
declarations.statement:
theorem isShortExact_units_of_isGlueingTwoPoints {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b) (hab : a ≫ f = b ≫ f) :
    ∃ (φ : unitsSheaf X.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace ⟶
        (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward AddCommGrpCat.{u} f.base).obj
          (unitsSheaf X'.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace))
      (ψ : (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward AddCommGrpCat.{u} f.base).obj
          (unitsSheaf X'.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace) ⟶
        skyscraperUnitsSheaf (k := k) X (gluedPoint f a))
      (hzero : φ ≫ ψ = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk φ ψ hzero).ShortExact ∧
      (∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : Γ(X, U)ˣ),
        φ.hom.app (op U) (Additive.ofMul s) =
          Additive.ofMul (Units.map (f.app U).hom.toMonoidHom s)) ∧
      (∀ (U : X.Opens) (hz : gluedPoint f a ∈ U)
        (ha : a.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k) ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ U)
        (hb : b.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k) ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (s : Γ(X', f ⁻¹ᵁ U)ˣ),
        skyscraperUnitsEval X (gluedPoint f a) hz
            (ψ.hom.app (op U) (Additive.ofMul s)) =
          Additive.ofMul (unitRatioAt a b (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) ha hb s))
declarations.comment: the units short exact sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.shortExact_units_of_isSquishingTangentVector
declarations.doc:
**The short exact sequence of sheaves of units of the squishing of a tangent vector.**
If `f : X' ⟶ X` squishes the tangent vector `ϑ` of `X'` to the rational point `x` of `X`, then

`1 ⟶ 𝒪_X^* ⟶ f_*𝒪_{X'}^* ⟶ (k, +)_x ⟶ 1`

is a short exact sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on `X`, the first map being pullback of
units along `f` and the second the logarithmic `ε`-derivative along `ϑ`. Both maps are pinned
down on sections — by `Stacks.GlueSquishUnits.unitsPushforwardMap_app` and
`Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.epsilonLogDerivSheafHom_app` — so the sequence is the one of
[Stacks, Tag 0C1N] and not merely some exact sequence with those terms.

Injectivity of the first map and exactness in the middle hold already on sections over every
open. Surjectivity of the second is local at the contracted point, where it is the surjectivity
of the logarithmic `ε`-derivative on the units of the stalk of `f_*𝒪_{X'}`; away from the
contracted point the skyscraper has no sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_units_of_isSquishingTangentVector {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ) :
    (ShortComplex.mk (unitsPushforwardMap f) (epsilonLogDerivSheafHom f θ)
      (unitsPushforwardMap_comp_epsilonLogDerivSheafHom f θ h)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the units short exact sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic `k`-schemes squishes a tangent vector if that vector is a closed
immersion which is contracted to a rational point, the morphism is finite and an isomorphism
off that point, and taking the coefficient of `ε` gives the skyscraper quotient of the
pushforward structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def IsSquishingTangentVector {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X') : Prop
declarations.comment: squishing_tangent_vector

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.shortExact_of_isSquishingTangentVector
declarations.doc:
**The short exact sequence of sheaves attached to the squishing of a tangent vector.**

If `f : X' ⟶ X` squishes the tangent vector `ϑ` of `X'` to the rational point `x` of `X`, then
there is a map of additive sheaves `ψ : f_*𝒪_{X'} ⟶ (k, +)_x` to the additive skyscraper at `x`
for which

`0 → 𝒪_X → f_*𝒪_{X'} → (k, +)_x → 0`

is short exact, and `ψ` is given on every neighbourhood `U` of `x` by the coefficient of `ε` of
the restriction along `ϑ` of a section of `𝒪_{X'}` over `f⁻¹U`. This is the clause of
[Stacks, Tag 0C1K] that the exactness statements of Tags 0C1M and 0C1N consume.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_of_isSquishingTangentVector {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ) :
    ∃ (ψ : pushforwardAddSheaf f ⟶ skyscraperAddSheaf (k := k) X
        ((θ ≫ f).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (DualNumber k))))
      (hzero : structureToPushforwardAddSheaf f ≫ ψ = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk (structureToPushforwardAddSheaf f) ψ hzero).ShortExact ∧
        ∀ (U : X.Opens)
          (hx : (θ ≫ f).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (DualNumber k)) ∈ U)
          (s : Γ(X', f ⁻¹ᵁ U)),
          ψ.hom.app (op U) s =
            skyscraperAddSheafMk X ((θ ≫ f).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (DualNumber k))) hx
              (epsilonCoefficientAt θ (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (by exact hx) s)
declarations.comment: the short exact sequence of sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.algEquiv_prod_or_dualNumber_of_minimal
declarations.doc:
**The local algebra of a minimal step of [Stacks, Tag 0C1L].** Let `k` be an algebraically
closed field, let `A` be a local `k`-algebra whose residue field is `k` (hypothesis `hres`: every
element of `A` is a scalar modulo the maximal ideal), and let `B` be a module-finite `A`-algebra
which is not generated by `A` (hypothesis `hne`) and admits no `A`-subalgebra strictly between
`A` and `B` (hypothesis `hmin`). Then the fibre `B ⧸ m_A B` is, as a `k`-algebra, either the
product `k × k` or the dual numbers `k[ε]`.

In the source this is the whole of the case `n = 1`: with `A = 𝒪_{X, x}` and
`B = (f_*𝒪_{X'})_x`, the absence of a proper intermediate subalgebra forces `B = A + m_A B`
(Nakayama) and then forces the fibre `C = B / m_A B` to have exactly two `k`-subalgebras, so
[Stacks, Tag 0C1I] applies. The two outcomes are what make the step a glueing of two points
respectively a squishing of a tangent vector.

This is the mathematical heart of [Stacks, Tag 0C1L], but not the whole lemma: see the
implementation notes of this file for the geometric statements that remain.
declarations.statement:
theorem algEquiv_prod_or_dualNumber_of_minimal (k : Type u) (A B : Type v) [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsLocalRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower k A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    (hres : ∀ a : A, ∃ c : k, a - algebraMap k A c ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (hne : (⊥ : Subalgebra A B) ≠ ⊤) (hmin : ∀ E : Subalgebra A B, E = ⊥ ∨ E = ⊤) :
    Nonempty ((B ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B)) ≃ₐ[k] k × k) ∨
      Nonempty ((B ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B)) ≃ₐ[k] DualNumber k)
declarations.comment: the local algebra of a minimal step

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.IsElementaryStep
declarations.doc:
**One step of the factorization of [Stacks, Tag 0C1L]**: a morphism of algebraic
`k`-schemes which either glues two rational points ([Stacks, Tag 0C1J]) or squishes a tangent
vector ([Stacks, Tag 0C1K]).
declarations.statement:
def IsElementaryStep {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {Y' Y : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (f : Y' ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: the elementary modifications

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.IsElementaryChain
declarations.doc:
**The conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 0C1L], as a predicate on one morphism.** `f` is a composite
of finitely many elementary modifications and isomorphisms, which is the content of the source's
chain `X' = X_n ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X_0 = X` together with its endpoint identifications. The recursor is the
induction on the length that the source's proof performs.
declarations.statement:
inductive IsElementaryChain (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] :
    {Y' Y : Over (Spec (.of k))} → (Y' ⟶ Y) → Prop
declarations.comment: the factorization, as an inductive predicate

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.toIntermediateOver
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `X' ⟶ Spec_X(A)` over `X` attached to a morphism `ψ : A ⟶ f_* 𝒪_{X'}` of
`𝒪_X`-algebras.** It is the morphism corresponding to `ψ` under the universal property of the
relative spectrum, read through the identification `(Spec_X(A) ⟶ X)_* 𝒪 ≅ A`.
declarations.statement: def toIntermediateOver : Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk (relativeSpecToBase A)
declarations.comment: the intermediate factorization attached to a subalgebra

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.toIntermediate_comp_relativeSpecToBase
declarations.doc:
**The factorization of `f` attached to a morphism `ψ : A ⟶ f_* 𝒪_{X'}`.** The morphism
`X' ⟶ Spec_X(A)` of `Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.toIntermediate`, followed by the structure morphism
of the relative spectrum, is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toIntermediate_comp_relativeSpecToBase :
    toIntermediate f A ψ ≫ relativeSpecToBase A = f
declarations.comment: the intermediate factorization attached to a subalgebra

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.isoRelativeSpecOfAffine
declarations.doc:
**A scheme affine over `X` is the relative spectrum of its algebra of functions over `X`.**
For `g : Y ⟶ X` affine, the comparison morphism `Y ⟶ Spec_X(g_* 𝒪_Y)` is an isomorphism of
schemes over `X`. This is [Stacks, Tag 01SA] in the form used by [Stacks, Tag 0C1L]: an
intermediate factorization with affine second half is a relative spectrum.
declarations.statement:
def isoRelativeSpecOfAffine :
    Over.mk g ≅ Over.mk (relativeSpecToBase (pushforwardAlgebra g))
declarations.comment: every affine intermediate factorization comes from a subalgebra

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.toIntermediateOver_factorizationAlgebraHom
declarations.doc:
**Every intermediate factorization with affine second half comes from an algebra.** For a
factorization `f = u ≫ g` with `g` affine, the comparison isomorphism
`Y ≅ Spec_X(g_* 𝒪_Y)` carries `u` to the morphism attached by
`Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.toIntermediateOver` to the algebra map `g_* 𝒪_Y ⟶ f_* 𝒪_{X'}` of the
factorization.
declarations.statement:
theorem toIntermediateOver_factorizationAlgebraHom :
    toIntermediateOver f (pushforwardAlgebra g) (factorizationAlgebraHom f u g hu) =
      (Over.homMk u hu : Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk g) ≫ toRelativeSpecOfAffine g
declarations.comment: every affine intermediate factorization comes from a subalgebra

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.exists_split_of_algebraHom
declarations.doc:
**The splitting step of [Stacks, Tag 0C1L].** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a finite morphism of
schemes over a base `S` with `𝒪_X ⊂ f_*𝒪_{X'}` which is an isomorphism over an open `U` of `X`,
and let `𝒜` be a finite quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras with an injection
`ψ : 𝒜 ⟶ f_*𝒪_{X'}` of `𝒪_X`-algebras. Then `f` factors over `S` as `p ≫ q` with

* `q : Spec_X(𝒜) ⟶ X` finite, with `𝒪_X ⊂ q_*𝒪`, and an isomorphism over `U`;
* `p : X' ⟶ Spec_X(𝒜)` finite, with `𝒪_{Spec_X(𝒜)} ⊂ p_*𝒪_{X'}`, and an isomorphism over
  `q⁻¹U`.

Finiteness of `q` is the finiteness of `𝒜`; finiteness of `p` is finiteness of `f` cancelled
against it; `𝒪_X ⊂ q_*𝒪` is the chain `𝒪_X ⊂ 𝒜 ⊂ f_*𝒪_{X'}`;
`𝒪_{Spec_X(𝒜)} ⊂ p_*𝒪_{X'}` is `ψ` propagated from the preimages of the affine opens of `X`
to every open of `Spec_X(𝒜)` by
`Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.mono_hom_pushforwardAlgebra_toIntermediate`; and the two statements
over `U` are the squeeze
`Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.isIso_morphismRestrict_relativeSpecToBase` together with cancellation
of `q ∣_ U` out of `f ∣_ U`.

The last clause is the *capture* clause: over every open `V` of `X` the sections of `𝒜` are
sections of the intermediate scheme, by
`Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.mem_range_appLE_toIntermediate`. It is what makes the splitting
nontrivial — without it a splitting is produced even by `𝒜 = 𝒪_X`, for which `q` is an
isomorphism and nothing has happened.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_split_of_algebraHom {S : Scheme.{u}} {W' W : Over S} (f : W' ⟶ W)
    [IsFinite f.left] [Mono (pushforwardAlgebra f.left).hom] (A : AlgebraSheaf W.left)
    [AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A] (hAfin : AlgebraSheaf.IsFinite A)
    (ψ : A ⟶ pushforwardAlgebra f.left)
    (hψ : ∀ V : W.left.Opens, Function.Injective (ψ.right.hom.app (op V)).hom)
    {U : W.left.Opens} (hU : IsIso (f.left ∣_ U)) :
    ∃ (Z : Over S) (p : W' ⟶ Z) (q : Z ⟶ W), p ≫ q = f ∧ IsFinite q.left ∧
      Mono (pushforwardAlgebra q.left).hom ∧ IsIso (q.left ∣_ U) ∧ IsFinite p.left ∧
      Mono (pushforwardAlgebra p.left).hom ∧ IsIso (p.left ∣_ (q.left ⁻¹ᵁ U)) ∧
      ∀ (V : W.left.Opens) (hle : f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤ p.left ⁻¹ᵁ (q.left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
        (s : Γ(W'.left, f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V)), s ∈ Set.range (ψ.right.hom.app (op V)).hom →
          s ∈ Set.range (p.left.appLE (q.left ⁻¹ᵁ V) (f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V) hle).hom
declarations.comment: the splitting attached to a finite intermediate subalgebra

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.exists_split_isAlmostIso_of_algebraHom
declarations.doc:
**The splitting step of [Stacks, Tag 0C1L], read against the hypotheses of the lemma.** An
almost isomorphism of algebraic `k`-schemes and a finite quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-subalgebra `𝒜` of
`f_*𝒪_{X'}` give a factorization `f = p ≫ q` over `Spec k` in which *both* halves are again
almost isomorphisms, so both satisfy every hypothesis of the source.

Together with a measure which drops along this factorization, this is the hypothesis `hsplit`
of `Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.isElementaryChain_of_isAlmostIso`. No measure is constructed
here. The last clause records that the splitting *captures* the sections of `𝒜`, which is what
distinguishes it from the trivial splitting by `𝒜 = 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_split_isAlmostIso_of_algebraHom {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : X' ⟶ X) (hf : IsAlmostIso f) (A : AlgebraSheaf X.left)
    [AlgebraSheaf.IsQuasicoherent A] (hAfin : AlgebraSheaf.IsFinite A)
    (ψ : A ⟶ pushforwardAlgebra f.left)
    (hψ : ∀ V : X.left.Opens, Function.Injective (ψ.right.hom.app (op V)).hom) :
    ∃ (Z : Over (Spec (.of k))) (p : X' ⟶ Z) (q : Z ⟶ X),
      p ≫ q = f ∧ IsAlmostIso q ∧ IsAlmostIso p ∧
      ∀ (V : X.left.Opens) (hle : f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤ p.left ⁻¹ᵁ (q.left ⁻¹ᵁ V))
        (s : Γ(X'.left, f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V)), s ∈ Set.range (ψ.right.hom.app (op V)).hom →
          s ∈ Set.range (p.left.appLE (q.left ⁻¹ᵁ V) (f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V) hle).hom
declarations.comment: the splitting, read against the hypotheses of the lemma

declarations.name: Stacks.GlueSquishFactor.IsAlmostIso.isElementaryChain
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C1L].** A finite morphism of algebraic `k`-schemes which is injective on
structure sheaves and an isomorphism away from a finite set of points is a composite of glueings
of two rational points and squishings of tangent vectors.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsAlmostIso.isElementaryChain {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : X' ⟶ X) (hf : IsAlmostIso f) : IsElementaryChain k f

declarations.name: Stacks.GluePicard.surjective_schemePullbackClassHom
declarations.doc:
**Pullback of invertible modules along the glueing of two rational points is surjective on
Picard groups.** The glueing is finite and is an isomorphism away from a single point, so
[Stacks, Tag 0C0T] descends a representative of any class on `X'` to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_schemePullbackClassHom {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b) :
    Function.Surjective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f)
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.GluePicard.exists_globalUnit_sectionAt_eq_of_ne_connectedComponents
declarations.doc:
**The first map of the sequence of Stacks Tag 0C1M is zero when the two glued points lie
on different connected components of `X'`**, in the form that the connecting homomorphism
consumes: every scalar `c` is the ratio of the values at `a` and at `b` of a unit on all of
`X'`, so the invertible module obtained by glueing the fibres at `a` and `b` with ratio `c` is
trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_globalUnit_sectionAt_eq_of_ne_connectedComponents
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b)
    (hab : ConnectedComponents.mk (a.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)) ≠
      ConnectedComponents.mk (b.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k))) (c : kˣ) :
    ∃ s : Γ(X', ⊤)ˣ,
      AlgebraicGeometry.sectionAt a ⊤ (Opens.mem_top _) (s : Γ(X', ⊤)) = (c : k) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.sectionAt b ⊤ (Opens.mem_top _) (s : Γ(X', ⊤)) = 1
declarations.comment: the lifting criterion for vanishing at points on different components

declarations.name: Stacks.GluePicard.schemePullbackClassHom_eq_zero_iff_exists_picardGluingHom
declarations.doc:
**Exactness at `Pic(X)` of the sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0C1M].** For `k` algebraically
closed and `f : X' ⟶ X` the glueing of the two rational points `a` and `b` of `X'`, a Picard
class of `X` pulls back to zero on `X'` exactly when it is the value of the gluing homomorphism
`Stacks.GluePicard.picardGluingHom` at a scalar; that is, the kernel of `Pic(X) ⟶ Pic(X')` is
the image of `k^* ⟶ Pic(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemePullbackClassHom_eq_zero_iff_exists_picardGluingHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b) (L : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X) :
    Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f L = 0 ↔
      ∃ c : Additive kˣ, picardGluingHom f a b h c = L
declarations.comment: exactness at Pic(X): the kernel of pullback is the image of k^*

declarations.name: Stacks.GluePicard.exact_picardGluingHom_schemePullbackClassHom
declarations.doc:
**Exactness at `Pic(X)` of the sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0C1M]**, in the `Function.Exact`
spelling: the kernel of pullback of Picard classes is the range of the gluing homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_picardGluingHom_schemePullbackClassHom {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b) :
    Function.Exact (picardGluingHom f a b h) (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f)
declarations.comment: exactness at Pic(X): the kernel of pullback is the image of k^*

declarations.name: Stacks.GluePicard.picardGluingHom_eq_zero_of_ne_connectedComponents
declarations.doc:
**The first map of the sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0C1M] is zero when the two glued points lie
on different connected components of `X'`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem picardGluingHom_eq_zero_of_ne_connectedComponents {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b)
    (hab : ConnectedComponents.mk (a.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)) ≠
      ConnectedComponents.mk (b.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k))) :
    picardGluingHom f a b h = 0
declarations.comment: the first map is zero if a and b are on different connected components of X'

declarations.name: Stacks.GluePicard.picardGluingHom
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0C1M.** The gluing homomorphism `k^* ⟶ Pic(X)`.
declarations.statement:
def picardGluingHom {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b) :
    Additive kˣ →+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X
declarations.comment: the gluing homomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.GluePicard.injective_picardGluingHom_of_connectedComponents_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1M.** The gluing homomorphism is injective when `X'` is proper and
the two glued points lie on the same connected component of `X'`: a scalar in its kernel is the
ratio of the two values of a unit on `X'`, and on a connected component of a proper scheme over
an algebraically closed field the two values of any function agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_picardGluingHom_of_connectedComponents_eq
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (a b : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsGlueingTwoPoints f a b) [IsProper (X' ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (hab : ConnectedComponents.mk (a.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)) =
      ConnectedComponents.mk (b.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k))) :
    Function.Injective (picardGluingHom f a b h)
declarations.comment: injectivity if X' is proper and the two points lie on the same connected component

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishPicard.picardPullback_zero_and_add
declarations.doc: Pullback of Picard classes is a homomorphism of abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardPullback_zero_and_add {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X) :
    Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f 0 = 0 ∧
      ∀ x y : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X,
        Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f (x + y) =
          Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f x +
            Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f y
declarations.comment: the Picard pullback homomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishPicard.surjective_schemePullbackClassHom
declarations.doc: Pullback along the squishing of a tangent vector is surjective on Picard groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_schemePullbackClassHom {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ) :
    Function.Surjective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f)
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishPicard.epsilonCoefficientAt_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**The first map of the sequence of Stacks Tag 0C1N is injective when `X'` is proper and
reduced**, in the form that the connecting homomorphism consumes: the `ε`-coefficient along the
squished tangent vector of every global section of `𝒪_{X'}` vanishes.

The global functions of a scheme proper over `k` are integral over `k`, and those of a reduced
scheme are a reduced ring, so the minimal polynomial over `k` of a global section is squarefree.
Its image in `k[ε]` therefore cannot be a double root of a linear polynomial, which is what a
nonzero `ε`-coefficient would make it.
declarations.statement:
theorem epsilonCoefficientAt_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ)
    [IsProper (X' ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsReduced X'] (s : Γ(X', ⊤)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.epsilonCoefficientAt θ ⊤ trivial s = 0
declarations.comment: the lifting criterion for injectivity on a proper reduced scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishPicard.epsilonCoefficientAt_unit_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
The criterion of `Stacks.SquishPicard.epsilonCoefficientAt_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced`
for a global unit: the logarithmic `ε`-derivative of a unit on a proper reduced `X'` vanishes, so
no nonzero scalar is hit by the units sequence and the first map of Tag 0C1N is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem epsilonCoefficientAt_unit_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ)
    [IsProper (X' ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsReduced X'] (s : Γ(X', ⊤)ˣ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.epsilonCoefficientAt θ ⊤ trivial (s : Γ(X', ⊤)) = 0
declarations.comment: the lifting criterion for injectivity on a proper reduced scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.schemePullbackClassHom_eq_zero_iff_exists_picardTangentHom
declarations.doc:
**Exactness at `Pic(X)` of the sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0C1N].**  For `k` algebraically
closed and `f : X' ⟶ X` the squishing of the tangent vector `θ` of `X'`, a Picard class of `X`
pulls back to zero on `X'` exactly when it is the value of the tangent homomorphism
`Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.picardTangentHom` at a scalar; that is, the kernel of
`Pic(X) ⟶ Pic(X')` is the image of `(k, +) ⟶ Pic(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemePullbackClassHom_eq_zero_iff_exists_picardTangentHom (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ) (L : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X) :
    Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f L = 0 ↔
      ∃ a : k, picardTangentHom f θ h a = L
declarations.comment: exactness

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.exact_picardTangentHom_schemePullbackClassHom
declarations.doc:
**Exactness at `Pic(X)` of the sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0C1N]**, in the `Function.Exact`
spelling: the kernel of pullback of Picard classes is the range of the tangent homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_picardTangentHom_schemePullbackClassHom (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ) :
    Function.Exact (picardTangentHom f θ h) (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom f)
declarations.comment: exactness

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.picardTangentHom
declarations.doc:
**The tangent homomorphism `(k, +) ⟶ Pic(X)` of [Stacks, Tag 0C1N].** It is the connecting
homomorphism of the short exact sequence of sheaves of units of a squishing, read through the
five-term low-degree cohomology sequence over the whole space and through the identification of
`H¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` with the Picard group of [Stacks, Tag 09NU].
declarations.statement:
def picardTangentHom {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X' X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ) : k →+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X
declarations.comment: the tangent homomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.injective_picardTangentHom_of_isProper_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**The tangent homomorphism is injective when `X'` is proper and reduced.** A scalar in its
kernel is the logarithmic `ε`-derivative of a unit on `X'`, and on a proper reduced `X'` the
logarithmic `ε`-derivative of a global unit vanishes by
`Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.epsilonLogDeriv_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_picardTangentHom_of_isProper_of_isReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ)
    [IsProper (X' ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsReduced X'] :
    Function.Injective (picardTangentHom f θ h)
declarations.comment: injectivity on a proper reduced scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.epsilonLogDerivSheafHom_app
declarations.doc:
**The quotient map of the units sequence is the logarithmic `ε`-derivative** on the units of
the sections over every neighbourhood of the contracted point.
declarations.statement:
theorem epsilonLogDerivSheafHom_app {k : Type u} [Field k] {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X') (U : X.Opens)
    (hx : (θ ≫ f).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (DualNumber k)) ∈ U)
    (s : Γ(X', f ⁻¹ᵁ U)ˣ) :
    (epsilonLogDerivSheafHom f θ).hom.app (op U) (Additive.ofMul s) =
      skyscraperAddSheafMk X ((θ ≫ f).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (DualNumber k))) hx
        (epsilonLogDeriv θ (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) hx s)
declarations.comment: the quotient map of the sequence of sheaves of units

declarations.name: Stacks.SquishSheafSequence.epsilonLogDeriv_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**On a proper reduced `X'` the logarithmic `ε`-derivative of a global unit vanishes**, so the
arrow to `(k, +)` of the units sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0C1N] kills the global units and the
connecting homomorphism `(k, +) → Pic(X)` is injective. The `ε`-coefficient of every global
section already vanishes, by
`Stacks.SquishPicard.epsilonCoefficientAt_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epsilonLogDeriv_eq_zero_of_isProper_of_isReduced
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} [X'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (θ : Spec (.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X')
    (h : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSquishingTangentVector f θ)
    [IsProper (X' ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsReduced X'] (u : Γ(X', ⊤)ˣ) :
    epsilonLogDeriv θ ⊤ (Opens.mem_top _) u = 0
declarations.comment: vanishing of the logarithmic derivative on a proper reduced scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.embeddingDimension
declarations.doc:
The dimension of the cotangent space of the local ring of `X` at `x`, over its
residue field.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Scheme.embeddingDimension (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X) [FiniteDimensional
    (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (CotangentSpace (X.presheaf.stalk x))] : ℕ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isBirational_normalization_morphismRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** Over every open of a reduced scheme, the normalization
morphism is birational.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBirational_normalization_morphismRestrict (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (V : X.Opens) : IsBirational (X.normalization hX ∣_ V)
declarations.comment: finite_normalization

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NormalizationQuotient.existsUnique_linearEquiv_quotient_adicCompletion_normalizationPushforwardStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** Let `X` be a reduced scheme of dimension one with
normalization `ν`, let `x ∈ X`, write `A = 𝒪_{X,x}` and `A' = (ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν})_x`, and complete at
the maximal ideal of `A`.  There is exactly one `A`-linear isomorphism `A'/A ≅ A'^∧/A^∧`
compatible with the canonical maps to the completions.

The closedness of the point assumed in the source is not used; the dimension hypothesis is.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_linearEquiv_quotient_adicCompletion_normalizationPushforwardStalk
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X] (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1)
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) :=
      normalizationPushforwardStalkAlgebra X hX x
    ∃! e :
        (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x ⧸
            LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
              (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x))) ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
          (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
              (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) ⧸
            LinearMap.range (AdicCompletion.map
              (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
              (Algebra.linearMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
                (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x)))),
      ∀ a : normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x,
        e (Submodule.mkQ _ a) = Submodule.mkQ _
          (AdicCompletion.of (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
            (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) a)
declarations.comment: quotient_completion

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NormalizationQuotient.normalizationQuotient_iso_coproduct_skyscraperModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R(2).** For a reduced Nagata scheme of dimension one the quotient
`ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν} / 𝒪_X` is the direct sum of the skyscraper sheaves of its stalks at the singular
points: the quotient's stalk vanishes at every regular point, and the singular locus is closed
and discrete.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalizationQuotient_iso_coproduct_skyscraperModule (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsReduced X] (hX : IsNagataScheme X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    Nonempty
      (normalizationQuotient X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) ≅
        ∐ fun z : singularLocus X =>
          skyscraperModule X z.1
            (normalizationQuotientStalk X
              (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) z.1))
declarations.comment: quotient_sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NormalizationQuotient.normalizationQuotientStalk_linearEquiv_quotient_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** The stalk of the normalization quotient `ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν} / 𝒪_X`
at a point of a reduced scheme is the normalization stalk modulo the image of the local ring.

Neither the Nagata hypothesis, nor the dimension of `X`, nor closedness of the point is
needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalizationQuotientStalk_linearEquiv_quotient_range
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) :=
      normalizationPushforwardStalkAlgebra X hX x
    Nonempty (normalizationQuotientStalk X hX x ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
      (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x ⧸
        LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x))))
declarations.comment: delta_length

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NormalizationQuotient.length_normalizationQuotientStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** The length of the stalk of the normalization quotient is the
delta invariant of the local ring.

Neither the Nagata hypothesis, nor the dimension of `X`, nor closedness of the point is needed;
without them both sides may be infinite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem length_normalizationQuotientStalk (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (x : X) :
    Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationQuotientStalk X hX x) =
      Ring.deltaInvariant (X.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: delta_length

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NormalizationQuotient.isFiniteLength_normalizationQuotientStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** On a reduced Nagata scheme of dimension one the stalk of the
normalization quotient has finite length.

Closedness of the point is not needed, and the dimension hypothesis is used only through the
dimension of the local ring at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLength_normalizationQuotientStalk (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1)
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (x : X) :
    IsFiniteLength (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationQuotientStalk X hX x)
declarations.comment: delta_length

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NormalizationQuotientDirectSum.normalizationQuotientIsoCoproductSkyscraper
declarations.doc:
For a reduced Nagata scheme `X` of dimension one, the normalization quotient of `X` is
isomorphic to the direct sum, over the singular points `x` of `X`, of the skyscraper modules at
`x` of its stalks.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalizationQuotientIsoCoproductSkyscraper (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hX : IsNagataScheme X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    Nonempty
      (normalizationQuotient X
          (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Normalization.finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme
            X hX) ≅
        ∐ fun x : singularLocus X =>
          skyscraperModule X x.1
            (normalizationQuotientStalk X
              (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Normalization.finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme
                X hX) x.1))
declarations.comment: quotient_sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_algHom_normalizationPushforwardStalk_fractionRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** At a point of a reduced scheme the stalk of the pushforward of
the structure sheaf of the normalization carries exactly one injective algebra map into the total
ring of fractions of the local ring whose image is the integral closure: the canonical embedding
of the normalization stalk.

Neither the dimension-one hypothesis nor the closedness of the point is used, and the Nagata
hypothesis of the source enters only through the finiteness of irreducible components needed to
form the normalization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_algHom_normalizationPushforwardStalk_fractionRing
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) :=
      normalizationPushforwardStalkAlgebra X hX x
    ∃! f : normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x →ₐ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
        FractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x),
      Function.Injective f ∧
        f.range = integralClosure (X.presheaf.stalk x) (FractionRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
declarations.comment: normalization_stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_pi_isDiscreteValuationRing_adicCompletion_normalizationStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** At a point of a reduced Nagata scheme whose local ring has
dimension one, the completion of the stalk of the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the
normalization, along the ideal generated by the maximal ideal of the local ring, is a nonempty
finite product of complete discrete valuation rings.

Neither the dimension of `X` nor the closedness of the point is needed: the dimension
hypothesis of the source enters only through the dimension of the local ring at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pi_isDiscreteValuationRing_adicCompletion_normalizationStalk
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X] (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X)
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (x : X)
    (hxdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) :=
      normalizationPushforwardStalkAlgebra X hX x
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (D : Fin n → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (D i)) (_ : ∀ i, IsDomain (D i))
        (_ : ∀ i, IsDiscreteValuationRing (D i)),
      0 < n ∧ (∀ i, IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal (D i)) (D i)) ∧
        Nonempty (AdicCompletion
          ((maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)).map
            (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x)))
          (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) ≃+* ∀ i, D i)
declarations.comment: complete_dvr_product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_injective_range_eq_integralClosure_adicCompletion_normalizationStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R.** Completing the stalk of the pushforward of the structure sheaf
of the normalization of a reduced one-dimensional Nagata scheme, along the ideal generated by
the maximal ideal of the local ring at the point, gives the integral closure of the completed
local ring in its own total ring of fractions.

The two compatibility equations say that the resulting embedding extends the structure map of
the completed local ring and the given embedding `f₀` of the normalization stalk; the embedding
`f₀` exists and is unique by
`existsUnique_algHom_normalizationPushforwardStalk_fractionRing`.

Closedness of the point is not needed.  The points whose local ring is zero-dimensional are
covered: there the local ring is a field and both completions are trivial.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_injective_range_eq_integralClosure_adicCompletion_normalizationStalk
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X] (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1)
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) (normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x) :=
      normalizationPushforwardStalkAlgebra X hX x
    let A := X.presheaf.stalk x
    let A' := normalizationPushforwardStalk X hX x
    let Ac := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A
    let J := (maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A A')
    let C := AdicCompletion J A'
    let k : Ac →+* C := adicCompletionMap (algebraMap A A') (maximalIdeal A) J le_rfl
    ∀ f₀ : A' →ₐ[A] FractionRing A, Function.Injective f₀ →
      f₀.range = integralClosure A (FractionRing A) →
      ∃ q : FractionRing A →+* FractionRing Ac,
        (∀ a : A, q (algebraMap A (FractionRing A) a) =
          algebraMap Ac (FractionRing Ac) (algebraMap A Ac a)) ∧
        ∃ g : C →+* FractionRing Ac,
          Function.Injective g ∧
          g.range = (integralClosure Ac (FractionRing Ac)).toSubring ∧
          (∀ y : Ac, g (k y) = algebraMap Ac (FractionRing Ac) y) ∧
          (∀ a' : A', g (algebraMap A' C a') = q (f₀ a'))
declarations.comment: normalization_after_completion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isFinite_surjective_isBirational_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R, part (1).** The normalization `ν : X^ν ⟶ X` of a reduced Nagata
scheme is finite, surjective and birational.

The dimension of `X` is not used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFinite_surjective_isBirational_normalization (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hX : IsNagataScheme X) :
    IsFinite (X.normalization (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX)) ∧
      Surjective (X.normalization (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX)) ∧
      IsBirational (X.normalization (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX))
declarations.comment: part (1): ν is finite, surjective and birational

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationQuotient_mono_iso_coproduct_skyscraperModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R, part (2).** For a reduced Nagata scheme `X` of dimension one,
`𝒪_X ⊂ ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν}` — the map is a monomorphism both of sheaves of rings and of `𝒪_X`-modules —
and the quotient `ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν} / 𝒪_X` is the direct sum, over the singular points `x` of `X`, of
the skyscraper sheaves at `x` with value `𝒬_x`, the stalk of the quotient at `x`; that stalk is
nonzero exactly at the singular points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalizationQuotient_mono_iso_coproduct_skyscraperModule (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsReduced X] (hX : IsNagataScheme X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    Mono (Scheme.Hom.toRingCatSheafHom
        (X.normalization (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX))) ∧
      Mono (normalizationModuleMap X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX)) ∧
      Nonempty
        (normalizationQuotient X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) ≅
          ∐ fun z : singularLocus X =>
            skyscraperModule X z.1
              (normalizationQuotientStalk X
                (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) z.1)) ∧
      ∀ x : X, ¬ IsZero (normalizationQuotientStalk X
          (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x) ↔ x ∈ singularLocus X
declarations.comment: part (2): O_X ⊂ ν_*O, the quotient a sum of skyscrapers Q_x at singular points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationQuotientStalk_finiteLength_eq_deltaInvariant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R, part (4).** On a reduced Nagata scheme of dimension one, the
stalk `𝒬_x` of `ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν} / 𝒪_X` at `x` is `A' / A`, where `A = 𝒪_{X,x}` and
`A' = (ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν})_x`; it has finite length over `A`, and that length is the `δ`-invariant of
`X` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalizationQuotientStalk_finiteLength_eq_deltaInvariant (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsReduced X] (hX : IsNagataScheme X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (normalizationPushforwardStalk X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x) :=
      normalizationPushforwardStalkAlgebra X _ x
    Nonempty (normalizationQuotientStalk X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x
        ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
        (normalizationPushforwardStalk X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x ⧸
          LinearMap.range (Algebra.linearMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
            (normalizationPushforwardStalk X
              (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x)))) ∧
      IsFiniteLength (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (normalizationQuotientStalk X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x) ∧
      Module.length (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (normalizationQuotientStalk X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x) =
        Ring.deltaInvariant (X.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: part (4): Q_x = A'/A has finite length equal to the δ-invariant

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationPushforwardStalk_semilocal_finiteProductOfDedekindDomains
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R, part (5).** On a Nagata scheme of dimension one, the stalk
`A' = (ν_* 𝒪_{X^ν})_x` is a semi-local ring — it has finitely many maximal ideals — which is a
finite product of Dedekind domains.

Reducedness of `X` is not used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalizationPushforwardStalk_semilocal_finiteProductOfDedekindDomains
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : IsNagataScheme X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (x : X) :
    Finite (MaximalSpectrum
        (normalizationPushforwardStalk X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x)) ∧
      IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsFiniteProductOfDedekindDomains
        (normalizationPushforwardStalk X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hX) x)
declarations.comment: part (5): A' is semi-local and a finite product of Dedekind domains

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.adicCompletion_stalk_reduced_noetherian_complete_local_dim_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R, part (6)**, at a point whose local ring has dimension one. For a
reduced Nagata scheme `X` and a point `x` with `dim 𝒪_{X,x} = 1`, the completion `A^∧` of
`A = 𝒪_{X,x}` at its maximal ideal is a reduced Noetherian complete local ring of dimension one.

The hypothesis on `dim 𝒪_{X,x}` corrects the source: at a closed point of a one-dimensional scheme
whose local ring is a field (an isolated point), `A^∧ = A` has dimension zero.  Everything except
the dimension holds without it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_stalk_reduced_noetherian_complete_local_dim_one (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsReduced X] (hX : IsNagataScheme X) (x : X)
    (hxdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1) :
    _root_.IsReduced (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
      IsNoetherianRing (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
      ∃ _ : IsLocalRing
          (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)),
        IsAdicComplete
            (maximalIdeal
              (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)))
            (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧
          ringKrullDim
              (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)) = 1
declarations.comment: part (6): A^ is reduced Noetherian complete local of dimension 1 (dim A = 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.adicCompletion_stalk_reduced_noetherian_complete_local_ringKrullDim_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C1R, part (6)**, at every point. Let `X` be a reduced Nagata scheme of
dimension one, `x ∈ X` and `A = 𝒪_{X,x}`.  The completion `A^∧` of `A` at its maximal ideal is a
reduced Noetherian complete local ring with `dim A^∧ = dim A`; moreover `dim A ≤ 1`, with
`dim A = 1` exactly when `A` is not a field.  So the source's "of dimension 1" is precisely the
case `dim A = 1`, the one `adicCompletion_stalk_reduced_noetherian_complete_local_dim_one` states.

Part (6) as printed fails when `A` is a field, which happens at an isolated point: the scheme
`X = Spec (k × k[t])` is reduced, Nagata and of dimension one, its point `Spec k` is closed, and
there `A = A^∧ = k` has dimension zero.  Neither closedness of `x` nor any hypothesis on `dim A` is
used.
declarations.statement:
