    Subsingleton (Scheme.Opens.toScheme (exceptionalIdeal (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)))).support.compl).picardGroup
declarations.comment: the third step of the source's proof: triviality of the Picard group of the complement of the exceptional divisor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardGroupEquivInt_blowUp_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5G, granted the two missing inputs.** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a regular
local ring of dimension two and let `X ⟶ Spec A` be the blowup of `Spec A` in `𝔪`, with
exceptional divisor `E`. Granted that `E` is an exceptional curve of the first kind over `κ` and
that every Picard class of `X` is an integral multiple of `[𝒪_X(E)]`, the map `n ↦ n • [𝒪_X(E)]`
is an isomorphism `ℤ ≃+ Pic(X)`; so `Pic(X) = ℤ`, generated by `𝒪_X(E)`.
declarations.statement:
def picardGroupEquivInt_blowUp_maximalIdeal (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (_hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    {e : projectiveLineProj (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) ≅
      (exceptionalIdeal (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
        (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)))).subscheme}
    (hE : (exceptionalIdeal (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
        (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)))).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) e)
    (hgen : Function.Surjective fun n : ℤ => n • Stacks.Divisors.picardClass
      (exceptionalIdeal (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
        (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))))) :
    ℤ ≃+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme (blowUp (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))))
declarations.comment: granted the two inputs the library lacks, both hypothesized: that the exceptional divisor is an exceptional curve of the first kind over the residue field (the unproved half of Tag 0AGQ), and generation of the Picard group by its class

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_zsmul_picardClass_exceptionalIdealData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5G, the generation half, with nothing assumed.** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a
regular local ring of dimension two, let `X ⟶ Spec A` be the blowing up of `Spec A` in `𝔪` and
let `E` be its exceptional divisor. Then every Picard class of `X` is an integral multiple of the
class of `𝒪_X(E)`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_zsmul_picardClass_of_subsingleton_picardGroup_compl` is applied to
`E`. Its hypotheses are: `X` integral, locally Noetherian and normal, which transport along the
identification of the affine blowup with the blowup of the ideal sheaf of the closed point, where
they are [Stacks, Tag 0AGR] and properness over a Noetherian base; the closed subscheme of `E` is
integral, being the projective line over `κ` by part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0AGQ]; and `Pic(X ∖ E)`
is trivial, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_picardGroup_compl_exceptionalIdeal` transported along the same
identification, under which the two exceptional ideal sheaves correspond.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_zsmul_picardClass_exceptionalIdealData (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) :
    Function.Surjective fun n : ℤ => n • Stacks.Divisors.picardClass
      (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A))
declarations.comment: the generation half, with nothing assumed: every Picard class of the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal ideal is an integral multiple of the class of O_X(E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_zero_of_zsmul_picardClass_exceptionalIdealData_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5G, the infinite-order half for the blowup itself.** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)`
be a regular local ring of dimension two, let `X ⟶ Spec A` be the blowing up of `Spec A` in `𝔪`
and let `E` be its exceptional divisor. Then no nonzero multiple of the class of `𝒪_X(E)`
vanishes in `Pic(X)`.

`Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind.eq_zero_of_zsmul_picardClass_eq_zero` proves
this for an exceptional curve of the first kind, and `E` is one: parts (1) and (3) of
[Stacks, Tag 0AGQ], read as the predicate by
`Stacks.Blowup.exists_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind_exceptionalIdealData`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_zsmul_picardClass_exceptionalIdealData_eq_zero (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (n : ℤ)
    (hn : n • Stacks.Divisors.picardClass
      (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)) = 0) :
    n = 0
declarations.comment: the infinite-order half for the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal ideal, with nothing assumed: no nonzero multiple of the class of O_X(E) vanishes in Pic(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardGroupEquivInt_blowUpSpec_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5G.** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a regular local ring of dimension two and
let `X ⟶ Spec A` be the blowing up of `Spec A` in `𝔪`, with exceptional divisor `E`. Then
`n ↦ n • [𝒪_X(E)]` is an isomorphism `ℤ ≃+ Pic(X)`: so `Pic(X)` is infinite cyclic, generated by
`𝒪_X(E)`.

The map is injective because `[𝒪_X(E)]` has infinite order, which is
`Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind.eq_zero_of_zsmul_picardClass_eq_zero` applied
to `E` through parts (1) and (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0AGQ], and surjective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_zsmul_picardClass_exceptionalIdealData`. Nothing is assumed beyond
regularity and dimension two.
declarations.statement:
def picardGroupEquivInt_blowUpSpec_maximalIdeal (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) :
    ℤ ≃+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpSpec (maximalIdeal A))
declarations.comment: the identification Z ≃+ Pic(X) for the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal ideal, with nothing assumed: both halves, generation and infinite order, are proved for the exceptional divisor of this blowup

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardGroupEquivInt_blowUpSpec_maximalIdeal_one
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `ℤ ≃+ Pic(X)` of the blowup carries `1` to the class of `𝒪_X(E)`, so
`Pic(X)` is infinite cyclic on that class.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardGroupEquivInt_blowUpSpec_maximalIdeal_one (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) :
    picardGroupEquivInt_blowUpSpec_maximalIdeal A hdim 1 =
      Stacks.Divisors.picardClass
        (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A))
declarations.comment: the generator clause for the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal ideal, with nothing assumed: the isomorphism carries 1 to the class of O_X(E)

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.exists_pointBlowupChain_resolving_partialMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5H.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a scheme over `S` all of whose
local rings are regular, and let `Y` be proper over `S`. Given an `S`-rational map from `X` to
`Y`, displayed on the dense open `f.domain`, there is a chain of blowups at closed points not
lying over `f.domain`, with composite `p : Z ⟶ X`, and an `S`-morphism `h : Z ⟶ Y` which agrees
with the rational map over `f.domain`.

Three inputs are hypotheses rather than theorems here: `descent`, the local splitting of
[Stacks, Tag 0AGT] in the shape the library's [Stacks, Tag 0AHH] consumes; `domination`,
[Stacks, Tag 0AHI]; and `reduction`, the source's reduction to a domain containing every
codimension-one point, resting on [Stacks, Tag 0BX7], bundled with the dominating
`U`-admissible blowup of [Stacks, Tag 081T] for the enlarged domain.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pointBlowupChain_resolving_partialMap
    (descent : ∀ (A : Scheme.{u}) (W : Finset A) (J : A.IdealSheafData),
      (∀ y ∈ W, IsClosed ({y} : Set A)) →
      (∀ y ∈ W, IsRegularLocalRing (A.presheaf.stalk y)) →
      (∀ y ∈ W, ringKrullDim (A.presheaf.stalk y) = 2) →
      (J.support : Set A) ⊆ (W : Set A) →
      ∀ y ∈ (J.support : Set A), ∀ hy : IsClosed ({y} : Set A),
      ∀ M : A.IdealSheafData, M = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨{y}, hy⟩ →
        ∃ (d : ℕ) (W' : Finset (blowUp M)) (J' : (blowUp M).IdealSheafData),
          exceptionalIdeal M ^ d * J' = J.comap (blowUpToBase M) ∧
          (∀ z ∈ W', IsClosed ({z} : Set (blowUp M))) ∧
          (∀ z ∈ W', IsRegularLocalRing ((blowUp M).presheaf.stalk z)) ∧
          (∀ z ∈ W', ringKrullDim ((blowUp M).presheaf.stalk z) = 2) ∧
          (J'.support : Set (blowUp M)) ⊆ (W' : Set (blowUp M)) ∧
          (∀ z ∈ W', (blowUpToBase M).base z ∈ W) ∧
          totalColength J' W' < totalColength J W)
    (domination : ∀ (_descent : ∀ (A : Scheme.{u}) (W : Finset A) (J : A.IdealSheafData),
        (∀ y ∈ W, IsClosed ({y} : Set A)) →
        (∀ y ∈ W, IsRegularLocalRing (A.presheaf.stalk y)) →
        (∀ y ∈ W, ringKrullDim (A.presheaf.stalk y) = 2) →
        (J.support : Set A) ⊆ (W : Set A) →
        ∀ y ∈ (J.support : Set A), ∀ hy : IsClosed ({y} : Set A),
        ∀ M : A.IdealSheafData, M = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨{y}, hy⟩ →
          ∃ (d : ℕ) (W' : Finset (blowUp M)) (J' : (blowUp M).IdealSheafData),
            exceptionalIdeal M ^ d * J' = J.comap (blowUpToBase M) ∧
            (∀ z ∈ W', IsClosed ({z} : Set (blowUp M))) ∧
            (∀ z ∈ W', IsRegularLocalRing ((blowUp M).presheaf.stalk z)) ∧
            (∀ z ∈ W', ringKrullDim ((blowUp M).presheaf.stalk z) = 2) ∧
            (J'.support : Set (blowUp M)) ⊆ (W' : Set (blowUp M)) ∧
            (∀ z ∈ W', (blowUpToBase M).base z ∈ W) ∧
            totalColength J' W' < totalColength J W),
      ∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian A] (T : Finset A)
      (V : A.Opens), (V : Set A) = (T : Set A)ᶜ →
      (∀ x ∈ T, IsClosed ({x} : Set A)) →
      (∀ x ∈ T, IsRegularLocalRing (A.presheaf.stalk x)) →
      (∀ x ∈ T, ringKrullDim (A.presheaf.stalk x) = 2) →
      ∀ (q : B ⟶ A) [IsProper q] [IsIso (q ∣_ V)],
      (∃ (A' : Scheme.{u}) (b : A' ⟶ A), Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup V b ∧
          ∃ h : A' ⟶ B, h ≫ q = b) →
        ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (r : Z ⟶ A), PointBlowupChain A (T : Set A) Z r ∧
          ∃ s : Z ⟶ B, s ≫ q = r)
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over S] [Y.Over S] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X]
    [IsProper (Y ↘ S)] (hreg : ∀ x : X, IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (f : X.PartialMap Y) [f.IsOver S]
    (reduction : ∃ (T : Finset X) (V : X.Opens) (hle : f.domain ≤ V)
      (g : (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ Y),
      (V : Set X) = (T : Set X)ᶜ ∧
      (∀ x ∈ T, IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ T, ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 2) ∧
      g ≫ (Y ↘ S) = V.ι ≫ (X ↘ S) ∧
      X.homOfLE hle ≫ g = f.hom ∧
      ∀ {B : Scheme.{u}} (q : B ⟶ X) [IsProper q] [IsIso (q ∣_ V)],
        ∃ (A' : Scheme.{u}) (b : A' ⟶ X), Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup V b ∧
          ∃ h : A' ⟶ B, h ≫ q = b) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (p : Z ⟶ X) (h : Z ⟶ Y),
      PointBlowupChain X ((f.domain : Set X)ᶜ) Z p ∧
        h ≫ (Y ↘ S) = p ≫ (X ↘ S) ∧
          pullback.fst p f.domain.ι ≫ h = pullback.snd p f.domain.ι ≫ f.hom
declarations.comment: granted hypotheses descent (the local splitting of Tag 0AGT), domination (Tag 0AHI, exists_pointBlowupChain_factorization) and reduction (the Tag 0BX7 enlargement of the domain to a cofinite open, bundled with Tag 081T for that open)

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.exists_pointBlowupChain_resolving_partialMap_of_dim_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5H.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a regular Noetherian scheme
over `S` of dimension two, and let `Y` be proper over `S`. Given an `S`-rational map from `X` to
`Y`, displayed on the dense open `f.domain`, there is a chain of blowups at closed points not
lying over `f.domain`, with composite `p : Z ⟶ X`, and an `S`-morphism `h : Z ⟶ Y` which agrees
with the rational map over `f.domain`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pointBlowupChain_resolving_partialMap_of_dim_two
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over S] [Y.Over S] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X]
    [IsProper (Y ↘ S)] (hreg : ∀ x : X, IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 2) (f : X.PartialMap Y) [f.IsOver S] :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (p : Z ⟶ X) (h : Z ⟶ Y),
      PointBlowupChain X ((f.domain : Set X)ᶜ) Z p ∧
        h ≫ (Y ↘ S) = p ≫ (X ↘ S) ∧
          pullback.fst p f.domain.ι ≫ h = pullback.snd p f.domain.ι ≫ f.hom

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.exists_normalizedBlowUpChain_resolving_partialMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5I.** Let `X` be a Noetherian Nagata scheme of dimension two over
`S` and let `Y` be proper over `S`. Any `S`-rational map from `X` to `Y` becomes an `S`-morphism
after passing to the normalization of `X` followed by finitely many normalized blowups at closed
points, and the resulting morphism agrees with the rational map over its domain.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normalizedBlowUpChain_resolving_partialMap
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over S] [Y.Over S] [IsNoetherian X] [IsProper (Y ↘ S)]
    (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 2)
    (f : X.PartialMap Y) [f.IsOver S] :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (g : Z ⟶ X) (h : Z ⟶ Y),
      NormalizedBlowUpChain X finite_irreducibleComponents_isCompactOpen_of_isNoetherian Z g ∧
        h ≫ (Y ↘ S) = g ≫ (X ↘ S) ∧
          Limits.pullback.fst g f.domain.ι ≫ h =
            Limits.pullback.snd g f.domain.ι ≫ f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_comp_eq_of_isContractionOfExceptionalCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5J.** Let `E ⊆ X` be an exceptional curve of the first kind on a
Noetherian scheme, given by its ideal sheaf `D`, and let `b : X ⟶ X'` be a contraction of `E`.
Then every morphism `φ : X ⟶ Y` carrying `E` to a single point factors as `φ = b ≫ ψ` for a
unique `ψ : X' ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_comp_eq_of_isContractionOfExceptionalCurve
    {X X' Y : Scheme.{u}} (D : X.IdealSheafData) (b : X ⟶ X')
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b) (φ : X ⟶ Y)
    (hφ : ∃ y : Y, ∀ z : D.subscheme, φ (D.subschemeι z) = y) :
    ∃! ψ : X' ⟶ Y, b ≫ ψ = φ
declarations.comment: unique factorization through the contraction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_iso_of_isContractionOfExceptionalCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5K.** A contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind is
unique up to unique isomorphism: if `b₁ : X ⟶ X₁` and `b₂ : X ⟶ X₂` both contract the ideal
sheaf `D`, there is exactly one isomorphism `X₁ ≅ X₂` compatible with them.
declarations.comment: a contraction is unique up to unique isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.contractionPicardExactness_of_isContraction
declarations.doc:
Let `b : X ⟶ X'` contract the exceptional curve of the first kind cut out by `D`, presented as
`𝐏¹_k` by `e`. Then every Picard class of `X` of degree zero on the exceptional curve is pulled
back along `b`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem contractionPicardExactness_of_isContraction
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b) :
    D.ContractionPicardExactness k e b
declarations.comment: exactness at Pic(X), the inclusion of the kernel of the degree in the image of b^*, for a general contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind: with nothing assumed beyond the contraction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalRestrictionHom_negativeExceptionalMultiple
declarations.doc:
The restriction of `𝒪_X(-nE)` to the exceptional curve is `𝒪(n)`, written as the `(-n)`-th
multiple of the class of `𝒪(-1)` in `Pic(𝐏¹_k)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalRestrictionHom_negativeExceptionalMultiple
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) (n : ℤ) :
    exceptionalRestrictionHom D k e (negativeExceptionalMultipleHom D n) =
      (-n) • Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass (projectiveLineProj k).presheaf
        (structureIsSheaf (projectiveLineProj k).toRingedSpace)
        (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf
          (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (-1))
        (isInvertible_twistingSheaf_projectiveLine k (-1))
declarations.comment: the splitting map n ↦ O_X(-nE), stated through Pic(P¹_k) rather than Z: the restriction of O_X(-nE) to the exceptional curve is O(n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalDegreeHom_negativeExceptionalMultiple
declarations.doc:
If `φ : ℤ ≃+ Pic(𝐏¹_k)` carries `-1` to the class of `𝒪(-1)`, then the degree of `𝒪_X(-nE)`
on the exceptional curve is `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDegreeHom_negativeExceptionalMultiple
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (hφ : φ (-1) = Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass (projectiveLineProj k).presheaf
      (structureIsSheaf (projectiveLineProj k).toRingedSpace)
      (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (-1))
      (isInvertible_twistingSheaf_projectiveLine k (-1)))
    (n : ℤ) :
    exceptionalDegreeHom D k e φ (negativeExceptionalMultipleHom D n) = n
declarations.comment: the splitting: the degree of O_X(-nE) on the exceptional curve is n. The identification Z ≃+ Pic(P¹_k) of Tag 0BXJ is an explicit hypothesis, the library having only the injectivity half of that tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalDegreeHom_picardClass
declarations.doc:
If `φ : ℤ ≃+ Pic(𝐏¹_k)` carries `-1` to the class of `𝒪(-1)`, then the degree of `𝒪_X(E)` on
the exceptional curve is `-1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDegreeHom_picardClass
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (hφ : φ (-1) = Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass (projectiveLineProj k).presheaf
      (structureIsSheaf (projectiveLineProj k).toRingedSpace)
      (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (-1))
      (isInvertible_twistingSheaf_projectiveLine k (-1))) :
    exceptionalDegreeHom D k e φ (Stacks.Divisors.picardClass D) = -1
declarations.comment: the normalization of the degree map: O_X(E) has degree -1 on the exceptional curve. The identification Z ≃+ Pic(P¹_k) of Tag 0BXJ is an explicit hypothesis, the library having only the injectivity half of that tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalDegreeHom_surjective
declarations.doc:
If `φ : ℤ ≃+ Pic(𝐏¹_k)` carries `-1` to the class of `𝒪(-1)`, then the degree map on the
exceptional curve is surjective onto `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDegreeHom_surjective
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (hφ : φ (-1) = Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass (projectiveLineProj k).presheaf
      (structureIsSheaf (projectiveLineProj k).toRingedSpace)
      (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (-1))
      (isInvertible_twistingSheaf_projectiveLine k (-1))) :
    Function.Surjective (exceptionalDegreeHom D k e φ)
declarations.comment: right exactness: the degree map Pic(X) ⟶ Z on the exceptional curve is surjective, witnessed by the splitting n ↦ O_X(-nE). The identification Z ≃+ Pic(P¹_k) of Tag 0BXJ is an explicit hypothesis, the library having only the injectivity half of that tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.negativeExceptionalMultipleHom_injective
declarations.doc:
If `φ : ℤ ≃+ Pic(𝐏¹_k)` carries `-1` to the class of `𝒪(-1)`, then `n ↦ [𝒪_X(-nE)]` is
injective, so `ℤ` is a direct summand of `Pic(X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem negativeExceptionalMultipleHom_injective
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (hφ : φ (-1) = Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass (projectiveLineProj k).presheaf
      (structureIsSheaf (projectiveLineProj k).toRingedSpace)
      (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (-1))
      (isInvertible_twistingSheaf_projectiveLine k (-1))) :
    Function.Injective (negativeExceptionalMultipleHom D)
declarations.comment: the splitting n ↦ O_X(-nE) is injective, so Z is a direct summand of Pic(X). The identification Z ≃+ Pic(P¹_k) of Tag 0BXJ is an explicit hypothesis, the library having only the injectivity half of that tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalDegree_negativeExceptionalMultiple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5L, the splitting.** The degree of `𝒪_X(-nE)` on the exceptional
curve is `n`, so the sequence of the tag is split by `n ↦ 𝒪_X(-nE)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDegree_negativeExceptionalMultiple
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) (n : ℤ) :
    D.exceptionalDegree k e (negativeExceptionalMultipleHom D n) = n
declarations.comment: the splitting: the degree of O_X(-nE) on the exceptional curve is n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalDegree_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5L, right exactness.** The degree map on the exceptional curve is
surjective onto `ℤ`, because `𝒪_X(-nE)` has degree `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDegree_surjective (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) :
    Function.Surjective (D.exceptionalDegree k e)
declarations.comment: right exactness: the degree map Pic(X) ⟶ Z on the exceptional curve is surjective, witnessed by the splitting n ↦ O_X(-nE)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalDegree_picardClass
declarations.doc:
**The degree of `𝒪_X(E)` on the exceptional curve is `-1`**, the source's reading of the
definition of an exceptional curve of the first kind.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDegree_picardClass (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) :
    D.exceptionalDegree k e (Stacks.Divisors.picardClass D) = -1
declarations.comment: the normalization of the degree map: O_X(E) has degree -1 on the exceptional curve

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.negativeExceptionalMultipleHom_injective'
declarations.doc:
**The splitting of the sequence is injective**, so `ℤ` is a direct summand of `Pic(X)`:
distinct multiples `𝒪_X(-nE)` have distinct degrees on the exceptional curve.
declarations.statement:
public theorem negativeExceptionalMultipleHom_injective'
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) :
    Function.Injective (negativeExceptionalMultipleHom D)
declarations.comment: the splitting n ↦ O_X(-nE) is injective, so Z is a direct summand of Pic(X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.injective_schemePullbackClassHom_of_isContraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5L, left exactness.** Pullback of Picard classes along the
contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind is injective: the structure-sheaf
comparison `𝒪_{X'} ⟶ b_*𝒪_X` of a contraction is an isomorphism, and pullback along a morphism
with that property is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_schemePullbackClassHom_of_isContraction
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b) :
    Function.Injective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b)
declarations.comment: left exactness: pullback Pic(X') ⟶ Pic(X) along the contraction of the exceptional curve is injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exceptionalDegree_schemePullbackClassHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5L, the inclusion `im(b^*) ⊆ ker(deg)`.** A Picard class pulled back
along the contraction has degree zero on the exceptional curve: the curve maps into the
one-point subscheme it is contracted to, whose Picard group vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalDegree_schemePullbackClassHom
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b) (L' : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X') :
    D.exceptionalDegree k e (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b L') = 0
declarations.comment: exactness at Pic(X), the inclusion of the image of b^* in the kernel of the degree: a class pulled back along the contraction has degree zero on the exceptional curve

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.contractionPicardExactness_exceptionalIdealData
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a regular local ring of dimension two, let `X ⟶ Spec A` be the blowing up of
`Spec A` in `𝔪` and let `E` be its exceptional divisor, presented as an exceptional curve of the
first kind by `e : 𝐏¹_k ≅ E`. Then every Picard class of `X` of degree zero on `E` is pulled back
along any morphism out of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem contractionPicardExactness_exceptionalIdealData (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {e : projectiveLineProj k ≅
      (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)).subscheme}
    (hE : (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    {X' : Scheme.{u}} (b : Stacks.Blowup.blowUpSpec (maximalIdeal A) ⟶ X') :
    (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)).ContractionPicardExactness k e b
declarations.comment: exactness at Pic(X), the inclusion of the kernel of the degree in the image of b^*, for the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal ideal: with nothing assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.picardShortExactSequence_of_isContraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5L: the Picard short exact sequence of the contraction of an
exceptional curve of the first kind, together with its splitting.** Let `b : X ⟶ X'` contract the
exceptional curve of the first kind `E ⊆ X` cut out by the ideal sheaf `D` and presented as
`𝐏¹_k` by the isomorphism `e`. Then

`0 ⟶ Pic(X') ⟶ Pic(X) ⟶ ℤ ⟶ 0`

is exact, and split by `n ↦ 𝒪_X(-nE)`; the first map is pullback along `b` and the second is the
degree on `E`. The five clauses below are, in order:

* exactness at `Pic(X')`: pullback along `b` is injective;
* exactness at `Pic(X)`, both inclusions at once: a class of `X` has degree zero on `E` if and
  only if it is pulled back along `b`;
* exactness at `ℤ`: the degree on `E` is onto `ℤ`;
* the splitting: `𝒪_X(-nE)` has degree `n` on `E`, so `n ↦ 𝒪_X(-nE)` is a section of the degree
  map;
* the normalization of the degree: `𝒪_X(E)` has degree `-1` on `E`.

Being an effective Cartier divisor is the first clause of the hypothesis that `D` cuts out an
exceptional curve of the first kind, so nothing is assumed here beyond the contraction and the
curve it contracts.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picardShortExactSequence_of_isContraction
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) :
    Function.Injective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b) ∧
      (∀ L : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X, D.exceptionalDegree k e L = 0 ↔
        ∃ L' : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X', Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b L' = L) ∧
      Function.Surjective (D.exceptionalDegree k e) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, D.exceptionalDegree k e (negativeExceptionalMultipleHom D n) = n) ∧
      D.exceptionalDegree k e (Stacks.Divisors.picardClass D) = -1
declarations.comment: the short exact sequence 0 → Pic(X') → Pic(X) → Z → 0 of the contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind, in one statement with every clause written out: pullback along b is injective, a class has degree zero on the exceptional curve iff it is pulled back along b, the degree is surjective onto Z, the splitting n ↦ O_X(-nE) is a section of the degree, and O_X(E) has degree -1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.picardDecomposition_of_isContraction
declarations.doc:
The identification `Pic(X) = Pic(X') ⊕ ℤ` for `b : X ⟶ X'` the contraction of an exceptional
curve of the first kind `E ⊆ X`: a class `ℒ` on `X` corresponds to the pair `(ℒ', n)` with `n` the
degree of `ℒ` on `E`, and a pair `(ℒ', n)` to the class of `(b^*ℒ')(-nE)`.
declarations.statement:
public def picardDecomposition_of_isContraction
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) :
    Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X ≃+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X' × ℤ
declarations.comment: the identification Pic(X) = Pic(X') ⊕ Z for a general contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind: with nothing assumed beyond the contraction, exactness at Pic(X) discharged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.contractedPicardHom_of_isContraction
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `ℒ ↦ ℒ'` of the contraction `b : X ⟶ X'` of an exceptional curve of the first
kind. It sends a Picard class `ℒ` of `X` to the unique class `ℒ'` on `X'` with `ℒ(nE) = b^*ℒ'`,
where `n` is the degree of `ℒ` on the exceptional curve.
declarations.statement:
public def contractedPicardHom_of_isContraction
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) :
    Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X →+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X'
declarations.comment: the assignment L ↦ L' is a group homomorphism, for a general contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind: with nothing assumed beyond the contraction, exactness at Pic(X) discharged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.picardDecomposition_of_isContraction_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
For the contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind, a class `ℒ` corresponds under
the decomposition to the pair `(ℒ', n)` if and only if `ℒ = (b^*ℒ')(-nE)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picardDecomposition_of_isContraction_eq_iff
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) (L : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X)
    (L' : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X') (n : ℤ) :
    D.picardDecomposition_of_isContraction k e b hb hE L = (L', n) ↔
      L = Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b L' + negativeExceptionalMultipleHom D n
declarations.comment: the characterisation: L corresponds to the pair (L', n) if and only if L = (b^*L')(-nE), for a general contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind: with nothing assumed beyond the contraction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.picardDecomposition_of_isContraction_eq_iff_exceptionalTwist
declarations.doc:
For the contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind, a class `ℒ` corresponds under
the decomposition to the pair `(ℒ', n)` if and only if `ℒ(nE)` is the pullback of `ℒ'` along
`b`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picardDecomposition_of_isContraction_eq_iff_exceptionalTwist
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e) (L : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X)
    (L' : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X') (n : ℤ) :
    D.picardDecomposition_of_isContraction k e b hb hE L = (L', n) ↔
      D.exceptionalTwist n L = Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b L'
declarations.comment: the characterisation in the source's second form: L corresponds to (L', n) if and only if L(nE) = b^*L', for a general contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind: with nothing assumed beyond the contraction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.picardDecomposition_of_isContraction_apply_fst_pushforward
declarations.doc:
For the contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind, the `Pic(X')`-component of the
decomposition is `p(ℒ(nE))`, with `n` the degree of `ℒ` on the exceptional curve, for every
pushforward `p` on Picard classes left inverse to `b^*`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picardDecomposition_of_isContraction_apply_fst_pushforward
    (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (p : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X →+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X')
    (hp : ∀ L' : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X',
      p (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b L') = L')
    (L : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X) :
    (D.picardDecomposition_of_isContraction k e b hb hE L).1 =
      p (D.exceptionalTwist (D.exceptionalDegree k e L) L)
declarations.comment: the formula L' = b_*L(nE) read off the proof of Tag 0C5L, stated for every pushforward on Picard classes left inverse to b^*, for a general contraction of an exceptional curve of the first kind: with nothing assumed beyond the contraction, exactness at Pic(X) discharged and such a pushforward exhibited

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.picardDecomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5M: the identification `Pic(X) = Pic(X') ⊕ ℤ`.** For the contraction
`b : X ⟶ X'` of an exceptional curve of the first kind, a class `ℒ` on `X` is sent to the pair
`(b_*ℒ(nE), n)` with `n` the degree of `ℒ` on the exceptional curve, and a pair `(ℒ', n)` back
to the class of `(b^*ℒ')(-nE)`.
declarations.statement:
public def picardDecomposition (hb : D.ContractionPicardSplitting k e φ b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (hφ : φ (-1) = projectiveLineTwistPicardClass k (-1)) :
    Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X ≃+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X' × ℤ
declarations.comment: the identification Pic(X) = Pic(X') ⊕ Z, granted the two halves of Tag 0C5L the library does not prove — a pushforward b_* left inverse to b^*, and exactness at Pic(X) — bundled as the hypothesis ContractionPicardSplitting, and granted the identification Z ≃+ Pic(P¹_k) of Tag 0BXJ, of which the library has only the injectivity half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.picardDecomposition_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5M: the characterisation of the decomposition.** A class `ℒ`
corresponds to the pair `(ℒ', n)` if and only if `ℒ = (b^*ℒ')(-nE)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picardDecomposition_eq_iff (hb : D.ContractionPicardSplitting k e φ b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (hφ : φ (-1) = projectiveLineTwistPicardClass k (-1)) (L : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X)
    (L' : Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X') (n : ℤ) :
    picardDecomposition hb hE hφ L = (L', n) ↔
      L = Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom b L' + D.negativeExceptionalMultipleHom n
declarations.comment: the characterisation: L corresponds to the pair (L', n) if and only if L = (b^*L')(-nE), granted the two halves of Tag 0C5L the library does not prove, bundled as the hypothesis ContractionPicardSplitting, and the identification Z ≃+ Pic(P¹_k) of Tag 0BXJ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.contractedPicardHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5M: the assignment `ℒ ↦ ℒ'` is a group homomorphism.** It is the
`Pic(X')`-component of the decomposition `Pic(X) ≃+ Pic(X') × ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
public def contractedPicardHom (hb : D.ContractionPicardSplitting k e φ b)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind k e)
    (hφ : φ (-1) = projectiveLineTwistPicardClass k (-1)) :
    Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X →+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme X'
declarations.comment: the assignment L ↦ L' is a group homomorphism, granted the two halves of Tag 0C5L the library does not prove, bundled as the hypothesis ContractionPicardSplitting, and granted the identification Z ≃+ Pic(P¹_k) of Tag 0BXJ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.picardDecomposition_exceptionalIdealData
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a regular local ring of dimension two and let `b : X ⟶ Spec A` be the
blowing up of `Spec A` in `𝔪`, with exceptional divisor `E` presented as an exceptional curve of
the first kind by `e : 𝐏¹_k ≅ E`. Then `Pic(X) ≃+ Pic(Spec A) × ℤ`, a class `ℒ` corresponding to
the pair `(ℒ', n)` with `n` the degree of `ℒ` on `E` exactly when `ℒ = (b^*ℒ')(-nE)`.
declarations.statement:
public def picardDecomposition_exceptionalIdealData (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {e : projectiveLineProj k ≅
      (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)).subscheme}
    (hE : (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
      k e) :
    Stacks.Picard.ofScheme (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpSpec (maximalIdeal A)) ≃+
      Stacks.Picard.ofScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) × ℤ
declarations.comment: the identification Pic(X) = Pic(X') ⊕ Z for the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal ideal: with nothing assumed, both hypotheses of the general decomposition discharged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.contractedPicardHom_exceptionalIdealData
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism `ℒ ↦ ℒ'` of the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal
ideal. It sends a Picard class `ℒ` of the blowup to the unique class `ℒ'` on `Spec A` with
`ℒ(nE) = b^*ℒ'`, where `n` is the degree of `ℒ` on the exceptional curve. It is the
`Pic(Spec A)`-component of `AlgebraicGeometry.picardDecomposition_exceptionalIdealData`.
declarations.statement:
public def contractedPicardHom_exceptionalIdealData (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {e : projectiveLineProj k ≅
      (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)).subscheme}
    (hE : (Stacks.Blowup.exceptionalIdealData (maximalIdeal A)).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
      k e) :
    Stacks.Picard.ofScheme (Stacks.Blowup.blowUpSpec (maximalIdeal A)) →+
      Stacks.Picard.ofScheme (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))
declarations.comment: the assignment L ↦ L' is a group homomorphism, for the blowup of a regular local ring of dimension two in its maximal ideal: with nothing assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_of_isRegular_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5N.** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and `f : X ⟶ S` a separated
morphism of finite type with `X` regular of dimension (at most) two. Then `f` is quasi-projective.

The source assumes `dim X = 2`; the argument only uses `dim X ≤ 2`, which is what is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiProjective_of_isRegular_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_two
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S] (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hreg : IsRegular X)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 2) : IsQuasiProjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_of_isRegular_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5P.** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and `f : X ⟶ S` a proper morphism
with `X` regular of dimension (at most) two. Then `f` is projective.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0C5N] together with [Stacks, Tag 0BCL]: a proper quasi-projective morphism
to a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is projective. The source assumes `dim X = 2`; the
argument only uses `dim X ≤ 2`.

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.factorsAsPointBlowups_of_proper_birational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5R.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper birational morphism between
integral Noetherian schemes regular of dimension two. Then `f` is a sequence of blowups in closed
points, that is, `f` is up to an isomorphism of its source the composite of a chain of blowups at
closed points.

Three inputs are arguments rather than theorems: `hsec`, the second arrow of
[Stacks, Tag 067L]; `blowUpSurface`, the regularity ([Stacks, Tag 0AGR] globally) and the
dimension of the blowup at a closed point; and `square`, the reduction of [Stacks, Tag 0C5H]
to a single blowup together with the dichotomy of the source's step 3. The fourth argument
`descent` is the strict drop of the measure `μ`, the bookkeeping the source omits. None of them
is inter-derivable with the conclusion; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem factorsAsPointBlowups_of_proper_birational
    (hsec : ConormalSequenceSecondArrow.{u}) (μ : ∀ (A B : Scheme.{u}), (B ⟶ A) → ℕ)
    (blowUpSurface : ∀ (A : Scheme.{u}) (a : A) (ha : IsClosed ({a} : Set A)),
      IsIntegralRegularSurface A →
        IsRegular (pointBlowUp ha) ∧ topologicalKrullDim (pointBlowUp ha) = 2)
    (square : ∀ (A B : Scheme.{u}) (g : B ⟶ A), IsIntegralRegularSurface A →
      IsIntegralRegularSurface B → IsProper g → IsBirational g → ¬ IsIso g →
      ∀ (a : A) (ha : IsClosed ({a} : Set A)) (U : A.Opens),
        IsGreatest { V : A.Opens | IsIso (g ∣_ V) } U → a ∉ U →
          HasExceptionalSquareAt g a ha)
    (descent : ∀ (A B : Scheme.{u}) (g : B ⟶ A), IsIntegralRegularSurface A →
      IsIntegralRegularSurface B → IsProper g → IsBirational g → ¬ IsIso g →
      ∀ (a : A) (ha : IsClosed ({a} : Set A)) (U : A.Opens),
        IsGreatest { V : A.Opens | IsIso (g ∣_ V) } U → a ∉ U →
          ∀ ψ : B ⟶ pointBlowUp ha, ψ ≫ pointBlowUpToBase ha = g →
            μ (pointBlowUp ha) B ψ < μ A B g)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hY : IsIntegralRegularSurface Y)
    (hX : IsIntegralRegularSurface X) (hproper : IsProper f) (hbirational : IsBirational f) :
    FactorsAsPointBlowups Y Set.univ X f
declarations.comment: the conclusion in full; the inputs hsec, blowUpSurface and square remain named arguments and descent is reduced to the drop of the measure, as the module documentation records

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.factorsAsPointBlowups_of_isProper_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5R.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper birational morphism between
integral Noetherian schemes regular of dimension two. Then `f` is a sequence of blowups in closed
points.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsAsPointBlowups_of_isProper_of_isBirational {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsIntegralRegularSurface Y) (hX : IsIntegralRegularSurface X) (hproper : IsProper f)
    (hbirational : IsBirational f) : FactorsAsPointBlowups Y Set.univ X f

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.birationalOver_comp_of_factorsAsPointBlowups
declarations.doc:
**The converse direction of [Stacks, Tag 0C5S], whose proof the source omits.** A morphism
which is a finite sequence of blowups at closed points of an integral Noetherian scheme regular
of dimension two makes its source birational to the target over any base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem birationalOver_comp_of_factorsAsPointBlowups
    (blowUpSurface : ∀ (A : Scheme.{u}) (a : A) (ha : IsClosed ({a} : Set A)),
      IsIntegralRegularSurface A →
        IsIntegralRegularSurface
          (blowUp (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (⟨{a}, ha⟩ : Closeds A))))
    {S X Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ S) (hX : IsIntegralRegularSurface X) {f : Z ⟶ X}
    (hf : FactorsAsPointBlowups X Set.univ Z f) :
    Scheme.BirationalOver (f ≫ sX) sX
declarations.comment:
the converse direction, which the source states without proof: a two-sided
chain of blowups in closed points makes `X` and `Y` birational over the base. Unconditional
apart from blowUpSurface (the globalization of Tag 0AGR); the route is Tag 02OS, nonvanishing
of the point's ideal sheaf, and Tag 0BAD

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.birationalOver_comp_of_factorsAsPointBlowups_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**One side of the converse direction of [Stacks, Tag 0C5S], whose proof the source omits.** A
morphism which is a finite sequence of blowups at closed points of an integral Noetherian scheme
regular of dimension two makes its source birational to the target over any base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem birationalOver_comp_of_factorsAsPointBlowups_unconditional
    {S X Z : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ S) (hX : IsIntegralRegularSurface X) {f : Z ⟶ X}
    (hf : FactorsAsPointBlowups X Set.univ Z f) :
    Scheme.BirationalOver (f ≫ sX) sX
declarations.comment:
one side of the converse direction, which the source states without proof: a
chain of blowups in closed points out of `X` makes its source birational to `X` over the base.
The route is Tag 02OS, nonvanishing of the point's ideal sheaf, and Tag 0BAD, and the blowup of
such a scheme at a closed point is again such a scheme by the globalization of Tag 0AGR,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_and_topologicalKrullDim_blowUp_vanishingIdeal_singleton`

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.birationalOver_of_exists_factorsAsPointBlowups
declarations.doc:
**The converse direction of [Stacks, Tag 0C5S], whose proof the source omits.** Let `S` be a
Noetherian scheme and let `X` and `Y` be proper integral schemes over `S` which are regular of
dimension two. If there is a scheme `Z` with `S`-morphisms `f : Z ⟶ X` and `g : Z ⟶ Y`, each a
finite sequence of blowups at closed points, then `X` and `Y` are `S`-birational.

This is the implication of the source's `if and only if` that the source states without proof,
and it is proved here with nothing assumed: each of the two sides makes `Z` birational to its
target over `S` by
`Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.birationalOver_comp_of_factorsAsPointBlowups_unconditional`,
and `S`-birationality is symmetric and transitive.
declarations.statement:
public theorem birationalOver_of_exists_factorsAsPointBlowups
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over S] [Y.Over S]
    (hX : IsIntegralRegularSurface X) (hY : IsIntegralRegularSurface Y)
    (h : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y),
      f ≫ (X ↘ S) = g ≫ (Y ↘ S) ∧
        FactorsAsPointBlowups X Set.univ Z f ∧ FactorsAsPointBlowups Y Set.univ Z g) :
    Scheme.BirationalOver (X ↘ S) (Y ↘ S)
declarations.comment:
the implication from the two-sided chain of blowups in closed points to
`S`-birationality of `X` and `Y`, which is the direction the source states without proof. Nothing
is assumed: the two sides are composed through
`Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.birationalOver_comp_of_factorsAsPointBlowups_unconditional` and the
symmetry and transitivity of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.BirationalOver`

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.birationalOver_iff_exists_factorsAsPointBlowups_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and let `X` and `Y` be proper integral schemes over `S` which
are regular of dimension two. Then `X` and `Y` are `S`-birational if and only if there is a scheme
`Z` with `S`-morphisms `f : Z ⟶ X` and `g : Z ⟶ Y`, each a finite sequence of blowups at closed
points.

Of `X` and `Y` only the tag's own conditions are assumed: integral, regular, of dimension two,
and proper over the Noetherian base. Their Noetherianness, which
`Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.IsIntegralRegularSurface` demands in addition, is derived from
properness over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem birationalOver_iff_exists_factorsAsPointBlowups_of_isRegular
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] [X.Over S] [Y.Over S]
    [IsProper (X ↘ S)] [IsProper (Y ↘ S)]
    (hXintegral : AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X) (hXregular : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular X)
    (hXdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 2) (hYintegral : AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral Y)
    (hYregular : AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular Y) (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y = 2) :
    Scheme.BirationalOver (X ↘ S) (Y ↘ S) ↔
      ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y),
        f ≫ (X ↘ S) = g ≫ (Y ↘ S) ∧
          FactorsAsPointBlowups X Set.univ Z f ∧ FactorsAsPointBlowups Y Set.univ Z g
declarations.comment:
the tag's hypothesis list, with the surface predicate derived rather than assumed:
  `S` is Noetherian and `X` and `Y` are proper over `S`, integral, regular and of dimension two.
  The bundled `Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.IsIntegralRegularSurface` of the other registration
  asks of the two schemes that they be Noetherian as well; here that is obtained from properness
  over `S` by Tag 01T6

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.birationalOver_iff_exists_factorsAsPointBlowups_of_isIntegralRegularSurface
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5S.** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and let `X` and `Y` be proper
integral schemes over `S` which are regular of dimension two. Then `X` and `Y` are `S`-birational
if and only if there is a scheme `Z` with `S`-morphisms `Z ⟶ X` and `Z ⟶ Y`, each a sequence of
blowups in closed points.
declarations.statement:
theorem birationalOver_iff_exists_factorsAsPointBlowups_of_isIntegralRegularSurface
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] [X.Over S] [Y.Over S]
    [IsProper (X ↘ S)] [IsProper (Y ↘ S)] (hX : IsIntegralRegularSurface X)
    (hY : IsIntegralRegularSurface Y) :
    Scheme.BirationalOver (X ↘ S) (Y ↘ S) ↔
      ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y),
        f ≫ (X ↘ S) = g ≫ (Y ↘ S) ∧
          FactorsAsPointBlowups X Set.univ Z f ∧ FactorsAsPointBlowups Y Set.univ Z g

declarations.name: Matrix.det_ne_zero_of_sum_row_lt_diag_weighted
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C5U, part (2).** A square matrix over a normed field whose diagonal strictly
dominates its off-diagonal entries after weighting the columns by a vector `m` has nonzero
determinant.

Weighting the columns is right multiplication by `Matrix.diagonal m`, whose determinant is the
product of the `m i`, so the weighted matrix has nonzero determinant by part (1) and the
determinants differ by that product. Positivity of the weights is not needed: the hypothesis
already forces each `m i` to be nonzero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem det_ne_zero_of_sum_row_lt_diag_weighted {K n : Type*} [NormedField K] [Fintype n]
    [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n K) (m : n → K)
    (h : ∀ i, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, ‖A i j * m j‖ < ‖A i i * m i‖) :
    A.det ≠ 0
declarations.comment: part (2)

registrations.name: det_ne_zero_of_sum_row_lt_diag
registrations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Matrix.ker_mulVecLin_eq_span_indicator
declarations.doc:
The kernel of a symmetric matrix with nonnegative off-diagonal entries,
diagonally dominant relative to a positive vector `m`, is spanned by the
weighted indicator vectors of its isolated equality subsets.
declarations.statement:
public lemma ker_mulVecLin_eq_span_indicator {n : ℕ}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (m : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hA : A.IsSymm)
    (hoff : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → 0 ≤ A i j)
    (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i)
    (hdom : ∀ i, ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, A i j * m j ≤ -A i i * m i) :
    LinearMap.ker A.mulVecLin =
      Submodule.span ℝ {x | ∃ I : Set (Fin n),
        x = I.indicator m ∧
        (∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j ∉ I, A i j = 0) ∧
        (∀ i ∈ I, -A i i * m i = ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, A i j * m j)}

declarations.name: Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec_nonpos_of_positive_kernel
declarations.doc:
A symmetric matrix with nonnegative off-diagonal entries which kills a
strictly positive vector has nonpositive associated quadratic form.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotProduct_mulVec_nonpos_of_positive_kernel
    {A : Matrix ι ι R} {m : ι → R} (hA : A.IsSymm)
    (hoffDiag : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → 0 ≤ A i j) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i)
    (hAm : A *ᵥ m = 0) (x : ι → R) :
    x ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ x) ≤ 0
declarations.comment: negative semidefiniteness

declarations.name: Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec_eq_zero_iff_of_positive_kernel
declarations.doc:
If, in addition, no proper nonempty set of indices is disconnected from
its complement, the zero locus of the quadratic form is the line spanned by
the positive kernel vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotProduct_mulVec_eq_zero_iff_of_positive_kernel
    {A : Matrix ι ι R} {m x : ι → R} (hA : A.IsSymm)
    (hoffDiag : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → 0 ≤ A i j) (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i)
    (hAm : A *ᵥ m = 0)
    (hconnected : ∀ I : Set ι, I.Nonempty → I ≠ Set.univ →
      ¬ ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j ∉ I, A i j = 0) :
    x ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ x) = 0 ↔ ∃ q : R, x = q • m
declarations.comment: equality case

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_specialFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5Z.** The scheme-theoretic special fibre of a scheme flat over a
discrete valuation ring is an effective Cartier divisor: on every affine chart it is the zero
scheme of the image of a uniformizer, which flatness keeps a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_specialFiber
    {R k : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    [Field k] [Algebra R k]
    (residueEquiv : IsLocalRing.ResidueField R ≃ₐ[R] k)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [Flat f] :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R k)))).ker
declarations.comment: special_fibre_cartier

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_specialFiberComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5Z (component clause).** Each irreducible component of the special
fibre of a regular model, taken with its reduced induced structure as a closed subscheme of the
model, is an effective Cartier divisor on the model.

It is an integral closed subscheme of codimension one, and every local ring of the regular
scheme `X` is factorial, so Tag 0AGA applies.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_specialFiberComponent :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z)
declarations.comment: component_cartier

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.specialFiberIdeal_eq_prod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C5Z, part (3).** The special fibre of a regular model is the sum
`X_k = ∑ mᵢ Cᵢ` of its irreducible components `Cᵢ`, as effective Cartier divisors, with `mᵢ`
the multiplicity of `Cᵢ` in `X_k`. Divisor sums are written multiplicatively.

The components are integral effective Cartier divisors covering the special fibre, so
[Stacks, Tag 0BCP] writes `X_k` as some nonnegative combination `∑ aᵢ Cᵢ`; reading off the order
at the generic point of each `Cᵢ`, which is a discrete valuation ring, gives `aᵢ = mᵢ`.
declarations.comment: part (3): X_k = ∑ mᵢ Cᵢ with mᵢ the multiplicity of Cᵢ in X_k

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.invertibleSheafIsoUnit_specialFiber
declarations.doc:
**The invertible sheaf of the special fibre is trivial**, `𝒪_X(X_k) ≅ 𝒪_X`, for any scheme
flat over a discrete valuation ring: the special fibre is the zero scheme of the regular global
section determined by a uniformizer, and the divisor of a regular section of an invertible
module reproduces that module.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def invertibleSheafIsoUnit_specialFiber
    (residueEquiv : IsLocalRing.ResidueField R ≃ₐ[R] k)
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [Flat f] {π : R} (hπ : Irreducible π) :
    invertibleSheaf' (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R k)))).ker ≅
      SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf
declarations.comment: part (4): the special fibre has trivial invertible sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.isGorenstein_model
declarations.doc:
The structure morphism of a regular model of a smooth curve over a discrete valuation ring is
a Gorenstein morphism.

Local Noetherianity of the fibres is not an extra assumption — it follows from local
Noetherianity of the total space — so it is packaged existentially, as the Gorenstein-morphism
predicate of Tag 0C04 takes a proof of it as an argument.
declarations.comment: part (1): Gorenstein morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.relativeDimension_model
declarations.doc:
Every nonempty fibre of the structure morphism of a regular model of a smooth curve is
equidimensional of dimension one.

The generic fibre is the curve `C`, so it is irreducible of dimension one; the total space is
integral by Tag 0BCM, and Tag 0B2J transports both conclusions to the special fibre.
declarations.statement: public theorem relativeDimension_model : RelativeDimension S.X_to_R 1
declarations.comment: part (1): relative dimension one

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.isGorenstein_specialFiberComponent
declarations.doc:
Each irreducible component `Cᵢ` of the special fibre of a regular model, taken with its
reduced induced structure as a closed subscheme of the model, is a Gorenstein scheme.

The component is an effective Cartier divisor on `X` by the component clause of Tag 0C5Z, and
`X` is regular, hence Gorenstein, so the scheme-theoretic form of Tag 0BJJ applies.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_specialFiberComponent (Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.isGorenstein_model_and_specialFiberComponents
declarations.doc:
For a regular model `X` of a smooth curve `C` over `K`: the structure morphism
`X ⟶ Spec(R)` is a Gorenstein morphism of relative dimension one, and each irreducible component
of the special fibre `X_k` is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGorenstein_model_and_specialFiberComponents :
    (∃ hf : ∀ y : Spec (.of S.R), IsLocallyNoetherian (S.X_to_R.fiber y),
        S.X_to_R.IsGorenstein hf) ∧
      RelativeDimension S.X_to_R 1 ∧
      ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber,
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C61.** The standing situation of the geometry of a regular model: a
discrete valuation ring with a chosen uniformizer, a smooth projective curve over its fraction
field whose only global functions are the constants, and a regular proper model of that
curve.
declarations.statement: public structure RegularProperModelSituation extends RegularModelSituation.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.connectedSpace_specialFiber
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C62].**  In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0C61] the special fibre `X_k` of the
regular proper model is connected.

This is the second conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 0AY8] — geometric connectedness of the fibres,
`RegularProperModelSituation.geometricallyConnected_X_to_R` — read at the closed point of
`Spec(R)`:  the special fibre is the base change of the model along `Spec(k) ⟶ Spec(R)`, whose
source is a one-point scheme, and a scheme geometrically connected over a one-point base is
connected.
declarations.statement: public theorem connectedSpace_specialFiber : ConnectedSpace S.specialFiber
declarations.comment: the special fibre X_k of a regular proper model is connected

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.multiplicityHom_one
declarations.doc: The first map of the sequence sends `1` to the vector `(m₁, …, mₙ)` of multiplicities.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicityHom_one {ι : Type*} (m : ι → ℕ) :
    multiplicityHom m 1 = fun i => (m i : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the first map, which sends 1 to (m_1, ..., m_n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.componentPicardHom_single
declarations.doc:
The second map of the sequence sends the `i`th basis vector of `ℤ^{⊕n}` to the class of
`𝒪_X(Cᵢ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentPicardHom_single [DecidableEq ι] (i : ι) :
    componentPicardHom S C (Pi.single i 1) = picardClass (C i)
declarations.comment: the second map, which sends the ith basis vector to O_X(C_i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.genericFiberPicardRestriction
declarations.doc:
**The third map `Pic(X) ⟶ Pic(C)` of the Picard sequence of a regular model**: restriction
of Picard classes along the inclusion of the generic fibre.
declarations.statement: def genericFiberPicardRestriction : ofScheme S.X →+ ofScheme S.C
declarations.comment: the third map, restriction of Picard classes to the generic fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.componentPicardHom_multiplicityHom
declarations.doc: The composite of the first two maps of the sequence vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentPicardHom_multiplicityHom (a : ℤ) :
    componentPicardHom S C (multiplicityHom m a) = 0
declarations.comment: the composite Z -> Z^n -> Pic(X) vanishes

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.injective_multiplicityHom
declarations.doc: The first map of the sequence is injective, which is exactness at `ℤ`.
declarations.statement: theorem injective_multiplicityHom : Function.Injective (multiplicityHom (ι := ι) m)
declarations.comment: exactness at Z, i.e. injectivity of the first map

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.picardSequence_specialFiberComponents
declarations.doc:
Take the family `C₁, …, Cₙ` to be the irreducible components of `X_k` with their reduced
induced structure, and let `mᵢ` be multiplicities with `X_k = Σ mᵢ Cᵢ`. Then the first map of
the sequence sends `1` to `(m₁, …, mₙ)`, the second sends the `i`th basis vector to
`[𝒪_X(Cᵢ)]`, the composite of the two vanishes, and the first map is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardSequence_specialFiberComponents
    (hdec : S.specialFiberIdeal =
      ∏ Z, RegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.toRegularModelSituation Z ^ m Z) :
    multiplicityHom m 1 = (fun Z => (m Z : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ Z, componentPicardHom S
          (RegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.toRegularModelSituation)
          (Pi.single Z 1) =
        picardClass
          (RegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.toRegularModelSituation Z)) ∧
      (∀ a, componentPicardHom S
        (RegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.toRegularModelSituation)
        (multiplicityHom m a) = 0) ∧
      Function.Injective (multiplicityHom m)
declarations.comment: the two named maps and the clauses proved here, for the components of X_k

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.picardSequence_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C63.** In Situation 0C61 there is an exact sequence

`0 ⟶ ℤ ⟶ ℤ^{⊕n} ⟶ Pic(X) ⟶ Pic(C) ⟶ 0`

where the first map sends `1` to the vector `(m₁, …, mₙ)` of multiplicities of the irreducible
components `C₁, …, Cₙ` of the special fibre, and the second map sends the `i`th basis vector to
the class of `𝒪_X(Cᵢ)`.

The three maps are the group homomorphisms `Stacks.Models.multiplicityHom`,
`Stacks.Models.componentPicardHom` and `Stacks.Models.genericFiberPicardRestriction`, the last
being pullback of Picard classes along the inclusion of the generic fibre; the components are the
irreducible components of `X_k` with their reduced induced structure, which are effective Cartier
divisors by [Stacks, Tag 0C5Z]; and `ℤ^{⊕n}` is the group of integer families on them, the
components being finitely many. The decomposition `X_k = Σ mᵢ Cᵢ` with which the situation opens
is part of the conclusion, and the seven conjuncts are, in order: that decomposition, the value
of the first map on `1`, the values of the second map on the basis vectors, exactness at `ℤ`
(injectivity of the first map), exactness at `ℤ^{⊕n}`, exactness at `Pic(X)`, and exactness at
`Pic(C)` (surjectivity of the third map).
declarations.statement:
theorem picardSequence_exact (S : RegularProperModelSituation.{u}) :
    ∃ m : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℕ,
      S.specialFiberIdeal =
          ∏ Z, S.toRegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z ^ m Z ∧
        multiplicityHom m 1 = (fun Z => (m Z : ℤ)) ∧
        (∀ Z, componentPicardHom S S.toRegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal
            (Pi.single Z 1) =
          Stacks.Divisors.picardClass
            (S.toRegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z)) ∧
        Function.Injective (multiplicityHom m) ∧
        Function.Exact (multiplicityHom m)
            (componentPicardHom S S.toRegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal) ∧
        Function.Exact
            (componentPicardHom S S.toRegularModelSituation.specialFiberComponentIdeal)
            (genericFiberPicardRestriction S) ∧
        Function.Surjective (genericFiberPicardRestriction S)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberDegreePairing_bilinear_and_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C64.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61], let `C_Z` run over the
irreducible components of the special fibre of the regular proper model `X ⟶ Spec(R)`, each with
its reduced induced structure as a closed subscheme of `X`. For an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ`
and an integer family `a` the degree pairing is

`⟨a, ℒ⟩ = ∑_Z a_Z · deg(ℒ|_{C_Z})`;

it is bilinear, and for integer families `a` and `b`

`⟨a, 𝒪_X(∑_Y b_Y C_Y)⟩ = ⟨b, 𝒪_X(∑_Z a_Z C_Z)⟩`.

The four clauses are, in order: the defining formula for the pairing, additivity in the
coefficient family, additivity in the invertible module — the Picard group being written
multiplicatively, so that addition of its elements is the tensor product — and the symmetry.
The third is the invertible case of [Stacks, Tag 0AYX] on each component, and the fourth is
proved as the source proves it: expand both sides by the first three clauses and appeal to the
symmetry of the intersection matrix
`deg(𝒪_X(C_Y)|_{C_Z}) = deg(𝒪_X(C_Z)|_{C_Y})`, which is
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.componentDegree_specialFiberComponent_comm`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFiberDegreePairing_bilinear_and_comm
    (s : Finset (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)) :
    (∀ (a : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ) (L : S.X.Modules)
        (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L),
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a L hL =
          ∑ Z ∈ s, a Z * S.specialFiberComponentDegree Z L hL) ∧
      (∀ (a a' : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ) (L : S.X.Modules)
        (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L),
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s (a + a') L hL =
          S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a L hL + S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a' L hL) ∧
      (∀ (a : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ) (L M : S.X.Modules)
        (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L)
        (hM : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property M)
        (hLM : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property
            ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
              ⟨(S.X.toRingedSpace).presheaf, (S.X.toRingedSpace).IsSheaf⟩).obj (L)).obj (M)))),
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨(S.X.toRingedSpace).presheaf, (S.X.toRingedSpace).IsSheaf⟩).obj (L)).obj (M))) hLM =
          S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a L hL + S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a M hM) ∧
      (∀ a b : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ,
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a (S.specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s b)
            (S.isInvertible_specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s b) =
          S.specialFiberDegreePairing s b (S.specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s a)
            (S.isInvertible_specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s a))
declarations.comment: the pairing ⟨a, L⟩ = ∑ a_Z deg(L|_{C_Z}), its bilinearity, and the symmetry ⟨a, O_X(∑ b_Y C_Y)⟩ = ⟨b, O_X(∑ a_Z C_Z)⟩ at integer coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.degreePairing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C64.** The degree pairing `⟨a, ℒ⟩ = ∑ᵢ aᵢ · deg(ℒ|_{Cᵢ})` of an
integer coefficient family `a` against an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, over a finite family of
components `Cᵢ` of the special fibre that are proper curves over the residue field.
declarations.comment: the pairing ⟨a, L⟩ = ∑ aᵢ deg(L|_{Cᵢ}); the whole tag, its bilinearity and its symmetry together, is Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberDegreePairing_bilinear_and_comm of StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/Models/DegreePairingSymmetry.lean

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionProduct_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C65, second equality**, on nonnegative coefficient families: the
intersection product of the components of the special fibre is symmetric,
`(∑_Z a_Z C_Z · ∑_Y b_Y C_Y) = (∑_Y b_Y C_Y · ∑_Z a_Z C_Z)`.

This is `Stacks.Models.intersectionProduct_comm_of_expansion_of_matrix_symm` with both of its
hypotheses discharged: `hexpand` by
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberDivisorDegree_eq_sum` and `hsymm` by
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix_comm`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFiberIntersectionProduct_comm
    (a b : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℕ) :
    S.specialFiberIntersectionProduct (fun Z => (a Z : ℤ)) b =
      S.specialFiberIntersectionProduct (fun Z => (b Z : ℤ)) a
declarations.comment: the second displayed equality, the symmetry ⟨a, O_X(∑ b_Y C_Y)⟩ = ⟨b, O_X(∑ a_Z C_Z)⟩, at the irreducible components of the special fibre and on nonnegative coefficient families; at integer coefficients it is the fourth clause of Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberDegreePairing_bilinear_and_comm

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberDegreePairing_bilinear_and_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C64.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61], let `C_Z` run over the
irreducible components of the special fibre of the regular proper model `X ⟶ Spec(R)`, each with
its reduced induced structure as a closed subscheme of `X`. For an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ`
and an integer family `a` the degree pairing is

`⟨a, ℒ⟩ = ∑_Z a_Z · deg(ℒ|_{C_Z})`;

it is bilinear, and for integer families `a` and `b`

`⟨a, 𝒪_X(∑_Y b_Y C_Y)⟩ = ⟨b, 𝒪_X(∑_Z a_Z C_Z)⟩`.

The four clauses are, in order: the defining formula for the pairing, additivity in the
coefficient family, additivity in the invertible module — the Picard group being written
multiplicatively, so that addition of its elements is the tensor product — and the symmetry.
The third is the invertible case of [Stacks, Tag 0AYX] on each component, and the fourth is
proved as the source proves it: expand both sides by the first three clauses and appeal to the
symmetry of the intersection matrix
`deg(𝒪_X(C_Y)|_{C_Z}) = deg(𝒪_X(C_Z)|_{C_Y})`, which is
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.componentDegree_specialFiberComponent_comm`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFiberDegreePairing_bilinear_and_comm
    (s : Finset (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)) :
    (∀ (a : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ) (L : S.X.Modules)
        (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L),
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a L hL =
          ∑ Z ∈ s, a Z * S.specialFiberComponentDegree Z L hL) ∧
      (∀ (a a' : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ) (L : S.X.Modules)
        (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L),
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s (a + a') L hL =
          S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a L hL + S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a' L hL) ∧
      (∀ (a : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ) (L M : S.X.Modules)
        (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L)
        (hM : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property M)
        (hLM : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property
            ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
              ⟨(S.X.toRingedSpace).presheaf, (S.X.toRingedSpace).IsSheaf⟩).obj (L)).obj (M)))),
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨(S.X.toRingedSpace).presheaf, (S.X.toRingedSpace).IsSheaf⟩).obj (L)).obj (M))) hLM =
          S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a L hL + S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a M hM) ∧
      (∀ a b : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℤ,
        S.specialFiberDegreePairing s a (S.specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s b)
            (S.isInvertible_specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s b) =
          S.specialFiberDegreePairing s b (S.specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s a)
            (S.isInvertible_specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf s a))
declarations.comment: the second displayed equality ⟨a, O_X(∑ b_Y C_Y)⟩ = ⟨b, O_X(∑ a_Z C_Z)⟩ at INTEGER coefficient families a, b, which is the fourth clause. Here O_X(∑ b_Y C_Y) is Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf, the difference twist of Stacks 01WX part (4) at the positive and negative parts of b; its degree on C_Z is ∑_Y b_Y (C_Z · C_Y) by Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberComponentDegree_specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf_eq_sum, and on a nonnegative family the pairing against it is the intersection product Stacks.Models.intersectionProduct of the first displayed equality, by Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberDegreePairing_specialFiberVerticalDivisorSheaf_natCast

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.intersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C65, the definition of the intersection product.** For an integer
family `a` and a nonnegative family `b` on components `Cᵢ` that are effective Cartier divisors,
`(∑ᵢ aᵢCᵢ · ∑ⱼ bⱼCⱼ)` is the degree pairing of `a` against `𝒪_X(∑ⱼ bⱼCⱼ)`.
declarations.statement:
def intersectionProduct (a : ι → ℤ) (b : ι → ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ i ∈ s, Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (C i)) : ℤ
declarations.comment: the product, defined as ⟨a, O_X(∑ bⱼCⱼ)⟩; its symmetry on the components of the special fibre is Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionProduct_comm of StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/Models/DegreePairingSymmetry.lean

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.intersectionProduct_eq_degreePairing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C65, first equality.** The intersection product
`(∑ᵢ aᵢCᵢ · ∑ⱼ bⱼCⱼ)` is the degree pairing `⟨a, 𝒪_X(∑ⱼ bⱼCⱼ)⟩`.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersectionProduct_eq_degreePairing (a : ι → ℤ) (b : ι → ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ i ∈ s, Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (C i)) :
    intersectionProduct S s C g hg hdim a b hC =
      degreePairing S s C g hg hdim a (Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' (∏ j ∈ s, C j ^ b j))
        (@Stacks.Divisors.isTensorInvertible_invertibleSheaf _ (∏ j ∈ s, C j ^ b j)
          (Stacks.Divisors.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_prod s C b hC))
declarations.comment: the first displayed equality, which is the definition

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.intersectionProduct_specialFiber_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The special fibre is orthogonal to every integral combination of the components**,
`(Σ aᵢCᵢ · Σ mᵢCᵢ) = 0`, because the sheaf `𝒪_X(Σ mᵢCᵢ) = 𝒪_X(X_k)` is trivial and the structure
sheaf has degree zero on each component.

This is part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0C66] at an abstract family of components and in the orientation
that the triviality of `𝒪_X(X_k)` gives directly. The clause as the source states it,
`(Σ mᵢCᵢ · Cⱼ) = 0` at the irreducible components of the special fibre, is
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionProduct_multiplicity_eq_zero`
of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/Models/SpecialFiberIntersectionForm.lean`, and follows
from this statement by the symmetry of the form, [Stacks, Tag 0C64]. Both are registered.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersectionProduct_specialFiber_eq_zero (a : ι → ℤ) (m : ι → ℕ)
    (hC : ∀ j ∈ s, Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (C j))
    (hdec : S.specialFiberIdeal = ∏ j ∈ s, C j ^ m j) :
    intersectionProduct S s C g hg hdim a m hC = 0
declarations.comment: part (2), in the orientation (∑ aᵢCᵢ · ∑ mᵢCᵢ) = 0 of the symmetric form

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix_nonneg_and_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C66, part (1).** For two distinct irreducible components `C_Z ≠ C_Y` of
the special fibre of a regular proper model, `(C_Z · C_Y) ≥ 0`, and `(C_Z · C_Y) = 0` if and only
if `C_Z ∩ C_Y = ∅`.

The entry `(C_Z · C_Y)` is the degree of `𝒪_X(C_Y)` on `C_Z`. Since `C_Z ≠ C_Y` are distinct
irreducible components, `C_Z ⊄ C_Y`, so the canonical section of `𝒪_X(C_Y)` restricts to a
*nonzero* global section of `𝒪_X(C_Y)|_{C_Z}` on the integral proper curve `C_Z`, whose zero
scheme is the scheme-theoretic intersection `C_Z ∩ C_Y`. Part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0B40] then
gives `(C_Z · C_Y) ≥ 0`, and part (2) of that tag gives `(C_Z · C_Y) > 0` exactly when the zero
scheme is nonempty, that is exactly when `C_Z` meets `C_Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFiberIntersectionMatrix_nonneg_and_eq_zero_iff
    {Z Y : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber} (h : Z ≠ Y) :
    0 ≤ S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z Y ∧
      (S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z Y = 0 ↔ (Z.1 : Set S.specialFiber) ∩ Y.1 = ∅)
declarations.comment: part (1): (C_Z · C_Y) ≥ 0 for Z ≠ Y, with equality if and only if C_Z ∩ C_Y = ∅

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionProduct_multiplicity_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C66, part (2).** The special fibre `X_k = ∑_Z m_Z C_Z` of a regular
proper model is orthogonal to each of its irreducible components, `(∑_Z m_Z C_Z · C_Y) = 0`.

This is the orientation in which the source states the clause. By the symmetry of the form,
[Stacks, Tag 0C64], it equals `(C_Y · ∑_Z m_Z C_Z)`, which is the degree on `C_Y` of
`𝒪_X(∑_Z m_Z C_Z) = 𝒪_X(X_k)`; and that invertible module is trivial, the special fibre being cut
out by a uniformizer of the discrete valuation ring, so the degree vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFiberIntersectionProduct_multiplicity_eq_zero
    (Y : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) :
    S.specialFiberIntersectionProduct (fun Z => (S.specialFiberMultiplicity Z : ℤ))
      (Pi.single Y 1) = 0
declarations.comment: part (2): (∑_Z m_Z C_Z · C_Y) = 0, the special fibre is orthogonal to each component

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.not_forall_specialFiberIntersectionMatrix_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C66, part (3).** There is no nonempty proper set `I` of irreducible
components of the special fibre with `(C_Z · C_Y) = 0` for all `Z ∈ I` and all `Y ∉ I`.

By part (1) such an `I` would make every component in `I` disjoint from every component not in
`I`, so the special fibre would be the union of the two disjoint nonempty closed sets
`⋃_{Z ∈ I} C_Z` and `⋃_{Y ∉ I} C_Y` — the components cover the special fibre, and there are
finitely many of them, so both unions are closed. That contradicts the connectedness of the
special fibre, [Stacks, Tag 0C62].
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_specialFiberIntersectionMatrix_eq_zero
    (I : Set (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)) (hne : I.Nonempty) (hI : I ≠ Set.univ) :
    ¬ ∀ Z ∈ I, ∀ Y ∉ I, S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z Y = 0
declarations.comment: part (3): no nonempty proper set I of components has (C_Z · C_Y) = 0 for all Z in I and all Y not in I

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionForm_nonpos_and_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C66, part (4).** For every family `a` of *rational* coefficients on the
irreducible components of the special fibre of a regular proper model,

`(∑_Z a_Z C_Z · ∑_Z a_Z C_Z) ≤ 0`,

and equality holds if and only if there is a single `q ∈ ℚ` with `a_Z = q m_Z` for every `Z`.

This is the source's own deduction from the other three parts through the linear algebra of
[Stacks, Tag 0C5X]: the intersection matrix is symmetric by [Stacks, Tag 0C64], has nonnegative
off-diagonal entries by part (1), kills the strictly positive multiplicity vector `m` by part (2)
— each multiplicity is positive by [Stacks, Tag 0C5Z] — and is irreducible by part (3). A
symmetric matrix with those three properties is negative semidefinite with nullspace exactly the
line spanned by `m`.

The form is written as the double sum `∑_Z ∑_Y a_Z a_Y (C_Z · C_Y)`, which is the bilinear
