extension to rational coefficients of the form of [Stacks, Tag 0C65]; the two agree wherever both
are defined, by
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberIntersectionProduct_eq_sum_sum`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFiberIntersectionForm_nonpos_and_eq_zero_iff
    (a : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber → ℚ) :
    ∑ Z, ∑ Y, a Z * a Y * (S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z Y : ℚ) ≤ 0 ∧
      (∑ Z, ∑ Y, a Z * a Y * (S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z Y : ℚ) = 0 ↔
        ∃ q : ℚ, ∀ Z, a Z = q * (S.specialFiberMultiplicity Z : ℚ))
declarations.comment: part (4): (∑_Z a_Z C_Z · ∑_Z a_Z C_Z) ≤ 0 for rational a, with equality if and only if a_Z = q m_Z for a single rational q

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_reducedSpecialFibre
declarations.doc:
**The reduced fibre of a decomposition into effective Cartier divisors is an effective
Cartier divisor**, being a sum of nonnegative multiples of effective Cartier divisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_reducedSpecialFibre
    (hC : ∀ i ∈ s, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (C i)) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (reducedSpecialFibre s C m)
declarations.comment: D is an effective Cartier divisor, given a decomposition of X_k

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.zsmul_picardClass_reducedSpecialFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67.** The invertible sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` of the reduced special fibre
`D = Σ (mᵢ/d) Cᵢ` of a regular proper model has order dividing `d` in `Pic(X)`:
`𝒪_X(D)^{⊗d} = 𝒪_X(dD) = 𝒪_X(X_k) = 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zsmul_picardClass_reducedSpecialFibre
    (hdec : S.specialFiberIdeal = ∏ i ∈ s, C i ^ m i) :
    ((s.gcd m : ℕ) : ℤ) • picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre s C m) = 0
declarations.comment: O_X(D) has order dividing d in Pic(X), given a decomposition of X_k

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.isInvertible_immersionConormalSheaf_reducedSpecialFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67.** The conormal module `𝒞_{D/X}` of the reduced special fibre
`D = Σ (mᵢ/d) Cᵢ` is an invertible `𝒪_D`-module: it is the restriction `ℐ_D|_D` of the ideal
sheaf of an effective Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_immersionConormalSheaf_reducedSpecialFibre :
    IsInvertible (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.presheaf
      (structureIsSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.toRingedSpace)
      (Stacks.Thickenings.immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subschemeι)
declarations.comment: the conormal sheaf of D is an invertible O_D-module

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.zsmul_picardClass_immersionConormalSheaf_reducedSpecialFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67.** The conormal module `𝒞_{D/X}` of the reduced special fibre
`D = Σ (mᵢ/d) Cᵢ` has order dividing `d` in `Pic(D)`: it is the pullback to `D` of
`𝒪_X(-D) = -[𝒪_X(D)]`, and pullback is a homomorphism of Picard groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem zsmul_picardClass_immersionConormalSheaf_reducedSpecialFibre
    (hdec : S.specialFiberIdeal = ∏ i ∈ s, C i ^ m i) :
    ((s.gcd m : ℕ) : ℤ) • picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.presheaf
        (structureIsSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.toRingedSpace)
        (Stacks.Thickenings.immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subschemeι)
        (isInvertible_immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m)) = 0
declarations.comment: the conormal class has order dividing d in Pic(D)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.reducedSpecialFibre_order_dvd_gcd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67.** All four conclusions at once: the reduced special fibre
`D = Σ (mᵢ/d) Cᵢ` of a regular proper model is an effective Cartier divisor, `𝒪_X(D)` has order
dividing `d = gcd(mᵢ)` in `Pic(X)`, and `𝒞_{D/X}` is an invertible `𝒪_D`-module of order
dividing `d` in `Pic(D)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reducedSpecialFibre_order_dvd_gcd
    (hC : ∀ i ∈ s, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (C i))
    (hdec : S.specialFiberIdeal = ∏ i ∈ s, C i ^ m i) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (reducedSpecialFibre s C m) ∧
      ((s.gcd m : ℕ) : ℤ) • picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre s C m) = 0 ∧
      IsInvertible (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.presheaf
        (structureIsSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.toRingedSpace)
        (Stacks.Thickenings.immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subschemeι) ∧
      ((s.gcd m : ℕ) : ℤ) • picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.presheaf
        (structureIsSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.toRingedSpace)
        (Stacks.Thickenings.immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subschemeι)
        (isInvertible_immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre s C m)) = 0
declarations.comment: all four conclusions, given a decomposition of X_k rather than a canonical one

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_reducedSpecialFibre_specialFiberComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67, at the canonical decomposition.** The reduced special fibre
`D = Σ (mᵢ/d) Cᵢ` of the decomposition of `X_k` into its irreducible components is an effective
Cartier divisor on the model: the components are effective Cartier divisors by part (2) of
[Stacks, Tag 0C5Z], and a nonnegative combination of effective Cartier divisors is one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_reducedSpecialFibre_specialFiberComponents :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
      S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity)
declarations.comment: D is an effective Cartier divisor, at the canonical decomposition of X_k into its irreducible components

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.reducedSpecialFibre_order_dvd_gcd_specialFiberComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67, at the canonical decomposition into irreducible components.**
Let `C₁, …, Cₙ` be the irreducible components of the special fibre `X_k` of a regular proper
model, with their reduced induced structure, let `mᵢ` be the multiplicity of `Cᵢ` in `X_k`, put
`d = gcd(m₁, …, mₙ)` and let `D = Σ (mᵢ/d) Cᵢ`. Then `D` is an effective Cartier divisor,
`𝒪_X(D)` has order dividing `d` in `Pic(X)`, and the conormal module `𝒞_{D/X}` is an invertible
`𝒪_D`-module of order dividing `d` in `Pic(D)`.

This is `Stacks.Models.reducedSpecialFibre_order_dvd_gcd` with both of its hypotheses supplied
from [Stacks, Tag 0C5Z]: effectivity of the components is part (2) and `X_k = Σ mᵢ Cᵢ` is
part (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem reducedSpecialFibre_order_dvd_gcd_specialFiberComponents :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
        S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity) ∧
      ((Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity : ℕ) : ℤ) •
          picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
            S.specialFiberMultiplicity) = 0 ∧
      IsInvertible (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
          S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme.presheaf
        (structureIsSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
          S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme.toRingedSpace)
        (Stacks.Thickenings.immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
          S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subschemeι) ∧
      ((Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity : ℕ) : ℤ) •
          picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
              S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme.presheaf
            (structureIsSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
              S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme.toRingedSpace)
            (Stacks.Thickenings.immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
              S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subschemeι)
            (isInvertible_immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
              S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity)) = 0
declarations.comment: all four conclusions at the canonical decomposition of X_k into its irreducible components, whose two inputs are parts (2) and (3) of 0C5Z: C_i the components with their reduced induced structure, m_i the multiplicity of C_i in X_k, d = gcd(m_i) and D = sum (m_i/d)C_i

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.addOrderOf_picardClass_reducedSpecialFibre_specialFiberComponents_dvd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67, at the canonical decomposition**, as a statement about additive
orders: the class of `𝒪_X(D)` in `Pic(X)` has order dividing `d = gcd(mᵢ)`, for `D` the reduced
special fibre of the decomposition of `X_k` into its irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem addOrderOf_picardClass_reducedSpecialFibre_specialFiberComponents_dvd :
    addOrderOf (picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
      S.specialFiberMultiplicity)) ∣ Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity
declarations.comment: O_X(D) has order dividing d in Pic(X), at the canonical decomposition of X_k into its irreducible components

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.addOrderOf_picardClass_immersionConormalSheaf_specialFiberComponents_dvd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C67, at the canonical decomposition**, as a statement about additive
orders: the class of the conormal module `𝒞_{D/X}` in `Pic(D)` has order dividing
`d = gcd(mᵢ)`, for `D` the reduced special fibre of the decomposition of `X_k` into its
irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem addOrderOf_picardClass_immersionConormalSheaf_specialFiberComponents_dvd :
    addOrderOf (picardClass (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
        S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme.presheaf
      (structureIsSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
        S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme.toRingedSpace)
      (Stacks.Thickenings.immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
        S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subschemeι)
      (isInvertible_immersionConormalSheaf (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
        S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity))) ∣
      Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity
declarations.comment: the conormal class of D has order dividing d in Pic(D), at the canonical decomposition of X_k into its irreducible components

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.exists_chain_reducedSpecialFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C68** [Artin–Winters, Lemma 2.6].  In Situation
[Stacks, Tag 0C61], write the special fibre as a sum of effective Cartier divisors
`X_k = Σ mᵢCᵢ`, put `d = gcd(mᵢ)` and let `D = Σ (mᵢ/d)Cᵢ`.  Then there is a sequence of
effective Cartier divisors `(X_k)_red = Z₀ ⊆ Z₁ ⊆ … ⊆ Z_M = D` in which each step
`Z_{j+1} = Z_j + C_{i_j}` adds a single component, and such that `H⁰(Z_j, 𝒪_{Z_j})` is a field,
finite over the residue field `k` for the algebra structure induced by the base ring, for every
`j = 0, …, M`.

Every input of the source's induction is proved here.  Connectedness of the reduced special
fibre is [Stacks, Tag 0C62],
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.connectedSpace_subscheme_radical_specialFiberIdeal`;
finiteness of the global functions of a proper scheme over `k` is clause (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 0BUG],
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperSectionsGeom.moduleFinite_globalSections_of_isProper`; finite
dimensionality of coherent cohomology over a field is [Stacks, Tag 02O6],
`AlgebraicGeometry.forall_finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_unit`; and the geometric step is
`Stacks.Models.exists_componentDegree_negativeTwist_neg`, which runs the four properties of
[Stacks, Tag 0C66] at the given decomposition.  [Stacks, Tag 0C4T] and part (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 0B40] enter through
`Stacks.Models.injective_inclusion_appTop_of_forall_eq_zero`.  See the implementation notes of
this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chain_reducedSpecialFibre
    (hC : ∀ i ∈ s, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (C i))
    (hm : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < m i)
    (hdec : S.specialFiberIdeal = ∏ i ∈ s, C i ^ m i)
    (hred : S.specialFiberIdeal.radical = ∏ i ∈ s, C i)
    (g : ∀ i, (C i).subscheme ⟶ Spec (.of S.k)) (_hgproper : ∀ i, IsProper (g i))
    (hdim : ∀ i, topologicalKrullDim (C i).subscheme ≤ 1)
    (hint : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral (C i).subscheme) :
    ∃ (M : ℕ) (Z : ℕ → S.X.IdealSheafData),
      Z 0 = S.specialFiberIdeal.radical ∧ Z M = reducedSpecialFibre s C m ∧
      (∀ j < M, ∃ i ∈ s, Z (j + 1) = Z j * C i ∧ Z (j + 1) ≤ Z j) ∧
      ∀ j ≤ M, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (Z j) ∧ IsField Γ((Z j).subscheme, ⊤) ∧
        ∃ φ : S.k →+* Γ((Z j).subscheme, ⊤),
          φ.comp (algebraMap S.R S.k) = fibreSubschemeBaseMap S (Z j) ∧ φ.Finite
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: the increasing chain of effective Cartier divisors from the reduced special fibre (X_k)_red to the divisor D = sum (mᵢ/d)Cᵢ, d = gcd(mᵢ), each step adding a single component, with H⁰(Z_j, O_{Z_j}) a field finite over the residue field at every stage. Stated at a decomposition X_k = sum mᵢCᵢ of the special fibre into integral proper curves over the residue field, which is the opening phrase of Situation 0C61

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.one_sub_genus_eq_gcd_mul_finrank_mul_one_sub_genus_reducedSpecialFibre
declarations.doc:
**The formula of [Stacks, Tag 0C69]** [Artin-Winters, Lemma 2.6].  In Situation
[Stacks, Tag 0C61], written at a decomposition `X_k = Σ mᵢCᵢ` of the special fibre into integral
proper curves over the residue field, with `d = gcd(mᵢ)`, `D = Σ (mᵢ/d)Cᵢ` the reduced special
fibre and `κ = H⁰(D, 𝒪_D)`:

`1 - g_C = d · [κ : k] · (1 - g_D)`,

where `g_C` is the genus of `C` over `K` and `g_D` the genus of `D` over `κ`.  That `κ` is a
field, finite over `k`, is part of the conclusion rather than a hypothesis: it is the top stage
of the chain of [Stacks, Tag 0C68].

The binder list is exactly that of `Stacks.Models.exists_chain_reducedSpecialFibre`, whose
conclusion at its top stage is what makes `κ` a field finite over `k`.  The source's proof is
the composite of four identities, each of them a theorem here:
`1 - g_C = χ(C, 𝒪_C)` is `Stacks.Models.one_sub_genus_curve_eq_eulerCharacteristic`;
`χ(C, 𝒪_C) = χ(X_k, 𝒪_{X_k})` is
`RegularProperModelSituation.eulerCharacteristic_unit_eq_eulerCharacteristic_unit_specialFibre`;
`χ(X_k, 𝒪_{X_k}) = d·χ(D, 𝒪_D)` is `Stacks.Models.fibreEuler_specialFiberIdeal_eq`; and
`χ(D, 𝒪_D) = [κ : k](1 - g_D)` is `Stacks.Models.fibreEuler_reducedSpecialFibre_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_sub_genus_eq_gcd_mul_finrank_mul_one_sub_genus_reducedSpecialFibre
    (hC : ∀ i ∈ s, IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (C i))
    (hm : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < m i)
    (hdec : S.specialFiberIdeal = ∏ i ∈ s, C i ^ m i)
    (hred : S.specialFiberIdeal.radical = ∏ i ∈ s, C i)
    (g : ∀ i, (C i).subscheme ⟶ Spec (.of S.k)) (hgproper : ∀ i, IsProper (g i))
    (hdimC : ∀ i, topologicalKrullDim (C i).subscheme ≤ 1)
    (hint : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral (C i).subscheme) :
    ∃ hκ : IsField Γ((reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme, ⊤),
      letI : Algebra S.k Γ((reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme, ⊤) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S.k)).inv ≫ (S.fibreSubschemeToSpec
          (reducedSpecialFibre s C m)
          (specialFiberIdeal_le_reducedSpecialFibre S s C m hdec)).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
      letI : Field Γ((reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme, ⊤) := hκ.toField
      Module.Finite S.k Γ((reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme, ⊤) ∧
        (1 : ℤ) - (AlgebraicGeometry.genus S.C_to_K : ℤ) =
          ((s.gcd m : ℕ) : ℤ) *
            (Module.finrank S.k Γ((reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme, ⊤) : ℤ) *
            (1 - (AlgebraicGeometry.genus
              (reducedSpecialFibre s C m).subscheme.toSpecΓ : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the formula 1 - g_C = d [kappa:k](1 - g_D) at a decomposition X_k = sum m_i C_i of the special fibre into integral proper curves over the residue field whose product is the reduced special fibre, of which the irreducible components of Situation 0C61 are the case: d = gcd(m_i), D = sum (m_i/d)C_i, kappa = H^0(D, O_D), and g_D the genus of D over kappa. That kappa is a field finite over the residue field is part of the conclusion

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.one_sub_genus_eq_gcd_mul_finrank_mul_one_sub_genus_specialFiberComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C69** [Artin-Winters, Lemma 2.6], at the irreducible components of
the special fibre, which is the setting of Situation [Stacks, Tag 0C61].  With `C₁, …, Cₙ` the
irreducible components of `X_k`, `mᵢ` their multiplicities, `d = gcd(mᵢ)`, `D = Σ (mᵢ/d)Cᵢ` and
`κ = H⁰(D, 𝒪_D)`:

`1 - g_C = d · [κ : k] · (1 - g_D)`.

Every binder of the general statement is discharged at the canonical family: the components are
integral effective Cartier divisors, proper of dimension at most one over the residue field with
positive multiplicities, `X_k = Σ mᵢCᵢ` is part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0C5Z], and the reduction
`(X_k)_red = Σ Cᵢ` is
`Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.radical_specialFiberIdeal_eq_prod`.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_sub_genus_eq_gcd_mul_finrank_mul_one_sub_genus_specialFiberComponents :
    ∃ hκ : IsField Γ((reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
        S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme, ⊤),
      letI : Algebra S.k Γ((reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
          S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme, ⊤) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S.k)).inv ≫ (S.fibreSubschemeToSpec
          (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
            S.specialFiberMultiplicity)
          (specialFiberIdeal_le_reducedSpecialFibre S Finset.univ
            S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity
            S.specialFiberIdeal_eq_prod)).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
      letI : Field Γ((reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
        S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme, ⊤) := hκ.toField
      Module.Finite S.k Γ((reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal
        S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme, ⊤) ∧
        (1 : ℤ) - (AlgebraicGeometry.genus S.C_to_K : ℤ) =
          ((Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity : ℕ) : ℤ) *
            (Module.finrank S.k Γ((reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
              S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme, ⊤) : ℤ) *
            (1 - (AlgebraicGeometry.genus (reducedSpecialFibre Finset.univ
              S.specialFiberComponentIdeal S.specialFiberMultiplicity).subscheme.toSpecΓ : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the formula 1 - g_C = d [kappa:k](1 - g_D) at the irreducible components of the special fibre, which is the setting of Situation 0C61: d = gcd(m_i) for m_i the multiplicity of C_i in X_k, D = sum (m_i/d)C_i the reduced special fibre, kappa = H^0(D, O_D), and g_D the genus of D over kappa. That kappa is a field finite over the residue field is part of the conclusion

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.specialFiberMultiplicity_eq_one_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6A: `m₁ = m₂ = 1`.** Every irreducible component of the special
fibre occurs in `X_k` with multiplicity one.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFiberMultiplicity_eq_one_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
    {i j : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber} (hij : i ≠ j)
    {κi κj : Type u} [Field κi] [Field κj]
    {ei : projectiveLineProj κi ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).subscheme}
    {ej : projectiveLineProj κj ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme}
    (hi : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κi ei)
    (hj : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κj ej)
    (hmeet : Nonempty
      (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme) :
    ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber, S.specialFiberMultiplicity Z = 1
declarations.comment: m_1 = m_2 = 1, every component of the special fibre has multiplicity one

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.genus_eq_zero_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0C6A: the generic curve has genus zero.**
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_eq_zero_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
    {i j : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber} (hij : i ≠ j)
    {κi κj : Type u} [Field κi] [Field κj]
    {ei : projectiveLineProj κi ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).subscheme}
    {ej : projectiveLineProj κj ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme}
    (hi : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κi ei)
    (hj : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κj ej)
    (hmeet : Nonempty
      (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme) :
    genus S.C_to_K = 0
declarations.comment: C has genus 0, the generic fibre of the model has genus zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.exists_section_fibreSubschemeToSpec_sup_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6A: the two components meet in a `k`-rational point.** The
scheme-theoretic intersection `C_i ∩ C_j`, as a closed subscheme of the model, carries a
structure morphism over the residue field compatible with the model morphism, and that morphism
is an isomorphism — so the intersection is a single rational point of `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_section_fibreSubschemeToSpec_sup_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
    {i j : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber} (hij : i ≠ j)
    {κi κj : Type u} [Field κi] [Field κj]
    {ei : projectiveLineProj κi ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).subscheme}
    {ej : projectiveLineProj κj ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme}
    (hi : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κi ei)
    (hj : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κj ej)
    (hmeet : Nonempty
      (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme) :
    ∃ f : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔
        S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme ⟶ Spec (.of S.k),
      (f ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S.R S.k)) =
        (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔
          S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subschemeι ≫ S.X_to_R) ∧
      ∃ e : Spec (.of S.k) ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔
        S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme, e.hom ≫ f = 𝟙 (Spec (.of S.k))
declarations.comment: C_1 and C_2 meet in a k-rational point

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.exists_iso_projectiveLineProj_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6A: `C₁ ≅ 𝐏¹_k` and `C₂ ≅ 𝐏¹_k`.** Each irreducible component of
the special fibre is the projective line over the residue field, compatibly with the structure
morphism of the model: the component carries a morphism to `Spec k` lying over `Spec R`, and an
isomorphism with `𝐏¹_k` carrying that morphism to the structure morphism of `𝐏¹_k`.

The projective line is the graded model `Proj k[T₀, T₁]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_projectiveLineProj_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
    {i j : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber} (hij : i ≠ j)
    {κi κj : Type u} [Field κi] [Field κj]
    {ei : projectiveLineProj κi ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).subscheme}
    {ej : projectiveLineProj κj ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme}
    (hi : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κi ei)
    (hj : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κj ej)
    (hmeet : Nonempty
      (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme) :
    ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber,
      ∃ f : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme ⟶ Spec (.of S.k),
        (f ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S.R S.k)) =
          (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subschemeι ≫ S.X_to_R) ∧
        ∃ e : projectiveLineProj S.k ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme,
          e.hom ≫ f = projToSpecCoeff S.k 1
declarations.comment: C_1 and C_2 are isomorphic to the projective line over the residue field

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.nonempty_fin_two_equiv_irreducibleComponents_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6A: `n = 2`.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0C61], if two distinct
irreducible components `C_i` and `C_j` of the special fibre are exceptional curves of the first
kind and meet, then the special fibre has exactly two irreducible components.

The components are indexed by `irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber` itself, so the assertion
`n = 2` is an equivalence of that index type with `Fin 2`; no ordering of the components is
chosen.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_fin_two_equiv_irreducibleComponents_of_isExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind
    {i j : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber} (hij : i ≠ j)
    {κi κj : Type u} [Field κi] [Field κj]
    {ei : projectiveLineProj κi ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).subscheme}
    {ej : projectiveLineProj κj ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme}
    (hi : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κi ei)
    (hj : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κj ej)
    (hmeet : Nonempty
      (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal i ⊔ S.specialFiberComponentIdeal j).subscheme) :
    Nonempty (Fin 2 ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)
declarations.comment: n = 2, the special fibre has exactly two irreducible components

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.exists_isMinimalModel_and_existsUnique_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6B.** Let `C` be a smooth projective curve over `K` with
`H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K` and genus `> 0`. There is a unique minimal model for `C`: a minimal model exists,
and any two minimal models are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism of models, that is, over `R`
and compatible with the identifications of their generic fibres with `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isMinimalModel_and_existsUnique_iso {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (hproj : Stacks.HProjective.IsHProjective c)
    (hH0 : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)) (hg : 0 < genus c) :
    (∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
      (e : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))),
      IsMinimalModel c p e) ∧
    ∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (.of R))
      (eX : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))))
      (eY : C ≅ pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))),
      IsMinimalModel c p eX → IsMinimalModel c q eY →
        ∃! φ : X ≅ Y, φ.hom ≫ q = p ∧
          eX.hom ≫ pullback.fst p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ≫ φ.hom =
            eY.hom ≫ pullback.fst q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.contractedSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6C, the contracted model.** Let `f : X ⟶ X'` contract an
irreducible component `C_n` of the special fibre of a regular proper model `X` of `C`. Then `X'`,
with the structure morphism through which `X ⟶ Spec R` factors, is again a regular proper model
of `C` over the same discrete valuation ring: it is the standing situation of
[Stacks, Tag 0C61] with `X'` in place of `X`.
declarations.comment: X' is as in Situation 0C61: a regular proper model of the same curve

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.exists_isContractionOfExceptionalCurve_specialFiberComponentIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6C, the contraction.** In Situation 0C61, an irreducible component
`C_n` of the special fibre which is an exceptional curve of the first kind can be contracted:
there is a contraction `f : X ⟶ X'` of `C_n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isContractionOfExceptionalCurve_specialFiberComponentIdeal
    (N : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) {κ : Type u} [Field κ]
    {e : projectiveLineProj κ ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).subscheme}
    (hN : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κ e) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f : S.X ⟶ X'),
      IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N) f
declarations.comment: the contraction f : X -> X' of the exceptional component C_n exists

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.exists_contractedComponentEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The components and multiplicities of the contracted model.** Let
`f : X ⟶ X'` contract the component `C_n` of the special fibre of a regular proper model `X`,
and let `X'` be the regular proper model of
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.contractedSituation`. Then `f` lies over `Spec R` and
over the identification of both generic fibres with `C`, and the images `C'_i = f(C_i)` of the
components `C_i ≠ C_n` are exactly the `n - 1` irreducible components of `X'_k`, with
multiplicities `m'_i = m_i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_contractedComponentEquiv
    (hf : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N) f) :
    f ≫ (S.contractedSituation hf).X_to_R = S.X_to_R ∧
      (S.contractedSituation hf).genericFiberIso.hom ≫
          pullback.fst (S.contractedSituation hf).X_to_R
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S.R S.K))) =
        S.genericFiberIso.hom ≫ pullback.fst S.X_to_R _ ≫ f ∧
      Fintype.card (irreducibleComponents (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiber) + 1 =
        Fintype.card (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) ∧
      ∃ σ : {Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber // Z ≠ N} ≃
          irreducibleComponents (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiber,
        ∀ Z, (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberι.base ''
              ((σ Z).1 : Set (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiber) =
            f.base '' (S.specialFiberι.base '' (Z.1.1 : Set S.specialFiber)) ∧
          (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberMultiplicity (σ Z) =
            S.specialFiberMultiplicity Z.1
declarations.comment: the components C'_i = f(C_i), i < n, of X'_k and their multiplicities m'_i = m_i

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.exists_contractedComponentMap
declarations.doc:
**The maps `κ_i ← κ'_i → κ_n`.** If `C_i` meets `C_n`, there are morphisms `C_i ⟶ C'_i` and
`C_n ⟶ C'_i` compatible with the contraction and with the closed immersions into `X` and `X'`,
and their maps of global sections are ring maps `κ_i ← κ'_i → κ_n`, where `κ_i`, `κ'_i`, `κ_n`
are the rings of global functions on `C_i`, `C'_i`, `C_n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_contractedComponentMap
    (hf : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N) f)
    (Z : {Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber // Z ≠ N})
    (hmeet : ((Z.1.1 : Set S.specialFiber) ∩ N.1).Nonempty) :
    ∃ (φ : Γ(((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentIdeal
          (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z)).subscheme, ⊤) ⟶
          Γ((S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z.1).subscheme, ⊤))
      (ψ : Γ(((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentIdeal
          (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z)).subscheme, ⊤) ⟶
          Γ((S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).subscheme, ⊤))
      (g : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z.1).subscheme ⟶
        ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentIdeal
          (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z)).subscheme)
      (h : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).subscheme ⟶
        ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentIdeal
          (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z)).subscheme),
      g ≫ ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentIdeal
          (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z)).subschemeι =
          (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z.1).subschemeι ≫ f ∧
        h ≫ ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentIdeal
          (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z)).subschemeι =
          (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).subschemeι ≫ f ∧
        g.appTop = φ ∧ h.appTop = ψ
declarations.comment: part (2): maps κ_i ← κ'_i → κ_n when C_i meets C_n

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.contractedSpecialFiberIntersectionMatrix
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6C, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ X'` contract the component `C_n` of the
special fibre of a regular proper model, and let `C'_i = f(C_i)`, `i < n`, be the components of
the special fibre of the contracted model. Then for `i, j < n`

`(C'_i · C'_j) = (C_i · C_j) - (C_i · C_n)(C_j · C_n) / (C_n · C_n)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem contractedSpecialFiberIntersectionMatrix
    (hf : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N) f)
    [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)]
    [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiber)]
    (Z W : {Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber // Z ≠ N}) :
    ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberIntersectionMatrix (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z)
        (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf W) : ℚ) =
      S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z.1 W.1 -
        S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z.1 N * S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix W.1 N /
          S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix N N
declarations.comment: part (1): (C'_i · C'_j) = (C_i · C_j) - (C_i · C_n)(C_j · C_n)/(C_n · C_n)

declarations.name: TensorAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_baseChange
declarations.doc:
The tensor algebra of a base change is isomorphic to the base change of the tensor
algebra, sending `ι (1 ⊗ₜ m)` to `1 ⊗ₜ ι m`.
Taking `A = S⁻¹R` gives compatibility with localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem TensorAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_baseChange :
    ∃ e : TensorAlgebra A (A ⊗[R] M) ≃ₐ[A] A ⊗[R] TensorAlgebra R M,
      ∀ m : M, e (ι A (1 ⊗ₜ[R] m)) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] ι R m

declarations.name: SymmetricAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_baseChange
declarations.doc:
The symmetric algebra of a base change is isomorphic to the base change of the symmetric
algebra, sending `ι (1 ⊗ₜ m)` to `1 ⊗ₜ ι m`.
Taking `A = S⁻¹R` gives compatibility with localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem SymmetricAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_baseChange :
    ∃ e : SymmetricAlgebra A (A ⊗[R] M) ≃ₐ[A] A ⊗[R] SymmetricAlgebra R M,
      ∀ m : M, e (ι A (A ⊗[R] M) (1 ⊗ₜ[R] m)) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] ι R M m

declarations.name: ExteriorAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_baseChange
declarations.doc:
The exterior algebra of a base change is isomorphic to the base change of the exterior
algebra, sending `ι (1 ⊗ₜ m)` to `1 ⊗ₜ ι m`.
Taking `A = S⁻¹R` gives compatibility with localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem ExteriorAlgebra.exists_algEquiv_baseChange :
    ∃ e : ExteriorAlgebra A (A ⊗[R] M) ≃ₐ[A] A ⊗[R] ExteriorAlgebra R M,
      ∀ m : M, e (ι A (1 ⊗ₜ[R] m)) = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] ι R m

declarations.name: Module.depth_eq_supportDim_iff_quotSMulTop
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C6G.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal `𝔪`, let `M` be a
finite `R`-module and let `x ∈ 𝔪` be a nonzerodivisor on `M`. Then `M` is Cohen-Macaulay if and
only if `M/xM` is, Cohen-Macaulayness of a module `N` being the equality
`depth_𝔪(N) = dim Supp(N)` — the definiens of `Module.IsCohenMacaulayAtMaximalIdeal R N`
(Definition 00N3), written out so that each side is what Stacks 0BUS assumes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_eq_supportDim_iff_quotSMulTop {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] {x : R}
    (hx : x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (hreg : IsSMulRegular M x) :
    (depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) M : WithBot ℕ∞) = supportDim R M ↔
      (depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (QuotSMulTop x M) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
        supportDim R (QuotSMulTop x M)
declarations.comment: Cohen-Macaulayness is written out as the equation `depth_𝔪(N) = dim Supp(N)` that Definition 00N3 is, rather than as the predicate, so that each side is verbatim the hypothesis of Stacks 0BUS; the two differ by unfolding a definition. It is not spelled as the existence of an `M`-regular sequence of length `dim Supp(M)`, which needs Stacks 090R(2) to be the same condition.

declarations.name: isCohenMacaulayModule_iff_isCohenMacaulayModule_quotSMulTop
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0C6G.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring, `M` a finite `R`-module and `x ∈ m` a
nonzerodivisor on `M`. Then `M` is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if `M/xM` is.

Both the depth and the dimension of the support drop by exactly one along `x`: the first by
Stacks `090R` (`depth_quotient_succ_of_isSMulRegular`) and the second by Stacks `0B52`
(`Module.supportDim_quotSMulTop_succ_eq_supportDim`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulayModule_iff_isCohenMacaulayModule_quotSMulTop
    {x : R} (hx : x ∈ maximalIdeal R) (hreg : IsSMulRegular M x) :
    IsCohenMacaulayModule R M ↔ IsCohenMacaulayModule R (QuotSMulTop x M)

declarations.name: quasiFiniteAt_of_comp_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
Permanence of quasi-finiteness (Stacks tag 0C6H): if the composite of
`f : A →+* B` and `g : B →+* C` is quasi-finite at a prime `r` of `C`, then `g`
itself is quasi-finite at `r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFiniteAt_of_comp_quasiFiniteAt
    {A B C : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C)
    (r : Ideal C) [r.IsPrime]
    (h : (g.comp f).QuasiFiniteAt r) :
    g.QuasiFiniteAt r

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafHomPullback.pullbackSheafHomComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6I.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of
ringed spaces. If `F` is a finitely presented `𝒪_Y`-module, then the canonical
map
`f^* SheafHom(F, G) ⟶ SheafHom(f^*F, f^*G)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackSheafHomComparison_isIso
    {X Y : RingedSpace.{u, u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlat f)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y)) [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (H : SheafHom Y.sheaf F G)
    (H' : SheafHom X.sheaf ((modulePullback f).obj F)
      ((modulePullback f).obj G))
    (comparison : PullbackSheafHomComparison f F G H H') :
    IsIso (pullbackSheafHomComparison f F G H H' comparison)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAmple.isIso_relativeAmpleProjHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C6J].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a universally closed morphism of schemes and `L` an
invertible `𝒪_X`-module ample relative to `f`. Then the canonical morphism
`r : X ⟶ Proj_S(⨁_{d ≥ 0} f_* L^{⊗ d})` of [Stacks, Tag 01VJ] is an isomorphism.

Here `⨁_{d ≥ 0} f_* L^{⊗ d}` is `directImageAlgebra f L`, the relative `Proj` is that of
[Stacks, Tag 01NQ], and `r` is `relativeAmpleProjHom f L hL`, the morphism `r_{L, ψ}` of
[Stacks, Tag 01O9] for the adjunction map `ψ` on its source `U(ψ) = X`. The quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness of `f` that the algebra needs are part of, resp. a consequence of, relative
ampleness ([Stacks, Tags 01VH, 01VI]); they are not hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_relativeAmpleProjHom {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f]
    (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    haveI := hL.quasiCompact
    haveI := hL.quasiSeparated
    IsIso (relativeAmpleProjHom f L hL)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.shortExact_divisor_normal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0C6K, the label `divisor_normal_sequence`.** For an effective Cartier divisor
`D ⊆ X` with inclusion `i`, the normal sheaf `𝒩_{D/X}` is the restriction `i^* 𝒪_X(D)`, and

`0 ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_X(D) ⟶ i_* 𝒩_{D/X} ⟶ 0`

is short exact, the first map being multiplication by the canonical section `1_D` and the second
the unit of `i^* ⊣ i_*` followed by the pushforward of that identification.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_divisor_normal :
    let i := D.subschemeι
    let L : X.Modules := invertibleSheaf D
    let N : D.subscheme.Modules := normalSheaf i
    ∃ e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L ≅ N,
      let O : X.Modules := SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf
      let f : O ⟶ L := L.unitHomEquiv.symm (canonicalSections D)
      let g : L ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N :=
        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction i).unit.app L ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).map e.hom
      ∃ h : f ≫ g = 0, (ShortComplex.mk f g h).ShortExact
declarations.comment: divisor_normal_sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.shortExact_zeroScheme_ideal_of_isRegularSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0C6K, the label `regular_section_ideal_sequence`.** For an invertible module
`L` on a scheme `X` and a regular global section `s` of `L` ([Stacks, Tag 01WY]), the sequence

`0 ⟶ L^{⊗ -1} ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ i_* 𝒪_{Z(s)} ⟶ 0`

is short exact, where `i` is the inclusion of the zero scheme of `s`, the first map is
multiplication by `s` through the canonical trivialization `L^{⊗ -1} ⊗ L ≅ 𝒪_X` and the second
is restriction to the zero scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_zeroScheme_ideal_of_isRegularSection (s : L.sections)
    (hs : IsRegularSection X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property s) :
    let i := (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι
    let Linv : X.Modules := inverseTensorPower X L
    let u : Linv ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf :=
      ((ρ_ Linv).inv ≫ Linv ◁ L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) ≫ (inverseTensorPowerIsoUnit X L).hom
    let q : SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subscheme.ringCatSheaf) :=
      SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit i.toRingCatSheafHom
    ∃ h : u ≫ q = 0, (ShortComplex.mk u q h).ShortExact
declarations.comment: regular_section_ideal_sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_and_shortExact_sequences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0C6K.** Let `X` be a scheme.

1. For an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` and a regular section `s` of `L` ([Stacks, Tag 01WY]),
   with `i` the inclusion of the zero scheme `Z(s)`: `Z(s)` is an effective Cartier divisor on
   `X`, the sequence `0 ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ L ⟶ i_* i^* L ⟶ 0` is short exact (first map multiplication by
   `s`, second the unit of `i^* ⊣ i_*`), and the sequence `0 ⟶ L^{⊗ -1} ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ i_* 𝒪_{Z(s)} ⟶ 0`
   is short exact (first map multiplication by `s` read through `L^{⊗ -1} ⊗ L ≅ 𝒪_X`, second
   restriction to the zero scheme).
2. For an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X` with inclusion `i`: the normal sheaf `𝒩_{D/X}` is
   `i^* 𝒪_X(D)` and `0 ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_X(D) ⟶ i_* 𝒩_{D/X} ⟶ 0` is short exact (first map
   multiplication by the canonical section `1_D`), and `0 ⟶ ℐ_D ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ i_* 𝒪_D ⟶ 0` is short
   exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_zeroScheme_and_shortExact_sequences (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (∀ (L : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
        (s : L.sections), IsRegularSection X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property s →
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))) ∧
      (let i := (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι
        let O : X.Modules := SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf
        let f : O ⟶ L := L.unitHomEquiv.symm s
        let g : L ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L) :=
          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction i).unit.app L
        ∃ h : f ≫ g = 0, (ShortComplex.mk f g h).ShortExact) ∧
      (let i := (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι
        let Linv : X.Modules := inverseTensorPower X L
        let u : Linv ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf :=
          ((ρ_ Linv).inv ≫ Linv ◁ L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) ≫ (inverseTensorPowerIsoUnit X L).hom
        let q : SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf ⟶
            (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj
              (SheafOfModules.unit (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subscheme.ringCatSheaf) :=
          SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit i.toRingCatSheafHom
        ∃ h : u ≫ q = 0, (ShortComplex.mk u q h).ShortExact)) ∧
    (∀ (D : X.IdealSheafData) [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D],
      (let i := D.subschemeι
        let L : X.Modules := Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf D
        let N : D.subscheme.Modules := Stacks.Divisors.normalSheaf i
        ∃ e : (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L ≅ N,
          let O : X.Modules := SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf
          let f : O ⟶ L := L.unitHomEquiv.symm (Stacks.Divisors.canonicalSections D)
          let g : L ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N :=
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction i).unit.app L ≫
              (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).map e.hom
          ∃ h : f ≫ g = 0, (ShortComplex.mk f g h).ShortExact) ∧
      ∃ hz : Stacks.IdealSheafSequence.divisorIdealMap D ≫
          Stacks.IdealSheafSequence.divisorQuotientMap D = 0,
        (ShortComplex.mk (Stacks.IdealSheafSequence.divisorIdealMap D)
          (Stacks.IdealSheafSequence.divisorQuotientMap D) hz).ShortExact)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_cokernelIso_unit_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
For an invertible module `L` on a scheme `X` and a global section `s`, the unit of the
pullback–pushforward adjunction along the inclusion `i` of the zero scheme `Z(s)` realizes
`i_* i^* L` as the cokernel of multiplication by `s`.

No regularity hypothesis on `s` is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cokernelIso_unit_zeroScheme (s : L.sections) :
    let i := (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι
    ∃ e : cokernel (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L),
      cokernel.π (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) ≫ e.hom =
        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction i).unit.app L
declarations.comment: regular_section_sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.shortExact_zeroScheme_of_isRegularSection
declarations.doc:
For an invertible module `L` on a scheme `X` and a regular global section `s`
([Stacks, Tag 01WY]), the sequence `0 ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ L ⟶ i_* i^* L ⟶ 0` is short exact, where `i` is the
inclusion of the zero scheme of `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_zeroScheme_of_isRegularSection (s : L.sections)
    (hs : IsRegularSection X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property s) :
    let i := (zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι
    let O : X.Modules := SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf
    let f : O ⟶ L := L.unitHomEquiv.symm s
    let g : L ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj L) :=
      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction i).unit.app L
    ∃ h : f ≫ g = 0, (ShortComplex.mk f g h).ShortExact
declarations.comment: regular_section_sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealSheafSequence.divisorIdeal_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0C6K, the label `divisor_ideal_sequence`.** For a closed subscheme `D` of a
scheme `X` with inclusion `i`, the canonical sequence `0 ⟶ ℐ_D ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ i_* 𝒪_D ⟶ 0` of sheaves
of `𝒪_X`-modules is short exact.

The effective-Cartier hypothesis of Tag 0C6K is not used: it is what makes `ℐ_D` the invertible
module `𝒪_X(-D)`, and the exactness of the sequence does not depend on it.
declarations.statement:
theorem divisorIdeal_shortExact :
    ∃ hz : divisorIdealMap D ≫ divisorQuotientMap D = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (divisorIdealMap D) (divisorQuotientMap D) hz).ShortExact
declarations.comment: divisor_ideal_sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag0C6KSectionIdeal.exists_cokernelIso_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**The first assertion of Stacks Tag 0C6K's label `regular_section_sequence`.** For `L` an
invertible `𝒪_X`-module and `s` a global section of `L`, the restriction map
`L ⟶ i_* (L|_{Z(s)})` to the zero scheme of `s` *is* the cokernel of multiplication by `s`,
compatibly with the cokernel projection. No regularity of `s` is used, as in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cokernelIso_zeroScheme (L : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : L.sections) :
    ∃ e : cokernel (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) ≅
        (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.zeroScheme X L
            (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι.toRingCatSheafHom).obj
          ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.zeroScheme X L
            (s.eval (op ⊤))).subschemeι.toRingCatSheafHom).obj L),
      cokernel.π (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s) ≫ e.hom =
        Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.restrictionUnit
          (Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))) L
declarations.comment: regular_section_sequence

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag0C6KSectionIdeal.shortExact_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**The second assertion of Stacks Tag 0C6K's label `regular_section_sequence`.** For `s` a
*regular* global section of an invertible module — regularity being monicity of multiplication by
`s`, which is Stacks Tag 01WY and is literally the hypothesis below — the sequence
`0 ⟶ 𝒪_X ⟶ L ⟶ i_* (L|_{Z(s)}) ⟶ 0` is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_zeroScheme (L : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L] (s : L.sections)
    [Mono (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s)] :
    ∃ h : L.unitHomEquiv.symm s ≫ Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.restrictionUnit
        (Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))) L = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (L.unitHomEquiv.symm s)
        (Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.restrictionUnit
          (Stacks.RegularSectionSequence.zeroScheme X L (s.eval (op ⊤))) L) h).ShortExact
declarations.comment: regular_section_sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTrivial_of_genus_eq_zero_of_invertibleCurveDegree_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper curve over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`. If `X` has genus `0`, then
every invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` of degree `0` is trivial.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTrivial_of_genus_eq_zero_of_invertibleCurveDegree_eq_zero [IsCurve k f]
    [IsProper f] [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)] (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (hgenus : genus f = 0)
    (hdeg : invertibleCurveDegree k f
      (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (k := k) (f := f)).le L = 0) :
    SheafOfModules.IsTrivial X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_planeCurveData_deg_two_of_isGorenstein
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper curve over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`. If `X` is Gorenstein and
has genus `0`, then `X` is isomorphic over `k` to a plane curve of degree `2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_planeCurveData_deg_two_of_isGorenstein [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)] [IsGorenstein X]
    (hgenus : genus f = 0) :
    ∃ C : ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.PlaneCurveData k, C.deg = 2 ∧
      ∃ e : X ≅ C.Z, e.hom ≫ C.toSpec = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isField_and_finite_globalSections
declarations.doc:
For a proper scheme over a field which is reduced and connected, the ring of global sections
is a finite field extension of the base field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_and_finite_globalSections (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsReduced X] [ConnectedSpace X] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    IsField Γ(X, ⊤) ∧ Module.Finite k Γ(X, ⊤)
declarations.comment: the global sections are a finite field extension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_globalSections_dvd_curveDegree
declarations.doc:
For a proper scheme over a field which is reduced and connected and of dimension at most one,
the degree of the extension `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)/k` divides the degree of every finite locally free sheaf
of constant rank on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_globalSections_dvd_curveDegree (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsReduced X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (rank : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E rank] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    (Module.finrank k Γ(X, ⊤) : ℤ) ∣ curveDegree k f hdim E rank
declarations.comment: w divides the degree of a finite locally free sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_globalSections_dvd_finrank_residueField
declarations.doc:
For a proper scheme over a field which is reduced and connected, the degree of the extension
`Γ(X, 𝒪_X)/k` divides the degree over `k` of the residue field at every point.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_globalSections_dvd_finrank_residueField (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsReduced X] [ConnectedSpace X] (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra k (X.residueField x) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation x).hom.toAlgebra
    Module.finrank k Γ(X, ⊤) ∣ Module.finrank k (X.residueField x)
declarations.comment: w divides the degree of a residue field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_globalSections_dvd_finrank_globalSections_of_dimension_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field which is reduced and connected and let `D ⊆ X` be a
closed subscheme of dimension zero. Then `D` is finite locally free over `k` of rank
`dim_k Γ(D, 𝒪_D)`, and the degree of the extension `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)/k` divides it.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_globalSections_dvd_finrank_globalSections_of_dimension_zero (k : Type u)
    [Field k] {X D : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsReduced X]
    [ConnectedSpace X] (i : D ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (hdimD : topologicalKrullDim D = 0) :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra k Γ(D, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (i ≫ f).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (i ≫ f) (Module.finrank k Γ(D, ⊤)) ∧
      Module.finrank k Γ(X, ⊤) ∣ Module.finrank k Γ(D, ⊤)
declarations.comment: w divides the degree of a zero-dimensional closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.thickeningShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
The sequence of sheaves `0 ⟶ ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_{X'}^* ⟶ i_* 𝒪_X^* ⟶ 0` of a first-order thickening is
short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem thickeningShortComplex_shortExact (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) :
    (thickeningShortComplex i hi).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the short exact sequence of sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.injective_idealToUnitsCohomology_zero
declarations.doc:
The sequence starts with an injection: a global section of the ideal sheaf giving the unit
`1` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_idealToUnitsCohomology_zero (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) :
    Function.Injective (idealToUnitsCohomology i hi 0)
declarations.comment: injectivity at the global sections of the ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.exact_idealToUnitsCohomology
declarations.doc: Exactness at `H^n(X', 𝒪_{X'}^*)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_idealToUnitsCohomology (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Exact (idealToUnitsCohomology i hi n) (unitsToSubCohomology i n)
declarations.comment: exactness at the cohomology of the units of the thickening

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.exact_unitsToSubCohomology
declarations.doc: Exactness at `H^n(X, 𝒪_X^*)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_unitsToSubCohomology (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i)
    (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Exact (unitsToSubCohomology i n) (thickeningBoundary i hi n)
declarations.comment: exactness at the cohomology of the units of the closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.exact_thickeningBoundary
declarations.doc: Exactness at `H^{n+1}(X, ℐ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_thickeningBoundary (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Exact (thickeningBoundary i hi n) (idealToUnitsCohomology i hi (n + 1))
declarations.comment: exactness at the cohomology of the ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.exact_picardOfIdeal
declarations.doc: Exactness at `Pic(X')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_picardOfIdeal (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) :
    Function.Exact (picardOfIdeal i hi) (picardRestriction i hi)
declarations.comment: exactness at the Picard group of the thickening

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.exact_picardRestriction
declarations.doc: Exactness at `Pic(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_picardRestriction (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsFirstOrderThickening i) :
    Function.Exact (picardRestriction i hi) (picardBoundary i hi)
declarations.comment: exactness at the Picard group of the closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.unitsKernelShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6R** for an arbitrary thickening: the sequence of sheaves
`0 ⟶ 𝒦 ⟶ 𝒪_{X'}^* ⟶ i_* 𝒪_X^* ⟶ 0` is short exact, where `𝒦` is the kernel of restriction of
units, i.e. the sheaf of units congruent to `1` modulo the ideal of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem unitsKernelShortComplex_shortExact (i : X ⟶ X') (hi : IsThickening i) :
    (unitsKernelShortComplex i).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the short exact sequence of sheaves, for an arbitrary thickening, with the sheaf of units congruent to one presented as a kernel

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.bijOn_schemePullbackClass_zsmulTorsion_of_globalUnitsPowerLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6S** in its corrected form (an erratum to the printed statement).
For a thickening `i : X ⟶ X'` and an integer `n` invertible in `𝒪_X`, assuming every invertible
global function on `X` is an `n`-th power times the restriction of an invertible global function
on `X'`, restriction of invertible modules is a bijection `Pic(X')[n] → Pic(X)[n]`.

The original statement omitted that assumption and is refuted by
`Stacks.Examples.TwistedDoubledLine.not_forall_bijOn_schemePullbackClass_zsmulTorsion`; the
assumption is not merely sufficient but necessary, by
`Stacks.Thickenings.bijOn_schemePullbackClass_zsmulTorsion_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_schemePullbackClass_zsmulTorsion_of_globalUnitsPowerLift (i : X ⟶ X')
    (hi : IsThickening i) {n : ℤ} (hn : IsUnit ((n : ℤ) : Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (hpow : GlobalUnitsPowerLift i n) :
    Set.BijOn (schemePullbackClass i) (zsmulTorsion (ofScheme X') n)
      (zsmulTorsion (ofScheme X) n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cohomologyOverField_one_of_genus_zero_of_degree_pos
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C6T]: the vanishing `H¹(X, ℒ) = 0` of assertion (1).** Let `X` be a proper
curve over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and genus zero, and let `ℒ` be an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module of positive degree. Then `H¹(X, ℒ) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cohomologyOverField_one_of_genus_zero_of_degree_pos [IsProper f]
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (L : X.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hgenus : genus f = 0) (hpos : 0 < invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L) :
    IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f L 1)
declarations.comment: part (1), the clause `dim_k H¹(X, ℒ) = 0`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_eq_degree_add_one_of_genus_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C6T]: the dimension count `dim_k H⁰(X, ℒ) = d + 1` of assertion (1).** On a
proper curve over a field with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and genus zero, an invertible module `ℒ` whose
degree `d` is positive has `dim_k H⁰(X, ℒ) = d + 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_eq_degree_add_one_of_genus_zero
    [IsProper f] [IsIntegral X] [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hgenus : genus f = 0) (hpos : 0 < invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L) :
    (Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k f L 0) : ℤ) =
      invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L + 1
declarations.comment: part (1), the clause `dim_k H⁰(X, ℒ) = d + 1`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativelyVeryAmple_and_isClosedImmersion_of_basis
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0C6T] part (2).** Let `X` be a proper integral scheme of dimension at most one
over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and genus `0`, and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module of
degree `d > 0`. Then `ℒ` is very ample over `k`, and for every basis `s₀, …, s_d` of `H⁰(X, ℒ)` the
sections generate `ℒ` and the morphism `φ_{(ℒ, (s₀, …, s_d))} : X ⟶ 𝐏^d_k` they define is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_and_isClosedImmersion_of_basis [IsProper f] [IsIntegral X]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (hgenus : genus f = 0) (L : X.Modules) [Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule X L] {d : ℕ}
    (hdeg : invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L = d) (hd : 0 < d)
    (b : Module.Basis (Fin (d + 1)) k ((restrictScalarsOverBase k f).obj
      ((SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op (⊤ : X.Opens))).obj L))) :
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple f L ∧
      ∃ hs : GeneratesStalks (fun j => (show Γ(L, ⊤) from b j)),
        IsClosedImmersion (Stacks.ProjectiveSpaceChartRatio.toPolynomialModel
          (fun j => (show Γ(L, ⊤) from b j)) hs f)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveLine_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLine_tfae [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f] :
    List.TFAE [
      ∃ e : X ≅ AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjPolyChart.polyGrading k 1),
        e.hom ≫ Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjPolyChart.projToSpecCoeff k 1 = f,
      Smooth f ∧ GeometricallyIrreducible f ∧ genus f = 0 ∧
        ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
          Odd (invertibleCurveDegree k f (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)).le L),
      GeometricallyIntegral f ∧ genus f = 0 ∧ IsGorenstein X ∧
        ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
          Odd (invertibleCurveDegree k f (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)).le L),
      IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop) ∧ genus f = 0 ∧ IsGorenstein X ∧
        ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
          Odd (invertibleCurveDegree k f (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)).le L),
      GeometricallyIntegral f ∧ genus f = 0 ∧
        ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
          invertibleCurveDegree k f (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)).le L = 1,
      IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop) ∧ genus f = 0 ∧
        ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
          invertibleCurveDegree k f (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)).le L = 1,
      IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 1) ∧
        ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
          invertibleCurveDegree k f (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)).le L = 1,
      IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 1) ∧
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X), (∀ i, IsClosed ({x i} : Set X)) ∧
          (∀ i, IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk (x i))) ∧
          Finset.univ.gcd (fun i => letI : Algebra k (X.residueField (x i)) :=
              ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation (x i)).hom.toAlgebra
            Module.finrank k (X.residueField (x i))) = 1]
declarations.comment: the final item (9) of the source is the placeholder `add more here`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveLineCriterion.projectiveLine_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveLine_tfae [IsProper f] [IsCurve k f] :
    List.TFAE
      [Nonempty (Over.mk f ≅
          Over.mk (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k))),
        Smooth f ∧ GeometricallyIrreducible f ∧ genus f = 0 ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
            Odd (invertibleCurveDegree k f
              (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f))) L),
        GeometricallyIntegral f ∧ genus f = 0 ∧ IsGorenstein X ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
            Odd (invertibleCurveDegree k f
              (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f))) L),
        IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop) ∧ genus f = 0 ∧ IsGorenstein X ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
            Odd (invertibleCurveDegree k f
              (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f))) L),
        GeometricallyIntegral f ∧ genus f = 0 ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
            invertibleCurveDegree k f (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)))
              L = 1,
        IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop) ∧ genus f = 0 ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
            invertibleCurveDegree k f (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)))
              L = 1,
        IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 1) ∧
          ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
            invertibleCurveDegree k f (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := f)))
              L = 1,
        IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 1) ∧
          ∃ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → X), (∀ i, IsClosed ({x i} : Set X)) ∧
            (∀ i, IsNormalRing (X.presheaf.stalk (x i))) ∧
            Finset.univ.gcd (fun i => letI : Algebra k (X.residueField (x i)) :=
                ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation (x i)).hom.toAlgebra
              Module.finrank k (X.residueField (x i))) = 1]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveLineCriterion.exists_iso_projectiveLine_of_invertibleCurveDegree_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**A genus-zero curve with an invertible module of degree one is isomorphic to `ℙ¹_k` over
`k`.** Let `X` be a proper integral scheme of dimension at most one over a field `k` with
`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and genus `0`, and let `ℒ` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module of degree `1`. Then
`X ≅ ℙ¹_k` as schemes over `k`. The isomorphism is the morphism of a basis of `H⁰(X, ℒ)`
(`exists_iso_proj_of_invertibleCurveDegree_eq_one`), read in the base-change model
`ℙ¹_k = Spec k ×_{Spec ℤ} ℙ¹_ℤ` through
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjBaseChange.polynomialComparison`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_projectiveLine_of_invertibleCurveDegree_eq_one [IsProper f] [IsIntegral X]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (hgenus : genus f = 0) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L]
    (hdeg : invertibleCurveDegree k f hdim L = 1) :
    Nonempty (Over.mk f ≅ Over.mk (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)))
declarations.comment: condition (6) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_injective_to_discriminantGroup_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6V (left-hand map).**  The quotient by a saturated
submodule and its orthogonal complement injects into the discriminant group of
the submodule.  The cokernel of this injection is a quotient of the
discriminant group of the ambient lattice.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_injective_to_discriminantGroup_left
    {L : Type*} [AddCommGroup L] [Module.Free ℤ L] [Module.Finite ℤ L]
    (form : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ L) (hform_symm : form.IsSymm)
    (hform_pos : ∀ x : L, x ≠ 0 → 0 < form x x)
    (A : Submodule ℤ L) (hA : Module.IsTorsionFree ℤ (L ⧸ A)) :
    ∃ i : OrthogonalSumQuotient form A →ₗ[ℤ]
        SubmoduleDiscriminantGroup form A,
      Function.Injective i ∧
        ∃ q : DiscriminantGroup form →ₗ[ℤ]
            (SubmoduleDiscriminantGroup form A ⧸ LinearMap.range i),
          Function.Surjective q
declarations.comment: the map to the discriminant group of A

declarations.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_injective_to_discriminantGroup_orthogonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6V (right-hand map).**  The quotient by a saturated
submodule and its orthogonal complement injects into the discriminant group of
the orthogonal complement.  The cokernel of this injection is a quotient of
the discriminant group of the ambient lattice.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_injective_to_discriminantGroup_orthogonal
    {L : Type*} [AddCommGroup L] [Module.Free ℤ L] [Module.Finite ℤ L]
    (form : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ L) (hform_symm : form.IsSymm)
    (hform_pos : ∀ x : L, x ≠ 0 → 0 < form x x)
    (A : Submodule ℤ L) (hA : Module.IsTorsionFree ℤ (L ⧸ A)) :
    ∃ i : OrthogonalSumQuotient form A →ₗ[ℤ]
        SubmoduleDiscriminantGroup form (A.orthogonalBilin form),
      Function.Injective i ∧
        ∃ q : DiscriminantGroup form →ₗ[ℤ]
            (SubmoduleDiscriminantGroup form (A.orthogonalBilin form) ⧸
              LinearMap.range i),
          Function.Surjective q
declarations.comment: the map to the discriminant group of B

declarations.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.torsionCokernelEquiv_discriminantGroup_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C6W.** For a pair of adjoint maps of positive
definite integral lattices, when the form on the source is unimodular, the
torsion in the cokernel of `dStar.comp d` is isomorphic to the discriminant
group of the image lattice.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torsionCokernelEquiv_discriminantGroup_range
    {L₀ L₁ : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup L₀] [Module.Free ℤ L₀] [Module.Finite ℤ L₀]
    [AddCommGroup L₁] [Module.Free ℤ L₁] [Module.Finite ℤ L₁]
    (form₀ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ L₀) (form₁ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ L₁)
    (hform₀_symm : form₀.IsSymm) (hform₁_symm : form₁.IsSymm)
    (hform₀_pos : ∀ x : L₀, x ≠ 0 → 0 < form₀ x x)
    (hform₁_pos : ∀ x : L₁, x ≠ 0 → 0 < form₁ x x)
    (d : L₀ →ₗ[ℤ] L₁) (dStar : L₁ →ₗ[ℤ] L₀)
    (hadjoint : LinearMap.IsAdjointPair form₀ form₁ d dStar)
    (hunimodular : Function.Bijective form₀) :
    Nonempty
      (AddCommGroup.torsion (L₀ ⧸ LinearMap.range (dStar.comp d)) ≃ₗ[ℤ]
        SubmoduleDiscriminantGroup form₁ (LinearMap.range d))

declarations.name: Matrix.finrank_torsionBy_matrixCokernel_le_cycleRank
declarations.doc:
The prime torsion in the cokernel of a connected recurring symmetric
integer matrix has dimension at most the cycle rank of its support graph.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_torsionBy_matrixCokernel_le_cycleRank
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [LinearOrder ι] {A : Matrix ι ι ℤ}
    {m : ι → ℤ} {ℓ : ℕ} [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (hA : A.IsSymm)
    (hoffDiag : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → 0 ≤ A i j)
    (hm : ∀ i, 0 < m i)
    (hAm : A *ᵥ m = 0)
    (hconnected : ∀ I : Set ι, I.Nonempty → I ≠ Set.univ →
      ¬ ∀ i ∈ I, ∀ j ∉ I, A i j = 0)
    (hℓA : ∀ i j, 0 < A i j → IsCoprime (ℓ : ℤ) (A i j))
    (hℓm : ∀ i, IsCoprime (ℓ : ℤ) (m i)) :
    let C := (ι → ℤ) ⧸ LinearMap.range A.mulVecLin
    let T := AddSubgroup.torsionBy C (ℓ : ℤ)
    letI : Module (ZMod ℓ) T := AddSubgroup.torsionBy.zmodModule
    Module.finrank (ZMod ℓ) T + Fintype.card ι ≤
      1 + (Finset.univ.filter fun p : ι × ι => p.1 < p.2 ∧ 0 < A p.1 p.2).card

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType
declarations.doc:
A **numerical type**: positive integer multiplicities and weights, nonnegative component
genera, and a connected symmetric intersection matrix whose weighted rows vanish and whose entries
in each row are divisible by that row's weight.
declarations.statement: public structure NumericalType

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.Equivalent
declarations.doc:
Two numerical types are **equivalent** if a bijective relabelling of their components preserves
all four families of numerical data.
declarations.statement: public def Equivalent (T T' : NumericalType) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.cast_genus
declarations.doc:
The rational expression defining the genus of a numerical type is the image of
an integer.
declarations.statement:
public lemma cast_genus (T : NumericalType) :
    (genus T : ℚ) =
      1 + ∑ i, (T.multiplicity i : ℚ) *
        ((T.weight i : ℚ) * ((T.componentGenus i : ℚ) - 1) -
          (T.intersection i i : ℚ) / 2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.genus
declarations.doc: The integer genus of a numerical type.
declarations.statement: public def genus (T : NumericalType) : ℤ
declarations.comment: a numerical type of genus g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.intersection_self_eq_zero_of_componentCount_eq_one
declarations.doc: The diagonal intersection number of the unique component is zero.
declarations.statement:
public lemma intersection_self_eq_zero_of_componentCount_eq_one
    (T : NumericalType) (hT : T.componentCount = 1) :
    T.intersection ⟨0, T.componentCount_pos⟩ ⟨0, T.componentCount_pos⟩ = 0
declarations.comment: diagonal intersection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.genus_eq_of_componentCount_eq_one
declarations.doc: The genus formula for a one-component numerical type.
declarations.statement:
public lemma genus_eq_of_componentCount_eq_one (T : NumericalType)
    (hT : T.componentCount = 1) :
    genus T = 1 + T.multiplicity ⟨0, T.componentCount_pos⟩ *
      T.weight ⟨0, T.componentCount_pos⟩ *
        (T.componentGenus ⟨0, T.componentCount_pos⟩ - 1)
declarations.comment: genus formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.componentGenus_eq_zero_of_genus_neg
declarations.doc: In negative genus, the unique component has genus zero.
declarations.comment: negative genus component

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.irreducibleTypes_equiv_factorizations_of_genus_neg
declarations.doc:
In negative genus, one-component numerical types correspond exactly to
positive factorizations of `1 - g`, via multiplicity and weight.
declarations.statement:
public lemma irreducibleTypes_equiv_factorizations_of_genus_neg (g : ℤ) (hg : g < 0) :
    ∃ e : IrreducibleTypes g ≃
        {p : ℤ × ℤ // 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ p.1 * p.2 = 1 - g},
      ∀ T, (e T : ℤ × ℤ) =
        (T.1.multiplicity ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩,
          T.1.weight ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩)
declarations.comment: negative genus classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.finite_irreducibleTypes_of_genus_neg
declarations.doc:
For fixed negative genus there are only finitely many one-component
numerical types.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finite_irreducibleTypes_of_genus_neg (g : ℤ) (hg : g < 0) :
    Set.Finite {T : NumericalType | T.componentCount = 1 ∧ genus T = g}
declarations.comment: negative genus finiteness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.multiplicity_eq_one_of_genus_zero
declarations.doc: In genus zero, the unique multiplicity is one.
declarations.statement:
public lemma multiplicity_eq_one_of_genus_zero (T : IrreducibleTypes 0) :
    T.1.multiplicity ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩ = 1
declarations.comment: genus zero multiplicity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.weight_eq_one_of_genus_zero
declarations.doc: In genus zero, the unique weight is one.
declarations.statement:
public lemma weight_eq_one_of_genus_zero (T : IrreducibleTypes 0) :
    T.1.weight ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩ = 1
declarations.comment: genus zero weight

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.componentGenus_eq_zero_of_genus_zero
declarations.doc: In genus zero, the unique component has genus zero.
declarations.statement:
public lemma componentGenus_eq_zero_of_genus_zero (T : IrreducibleTypes 0) :
    T.1.componentGenus ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩ = 0
declarations.comment: genus zero component

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.componentGenus_eq_one_of_genus_one
declarations.doc: In genus one, the unique component has genus one.
declarations.statement:
public lemma componentGenus_eq_one_of_genus_one (T : IrreducibleTypes 1) :
    T.1.componentGenus ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩ = 1
declarations.comment: genus one component

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.irreducibleTypes_equiv_positive_pairs_of_genus_one
declarations.doc:
In genus one, multiplicity and weight range independently over all positive
integers.
declarations.statement:
public lemma irreducibleTypes_equiv_positive_pairs_of_genus_one :
    ∃ e : IrreducibleTypes 1 ≃ {p : ℤ × ℤ // 0 < p.1 ∧ 0 < p.2},
      ∀ T, (e T : ℤ × ℤ) =
        (T.1.multiplicity ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩,
          T.1.weight ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩)
declarations.comment: genus one classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.one_lt_componentGenus_of_one_lt_genus
declarations.doc: Above genus one, the unique component has genus greater than one.
declarations.comment: positive genus component

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.irreducibleTypes_equiv_factorizations_of_one_lt_genus
declarations.doc:
Above genus one, one-component numerical types correspond exactly to
positive three-factor factorizations of `g - 1`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma irreducibleTypes_equiv_factorizations_of_one_lt_genus (g : ℤ) (hg : 1 < g) :
    ∃ e : IrreducibleTypes g ≃
        {p : (ℤ × ℤ) × ℤ //
          0 < p.1.1 ∧ 0 < p.1.2 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ p.1.1 * p.1.2 * p.2 = g - 1},
      ∀ T, (e T : (ℤ × ℤ) × ℤ) =
        ((T.1.multiplicity ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩,
            T.1.weight ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩),
          T.1.componentGenus ⟨0, T.1.componentCount_pos⟩ - 1)
declarations.comment: positive genus classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.finite_irreducibleTypes_of_one_lt_genus
declarations.doc:
For fixed genus greater than one there are only finitely many one-component
numerical types.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finite_irreducibleTypes_of_one_lt_genus (g : ℤ) (hg : 1 < g) :
    Set.Finite {T : NumericalType | T.componentCount = 1 ∧ genus T = g}
declarations.comment: positive genus finiteness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.intersection_self_neg_of_one_lt_componentCount
declarations.doc:
Every diagonal intersection number of a numerical type with more than one
component is strictly negative.
declarations.statement:
public lemma intersection_self_neg_of_one_lt_componentCount
    (T : NumericalType) (hcomponentCount : 1 < T.componentCount)
    (i : Fin T.componentCount) :
    T.intersection i i < 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.componentGenus_eq_zero_of_contribution_neg
declarations.doc: A component with negative contribution to the genus has component genus zero.
declarations.statement:
public lemma componentGenus_eq_zero_of_contribution_neg
    (T : NumericalType) (hn : 1 < T.componentCount) (i : Fin T.componentCount)
    (hi : (T.multiplicity i : ℚ) *
      ((T.weight i : ℚ) * ((T.componentGenus i : ℚ) - 1) -
        (T.intersection i i : ℚ) / 2) < 0) :
    T.componentGenus i = 0
declarations.comment: component genus
