declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.not_exists_branched_chain_of_eight_minus_two_indices
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8N.** If a numerical type has more than eight
components, it has no eight distinct minus-two indices forming a seven-vertex
chain with an extra vertex joined to the fourth vertex.
declarations.statement:
public lemma not_exists_branched_chain_of_eight_minus_two_indices
    (T : NumericalType) (hcount : 8 < T.componentCount) :
    ¬ ∃ i : Fin 8 → Fin T.componentCount,
      Function.Injective i ∧
      (∀ r, IsMinusTwoIndex T (i r)) ∧
      T.intersection (i 0) (i 1) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 1) (i 2) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 2) (i 3) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 3) (i 4) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 4) (i 5) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 5) (i 6) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 7) (i 3) ≠ 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.not_exists_branched_chain_of_nine_minus_two_indices
declarations.doc:
If a numerical type has more than nine components, it has no nine distinct
minus-two indices forming an eight-vertex chain with an extra vertex joined to
the fifth vertex.

This is the configuration of the source's displayed *formula*: it asks for nine
distinct `(-2)`-indices `d, e, f, g, h, i, j, k, l` with
`a_{de}, a_{ef}, a_{fg}, a_{gh}, a_{hi}, a_{ij}, a_{jk}, a_{lh}` nonzero, so the
chain is `d - e - f - g - h - i - j - k` and the extra index `l` is joined to
`h`, the fifth vertex of that chain.  The source's displayed *diagram* instead
hangs the extra vertex below the sixth bullet of the chain; the two readings
differ, and `not_exists_branched_chain_of_nine_minus_two_indices_at_sixth` is
the diagram reading.
declarations.statement:
public lemma not_exists_branched_chain_of_nine_minus_two_indices
    (T : NumericalType) (hcount : 9 < T.componentCount) :
    ¬ ∃ i : Fin 9 → Fin T.componentCount,
      Function.Injective i ∧
      (∀ r, IsMinusTwoIndex T (i r)) ∧
      T.intersection (i 0) (i 1) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 1) (i 2) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 2) (i 3) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 3) (i 4) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 4) (i 5) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 5) (i 6) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 6) (i 7) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 8) (i 4) ≠ 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.not_exists_branched_chain_of_nine_minus_two_indices_at_sixth
declarations.doc:
The configuration drawn in the source's diagram, with the extra vertex
joined to the sixth vertex of the chain rather than the fifth: the affine Dynkin
diagram `Ẽ₈`, which likewise does not occur in a numerical type with more than
nine components.

The source's diagram and its displayed formula disagree about which chain vertex
carries the extra index: the diagram shows the sixth, the formula writes
`a_{lh}` with `h` the fifth; `not_exists_branched_chain_of_nine_minus_two_indices`
is the formula reading.
declarations.statement:
public lemma not_exists_branched_chain_of_nine_minus_two_indices_at_sixth
    (T : NumericalType) (hcount : 9 < T.componentCount) :
    ¬ ∃ i : Fin 9 → Fin T.componentCount,
      Function.Injective i ∧
      (∀ r, IsMinusTwoIndex T (i r)) ∧
      T.intersection (i 0) (i 1) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 1) (i 2) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 2) (i 3) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 3) (i 4) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 4) (i 5) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 5) (i 6) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 6) (i 7) ≠ 0 ∧
      T.intersection (i 8) (i 5) ≠ 0
declarations.comment: the configuration of the source's diagram, extra vertex at the sixth chain vertex rather than the fifth of the displayed formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.classify_connected_proper_minusTwo_subgraph
declarations.doc:
A connected proper subset of minus-two indices has, up to reordering, one
of the listed A, B, C, D, E, F, or G configurations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem classify_connected_proper_minusTwo_subgraph (T : NumericalType)
    (I : Finset (Fin T.componentCount))
    (hcard : 2 ≤ I.card) (hproper : I.card < T.componentCount)
    (hminus : ∀ i ∈ I, IsMinusTwoIndex T i)
    (hconnected : ¬ ∃ J : Finset (Fin T.componentCount),
      J.Nonempty ∧ J ⊂ I ∧
        (∀ i ∈ J, ∀ j ∈ I, j ∉ J → T.intersection i j = 0)) :
    ∃ v : Fin I.card → Fin T.componentCount,
      Function.Injective v ∧ Set.range v = (I : Set (Fin T.componentCount)) ∧
        ∃ (d : DynkinShape) (w : ℤ), IsDynkinConfiguration T v d w

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.componentCount_eq_one_of_isMinimal_of_genus_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A minimal numerical type of genus zero has exactly one component.
declarations.statement:
public lemma componentCount_eq_one_of_isMinimal_of_genus_eq_zero
    (T : NumericalType) (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (hgenus : genus T = 0) :
    T.componentCount = 1
declarations.comment: component count

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.existsUnique_minimal_genus_zero
declarations.doc: There is exactly one minimal numerical type of genus zero.
declarations.statement:
public lemma existsUnique_minimal_genus_zero :
    ∃! T : NumericalType, IsMinimal T ∧ genus T = 0
declarations.comment: existence and uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.data_of_isMinimal_of_genus_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The minimal numerical type of genus zero, explicitly: a minimal numerical
type of genus zero has a single component, of multiplicity one, self-intersection
number zero, weight one and component genus zero. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.existsUnique_minimal_genus_zero` this identifies
the only minimal numerical type of genus zero as `n = 1`, `m₁ = 1`, `a₁₁ = 0`,
`w₁ = 1`, `g₁ = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma data_of_isMinimal_of_genus_eq_zero
    (T : NumericalType) (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (hgenus : genus T = 0) :
    T.componentCount = 1 ∧ (∀ i, T.multiplicity i = 1) ∧
      (∀ i j, T.intersection i j = 0) ∧ (∀ i, T.weight i = 1) ∧
      (∀ i, T.componentGenus i = 0)
declarations.comment: explicit numerical type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_neighborCount_le_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T** for a numerical type each of whose components meets at most two
others. With at least five components it is minimal of genus one exactly when it is the cycle —
case (16) for five components and case (25) for six or more — or one of the chains: cases (17)
to (21) for five components, and cases (26), (27) and (28) for six or more. From six components
on, which of the three chains occurs is decided by the two end weights: both twice the interior
weight gives (28), one half and one twice gives (26), both half gives (27), and an end weight
equal to the interior weight is impossible.
declarations.comment: the classification when every component meets at most two others and there are at least five of them: the cycle, cases (16) and (25), and the chains, cases (17)-(21) for five components and cases (26), (27) and (28) for six or more

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_of_isGenusOneConfiguration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T**, the direction from the list to minimality and genus one.
Every configuration on the genus-one list is a minimal numerical type of genus one.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_of_isGenusOneConfiguration (T : NumericalType)
    (h : IsGenusOneConfiguration T) : IsMinimal T ∧ genus T = 1
declarations.comment: every numerical type on the list is minimal of genus one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_componentCount_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T**, case (1). A numerical type with a single component is
minimal of genus one exactly when it is the one-component genus-one configuration: diagonal
intersection number zero, component genus one, and arbitrary positive multiplicity and
weight.
declarations.comment: the classification for one component, case (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_componentCount_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T**, cases (2) and (3). A numerical type with two components is
minimal of genus one exactly when it is one of the first two exceptional configurations.
declarations.comment: the classification for two components, cases (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_componentCount_eq_four
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T**, cases (10)-(15). A numerical type with four components is
minimal of genus one exactly when it is one of the six four-component exceptional
configurations: the affine cycle, the three affine chains and the two affine forks.
declarations.comment: the classification for four components, cases (10)-(15)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_componentCount_eq_three
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T**, cases (4)-(9). A numerical type with three components is
minimal of genus one exactly when it is one of the six three-component exceptional
configurations: the affine cycle and the five affine chains.
declarations.comment: the classification for three components, cases (4)-(9)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_two_le_neighborCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T** for a numerical type each of whose components meets at least
two others and which has at least five components: it is minimal of genus one exactly when it
is the `n`-cycle, case (16) for five components and case (25) for six or more.
declarations.comment: the classification when every component meets at least two others and there are at least five of them: the n-cycle, case (16) for five components and case (25) for six or more

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_affine_extension_of_three_le_neighborCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T**, the reduction for a component meeting three or more others.
In a minimal numerical type of genus one with at least five components, one of which meets three
or more others, some component `l` meets exactly one other component `x`; the remaining
components carry a Dynkin configuration `v` of shape `d` and scale `w` with `x = v r₀`, their
multiplicities are annihilated by the weighted Cartan matrix of `d` away from `r₀` and satisfy
`2 (M m)_{r₀} = k wf(r₀) m_{r₀}` there; and the shape, the attachment vertex and the level are
one of seven explicit possibilities.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_affine_extension_of_three_le_neighborCount (T : NumericalType)
    (hmin : IsMinimal T) (hgenus : genus T = 1) (hn : 5 ≤ T.componentCount)
    (i₀ : Fin T.componentCount) (hdeg : 3 ≤ neighborCount T i₀) :
    ∃ (l x : Fin T.componentCount) (t : ℕ) (v : Fin t → Fin T.componentCount)
      (d : DynkinShape) (w : ℤ) (r₀ : Fin t) (k : ℤ),
      t + 1 = T.componentCount ∧ l ≠ x ∧
        (∀ y, y ≠ l → T.intersection l y ≠ 0 → y = x) ∧
        Function.Injective v ∧ (∀ r, v r ≠ l) ∧ (∀ y, y ≠ l → ∃ r, v r = y) ∧
        IsDynkinConfiguration T v d w ∧ v r₀ = x ∧
        (∀ r, r ≠ r₀ → ∑ s, d.weightedCartan r s * T.multiplicity (v s) = 0) ∧
        2 * ∑ s, d.weightedCartan r₀ s * T.multiplicity (v s)
          = k * d.weightFactor r₀ * T.multiplicity (v r₀) ∧
        ((d = .D ∧ ((r₀.val = 0 ∧ k = 2) ∨ (r₀.val = 1 ∧ k = 1) ∨
              ((r₀.val + 1 = t ∨ r₀.val + 2 = t) ∧ k * t = 8))) ∨
          (d = .B ∧ r₀.val = 1 ∧ k = 1) ∨ (d = .C ∧ r₀.val = 1 ∧ k = 1) ∨
          (d = .A ∧ k = 1 ∧ ((t = 7 ∧ r₀.val = 3) ∨ (t = 8 ∧ (r₀.val = 2 ∨ r₀.val = 5)))) ∨
          (d = .E6 ∧ r₀.val = 5 ∧ k = 1) ∨ (d = .E7 ∧ r₀.val = 5 ∧ k = 1) ∨
          (d = .E8 ∧ r₀.val = 0 ∧ k = 1))
declarations.comment: the reduction for at least five components one of which meets three or more others — cases (22), (23), (24), (29), (30), (31), (32), (33) and (34): deleting a component that meets exactly one other leaves a Dynkin configuration whose shape, attachment vertex and level are one of seven explicit possibilities

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_three_le_neighborCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T** for a numerical type with at least five components one of
which meets three or more others: it is minimal of genus one exactly when it is one of the forks
and stars on the list, cases (22), (23), (24), (29), (30), (31), (32), (33) and (34).
declarations.comment: the classification when some component meets three or more others and there are at least five of them: cases (22), (23) and (24) for five components, the unbounded fork families (29), (30) and (31) for six or more, and the exceptional configurations (32), (33) and (34) on seven, eight and nine components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff_of_five_le_componentCount
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T** for five or more components. A numerical type with at least
five components is minimal of genus one exactly when it is one of the configurations on the
list. Whether some component meets three or more others decides which half of the list it lies
in: if none does, the type is the cycle or one of the chains — cases (16) to (21) for five
components and cases (25) to (28) for six or more — and otherwise it is one of the forks and
stars, cases (22), (23), (24), (29), (30), (31), (32), (33) and (34).
declarations.comment: the classification for at least five components: cases (16)-(34)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C8T.** A numerical type is minimal of genus one exactly when it is
one of the thirty-four configurations of the list: the single component of genus one, case (1);
the twenty-six exceptional coefficient tables on two to nine components, cases (2)-(24) and
(32)-(34); and the seven unbounded families on six or more, cases (25)-(31).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMinimal_and_genus_eq_one_iff (T : NumericalType) :
    (IsMinimal T ∧ genus T = 1) ↔ IsGenusOneConfiguration T
declarations.comment: the classification: a numerical type is minimal of genus one exactly when it is one of the thirty-four configurations listed, cases (1)-(34)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.multiplicity_mul_intersection_le
declarations.doc:
A positive intersection with a component is bounded, after multiplication by
its multiplicity, by the absolute diagonal contribution of the other component.
declarations.statement:
public lemma multiplicity_mul_intersection_le (T : NumericalType)
    (i j : Fin T.componentCount) (hij : 0 < T.intersection i j) :
    T.multiplicity i * T.intersection i j ≤
      T.multiplicity j * |T.intersection j j|
declarations.comment: intersection bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.multiplicity_mul_weight_le
declarations.doc:
The multiplicity-weight product of a component meeting another component is
bounded by the latter component's absolute diagonal contribution.
declarations.statement:
public lemma multiplicity_mul_weight_le (T : NumericalType)
    (i j : Fin T.componentCount) (hij : 0 < T.intersection i j) :
    T.multiplicity i * T.weight i ≤
      T.multiplicity j * |T.intersection j j|
declarations.comment: weight bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.multiplicity_mul_abs_intersection_self_le
declarations.doc:
At a non-minus-two index of a minimal numerical type of genus at least two,
the multiplicity times the absolute diagonal intersection is at most six times
the genus minus six.
declarations.statement:
public lemma multiplicity_mul_abs_intersection_self_le
    (T : NumericalType) (g : ℤ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (hgenus : genus T = g)
    (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (hn : 1 < T.componentCount)
    (j : Fin T.componentCount) (hj : ¬ IsMinusTwoIndex T j) :
    T.multiplicity j * |T.intersection j j| ≤ 6 * g - 6
declarations.comment: bound_diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.card_non_minus_two_indices_le
declarations.doc:
A minimal numerical type with more than one component has at most twice its
genus minus two non-minus-two indices.
declarations.statement:
public lemma card_non_minus_two_indices_le
    (T : NumericalType) (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (hn : 1 < T.componentCount) :
    ((Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin T.componentCount => ¬ IsMinusTwoIndex T i)).card : ℤ) ≤
      2 * genus T - 2
declarations.comment: bound_non_minus_two_indices

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.multiplicity_mul_intersection_le_genus
declarations.doc:
The multiplicity-weighted intersection with a non-minus-two component of a
minimal numerical type is at most six times its genus minus six.
declarations.statement:
public lemma multiplicity_mul_intersection_le_genus
    (T : NumericalType) (g : ℤ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (hgenus : genus T = g)
    (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (hn : 1 < T.componentCount)
    (i j : Fin T.componentCount) (hj : ¬ IsMinusTwoIndex T j) :
    T.multiplicity i * T.intersection i j ≤ 6 * g - 6
declarations.comment: bound_off_diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.componentGenus_lt_genus
declarations.doc:
A non-minus-two component of a minimal numerical type of genus at least two
has genus strictly less than that of the numerical type.
declarations.statement:
public lemma componentGenus_lt_genus
    (T : NumericalType) (g : ℤ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (hgenus : genus T = g)
    (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (hn : 1 < T.componentCount)
    (j : Fin T.componentCount) (hj : ¬ IsMinusTwoIndex T j) :
    T.componentGenus j < g
declarations.comment: component_genus_lt

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.multiplicity_mul_abs_intersection_le
declarations.doc:
For a minimal numerical type of genus at least two, each multiplicity-weighted
absolute intersection is at most 768 times its genus.
declarations.statement:
public lemma multiplicity_mul_abs_intersection_le
    (T : NumericalType) (g : ℤ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (hgenus : genus T = g)
    (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (i j : Fin T.componentCount) :
    T.multiplicity i * |T.intersection i j| ≤ 768 * g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.finrank_picardGroup_torsionBy_le_genus
declarations.doc:
The prime torsion of the Picard group of a numerical type has dimension
at most its genus, provided the prime exceeds 768 times the genus.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finrank_picardGroup_torsionBy_le_genus
    (T : NumericalType) (g : ℤ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (hgenus : genus T = g)
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hℓ : 768 * g < (ℓ : ℤ)) :
    let P := AddSubgroup.torsionBy (picardGroup T) (ℓ : ℤ)
    let : Module (ZMod ℓ) P := AddSubgroup.torsionBy.zmodModule
    (Module.finrank (ZMod ℓ) P : ℤ) ≤ g
declarations.comment: genus bound

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.finrank_picardGroup_torsionBy_le_topGenus_of_isMinimal
declarations.doc:
For a minimal numerical type, the topological genus bounds the dimension
of the prime torsion of its Picard group.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finrank_picardGroup_torsionBy_le_topGenus_of_isMinimal
    (T : NumericalType) (g : ℤ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (hgenus : genus T = g)
    (hminimal : IsMinimal T) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (hℓ : 768 * g < (ℓ : ℤ)) :
    let P := AddSubgroup.torsionBy (picardGroup T) (ℓ : ℤ)
    let : Module (ZMod ℓ) P := AddSubgroup.torsionBy.zmodModule
    (Module.finrank (ZMod ℓ) P : ℤ) ≤
      (1 : ℤ) - T.componentCount + edgeCount T
declarations.comment: topological genus bound for minimal types

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.topGenus_le_genus_of_isMinimal
declarations.doc:
The topological genus of a minimal numerical type of genus at least two
does not exceed its genus.
declarations.statement:
public lemma topGenus_le_genus_of_isMinimal
    (T : NumericalType) (g : ℤ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) (hgenus : genus T = g)
    (hminimal : IsMinimal T) :
    (1 : ℤ) - T.componentCount + edgeCount T ≤ g
declarations.comment: topological genus at most genus

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.existsUnique_exceptionalContractionSequence_of_isMinimalModel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0C9Z.** Let `C` be a smooth projective curve over `K` with
`H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K` and genus `> 0`, let `X` be the minimal model of `C` and let `Y` be a regular
proper model of `C`. Then there is a unique morphism of models `Y ⟶ X` which is a sequence of
contractions of exceptional curves of the first kind.

A morphism of models is a morphism over `R` compatible with the identifications of the generic
fibres with `C`; "a sequence of contractions" is a sequence `Y = Xₘ → ⋯ → X₀` of contractions of
exceptional curves of the first kind between regular proper models of `C`
(`Stacks.Models.ExceptionalContractionSequence`), followed by an isomorphism of `X₀` with `X`
over `R`. The morphism is unique among all morphisms of models, and is a sequence of contractions
by [Stacks, Tag 0CD9] and [Stacks, Tag 0C6B].
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_exceptionalContractionSequence_of_isMinimalModel {C X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (hg : 0 < genus c)
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (eX : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))))
    (hX : IsMinimalModel c p eX) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    (eY : C ≅ pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))))
    (hmod : IsModel c q eY) [IsProper q] (hreg : IsRegular Y) :
    ∃! f : Y ⟶ X, (f ≫ p = q ∧
      eY.hom ≫ pullback.fst q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ≫ f =
        eX.hom ≫ pullback.fst p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))) ∧
      ∃ (X₀ : Scheme.{u}) (p₀ : X₀ ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (g : Y ⟶ X₀) (ψ : X₀ ≅ X),
        ExceptionalContractionSequence c q p₀ g ∧ ψ.hom ≫ p = p₀ ∧ g ≫ ψ.hom = f

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.GenusZero.minimalModel_not_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CA0: in genus zero, minimal models are not unique.** Let `R` be a
discrete valuation ring with fraction field `K`, residue field `k` and uniformizer `π`, and let
`X = Proj R[T₀, T₁, T₂]/(T₁T₂ - πT₀²)`.

1. `X` is a closed subscheme of `ℙ²_R`, regular and proper over `R`, and a model of `ℙ¹_K`, its
   generic fibre being identified with `ℙ¹_K` by `[u : v] ↦ [uv : v² : πu²]`.
2. The special fibre of `X` is the union, and as a divisor the sum, of the lines
   `C₁ = V(π, T₁)` and `C₂ = V(π, T₂)`; each is a copy of `ℙ¹_k` and an exceptional curve of the
   first kind on `X`. In particular `X` is not a minimal model.
3. The projection `[T₂ : T₀]` from `(0 : 1 : 0)` is a morphism of models from `X` to `ℙ¹_R` with
   the identification `e₂` of its generic fibre twisted by `[u : v] ↦ [πu : v]`; it contracts
   `C₂` to a `k`-point and maps `C₁` isomorphically onto the special fibre of `ℙ¹_R`. The
   projection `[T₀ : T₁]` from `(0 : 0 : 1)` is a morphism of models from `X` to `ℙ¹_R` with the
   canonical identification `e₁`; it contracts `C₁` and maps `C₂` isomorphically onto the special
   fibre of `ℙ¹_R`.
4. `(ℙ¹_R, e₁)` and `(ℙ¹_R, e₂)` are minimal models of `ℙ¹_K`, and no isomorphism of models
   relates them.
declarations.statement:
theorem minimalModel_not_unique (hπ : Irreducible π) :
    -- (1) `X ⊆ ℙ²_R` is a regular proper model of `ℙ¹_K`
    IsClosedImmersion (PlaneCurveModel.embedding (conicEquation π)
      (isHomogeneous_conicEquation π)) ∧
    IsRegular (conicScheme π) ∧ IsProper (conicToSpec π) ∧
    IsModel (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of K) ↘ Spec (.of K)) (conicToSpec π)
      (conicGenericFibreIso (K := K) hπ) ∧
    -- (2) the special fibre is `C₁ + C₂`, two exceptional curves of the first kind
    Set.range (pullback.fst (conicToSpec π) (residueSpecMap R)) =
      Set.range (firstLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ)) ∪
        Set.range (secondLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ)) ∧
    (pullback.fst (conicToSpec π) (residueSpecMap R)).ker =
      (firstLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ)).ker *
        (secondLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ)).ker ∧
    (firstLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ)).ker.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κ
      (firstLineIso hπ) ∧
    (secondLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ)).ker.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κ
      (secondLineIso hπ) ∧
    (conicScheme π).HasExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind ∧
    -- (3) the projection from `(0 : 1 : 0)` contracts `C₂` and maps `C₁` onto the special fibre
    IsModelHom (conicToSpec π) (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R))
      (conicGenericFibreIso (K := K) hπ) (twistedGenericFibreIso (K := K) hπ) (secondProjection π) ∧
    (∃ q : Spec (.of κ) ⟶ projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R),
      secondLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ) ≫ secondProjection π =
        projToSpecCoeff κ 1 ≫ q) ∧
    (∃ e : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (lineGrading κ) ≅
        pullback (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R)) (residueSpecMap R),
      firstLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ) ≫ secondProjection π =
        e.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _) ∧
    -- the projection from `(0 : 0 : 1)` contracts `C₁` and maps `C₂` onto the special fibre
    IsModelHom (conicToSpec π) (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R))
      (conicGenericFibreIso (K := K) hπ) (projectiveLineGenericFibreIso (K := K))
      (firstProjection π) ∧
    (∃ q : Spec (.of κ) ⟶ projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R),
      firstLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ) ≫ firstProjection π =
        projToSpecCoeff κ 1 ≫ q) ∧
    (∃ e : AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (lineGrading κ) ≅
        pullback (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R)) (residueSpecMap R),
      secondLine (mem_maximalIdeal_of_irreducible hπ) ≫ firstProjection π =
        e.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _) ∧
    -- (4) two minimal models of `ℙ¹_K`, not isomorphic as models
    IsMinimalModel (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of K) ↘ Spec (.of K))
      (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R)) (projectiveLineGenericFibreIso (K := K)) ∧
    IsMinimalModel (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of K) ↘ Spec (.of K))
      (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R)) (twistedGenericFibreIso (K := K) hπ) ∧
    ¬ ∃ g : projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ⟶ projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R), IsIso g ∧
      IsModelHom (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R))
        (projectiveSpaceOverRing 1 (.of R) ↘ Spec (.of R))
        (projectiveLineGenericFibreIso (K := K)) (twistedGenericFibreIso hπ) g

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.eulerCharacteristic_addComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CA2.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61] let `Cᵢ` be an
irreducible component of the special fibre `X_k` and let `D, D' ⊂ X` be effective Cartier
divisors with `D' = D + Cᵢ` and `D' ⊂ X_k`. Then

`χ(X_k, 𝒪_{D'}) - χ(X_k, 𝒪_D) = χ(X_k, 𝒪_X(-D)|_{Cᵢ}) = -(D · Cᵢ) + χ(Cᵢ, 𝒪_{Cᵢ})`.

Divisor sums are products of ideal sheaves, so `D' = D + Cᵢ` is `D' = D * Cᵢ`, and `D' ⊂ X_k` is
the containment `ℐ_{X_k} ⊆ ℐ_{D'}`. The modules `𝒪_{D'}`, `𝒪_D` and `𝒪_X(-D)|_{Cᵢ}` are taken on
`X_k` as direct images along the closed immersions into `X_k`. The intersection number
`(D · Cᵢ)` is the intersection product `Stacks.Models.intersectionProduct` of [Stacks, Tag 0C65]
on the components of `X_k`, with `D` read as the formal sum `∑ⱼ bⱼCⱼ` of its coefficients
`bⱼ = Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.specialFiberDivisorCoeff D Cⱼ`, which is `D` by
`Stacks.Models.RegularModelSituation.eq_prod_specialFiberDivisorCoeff`.

The first equality is additivity of the Euler characteristic ([Stacks, Tag 08AA]) on the short
exact sequence `0 ⟶ 𝒪_X(-D)|_{Cᵢ} ⟶ 𝒪_{D'} ⟶ 𝒪_D ⟶ 0` of [Stacks, Tag 0C4T], brought from `X`
to `X_k` along the closed immersion `X_k ⟶ X`. The second is the definition of the degree,
`deg(𝒪_X(-D)|_{Cᵢ}) = -deg(𝒪_X(D)|_{Cᵢ})`, and the symmetry of [Stacks, Tag 0C64].
declarations.statement:
public theorem eulerCharacteristic_addComponent
    [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)]
    (Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) (D D' : S.X.IdealSheafData)
    [hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D]
    (hsum : D' = D * S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z) (hk : S.specialFiberIdeal ≤ D') :
    eulerCharacteristic S.k S.specialFiberToSpec
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (S.fibreSubschemeι D' hk)).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit D'.subscheme.ringCatSheaf)) -
        eulerCharacteristic S.k S.specialFiberToSpec
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (S.fibreSubschemeι D
            (hk.trans (hsum ▸ Scheme.IdealSheafData.mul_le_left D _)))).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit D.subscheme.ringCatSheaf)) =
      eulerCharacteristic S.k S.specialFiberToSpec
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (S.specialFiberComponentι Z)).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subschemeι).obj
              (Stacks.Divisors.negativeTwist D))) ∧
    eulerCharacteristic S.k S.specialFiberToSpec
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (S.specialFiberComponentι Z)).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subschemeι).obj
              (Stacks.Divisors.negativeTwist D))) =
      -intersectionProduct S Finset.univ (fun Y => S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Y)
          (fun Y => S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Y)
          (fun Y => S.isProper_specialFiberComponentToSpec Y)
          (fun Y => S.toRegularModelSituation.topologicalKrullDim_specialFiberComponent Y)
          (fun Y => (S.specialFiberDivisorCoeff D Y : ℤ)) (Pi.single Z 1)
          (fun Y _ => S.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_specialFiberComponent Y) +
        eulerCharacteristic S.k (S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Z)
          (SheafOfModules.unit (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme.ringCatSheaf)
declarations.comment: χ(X_k, O_D') - χ(X_k, O_D) = χ(X_k, O_X(-D)|_Cᵢ) = -(D · Cᵢ) + χ(Cᵢ, O_Cᵢ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.cast_genus_eq_one_add_sum_specialFiberComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CA3.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61] — `R` a discrete
valuation ring with fraction field `K` and residue field `k`, `C` a smooth projective curve over
`K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`, `X` a regular proper model of `C`, `C₁, …, Cₙ` the irreducible
components of the special fibre and `X_k = Σ mᵢCᵢ` as in [Stacks, Tag 0C5Z] —

`g_C = 1 + Σᵢ mᵢ([κᵢ : k](gᵢ - 1) - ½(Cᵢ · Cᵢ))`,

where `κᵢ = H⁰(Cᵢ, 𝒪_{Cᵢ})`, `gᵢ` is the genus of `Cᵢ` (over `κᵢ`), `g_C` is the genus of `C` and
`(Cᵢ · Cᵢ) = deg(𝒪_X(Cᵢ)|_{Cᵢ})` is the self-intersection number of [Stacks, Tag 0C64]. The
components are indexed by `irreducibleComponents X_k`, and the formula is stated over `ℚ`.

The proof is the source's: `1 - g_C = χ(C, 𝒪_C) = χ(X_k, 𝒪_{X_k})`, the chain of
[Stacks, Tag 0CA2] from the empty divisor to `X_k` collapsed by part (2) of
[Stacks, Tag 0C66], and `χ(Cᵢ, 𝒪_{Cᵢ}) = [κᵢ : k](1 - gᵢ)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cast_genus_eq_one_add_sum_specialFiberComponent :
    (genus S.C_to_K : ℚ) = 1 + ∑ Z, (S.specialFiberMultiplicity Z : ℚ) *
      ((S.specialFiberComponentWeight Z : ℚ) * ((S.specialFiberComponentGenus Z : ℚ) - 1) -
        (S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z Z : ℚ) / 2)
declarations.comment: g_C = 1 + Σ mᵢ([κᵢ : k](gᵢ - 1) - (Cᵢ · Cᵢ)/2) at the canonical data of the model

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.associatedNumericalType_spec_and_genus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CA4.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61], with `C₁, …, Cₙ` the
irreducible components of the special fibre enumerated by `e`, `κᵢ = H⁰(Cᵢ, 𝒪_{Cᵢ})` and `gᵢ`
the genus of `Cᵢ` over `κᵢ`, the data `n, mᵢ, (Cᵢ · Cⱼ), [κᵢ : k], gᵢ` form a numerical type —
the numerical type `Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.associatedNumericalType`, whose
fields carry the laws of [Stacks, Tag 0C6Z] — and its genus is the genus `g_C` of `C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem associatedNumericalType_spec_and_genus (n : ℕ)
    (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) :
    ((S.associatedNumericalType n e).componentCount = n ∧
      (∀ i, (S.associatedNumericalType n e).multiplicity i =
        (S.specialFiberMultiplicity (e i) : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ i j, (S.associatedNumericalType n e).intersection i j =
        S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix (e i) (e j)) ∧
      (∀ i, (S.associatedNumericalType n e).weight i =
        (S.specialFiberComponentWeight (e i) : ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ i, (S.associatedNumericalType n e).componentGenus i =
        (S.specialFiberComponentGenus (e i) : ℤ))) ∧
    (S.associatedNumericalType n e).genus = (genus S.C_to_K : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the data n, m_i, (C_i . C_j), [kappa_i : k], g_i form a numerical type of genus the genus of C

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.associatedNumericalType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CA5: the numerical type associated to `X`**, in the situation of
[Stacks, Tag 0C61]: the numerical type described in [Stacks, Tag 0CA4], whose data are the number
`n` of irreducible components `C₁, …, Cₙ` of the special fibre (enumerated by `e`), their
multiplicities `mᵢ` (Tag 0C5Z), their intersection numbers `(Cᵢ · Cⱼ)`, their weights
`[κᵢ : k]` with `κᵢ = H⁰(Cᵢ, 𝒪_{Cᵢ})`, and their genera `gᵢ` over `κᵢ`. All the laws of a
numerical type are proved: the multiplicities are positive, the intersection matrix is the degree
matrix of the components, symmetric, nonnegative off the diagonal, connected and annihilates
`(mᵢ)`, and `[κᵢ : k]` divides every `(Cᵢ · Cⱼ)`. The enumeration is immaterial by
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.equivalent_associatedNumericalType`, which is what
licenses the definite article.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedNumericalType (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType
declarations.comment: the numerical type associated to X: n, m_i, (C_i . C_j), [kappa_i : k], g_i of the components of the special fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.isMinimalModel_iff_isMinimal_associatedNumericalType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CA6.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61], let `C₁, …, Cₙ` be the
irreducible components of the special fibre, enumerated by `e`. Then `X` is a minimal model if and
only if the numerical type associated to `X` ([Stacks, Tag 0CA5]) is minimal
([Stacks, Tag 0C7A]).
declarations.statement:
theorem isMinimalModel_iff_isMinimal_associatedNumericalType
    (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) :
    IsMinimalModel S.C_to_K S.X_to_R S.genericFiberIso ↔
      (S.associatedNumericalType n e).IsMinimal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_genus_neg_not_equivalent_associatedNumericalType
declarations.doc:
**Not every numerical type comes from a model**: there is a numerical type of negative genus,
and it is equivalent to no numerical type associated to a regular proper model of a smooth
projective curve over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_genus_neg_not_equivalent_associatedNumericalType :
    ∃ T : NumericalType, genus T < 0 ∧
      ∀ (S : RegularProperModelSituation.{u}) [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)]
        (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber),
        ¬ (S.associatedNumericalType n e).Equivalent T
declarations.comment: not every numerical type is the numerical type associated to a model, as there are numerical types of negative genus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_isMinimal_genus_one_not_equivalent_associatedNumericalType
declarations.doc:
**A minimal numerical type of positive genus not coming from a model**: the data `n = 1`,
`m₁ = 1`, `a₁₁ = 0`, `w₁ = 6`, `g₁ = 1` form a minimal numerical type of genus one which is
equivalent to no numerical type associated to a regular proper model, over a discrete valuation
ring `R`, of a smooth projective curve `C` over the fraction field `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`; in
particular of a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over `K`. The special fibre of
such a model would live over an extension of degree `6` of the residue field, against its
geometric connectedness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isMinimal_genus_one_not_equivalent_associatedNumericalType :
    ∃ T : NumericalType, T.componentCount = 1 ∧
      (∀ i, T.multiplicity i = 1) ∧
      (∀ i j, T.intersection i j = 0) ∧
      (∀ i, T.weight i = 6) ∧
      (∀ i, T.componentGenus i = 1) ∧
      IsMinimal T ∧ genus T = 1 ∧
      ∀ (S : RegularProperModelSituation.{u}) [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)]
        (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber),
        ¬ (S.associatedNumericalType n e).Equivalent T
declarations.comment: n = 1, m₁ = 1, a₁₁ = 0, w₁ = 6, g₁ = 1 is a minimal numerical type of genus one which is not the numerical type associated to a model

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_isMinimal_genus_seven_not_equivalent_associatedNumericalType
declarations.doc:
**A second minimal numerical type of positive genus not coming from a model**: the data
`n = 2`, `m₁ = m₂ = 1`, `-a₁₁ = -a₂₂ = a₁₂ = a₂₁ = 6`, `w₁ = w₂ = 6`, `g₁ = g₂ = 1` form a minimal
numerical type of genus seven which is equivalent to no numerical type associated to a regular
proper model, over a discrete valuation ring `R`, of a smooth projective curve `C` over the
fraction field `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`; in particular of a smooth projective geometrically
irreducible curve over `K`. As for the one-component example, the reduced special fibre of such a
model would live over an extension of degree `6` of the residue field, against its geometric
connectedness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isMinimal_genus_seven_not_equivalent_associatedNumericalType :
    ∃ T : NumericalType, T.componentCount = 2 ∧
      (∀ i, T.multiplicity i = 1) ∧
      (∀ i, T.intersection i i = -6) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → T.intersection i j = 6) ∧
      (∀ i, T.weight i = 6) ∧
      (∀ i, T.componentGenus i = 1) ∧
      IsMinimal T ∧ genus T = 7 ∧
      ∀ (S : RegularProperModelSituation.{u}) [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)]
        (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber),
        ¬ (S.associatedNumericalType n e).Equivalent T
declarations.comment: n = 2, m₁ = m₂ = 1, -a₁₁ = -a₂₂ = a₁₂ = a₂₁ = 6, w₁ = w₂ = 6, g₁ = g₂ = 1 is a minimal numerical type of genus seven which is not the numerical type associated to a model

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_genus_neg
declarations.doc:
There is a numerical type whose genus is negative. The numerical type of a model has the
genus of the generic curve, which is nonnegative, so no such type comes from a model.
declarations.statement: public theorem exists_genus_neg : ∃ T : NumericalType, genus T < 0
declarations.comment: there exist numerical types whose genus is negative

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_isMinimal_genus_one_weight_six
declarations.doc:
The data `n = 1`, `m₁ = 1`, `a₁₁ = 0`, `w₁ = 6`, `g₁ = 1` is a minimal numerical type of
genus one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isMinimal_genus_one_weight_six :
    ∃ T : NumericalType, T.componentCount = 1 ∧
      (∀ i, T.multiplicity i = 1) ∧
      (∀ i j, T.intersection i j = 0) ∧
      (∀ i, T.weight i = 6) ∧
      (∀ i, T.componentGenus i = 1) ∧
      IsMinimal T ∧ genus T = 1
declarations.comment: n = 1, m₁ = 1, a₁₁ = 0, w₁ = 6, g₁ = 1 is a minimal numerical type of genus one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_isMinimal_genus_seven_weight_six
declarations.doc:
The data `n = 2`, `m₁ = m₂ = 1`, `-a₁₁ = -a₂₂ = a₁₂ = a₂₁ = 6`, `w₁ = w₂ = 6`,
`g₁ = g₂ = 1` is a minimal numerical type of genus seven.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isMinimal_genus_seven_weight_six :
    ∃ T : NumericalType, T.componentCount = 2 ∧
      (∀ i, T.multiplicity i = 1) ∧
      (∀ i, T.intersection i i = -6) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → T.intersection i j = 6) ∧
      (∀ i, T.weight i = 6) ∧
      (∀ i, T.componentGenus i = 1) ∧
      IsMinimal T ∧ genus T = 7
declarations.comment: n = 2, m₁ = m₂ = 1, -a₁₁ = -a₂₂ = a₁₂ = a₂₁ = 6, w₁ = w₂ = 6, g₁ = g₂ = 1 is a minimal numerical type of genus seven

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.cast_specialFiberComponentGenus_contractedComponentEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The genus of a component after contracting an exceptional curve** ([Stacks, Remark 0CA8]).
In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C6C] — `X` a regular proper model of `C` over a discrete
valuation ring with residue field `k`, `C_n` a component of the special fibre which is an
exceptional curve of the first kind, `f : X ⟶ X'` its contraction, and `C'_i = f(C_i)` for
`i ≠ n` — the genus `g'_i` of `C'_i` is

`g'_i = (w_i/w'_i)(g_i - 1) + 1 + ((C_i · C_n)² - w_n(C_i · C_n)) / (2 w'_i w_n)`,

where `w_i = [κ_i : k]`, `w_n = [κ_n : k]`, `w'_i = [κ'_i : k]` and `g_i` is the genus of `C_i`.
Here `X'` is the regular proper model
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.contractedSituation` and `C'_i` its component
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.contractedComponentEquiv`. The components are indexed
by `irreducibleComponents X_k`, the exceptional curve being presented as `𝐏¹_κ` by `ε`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cast_specialFiberComponentGenus_contractedComponentEquiv
    [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)]
    (hf : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N) f)
    (κ : Type u) [Field κ] {ε : projectiveLineProj κ ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).subscheme}
    (hE : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κ ε)
    (Z : {Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber // Z ≠ N}) :
    ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentGenus (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z) : ℚ) =
      (S.specialFiberComponentWeight Z.1 : ℚ) /
          ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentWeight
            (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z) : ℚ) *
          ((S.specialFiberComponentGenus Z.1 : ℚ) - 1) + 1 +
        ((S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z.1 N : ℚ) ^ 2 -
            (S.specialFiberComponentWeight N : ℚ) * S.specialFiberIntersectionMatrix Z.1 N) /
          (2 * ((S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiberComponentWeight
            (S.contractedComponentEquiv hf Z) : ℚ) * (S.specialFiberComponentWeight N : ℚ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.isContractionUpToWeight_associatedNumericalType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CA9.** Let `f : X ⟶ X'` contract a component `C_n` of the special
fibre of a regular proper model which is an exceptional curve of the first kind. Enumerate the
components of `X_k` by `e`, with `C_n` last, and those of `X'_k` by `e'`, compatibly with
`C'_i = f(C_i)`. Let `T` and `T'` be the numerical types associated to `X` and `X'`. Then `n` is a
`(-1)`-index of `T`, and `T'` agrees with the contraction of `T` of Tag 0C77 except for the
weights: `n' = n - 1`, `m'_i = m_i`, `a'_{ij} = a_{ij} - a_{in}a_{jn}/a_{nn}`, `g'_i` is the genus
formula at `w'_i`, and `w'_i` is a positive integer dividing `w_i`. Moreover `w'_i` divides `w_n`
whenever `a_{in} ≠ 0`, i.e. whenever `C_i` meets `C_n`, and `w'_i = w_i` whenever `a_{in} = 0`. The
source asserts `w'_i ∣ w_n` without that condition; it is stated here only where the maps
`κ_i ← κ'_i → κ_n` of Tag 0C6C (2) exist, since for a component missing `C_n` the weight is `w_i`,
which need not divide `w_n`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.exists_intersection_eq_zero_not_weight_dvd`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isContractionUpToWeight_associatedNumericalType
    [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)]
    (hf : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N) f)
    [DecidableEq (irreducibleComponents (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiber)]
    (κ : Type u) [Field κ] {ε : projectiveLineProj κ ≅ (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).subscheme}
    (hE : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal N).IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κ ε)
    (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)
    (e' : Fin (n - 1) ≃ irreducibleComponents (S.contractedSituation hf).specialFiber)
    (hN : e (lastIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e)) = N)
    (he' : ∀ i, ((S.contractedComponentEquiv hf).symm (e' i)).1 =
      e (remainingIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e) i)) :
    IsMinusOneIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e) (lastIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e)) ∧
      ∃ hT : IsContractionUpToWeight (S.associatedNumericalType n e)
          ((S.contractedSituation hf).associatedNumericalType (n - 1) e'),
        (∀ i, (S.associatedNumericalType n e).intersection
            (remainingIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e) i)
            (lastIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e)) ≠ 0 →
          ((S.contractedSituation hf).associatedNumericalType (n - 1) e').weight
              (Fin.cast hT.componentCount_eq.symm i) ∣
            (S.associatedNumericalType n e).weight (lastIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e))) ∧
        ∀ i, (S.associatedNumericalType n e).intersection
            (remainingIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e) i)
            (lastIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e)) = 0 →
          ((S.contractedSituation hf).associatedNumericalType (n - 1) e').weight
              (Fin.cast hT.componentCount_eq.symm i) =
            (S.associatedNumericalType n e).weight
              (remainingIndex (S.associatedNumericalType n e) i)
declarations.comment: corrected: the numerical type of X' is the 0C77 contraction of that of X except for w'_i, a positive integer dividing w_i; w'_i | w_n is stated only when C_i meets C_n, where 0C6C (2) gives the maps; when C_i misses C_n, w'_i = w_i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.isGreatest_contractLast_weight
declarations.doc:
**The weight of the contraction of a numerical type is the largest admissible one.** For a
minus-one index `n`, the weight `w'ᵢ` chosen in Tag 0C77 is the largest positive integer dividing
`wᵢ` for which the genus formula `(wᵢ/w'ᵢ)(gᵢ - 1) + 1 + (aᵢₙ² - wₙaᵢₙ)/(2w'ᵢwₙ)` is an integer.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGreatest_contractLast_weight (T : NumericalType)
    (h : IsMinusOneIndex T (lastIndex T)) (i : Fin (T.componentCount - 1)) :
    IsGreatest {d : ℤ | 0 < d ∧ d ∣ T.weight (remainingIndex T i) ∧
        ∃ G : ℤ, (G : ℚ) = (T.weight (remainingIndex T i) : ℚ) / d *
            ((T.componentGenus (remainingIndex T i) : ℚ) - 1) + 1 +
          ((T.intersection (remainingIndex T i) (lastIndex T) : ℚ) ^ 2 -
              T.weight (lastIndex T) * T.intersection (remainingIndex T i) (lastIndex T)) /
            (2 * d * T.weight (lastIndex T))}
      ((contractLast T h).val.weight
        (Fin.cast (contractLast T h).property.componentCount_eq.symm i))
declarations.comment: in the numerical case w'_i is the largest integer dividing w_i such that g'_i, as given by the formula, is an integer

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.IsContractionUpToWeight.picardMap_injective
declarations.doc:
**The injectivity of Tag 0C7J holds for smaller weights.** If `T'` is the contraction of a
minus-one index of `T` in every datum except that its weights `w'ᵢ` are only divisors of `wᵢ`,
the homomorphism `Pic(T) → Pic(T')` induced by `p` is still injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picardMap_injective (h : IsMinusOneIndex T (lastIndex T)) :
    Function.Injective (hT.picardMap h)
declarations.comment: the injectivity of Pic(T) → Pic(T') of Tag 0C7J works as well for smaller w'_i

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.nonempty_tensorPower_gcd_iso_unit_of_componentDegree_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAB.** Let `X ⟶ Spec(R)` be a regular proper model of a smooth
projective curve `C` over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring, write the special fibre
as `X_k = Σ m_Z C_Z` over its irreducible components and put `d = gcd(m_Z)`. An invertible
`𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` whose restriction to the generic fibre `C` is trivial and which has degree `0` on
every component of the special fibre satisfies `ℒ^{⊗d} ≅ 𝒪_X`.

Both hypotheses are the tag's own. Triviality on `C` is the vanishing of the class of `ℒ` in
`Pic(C)`, and exactness of the sequence `0 ⟶ ℤ ⟶ ℤ^{⊕n} ⟶ Pic(X) ⟶ Pic(C) ⟶ 0` at `Pic(X)`,
[Stacks, Tag 0C63], writes the class of `ℒ` as a combination `Σ a_Z[𝒪_X(C_Z)]`. The vanishing of
the degrees then makes `(a_Z)` a rational multiple `q(m_Z)` by part (4) of [Stacks, Tag 0C66]. The
greatest common divisor of the `m_Z` is an integral combination of them, so `dq` is an integer and
`d · Σ a_Z[𝒪_X(C_Z)]` is an integral multiple of `Σ m_Z[𝒪_X(C_Z)]`, which vanishes because
`Σ m_Z C_Z` is the special fibre and its invertible module is trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_tensorPower_gcd_iso_unit_of_componentDegree_eq_zero
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf
      S.X.presheaf (structureIsSheaf S.X.toRingedSpace)))
    (hL : IsInvertible S.X.presheaf (structureIsSheaf S.X.toRingedSpace) L)
    (hgen : genericFiberPicardRestriction S
      (picardClass S.X.presheaf (structureIsSheaf S.X.toRingedSpace) L hL) = 0)
    (hdeg : ∀ Z, S.specialFiberComponentDegree Z L hL = 0) :
    Nonempty (tensorPower S.X.presheaf (structureIsSheaf S.X.toRingedSpace) L
        ((Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity : ℕ) : ℤ) ≅
      _root_.SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.structureSheaf
        S.X.presheaf (structureIsSheaf S.X.toRingedSpace)))
declarations.comment: at the irreducible components of the special fibre: an invertible module trivial on the generic fibre C and of degree zero on every component has trivial d-th tensor power, for d the greatest common divisor of the multiplicities

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.picardNumericalTypeHom_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAC.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61] let `T` be the
numerical type associated to `X` ([Stacks, Tag 0CA5]). The canonical map
`Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.picardNumericalTypeHom : Pic(C) ⟶ Pic(T)` sends the
restriction of the class of an invertible module `ℒ` on `X` to the class of
`(deg(ℒ|_{C₁})/w₁, …, deg(ℒ|_{Cₙ})/wₙ)`, and its kernel is exactly the classes of the invertible
modules on `C` that are restrictions of invertible modules `ℒ` on `X` with
`deg_{Cᵢ}(ℒ|_{Cᵢ}) = 0` for every `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardNumericalTypeHom_spec :
    (∀ (L : S.X.Modules) (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L),
      S.picardNumericalTypeHom n e (genericFiberPicardRestriction S
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass S.X.presheaf
            (Stacks.RingedSpace.structureIsSheaf S.X.toRingedSpace) L hL)) =
        Submodule.Quotient.mk (fun i =>
          S.specialFiberComponentDegree (S.associatedEnumeration n e i) L hL /
            (S.specialFiberComponentWeight (S.associatedEnumeration n e i) : ℤ))) ∧
    ∀ y : ofScheme S.C, S.picardNumericalTypeHom n e y = 0 ↔
      ∃ (L : S.X.Modules) (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.X.presheaf
          (structureSheafRing S.X.toRingedSpace).property L),
        genericFiberPicardRestriction S
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass S.X.presheaf
              (Stacks.RingedSpace.structureIsSheaf S.X.toRingedSpace) L hL) = y ∧
          ∀ Z, S.specialFiberComponentDegree Z L hL = 0
declarations.comment: the canonical map Pic(C) -> Pic(T) and its kernel

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.picardTorsionSequence_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAD.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61] let
`d = gcd(m₁, …, mₙ)` for the multiplicities `mᵢ` of the irreducible components of the special
fibre, let `T` be the numerical type associated to `X` (through an enumeration `e` of the
components), and let `h ≥ 1` be prime to `d`. Then

`0 ⟶ Pic(X)[h] ⟶ Pic(C)[h] ⟶ Pic(T)[h]`

is exact, where the first map is restriction to the generic fibre and the second is the
canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0CAC]: the first map is injective and the kernel of the second is
the image of the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem picardTorsionSequence_exact (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)
    {h : ℕ} (hh : 1 ≤ h) (hcop : Nat.Coprime h (Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity)) :
    Function.Injective (S.picardTorsionRestriction (h : ℤ)) ∧
      Function.Exact (S.picardTorsionRestriction (h : ℤ))
        (S.picardTorsionToNumericalType n e (h : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the exact sequence 0 -> Pic(X)[h] -> Pic(C)[h] -> Pic(T)[h] for h prime to d = gcd(m_i), with T the numerical type associated to X

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.injOn_schemePullbackClass_specialFiberRedι_zsmulTorsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAE.** In Situation 0C61, let `h` be an integer prime to the
characteristic of the residue field `k`. Then restriction of invertible modules
`Pic(X)[h] ⟶ Pic((X_k)_red)[h]` is injective.

The proof is the source's. For every truncation `X_n = X ×_{Spec R} Spec(R/π^{n+1})` the reduced
special fibre `(X_k)_red ⟶ X_n` is a thickening, and restriction is injective on `h`-torsion along
it by [Stacks, Tag 0C6S]: the units condition of that tag holds because the global functions on
`(X_k)_red` form a field purely inseparable over `k`, the special fibre being geometrically
connected. So an `h`-torsion class trivial on `(X_k)_red` is trivial on every `X_n`, and then
trivial on `X` by the theorem on formal functions and the properness of `X ⟶ Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injOn_schemePullbackClass_specialFiberRedι_zsmulTorsion
    (S : RegularProperModelSituation.{u}) {h : ℤ} (hh : IsUnit ((h : ℤ) : S.k)) :
    Set.InjOn (schemePullbackClass S.specialFiberRedι) (zsmulTorsion (ofScheme S.X) h)
declarations.comment: restriction Pic(X)[h] → Pic((X_k)_red)[h] is injective for h prime to the characteristic of k

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.ConstantSheafGenerators.exists_epi_from_coproduct_jExtendConst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CAH (Lemma 17.19.1).**  Let `X` be a topological space, `B` a basis for the
topology on `X`, and `F` a sheaf of sets on `X`.  Then there is an index set `I`, a family of
basis opens `U i ∈ B`, a family of finite sets `S i`, and a *surjection* (epimorphism in
`Sh(X)`)

  `φ : ∐_i j_{U i !}(constant sheaf S i on U i) ⟶ F`

from the categorical coproduct (Def. 5) of the extensions-by-empty-set `jExtendConst X (U i) (S i)`
of the constant sheaves `constant sheaf (S i)` on `U i`.  Here `Epi φ` expresses that `φ` is a
surjection in the sense of Definition 6.

INFORMAL PROOF (Stacks 0CAH).
Take the index set `I = Σ x : X, F_x = {(x,s) : x ∈ X, s ∈ F_x}`, every `S i = PUnit` (a singleton,
hence finite).  For each `i = (x,s)`, since `B` is a basis and the stalk is a colimit over open
neighborhoods, `germ_exist_of_isBasis hB` provides a basis open `U i ∈ B` with `x ∈ U i` and a
section `σ i ∈ F(U i)` with germ `(σ i)_x = s`.  By Sub-lemma 1 (`exists_jExtendConst_hom_germ`),
the section `σ i` yields a morphism `ψ i : j_{U i !}underline{PUnit} ⟶ F` together with a stalk
element `t i` of `j_{U i !}underline{PUnit}` at `x` with `stalkMap (ψ i) (t i) = s`.  Assemble the
`ψ i` via the coproduct universal property (`Sigma.desc`) into
`φ : ∐_i j_{U i !}underline{PUnit} ⟶ F`.

For `Epi φ` we use the criterion (Def. 6): `φ` is epi iff stalkwise surjective
(`TopCat.Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi` ∘ `locally_surjective_iff_surjective_on_stalks`).
Fix `x : X` and `s ∈ F_x`; let `i = ⟨x, s⟩`.  Since `Sigma.ι i ≫ φ = ψ i`
(`Sigma.ι_desc`), applying the stalk functor and functoriality gives
`stalkMap φ (stalkMap (Sigma.ι i) (t i)) = stalkMap (ψ i) (t i) = s`.  Hence `s` is in the image of
`stalkMap φ`, so `φ` is surjective on every stalk, therefore `Epi`. ∎
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_from_coproduct_jExtendConst
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) X) (B : Set (Opens X)) (hB : Opens.IsBasis B) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Opens X) (S : I → Type u),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ B) ∧
      (∀ i, Finite (S i)) ∧
      ∃ φ : (∐ fun i => jExtendConst X (U i) (S i)) ⟶ F, Epi φ

declarations.name: Stacks.isFilteredColimit_of_hasCompactBasis
declarations.doc:
Every sheaf of sets on a space admitting a basis of quasi-compact opens is
a filtered colimit of sheaves with finite basis coequalizer presentations.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFilteredColimit_of_hasCompactBasis (B : Set (Opens X))
    (hBasis : IsTopologicalBasis ((fun U : Opens X ↦ (U : Set X)) '' B))
    (hB : ∀ U ∈ B, IsCompact (U : Set X))
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (TopCat.of X)) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsFiltered J)
      (D : J ⥤ TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (TopCat.of X))
      (ι : D ⟶ (Functor.const J).obj F),
      ∃ (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk F ι)),
        ∀ j, HasFiniteBasisCoequalizerPresentation B (D.obj j)

declarations.name: Stacks.exists_pullback_from_finite_sober_of_hasFiniteBasisCoequalizerPresentation
declarations.doc:
A sheaf with a finite coequalizer presentation over the quasi-compact
opens of a spectral space descends to a sheaf with finite stalks on a finite
sober space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pullback_from_finite_sober_of_hasFiniteBasisCoequalizerPresentation
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (TopCat.of X))
    (hF : HasFiniteBasisCoequalizerPresentation
      {U : Opens X | IsCompact (U : Set X)} F) :
    ∃ (Y : Type u) (_ : TopologicalSpace Y) (_ : Finite Y)
      (_ : QuasiSober Y) (_ : T0Space Y) (f : TopCat.of X ⟶ TopCat.of Y)
      (G : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (TopCat.of Y)),
      IsSpectralMap f ∧
        (∀ y, Finite (G.presheaf.stalk y)) ∧
        Nonempty ((TopCat.Sheaf.pullback (Type u) f).obj G ≅ F)

declarations.name: Stacks.exists_mono_to_pi_constantSheafPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAL.** A constructible sheaf of sets on a spectral space — one with
a finite presentation by finite constant sheaves extended from quasi-compact opens — is
isomorphic to a subsheaf of a finite product of pushforwards of finite constant sheaves from
closed constructible subspaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_to_pi_constantSheafPushforward [SpectralSpace X]
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (TopCat.of X))
    (hF : HasFiniteBasisCoequalizerPresentation
      { U : Opens X | IsCompact (U : Set X) } F) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (Z : Fin n → Set X),
      (∀ i, IsClosed (Z i)) ∧ (∀ i, Topology.IsConstructible (Z i)) ∧
        ∃ (S : Fin n → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (S i))
          (f : F ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun i ↦ constantSheafPushforward (Z i) (S i)), Mono f

declarations.name: exists_isClosed_partition
declarations.doc:
A partition of a closed subset `Z` into two relatively closed pieces extends to a
partition of the ambient spectral space into two closed pieces, provided `Z` meets the
closure of each point in a connected set.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_isClosed_partition
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [SpectralSpace X]
    {Z Z₁ Z₂ : Set X} (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (hconnected : ∀ x : X, IsConnected (Z ∩ closure ({x} : Set X)))
    (hZ₁ : IsClosed ((Subtype.val : Z → X) ⁻¹' Z₁))
    (hZ₂ : IsClosed ((Subtype.val : Z → X) ⁻¹' Z₂))
    (hunion : Z₁ ∪ Z₂ = Z) (hdisjoint : Disjoint Z₁ Z₂) :
    ∃ X₁ X₂ : Set X,
      IsClosed X₁ ∧ IsClosed X₂ ∧ X₁ ∪ X₂ = univ ∧ Disjoint X₁ X₂ ∧
        Z₁ = Z ∩ X₁ ∧ Z₂ = Z ∩ X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.NilpotentIdeal.PowerMap.powMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
If `I` is locally nilpotent and `n ≥ 1` is invertible in `R/I`, then the `n`th power map
`1 + x ↦ (1 + x)^n` on `1 + I` is a bijection.
declarations.statement:
theorem powMap_bijective
    (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsNilpotent x) {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hnu : IsUnit ((n : R ⧸ I))) :
    Function.Bijective (powMap I n)

declarations.name: Stacks.NilpotentIdeal.PowerMap.isUnit_pow_iff
declarations.doc:
If `I` is locally nilpotent and `n ≥ 1` is invertible in `R/I`, then a unit `u ∈ Rˣ` is
an `n`th power in `R` if and only if its image in `R/I` is an `n`th power (as a unit) in `R/I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnit_pow_iff
    (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsNilpotent x) {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hnu : IsUnit ((n : R ⧸ I))) (u : Rˣ) :
    (∃ v : Rˣ, u = v ^ n) ↔
      (∃ w : (R ⧸ I)ˣ, (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (u : R) : R ⧸ I) = (w : R ⧸ I) ^ n)

declarations.name: smooth_descends_to_filtered_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0CAQ (Lemma 10.138.15).** Let `I` be a filtered category and
`F : I ⥤ CommRingCat` a filtered system of commutative rings with colimit
`A = colimit F` and structure maps `ψ_i = colimit.ι F i`. If `A → B` (given by a
morphism `f : colimit F ⟶ B`) is a smooth ring map, then there exist an index `i`,
a commutative ring `B_i`, and a smooth ring map `g : A_i → B_i`, such that `B` is
isomorphic, as an `A`-algebra, to the base change `B_i ⊗_{A_i} A` of `B_i` along
the structure map `ψ_i : A_i → A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_descends_to_filtered_colimit
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (B : CommRingCat.{u}) (f : colimit F ⟶ B) :
    letI : Algebra (↑(colimit F) : Type u) (↑B : Type u) := f.hom.toAlgebra
    RingHom.Smooth f.hom →
    ∃ (i : I) (Bi : CommRingCat.{u}) (g : F.obj i ⟶ Bi),
      letI : Algebra (↑(F.obj i) : Type u) (↑Bi : Type u) := g.hom.toAlgebra
      letI : Algebra (↑(F.obj i) : Type u) (↑(colimit F) : Type u) :=
        (colimit.ι F i).hom.toAlgebra
      RingHom.Smooth g.hom ∧
      (letI : Algebra (↑(colimit F) : Type u) (↑B : Type u) := f.hom.toAlgebra
       letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
         (R := (↑(F.obj i) : Type u)) (A := (↑Bi : Type u)) (B := (↑(colimit F) : Type u))
       Nonempty ((↑B : Type u) ≃ₐ[(↑(colimit F) : Type u)]
         TensorProduct (↑(F.obj i) : Type u) (↑Bi : Type u) (↑(colimit F) : Type u)))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.artinApproximationGRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CAR (Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 16.13.4).** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, let `𝔭`
be a prime of `A` such that `A_𝔭` is a G-ring, and let `f₁, …, f_m` be polynomials over `A` in
`n` variables. If the system `f = 0` has a solution `(a₁, …, a_n)` in the completion of `A_𝔭`,
then for every `N` there are an étale ring map `A → A'`, a prime `𝔭' ⊂ A'` lying over `𝔭` with
`κ(𝔭) = κ(𝔭')`, and a solution `(b₁, …, b_n)` of the system in `A'` with
`a_i - b_i ∈ (𝔭')^N (A'_{𝔭'})^∧`.

Both inputs of the source's proof are proved: Theorem 07QZ is `localApproximationProperty` and
Algebra, Lemma 00U2 (9) is `etaleDescentAlongLocalization`.
declarations.statement: theorem artinApproximationGRing : ArtinApproximationGRing.{u}
declarations.comment: the full conclusion — étaleness of `A → A'`, `𝔭'` lying over `𝔭`, the solution in `A'`, the residue field equality `κ(𝔭) = κ(𝔭')` and the congruence `a_i - b_i ∈ (𝔭')^N (A'_{𝔭'})^∧` for every `i` and every `N` — in the spelling of `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.ArtinApproximationGRing`, with NO carried hypotheses. The source's proof has two inputs and both are proved. The second, Algebra Lemma 00U2 (9), is `etaleDescentAlongLocalization`, from the public `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etale_pushout_of_localization`. The first is Theorem 07QZ, `Stacks.Smoothing.exists_localEtaleSolution_of_isGRing`, itself unconditional because Popescu's Theorem 07GC is (`indSmooth_of_isRegularRingMap`, resting on Lemma 07FJ `canBeResolvedInPositiveCharacteristic`, whose λ-choice repair is due to Brian Nugent); the shape 0CAR's proof consumes it in is `localApproximationProperty`. The reduction of 0CAR to 07QZ — the base change of the system to `A_𝔭`, the descent of the solution and its equations to a principal localization, the identification of `𝔭'` and of `A'_{𝔭'}` with `S_q`, the residue field equality and the transport of the congruence — is `artinApproximationGRing_of_local`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleNeighborhood_fiber_openImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAS.** An étale neighborhood on a fiber can be
refined by an open immersion from the fiber of an étale neighborhood on the
total space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_fiber_openImmersion
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    (V : EtaleNeighborhood (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x)) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x)
      (u : (U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x))
      (p : (U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x) ⟶ f.fiber (f x))
      (h : (U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x) ⟶ V.scheme),
      (U.toBase ≫ f).fiberι (f x) u = U.point ∧
      p ≫ f.fiberι (f x) = (U.toBase ≫ f).fiberι (f x) ≫ U.toBase ∧
      Etale p ∧
      p u = f.asFiber x ∧
      h ≫ V.toBase = p ∧
      h u = V.point ∧
      IsOpenImmersion h

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_approximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAU (More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.39.1).** Let `S` be a locally
Noetherian scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, and let `x ∈ X`
and `y ∈ Y` lie over the same point `s = f x = g y` of `S`. Assume `𝒪_{S, s}` is a G-ring, and
let `φ : 𝒪_{Y, y} → 𝒪^∧_{X, x}` be a local homomorphism of `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras. Then for every
`N ≥ 1` there are an elementary étale neighbourhood `(U, u)` of `(X, x)` and a morphism
`F : U ⟶ Y` over `S` with `F u = y` such that the square formed by `φ`, the map
`𝒪^∧_{X, x} → 𝒪^∧_{U, u}`, the map `F^♯_u : 𝒪_{Y, y} → 𝒪_{U, u}` and `𝒪_{U, u} → 𝒪^∧_{U, u}`
commutes modulo `𝔪_u^N`.

The proof reduces to the affine case
`StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_etaleApproximation`, which rests on Stacks 0CAR
`StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.artinApproximationGRing`: it chooses affine charts, transports
`φ` to the charts, and reads `Spec A'` as an elementary étale neighbourhood of `(X, x)` with a
morphism to `Y` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_approximation
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (x : X) (y : Y) (hxy : f x = g y)
    (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (φ : Y.presheaf.stalk y →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hφ : IsLocalHom φ)
    (hbase : φ.comp ((S.presheaf.stalkCongr (.of_eq hxy)).hom ≫ g.stalkMap y).hom =
      (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))).comp
        (f.stalkMap x).hom) :
    ∃ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x, U.IsElementary ∧
      ∃ (F : U.scheme ⟶ Y) (hF : F U.point = y), F ≫ g = U.toBase ≫ f ∧
        ∀ a : Y.presheaf.stalk y,
          adicCompletionMap
              (((X.presheaf.stalkCongr (.of_eq U.map_point.symm)).hom ≫
                U.toBase.stalkMap U.point).hom)
              (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
              (maximalIdeal (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point))
              (map_maximalIdeal_le_etaleNeighborhood U) (φ a) -
            algebraMap (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point)
              (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point))
                (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point))
              (((Y.presheaf.stalkCongr (.of_eq hF.symm)).hom ≫ F.stalkMap U.point).hom a) ∈
            Ideal.map
              (algebraMap (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point))
                  (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point) ^ N)
declarations.comment: the full scheme-level statement, with the congruence in the completed local ring of the neighbourhood. The hypotheses are exactly the source's own: `S` locally Noetherian, `f` and `g` locally of finite type, `x` and `y` over the same point, `𝒪_{S, s}` a G-ring, and the local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map `φ : 𝒪_{Y, y} → 𝒪^∧_{X, x}`. The affine case enters through the unconditional Stacks 0CAR `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.artinApproximationGRing`. The source's own proof of 37.39.1 is the reduction to the affine case, and that reduction is what is PROVED here on top of the affine case `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_etaleApproximation`: the affine charts, the chart descriptions of the three local rings, the elementariness of the neighbourhood from the ring-level residue field equality, and the transport of the congruence. The source states the conclusion for a diagram; here it is the single congruence that the diagram expresses.

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_common_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_of_adicCompletion_ringEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAV (More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.39.2).** Let `S` be a locally
Noetherian scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, and let `x ∈ X`
and `y ∈ Y` lie over a common point `s` of `S` whose local ring is a G-ring. Suppose given an
isomorphism `Φ : 𝒪^∧_{Y, y} ≅ 𝒪^∧_{X, x}` which is compatible with the two maps from
`𝒪_{S, s}`. Then for every `N ≥ 1` there is a single pointed scheme `(U, u)` sitting in a
diagram `(X, x) ← (U, u) → (Y, y)` over `S` in which *both* legs are elementary étale
neighbourhoods, and over which the triangle of completed local rings commutes modulo
`𝔪_u ^ N`: for every `z ∈ 𝒪^∧_{Y, y}`, the two images of `z` in `𝒪^∧_{U, u}` — one obtained by
transporting `z` through `Φ` and then along the first leg, the other by going directly along the
second leg — differ by an element of `𝔪_u ^ N · 𝒪^∧_{U, u}`.

Tag 0CAU already produces the neighbourhood `(U₀, u₀)` of `(X, x)` and a morphism `F : U₀ ⟶ Y`
over `S` whose congruence holds on the image of `𝒪_{Y, y}`. The content added here is that `F`
is étale at `u₀`, which is extracted from the congruence itself: it forces the induced map
`𝒪^∧_{Y, y} → 𝒪^∧_{U₀, u₀}` to be bijective, and a bijection of completions upgrades to
étaleness of local rings by Tag 039M. Shrinking `U₀` to an open on which `F` is étale gives the
required `(U, u)`.

The difference of the two completion maps is written with an explicit `HSub` instance because
the two completions are only definitionally, not reducibly, the same ring: the second is indexed
by the scheme of `EtaleNeighborhood.along`, whose `scheme` field is the first one by `rfl`. The
term is the ordinary `_ - _`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_common_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_of_adicCompletion_ringEquiv
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (x : X) (y : Y) (hxy : f x = g y)
    (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (Φ : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ≃+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hΦ : Φ.toRingHom.comp ((algebraMap (Y.presheaf.stalk y)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y))).comp
          ((S.presheaf.stalkCongr (.of_eq hxy)).hom ≫ g.stalkMap y).hom) =
      (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))).comp
          (f.stalkMap x).hom) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (q : U.scheme ⟶ Y) (hqEt : Etale q) (hq : q U.point = y),
      U.IsElementary ∧ (U.along q hqEt hq).IsElementary ∧ q ≫ g = U.toBase ≫ f ∧
        ∀ z : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y),
          @HSub.hSub _ _ _ instHSub (U.completionMap (Φ z))
              ((U.along q hqEt hq).completionMap z) ∈
            Ideal.map (algebraMap (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point)
              (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point))
                (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (U.scheme.presheaf.stalk U.point) ^ N)
declarations.comment: with NO carried hypotheses, exactly as Tag 0CAU it rests on: the only hypotheses are the source's own. Everything in the source's own proof of 37.39.2 is proved here. The congruence is stated on the whole completed local ring of the neighbourhood rather than only on the image of the local ring, which is what the source's diagram of complete local rings asserts

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_baseApproximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAW, first stage: clauses (1) for `(v, τ)`, (2) and (3).** Let `S` be
a locally Noetherian scheme, let `h : T ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `t ∈ T` lie over
`s ∈ S`, assume `𝒪_{S, s}` is a G-ring, and let `σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` be a local
homomorphism of `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras. Then for every `N ≥ 1` there are an elementary étale
neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `(S, s)` and a morphism `τ : V ⟶ T` over `S` with `τ v = t` such that
the square
```
𝒪^∧_{S, s} ⟶ 𝒪^∧_{V, v}
    ↑σ             ↑
𝒪_{T, t}  —τ^♯—→ 𝒪_{V, v}
```
commutes modulo `𝔪_v ^ N`.

This is Tag 0CAU for the pointed diagram `(S, s) ← (S, s)`, `(T, t) → (S, s)` and the map `σ`:
the source's own proof of 0CAW ends by applying 0CAU "one more time to `Spec C` and `Spec R` over
`Spec R` and the map `C → R^∧`", and that application is this statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_baseApproximation
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType h]
    (t : T) (s : S) (hts : h t = s)
    (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (σ : T.presheaf.stalk t →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hσ : IsLocalHom σ)
    (hσbase : σ.comp (h.stalkHomAt hts) =
      algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s))) :
    ∃ V : EtaleNeighborhood S s, V.IsElementary ∧
      ∃ (τ : V.scheme ⟶ T) (hτ : τ V.point = t), τ ≫ h = V.toBase ∧
        ∀ a : T.presheaf.stalk t,
          V.completionMap (σ a) -
              algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)) (τ.stalkHomAt hτ a) ∈
            Ideal.map
              (algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point) ^ N)
declarations.comment: the FIRST STAGE of the conclusion: clause (1) for `v` and `τ` (`v ↦ s` and `τ(v) = t`), clause (2) (`(V, v) → (S, s)` is an elementary étale neighbourhood) and clause (3) (the square relating `σ` to `τ^♯_v` commutes modulo `𝔪_v ^ N`), with `τ` a morphism over `S`. This is the source's own last step, Tag 0CAU applied to `(S, s) ← (S, s)`, `(T, t) → (S, s)` and `σ`. Clauses (4) and (5) are NOT established by this declaration; see `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_relativeApproximation`. There is NO hypothesis beyond the source's: the Tag 0CAU used here is unconditional, Theorem 07QZ being proved as `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.localApproximationProperty`

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_relativeApproximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAW, second stage: the rest of clause (1), clause (4), and clause (5)
in the form of a congruence in `𝒪^∧_{W, w}`.** Given the first stage — an elementary étale
neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `(S, s)` and a morphism `τ : V ⟶ T` — a point `y_τ` of
`Y ×_{T, τ} V` lying over `v`, and a local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map
`φ : 𝒪_{X, x} → 𝒪^∧_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ}`, there are for every `N ≥ 1` an elementary étale
neighbourhood `(W, w)` of `(Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ)` and a morphism `F : W ⟶ X` over `S` with
`F w = x`, hence a morphism `W ⟶ X ×_S V` carrying `w` to `(x, v)`, such that `φ` followed by
the map `𝒪^∧_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ} → 𝒪^∧_{W, w}` agrees modulo `𝔪_w ^ N` with the map
`𝒪_{X, x} → 𝒪_{W, w}` induced by `F`.

This is Tag 0CAU for the pointed diagram `(Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ) → (S, s)`, `(X, x) → (S, s)`, the
first leg being read over `S` through `V ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_relativeApproximation
    {S T X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ T)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (x : X) (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
    (V : EtaleNeighborhood S (f x)) (τ : V.scheme ⟶ T)
    (yτ : ↥(pullback g τ)) (hyτ : pullback.snd g τ yτ = V.point)
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (φ : X.presheaf.stalk x →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal ((pullback g τ).presheaf.stalk yτ))
        ((pullback g τ).presheaf.stalk yτ))
    (hφ : IsLocalHom φ)
    (hφbase : φ.comp (f.stalkMap x).hom =
      (algebraMap ((pullback g τ).presheaf.stalk yτ)
          (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal ((pullback g τ).presheaf.stalk yτ))
            ((pullback g τ).presheaf.stalk yτ))).comp
        (((pullback.snd g τ).stalkHomAt hyτ).comp V.stalkHom)) :
    ∃ W : EtaleNeighborhood (pullback g τ) yτ, W.IsElementary ∧
      ∃ (F : W.scheme ⟶ X) (hF : F W.point = x),
        F ≫ f = W.toBase ≫ pullback.snd g τ ≫ V.toBase ∧
        (∃ fW : W.scheme ⟶ pullback f V.toBase,
          fW ≫ pullback.fst f V.toBase = F ∧
            fW ≫ pullback.snd f V.toBase = W.toBase ≫ pullback.snd g τ) ∧
        ∀ a : X.presheaf.stalk x,
          W.completionMap (φ a) -
              algebraMap (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point))
                  (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point)) (F.stalkHomAt hF a) ∈
            Ideal.map
              (algebraMap (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point))
                  (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point) ^ N)
declarations.comment: the SECOND STAGE of the conclusion, for a first stage supplied as hypotheses: the remaining part of clause (1) — `w ↦ (y, v)`, which is `W.map_point`, and the morphism `f : W ⟶ X ×_S V` with `f(w) = (x, v)`, delivered as the two projection identities of `f` together with `F w = x` and the hypothesis placing `y_τ` over `v` — clause (4) (`(W, w) → (Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v))` is an elementary étale neighbourhood), and clause (5) in the form of the congruence modulo `𝔪_w ^ N` in `𝒪^∧_{W, w}` that the source's square expresses once the identification `𝒪_{Y_σ, y_σ}/𝔪^N = 𝒪_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v)}/𝔪^N` is removed from both sides. HYPOTHESES BEYOND THE SOURCE'S, all stated explicitly — Theorem 07QZ is NOT among them, the Tag 0CAU used here being unconditional: (a) the first stage itself, i.e. the elementary étale neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `(S, s)` with the morphism `τ : V ⟶ T`, which `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_baseApproximation` produces from the source's hypotheses; (b) the point `y_τ` of `Y ×_{T, τ} V` over `v`; (c) the local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map `φ : 𝒪_{X, x} → 𝒪^∧_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ}` in place of the source's `φ : 𝒪_{X, x} → 𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}`, the bridge between the two being the canonical isomorphism of `Y_σ` with `Y ×_{T, τ} V` over `𝒪_{V, v}/𝔪_v ^ N = 𝒪_{S, s}/𝔪_s ^ N` which clauses (2) and (3) make available.
