That identification IS constructed, as `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_truncationEquiv_stalk_relativeBaseChange`, but only as an isomorphism of the local rings TRUNCATED at `𝔪 ^ N`, which is the shape clause (5) uses it in; it does not produce a map into the COMPLETED local ring `𝒪^∧_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v)}` out of the source's `φ`, and no isomorphism of the completions exists, so hypothesis (c) is not discharged by it

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_relativeMapApproximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CAW (More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.39.6).** Let `S` be a locally
Noetherian scheme, let `p : X ⟶ S`, `q : Y ⟶ T` and `h : T ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let
`x ∈ X` lie over `s ∈ S` and `y ∈ Y` over `t ∈ T` with `h t = s`, and assume `𝒪_{S, s}` is a
G-ring. Let `σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` be a local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map, write
`Y_σ = Y ×_{T, σ} Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}`, let `y_σ` be a point of `Y_σ` over `y` — the only one, since
such a point lies over the closed point by
`StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.snd_eq_closedPoint_of_fst_eq` — and let
`φ : 𝒪_{X, x} → 𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}` be a local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map.

Then for every `N ≥ 1` there is a commutative diagram
```
X ← X ×_S V ←—f— W —→ Y ×_{T, τ} V → Y
↓               ↓                     ↓
S ←——————————— V ———τ——————————————→ T
```
of schemes over `S` with points `w ∈ W` and `v ∈ V` such that
1. `v ↦ s`, `τ v = t`, `f w = (x, v)` and `w ↦ (y, v)`;
2. `(V, v) → (S, s)` is an elementary étale neighbourhood;
3. the square relating `σ` to `τ^♯_v` commutes modulo `𝔪_v ^ N`;
4. `(W, w) → (Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v))` is an elementary étale neighbourhood;
5. the square
```
𝒪_{X, x} —φ→ 𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ} → 𝒪_{Y_σ, y_σ}/𝔪^N —θ→ 𝒪_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v)}/𝔪^N
   ‖                                                           ↓
𝒪_{X, x} → 𝒪_{X ×_S V, (x, v)} —f^♯_w→ 𝒪_{W, w} ———————→ 𝒪_{W, w}/𝔪^N
```
commutes, where `θ` is the canonical isomorphism of `Y_σ` with `Y ×_{T, τ} V` over
`𝒪_{V, v}/𝔪_v ^ N = 𝒪_{S, s}/𝔪_s ^ N` that clauses (2) and (3) provide.

The isomorphism `θ` is exhibited, together with the compatibilities which characterise it: it
matches the two maps from `𝒪_{Y, y}` and the two maps from `𝒪_{S, s}`. Only the `𝔪 ^ N`
truncations are identified; the completions `𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}` and `𝒪^∧_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v)}`
need not be isomorphic, as the cusp-versus-node example in the module docstring of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/EtaleNeighbourhood/FiniteTypeBaseApproximation.lean`
shows. The correspondence of `(y, v)` with `y_σ` on the closed fibres is recorded in addition, as
in Tag 0GDX.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_relativeMapApproximation
    {X S Y T : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (p : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ T) (h : T ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [LocallyOfFiniteType h]
    {x : X} {s : S} {y : Y} {t : T} (hx : p x = s) (hy : q y = t) (hts : h t = s)
    (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (σ : T.presheaf.stalk t →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hσ : IsLocalHom σ)
    (hσbase : σ.comp (h.stalkHomAt hts) =
      algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)))
    (yσ : (pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hyσY : pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) yσ = y)
    (φ : X.presheaf.stalk x →+*
      AdicCompletion
        (maximalIdeal
          ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
        ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
    (hφ : IsLocalHom φ)
    (hφbase : φ.comp (p.stalkHomAt hx) =
      (algebraMap ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ)
          (AdicCompletion
            (maximalIdeal
              ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
            ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))).comp
        (((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).stalkHomAt
            (snd_eq_closedPoint_of_fst_eq h q hy hts σ hσbase
              (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) rfl yσ hyσY)).comp
          ((specCompletedStalkTo S s).stalkHomAt
            (specCompletedStalkTo_specCompletedStalkPoint S s)))) :
    ∃ (V : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (τ : V.scheme ⟶ T) (hτ : τ V.point = t)
      (yτ : (pullback q τ : Scheme.{u}))
      (hyτY : pullback.fst q τ yτ = y) (hyτV : pullback.snd q τ yτ = V.point)
      (W : EtaleNeighborhood (pullback q τ) yτ) (F : W.scheme ⟶ X) (hF : F W.point = x)
      (f : W.scheme ⟶ pullback p V.toBase),
      V.IsElementary ∧ W.IsElementary ∧ τ ≫ h = V.toBase ∧
        f ≫ pullback.fst p V.toBase = F ∧
        f ≫ pullback.snd p V.toBase = W.toBase ≫ pullback.snd q τ ∧
        F ≫ p = W.toBase ≫ pullback.snd q τ ≫ V.toBase ∧
        (∀ b : T.presheaf.stalk t,
          V.completionMap (σ b) -
              algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)) (τ.stalkHomAt hτ b) ∈
            Ideal.map
              (algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point) ^ N)) ∧
        (∃ θ : ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ ⧸
              maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ) ^ N) ≃+*
            ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ ⧸
              maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N),
          (∀ b : Y.presheaf.stalk y,
            θ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).stalkHomAt hyσY b)) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.fst q τ).stalkHomAt hyτY b)) ∧
          (∀ c : S.presheaf.stalk s,
            θ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).stalkHomAt
                  (snd_eq_closedPoint_of_fst_eq h q hy hts σ hσbase
                    (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) rfl yσ hyσY)
                  ((specCompletedStalkTo S s).stalkHomAt
                    (specCompletedStalkTo_specCompletedStalkPoint S s) c))) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.snd q τ).stalkHomAt hyτV (V.stalkHom c))) ∧
          ∀ (α : X.presheaf.stalk x) (z : (pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ),
            θ (AdicCompletion.evalₐ (maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ)) N
                (φ α)) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N) z →
            Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point) ^ N)
                (W.stalkHom z) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point) ^ N)
                (F.stalkHomAt hF α)) ∧
        ∃ (eBase : (specCompletedStalk S s).residueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≅
            V.scheme.residueField V.point)
          (eFiber : (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiber
              (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≅
            (pullback.snd q τ).fiber V.point),
          (Spec.map eBase.inv ≫ V.scheme.fromSpecResidueField V.point ≫ V.toBase =
            (specCompletedStalk S s).fromSpecResidueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              specCompletedStalkTo S s) ∧
          (Spec.map eBase.inv ≫ V.scheme.fromSpecResidueField V.point ≫ τ =
            (specCompletedStalk S s).fromSpecResidueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) ∧
          (eFiber.hom ≫ (pullback.snd q τ).fiberι V.point ≫ pullback.fst q τ =
            (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberι
                (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)) ∧
          (eFiber.hom ≫ (pullback.snd q τ).fiberToSpecResidueField V.point =
            (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberToSpecResidueField
                (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫ Spec.map eBase.inv) ∧
          (eFiber.hom (((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberHomeo
              (specCompletedStalkPoint S s)).symm
              ⟨yσ, snd_eq_closedPoint_of_fst_eq h q hy hts σ hσbase
                (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) rfl yσ hyσY⟩) =
            ((pullback.snd q τ).fiberHomeo V.point).symm ⟨yτ, hyτV⟩)
declarations.comment: the source's own hypotheses, with nothing beyond them: `h : T ⟶ S` locally of finite type, a G-ring `𝒪_{S, s}`, a local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map `σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}`, the base change `Y_σ = Y ×_{T, σ} Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}`, a point `y_σ` of `Y_σ` over `y` (the source's `the` point: lying over `y` forces it over the closed point, by `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.snd_eq_closedPoint_of_fst_eq`, so no second hypothesis places it there) and a local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map `φ : 𝒪_{X, x} → 𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}`. Theorem 07QZ is discharged, not an input: the `LocalApproximationProperty` hypothesis of Tag 0CAU behind both stages is supplied by `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.localApproximationProperty`, which rests on the unconditional Tag 07QZ `Stacks.Smoothing.exists_localEtaleSolution_of_isGRing` and hence on the unconditional Popescu Theorem 07GC `Stacks.Smoothing.indSmooth_of_isRegularRingMap`. The conclusion is the source's whole diagram: clause (1) — `v ↦ s`, `τ(v) = t`, `f(w) = (x, v)` as the two projection identities of `f` with `F w = x`, and `w ↦ (y, v)` as `W.map_point` with the point of `Y ×_{T, τ} V` lying over `y` and `v`; clause (2); clause (3); clause (4); and clause (5), the commuting square, whose `=` between `𝒪_{Y_σ, y_σ}/𝔪^N` and `𝒪_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v)}/𝔪^N` is exhibited as the ring isomorphism `θ` together with the two compatibilities that characterise it as the source's canonical identification over `𝒪_{V, v}/𝔪_v ^ N = 𝒪_{S, s}/𝔪_s ^ N`: it matches the two maps from `𝒪_{Y, y}` and the two maps from `𝒪_{S, s}`. Only the truncations are identified; the completions need not be isomorphic, as the cusp-versus-node example in the module docstring of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/EtaleNeighbourhood/FiniteTypeBaseApproximation.lean` shows. The route is the source's own: Tag 0CAU over `Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` replaces `φ` by a morphism to `X` out of an elementary étale neighbourhood of `(Y_σ, y_σ)`, that pointed span descends to a smooth stage of Popescu's presentation of `𝒪^∧_{S, s}`, and Tag 0CAU applied one more time to `Spec 𝒪_{T, t}` and `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}` over `Spec 𝒪_{S, s}` replaces the stage by `(V, v)`; `θ` is the order-`N` comparison of the two base changes of the stage object, along `Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s} ⟶ D` and along `V ⟶ D`, read through the two étale legs. The identification of the closed fibres `(Y_σ)_s ≅ (Y ×_T V)_v` of Tag 0GDX is recorded as well

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteType_pointed_extension_agree_mod_maximalIdeal_pow
declarations.doc:
A local map from the stalk of a finite-type Noetherian scheme to the completed local ring
of its base can be made rigid modulo any positive power of the base maximal ideal after a
pointed finite-type extension.

This is the source's statement, in which the comparison maps `σ'` are required to be local. It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteType_pointed_extension_agree_mod_maximalIdeal_pow_of_factors`,
which proves the agreement clause for every `σ'` factoring through the extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_pointed_extension_agree_mod_maximalIdeal_pow
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S)
    [IsNoetherian S] [IsNoetherian T]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (s : S) (t : T) (ht : f t = s)
    (sigma : T.presheaf.stalk t →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hsigma : IsLocalHom sigma)
    (hsigma_base :
      sigma.comp ((f.stalkMap t).hom.comp
        (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) ht).symm).hom) =
        algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
          (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)))
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : T' ⟶ T) (t' : T') (hgt : g t' = t)
      (_ : LocallyOfFiniteType g) (_ : QuasiCompact g),
      ∃ tau : T'.presheaf.stalk t' →+*
          AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s),
        IsLocalHom tau ∧
        sigma = tau.comp ((g.stalkMap t').hom.comp
          (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ T.presheaf.stalk z) hgt).symm).hom) ∧
        tau.comp ((g.stalkMap t').hom.comp
          ((eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ T.presheaf.stalk z) hgt).symm).hom.comp
            ((f.stalkMap t).hom.comp
              (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) ht).symm).hom))) =
          algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
            (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)) ∧
        (∀ (sigma' : T.presheaf.stalk t →+*
            AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)),
          IsLocalHom sigma' →
          sigma'.comp ((f.stalkMap t).hom.comp
              (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ S.presheaf.stalk z) ht).symm).hom) =
              algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s))
                  (S.presheaf.stalk s)) →
          (∃ tau' : T'.presheaf.stalk t' →+*
              AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s),
            sigma' = tau'.comp ((g.stalkMap t').hom.comp
              (eqToHom (congrArg (fun z ↦ T.presheaf.stalk z) hgt).symm).hom)) →
          ∀ a : T.presheaf.stalk t,
            sigma a - sigma' a ∈
              Ideal.map
                (algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
                  (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s))
                    (S.presheaf.stalk s)))
                (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s) ^ N))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConormalApproximation.exists_finiteType_pointed_extension_conormalAlgebra_iso_of_isLocalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CAY.** Let `Y → T → S` be finite type morphisms of Noetherian schemes, let `t ∈ T`
lie over `s ∈ S` and let `σ : 𝒪_{T,t} → 𝒪^∧_{S,s}` be a local `𝒪_{S,s}`-algebra map. Then there
is a finite type morphism of pointed schemes `(T', t') → (T, t)` through which `σ` factors by a
local homomorphism, such that for *every* local `𝒪_{S,s}`-algebra map
`σ' : 𝒪_{T,t} → 𝒪^∧_{S,s}` factoring through `𝒪_{T',t'}` the two closed immersions
`Y_σ ← Y_t → Y_{σ'}` of the fibre into the two base changes exist and have isomorphic conormal
algebras.

The hypotheses are the source's and nothing more: `σ` is assumed local because the source assumes
it ("let `σ : 𝒪_{T,t} → 𝒪_{S,s}^∧` be a local `𝒪_{S,s}`-algebra map"), and it is in any case
forced — a factorisation of `σ` through a local homomorphism out of the stalk of an extension
makes `σ` local.

This is
`Stacks.ConormalApproximation.exists_finiteType_pointed_extension_conormalAlgebra_iso_of_bound`
with its comparison hypothesis discharged by
`Stacks.ConormalApproximation.hasConormalBoundAlongExtension_of_isLocalHom`. The two facts that
discharge it are the locality of the identity-induced comparison
(`Stacks.ArtinRees.sameDenominator_iff_exists_isInducedByIdentity` together with
`Stacks.ConormalApproximation.sameDenominator_of_presentations` and
`Stacks.ConormalApproximation.sameDenominator_of_localization`), which lets the chart-local
comparison be propagated from a chart to the basic opens inside it, and the compactness of the
fibre, which makes finitely many charts enough — so the per-presentation Artin-Rees bound of the
affine core suffices, which is exactly the source's "cover `Y` by finitely many affines and glue
by uniqueness".
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_pointed_extension_conormalAlgebra_iso_of_isLocalHom
    {S T Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S) (p : Y ⟶ T)
    [IsNoetherian S] [IsNoetherian T] [IsNoetherian Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p]
    (s : S) (t : T) (ht : f t = s)
    (sigma : T.presheaf.stalk t →+* completedStalk S s) (hsigma : IsLocalHom sigma)
    (hsigma_base : sigma.comp (pointedStalkMap f ht) =
      algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s) (completedStalk S s)) :
    ∃ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : T' ⟶ T) (t' : T') (hgt : g t' = t)
      (_ : LocallyOfFiniteType g) (_ : QuasiCompact g),
      ∃ tau : T'.presheaf.stalk t' →+* completedStalk S s,
        IsLocalHom tau ∧
        sigma = tau.comp (pointedStalkMap g hgt) ∧
        ∀ sigma' : T.presheaf.stalk t →+* completedStalk S s,
          IsLocalHom sigma' →
          sigma'.comp (pointedStalkMap f ht) =
            algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s) (completedStalk S s) →
          (∃ tau' : T'.presheaf.stalk t' →+* completedStalk S s,
            sigma' = tau'.comp (pointedStalkMap g hgt)) →
          HasIsoConormalFibreImmersions p t
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom sigma) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t)
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom sigma') ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t)

declarations.name: Stacks.SyzygyCoefficients.exact_resolution
declarations.doc:
Let `P` present `B` as `C[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_m)`, let `σ : C → D` make `D` a
`C`-algebra and let `a_{kj} ∈ D[x_1, …, x_n]`, `k = 1, …, K`, generate the module of relations
among the `σ(f_j)`. Then `D[x]^{⊕K} → D[x]^{⊕m} → D[x] → B ⊗_{C, σ} D → 0` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_resolution
    {C : Type u} {B : Type v} {D : Type w}
    [CommRing C] [CommRing B] [CommRing D] [Algebra C B] [Algebra C D]
    {n m K : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Presentation C B (Fin n) (Fin m))
    (a : Fin K → Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) D)
    (ha : ∀ k, ∑ j, a k j * MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C D) (P.relation j) = 0)
    (hgen : ∀ v : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) D,
      (∑ j, v j * MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C D) (P.relation j) = 0) →
      ∃ w : Fin K → MvPolynomial (Fin n) D, ∀ j, v j = ∑ k, w k * a k j) :
    LinearMap.ker (relationMap D P) = LinearMap.range (syzygyMap a) ∧
      LinearMap.range (relationMap D P) =
        RingHom.ker (aeval (R := D) (S₁ := D ⊗[C] B) (P.baseChange D).val) ∧
      Function.Surjective (aeval (R := D) (S₁ := D ⊗[C] B) (P.baseChange D).val)

declarations.name: Stacks.SyzygyCoefficients.exists_finiteType_resolution
declarations.doc:
Let `P` present `B` as `C[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_m)`, let `D` be a `C`-algebra, and let
`a_{kj} ∈ D[x_1, …, x_n]`, `k = 1, …, K`, be syzygies `∑_j a_{kj} f_j = 0` generating all
syzygies among the images of the `f_j`. Then there are a `C`-algebra `C'` of finite type, a
`C`-algebra map `τ : C' → D` and polynomials `t_{kj} ∈ C'[x_1, …, x_n]` with `∑_j t_{kj} f_j = 0`,
such that `τ` carries the `t_{kj}` to the `a_{kj}` and the four-term complex over
`C'[x_1, …, x_n]` built from the `t_{kj}` and the `f_j` is exact at `C'[x_1, …, x_n]` and at
`B ⊗_C C'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_resolution
    {C : Type u} {B : Type v} {D : Type w}
    [CommRing C] [CommRing B] [CommRing D] [Algebra C B] [Algebra C D]
    {n m K : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Presentation C B (Fin n) (Fin m))
    (a : Fin K → Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) D)
    (ha : ∀ k, ∑ j, a k j * MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C D) (P.relation j) = 0)
    (_hgen : ∀ v : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) D,
      (∑ j, v j * MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C D) (P.relation j) = 0) →
      ∃ w : Fin K → MvPolynomial (Fin n) D, ∀ j, v j = ∑ k, w k * a k j) :
    ∃ (C' : Type u) (_ : CommRing C') (_ : Algebra C C') (_ : Algebra.FiniteType C C')
      (τ : C' →ₐ[C] D) (t : Fin K → Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) C'),
      (∀ k, ∑ j, t k j * MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C C') (P.relation j) = 0) ∧
      (∀ k j, MvPolynomial.map (τ : C' →+* D) (t k j) = a k j) ∧
      (∀ j, MvPolynomial.map (τ : C' →+* D)
        (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C C') (P.relation j)) =
        MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C D) (P.relation j)) ∧
      Ideal.span (Set.range fun j : Fin m =>
          MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap C C') (P.relation j)) =
        RingHom.ker (aeval (R := C') (S₁ := C' ⊗[C] B) (P.baseChange C').val) ∧
      Function.Surjective (aeval (R := C') (S₁ := C' ⊗[C] B) (P.baseChange C').val)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_etale_relativeIsomorphismApproximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB1 (More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.39.7).** With the notation and
assumptions of Tag 0CAW — a locally Noetherian `S`, morphisms `p : X ⟶ S`, `q : Y ⟶ T` and
`h : T ⟶ S` locally of finite type, points `x ↦ s` and `y ↦ t ↦ s`, a G-ring `𝒪_{S, s}`, a
local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map `σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}`, the base change
`Y_σ = Y ×_{T, σ} Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` and a point `y_σ` of it over `y` and over the closed point —
assume moreover that `φ` induces an isomorphism `𝒪^∧_{X, x} ≅ 𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}` of
`𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras on completions. Then for every `N ≥ 1` the diagram of Tag 0CAW can be
chosen with `f` étale: there are an elementary étale neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `(S, s)`, a
morphism `τ : V ⟶ T` over `S` with `τ v = t` whose square with `σ` commutes modulo `𝔪_v ^ N`, a
point `y_τ` of `Y ×_{T, τ} V` over `y` and `v` which corresponds to `y_σ` on the closed fibres,
an elementary étale neighbourhood `(W, w)` of `(Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ)`, a morphism `F : W ⟶ X`
over `S` carrying `w` to `x`, and an **étale** `f : W ⟶ X ×_S V` with `f ≫ pr₁ = F` and
`f ≫ pr₂ = W ⟶ Y ×_{T, τ} V ⟶ V`, so that `f w = (x, v)`.

Clause (5) of Tag 0CAW is the ring isomorphism
`θ : 𝒪_{Y_σ, y_σ}/𝔪_{y_σ} ^ N ≅ 𝒪_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v)}/𝔪_{(y, v)} ^ N`
which the conclusion exhibits, compatible with the two maps from `𝒪_{Y, y}` and with the two
maps from `𝒪_{S, s}` — the compatibilities which make `θ` the source's canonical identification
of the two base changes over `𝒪_{V, v}/𝔪_v ^ N = 𝒪_{S, s}/𝔪_s ^ N` — together with the
commutativity of the source's square: `φ` read on `𝒪_{X, x}` through `θ` and then through the
elementary étale neighbourhood `W ⟶ Y ×_{T, τ} V` is `F^♯_w` modulo `𝔪_w ^ N`. No isomorphism
of the completions `𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}` and `𝒪^∧_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ}` is asserted: only the
`𝔪 ^ N`-truncations are identified, and for a pair `(V, τ)` satisfying clauses (2) and (3)
alone the completions can be a cusp and a node.

The correspondence of `y_τ` with `y_σ` is recorded in addition, as in Tag 0GDX: an isomorphism
`eBase` of the residue fields of the two bases compatible with their maps to `S` and to `T`, and
an isomorphism `eFiber` of the scheme-theoretic closed fibres compatible with the two maps to
`Y` and with `eBase`, carrying the point above `y_σ` to the point above `y_τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_relativeIsomorphismApproximation
    {X S Y T : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (p : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ T) (h : T ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [LocallyOfFiniteType q] [LocallyOfFiniteType h]
    {x : X} {s : S} {y : Y} {t : T} (hx : p x = s) (hy : q y = t) (hts : h t = s)
    (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (σ : T.presheaf.stalk t →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hσ : IsLocalHom σ)
    (hσbase : σ.comp (h.stalkHomAt hts) =
      algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)))
    (yσ : (pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hyσY : pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) yσ = y)
    (hyσZ : pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) yσ =
      specCompletedStalkPoint S s)
    (φ : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) ≃+*
      AdicCompletion
        (maximalIdeal
          ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
        ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
    (hφ : φ.toRingHom.comp ((algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))).comp
        (p.stalkHomAt hx)) =
      (algebraMap ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ)
          (AdicCompletion
            (maximalIdeal
              ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
            ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))).comp
        (((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).stalkHomAt hyσZ).comp
          ((specCompletedStalkTo S s).stalkHomAt
            (specCompletedStalkTo_specCompletedStalkPoint S s)))) :
    ∃ (V : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (τ : V.scheme ⟶ T) (hτ : τ V.point = t)
      (yτ : (pullback q τ : Scheme.{u}))
      (hyτY : pullback.fst q τ yτ = y) (hyτV : pullback.snd q τ yτ = V.point)
      (W : EtaleNeighborhood (pullback q τ) yτ) (F : W.scheme ⟶ X) (hF : F W.point = x)
      (f : W.scheme ⟶ pullback p V.toBase),
      V.IsElementary ∧ W.IsElementary ∧ τ ≫ h = V.toBase ∧ Etale f ∧
        f ≫ pullback.fst p V.toBase = F ∧
        f ≫ pullback.snd p V.toBase = W.toBase ≫ pullback.snd q τ ∧
        F ≫ p = W.toBase ≫ pullback.snd q τ ≫ V.toBase ∧
        (∀ b : T.presheaf.stalk t,
          V.completionMap (σ b) -
              algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)) (τ.stalkHomAt hτ b) ∈
            Ideal.map
              (algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point) ^ N)) ∧
        (∃ θ : ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ) ⧸
              (maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ) ^ N) ≃+*
            ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ⧸
              (maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N),
          (∀ b : Y.presheaf.stalk y,
            θ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).stalkHomAt hyσY b)) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.fst q τ).stalkHomAt hyτY b)) ∧
          (∀ c : S.presheaf.stalk s,
            θ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).stalkHomAt hyσZ
                  ((specCompletedStalkTo S s).stalkHomAt
                    (specCompletedStalkTo_specCompletedStalkPoint S s) c))) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N)
                ((pullback.snd q τ).stalkHomAt hyτV (V.stalkHom c))) ∧
          ∀ (α : X.presheaf.stalk x) (z : (pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ),
            θ (AdicCompletion.evalₐ (maximalIdeal
                ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ)) N
                (φ (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
                  (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
                    (X.presheaf.stalk x)) α))) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal ((pullback q τ).presheaf.stalk yτ) ^ N) z →
            Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point) ^ N)
                (W.stalkHom z) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal (W.scheme.presheaf.stalk W.point) ^ N)
                (F.stalkHomAt hF α)) ∧
        ∃ (eBase : (specCompletedStalk S s).residueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≅
            V.scheme.residueField V.point)
          (eFiber : (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiber
              (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≅
            (pullback.snd q τ).fiber V.point),
          (Spec.map eBase.inv ≫ V.scheme.fromSpecResidueField V.point ≫ V.toBase =
            (specCompletedStalk S s).fromSpecResidueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              specCompletedStalkTo S s) ∧
          (Spec.map eBase.inv ≫ V.scheme.fromSpecResidueField V.point ≫ τ =
            (specCompletedStalk S s).fromSpecResidueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) ∧
          (eFiber.hom ≫ (pullback.snd q τ).fiberι V.point ≫ pullback.fst q τ =
            (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberι
                (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)) ∧
          (eFiber.hom ≫ (pullback.snd q τ).fiberToSpecResidueField V.point =
            (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberToSpecResidueField
                (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫ Spec.map eBase.inv) ∧
          (eFiber.hom (((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberHomeo
              (specCompletedStalkPoint S s)).symm ⟨yσ, hyσZ⟩) =
            ((pullback.snd q τ).fiberHomeo V.point).symm ⟨yτ, hyτV⟩)
declarations.comment: the source's own hypotheses, with nothing beyond them: `h : T ⟶ S` locally of finite type, `σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` a local `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebra map for `h`, the base change `Y_σ = Y ×_{T, σ} Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}`, a point `y_σ` of `Y_σ` over `y` and the closed point, and the isomorphism `φ : 𝒪^∧_{X, x} ≅ 𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}` of `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras which is what 0CB1 adds to Tag 0CAW. Theorem 07QZ is NOT carried: the `LocalApproximationProperty` hypothesis of Tag 0CAU behind Tag 0CAV and behind the first stage of Tag 0CAW is discharged with `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.localApproximationProperty`, which rests on the unconditional Tag 07QZ `Stacks.Smoothing.exists_localEtaleSolution_of_isGRing` and hence on the unconditional Popescu Theorem 07GC `Stacks.Smoothing.indSmooth_of_isRegularRingMap`. The conclusion is the source's whole diagram: clauses (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5) of Tag 0CAW together with the étaleness of `f : W ⟶ X ×_S V`, which is the content of 0CB1. Clause (5) is the ring isomorphism `θ : 𝒪_{Y_σ, y_σ}/𝔪^N ≅ 𝒪_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, (y, v)}/𝔪^N` which the conclusion exhibits, compatible with the two maps from `𝒪_{Y, y}` and with the two maps from `𝒪_{S, s}` — the compatibilities which characterise the source's canonical identification over `𝒪_{V, v}/𝔪_v ^ N = 𝒪_{S, s}/𝔪_s ^ N` — together with the source's commuting square: `φ` read on `𝒪_{X, x}` through `θ` and then through `W ⟶ Y ×_{T, τ} V` is `F^♯_w` modulo `𝔪_w ^ N`. Only the `𝔪 ^ N`-truncations are identified; the completions `𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}` and `𝒪^∧_{Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ}` need not be isomorphic, as the cusp-versus-node example in the module docstring of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/EtaleNeighbourhood/FiniteTypeBaseApproximation.lean` shows. The identification of the closed fibres `(Y_σ)_s ≅ (Y ×_T V)_v` of Tag 0GDX is recorded as well. The route to étaleness is Tag 0CAV over `Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` followed by the descent of Tag 0GDX, which delivers `W ⟶ X` étale directly, in place of the source's comparison of associated graded rings through Tag 0CAY; clause (5) comes from the congruence modulo `𝔪 ^ N` that Tag 0CAV supplies upstairs, transported to `W` by the order-`N` comparison of the two base changes of the stage object along `Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s} ⟶ D` and along `V ⟶ D`

declarations.name: encard_minimalPrimes_directLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB3.** For a directed system of rings with faithfully
flat transition maps, the number of minimal primes of the direct limit is the
supremum of the numbers of minimal primes at the individual stages.
declarations.statement:
theorem encard_minimalPrimes_directLimit
    {ι : Type u} [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : ι → Type v) [(i : ι) → CommRing (R i)]
    (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → R i →+* R j)
    [DirectedSystem R (fun i j h => (f i j h : R i → R j))]
    (hff : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), (f i j h).FaithfullyFlat) :
    Set.encard (minimalPrimes (Ring.DirectLimit R
      (fun i j h => (f i j h : R i → R j)))) =
      ⨆ i, Set.encard (minimalPrimes (R i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_iSup_encard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB4.** The number of geometric branches at a point is the
supremum, over all étale neighborhoods of that point, of the number of irreducible components
of the neighborhood passing through its distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
theorem numberOfGeometricBranches_eq_iSup_encard
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (x : X) :
    numberOfGeometricBranches X x =
      ⨆ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x,
        Set.encard {Z ∈ irreducibleComponents U.scheme | U.point ∈ Z}
declarations.comment: geometric_branches_supremum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numberOfBranches_eq_iSup_encard_irreducibleComponentsThrough
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB4.** The number of branches at a point is the
supremum, over elementary étale neighborhoods, of the number of irreducible
components passing through the distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
theorem numberOfBranches_eq_iSup_encard_irreducibleComponentsThrough
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X) :
    numberOfBranches X x =
      ⨆ (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (_ : U.IsElementary),
        Set.encard {Z ∈ irreducibleComponents U.scheme | U.point ∈ Z}
declarations.comment: branches_supremum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUnibranchAt_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB4.** A scheme is unibranch at a point if and only if every
elementary étale neighbourhood of that point has exactly one irreducible component passing
through its distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnibranchAt_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X) :
    IsUnibranchAt X x ↔
      ∀ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x, U.IsElementary →
        ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents U.scheme, U.point ∈ (Z : Set U.scheme)
declarations.comment: unibranch_iff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB4.** A scheme is geometrically unibranch at a point if and only if
every étale neighbourhood of that point has exactly one irreducible component passing through its
distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X) :
    IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt X x ↔
      ∀ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x,
        ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents U.scheme, U.point ∈ (Z : Set U.scheme)
declarations.comment: geometrically_unibranch_iff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numberOfBranches_fiber_eq_iSup_encard_irreducibleComponentsThrough
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB5.** The branches of a fibre are counted by
irreducible components through the distinguished points of fibres of
elementary étale neighborhoods.
declarations.statement:
public theorem numberOfBranches_fiber_eq_iSup_encard_irreducibleComponentsThrough
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    numberOfBranches (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) =
      ⨆ (U : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (_ : U.IsElementary),
        Set.encard
          {Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)) |
            ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiberHomeo (f x)).symm
              ⟨U.point, by simp [U.map_point]⟩ ∈ Z}
declarations.comment: fibre_branches

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.numberOfGeometricBranches_fiber_eq_iSup_encard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB5.** Geometric branches of a fibre are counted by
irreducible components through the distinguished points of fibres of étale
neighbourhoods.
declarations.statement:
public theorem numberOfGeometricBranches_fiber_eq_iSup_encard
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    numberOfGeometricBranches (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) =
      ⨆ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x,
        Set.encard
          {Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)) |
            ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiberHomeo (f x)).symm
              ⟨U.point, by simp [U.map_point]⟩ ∈ Z}
declarations.comment: fibre_geometric_branches

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isUnibranchAt_fiber_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB5.** The fibre is unibranch at the point if and only if for every
elementary étale neighbourhood of the point in the total space there is exactly one irreducible
component of its fibre passing through the distinguished point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isUnibranchAt_fiber_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    IsUnibranchAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) ↔
      ∀ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x, U.IsElementary →
        ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)),
          ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiberHomeo (f x)).symm ⟨U.point, by simp [U.map_point]⟩ ∈
            (Z : Set ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)))
declarations.comment: fibre_unibranch_iff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_fiber_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CB5, part (4), stated about the fibre.** The fibre is geometrically
unibranch at the point if and only if for every étale neighbourhood of the point in the total
space there is exactly one irreducible component of its fibre passing through the distinguished
point.

The source states part (4) as "`X` is geometrically unibranch at `x`", not `X_s`, while its
right-hand side is about the irreducible components of the *fibre* `U_s`. That pairing of `X`
with `U_s` is the asymmetry: parts (1), (2) and (3) are all about `X_s`, part (4) is the
geometric counterpart of part (3), and the cited proof (Tags 0CB4 and 0CAS) yields the statement
about the fibre. The fibre statement is what is proved here; the deviation from the literal text
of part (4) is recorded rather than silently adopted.

The deviation is not a choice between two defensible readings:
`AlgebraicGeometry.not_forall_isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent`
refutes the literal statement about `X`, so the reading about the fibre proved here is the only
true one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_fiber_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) ↔
      ∀ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x,
        ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)),
          ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiberHomeo (f x)).symm ⟨U.point, by simp [U.map_point]⟩ ∈
            (Z : Set ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)))
declarations.comment: fibre_geometrically_unibranch_iff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_forall_isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent
declarations.doc:
It is not true that for every morphism `f : X ⟶ S` and every point `x` of `X`, `X` is
geometrically unibranch at `x` if and only if for every étale neighbourhood `(U, u)` of `(X, x)`
there is exactly one irreducible component of the fibre of `U ⟶ S` over `f x` through `u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isGeometricallyUnibranchAt_iff_existsUnique_irreducibleComponent :
    ¬ ∀ (X S : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X),
        IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt X x ↔
          ∀ U : EtaleNeighborhood X x,
            ∃! Z : irreducibleComponents ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)),
              ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiberHomeo (f x)).symm ⟨U.point, by simp [U.map_point]⟩ ∈
                (Z : Set ((U.toBase ≫ f).fiber (f x)))
declarations.comment: part (4) as printed, about X rather than X_s, is FALSE: counterexample

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal_iff_exists_idealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
For a pre-admissible source, finite type modulo every weak ideal of definition is equivalent
to finite type modulo some ideal of definition, with tautness in both conditions.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal_iff_exists_idealOfDefinition
    {B A : Type*} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (φ : B →+* A) (hB : TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible B) :
    TopologicalRing.FiniteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal φ ↔
      (RingHom.IsTaut φ ∧
        ∃ J : Ideal B, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition J ∧
          (Ideal.quotientMap (I := J) (Ideal.closure (J.map φ)) φ
            (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp subset_closure)).FiniteType)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_diagonal
declarations.doc:
A property of all pairwise fibre products of representables over a presheaf passes to its
diagonal.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_diagonal (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (h : ∀ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : F.obj (op U)) (b : F.obj (op V)),
      ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (i : yoneda.obj W ≅ pullback (yonedaEquiv.symm a) (yonedaEquiv.symm b))
        (f : W ⟶ U ⨯ V),
        yoneda.map (f ≫ prod.fst) =
          i.hom ≫ pullback.fst (yonedaEquiv.symm a) (yonedaEquiv.symm b) ∧
        yoneda.map (f ≫ prod.snd) =
          i.hom ≫ pullback.snd (yonedaEquiv.symm a) (yonedaEquiv.symm b) ∧
        P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f)) :
    (P.inverseImage (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (diag F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheaf_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB7** for the sheafified Yoneda embedding of the big fppf site over `S`: if
every pair of scheme-valued points of an fppf sheaf `X` of `Type (u + 1)` has a fibre product
represented by an object `W` of the site whose canonical morphism to the product of the two
sources has `Q`, then the diagonal of `X` has `Q` relative to the sheafified Yoneda embedding.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheaf_diagonal (Q : MorphismProperty (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    [Q.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (h : ∀ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (α : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj U ⟶ X)
      (β : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj V ⟶ X),
      ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (i : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj W ≅ pullback α β)
        (f : W ⟶ U ⨯ V),
        (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map (f ≫ Limits.prod.fst) =
          i.hom ≫ pullback.fst α β ∧
        (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map (f ≫ Limits.prod.snd) =
          i.hom ≫ pullback.snd α β ∧
        Q f) :
    Q.relative (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) (diag X)
declarations.comment: for the sheafified Yoneda embedding, which is the one the diagonal of a formal algebraic space is tested against

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal_and_not_isIdealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the negative clause on the example of Stacks 0CB8. The maximal ideal of the
ring of integers of the field `ℂ_[p]` of `p`-adic complex numbers is a weak ideal of definition
of that admissible topological ring, and it is not an ideal of definition. So the two notions
differ, and the correspondence of Stacks 0AIV between weak ideals of definition and thickenings
cannot restrict to one between ideals of definition and thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal_and_not_isIdealOfDefinition :
    TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p)) ∧
      ¬ TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition (maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p))
declarations.comment: a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition, on the ring of integers of ℂ_[p]

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.isIdealOfDefinition_span_p
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ideal `(p)` is an ideal of definition of the ring of integers of
`ℂ_[p]`: its topology is the `(p)`-adic one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIdealOfDefinition_span_p :
    TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition
      (Ideal.span ({(p : PadicComplexInt p)} : Set (PadicComplexInt p)))
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.WeakIdealOfDefinitionExample.isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** In a local ring whose topology is `(π)`-adic, with the radical of `(π)` the
maximal ideal, the maximal ideal is a weak ideal of definition: it is open, and each of its
elements lies in the radical of `(π)`, hence is topologically nilpotent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal
    (hadic : IsAdic (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)))
    (hrad : (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)).radical = maximalIdeal A) :
    TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (maximalIdeal A)
declarations.comment: a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.WeakIdealOfDefinitionExample.isWeaklyAdmissible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** A complete local ring whose topology is `(π)`-adic, with the radical of
`(π)` the maximal ideal, is weakly admissible: the maximal ideal is a weak ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAdmissible
    (hadic : IsAdic (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)))
    (hcomplete : TopologicalRing.IsComplete A)
    (hrad : (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)).radical = maximalIdeal A) :
    TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A
declarations.comment: a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.WeakIdealOfDefinitionExample.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** A complete local ring whose topology is `(π)`-adic, with the radical of
`(π)` the maximal ideal, has an affine formal algebraic space as formal spectrum, with no
hypothesis on the chosen big fppf site beyond its containing the quotient spectra.

Completeness and the radical identity are part of the situation of the example but are not
needed for this particular conclusion, which holds for any adic topology; their names are
therefore prefixed by an underscore.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSpectrum
    (hadic : IsAdic (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)))
    (_hcomplete : TopologicalRing.IsComplete A)
    (_hrad : (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)).radical = maximalIdeal A)
    {B : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : B.Contains S}
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum D)
declarations.comment: a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.WeakIdealOfDefinitionExample.isRelativelyRepresentable_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The residue-field stage `Spec κ ⟶ Spf A` of the formal spectrum, that is
the colimit cocone map at the weak ideal of definition `𝔪`, is representable by objects of the
big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyRepresentable_residueField
    (hadic : IsAdic (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)))
    (hrad : (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)).radical = maximalIdeal A)
    {B : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : B.Contains S}
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    let J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I } :=
      ⟨maximalIdeal A, isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal π hadic hrad⟩
    (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable
      (formalSpectrumInclusion D (OrderDual.toDual J))
declarations.comment: a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.WeakIdealOfDefinitionExample.isThickening_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The residue-field stage `Spec κ ⟶ Spf A` of the formal spectrum is a
thickening: each of its base changes along a morphism from a represented sheaf is a thickening
of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_residueField
    (hadic : IsAdic (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)))
    (hrad : (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)).radical = maximalIdeal A)
    {B : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : B.Contains S}
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    let J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I } :=
      ⟨maximalIdeal A, isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal π hadic hrad⟩
    (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (formalSpectrumInclusion D (OrderDual.toDual J))
declarations.comment: a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.WeakIdealOfDefinitionExample.not_isIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** In a valuation ring whose topology is `(π)`-adic for some `π` in the
maximal ideal, the maximal ideal is not an ideal of definition if it is not finitely generated:
it is then idempotent, so all its powers coincide and cofinality of those powers would force
`𝔪 = (π)` to be principal.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal
    [IsDomain A] (hval : IsValuationRing A) (hπm : π ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (hadic : IsAdic (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)))
    (hnotfg : ¬ (maximalIdeal A).FG) :
    ¬ TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition (maximalIdeal A)
declarations.comment: a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: rationalPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** Finite sums `∑ a_α t^α` with `α` ranging over nonnegative rationals,
realised as the monoid algebra of `ℚ≥0` over `k`.
declarations.statement: abbrev rationalPolynomial (k : Type*) [CommRing k]
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: polynomialT
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0CB8.** The monomial `t = t^1` in `rationalPolynomial k`.
declarations.statement: def polynomialT (k : Type*) [CommRing k] : rationalPolynomial k
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: polynomialTIdeal
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0CB8.** The principal ideal `(t)` of `rationalPolynomial k`.
declarations.statement: def polynomialTIdeal (k : Type*) [CommRing k] : Ideal (rationalPolynomial k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: rationalPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of power series with nonnegative rational exponents over `k`,
constructed as the `(t)`-adic completion of `rationalPolynomial k`.
declarations.statement: abbrev rationalPowerSeries (k : Type*) [CommRing k]
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: CoefficientFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** Coefficient families `(a_α)_{α ∈ ℚ≥0}` in `k` having, for every natural
number `n`, only finitely many nonzero entries with `α ≤ n`.
declarations.statement: def CoefficientFamily (k : Type*) [Zero k]
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: coefficientRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The subring of `HahnSeries ℚ≥0 k` generated by the series whose support
is finite below every integer bound. `RationalPowerSeries.mem_coefficientRing_iff` shows that
the generating set is already a subring, so this is exactly the displayed ring of series.
declarations.statement: def coefficientRing (k : Type*) [CommRing k] : Subring (HahnSeries ℚ≥0 k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.t
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The element `π = t` of `rationalPowerSeries k`, the image of the
exponent-one monomial under the completion map.
declarations.statement: def t (k : Type*) [CommRing k] : rationalPowerSeries k
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.tIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The principal ideal `(t)` of `rationalPowerSeries k`, whose powers
define the topology.
declarations.statement: def tIdeal (k : Type*) [CommRing k] : Ideal (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.mem_coefficientRing_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** Membership in `coefficientRing k` is precisely local finiteness of the
support below every integer bound; in particular the generating set of `coefficientRing k` is
already a subring.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_coefficientRing_iff (k : Type*) [Field k] (f : HahnSeries ℚ≥0 k) :
    f ∈ coefficientRing k ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, {q : ℚ≥0 | q ≤ n ∧ f.coeff q ≠ 0}.Finite
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.exists_equiv_coefficientFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** Every coefficient family `(a_α)` is represented by a unique element of
the coefficient ring, with unchanged coefficients.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_equiv_coefficientFamily (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ∃ e : CoefficientFamily k ≃ coefficientRing k,
      ∀ f : CoefficientFamily k, ∀ q : ℚ≥0, ((e f).1).coeff q = f.1 q
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.exists_ringEquiv_coefficientRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The completed monoid algebra is the ring of locally finite coefficient
series, with the usual addition and convolution multiplication; the isomorphism preserves the
coefficients of polynomials.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringEquiv_coefficientRing (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ∃ e : rationalPowerSeries k ≃+* coefficientRing k,
      ∀ (p : rationalPolynomial k) (q : ℚ≥0),
        ((e (AdicCompletion.of (polynomialTIdeal k) (rationalPolynomial k) p)).1).coeff q =
          p.coeff q
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.isDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of power series with nonnegative rational exponents is a
domain.
declarations.statement: theorem isDomain (k : Type*) [Field k] : IsDomain (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.instIsDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of power series with nonnegative rational exponents is a
domain.
declarations.statement: instance instIsDomain (k : Type*) [Field k] : IsDomain (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.isLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of power series with nonnegative rational exponents is
local.
declarations.statement: theorem isLocalRing (k : Type*) [Field k] : IsLocalRing (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.instIsLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of power series with nonnegative rational exponents is
local.
declarations.statement: instance instIsLocalRing (k : Type*) [Field k] : IsLocalRing (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.isValuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** This local domain is a valuation ring: inside its fraction field it is
maximal for the domination order among local subrings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isValuationRing (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    IsValuationRing (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.t_mem_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The monomial `t` lies in the maximal ideal; in particular it is not a
unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem t_mem_maximalIdeal (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    t k ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.isAdic_span_t
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0CB8.** The topology of `rationalPowerSeries k` is the `(t)`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdic_span_t (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    IsAdic (Ideal.span ({t k} : Set (rationalPowerSeries k)))
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.isComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of power series with nonnegative rational exponents is
separated and complete for its `(t)`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isComplete (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    TopologicalRing.IsComplete (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.radical_span_t
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The radical of `(t)` is the maximal ideal: every non-unit has positive
order, so some power of it is divisible by `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem radical_span_t (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    (Ideal.span ({t k} : Set (rationalPowerSeries k))).radical =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (rationalPowerSeries k)
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.not_fg_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The maximal ideal is not finitely generated: finitely many elements of
the maximal ideal have a least positive order `a`, and the monomial of exponent `a / 2` is in
the maximal ideal but not in the ideal they generate.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_fg_maximalIdeal (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ¬ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (rationalPowerSeries k)).FG
declarations.comment: the rational power series valuation ring

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.isAdic_span_p
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The topology of the ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]`, inherited from `ℂ_[p]`, is
the `(p)`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdic_span_p :
    IsAdic (Ideal.span ({(p : PadicComplexInt p)} : Set (PadicComplexInt p)))
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.instIsLinearTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The topology of the ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]` is linear: the open ideals
form a basis of neighbourhoods of zero.
declarations.statement: instance instIsLinearTopology : IsLinearTopology (PadicComplexInt p) (PadicComplexInt p)
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.isComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]` is separated and complete for its
topology.
declarations.statement: theorem isComplete : TopologicalRing.IsComplete (PadicComplexInt p)
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.natCast_mem_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The element `p` of the ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]` lies in its maximal
ideal; in particular it is nonzero and not a unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem natCast_mem_maximalIdeal :
    (p : PadicComplexInt p) ∈ maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p)
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.radical_span_p
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The radical of the ideal `(p)` of the ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]` is its
maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem radical_span_p :
    (Ideal.span ({(p : PadicComplexInt p)} : Set (PadicComplexInt p))).radical =
      maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p)
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.isValuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]` is a valuation ring: inside its fraction
field it is maximal for the domination order among local subrings.
declarations.statement: theorem isValuationRing : IsValuationRing (PadicComplexInt p)
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.not_fg_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB8.** The maximal ideal of the ring of integers of `ℂ_[p]` is not finitely
generated: the valuation of `ℂ_[p]` takes arbitrarily small positive values, since `ℂ_[p]` is
algebraically closed, so no element of the maximal ideal generates it.
declarations.statement: theorem not_fg_maximalIdeal : ¬ (maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p)).FG
declarations.comment: the p-adic complex integers

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_iso_reduction_fibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CB9.** Let `X ⟶ Z` and `Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `iX : Xred ⟶ X`, `iY : Yred ⟶ Y` and `iZ : Zred ⟶ Z` be reductions and let `Xred ⟶ Zred` and
`Yred ⟶ Zred` be compatible with the two given morphisms. Let `P` be a fibre product of `X` and
`Y` over `Z`, let `Q` be a fibre product of `Xred` and `Yred` over `Zred`, and let
`iP : Pred ⟶ P` and `iQ : Qred ⟶ Q` be reductions of those two fibre products. Then the
inclusions of the reductions induce a morphism `Q ⟶ P` over which `Qred` and `Pred` are
isomorphic: `(X ×_Z Y)_red = (X_red ×_{Z_red} Y_red)_red`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_reduction_fibreProduct
    (_hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (_hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (_hZ : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (hiX : IsReduction B S hS X Xred iX) (hiY : IsReduction B S hS Y Yred iY)
    (hiZ : IsReduction B S hS Z Zred iZ)
    (hfred : fred ≫ iZ = iX ≫ f) (hgred : gred ≫ iZ = iY ≫ g)
    (hP : IsPullback p₁ p₂ f g) (hQ : IsPullback q₁ q₂ fred gred)
    (hiP : IsReduction B S hS P Pred iP) (hiQ : IsReduction B S hS Q Qred iQ) :
    ∃ (cmp : Q ⟶ P) (e : Qred ≅ Pred),
      cmp ≫ p₁ = q₁ ≫ iX ∧ cmp ≫ p₂ = q₂ ≫ iY ∧ e.hom ≫ iP = iQ ≫ cmp
declarations.comment: with reductions of the five spaces, and both fibre products, as hypotheses

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.LocalizationDiagram
declarations.doc:
A commutative localization diagram of countably indexed weakly admissible rings, with
étale horizontal maps and continuous vertical maps.
declarations.statement:
public structure LocalizationDiagram
    (A B A' B' : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [CommRing A'] [CommRing B']
declarations.comment: localization diagram

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocal
declarations.doc:
A property of morphisms of countably indexed weakly admissible rings is local if it
ascends along completed étale localization diagrams, descends along faithfully flat ones,
and is preserved by finite products of targets. The optional subclass parameter restricts
all four corners of each diagram and every ring in the finite-product family.
declarations.statement:
public structure PropertyIsLocal
    (P : ∀ {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
      [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A],
      (B →+* A) → Prop)
    (C : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R]
      [IsLinearTopology R R], Prop := IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible) : Prop
declarations.comment: local property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_monomorphismDiagonalSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CBB.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` and `g : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S`. If `f` is a monomorphism (Stacks 04ZW), then the canonical square

```text
  𝒳  --Δ_{𝒳/𝒴}-->  𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳
  |                     |
 f|                     | f × f
  v                     v
  𝒳' --Δ_{𝒳'/𝒴}--> 𝒳' ×_𝒴 𝒳'
```

`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.monomorphismDiagonalSquare` is a 2-fibre product in the 2-category of
algebraic stacks over `(Sch/S)_fppf`.

This is the source's proof: `𝒳 = 𝒳 ×_{𝒳'} 𝒳` by **Stacks 04ZZ**, the relative diagonal of the
monomorphism `f` being an equivalence, and the square is then the 2-cartesian square of
**Stacks 04Z1** precomposed with that equivalence.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.isEquivalence_monomorphism_diagonalComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CBB.** The square from the relative diagonal of a fully faithful functor `f` to
the relative diagonal of `f ⋙ g` is a 2-fibre product square: the induced functor into the
explicit 2-fibre product is an equivalence.

It is the composite of the relative diagonal of `f`, an equivalence because `f` is fully
faithful, with the Stacks 04Z1 comparison functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_monomorphism_diagonalComparison
    {X X' Y : Type*} [Category X] [Category X'] [Category Y]
    (f : X ⥤ X') (g : X' ⥤ Y) (hf : f.Full ∧ f.Faithful) :
    (relativeDiagonal f ⋙ toRelativeDiagonalPullback f f g).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_not_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CBC.** There exists an affine formal algebraic space which is not McQuillan: the
example of Stacks 0CBD admits no presentation by affine thickenings whose section-ring
projections are all surjective.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_sections_isField_reduction_infinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CBD.** There is an affine formal algebraic space whose regular functions do not
separate points: writing `X = colim X_λ` as in Stacks 0AI7, the inverse limit of the rings
`Γ(X_λ, O_{X_λ})` is a field, while the reduction of `X` has infinitely many points. The
reduction is exhibited as a reduced affine scheme `T` of the site together with a
representable thickening `T ⟶ X` through which every morphism to `X` from a reduced algebraic
space factors uniquely, which determines it up to unique isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_sections_isField_reduction_infinite :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (X : FppfSheaf B S hS),
      IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X ∧
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (pre : Preorder I),
        letI : Preorder I := pre
        Nonempty I ∧ IsDirected I (· ≤ ·) ∧
          ∃ D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS,
            (∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
              Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening
                ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f))) ∧
            Nonempty (X ≅ colimit
              (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
                Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))) ∧
            (letI : CommRing (sectionDiagram B S hS D ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}).sections :=
              @Subring.toCommRing (∀ j, (sectionDiagram B S hS D).obj j) _
                (RingCat.sectionsSubring
                  (sectionDiagram B S hS D ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat.{u}))
            IsField (sectionDiagram B S hS D ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}).sections)) ∧
      (∃ T : BigFppfOver B S hS,
        IsReduced ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) ∧
        Infinite ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) ∧
        ∃ ι : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T ⟶ X,
          (MorphismProperty.relative
            (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
            (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
              (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
              (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) ι ∧
          ∀ U : FppfSheaf B S hS, Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS U.obj →
            (∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).obj V ⟶ U.obj),
              (MorphismProperty.relative (uliftYoneda.{u + 1})
                (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
                  (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
                  (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) p ∧
              (MorphismProperty.relative (uliftYoneda.{u + 1})
                (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
                  (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
                  (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) p ∧
              IsReduced ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) →
            ∀ g : U ⟶ X, ∃! l : U ⟶
              (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T, l ≫ ι = g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_representable_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_not
declarations.doc:
There exists a representable morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of affine formal algebraic spaces with `Y`
McQuillan, but `X` not McQuillan. The morphism is representable by schemes, and every represented
base change of it is moreover an affine morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_representable_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_not :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (inS : B.Contains S) (X Y : FppfSheaf B S inS)
      (f : X ⟶ Y),
      IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S inS X ∧ IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S inS Y ∧
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S inS)).relativelyRepresentable f ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S inS)).relative
        (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S inS)) f ∧
      HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S inS Y ∧ ¬ HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S inS X

declarations.name: TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_directLimit
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` and `R → B` be ring maps, let `A = integralClosure R B` and let
`A' = integralClosure S (S ⊗[R] B)`. If `S` is `R`-algebra isomorphic to the colimit
`DirectLimit G F` of a directed system `G` of `R`-algebras and the canonical map
`G i ⊗[R] A → integralClosure (G i) (G i ⊗[R] B)` is bijective for every `i`, then the canonical
map `S ⊗[R] A → A'` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_directLimit
    {R S B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing B] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R B]
    {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, CommRing (G i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (G i)]
    (F : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → (G i →ₐ[R] G j)) [DirectedSystem G fun i j h ↦ F i j h]
    (e : DirectLimit G F ≃ₐ[R] S)
    (H : ∀ i, Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure R (G i) B)) :
    Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure R S B)
declarations.comment:
The colimit step of the tag, with the smoothness of the stages weakened to what
the argument uses: bijectivity of the map at each stage. The tag's own hypothesis is recovered in
`TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_directLimit_smooth` below. The filtered colimit is
spelled as a colimit over a directed nonempty preorder, presented by an `R`-algebra equivalence
`DirectLimit G F ≃ₐ[R] S` so that the conclusion is about an abstract `S`; the isomorphism of the
tag is bijectivity of Mathlib's canonical map `TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure`, as in the smooth
case 03GG. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_directLimit_smooth
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` and `R → B` be ring maps, let `A = integralClosure R B` and let
`A' = integralClosure S (S ⊗[R] B)`. If `S` is `R`-algebra isomorphic to the colimit
`DirectLimit G F` of a directed system `G` of smooth `R`-algebras, then the canonical map
`S ⊗[R] A → A'` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_directLimit_smooth
    {R S B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing B] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R B]
    {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, CommRing (G i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (G i)] [∀ i, Algebra.Smooth R (G i)]
    (F : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → (G i →ₐ[R] G j)) [DirectedSystem G fun i j h ↦ F i j h]
    (e : DirectLimit G F ≃ₐ[R] S) :
    Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure R S B)
declarations.comment:
The literal form of the tag, as the colimit step
`TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_directLimit` applied to the smooth case 03GG
(`TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_smooth`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_quasiFinite_affineSpace_factorization
declarations.doc: Relative Noether normalization on an affine neighbourhood of a point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_quasiFinite_affineSpace_factorization
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (x : X) (V : S.affineOpens) (hxV : f x ∈ V.1) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_hxU : x ∈ U.1)
      (_hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
      (π : U.1.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V.1.toScheme),
      (π ≫ (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V.1.toScheme).hom ≫ V.1.ι =
        U.1.ι ≫ f) ∧
      ((LocallyOfFiniteType π ∧ QuasiCompact π) ∧ LocallyQuasiFinite π)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_factorization_finite_fiber
declarations.doc: Noether normalization for a finite-type map of affine schemes at a chosen fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_finite_fiber {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (s : S) (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber s) = d) :
    ∃ π : X ⟶ 𝔸(ULift (Fin d); S),
      (π ≫ 𝔸(ULift (Fin d); S) ↘ S = f) ∧
      ∃ πs : f.fiber s ⟶ (𝔸(ULift (Fin d); S) ↘ S).fiber s,
        (πs ≫ (𝔸(ULift (Fin d); S) ↘ S).fiberι s = f.fiberι s ≫ π) ∧
        (πs ≫ (𝔸(ULift (Fin d); S) ↘ S).fiberToSpecResidueField s =
          f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
        IsFinite πs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBJ, unramified case.** A morphism of schemes unramified at `x`
factors, on an affine open neighbourhood of `x` lying over a prescribed affine open `V` of the
target, as an immersion into the spectrum of the derivative-localized monic hypersurface
`Γ(S, V)[t]_{g'}/(g)`, followed by the canonical map to the affine line over `V`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_isImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_unramifiedAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) (V : S.Opens)
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hxV : f x ∈ V) (hf : UnramifiedAt f x) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U)
      (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (P : StandardEtalePair Γ(S, V)),
      P.g = P.f.derivative ∧
        ∃ (j : U.toScheme ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.Ring)),
          IsImmersion j ∧
            j ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (aeval P.X).toRingHom) ≫
                Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Polynomial.C : Γ(S, V) →+* Γ(S, V)[X])) =
              f.resLE V U hUV ≫ hV.isoSpec.hom
declarations.comment:
unramified case; the étale case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_etaleAt`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBJ, étale case.** At a point where the morphism is étale, the
immersion of `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_unramifiedAt` may
be chosen to be an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_isOpenImmersion_specMap_derivativePair_of_etaleAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) (V : S.Opens)
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hxV : f x ∈ V) (hf : EtaleAt f x) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U)
      (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (P : StandardEtalePair Γ(S, V)),
      P.g = P.f.derivative ∧
        ∃ (j : U.toScheme ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.Ring)),
          IsOpenImmersion j ∧
            j ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (aeval P.X).toRingHom) ≫
                Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Polynomial.C : Γ(S, V) →+* Γ(S, V)[X])) =
              f.resLE V U hUV ≫ hV.isoSpec.hom
declarations.comment: étale case; the unramified case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteDimensional_relativeCotangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBK, finiteness of `r`.** For a morphism locally of finite type the
residue-field fibre at `x` of the stalk of the sheaf of relative differentials is a
finite-dimensional `κ(x)`-vector space, so the integer `r` of the tag is defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_relativeCotangentSpace {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    FiniteDimensional (X.residueField x) (relativeCotangentSpace f x)
declarations.comment: finiteness of r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_relativeCotangentSpace_eq_fiberRelativeCotangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBK, first equality defining `r`.** The residue-field fibre of the
stalk of `Ω_{X/S}` at `x` and the corresponding fibre computed on the scheme-theoretic fibre
through `x` have the same dimension over `κ(x)`:
`dim_{κ(x)} Ω_{X/S,x} ⊗ κ(x) = dim_{κ(x)} Ω_{X_s/s,x} ⊗ κ(x)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_relativeCotangentSpace_eq_fiberRelativeCotangentSpace
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    Module.finrank (X.residueField x) (relativeCotangentSpace f x) =
      Module.finrank (X.residueField x) (fiberRelativeCotangentSpace f x)
declarations.comment: first equality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_relativeCotangentSpace_eq_finrank_dottedTangentArrow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBK, second equality defining `r`.** The residue-field fibre of the
stalk of `Ω_{X/S}` at `x` and the relative tangent space at `x` have the same dimension over
`κ(x)`: `dim_{κ(x)} Ω_{X/S,x} ⊗ κ(x) = dim_{κ(x)} T_{X/S,x}`. The tangent space is the
`𝒪_{X,x}`-linear dual of the stalk, which is the `κ(x)`-linear dual of the fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_relativeCotangentSpace_eq_finrank_dottedTangentArrow
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X) :
    Module.finrank (X.residueField x) (relativeCotangentSpace f x) =
      Module.finrank (X.residueField x) (DottedTangentArrow f x)
declarations.comment: second equality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_factorization_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBK.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a finite type morphism of affine schemes
and let `x` be a point of `X`. If `r` is the dimension over `κ(x)` of the residue-field fibre at
`x` of the stalk of the sheaf of relative differentials, then `f` factors as `X ⟶ 𝐀^r_S ⟶ S`
with the first morphism unramified at `x`.

The coordinates of the factorization are `r` global sections of `X` whose differentials span
that fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_unramifiedAt {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (x : X) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : Module.finrank (X.residueField x) (relativeCotangentSpace f x) = r) :
    ∃ π : X ⟶ 𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin r); S),
      (π ≫ 𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin r); S) ↘ S = f) ∧ UnramifiedAt π x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_immersion_into_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBL, first clause.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let
`x` be a point of `X` and let `V` be an affine open neighbourhood of its image. If `r` is the
