dimension over `κ(x)` of the residue-field fibre at `x` of the stalk of the sheaf of relative
differentials, then `f` restricted to some affine open `U ∋ x` lying over `V` factors as an
immersion into relative affine `(r+1)`-space over `V` followed by the projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_immersion_into_affineSpace {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (V : S.affineOpens) (hxV : f x ∈ V.1) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : Module.finrank (X.residueField x) (relativeCotangentSpace f x) = r) :
    ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1) (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)
      (j : U.1.toScheme ⟶ 𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1)); V.1.toScheme)),
      IsImmersion j ∧
        j ≫ 𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin (r + 1)); V.1.toScheme) ↘ V.1.toScheme =
          f.resLE V.1 U.1 hUV
declarations.comment: clause (1): the immersion into affine (r+1)-space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closedImmersion_smoothFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBL, second clause.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_immersion_into_affineSpace`, the affine open `U` may instead
be taken to be a closed subscheme of a scheme smooth of relative dimension `r` over `V`, through
which the restriction of `f` factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedImmersion_smoothFactorization {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) (V : S.affineOpens) (hxV : f x ∈ V.1) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : Module.finrank (X.residueField x) (relativeCotangentSpace f x) = r) :
    ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ U.1) (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) (D : Scheme.{u})
      (j : U.1.toScheme ⟶ D) (g : D ⟶ V.1.toScheme),
      IsClosedImmersion j ∧ SmoothOfRelativeDimension r g ∧
        j ≫ g = f.resLE V.1 U.1 hUV
declarations.comment: clause (2): the closed immersion into a smooth scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalization_baseChange_henselization
declarations.doc:
The base change of the normalization morphism of a locally Noetherian scheme `X` to the
spectrum of the henselization of the local ring of `X` at a point is the normalization morphism
of that spectrum.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalization_baseChange_henselization (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (x : X) (Ah : Type u) [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ah]
    [IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) Ah] :
    haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ah :=
      IsLocalRing.isNoetherianRing_of_isHenselization (A := X.presheaf.stalk x) (B := Ah)
        (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    Nonempty
      (Over.mk (pullback.snd
          (Scheme.normalization X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isCompact X))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ah)) ≫
            X.fromSpecStalk x)) ≅
        Over.mk (Scheme.normalization (Spec (.of Ah))
          (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isCompact (Spec (.of Ah)))))
declarations.comment: henselization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalization_baseChange_strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
The base change of the normalization morphism of a locally Noetherian scheme `X` to the
spectrum of a strict henselization of the local ring of `X` at a point is the normalization
morphism of that spectrum.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normalization_baseChange_strictHenselization (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X) (Ash : Type u) [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash]
    [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash] (ksep : Type v) [Field ksep]
    [Algebra (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ksep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) ksep]
    [IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) ksep Ash] :
    haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ash :=
      IsLocalRing.isNoetherianRing_of_isHenselization (A := X.presheaf.stalk x) (B := Ash) ksep
    Nonempty
      (Over.mk (pullback.snd
          (Scheme.normalization X (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isCompact X))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash)) ≫
            X.fromSpecStalk x)) ≅
        Over.mk (Scheme.normalization (Spec (.of Ash))
          (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isCompact (Spec (.of Ash)))))
declarations.comment: strict_henselization

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBP.** The pullback of a strict normal crossings divisor along a
smooth morphism is a strict normal crossings divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_comap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) [Smooth f] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor D) :
    @IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor Y (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f)
      (D.comap f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isNormalCrossingsDivisor_comap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBQ.** The pullback of a normal crossings divisor along a smooth
morphism is a normal crossings divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalCrossingsDivisor_comap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) [Smooth f] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsNormalCrossingsDivisor D) :
    @IsNormalCrossingsDivisor Y (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f) (D.comap f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isClopen_normalizationDistinctLocus
declarations.doc:
`Z_n` is open and closed in the fibre power of the normalization, once the latter is
unramified.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClopen_normalizationDistinctLocus [Unramified (divisorNormalization D)]
    (n : ℕ) : IsClopen (fibrePowerDistinctLocus (divisorNormalization D) n)
declarations.comment:
first paragraph of the proof: `Z_n` is an open and closed subscheme of the fibre
power of the normalization. Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.unramified_normalizationDistinctToAmbient
declarations.doc:
Once the normalization of `D` is unramified, `Z_n ⟶ X` is unramified: it is the composition
of an open immersion, an iterated base change of the normalization, and a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_normalizationDistinctToAmbient
    [Unramified (divisorNormalization D)] (n : ℕ) :
    Unramified (normalizationDistinctToAmbient D n)
declarations.comment:
first paragraph of the proof: `Z_n ⟶ X` is unramified. Neither implication of the
equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.formallyUnramified_normalizationDistinctToAmbient
declarations.doc:
Once the normalization of `D` is unramified, `Z_n ⟶ X` is formally unramified, so that it
has a conormal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallyUnramified_normalizationDistinctToAmbient
    [Unramified (divisorNormalization D)] (n : ℕ) :
    FormallyUnramified (normalizationDistinctToAmbient D n)
declarations.comment:
first paragraph of the proof: `Z_n ⟶ X` is formally unramified, so the conormal
sheaf `𝒞_n` exists. Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.IsNormalizationCrossingsDivisor
declarations.doc:
Condition (2) of Tag 0CBR: the closed subscheme cut out by `D` is reduced, its normalization
is unramified, and every `Z_n` with `n ≥ 1` is regular and maps to the ambient scheme by a local
complete intersection morphism whose conormal sheaf is locally free of rank `n`.
declarations.statement: public def IsNormalizationCrossingsDivisor : Prop
declarations.comment:
condition (2). Its equivalence with condition (1),
`Stacks.Divisors.IsNormalCrossingsDivisor`, is not asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isReduced_of_isNormalCrossingsDivisor
declarations.doc:
A normal crossings divisor is reduced, which is the first clause of condition (2) of
Tag 0CBR. Étale-locally the divisor has strict normal crossings, hence is reduced by Tag 0BIA,
and reducedness descends along the faithfully flat maps that an étale chart induces on stalks of
the divisor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReduced_of_isNormalCrossingsDivisor (h : IsNormalCrossingsDivisor D) :
    IsReduced D.subscheme
declarations.comment:
the implication (1) to (2), restricted to its reducedness clause. The remaining
clauses of (2) under hypothesis (1), and the converse implication, are not asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isNormal_reducedComponent_of_isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor
declarations.doc:
An irreducible component of a strict normal crossings divisor, with its reduced induced
closed subscheme structure, is a normal scheme: it is regular by Tag 0BIA, and a regular scheme
is normal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_reducedComponent_of_isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor
    (h : IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor D) (C : irreducibleComponents D.subscheme) :
    IsNormal (D.subscheme.reducedComponent C)
declarations.comment: an input to the implication (1) to (2) in the strict case: an irreducible component of a strict normal crossings divisor, with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure, is normal. Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.unramified_divisorNormalization_of_isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor
declarations.doc:
The normalization of a strict normal crossings divisor is unramified, which is the
unramifiedness clause of condition (2) of Tag 0CBR in the strict case. The normalization is the
disjoint union of the normalizations of the irreducible components of the divisor, each component
is normal, so each of those normalization morphisms is an isomorphism, and what remains is a
disjoint union of closed immersions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_divisorNormalization_of_isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor
    (h : IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor D) : Unramified (divisorNormalization D)
declarations.comment: the implication (1) to (2) for a strict normal crossings divisor, restricted to the clause that the normalization of the divisor is unramified. The general normal crossings case, the remaining clauses of (2), and the converse implication are not asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isNormalCrossingsDivisor_iff_reduced_unramified_normalization
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and let `D ⊂ X` be a
closed subscheme. The following are equivalent:

1. `D` is a normal crossings divisor in `X`;
2. `D` is reduced, the normalization `ν : D^ν ⟶ D` is unramified, and for every `n ≥ 1` the
   scheme `Z_n`, obtained from the `n`-fold fibre power of `ν` over `D` by deleting the fat
   diagonal, is regular and the morphism `Z_n ⟶ X` is a local complete intersection morphism
   whose conormal sheaf is locally free of rank `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalCrossingsDivisor_iff_reduced_unramified_normalization {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData) :
    IsNormalCrossingsDivisor D ↔
      (IsReduced D.subscheme ∧
        ∃ hν : Unramified (divisorNormalization D), ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
          AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegular (normalizationDistinct D n) ∧
            IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism (normalizationDistinctToAmbient D n) ∧
              (letI : Unramified (divisorNormalization D) := hν
               haveI := formallyUnramified_normalizationDistinctToAmbient D n
               SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
                 (Stacks.Thickenings.universalConormalSheaf
                   (normalizationDistinctToAmbient D n)) n))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isIntegralHom_divisorNormalization
declarations.doc:
The normalization of the closed subscheme cut out by a divisor on a locally Noetherian scheme
is an integral morphism.
declarations.statement: public instance isIntegralHom_divisorNormalization : IsIntegralHom (divisorNormalization D)
declarations.comment: the proof of (2) to (1), first step: the normalization `ν : D^ν ⟶ D` is integral. Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isFinite_divisorNormalization
declarations.doc:
An unramified normalization of the closed subscheme cut out by a divisor on a locally
Noetherian scheme is finite: it is integral and, being unramified, locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
public instance isFinite_divisorNormalization [Unramified (divisorNormalization D)] :
    IsFinite (divisorNormalization D)
declarations.comment: the proof of (2) to (1), first step: an unramified `ν` is finite, being integral and locally of finite type (Tag 01WJ). Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isFinite_divisorNormalizationToAmbient
declarations.doc:
The morphism `D^ν ⟶ X` is finite when the normalization of `D` is unramified: it is the
composition of the finite normalization with a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
public instance isFinite_divisorNormalizationToAmbient
    [Unramified (divisorNormalization D)] : IsFinite (divisorNormalizationToAmbient D)
declarations.comment: the proof of (2) to (1), second step: `D^ν ⟶ X` is finite. Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.unramified_divisorNormalizationToAmbient
declarations.doc:
The morphism `D^ν ⟶ X` is unramified when the normalization of `D` is: it is the composition
of the unramified normalization with a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem unramified_divisorNormalizationToAmbient
    [Unramified (divisorNormalization D)] : Unramified (divisorNormalizationToAmbient D)
declarations.comment: the proof of (2) to (1), second step: `D^ν ⟶ X` is unramified. Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_closed_decomposition_divisorNormalization
declarations.doc:
Around any point of the ambient scheme the normalization of `D` becomes, after an étale base
change, a finite disjoint union of closed subschemes of the étale neighbourhood: the morphism
`D^ν ⟶ X` is finite and unramified, so Tag 04HJ applies to it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_disjoint_closed_decomposition_divisorNormalization
    [Unramified (divisorNormalization D)] (p : X) :
    ∃ (U : EtaleNeighborhood X p) (n : ℕ)
      (V : Fin n → (pullback (divisorNormalizationToAmbient D) U.toBase).Opens),
      sSup (Set.range V) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (Disjoint on V) ∧
        ∀ j, IsClosedImmersion
          ((V j).ι ≫ pullback.snd (divisorNormalizationToAmbient D) U.toBase)
declarations.comment: the proof of (2) to (1), third step: étale-locally on `X` the normalization is a finite disjoint union of closed subschemes of the étale neighbourhood (Tag 04HJ). The further shrinking making the chosen point lie on every `D_i` is not asserted, nor is either implication of the equivalence.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.normalizationDistinctOneIso
declarations.doc:
The scheme `Z_1` is the normalization of `D` itself: a one-fold fibre power has empty fat
diagonal and is the normalization.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def normalizationDistinctOneIso :
    normalizationDistinct D 1 ≅ divisorNormalizationScheme D
declarations.comment: the identification `Z_1 = D^ν` used in the proof of (2) to (1). Neither implication of the equivalence is asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isRegular_divisorNormalizationScheme
declarations.doc:
Condition (2) of Tag 0CBR makes the normalization of `D` a regular scheme: it is the scheme
`Z_1` of that condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_divisorNormalizationScheme (h : IsNormalizationCrossingsDivisor D) :
    IsRegular (divisorNormalizationScheme D)
declarations.comment: the proof of (2) to (1), fourth step, partially: the hypothesis on `Z_1` makes `D^ν` regular. The conclusion that each `D_i` is an effective Cartier divisor is not asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_divisorNormalizationToAmbient
declarations.doc:
Condition (2) of Tag 0CBR makes `D^ν ⟶ X` a local complete intersection morphism: it is the
morphism `Z_1 ⟶ X` of that condition, up to the identification of `Z_1` with the
normalization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_divisorNormalizationToAmbient
    (h : IsNormalizationCrossingsDivisor D) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism (divisorNormalizationToAmbient D)
declarations.comment: the proof of (2) to (1), fourth step, partially: the hypothesis on `Z_1` makes `D^ν ⟶ X` a local complete intersection morphism. The conclusion that each `D_i` is an effective Cartier divisor is not asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_comap_fromSpecStalk_of_isNormalCrossingsDivisor
declarations.doc:
**The strict henselization of a normal crossings divisor has strict normal crossings.** For `D`
a normal crossings divisor on a locally Noetherian scheme `X` and `x` a point of `D`, the pullback
of `D` to the spectrum of a strict henselization of `𝒪_{X, x}` is a strict normal crossings
divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_comap_fromSpecStalk_of_isNormalCrossingsDivisor
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsNormalCrossingsDivisor D) (x : X) (hx : ∃ y : D.subscheme, D.subschemeι y = x)
    (L : Type u) [Field L]
    [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) L]
    [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x)) L]
    (Ash : Type u) [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash]
    [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x) L Ash] :
    haveI : IsNoetherianRing Ash :=
      IsLocalRing.isNoetherianRing_of_isHenselization (A := X.presheaf.stalk x) L
    IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor (D.comap
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) Ash)) ≫
        X.fromSpecStalk x))

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_of_exists_regular_factorization
declarations.doc:
Let `D` be a closed subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme `X` which has strict normal
crossings at the strict henselizations, and suppose that at every point `p` of `D` the stalk ideal
is generated by a product `f₁ ⋯ f_k` of at least one element with each quotient
`𝒪_{X, p} / (fⱼ)` a regular local ring. Then `D` is a strict normal crossings divisor.

In Tag 0CBS the factorization hypothesis is what the J-2 or Nagata assumption produces, by
realizing a regular system of parameters of `𝒪^{sh}_{X, p}` on an étale neighbourhood and
shrinking it so that each of the resulting divisors is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor_of_exists_regular_factorization {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsStrictNormalCrossingsAtStrictHenselizations D)
    (hfac : ∀ x : X, x ∈ D.support → ∃ fs : List (X.presheaf.stalk x),
      (∀ f ∈ fs, IsRegularLocalRing ((X.presheaf.stalk x : Type u) ⧸ Ideal.span {f})) ∧
        1 ≤ fs.length ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheafData.stalk D x = Ideal.span {fs.prod}) :
    IsStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor D
declarations.comment:
(2) ⇒ (1), the step that upgrades condition (2) to strict normal crossings once
each local equation factors into regular factors. The construction of an étale chart on which it
does, which is where the J-2 or Nagata hypothesis of the lemma enters, is not asserted.

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isNormalCrossingsDivisor_iff_isStrictNormalCrossingsAtStrictHenselizations
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `D ⊂ X` a closed
subscheme. If `X` is J-2 or Nagata, then `D` is a normal crossings divisor in `X` if and only if
for every point `p` of `D` the pullback of `D` to the spectrum of the strict henselization
`𝒪^{sh}_{X, p}` is a strict normal crossings divisor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormalCrossingsDivisor_iff_isStrictNormalCrossingsAtStrictHenselizations
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsJ2 X ∨ IsNagataScheme X) :
    IsNormalCrossingsDivisor D ↔ IsStrictNormalCrossingsAtStrictHenselizations D

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_isStrictNormalCrossingsAtStrictHenselizations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBS, the effective Cartier divisor conjunct of (2) ⇒ (1).** A closed
subscheme of a locally Noetherian scheme whose inverse image to the spectrum of a strict
henselization of the local ring at each of its points is a strict normal crossings divisor is an
effective Cartier divisor. No J-2 or Nagata hypothesis is needed for this conjunct: the local
equation is recovered one point at a time by descent along the henselization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_of_isStrictNormalCrossingsAtStrictHenselizations
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (D : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hD : IsStrictNormalCrossingsAtStrictHenselizations D) :
    IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D
declarations.comment:
(2) ⇒ (1), the effective Cartier divisor conjunct of condition (1). The
étale-local strict normal crossings clause of (1) is not asserted, and no J-2 or Nagata
hypothesis is used for this conjunct.

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.quadraticAlgebra_equiv_adjoinRoot
declarations.doc:
The quadratic algebra of a node is isomorphic over the residue field `κ` to
`κ[X]/(a X² + b X + c)`, where `a`, `b`, `c` are the residues of the coefficients of a quadratic
relation `a x² + b x y + c y² ∈ 𝔪³` in lifted cotangent coordinates.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quadraticAlgebra_equiv_adjoinRoot (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (hA : IsNodalAlgebra k A)
    (x y : maximalIdeal A)
    (e : Module.Basis (BinaryIndex (ResidueField A)) (ResidueField A) (CotangentSpace A))
    (hx : e ⟨0⟩ = (maximalIdeal A).toCotangent x)
    (hy : e ⟨1⟩ = (maximalIdeal A).toCotangent y)
    (a b c : A) (ha : residue A a ≠ 0)
    (hdisc : residue A (4 * a * c - b ^ 2) ≠ 0)
    (hrelation : a * x.1 ^ 2 + b * x.1 * y.1 + c * y.1 ^ 2 ∈ (maximalIdeal A) ^ 3) :
    Nonempty (quadraticAlgebra A ≃ₐ[ResidueField A]
      AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.C (residue A a) * Polynomial.X ^ 2 +
        Polynomial.C (residue A b) * Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C (residue A c)))
declarations.comment: three_descriptions

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.quadraticAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The quadratic algebra associated to a local ring: the closed fibre of its normalization
inside its total ring of fractions.
declarations.statement: public abbrev quadraticAlgebra (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
declarations.comment: quadratic_algebra_associated_to_a_node

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.isSeparable_quadraticAlgebra_of_isNodalAlgebra
declarations.doc: The quadratic algebra of a nodal local ring is separable over its residue field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparable_quadraticAlgebra_of_isNodalAlgebra (hA : IsNodalAlgebra k A) :
    Algebra.IsSeparable (ResidueField A) (quadraticAlgebra A)
declarations.comment: degree_separable

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.finrank_quadraticAlgebra_of_isNodalAlgebra
declarations.doc: The quadratic algebra of a nodal local ring has degree two over its residue field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finrank_quadraticAlgebra_of_isNodalAlgebra (hA : IsNodalAlgebra k A) :
    Module.finrank (ResidueField A) (quadraticAlgebra A) = 2
declarations.comment: degree_separable

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.quadraticAlgebraSpecIsoNormalizationFiber
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of the quadratic algebra associated to a node is the fibre of the
normalization over that node.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quadraticAlgebraSpecIsoNormalizationFiber
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X)
    (hnode :
      let kToStalk : k →+* X.presheaf.stalk x :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom
      letI : Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x) := kToStalk.toAlgebra
      IsNodalAlgebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    let hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) →
        (irreducibleComponents U).Finite := fun U hU ↦ by
      let : CompactSpace U := isCompact_iff_compactSpace.mp hU
      let : NoetherianSpace U :=
        noetherianSpace_of_isLocallyNoetherianSpace U
          ((isLocallyNoetherianSpace_of_isLocallyNoetherian X).subtype U)
      exact NoetherianSpace.finite_irreducibleComponents
    letI : Algebra (X.residueField x)
        (quadraticAlgebra (X.presheaf.stalk x)) := by
      change Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x))
        (quadraticAlgebra (X.presheaf.stalk x))
      infer_instance
    Nonempty
      (Over.mk (Spec.map (
        let A := X.presheaf.stalk x
        let B := integralClosure A (FractionRing A)
        let J := (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B)
        let f : A →+* (B ⧸ J) := (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp (algebraMap A B)
        let g : IsLocalRing.ResidueField A →+* (B ⧸ J) :=
          Ideal.Quotient.lift (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) f fun _a ha ↦
            Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr
              (Ideal.mem_map_of_mem (algebraMap A B) ha)
        let g' : @RingHom (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (B ⧸ J)
            (X.residueField x).commRing.toCommSemiring.toNonAssocSemiring
            (CommRingCat.of (B ⧸ J)).commRing.toCommSemiring.toNonAssocSemiring := {
          toFun := g
          map_one' := g.map_one
          map_mul' := g.map_mul
          map_zero' := g.map_zero
          map_add' := g.map_add }
        CommRingCat.ofHom g')) ≅
        Over.mk (pullback.snd (Scheme.normalization X hX)
          (X.fromSpecResidueField x)))
declarations.comment: normalization_fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.proj_associatedGraded_iso_quadraticAlgebraSpec
declarations.doc:
The projectivized associated graded ring at a node is the spectrum of its normalization
fibre. The grading is the one by the powers of the maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem proj_associatedGraded_iso_quadraticAlgebraSpec
    (hA : IsNodalAlgebra k A)
    (𝒢 : ℕ → AddSubgroup (AssociatedGraded.gradedRing (maximalIdeal A)))
    [GradedRing 𝒢]
    (h𝒢 : ∀ n, 𝒢 n = AddMonoidHom.range
      (DirectSum.of (fun i => AssociatedGraded.piece (M := A) (maximalIdeal A) i) n)) :
    Nonempty (Proj 𝒢 ≅ Spec (.of
      (quadraticAlgebra A)))
declarations.comment: three_descriptions

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.isSplitNode_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a nodal local algebra over a field `k`, with residue field `κ`, and let
`κ' = Stacks.Curves.quadraticAlgebra A` be the associated separable `κ`-algebra of degree two.
Then the following are equivalent: `κ'` is `κ × κ`; the nondegenerate quadratic form of Stacks
Tag 0C49 can be chosen to be `x y`; `A` has two branches; the integral closure of `A` in its
total ring of fractions has two maximal ideals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSplitNode_tfae
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra k A] (hA : IsNodalAlgebra k A) :
    List.TFAE [
      Nonempty (quadraticAlgebra A ≃ₐ[ResidueField A] (ResidueField A × ResidueField A)),
      ∃ (x y : maximalIdeal A)
        (e : Module.Basis (BinaryIndex (ResidueField A)) (ResidueField A) (CotangentSpace A)),
        e ⟨0⟩ = (maximalIdeal A).toCotangent x ∧
          e ⟨1⟩ = (maximalIdeal A).toCotangent y ∧
          (x : A) * (y : A) ∈ (maximalIdeal A) ^ 3,
      numberOfBranchesOfLocalRing A = 2,
      Set.encard
        (Set.univ : Set (MaximalSpectrum ↥(integralClosure A (FractionRing A)))) = 2]
declarations.comment: conditions (1)-(4); the completion condition (5) is not formalized

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.nonempty_algEquiv_adicCompletion_quotient_X_mul_X_iff_numberOfBranches_eq_two
declarations.doc:
**The completion condition for a split node.** Let `A` be a nodal local algebra over a field
`k`, with residue field `κ`. Then the completion of `A` at its maximal ideal is `κ[[x, y]]/(x y)`
as a `k`-algebra if and only if `A` has two branches — hence if and only if any one of the four
conditions of `Stacks.Curves.isSplitNode_tfae` holds.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_algEquiv_adicCompletion_quotient_X_mul_X_iff_numberOfBranches_eq_two
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [Algebra k A] (hA : IsNodalAlgebra k A) :
    Nonempty (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A ≃ₐ[k]
        (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) (ResidueField A) ⧸
          Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) (ResidueField A)) *
                        MvPowerSeries.X 1})) ↔
      numberOfBranchesOfLocalRing A = 2
declarations.comment: condition (5), the completion condition

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.IsSplitNode
declarations.doc:
A point of a scheme over `k` is a split node if it is a node, the structure map `k → κ(x)`
is bijective, and the quadratic algebra of `𝒪_{X, x}` is the trivial quadratic extension
`κ(x) × κ(x)`.
declarations.statement: def IsSplitNode (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.isSplitNode_tfae_normalizationFibre_adicCompletion
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSplitNode_tfae_normalizationFibre_adicCompletion
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    letI : Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫
        X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom.toAlgebra
    let ν := normalizationOverField k (X ↘ Spec (.of k))
    let c₁ : Prop := IsSplitNode k X x
    let c₂ : Prop :=
      IsNode k X x ∧
        ∃ x₁ x₂ : normalizationSchemeOverField k (X ↘ Spec (.of k)),
          x₁ ≠ x₂ ∧
            {y : normalizationSchemeOverField k (X ↘ Spec (.of k)) | ν y = x} = {x₁, x₂} ∧
              Function.Bijective (fieldToResidue (ν ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k))) x₁).hom ∧
                Function.Bijective (fieldToResidue (ν ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k))) x₂).hom
    let c₃ : Prop :=
      Nonempty (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) ≃ₐ[k]
        (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k ⧸
          Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k) * MvPowerSeries.X 1}))
    List.TFAE [c₁, c₂, c₃]

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.exists_algEquiv_adicCompletion_quotient_mvPowerSeries_of_isSplitNode
declarations.doc:
The completion at a split node of a flat, locally finite-type family over a Noetherian
local base is a nodal smoothing `A⟦x,y⟧/(xy-h)` over the completed base ring `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_adicCompletion_quotient_mvPowerSeries_of_isSplitNode
    {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S) (t : T)
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom t)
    [IsNoetherianRing (S.presheaf.stalk (f t))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hnode : letI := f.fiberOverSpecResidueField (f t)
      IsSplitNode (S.residueField (f t)) (f.fiber (f t)) (f.asFiber t)) :
    let R := S.presheaf.stalk (f t)
    let Q := T.presheaf.stalk t
    let A := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R
    let B := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Q) Q
    let φ : A →+* B := adicCompletionMap (f.stalkMap t).hom
      (maximalIdeal R) (maximalIdeal Q)
      (map_maximalIdeal_le (f.stalkMap t).hom)
    letI : Algebra A B := φ.toAlgebra
    ∃ h : A, h ∈ maximalIdeal A ∧
      Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) A ⧸
        Ideal.span {MvPowerSeries.X 0 * MvPowerSeries.X 1 - MvPowerSeries.C h}) ≃ₐ[A] B)

declarations.name: Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.nonempty_standardNodalDiagram_of_isAtWorstNodal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CBY.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one
and let `x` be a point of `X` at which the fibre `X_s` through it is *singular*. Then there is a
commutative diagram
```
X ←—— U ——→ W ——→ Spec ℤ[u, v, a]/(uv - a)
↓     ↓     ↓                ↓
S ←———————— V ——————————→ Spec ℤ[a]
```
in which `U ⟶ X`, `V ⟶ S` and `U ⟶ W` are étale, the right-hand square is cartesian, and some
point of `U` maps to `x`. The diagram is packaged as
`Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.StandardNodalDiagram`.

The whole content is `nonempty_standardNodalDiagram_of_mem_relativeSingular`, which is the same
statement with the singular point read on the relative singular subscheme `Sing(f)`; the two
spellings agree by `mem_relativeSingular_iff_not_smoothAt_fiber`, which is [Stacks, Tag 0C3K]
on a fibre.
declarations.comment: the whole statement.  The diagram is the structure `Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.StandardNodalDiagram`, whose fields are the tag's four morphisms with the three etaleness assertions, the commutativity of the left and the middle square, the cartesianness of the right-hand square over the standard nodal family `Spec Z[u,v,a]/(uv-a) -> Spec Z[a]`, and the point of `U` over `x`. The singular point of the fibre is spelled as the failure of smoothness of the fibre `X_s` over `kappa(s)` at `x`; the equivalent spelling as a point of the relative singular subscheme `Sing(f)`, which is the one the source's own first step carries, is `nonempty_standardNodalDiagram_of_mem_relativeSingular`, and the two agree by `mem_relativeSingular_iff_not_smoothAt_fiber` ([Stacks, Tags 0C3I and 0C3K])

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_locally_principal_ideal_not_invertible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CC0.** A nonzero ideal in a domain can be principal at every prime localization
without being invertible as a module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_locally_principal_ideal_not_invertible :
    ∃ (A : Type*) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (I : Ideal A),
      I ≠ ⊥ ∧
      (∀ (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime],
        Submodule.IsPrincipal
          (I.map (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime q)))) ∧
      ¬ Module.Invertible A I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tfae_isDominant_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CC1.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of integral schemes, the
following are equivalent: `f` is dominant; it maps the generic point of `X` to that of `Y`;
the map on sections is injective for some, or for every, pair of nonempty affine opens
`U ⊆ X`, `V ⊆ Y` with `f(U) ⊆ V`; and the map on local rings is injective at some, or at
every, point of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_isDominant_of_isIntegral
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsDominant f,
      f (genericPoint X) = genericPoint Y,
      ∃ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens)
        (_ : Nonempty U.1) (_ : Nonempty V.1)
        (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        Function.Injective (f.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV),
      ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (V : Y.affineOpens)
        (_ : Nonempty U.1) (_ : Nonempty V.1)
        (hUV : U.1 ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        Function.Injective (f.appLE V.1 U.1 hUV),
      ∃ x : X, Function.Injective (f.stalkMap x),
      ∀ x : X, Function.Injective (f.stalkMap x)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.boundsFiberDegrees_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
declarations.doc: The degree of a finite locally free morphism bounds the degrees of all of its fibres.
declarations.statement:
theorem boundsFiberDegrees_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (d : ℕ)
    [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d] : BoundsFiberDegrees f (d : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTorsionFree_iff_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
On an integral regular scheme of dimension at most one a coherent module is torsion free if
and only if it is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_iff_isFiniteLocallyFree {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    (hregular : IsRegular X) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (F : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] :
    (let : F.IsQuasicoherent := _root_.isQuasicoherent_of_isCoherent F
     IsTorsionFree F) ↔ SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.injective_picardPullback_of_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CC5.** Let `k'/k` be a field extension and let `X` be a scheme over
`k` such that (1) `X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and (2) `R = H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` is
semi-local. Then the pullback map `Pic(X) → Pic(X_{k'})` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_picardPullback_of_fieldExtension
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] (φ : k →+* k')
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum Γ(X, ⊤))] :
    Function.Injective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom
      (Limits.pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))))
declarations.comment: The lemma proper; the parenthetical sufficient condition `dim_k H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) < ∞` for semi-locality is `injective_picardPullback_of_finiteDimensional`

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.injective_picardPullback_of_finiteDimensional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CC5** with its parenthetical hypothesis: hypothesis (2) holds as soon
as `dim_k H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` is finite, `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` being then Artinian and hence semi-local.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_picardPullback_of_finiteDimensional
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] (φ : k →+* k')
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (hfd : letI := globalSectionsAlgebra f; FiniteDimensional k Γ(X, ⊤)) :
    Function.Injective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom
      (Limits.pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))))
declarations.comment: The parenthetical sufficient condition `dim_k H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) < ∞` for hypothesis (2); the lemma proper is `injective_picardPullback_of_fieldExtension`

declarations.name: Stacks.Frobenius.absoluteFrobenius_naturality
declarations.doc:
The absolute Frobenius is natural with respect to morphisms of schemes in characteristic
`p`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.absoluteFrobenius_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
The absolute Frobenius of a scheme in positive prime characteristic is a universal
homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
instance absoluteFrobenius_universalHomeomorphism
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hX : IsInCharacteristic X p) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism (absoluteFrobenius X p hX)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.absoluteFrobenius_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc: The absolute Frobenius of a scheme in positive prime characteristic is integral.
declarations.statement:
instance absoluteFrobenius_isIntegralHom
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hX : IsInCharacteristic X p) :
    IsIntegralHom (absoluteFrobenius X p hX)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.absoluteFrobenius_residueFieldMap_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
The map on residue fields induced by the absolute Frobenius is purely inseparable at every
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem absoluteFrobenius_residueFieldMap_isPurelyInseparable
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hX : IsInCharacteristic X p)
    (x : X) :
    ((absoluteFrobenius X p hX).residueFieldMap x).hom.IsPurelyInseparable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.frobeniusTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CC9.** Frobenius twisting is base change along the absolute
Frobenius of the base scheme. Its value at `X : Over S` is `X ×_S S`, regarded as an
`S`-scheme through the second projection.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def frobeniusTwist (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) : Over S ⥤ Over S
declarations.comment: frobenius_twist

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_existsUnique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CC9.** The relative Frobenius is the unique morphism over `S`
whose first projection is the absolute Frobenius of `X` and whose second projection is the
structure morphism of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeFrobenius_existsUnique (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (X : Over S) :
    ∃! g : X ⟶ (frobeniusTwist S p hS).obj X,
      (g.left ≫ pullback.fst X.hom (absoluteFrobenius S p hS) =
          absoluteFrobenius X.left p (isInCharacteristic_of_hom X.hom p hS)) ∧
      (g.left ≫ pullback.snd X.hom (absoluteFrobenius S p hS) = X.hom)
declarations.comment: relative_frobenius_characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0CC9.** The relative Frobenius morphism of an `S`-scheme.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def relativeFrobenius (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (X : Over S) : X ⟶ (frobeniusTwist S p hS).obj X
declarations.comment: relative_frobenius

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_naturality
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0CCA.** The relative Frobenius is natural in an `S`-scheme.
declarations.statement:
public lemma relativeFrobenius_naturality (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) {X Y : Over S} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    relativeFrobenius S p hS X ≫ (frobeniusTwist S p hS).map f =
      f ≫ relativeFrobenius S p hS Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc: The relative Frobenius is a universal homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
instance relativeFrobenius_universalHomeomorphism
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p)
    (X : Over S) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc: The relative Frobenius is integral.
declarations.statement:
instance relativeFrobenius_isIntegralHom
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p)
    (X : Over S) :
    IsIntegralHom (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_residueFieldMap_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc: Every residue-field extension induced by the relative Frobenius is purely inseparable.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeFrobenius_residueFieldMap_isPurelyInseparable
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p)
    (X : Over S) (x : X.left) :
    (((relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left).residueFieldMap x).hom.IsPurelyInseparable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_toRelativeDifferentials_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCC.** The canonical map from the differentials of
`X` over `S` to the differentials of `X` over its Frobenius twist is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeFrobenius_toRelativeDifferentials_isIso
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (X : Over S) :
    IsIso (Scheme.Hom.toRelativeDifferentials
      (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left ((frobeniusTwist S p hS).obj X).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCD.** The relative Frobenius of an `S`-scheme locally of finite type
over `S` is finite.
declarations.statement:
instance relativeFrobenius_isFinite (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (X : Over S) [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] :
    IsFinite (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_iff_isReduced_frobeniusTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCE.** A scheme over a field of characteristic `p > 0` is
geometrically reduced if and only if its Frobenius twist is reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyReduced_iff_isReduced_frobeniusTwist
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    let hS : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p :=
      Stacks.Frobenius.isInCharacteristic_of_over (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))))
    GeometricallyReduced f ↔
      IsReduced (((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk f)).left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_frobeniusTwist_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCF.** For a reduced scheme `X` locally of finite type over a field
`k` of characteristic `p > 0`, the following are equivalent: the Frobenius twist of `X` is
reduced, `X` is geometrically reduced over `k`, and `X` has a dense open subscheme smooth over
`k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_frobeniusTwist_tfae
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsReduced X] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    let hS : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p :=
      Stacks.Frobenius.isInCharacteristic_of_over (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))))
    List.TFAE
      [IsReduced (((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk f)).left),
        GeometricallyReduced f,
        ∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f)]
declarations.comment: reduced_twist_tfae

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_frobeniusTwist_tfae_of_isVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCF.** For a variety `X` over a field `k` of characteristic `p > 0`,
the following are equivalent: the Frobenius twist of `X` is reduced, `X` is geometrically reduced
over `k`, and there is a nonempty open subscheme of `X` smooth over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_frobeniusTwist_tfae_of_isVariety
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f] :
    let hS : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p :=
      Stacks.Frobenius.isInCharacteristic_of_over (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))))
    List.TFAE
      [IsReduced (((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk f)).left),
        GeometricallyReduced f,
        ∃ U : X.Opens, (U : Set X).Nonempty ∧ Smooth (U.ι ≫ f)]
declarations.comment: reduced_twist_tfae, the variety form with a nonempty smooth open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.residueDegree_relativeFrobenius_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCF.** For a geometrically reduced integral scheme of dimension `d`,
locally of finite type over a field `k` of characteristic `p`, the residue degree of the
relative Frobenius at the generic point is `p ^ d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem residueDegree_relativeFrobenius_genericPoint
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] [IsIntegral X] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p) (hgeom : GeometricallyReduced pX)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d) :
    (relativeFrobenius (Spec (.of k)) p hS (Over.mk pX)).left.residueDegree (genericPoint X) =
      p ^ d
declarations.comment: frobenius_degree, as the residue degree at the generic point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.degreeOver_relativeFrobenius
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCF.** For a variety `X` of dimension `d` over a field `k` of
characteristic `p` whose Frobenius twist is reduced, the relative Frobenius of `X` has degree
`p ^ d` over the twist.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeOver_relativeFrobenius
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k pX]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (hS : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p)
    (hred : IsReduced (((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk pX)).left))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Over.mk pX).hom := inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType pX)
    letI : IsVariety k ((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk pX)).hom :=
      isVariety_frobeniusTwist_of_isReduced pX p hred
    degreeOver (relativeFrobenius (Spec (.of k)) p hS (Over.mk pX)).left = p ^ d
declarations.comment: frobenius_degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_isDominant
declarations.doc: The relative Frobenius is dominant over a base of prime characteristic.
declarations.statement:
instance relativeFrobenius_isDominant (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (X : Over S) :
    IsDominant (relativeFrobenius S p hS X).left
declarations.comment: finite_dominant

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVariety_frobeniusTwist_of_isReduced
declarations.doc: A reduced Frobenius twist of a variety over a field is a variety.
declarations.statement:
theorem isVariety_frobeniusTwist_of_isReduced
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsVariety k f] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] :
    let hchar : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p := by
      let φ : k →+* Γ(Spec (.of k), ⊤) := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv.hom
      change (p : Γ(Spec (.of k), ⊤)) = 0
      rw [← map_natCast φ, CharP.cast_eq_zero k p]
      exact map_zero φ
    IsReduced (((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hchar).obj (Over.mk f)).left) →
      IsVariety k (((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hchar).obj (Over.mk f)).hom)
declarations.comment: twist_variety

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nFoldFrobeniusTwist
declarations.doc:
The `n`-fold Frobenius twist of an `S`-scheme is its base change along the `n`-fold absolute
Frobenius of `S`, regarded as an `S`-scheme via the second projection.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev nFoldFrobeniusTwist (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (n : ℕ) (X : Over S) : Over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nFoldRelativeFrobenius
declarations.doc:
The morphism from an `S`-scheme to its `n`-fold Frobenius twist, with components the `n`-fold
absolute Frobenius and the structure morphism.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def nFoldRelativeFrobenius (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (n : ℕ) (X : Over S) :
    X ⟶ nFoldFrobeniusTwist S p hS n X
declarations.comment: n_fold_relative_frobenius

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nFoldRelativeFrobenius_eq_successiveRelativeFrobenius
declarations.doc:
The `(n+1)`-fold relative Frobenius is the composite of the relative Frobenius morphisms of
`X` and its first `n` successive twists, under the canonical identifications.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nFoldRelativeFrobenius_eq_successiveRelativeFrobenius
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ)
    [Fact p.Prime] (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (n : ℕ) (X : Over S) :
    nFoldRelativeFrobenius S p hS (n + 1) X =
      successiveRelativeFrobenius S p hS X n
declarations.comment: successive_composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeFrobenius_nFoldFrobeniusTwist
declarations.doc:
Under the canonical identification of the two orders of Frobenius twisting, relative
Frobenius on the `m`-fold twist is the `m`-fold base change of relative Frobenius on `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeFrobenius_nFoldFrobeniusTwist (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ)
    [Fact p.Prime] (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (m : ℕ) (X : Over S) :
    (Over.pullback (absoluteFrobeniusPow S p hS m)).map
        (relativeFrobenius S p hS X) ≫
      (frobeniusTwistCommIso S p hS m X).hom =
        relativeFrobenius S p hS (nFoldFrobeniusTwist S p hS m X)
declarations.comment: frobenius_on_twists

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nFoldRelativeFrobenius_eq_twistedRelativeFrobeniusComposite
declarations.doc:
The `(n+1)`-fold relative Frobenius is the composite of the first `n+1` Frobenius base
changes of the relative Frobenius of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nFoldRelativeFrobenius_eq_twistedRelativeFrobeniusComposite
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic S p) (n : ℕ) (X : Over S) :
    nFoldRelativeFrobenius S p hS (n + 1) X =
      twistedRelativeFrobeniusComposite S p hS X n
declarations.comment: twisted_composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_forall_exists_isAffineOpen

of schemes and let `D` be a descent datum relative to `f` whose underlying scheme `V` has the

        ∃ U : D.over.left.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ i, v i ∈ U) :
    DescentData.IsEffective D

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSeriesMorphism.exists_hom_over_and_hom_pullback_twistingSheafAtUniverse_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCP.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a nonsingular proper curve over `k` and
`(ℒ, V)` a `𝔤^r_d` on `X`. Then there are a morphism `φ : X ⟶ ℙ^r_k` of varieties over `k` — a
morphism lying over the structure morphism of `X` — and a map `α : φ ^* 𝒪(1) ⟶ ℒ` carrying
`φ ^* T_0, …, φ ^* T_r` to a basis of `V`.

Nonsingularity enters as integrality of `X` together with `hreg`; the properness and the
dimension bound are carried by `AlgebraicGeometry.LinearSeries`. The basis is the one supplied by
`nonempty_basis`, and the conclusion asserts that the `α`-images of the pulled-back coordinates
are the sections underlying it, which is the source's "are sent to a basis of `V`".
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hom_over_and_hom_pullback_twistingSheafAtUniverse_of_isRegular [IsIntegral X]
    (hreg : IsRegular X) (E : LinearSeries k f hdim d r) :
    ∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin (r + 1)) k E.V) (p : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOver r (Spec (.of k))),
      p ≫ (projectiveSpaceOver r (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) = f ∧
      ∃ α : (Scheme.Modules.pullback
          (p ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse r (Spec (.of k)))).obj
            (twistingSheafAtUniverse.{u} r) ⟶ E.L,
        ∀ i, α.app ⊤ (pullbackCoordSection.{u}
          (p ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse r (Spec (.of k))) i) =
          seriesSections E b i

    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (d r s : ℕ)
    (h : Nonempty (LinearSeries k f hdim d r)) (hs : s ≤ r) :
    Nonempty (LinearSeries k f hdim d s)

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSeriesMorphism.degreeOver_le_or_constant_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCR.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a nonsingular proper curve over `k`,
and `(ℒ, V)` a `𝔤¹_d` on `X`. Then the morphism `φ : X ⟶ 𝐏¹_k` of [Stacks, Tag 0CCP] either

1. is nonconstant and has degree `≤ d`, or
2. factors through a closed point of `𝐏¹_k`, and in this case `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) ≠ k`.

The whole tag is this one statement. **"The morphism of Lemma 53.3.2" is rendered by its
characterizing property.** [Stacks, Tag 0CCP] asserts the existence of a basis `b` of `V`, a
morphism `p : X ⟶ 𝐏¹_k` over `k`, and a map `α : p ^* 𝒪(1) ⟶ ℒ` carrying the pulled-back
coordinates `p ^* T₀, p ^* T₁` to the sections underlying `b`; it does not single one out, so
there is no term `φ (ℒ, V)` to name. The definite article is therefore read as the conjunction of
two assertions: the first is that such a triple `(b, p, α)` **exists** — which is
`Stacks.LinearSeriesMorphism.exists_hom_over_and_hom_pullback_twistingSheafAtUniverse_of_isRegular`
— and the second that **every** such triple satisfies the alternative, which is
`Stacks.LinearSeriesMorphism.degreeOver_le_or_constant` with its arguments universally
quantified. The second assertion is what makes this a statement about `φ` itself: it holds of
every morphism Tag 0CCP's property characterizes, so it is independent of any choice, and it is
strictly stronger than the assertion that *some* morphism to `𝐏¹_k` over `k` satisfies the
alternative. The two alternatives are mutually exclusive, by
`Stacks.LinearSeriesMorphism.not_constant_of_not_exists_eq`.

Hypotheses: `k` is a field; `X` is a proper curve over `k` (`[IsProper f]`, `[IsCurve k f]`) and
nonsingular (`hreg : IsRegular X`, integrality being already part of `IsCurve`); and
`E : LinearSeries k f hdim d 1` is a `𝔤¹_d`, the degree-`d` dimension-one linear series of
[Stacks, Tag 0CCN]. Nothing else is assumed.

Readings: the degree of `φ` is `AlgebraicGeometry.degreeOver`, the degree of the extension of
function fields ([Stacks, Tag 02NY]); `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) ≠ k` is `1 < Module.rank k H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)`, which
by `Stacks.LinearSeriesMorphism.not_nonempty_linearEquiv_of_one_lt_rank` rules out every
`k`-linear isomorphism `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) ≃ₗ[k] k`; and "factors through a closed point" is constancy
of `φ` together with closedness of its image point. **The closed point is not required to be
`k`-rational**, which is the point of Tongmu He's comment on the tag: over a `k` that is not
algebraically closed the morphism attached to two `k`-linearly independent sections can land on
a closed point whose residue field properly extends `k`, and alternative (2) asserts of `y` only
`IsClosed {y}`. See the module documentation for all of these.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeOver_le_or_constant_of_isRegular (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] [IsCurve k f] (hreg : IsRegular X)
    {hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1} {d : ℕ} (E : LinearSeries k f hdim d 1) :
    (∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin 2) k E.V) (p : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k))),
        p ≫ (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) = f ∧
        ∃ α : (Scheme.Modules.pullback
            (p ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse 1 (Spec (.of k)))).obj
              (twistingSheafAtUniverse.{u} 1) ⟶ E.L,
          ∀ i, α.app ⊤ (pullbackCoordSection.{u}
            (p ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse 1 (Spec (.of k))) i) =
            seriesSections E b i) ∧
      ∀ (b : Module.Basis (Fin 2) k E.V) (p : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)))
        (hp : p ≫ (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) = f)
        (α : (Scheme.Modules.pullback
            (p ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse 1 (Spec (.of k)))).obj
              (twistingSheafAtUniverse.{u} 1) ⟶ E.L),
        (∀ i, α.app ⊤ (pullbackCoordSection.{u}
          (p ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse 1 (Spec (.of k))) i) =
          seriesSections E b i) →
        (∃ _hnc : ¬ ∃ y : projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)), ∀ x : X, p.base x = y,
            @degreeOver X (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k))) p inferInstance inferInstance
              (locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k f
                (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) p hp)
              (isDominant_of_not_constant k f
                (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) p _hnc) ≤ d) ∨
          ((∃ y : projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)),
                IsClosed ({y} : Set (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)))) ∧
                ∀ x : X, p.base x = y) ∧
            1 < Module.rank k
              (cohomologyOverField k f (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) 0))
declarations.comment: the whole tag. `the morphism of Lemma 53.3.2` is rendered by the property that characterizes it: the data of Tag 0CCP exists for `(ℒ, V)`, and every datum of that shape satisfies the alternative. `factors through a closed point` is rendered as constancy of the morphism with closed image, nothing being asked of the residue field of that point, and `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) ≠ k` as `1 < Module.rank k H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.linearSeries_dimension_le_degree_and_genus_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper curve over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, spelled as invertibility of
the canonical map from `k`. If `X` has a `𝔤^r_d`, then `r ≤ d`, and if moreover `0 < d` and
`r = d`, then the genus of `X` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearSeries_dimension_le_degree_and_genus_eq_zero {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)]
    {hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1} {d r : ℕ} (series : LinearSeries k f hdim d r) :
    r ≤ d ∧ (0 < d → r = d → genus f = 0)
declarations.comment: both assertions, under the source's own hypotheses. Tag 02O6 at the structure sheaf, Tag 0B5T clause (4) and the ampleness of `ℒ` that the latter consumes are all proved here. `0 < d` is assumed for the equality clause because the source's statement is false at `r = d = 0`, by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_counterexample_to_displayed_statement_of_tag_0CCS_at_zero`

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.LinearlyEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCT.** Two effective Cartier divisors `D, D' ⊆ X` are *linearly
equivalent* when `𝒪_X(D) ≅ 𝒪_X(D')` as `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement: def LinearlyEquivalent (D D' : X.IdealSheafData) : Prop
declarations.comment: the classical definition of linear equivalence: 𝒪_X(D) ≅ 𝒪_X(D')

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.completeLinearSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCT.** The *complete linear system*, or *complete linear series*,
`|D|` of an effective Cartier divisor `D ⊆ X`: the set of effective Cartier divisors `E ⊆ X`
which are linearly equivalent to `D`.

declarations.comment: the complete linear system |D|: the effective Cartier divisors linearly equivalent to D

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSystemScheme.completeLinearSystem_eq_closedPoints_abelMapFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCT.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically
closed field `k` and `D ⊆ X` an effective Cartier divisor of degree `d`. The fibre
`Hilb^d_{X/k} ×_{Pic_{X/k}} Spec k` of the Abel map `γ_d : Hilb^d_{X/k} → Pic_{X/k}`,
`Z ↦ [𝒪(Z)]` (`AlgebraicGeometry.RigidifiedPicard.familyClass`), over the point `[𝒪_X(D)]` is
represented by `𝐏(H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨)`: its `T`-points are naturally the `k`-morphisms
`T ⟶ 𝐏(H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨)`. The closed points of this scheme are exactly the members of `|D|`, a
closed point corresponding to the image in `X` of the family over `Spec k` it classifies; the
closed point cut out by evaluation at a nonzero `s ∈ H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))` corresponds to the zero
scheme `Z(s)`. This is the scheme structure on `|D|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completeLinearSystem_eq_closedPoints_abelMapFibre {d : ℕ}
    (hd : invertibleCurveDegree k (B.inclusion.map g)
      (topologicalKrullDim_le_one k (B.inclusion.map g))
      (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) = d) :
    ∃ e : ∀ T : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk,
        ((BigFppfOver.toOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk).obj T ⟶
          (linearSystemScheme k (B.inclusion.map g) D).asOver (Spec (.of k))) ≃
          abelMapFibre B hX k g D d T,
      (∀ (T T' : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk) (h : T' ⟶ T)
          (p : (BigFppfOver.toOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk).obj T ⟶
            (linearSystemScheme k (B.inclusion.map g) D).asOver (Spec (.of k))),
        (e T' ((BigFppfOver.toOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk).map h ≫ p)).1.ideal =
          (e T p).1.ideal.comap (Stacks.Hilbert.familyBaseChangeMap
            (curveOver (B.inclusion.map g)) ((BigFppfOver.toOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk).map h))) ∧
      ∃ c : closedPoints (linearSystemScheme k (B.inclusion.map g) D) ≃
          Stacks.Divisors.completeLinearSystem D,
        (∀ x : closedPoints (linearSystemScheme k (B.inclusion.map g) D),
          (c x : (B.inclusion.obj (B.obj hX)).IdealSheafData) =
            (e (terminalTest B hk) (Over.homMk (@pointOfClosedPoint _ _ _ _
              (projectiveSpaceOfModuleToSpec k (dualSections k (B.inclusion.map g) D))
              (locallyOfFiniteType_linearSystemScheme k (B.inclusion.map g) D) x.1 x.2)
              (@pointOfClosedPoint_comp _ _ _ _ _
                (locallyOfFiniteType_linearSystemScheme k (B.inclusion.map g) D) x.1
                x.2))).1.ideal.comap
              (baseChangeTerminalIso B hX hk g).inv) ∧
        ∀ (s : cohomologyOverField k (B.inclusion.map g)
            (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) 0) (hs : s ≠ 0),
          (c ⟨ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.linearFunctionalPoint k _ (Module.Dual.eval k _ s)
              (eval_ne_zero k (B.inclusion.map g) D hs),
            ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.linearFunctionalPoint_isClosed k _ _
              (eval_ne_zero k (B.inclusion.map g) D hs)⟩ :
              (B.inclusion.obj (B.obj hX)).IdealSheafData) =
            zeroScheme _ (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D)
              (sectionOf k (B.inclusion.map g) (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) s)
declarations.comment: |D| is the set of closed points of the fibre of gamma_d : Hilb^d -> Pic over the point of O_X(D); this gives |D| a natural scheme structure

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSystemScheme.isLinearSystem_iff_exists_eq_iSup_zeroScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCT.** A closed subscheme `L ⊆ |D|` is a linear system exactly when it
is a closed subvariety cut out by linear equations: `L` is integral, and its ideal sheaf is
generated by the global sections of `𝒪(1)` given by the elements of a subspace
`E ⊆ W = H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨` of linear forms on `|D| = 𝐏(W)`, that is
`L = ⨆_{e ∈ E} Z(e)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLinearSystem_iff_exists_eq_iSup_zeroScheme
    (L : (linearSystemScheme k f D).IdealSheafData) :
    haveI := isInvertible_twistingSheaf_projectiveSpaceOfModule k (dualSections k f D)
      ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)
    IsLinearSystem k f D L ↔
      (∃ E : Submodule k (dualSections k f D),
        L = ⨆ e : E, AlgebraicGeometry.zeroScheme (linearSystemScheme k f D)
          (twistingSheafModule (fun n => SymPow.symmetricPower n k (dualSections k f D))
            ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
          (degreeSection (fun n => SymPow.symmetricPower n k (dualSections k f D)) 1
            ⟨SymmetricAlgebra.ι k (dualSections k f D) e,
              ProjectiveSpaceOfModule.ι_mem_symmetricPower_one k (dualSections k f D)
                (e : dualSections k f D)⟩)) ∧
        IsIntegral L.subscheme
declarations.comment: a linear system on X is a closed subvariety L of |D| which can be cut out by linear equations, the ideal sheaf of L being generated by linear forms

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSystemScheme.IsLinearSystem
declarations.doc:
A *linear system* (or *linear series*) on `X` is a closed subvariety `L ⊆ |D|` which can be
cut out by linear equations: `L` is the closed subscheme `V₊(E)` of a space `E` of linear forms
on `|D| = 𝐏(H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨)`, and it is integral.
declarations.statement: structure IsLinearSystem (L : (linearSystemScheme k f D).IdealSheafData) : Prop
declarations.comment: a linear system on X is a closed subvariety L of |D| which can be cut out by linear equations

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSystemScheme.IsLinearSystem.exists_eq_projectiveSpace
declarations.doc:
If a linear system `L ⊆ |D|` has dimension `r`, then `L = 𝐏(V^∨)` for a linear subspace
`V ⊆ H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))` of dimension `r + 1`: `L` is the image of the closed immersion
`𝐏(V^∨) ⟶ 𝐏(H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨)` induced by `V ⊆ H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))`, and it is isomorphic to
`𝐏(V^∨)` through that immersion. The subspace `V` is determined by `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLinearSystem.exists_eq_projectiveSpace {L : (linearSystemScheme k f D).IdealSheafData}
    (hL : IsLinearSystem k f D L) {r : ℕ} (hr : topologicalKrullDim L.subscheme = r) :
    ∃ (V : Submodule k (cohomologyOverField k f (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) 0))
      (_ : Module.finrank k V = r + 1),
      L = (subspaceImmersion k f D V).ker ∧
        (∀ V' : Submodule k
            (cohomologyOverField k f (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) 0),
          L = (subspaceImmersion k f D V').ker → V' = V) ∧
        ∃ φ : L.subscheme ≅ projectiveSpaceOfModule k (Module.Dual k V),
          φ.inv ≫ L.subschemeι = subspaceImmersion k f D V
declarations.comment: if L has dimension r, then L = P(V^dual) where V is a linear subspace of H^0(X, O_X(D)) of dimension r + 1

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSystemScheme.IsLinearSystem.linearSeries
declarations.doc:
The linear series `(𝒪_X(D), V)` of [Stacks, Tag 0CCN] corresponding to a linear system
`L ⊆ |D|` of dimension `r`, with `L = 𝐏(V^∨)` as in
`Stacks.LinearSystemScheme.IsLinearSystem.exists_eq_projectiveSpace`.
declarations.comment: the classical linear series L in |D| corresponds to the linear series (O_X(D), V)

declarations.name: Stacks.LinearSystemScheme.completeLinearSystem_iso_projectiveSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field `k`, `D ⊆ X` an
effective Cartier divisor of degree `d`, and `m` the integer with `m + 1 = h⁰(𝒪_X(D))`. The scheme
`|D| = 𝐏(H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨)` representing the fibre of the Abel map over the point of `𝒪_X(D)` is
isomorphic over `k` to `ℙ^m_k`; equivalently, that fibre is represented by `ℙ^m_k` — a natural
bijection between its `T`-points and the `k`-morphisms `T ⟶ ℙ^m_k`. Canonically, the fibre is
represented by `𝐏(H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))^∨)` itself, through the bijection sending the closed point cut out
by evaluation at a nonzero `s ∈ H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(D))` to the family whose image in `X` is the zero scheme
`Z(s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completeLinearSystem_iso_projectiveSpace {d m : ℕ}
    (hd : invertibleCurveDegree k f (topologicalKrullDim_le_one k f)
      (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) = d)
    (hm : Module.finrank k
      (cohomologyOverField k f (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) 0) = m + 1) :
    Nonempty ((linearSystemScheme k f D).asOver (Spec (.of k)) ≅
      (projectiveSpaceOverRing m (.of k)).asOver (Spec (.of k))) ∧
    (∃ e : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)),
        (T ⟶ (projectiveSpaceOverRing m (.of k)).asOver (Spec (.of k))) ≃ abelFibre f D d T,
      ∀ (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))) (h : T' ⟶ T)
          (g : T ⟶ (projectiveSpaceOverRing m (.of k)).asOver (Spec (.of k))),
        (e T' (h ≫ g)).1.ideal = (e T g).1.ideal.comap (familyBaseChangeMap (curveOver f) h)) ∧
    ∃ e : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)),
        (T ⟶ (linearSystemScheme k f D).asOver (Spec (.of k))) ≃ abelFibre f D d T,
      (∀ (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))) (h : T' ⟶ T)
          (g : T ⟶ (linearSystemScheme k f D).asOver (Spec (.of k))),
        (e T' (h ≫ g)).1.ideal = (e T g).1.ideal.comap (familyBaseChangeMap (curveOver f) h)) ∧
      ∀ (s : cohomologyOverField k f (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) 0) (hs : s ≠ 0),
        (e (fieldPoint k) (sectionPoint k f D hs)).1.ideal.comap
            (inv (pullback.fst f (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))))) =
          zeroScheme X (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D)
            (sectionOf k f (Stacks.Divisors.modulesInvertibleSheaf D) s)
declarations.comment: |D| is isomorphic to P^m_k with m + 1 = h^0(O_X(D)); canonically |D| = P(H^0(X, O_X(D))^dual)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.linearlyEquivalent_iff_weilDivisorClass_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCT.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically
closed field `k`. Two effective Cartier divisors `D, D' ⊆ X` are linearly equivalent exactly
when the Weil divisors `[D]` and `[D']` associated to them define the same element of the Weil
divisor class group `Cl(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearlyEquivalent_iff_weilDivisorClass_eq (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [IsProjectiveVariety k f] [Smooth f]
    (D D' : X.IdealSheafData) [hD : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D]
    [hD' : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D'] :
    haveI : IsNoetherian X := isNoetherian_of_isVariety k f
    haveI : IsIntegral X := (inferInstance : IsVariety k f).toIsIntegral
    LinearlyEquivalent D D' ↔
      (effectiveCartierWeilDivisor D hD : weilDivisorClassGroup X) =
        (effectiveCartierWeilDivisor D' hD' : weilDivisorClassGroup X)
declarations.comment: D and D' are linearly equivalent iff their Weil divisors have the same class in Cl(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.exists_isClosed_smoothAt_isSeparable_finrank_le_totalDegree
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CCU].**  Let `k` be an infinite field and `Z ⊆ 𝐏²_k` a closed subscheme whose
homogeneous ideal is generated by a nonzero homogeneous `F` of degree `d`.  If the structure
morphism `Z ⟶ Spec k` is smooth at one point, then there is a **closed** point `z` of `Z` at
which it is smooth and whose residue field is a finite **separable** extension of `k` of degree
at most `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosed_smoothAt_isSeparable_finrank_le_totalDegree [Infinite k]
    (i : Z ⟶ Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 3) k)) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    {d : ℕ} (F : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k) (hF0 : F ≠ 0)
    (hF : F ∈ MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 3) k (d • 1))
    (hideal : AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.idealOfClosedSubscheme
      (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 3) k) i = Ideal.span {F})
    (hsmooth : ∃ z' : Z, InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt
      (i ≫ Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjPolyChart.projToSpecCoeff k 2) z') :
    ∃ z : Z, IsClosed ({z} : Set Z) ∧
      InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt
        (i ≫ Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjPolyChart.projToSpecCoeff k 2) z ∧
      (letI : Algebra k (Z.residueField z) :=
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫
            (i ≫ Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjPolyChart.projToSpecCoeff k 2).appTop ≫
            Z.Γevaluation z).hom.toAlgebra;
        Module.Finite k (Z.residueField z) ∧
          Algebra.IsSeparable k (Z.residueField z) ∧
          Module.finrank k (Z.residueField z) ≤ F.totalDegree)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_surjective_of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCW.** A normal curve over a field is smooth if it is surjectively
dominated by a smooth curve over that field. A surjection onto a curve has nontrivial range, so
it is flat by `AlgebraicGeometry.isFlat_of_nonconstant_of_isNormal`, and smoothness descends
along a flat surjection.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_of_surjective_of_isNormal
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (_hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    [Surjective f] [Smooth pX] [IsNormal Y] :
    Smooth pY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isInseparableDegreePrime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCX.** Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p`. A nonconstant
morphism `f` of proper nonsingular curves over `k` whose extension of function fields is purely
inseparable factors as a chain of proper nonsingular curves over `k` in which every step has
degree `p` and induces an inseparable extension of function fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chain_isInseparableDegreePrime (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY]
    (hXreg : IsRegular X) (hYreg : IsRegular Y)
    (f : Over.mk pX ⟶ Over.mk pY) [IsDominant f.left]
    (hpure : letI : Algebra Y.functionField X.functionField :=
        (functionFieldMap f.left).toAlgebra
      IsPurelyInseparable Y.functionField X.functionField) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (Z : Fin (n + 1) → ProperNonsingularCurve k)
      (g : ∀ i : Fin n, (Z i.castSucc).obj ⟶ (Z i.succ).obj)
      (w : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), (Z i).obj ⟶ Over.mk pY)
      (e : Over.mk pX ⟶ (Z 0).obj),
      IsIso e ∧ IsIso (w (Fin.last n)) ∧ e ≫ w 0 = f ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, g i ≫ w i.succ = w i.castSucc) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ hdom : IsDominant (g i).left,
        letI : IsDominant (g i).left := hdom
        letI : Algebra (Z i.succ).obj.left.functionField
            (Z i.castSucc).obj.left.functionField := (functionFieldMap (g i).left).toAlgebra
        Module.finrank (Z i.succ).obj.left.functionField
            (Z i.castSucc).obj.left.functionField = p ∧
          ¬ Algebra.IsSeparable (Z i.succ).obj.left.functionField
            (Z i.castSucc).obj.left.functionField ∧
          (g i).left.residueDegree (genericPoint (Z i.castSucc).obj.left) = p
declarations.comment: the factorization into steps of degree p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_iso_frobeniusTwist_of_inseparable_degree_prime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCY.** A nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over a
field of characteristic `p`, with smooth source, whose extension of function fields is
inseparable of degree `p`, is the relative Frobenius up to a unique isomorphism of its target
with the Frobenius twist of its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_frobeniusTwist_of_inseparable_degree_prime
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY]
    (_hXreg : IsRegular X) (hYreg : IsRegular Y)
    [Smooth pX] (f : X ⟶ Y) (_hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    (hnonconstant : (Set.range f).Nontrivial)
    (hdegree : f.residueDegree (genericPoint X) = p)
    (hinseparable :
      letI := (f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint X)).hom.toAlgebra
      ¬ Algebra.IsSeparable
          (Y.residueField (f (genericPoint X))) (X.residueField (genericPoint X))) :
    ∃! i : Over.mk pY ≅
        (frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p
          (Stacks.Frobenius.isInCharacteristic_of_over
            (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))))).obj (Over.mk pX),
      f ≫ i.hom.left =
        (relativeFrobenius (Spec (.of k)) p
          (Stacks.Frobenius.isInCharacteristic_of_over (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k)))))
          (Over.mk pX)).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_nat_existsUnique_iso_nFoldFrobeniusTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CCZ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular
curves over a field `k` of characteristic `p`, with `X` smooth and the induced extension of
function fields purely inseparable. Then there is a unique number `n` of iterations and, for it, a
unique isomorphism over `k` of the `n`-fold Frobenius twist of `X` with `Y` carrying the `n`-fold
relative Frobenius of `X` to `f`.

Both inputs of the source's proof are supplied here: the degree-`p` factorization of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chain_isInseparableDegreePrime` ([Stacks, Tag 0CCX]), converted to the
indexing the assembly uses, and the degree of the relative Frobenius of a smooth curve,
`AlgebraicGeometry.residueDegree_relativeFrobenius_isCurve` ([Stacks, Tag 0CCF]).
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_nat_existsUnique_iso_nFoldFrobeniusTwist
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    (hS : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY] [Smooth pX]
    (hXreg : IsRegular X) (hYreg : IsRegular Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (hnonconstant : (Set.range f).Nontrivial)
    (hpure : (f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint X)).hom.IsPurelyInseparable) :
    ∃! m : ℕ, ∃! e : nFoldFrobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS m (Over.mk pX) ≅ Over.mk pY,
      nFoldRelativeFrobenius (Spec (.of k)) p hS m (Over.mk pX) ≫ e.hom = Over.homMk f hf
declarations.comment: the unique number of iterations and the unique isomorphism of the correspondingly iterated Frobenius twist of X with Y carrying the iterated relative Frobenius to f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_isPurelyInseparable_residueFieldMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD0, the smoothness of the target.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a nonconstant
morphism of proper nonsingular curves over a field `k` of characteristic `p`.  If `X` is smooth
and the extension of function fields is purely inseparable, then `Y` is smooth: by
[Stacks, Tag 0CCZ] it is a base change of `X` along an endomorphism of the ground field, and
smoothness is stable under base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_of_isPurelyInseparable_residueFieldMap
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY] [Smooth pX]
    (hXreg : IsRegular X) (hYreg : IsRegular Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (hnonconstant : (Set.range f).Nontrivial)
