    (hpure : (f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint X)).hom.IsPurelyInseparable) :
    Smooth pY
declarations.comment: the smoothness of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_globalSections_of_isPurelyInseparable_residueFieldMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD0, the global regular functions on the target.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be
a nonconstant morphism of proper nonsingular curves over a field `k` of characteristic `p`.  If
`X` is smooth, the global regular functions on `X` are the constants, and the extension of
function fields is purely inseparable, then the global regular functions on `Y` are again the
constants.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_globalSections_of_isPurelyInseparable_residueFieldMap
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY] [Smooth pX]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pX.appTop)]
    (hXreg : IsRegular X) (hYreg : IsRegular Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (hnonconstant : (Set.range f).Nontrivial)
    (hpure : (f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint X)).hom.IsPurelyInseparable) :
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ pY.appTop)
declarations.comment: the global regular functions on the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genus_eq_of_isPurelyInseparable_residueFieldMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD0, the genus of the target.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a nonconstant
morphism of proper nonsingular curves over a field `k` of characteristic `p`.  If `X` is smooth
and the extension of function fields is purely inseparable, then `Y` has the same genus as `X`:
it is a base change of `X` along an extension of the ground field, and the genus is invariant
under such a base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_eq_of_isPurelyInseparable_residueFieldMap
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY] [Smooth pX]
    (hXreg : IsRegular X) (hYreg : IsRegular Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (hnonconstant : (Set.range f).Nontrivial)
    (hpure : (f.residueFieldMap (genericPoint X)).hom.IsPurelyInseparable) :
    genus pY = genus pX
declarations.comment: the genus of the target

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.InseparableGenus.exists_charThree_notCube
declarations.doc:
**The hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0CD1] are satisfiable: `𝐅₃(a)` works.** There is a field of
characteristic three, in any universe, carrying an element which is not a cube.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_charThree_notCube :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K), CharP K 3 ∧ ∃ a : K, ∀ b : K, b ^ 3 ≠ a
declarations.comment: the example's remark that k = 𝐅₃(a) works: a field of characteristic three with an element that is not a cube

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.InseparableGenus.planeCubicProjection_inseparable_genus_change
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CD1].** Let `k` be a field of characteristic three and `a ∈ k` an element
which is not a cube (for instance `k = 𝐅₃(a)`, `exists_charThree_notCube`). Let
`Z = Proj (k[T₀, T₁, T₂] ⧸ (F))` be the plane cubic with homogeneous equation
`F = T₁²T₀ - T₂³ + aT₀³`, embedded in `𝐏²_k` by `planeCubicEmbedding`, and let
`f : Z ⟶ 𝐏¹_k` be the coordinate projection `planeCubicProjection`, which on `D₊(T₀)` sends
`(x, y)` to `x`. Then:

* `Z` is a closed subscheme of `𝐏²_k`, proper over `k`, a curve over `k`, and nonsingular;
* `𝐏¹_k` is proper over `k`, a curve over `k`, and nonsingular;
* `f` is a morphism over `Spec k`, it is the projection `(T₀ : T₁ : T₂) ↦ (T₀ : T₁)` in the
  sense that `f ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(G) = Z ∩ D₊(G(T₀, T₁))` for every homogeneous `G` of positive degree, and
  it is dominant;
* the extension `k(Z)/k(𝐏¹_k)` of function fields induced by `f` is purely inseparable of
  degree three;
* the genus of `Z` is `1` and the genus of `𝐏¹_k` is `0`.

So the genus is not preserved by a purely inseparable morphism of proper nonsingular curves.
Characteristic three is `ExpChar k 3`, which for the prime `3` is the same as `CharP k 3`.
declarations.statement:
theorem planeCubicProjection_inseparable_genus_change (k : Type u) [Field k] [ExpChar k 3]
    (a : k) (ha : ∀ b : k, b ^ 3 ≠ a) :
    letI := isIntegral_planeCubicCurve k a ha
    letI := isDominant_planeCubicProjection k a
    letI : Algebra (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj
        (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).functionField
        (planeCubicCurve k a).functionField :=
      (dominantFunctionFieldMap (planeCubicProjection k a)).toAlgebra
    IsClosedImmersion (planeCubicEmbedding k a) ∧
      IsProper (planeCubicEmbedding k a ≫ projToSpecCoeff k 2) ∧
      IsCurve k (planeCubicEmbedding k a ≫ projToSpecCoeff k 2) ∧
      IsRegular (planeCubicCurve k a) ∧
      IsProper (projToSpecCoeff k 1) ∧
      IsCurve k (projToSpecCoeff k 1) ∧
      IsRegular (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)) ∧
      planeCubicProjection k a ≫ projToSpecCoeff k 1 =
        planeCubicEmbedding k a ≫ projToSpecCoeff k 2 ∧
      (∀ (G : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (d : ℕ),
        G ∈ MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k d → 0 < d →
        planeCubicProjection k a ⁻¹ᵁ AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpen
            (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) G =
          planeCubicEmbedding k a ⁻¹ᵁ AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpen
            (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 3) k) (coordProjHom k G)) ∧
      IsDominant (planeCubicProjection k a) ∧
      IsPurelyInseparable (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj
          (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).functionField
          (planeCubicCurve k a).functionField ∧
      Module.finrank (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj
          (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).functionField
          (planeCubicCurve k a).functionField = 3 ∧
      genus (planeCubicEmbedding k a ≫ projToSpecCoeff k 2) = 1 ∧
      genus (projToSpecCoeff k 1) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_nFoldRelativeFrobenius_comp_isSeparable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD2.** Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0` and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a nonconstant morphism of proper smooth curves over `k`.  Then `f` factors as
`X ⟶ X^(p^n) ⟶ Y`, where `X^(p^n)` is the `n`-fold Frobenius twist of `X`, that is, the base
change of `X` along the `n`-fold absolute Frobenius of `Spec k`, the first morphism is the
`n`-fold relative Frobenius of `X`, and the second is a nonconstant morphism of proper smooth
curves over `k` inducing a separable extension of function fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nFoldRelativeFrobenius_comp_isSeparable {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ)
    [Fact p.Prime] (hk : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k pX] [IsCurve k pY] [Smooth pX] [Smooth pY] [IsProper pX] [IsProper pY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (hnonconstant : (Set.range f).Nontrivial) :
    ∃ n : ℕ,
      let T := nFoldFrobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hk n (Over.mk pX)
      ∃ (g : T.left ⟶ Y) (hcurve : IsCurve k T.hom) (hdom : IsDominant g),
        letI := hcurve
        letI := hdom
        Smooth T.hom ∧ IsProper T.hom ∧ g ≫ pY = T.hom ∧
          f = (nFoldRelativeFrobenius (Spec (.of k)) p hk n (Over.mk pX)).left ≫ g ∧
          (Set.range g).Nontrivial ∧ g (genericPoint T.left) = genericPoint Y ∧
          @Algebra.IsSeparable Y.functionField T.left.functionField _ _
            (functionFieldMap g).toAlgebra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_genericallyEtale_pencil_or_linearSeries_frobeniusTwist
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD3.** Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0`, let `X` be a
smooth proper curve over `k` and let `(ℒ, V)` be a `𝔤^r_d` on `X` with `r ≥ 1`. Then one of the
following holds: there is a `𝔤¹_d` on `X` whose corresponding morphism `X ⟶ ℙ¹_k` of
[Stacks, Tag 0CCP] is generically etale, or there is a `𝔤^r_{d'}` on the Frobenius twist
`X^{(p)}` with `d' ≤ d / p`.

Which alternative holds is decided by the ratios `s_j / s_0` of a basis `s_0, …, s_r` of `V`,
read at the generic point of `X` as elements of `k(X)`: if they all lie in the compositum of `k`
with the `p`-th powers of `k(X)` — the image of `k(X^{(p)})` — the morphism to `ℙ^r_k` factors
through the relative Frobenius and the second alternative holds; otherwise the pencil spanned by
`s_0` and an offending `s_j` gives the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_genericallyEtale_pencil_or_linearSeries_frobeniusTwist
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (hS : IsInCharacteristic (Spec (.of k)) p)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k pX] [Smooth pX] [IsProper pX]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) {d r : ℕ} (_hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (E : LinearSeries k pX hdim d r) :
    (∃ (E₁ : LinearSeries k pX hdim d 1) (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin 2) k E₁.V)
        (q : X ⟶ projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)))
        (_ : q ≫ (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of k)) ↘ Spec (.of k)) = pX)
        (α : (Scheme.Modules.pullback
            (q ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse 1 (Spec (.of k)))).obj
              (twistingSheafAtUniverse.{u} 1) ⟶ E₁.L),
        (∀ i, α.app ⊤ (pullbackCoordSection.{u}
            (q ≫ projectiveSpaceOver.toIntegralAtUniverse 1 (Spec (.of k))) i) =
          seriesSections E₁ b₁ i) ∧
          ∃ U : X.Opens, Nonempty U ∧ Etale (U.ι ≫ q)) ∨
      (letI : IsCurve k ((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk pX)).hom :=
          isCurve_frobeniusTwist_curve p hS pX
       letI : IsProper ((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk pX)).hom :=
          isProper_frobeniusTwist_curve p hS pX
       ∃ d' : ℕ, p * d' ≤ d ∧ d' ≤ d / p ∧
         Nonempty (LinearSeries k ((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk pX)).hom
           (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (k := k)
             (f := ((frobeniusTwist (Spec (.of k)) p hS).obj (Over.mk pX)).hom)).le d' r))
declarations.comment: both alternatives: a pencil of the same degree whose morphism to the projective line is generically etale, or a linear series of the same dimension and degree at most d / p on the Frobenius twist

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isClosed_isSeparable_finrank_residueField_le_two_mul_genus_sub_two
declarations.doc:
A smooth proper curve `X` over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and genus `g ≥ 2` has a
closed point `x` with `κ(x)/k` finite separable of degree at most `2g - 2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosed_isSeparable_finrank_residueField_le_two_mul_genus_sub_two
    (hg : 2 ≤ genus f) :
    ∃ x : X, IsClosed ({x} : Set X) ∧
      (letI := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.Γevaluation x).hom.toAlgebra;
      Module.Finite k (X.residueField x) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k (X.residueField x) ∧
        Module.finrank k (X.residueField x) ≤ 2 * genus f - 2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.bijOn_schemePullbackClass_zsmulTorsion_of_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD5.** Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0`, let `X` be a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, and let `n` be an
integer prime to `p`. Then for every purely inseparable extension `k'/k`, pullback along
`X_{k'} ⟶ X` is a bijection `Pic(X)[n] → Pic(X_{k'})[n]`.

Injectivity is Tag 0CC5. For surjectivity, a class of `Pic(X_{k'})[n]` is pulled back from a
class of `Pic(X_E)` for a finite subextension `E/k` (Tag 0B8W), which is again `n`-torsion
because pullback from `X_E` is injective (Tag 0CC5 at the stage), and the finite purely
inseparable case is
`Stacks.Picard.bijOn_schemePullbackClass_zsmulTorsion_of_hasExponent`, proved through the
absolute Frobenius.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_schemePullbackClass_zsmulTorsion_of_isPurelyInseparable
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [IsPurelyInseparable k k']
    (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) {n : ℤ} (hn : n.natAbs.Coprime p)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (hΓ : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)) :
    Set.BijOn
      (schemePullbackClass (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))))
      (zsmulTorsion (ofScheme X) n)
      (zsmulTorsion
        (ofScheme (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))) n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Curves.isNode_iff_of_finiteSeparable_baseField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD6.**  Let `k' / k` be a finite separable field extension and let `X`
be a one-dimensional scheme locally of finite type over `k'`.  A point of `X` is a node over `k'`
exactly when it is a node for the `k`-scheme structure obtained by composing with
`Spec k' ⟶ Spec k`.

The two conditions are joined through the base change `X ×_{Spec k} Spec k'`.  Its first
projection is étale, being a base change of the étale morphism `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k`, and the graph
of `f` is a section of that projection, hence itself étale.  Tag 0C56 identifies the node
condition over `k` with the one on the base change, and Tag 0C57 identifies the latter with the
node condition over `k'` on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNode_iff_of_finiteSeparable_baseField
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
    [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k'))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (x : X) :
    letI : X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k')) := ⟨f⟩
    letI : X.Over (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of k)) :=
      ⟨f ≫ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))⟩
    (IsNode k' X x ↔ IsNode k X x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD7.** A morphism of schemes smooth of relative dimension one is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one: it is syntomic with one-dimensional fibres, and its
relative singular subscheme is empty, hence unramified over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] :
    IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_comp_etale_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CD8.** Composing a morphism which is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one
with an étale morphism of the base again gives a morphism which is at-worst-nodal of relative
dimension one.

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.exists_exceptionalContractionSequence_isMinimalModel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CD9.** Let `C` be a smooth projective curve over `K` with
`H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`. If `X` is a regular proper model for `C`, then there is a sequence of morphisms
`X = Xₘ → Xₘ₋₁ → ⋯ → X₁ → X₀` of regular proper models of `C`, each the contraction of an
exceptional curve of the first kind, such that `X₀` is a minimal model.

The proof is the source's: `X` is projective over `R` ([Stacks, Tag 0C5P]), so an exceptional
curve of the first kind on it can be contracted onto a regular projective model
([Stacks, Tag 0C2N]), and the number of points of the special fibre with one-dimensional local
ring — the generic points of the irreducible components of the special fibre — drops by one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_exceptionalContractionSequence_isMinimalModel {C X : Scheme.{u}}
    (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (hproj : Stacks.HProjective.IsHProjective c)
    (hH0 : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    (e : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))))
    (hmod : IsModel c p e) [IsProper p] (hreg : IsRegular X) :
    ∃ (X₀ : Scheme.{u}) (p₀ : X₀ ⟶ Spec (.of R))
      (e₀ : C ≅ pullback p₀ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))) (g : X ⟶ X₀),
      ExceptionalContractionSequence c p p₀ g ∧ IsMinimalModel c p₀ e₀

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.isProjectiveLineSpecialFiber_of_isMinimalModel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDA.** Let `C` be a smooth projective curve over `K` with
`H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K` and genus `0`. If there is more than one minimal model for `C` — two minimal
models which are not isomorphic as models of `C` — then the special fibre of every minimal model
is isomorphic to `𝐏¹_k` over the residue field `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjectiveLineSpecialFiber_of_isMinimalModel {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (_hproj : Stacks.HProjective.IsHProjective c)
    (_hH0 : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)) (_hg : genus c = 0)
    (hmore : ∃ (X₁ X₂ : Scheme.{u}) (p₁ : X₁ ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (p₂ : X₂ ⟶ Spec (.of R))
      (e₁ : C ≅ pullback p₁ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))))
      (e₂ : C ≅ pullback p₂ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))),
      IsMinimalModel c p₁ e₁ ∧ IsMinimalModel c p₂ e₂ ∧
        ¬ ∃ φ : X₁ ≅ X₂, φ.hom ≫ p₂ = p₁ ∧
          e₁.hom ≫ pullback.fst p₁ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))) ≫ φ.hom =
            e₂.hom ≫ pullback.fst p₂ (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))))
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    (e : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K))))
    (hX : IsMinimalModel c p e) : IsProjectiveLineSpecialFiber p

declarations.name: Stacks.nodalModel
declarations.doc:
The standard nodal model `X = Spec R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)` of exponent `n`, an affine scheme over
`S = Spec R`.
declarations.statement: public def nodalModel (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (π : R) (n : ℕ) : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: the scheme X = Spec A of the family A = R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)

declarations.name: Stacks.nodalModelHom
declarations.doc:
The structure morphism `X ⟶ S = Spec R` of the standard nodal model, the morphism of schemes
induced by the ring map `R → A = R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)`.
declarations.statement:
public def nodalModelHom (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (π : R) (n : ℕ) :
    nodalModel R π n ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)
declarations.comment: the morphism X ⟶ S = Spec R induced by R → A = R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)

declarations.name: Stacks.smooth_nodalModelHom_zero
declarations.doc:
**The exponent zero model is smooth over the base.** For `n = 0` the defining relation reads
`xy = 1`, and `X ⟶ S` is smooth; no hypothesis on `R` or `π` is needed.
declarations.statement: public theorem smooth_nodalModelHom_zero (π : R) : Smooth (nodalModelHom R π 0)
declarations.comment: if n = 0 then X → S is smooth

declarations.name: Stacks.span_nodalGen_eq_nodalModelOrigin_one
declarations.doc:
**At exponent one the two coordinates generate the maximal ideal of the origin.** The
defining relation reads `π = xy`, so the uniformizer already lies in `(x, y)` and
`𝔪 = (π, x, y) = (x, y)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem span_nodalGen_eq_nodalModelOrigin_one (π : R) :
    Ideal.span {nodalGen R (π ^ 1) 0, nodalGen R (π ^ 1) 1} = nodalModelOrigin R π 1
declarations.comment: if n = 1 then (x, y) generate the maximal ideal 𝔪 = (π, x, y)

declarations.name: Stacks.span_nodalGen_lt_nodalModelOrigin_of_two_le
declarations.doc:
**For exponent at least two the two coordinates no longer generate the maximal ideal of the
origin.** The ideal `(x, y)` of `R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)` is strictly smaller than `𝔪 = (π, x, y)`.
declarations.comment: if n > 1 then (x, y) no longer generate the maximal ideal 𝔪 = (π, x, y)

declarations.name: Stacks.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_nodalModelHom_zero
declarations.doc:
**The exponent zero model is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over the base.** It is
smooth of relative dimension one, and a smooth family of curves has empty relative singular
subscheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_nodalModelHom_zero (π : R) :
    IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne (nodalModelHom R π 0)
declarations.comment: the exponent zero member of the family is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one

declarations.name: Stacks.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_nodalModelHom
declarations.doc:
**Every member of the family is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over the base.** For
every exponent `n` the morphism `X = Spec R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ) ⟶ S = Spec R` is syntomic of relative
dimension one and its relative singular subscheme, cut out by the two coordinates, is unramified
over `S`. No hypothesis on `R` or `π` is needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_nodalModelHom (π : R) (n : ℕ) :
    IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne (nodalModelHom R π n)
declarations.comment: for all n the morphism X → S is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension 1

declarations.name: Stacks.isRegular_nodalModel_one
declarations.doc:
**The exponent one model is regular.** For `π` a uniformizer of a discrete valuation ring the
scheme `Spec R[x, y]/(xy - π)` is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_nodalModel_one {π : R} (hπ : Irreducible π) :
    IsRegular (nodalModel R π 1)
declarations.comment: if n = 1 then X is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.not_isRegular_nodalModel_of_one_lt
declarations.doc:
**A model of exponent greater than one is not regular.** It is singular at the origin
`(π, x, y)`, where the two coordinates no longer span the maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_isRegular_nodalModel_of_one_lt {π : R} (hπ : Irreducible π) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : 1 < n) : ¬ IsRegular (nodalModel R π n)
declarations.comment: if n > 1 then X is not regular

declarations.name: Stacks.nodalModelBlowup
declarations.doc:
**The blowup `X'` of the standard nodal model `X = Spec R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)` in the ideal
`𝔪 = (π, x, y)` of its singular point.** It is the `Proj` of the Rees algebra of `𝔪`; that this
is the blowup of the scheme `X` in the ideal sheaf attached to `𝔪` is
`Stacks.Blowup.nonempty_over_iso_blowUpToBase`.
declarations.statement: public def nodalModelBlowup (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (π : R) (n : ℕ) : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: to ameliorate the situation in case n > 1 we consider the blowup b : X' → X of X in 𝔪: the scheme X'

declarations.name: Stacks.nodalModelBlowupHom
declarations.doc: **The blowup morphism `b : X' ⟶ X` of the standard nodal model in `𝔪 = (π, x, y)`.**
declarations.statement:
public def nodalModelBlowupHom (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (π : R) (n : ℕ) :
    nodalModelBlowup R π n ⟶ nodalModel R π n
declarations.comment: to ameliorate the situation in case n > 1 we consider the blowup b : X' → X of X in 𝔪: the morphism b

declarations.name: Stacks.iSup_opensRange_nodalModelBlowupChart
declarations.doc:
**By construction `X'` is covered by three affine pieces, the spectra of the blowup algebras
`A[𝔪/π]`, `A[𝔪/x]` and `A[𝔪/y]`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem iSup_opensRange_nodalModelBlowupChart (π : R) (n : ℕ) :
    ⨆ i, (nodalModelBlowupChart R π n i).opensRange = ⊤
declarations.comment: by construction X' is covered by three affine pieces corresponding to the blowup algebras A[𝔪/π], A[𝔪/x] and A[𝔪/y]

declarations.name: Stacks.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_nodalModelBlowupToBase
declarations.doc:
**`X' ⟶ S` is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.** The three charts cover `X'`, an
open immersion is étale, and over `S` each chart is a standard nodal model: the central one with
parameter `π^(n-2)`, the two outer ones with parameter `π`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_nodalModelBlowupToBase
    (hπ : π ≠ 0) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne (nodalModelBlowupToBase R π n)
declarations.comment: thus we see that X' → S is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension 1

declarations.name: Stacks.exists_isOpenImmersion_nodalModel_sub_two
declarations.doc:
**The one point at which `X'` can fail to be regular has an affine open neighbourhood
exactly as the original situation, with `n` replaced by `n - 2`.** The central chart `A[𝔪/π]` is
an affine open of `X'` which, over `S`, is the standard nodal model of exponent `n - 2`; the two
outer charts are regular by `Stacks.isRegular_spec_nodalXChart` and
`Stacks.isRegular_spec_nodalYChart`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_nodalModel_sub_two (hπ : π ≠ 0) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ j : nodalModel R π (n - 2) ⟶ nodalModelBlowup R π n,
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ j ≫ nodalModelBlowupToBase R π n = nodalModelHom R π (n - 2) ∧
        Set.range j.base = Set.range (nodalModelBlowupChart R π n 0).base
declarations.comment: X' is regular, except for one point which has an affine open neighbourhood exactly as above but with n replaced by n - 2: that neighbourhood, as the standard nodal model of exponent n - 2 over S

declarations.name: Stacks.isRegular_nodalModelBlowup_of_le_three
declarations.doc:
**For `2 ≤ n ≤ 3` the single blowup already resolves the singularity: `X'` is regular.** The
exponent drop `n ↦ n - 2` of the central chart lands on `0` or `1`, where the standard nodal
model is regular, and the two outer charts are regular for every `n ≥ 2`. Since `⌊n/2⌋ = 1` for
these `n`, the chain of blowing ups in closed points of [Stacks, Tag 0CDC] is here the single
blowup `b : X' ⟶ X`, and `X' ⟶ S` is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one by
`Stacks.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_nodalModelBlowupToBase`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_nodalModelBlowup_of_le_three {π : R} (hπ : Irreducible π) {n : ℕ}
    (h2 : 2 ≤ n) (h3 : n ≤ 3) : IsRegular (nodalModelBlowup R π n)
declarations.comment: using induction on n: for 2 ≤ n ≤ 3 the sequence of blowing ups in closed points X_{⌊n/2⌋} → … → X₁ → X₀ = X is the single blowup b : X' → X, and X_{⌊n/2⌋} = X' is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.exists_pointBlowupChainOfLength_nodalModel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDC.** Using induction on `n` there is a sequence of blowups at closed
points
```
X_{⌊n/2⌋} → … → X₁ → X₀ = X
```
of the standard nodal model `X = Spec R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)` over `S = Spec R` such that
`X_{⌊n/2⌋} → S` is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one and `X_{⌊n/2⌋}` is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pointBlowupChainOfLength_nodalModel {π : R} (hπ : Irreducible π) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ nodalModel R π n),
      PointBlowupChainOfLength (nodalModel R π n) Set.univ (n / 2) Y g ∧
      IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne (g ≫ nodalModelHom R π n) ∧ IsRegular Y
declarations.comment: using induction on n we conclude that there is a sequence of blowing ups in closed points X_{⌊n/2⌋} → … → X₁ → X₀ = X such that X_{⌊n/2⌋} → S is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension 1 and X_{⌊n/2⌋} is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.nodalXChart_equiv
declarations.doc:
**The `x`-chart of the blowup of the standard nodal model.** For `n ≥ 2` the affine blowup
algebra `A[𝔪/x]` of `A = R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)` at `x`, where `𝔪 = (π, x, y)`, is
`R[x, u]/(xu - π)`, the identification carrying `x` to `x` and `y` to `u·π^(n-1)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nodalXChart_equiv [IsDomain R] [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R]
    (hπ : π ≠ 0) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ e : ↥(nodalXChart π n S) ≃+* nodalChartRing R π,
      (∀ r : R, e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalXChart π n S)
          (algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) r))
        = algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R π) r) ∧
      e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalXChart π n S) (nodalGen R (π ^ n) 0))
        = nodalGen R π 0 ∧
      e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalXChart π n S) (nodalGen R (π ^ n) 1))
        = nodalGen R π 1 * algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R π) (π ^ (n - 1))
declarations.comment: the algebra A[𝔪/x] has generators x, u = π/x subject to the relation xu - π

declarations.name: Stacks.nodalCentralChart_equiv
declarations.doc:
**The central chart of the blowup of the standard nodal model, and the drop `n ↦ n - 2`.**
For `n ≥ 2` the affine blowup algebra `A[𝔪/π]` of `A = R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)` at `π`, where
`𝔪 = (π, x, y)`, is again a standard nodal model, with the exponent lowered by two:
`R[x', y']/(x'y' - π^(n-2))`, the identification carrying `x` to `πx'` and `y` to `πy'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nodalCentralChart_equiv [IsDomain R] [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R]
    (hπ : π ≠ 0) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ e : ↥(nodalCentralChart π n S) ≃+* nodalChartRing R (π ^ (n - 2)),
      (∀ r : R, e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalCentralChart π n S)
          (algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) r))
        = algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R (π ^ (n - 2))) r) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin 2,
        e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalCentralChart π n S)
            (nodalGen R (π ^ n) i))
          = algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R (π ^ (n - 2))) π *
              nodalGen R (π ^ (n - 2)) i)
declarations.comment: the algebra A[𝔪/π] has generators x' = x/π and y' = y/π with x'y' = π^(n-2), so this part of X' is the spectrum of R[x', y']/(x'y' - π^(n-2))

declarations.name: Stacks.nodalYChart_equiv
declarations.doc:
**The `y`-chart of the blowup of the standard nodal model.** For `n ≥ 2` the affine blowup
algebra `A[𝔪/y]` of `A = R[x, y]/(xy - πⁿ)` at `y`, where `𝔪 = (π, x, y)`, is
`R[y, v]/(yv - π)`, the identification carrying `y` to `y` and `x` to `v·π^(n-1)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nodalYChart_equiv [IsDomain R] [UniqueFactorizationMonoid R]
    (hπ : π ≠ 0) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∃ e : ↥(nodalYChart π n S) ≃+* nodalChartRing R π,
      (∀ r : R, e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalYChart π n S)
          (algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) r))
        = algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R π) r) ∧
      e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalYChart π n S) (nodalGen R (π ^ n) 1))
        = nodalGen R π 0 ∧
      e (algebraMap (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) ↥(nodalYChart π n S) (nodalGen R (π ^ n) 0))
        = nodalGen R π 1 * algebraMap R (nodalChartRing R π) (π ^ (n - 1))
declarations.comment: by symmetry the case of the algebra A[𝔪/y] is the same as the case of A[𝔪/x]

declarations.name: Stacks.isRegular_spec_nodalXChart
declarations.doc:
**The `x`-chart of the blowup of the standard nodal model is regular.** It is the exponent one
model `R[x, u]/(xu - π)`, by `Stacks.nodalXChart_equiv`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_spec_nodalXChart {π : R} (hπ : Irreducible π) {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) S]
    [IsLocalization.Away (nodalGen R (π ^ n) 0) S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsScalarTower R (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) S] :
    IsRegular (Spec (CommRingCat.of ↥(nodalXChart π n S)))
declarations.comment: the x-chart of X' is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.isRegular_spec_nodalYChart
declarations.doc: **The `y`-chart of the blowup of the standard nodal model is regular.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegular_spec_nodalYChart {π : R} (hπ : Irreducible π) {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) S]
    [IsLocalization.Away (nodalGen R (π ^ n) 1) S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsScalarTower R (nodalChartRing R (π ^ n)) S] :
    IsRegular (Spec (CommRingCat.of ↥(nodalYChart π n S)))
declarations.comment: the y-chart of X' is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.exists_etale_nodalChart_pow_uniformizer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CDD.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring, let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be at-worst-nodal
of relative dimension one, and let `x` be a point of the special fibre. Then there is an étale
extension `R ⊆ R'` of discrete valuation rings, a scheme `U` with étale morphisms `U ⟶ X` and
`U ⟶ Spec A` over `Spec R'`, and a point `x'` of `U` above `x`, with

`A = R'[u, v]/(uv)`  or  `A = R'[u, v]/(uv - π ^ n)`

for a uniformizer `π` of `R'` and `n ≥ 0`; the two cases are the vanishing and the nonvanishing
of the parameter `h`, which is a power of a uniformizer in the second case.

The étale local structure in chart form over an arbitrary affine étale base is carried as the
hypothesis `hCBY`; everything else — shrinking that base to a discrete valuation ring and
normalising the parameter — is proved here.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_nodalChart_pow_uniformizer
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    (_hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f)
    (x : X) (hx : f.base x = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R)
    (hCBY : NodalChartNeighbourhood f x) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : IsDomain R')
      (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R') (_ : Algebra R R')
      (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsExtension R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R') (h : R'),
      (h = 0 ∨ ∃ (π : R') (n : ℕ), Irreducible π ∧ h = π ^ n) ∧
        ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (g : U ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ Spec (.of (nodalChartRing R' h))) (x' : U),
          Etale g ∧ Etale j ∧ g.base x' = x ∧
            g ≫ f = j ≫
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R' (nodalChartRing R' h))) ≫
                Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R R'))
declarations.comment: the TRANSLATION STEP ONLY, with the etale local structure carried as a hypothesis. CARRIED HYPOTHESES, each inherited and not discharged here: `hCBY : Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.NodalChartNeighbourhood f x` is the EXISTENCE half of [Stacks, Tag 0CBY] -- an etale neighbourhood `U` of `x`, an affine etale neighbourhood `Spec B` of its image, a parameter `h` of `B` and an etale `U -> Spec B[x,y]/(xy-h)` over `Spec B` -- which is the CHART form of the tag and is still not proved in this repository. [Stacks, Tag 0CBY] ITSELF IS PROVED: `Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.nonempty_standardNodalDiagram_of_isAtWorstNodal` at StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Curves/NodalEtaleLocalStructureAssembly.lean proves the tag's own statement, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's, in the DIAGRAM form `Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.StandardNodalDiagram` -- etale `U -> X`, etale `V -> S`, etale `U -> W` and a cartesian square presenting `W` as a base change of the standard nodal family. What separates that from `hCBY` is not the existence but the PACKAGING: the chart form asks for the base `V` to be AFFINE, say `Spec B`, and for an actual parameter `h` in `B`, so passing from the diagram to the chart means shrinking `V` to an affine open and reading the local model off `Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.chartIsoOfIsPullback`, which is a step nobody has taken. `_hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f` is the tag's own hypothesis; it appears in the statement for faithfulness but is NOT consumed, because the whole use of nodality in the source proof is to produce `hCBY`. WHAT IS PROVED HERE, and is exactly what the source calls the translation: the affine etale base `Spec B` is shrunk to a discrete valuation ring `R'` with `R` -> `R'` etale and `R` ⊆ `R'` an extension of discrete valuation rings in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 09E4] (`exists_isDiscreteValuationRing_localizationAtPrime_of_etale`, the route of [Stacks, Tag 0AP2]); the chart is base changed along `B -> R'` and is again a nodal chart (`isPullback_specMap_nodalChartMap`); and the resulting parameter is normalised to `0` or a power of a uniformizer by rescaling a coordinate by a unit (`exists_pow_irreducible_nodalChartRing_algEquiv`). The SMOOTH case of the source proof, which routes through [Stacks, Tag 054L] instead of 0CBY, is not covered by this statement: see the module documentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.exists_etale_nodalChart_pow_uniformizer_of_isAtWorstNodal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CDD.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring, let `f : X ⟶ Spec R` be at-worst-nodal
of relative dimension one, and let `x` be a point of the special fibre. Then there is an étale
extension `R ⊆ R'` of discrete valuation rings, a scheme `U` with étale morphisms `U ⟶ X` and
`U ⟶ Spec A` over `Spec R'`, and a point `x'` of `U` above `x`, with

`A = R'[u, v]/(uv)`  or  `A = R'[u, v]/(uv - π ^ n)`

for a uniformizer `π` of `R'` and `n ≥ 0`; the two cases are the vanishing and the nonvanishing
of the parameter `h`, which is a power of a uniformizer in the second case.

The étale local structure in chart form is
`Stacks.NodalEtaleLocalStructure.nonempty_nodalChartNeighbourhood_of_isAtWorstNodal` (Tag 0CBY at
a singular point of the fibre, Tag 054L at a smooth one), and the translation into the
statement of the tag is `Stacks.Models.exists_etale_nodalChart_pow_uniformizer`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_nodalChart_pow_uniformizer_of_isAtWorstNodal
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    (hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f)
    (x : X) (hx : f.base x = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : IsDomain R')
      (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R') (_ : Algebra R R')
      (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsExtension R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R') (h : R'),
      (h = 0 ∨ ∃ (π : R') (n : ℕ), Irreducible π ∧ h = π ^ n) ∧
        ∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (g : U ⟶ X)
          (j : U ⟶ Spec (.of (nodalChartRing R' h))) (x' : U),
          Etale g ∧ Etale j ∧ g.base x' = x ∧
            g ≫ f = j ≫
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R' (nodalChartRing R' h))) ≫
                Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R R'))

declarations.name: Stacks.SemistableReduction.exists_nodalBlowupChain_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDE.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring and let `X` be a
quasi-compact scheme which is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over `R`, with smooth
generic fibre. Then there is a finite sequence `X_m ⟶ ⋯ ⟶ X_1 ⟶ X_0 = X` such that
1. each `X_{i+1} ⟶ X_i` is the blowing up of `X_i` in a closed point at which `X_i` is singular,
2. each `X_i ⟶ Spec R` is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, and
3. `X_m` is regular.

The sequence is `Stacks.SemistableReduction.NodalBlowupChain f Y h` with `h : Y ⟶ X` its
composite, which records (1) and (2) at every step, and (3) is `IsRegular Y`. The generic fibre is
the fibre of `f` over the generic point `⊥` of `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_nodalBlowupChain_isRegular {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) (hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f)
    (hsmooth : Smooth (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (⊥ : PrimeSpectrum R))) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (h : Y ⟶ X), NodalBlowupChain f Y h ∧ IsRegular Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_of_isContractionOfExceptionalCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDF.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring and let
`f : X ⟶ Spec R` be at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one. Let `b : X ⟶ X'` be the
contraction of an exceptional curve `E ⊆ X` of the first kind, presented by its ideal sheaf `D`
and an isomorphism `e : 𝐏¹_κ ≅ E`. Then `X'` is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over
`R`: there is a morphism `f' : X' ⟶ Spec R` with `b ≫ f' = f`, and it is at-worst-nodal of
relative dimension one.

Away from the contracted point `b` is an isomorphism, so the only issue is a neighbourhood of
that point. The closed fibre of `f` is reduced, so the uniformizer of `R` vanishes to order one
along `E` and therefore lies in the maximal ideal at the contracted point but not in its square.
The local ring there being regular of dimension two, the local ring of the closed fibre is
regular of dimension one; its residue field is geometrically reduced over the residue field of
`R` because the closed fibre of `f` is. Hence the closed fibre of `f'` is smooth at the
contracted point, and with flatness so is `f'`; a morphism smooth of relative dimension one is
at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne_of_isContractionOfExceptionalCurve
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (D : X.IdealSheafData) (κ : Type u) [Field κ]
    (e : projectiveLineProj κ ≅ D.subscheme)
    (hE : D.IsExceptionalCurveOfFirstKind κ e)
    (b : X ⟶ X') (hb : IsContractionOfExceptionalCurve D b)
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
    (hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f) :
    ∃ f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R),
      b ≫ f' = f ∧ IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.tfae_hasSemistableReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDG.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field `K` and
let `C` be a smooth projective curve over `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`. The following are equivalent:
1. there exists a proper model of `C` which is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over `R`,
2. there exists a minimal model of `C` which is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over
   `R`, and
3. any minimal model of `C` is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over `R`.

Condition (1) is the base's `Stacks.Models.HasSemistableReduction`, the definition of semistable
reduction ([Stacks, Tag 0CDH]); minimal models are `Stacks.Models.IsMinimalModel`
([Stacks, Tag 0C2V]).
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_hasSemistableReduction {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (hc : IsProjective c)
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)] :
    List.TFAE [HasSemistableReduction R c hc,
      ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
        (e : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))),
        IsMinimalModel c p e ∧ IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne p,
      ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
        (e : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))),
        IsMinimalModel c p e → IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne p]

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.HasSemistableReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDH.** A smooth projective curve `C` over the fraction field `K` of
a discrete valuation ring `R`, with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`, has *semistable reduction* if there is a
proper model `X ⟶ Spec R` of `C` which is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.
declarations.comment: existence of a proper model of the curve that is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.tfae_hasGoodReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDI.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field `K` and
let `C` be a smooth projective curve over `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`. The following are equivalent:
1. there exists a proper smooth model for `C`,
2. there exists a minimal model for `C` which is smooth over `R`,
3. any minimal model is smooth over `R`.

Condition (1) is the base's `Stacks.Models.HasGoodReduction`, the definition of good reduction
([Stacks, Tag 0CDJ]). A smooth proper model is minimal: its special fibre is connected
([Stacks, Tag 0C62]) and smooth, hence irreducible, so its numerical type is minimal
([Stacks, Tag 0CA6]).
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_hasGoodReduction {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (hc : IsProjective c)
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)] :
    List.TFAE [HasGoodReduction R c hc,
      ∃ (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
        (e : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))),
        IsMinimalModel c p e ∧ Smooth p,
      ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
        (e : C ≅ pullback p (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R K)))),
        IsMinimalModel c p e → Smooth p]

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.HasGoodReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDJ.** A smooth projective curve `C` over the fraction field `K` of
a discrete valuation ring `R`, with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`, has *good reduction* if there is a
proper model `X ⟶ Spec R` of `C` which is smooth over `R`.
declarations.comment: existence of a proper smooth model of the curve

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RealConicModel.realConic_example
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDL.** Let `R = ℝ[[π]]` with fraction field `K`, let
`X = V(T₁² + T₂² - πT₀²) ⊆ ℙ²_R` and let `C = V(T₁² + T₂² - πT₀²) ⊆ ℙ²_K` be its generic fibre.
1. The base change of `X` to `ℂ[[π]]` is the scheme `V(T₁T₂ - πT₀²)` of [Stacks, Tag 0CA0].
2. `X` is regular, and its special fibre is irreducible yet singular.
3. `X` is a minimal model of `C`, and the unique one: every minimal model of `C` is isomorphic to
   `X` as a model.
4. `C` has genus `0` and does not have good reduction over `R`: an extension of `R` is needed even
   in genus `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem realConic_example :
    IsPullback (splitMap PowerSeries.X (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) (PowerSeries ℂ))
        iPowerSeries_sq two_mul_halfPowerSeries
        (GenusZero.isHomogeneous_conicEquation (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℂ))
        (by rw [algebraMap_powerSeries_X]; rfl) ≫
        PlaneCurveModel.mapMap (equation PowerSeries.X) (isHomogeneous_equation _)
          (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) (PowerSeries ℂ)))
      (GenusZero.conicToSpec (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℂ))
      (toSpec (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) (PowerSeries ℂ)))) ∧
    IsRegular (scheme (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ)) ∧
    IrreducibleSpace (specialFiber (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (PowerSeries ℝ))) ∧
    ¬ IsRegular (specialFiber (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (PowerSeries ℝ))) ∧
    IsMinimalModel (toSpec (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K PowerSeries.X))
      (toSpec (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ)) (genericFiberIso K PowerSeries.X) ∧
    (∀ (Y : Scheme.{0}) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of (PowerSeries ℝ)))
      (eY : scheme (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K PowerSeries.X) ≅
        pullback pY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K)))),
      IsMinimalModel (toSpec (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K PowerSeries.X)) pY eY →
        ∃ φ : scheme (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ) ≅ Y,
          φ.hom ≫ pY = toSpec (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ) ∧
          (genericFiberIso K PowerSeries.X).hom ≫
              pullback.fst (toSpec (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℝ))
                (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K))) ≫ φ.hom =
            eY.hom ≫
              pullback.fst pY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K)))) ∧
    genus (toSpec (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K PowerSeries.X)) = 0 ∧
    ¬ HasGoodReduction (PowerSeries ℝ) (toSpec (algebraMap (PowerSeries ℝ) K PowerSeries.X))
      (isProjective_toSpec_powerSeries K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.semistableReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDN.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field `K` and
`C` a smooth projective curve over `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`. Then there is an extension of
discrete valuation rings `R ⊆ R'` inducing a finite separable extension `K'/K` of fraction fields
such that `C_{K'}` has semistable reduction over `R'`. More precisely:

1. if the genus of `C` is zero, there is a separable `K'/K` of degree `2` with `C_{K'} ≅ 𝐏¹_{K'}`,
   and `C_{K'}` is the generic fibre of the smooth projective `𝐏¹_{R'}` over the integral closure
   `R'` of `R` in `K'`;
2. if the genus of `C` is one, there is a finite separable `K'/K` such that `C_{K'}` has
   semistable reduction over `R'_𝔪` for every maximal ideal `𝔪` of the integral closure `R'` of `R`
   in `K'`, and the special fibre of the minimal model of `C_{K'}` over `R'_𝔪` is a smooth genus
   one curve or a cycle of rational curves;
3. if the genus `g` of `C` is at least two, there is a finite separable `K'/K` of degree at most
   `B_g` such that `C_{K'}` has semistable reduction over `R'_𝔪` for every maximal ideal `𝔪` of
   the integral closure `R'` of `R` in `K'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem semistableReduction
    (R K : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K]
    [IsFractionRing R K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c]
    (hproj : IsProjective c) [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)] :
    haveI : IsProper c := hproj.isProper
    (∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
      (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'), FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧
      ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : IsDomain R') (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R')
        (_ : Algebra R' K') (_ : IsFractionRing R' K') (_ : Algebra R R')
        (_ : IsScalarTower R R' K'), IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R') ∧
        HasSemistableReduction R'
          (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K'))))
          (hproj.pullback_snd _)) ∧
    (genus c = 0 →
      ∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
        (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'),
        FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧ Module.finrank K K' = 2 ∧
        Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K')))) ≅
          Over.mk (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of K')) ↘ Spec (.of K'))) ∧
        IsFractionRing (integralClosure R K') K' ∧
        Smooth (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ↘
          Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ∧
        IsProjective (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ↘
          Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ∧
        Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K')))) ≅
          Over.mk (pullback.snd (C := Scheme.{u})
            (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ↘
              Spec (.of (integralClosure R K')))
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (integralClosure R K') K')))))) ∧
    (genus c = 1 →
      ∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
        (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'), FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧
        HasSemistableReductionAtMaximalIdeals R K'
          (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K'))))
          (hproj.pullback_snd _) ∧
        HasGenusOneMinimalFibresAtMaximalIdeals R K'
          (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K'))))) ∧
    (2 ≤ genus c →
      ∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
        (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'), FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧
        Module.finrank K K' ≤
          AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.semistableReductionDegreeBound (genus c) ∧
        HasSemistableReductionAtMaximalIdeals R K'
          (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K'))))
          (hproj.pullback_snd _))

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.exists_genusOne_semistableReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDN (2), genus one.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring with fraction
field `K` and `C` a smooth projective curve of genus one over `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`. Then there
is a finite separable extension `K'/K` such that `C_{K'}` has semistable reduction over `R'_𝔪` for
every maximal ideal `𝔪` of the integral closure `R'` of `R` in `K'`, and the special fibre of the
minimal model of `C_{K'}` over `R'_𝔪` is a smooth genus one curve or a cycle of rational
curves.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_genusOne_semistableReduction
    (R K : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K]
    [IsFractionRing R K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c]
    (hproj : IsProjective c) [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)]
    (hg : genus c = 1) :
    haveI : IsProper c := hproj.isProper
    ∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
      (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'), FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧
      HasSemistableReductionAtMaximalIdeals R K'
        (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K'))))
        (hproj.pullback_snd _) ∧
      HasGenusOneMinimalFibresAtMaximalIdeals R K'
        (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K'))))
declarations.comment: (2), genus one

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.exists_hasSemistableReductionAtMaximalIdeals_of_two_le_genus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDN (3), genus at least two.** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring with
fraction field `K` and `C` a smooth projective curve over `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`, of genus
`g ≥ 2`. Then there is a finite separable extension `K'/K` of degree at most `B_g` such that
`C_{K'}` has semistable reduction over `R'_𝔪` for every maximal ideal `𝔪` of the integral closure
`R'` of `R` in `K'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hasSemistableReductionAtMaximalIdeals_of_two_le_genus
    (R K : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K]
    [IsFractionRing R K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c]
    (hproj : IsProjective c) [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)]
    (hg : 2 ≤ genus c) :
    haveI : IsProper c := hproj.isProper
    ∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
      (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'), FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧
      Module.finrank K K' ≤ AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.semistableReductionDegreeBound
        (genus c) ∧
      HasSemistableReductionAtMaximalIdeals R K'
        (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K'))))
        (hproj.pullback_snd _)
declarations.comment: (3), genus at least two

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.genusZero_splitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDN, part (1).** Let `R` be a discrete valuation ring with fraction
field `K` and `C` a smooth projective curve over `K` with `H⁰(C, 𝒪_C) = K`. If the genus of `C`
is zero, then there exists a separable extension `K'/K` of degree `2` such that
`C_{K'} ≅ 𝐏¹_{K'}`, and hence `C_{K'}` is isomorphic to the generic fibre of the smooth projective
scheme `𝐏¹_{R'}` over the integral closure `R'` of `R` in `K'` (whose fraction field is `K'`).

The extension `K'` is returned with an `R`-algebra structure compatible with `K ⟶ K'`, the
integral closure is `integralClosure R K'`, and the generic fibre is the base change of
`𝐏¹_{R'} ⟶ Spec R'` along `Spec K' ⟶ Spec R'`; both isomorphisms are over `K'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem genusZero_splitting (R K : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]
    [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] {C : Scheme.{u}} (c : C ⟶ Spec (.of K))
    [IsCurve K c] [Smooth c] (hc : IsProjective c)
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫ c.appTop)] (hgenus : genus c = 0) :
    ∃ (K' : Type u) (_ : Field K') (_ : Algebra K K') (_ : Algebra R K')
      (_ : IsScalarTower R K K'),
      FiniteDimensional K K' ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K K' ∧ Module.finrank K K' = 2 ∧
      Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K')))) ≅
        Over.mk (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of K')) ↘ Spec (.of K'))) ∧
      IsFractionRing (integralClosure R K') K' ∧
      Smooth (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ↘
        Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ∧
      IsProjective (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ↘
        Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ∧
      Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd c (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K K')))) ≅
        Over.mk (pullback.snd (C := Scheme.{u})
          (projectiveSpaceOver 1 (Spec (.of (integralClosure R K'))) ↘
            Spec (.of (integralClosure R K')))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (integralClosure R K') K')))))
declarations.comment: (1), genus zero

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.subsingleton_picardGroup_basicOpen_map_of_residueFieldAlgHom
declarations.doc:
**The Picard group of `ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}` dies over a field embedding `κ(t)`.** Let `t = V₊(f)` be
the closed point of `ℙ¹_k` cut out by a homogeneous irreducible form `f` not divisible by `T₁`,
and let `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}`. If a field `k'` admits a `k`-embedding of the residue field `κ(t)`,
then `Pic(X_{k'}) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_picardGroup_basicOpen_map_of_residueFieldAlgHom
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] {d : ℕ}
    {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} (hf : f.IsHomogeneous d) (hirr : Irreducible f)
    (hX : ¬ MvPolynomial.X (1 : Fin 2) ∣ f)
    [(Ideal.span {dehomogenize k f}).IsPrime]
    (ψ : (Ideal.span {dehomogenize k f}).ResidueField →ₐ[k] k') :
    Subsingleton (PicardGroup
      (Proj.basicOpen (grading k') (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k k') f)).toScheme.presheaf
      (Proj.basicOpen (grading k')
        (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k k') f)).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2)
declarations.comment: clause (6): after enlarging `k` to a field `k'` admitting a `k`-embedding `κ(t) → k'`, the Picard group of the base change of `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}` is trivial

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.subsingleton_picardGroup_basicOpen_map_of_X_one_dvd
declarations.doc:
**The Picard group of `ℙ¹_k ∖ {V₊(T₁)}` dies over every field extension.** If `T₁` divides
`f`, then the Picard group of the base change of `D₊(f)` to any field extension `k'` of `k` is
trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_picardGroup_basicOpen_map_of_X_one_dvd
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
    {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} (hdvd : MvPolynomial.X (1 : Fin 2) ∣ f) :
    Subsingleton (PicardGroup
      (Proj.basicOpen (grading k') (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k k') f)).toScheme.presheaf
      (Proj.basicOpen (grading k')
        (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k k') f)).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2)
declarations.comment: clause (6) at the point at infinity `t = V₊(T₁)`, i.e. for `T₁ ∣ f`: the Picard group of the base change of `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}` to an arbitrary field extension `k'` is trivial, with no hypothesis on `k'`

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.subsingleton_picardGroup_basicOpen_map_of_residueFieldAlgHom_of_isPrime
declarations.doc:
**The Picard group of `ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}` dies over a field embedding `κ(t)`.** Let `t = V₊(f)` be
the closed point of `ℙ¹_k` cut out by a homogeneous irreducible form `f`, with `κ(t)` the residue
field of the prime ideal generated by the dehomogenization of `f`, and let `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}`. If a
field `k'` admits a `k`-embedding of `κ(t)`, then `Pic(X_{k'}) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_picardGroup_basicOpen_map_of_residueFieldAlgHom_of_isPrime
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] {d : ℕ}
    {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} (hf : f.IsHomogeneous d) (hirr : Irreducible f)
    [(Ideal.span {dehomogenize k f}).IsPrime]
    (ψ : (Ideal.span {dehomogenize k f}).ResidueField →ₐ[k] k') :
    Subsingleton (PicardGroup
      (Proj.basicOpen (grading k') (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k k') f)).toScheme.presheaf
      (Proj.basicOpen (grading k')
        (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k k') f)).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2)
declarations.comment: clause (6) with the extra hypothesis `t ≠ V₊(T₁)` removed from the statement: for a closed point `t` of `ℙ¹_k` presented in the standard chart, a `k`-embedding `κ(t) → k'` makes the Picard group of the base change of `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}` trivial

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.surjective_complementRestrictHom
declarations.doc:
**The restriction map `ℤ = Pic(ℙ¹_k) → Pic(X)` is surjective**, for
`X = ℙ¹_k ∖ V₊(f)`.
declarations.statement: theorem surjective_complementRestrictHom : Function.Surjective (complementRestrictHom f)
declarations.comment: the displayed surjection `ℤ = Pic(ℙ¹_k) → Pic(X)` for `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}`, by Tag 0BD9 for the surjectivity and Tag 0BXJ for the identification of `Pic(ℙ¹_k)` with `ℤ`

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.surjective_complementZModHom
declarations.doc: **The map `ℤ/dℤ → Pic(X)` is surjective**, for `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ V₊(f)` and `d = deg f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_complementZModHom {d : ℕ} (hf : f ∈ grading k d) :
    Function.Surjective (complementZModHom f hf)
declarations.comment: the computation `Pic(X) = ℤ/dℤ` for `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}`, surjectivity half: the displayed map factors through `ℤ/dℤ` by a surjection, `d = deg f = [κ(t) : k]`

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.nsmul_finrank_residueField_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**`Pic(X)` is killed by `d = [κ(t) : k]`**, the residue degree of the removed closed point
`t = V₊(f)` of `ℙ¹_k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nsmul_finrank_residueField_eq_zero {d : ℕ} {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k}
    (hf : f.IsHomogeneous d) (hirr : Irreducible f)
    (hX : ¬ MvPolynomial.X (1 : Fin 2) ∣ f)
    [(Ideal.span {dehomogenize k f}).IsPrime]
    (c : (Proj.basicOpen (grading k) f).toScheme.picardGroup) :
    Module.finrank k (Ideal.span {dehomogenize k f}).ResidueField • c = 0
declarations.comment: `Pic(X)` is killed by `d = [κ(t) : k]` for `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}`, the residue degree read in the standard chart

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.complementZModEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`Pic(X) = ℤ/dℤ`.** Let `t = V₊(f)` be the closed point of `ℙ¹_k` cut out by a homogeneous
irreducible form `f` of degree `d`, and let `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}`. The surjection
`ℤ = Pic(ℙ¹_k) ↠ Pic(X)` has kernel `dℤ`, so it induces an isomorphism `ℤ/dℤ ≃ Pic(X)`.
declarations.comment: the computation `Pic(X) = ℤ/dℤ` for `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}`, as the isomorphism `ℤ/dℤ ≃+ Pic(X)` induced by the displayed surjection, `d = deg f = [κ(t) : k]`

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveLine.nontrivial_picardGroup_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
**`Pic(X) ≠ 0` for a non-rational point.** If the closed point `t = V₊(f)` of `ℙ¹_k` has
degree `d > 1`, equivalently is not a `k`-rational point, then the Picard group of
`X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}` is nonzero.
declarations.comment: `Pic(X) ≠ 0` for `X = ℙ¹_k ∖ {t}` when `t` is not a `k`-rational point, i.e. when `d = [κ(t) : k] > 1`; this is what makes the example a counterexample to Tag 0CC5

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.nonempty_equivalence_galoisDescentData_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Galois descent for quasi-coherent modules.**  For a finite Galois extension `K/k` with
group `G` and a scheme `X` over `k`, the category of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules is equivalent
to the category of systems `(ℱ, (φ_σ)_{σ ∈ G})` where `ℱ` is quasi-coherent on `X_K`, each
`φ_σ : ℱ ≅ f_σ^* ℱ` is an isomorphism, and `φ_(στ) = f_σ^*(φ_τ) ∘ φ_σ`.  Here
`f_σ = id_X × Spec σ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_equivalence_galoisDescentData_baseChange :
    Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Z.left.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ≌
      GaloisDescentData (K ≃ₐ[k] K) (baseChangeProjection k K Z)
        (baseChangeOverAction k K Z))

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.continuousSMul_galoisPicardAction
declarations.doc:
**The continuity clause of Stacks Tag 0CDT.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a quasi-compact,
quasi-separated scheme over `k`, and let `K/k` be a Galois extension. The action of `Gal(K/k)`
on `Pic(X_K)` by pullback along the twists `id_X × Spec(σ)` is continuous for the Krull topology
on the Galois group and the discrete topology on the Picard group: every class descends to a
finite subextension `E` (Tag 0B8W (2)), hence is fixed by the open subgroup `Gal(K/E)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuousSMul_galoisPicardAction (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [CompactSpace X.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X.left]
    [TopologicalSpace (ofScheme (SchemeOver.baseChange k K X))]
    [DiscreteTopology (ofScheme (SchemeOver.baseChange k K X))] :
    letI := galoisPicardAction k K X
    ContinuousSMul (K ≃ₐ[k] K) (ofScheme (SchemeOver.baseChange k K X))
declarations.comment: continuity of the action of `Gal(k'/k)` on `Pic(X_{k'})`, proved from Tag 0B8W (2) through `exists_finiteSubextension_schemePullbackClass_eq`

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.injective_schemePullbackClass_of_globalSectionsIso
declarations.doc:
**The injectivity half of Stacks Tag 0CDT.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated
scheme over a field `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k`, and let `k'/k` be a field extension. Then the
pullback map `Pic(X) → Pic(X_{k'})` is injective: `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` is then a field, hence
semi-local, and Tag 0CC5 applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_schemePullbackClass_of_globalSectionsIso {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k']
    (φ : k →+* k') {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (hf : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)) :
    Function.Injective (schemePullbackClass (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))))
declarations.comment: injectivity of `Pic(X) → Pic(X_{k'})`, proved from Tag 0CC5; the full identification is `bijOn_schemePullbackClass_galoisFixedClasses`

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.bijOn_schemePullbackClass_galoisFixedClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDT.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a quasi-compact,
quasi-separated scheme over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` admitting a `k`-rational point, and let
`k'/k` be a Galois extension. Then pullback along `X_{k'} ⟶ X` is a bijection of `Pic(X)` onto
the classes of `Pic(X_{k'})` fixed by `Gal(k'/k)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_schemePullbackClass_galoisFixedClasses (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k']
    [Algebra k k'] [IsGalois k k'] (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [CompactSpace X.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X.left]
    (hΓ : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ X.hom.appTop))
    (pt : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X.left) (hpt : pt ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    Set.BijOn (schemePullbackClass (pullback.fst X.hom
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))) Set.univ
      (galoisFixedClasses k k' X)
declarations.comment: the identification `Pic(X) = Pic(X_{k'})^{Gal(k'/k)}`. The continuity clause of the tag is `Stacks.Picard.continuousSMul_galoisPicardAction`

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.exists_finite_separable_torsionBy_of_genus_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDU (1).** Let `k` be a field, let `n` be prime to the characteristic
of `k`, and let `X` be a smooth proper curve over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and of genus `1`.
Then there is a finite separable extension `k'/k` such that `X_{k'}` has a `k'`-rational point
and `Pic(X_{k'})[n] ≅ (ℤ/nℤ)^{⊕2}`.

The point is a closed point with finite separable residue field, which exists by Tag 056U.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_separable_torsionBy_of_genus_eq_one [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] [IsProper f]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)] (hg : genus f = 1) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k'), FiniteDimensional k k' ∧
      Algebra.IsSeparable k k' ∧
      (∃ t : Spec (.of k') ⟶ pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))),
        t ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) = 𝟙 _) ∧
      Nonempty (Submodule.torsionBy ℤ
        (ofScheme (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))) (n : ℤ) ≃+
        (Fin 2 → ZMod n))

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.exists_finite_separable_torsionBy_of_two_le_genus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDU (2).** Let `k` be a field, let `n` be prime to the characteristic
of `k`, and let `X` be a smooth proper curve over `k` with `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = k` and of genus
`g ≥ 2`. Then there is a finite separable extension `k'/k` with `[k' : k] ≤ (2g - 2)(n^{2g})!`
such that `X_{k'}` has a `k'`-rational point and `Pic(X_{k'})[n] ≅ (ℤ/nℤ)^{⊕2g}`.

The closed point of degree at most `2g - 2` with separable residue field is Tag 0CD4.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_separable_torsionBy_of_two_le_genus [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] [IsProper f]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop)] (hg : 2 ≤ genus f) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k'), FiniteDimensional k k' ∧
      Algebra.IsSeparable k k' ∧
      Module.finrank k k' ≤ (2 * genus f - 2) * (n ^ (2 * genus f)).factorial ∧
      (∃ t : Spec (.of k') ⟶ pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))),
        t ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) = 𝟙 _) ∧
      Nonempty (Submodule.torsionBy ℤ
        (ofScheme (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))) (n : ℤ) ≃+
        (Fin (2 * genus f) → ZMod n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_iso_normalizationScheme_sigma_reducedComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDV.** Let `X` be a scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely
many irreducible components, and give each irreducible component of `X` its reduced induced
closed subscheme structure. Then the coproduct of the normalizations of those components, with
its canonical morphism to `X`, is the normalization of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_normalizationScheme_sigma_reducedComponent
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    ∃ e : (∐ fun Z : irreducibleComponents X ↦ (X.reducedComponent Z).normalizationScheme
        (X.finite_irreducibleComponents_reducedComponent Z)) ≅ X.normalizationScheme hX,
      e.hom ≫ X.normalization hX =
        Sigma.desc fun Z : irreducibleComponents X ↦
          (X.reducedComponent Z).normalization
            (X.finite_irreducibleComponents_reducedComponent Z) ≫ X.reducedComponentι Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIntegral_of_isVariety_of_smoothAt_rationalPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDW.** A variety over a field with a rational point at which its
structure morphism is smooth is geometrically integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyIntegral_of_isVariety_of_smoothAt_rationalPoint
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f]
    (s : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = 𝟙 _)
    (hsm : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f (s.base (genericPoint (Spec (.of k))))) :
    GeometricallyIntegral f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.exists_mulEquiv_globalSections_coherentMul_of_faithfullyFlat_trivialization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDX, the clause that the multiplication is an isomorphism.** For a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme `X` over `A`, a faithfully flat ring map `φ : A →+* B` and
an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` whose pullback to `X_B` is trivial, the canonical multiplication

`Γ(X, L) ⊗_{Γ(X, 𝒪_X)} Γ(X, L^{⊗ -1}) ⟶ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`

is an isomorphism. The multiplication is the coherent multiplication of Tag 01CU in degrees
`(1, -1)`, written out on pure tensors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mulEquiv_globalSections_coherentMul_of_faithfullyFlat_trivialization
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (hL : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial
      (Limits.pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).presheaf
      (Limits.pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).ringCatSheaf.property
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (Limits.pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))).obj L)) :
    letI : Module Γ(X, ⊤)
        ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L (-1)).val.obj (.op ⊤)) :=
      ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L (-1)).val.obj (.op ⊤)).isModule
    ∃ e : TensorProduct Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(L, ⊤)
        ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L (-1)).val.obj (.op ⊤))
        ≃ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)] Γ(X, ⊤),
      ∀ s t, e (TensorProduct.tmul Γ(X, ⊤) s t) =
        (((tensorPowerCoherence X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L).mulIso 1 (-1)).hom.val.app
            (.op ⊤)).hom
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorSheafification.toSheafify X.presheaf
            X.ringCatSheaf.property
            ((PresheafOfModules.tensorObj (O := X.presheaf)
              ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L 1).val)
              ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L (-1)).val)))).app (.op ⊤)).hom
            ((((tensorPowerOneIso X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L).inv.val.app
              (.op ⊤)).hom s) ⊗ₜ[Γ(X, ⊤)] t))
declarations.comment: multiplication is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.invertible_globalSections_tensorInverse_of_faithfullyFlat_trivialization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDX, the clause about the global sections of the inverse sheaf.** For
a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme `X` over `A`, a faithfully flat ring map `φ : A →+* B`
and an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` whose pullback to `X_B` is trivial, the global sections
`Γ(X, L^{⊗ -1})` of the inverse tensor power form an invertible module over the global functions
`Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertible_globalSections_tensorInverse_of_faithfullyFlat_trivialization
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [hinv : IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (hL : IsTrivial
      (Limits.pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).presheaf
      (Limits.pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).ringCatSheaf.property
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (Limits.pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))).obj L)) :
    letI : Module Γ(X, ⊤)
        ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L (-1)).val.obj (.op ⊤)) :=
      ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L (-1)).val.obj (.op ⊤)).isModule
    Module.Invertible Γ(X, ⊤)
      ((tensorPower X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L (-1)).val.obj (.op ⊤))
declarations.comment: global sections of the inverse sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.invertible_globalSections_of_faithfullyFlat_trivialization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDX, the clause about the global sections of the sheaf.** For a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme `X` over `A`, a faithfully flat ring map `φ : A →+* B` and
an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` whose pullback to `X_B` is trivial, the global sections `Γ(X, L)`
form an invertible module over the global functions `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem invertible_globalSections_of_faithfullyFlat_trivialization
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (L : X.Modules)
    [hinv : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsTrivial
      (Limits.pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).presheaf
      (Limits.pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).ringCatSheaf.property
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (Limits.pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))).obj L)) :
    Module.Invertible Γ(X, ⊤) Γ(L, ⊤)
declarations.comment: global sections of the sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.injective_picardPullback_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDY.** Let `A → B` be a faithfully flat ring map and let `X` be a
scheme over `A` which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and whose ring of global functions
`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X)` is semi-local. Then the pullback map `Pic(X) → Pic(X_B)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_picardPullback_of_faithfullyFlat
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat)
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum Γ(X, ⊤))] :
    Function.Injective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClassHom
      (Limits.pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.PicardBaseChange.injective_schemePullbackClass_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CDY.** Let `A → B` be faithfully flat and let `X` be a quasi-compact,
quasi-separated scheme over `A` whose ring of global functions is semilocal. Then pullback to the
base change `X_B` is injective on Picard groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_schemePullbackClass_of_faithfullyFlat
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum Γ(X, ⊤))] :
    Function.Injective (Stacks.Picard.schemePullbackClass
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))))
