declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus
declarations.doc:
The geometric genus `g_geom(X/k)` of a proper scheme `X` over a field `k`: the sum, over the
irreducible components of dimension one of the base change of `X` to an algebraic closure of
`k`, of the genus of the normalization of that component with its reduced structure.

This is the invariant introduced in the preamble of the source's section on genus versus
geometric genus.
declarations.statement:
public def geometricGenus (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProper g] : ℕ
declarations.comment: definition of the geometric genus g_geom(X/k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_eq_sum_components
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a proper scheme of dimension at most one over `k`. The
geometric genus of `X` over `k` is the sum of the geometric genera of
the irreducible components of `X` of dimension one, each taken with its reduced closed subscheme
structure; components of dimension zero contribute nothing.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricGenus_eq_sum_components {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) :
    letI : IsNoetherian X :=
      { toIsLocallyNoetherian := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian g
        toCompactSpace := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace g }
    letI : Finite (irreducibleComponents X) :=
      (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNoetherian (X := X)).to_subtype
    letI : Fintype (irreducibleComponents X) := Fintype.ofFinite _
    geometricGenus k g =
      ∑ C : irreducibleComponents X,
        if topologicalKrullDim (irreducibleComponentIdeal C).subscheme = 1 then
          geometricGenus k ((irreducibleComponentIdeal C).subschemeι ≫ g)
        else 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_reduction_birational_normalization
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a proper scheme of dimension at most one over `k`.  Then

1. the reduction `X_red` has the same geometric genus as `X`;
2. the source of a birational proper morphism `X' ⟶ X` has the same geometric genus as `X`; and
3. the normalization `X^ν` has the same geometric genus as `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricGenus_reduction_birational_normalization {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    letI : IsProper (normalizationOverField k g ≫ g) :=
      isProper_normalizationOverField_comp k g
    geometricGenus k (X.reductionι ≫ g) = geometricGenus k g ∧
      (∀ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f : X' ⟶ X) [IsProper f], IsBirational f →
        geometricGenus k (f ≫ g) = geometricGenus k g) ∧
      geometricGenus k (normalizationOverField k g ≫ g) = geometricGenus k g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genus_le_of_isAffineHom_of_isZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CE3] with its three cohomological inputs as hypotheses.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be
an affine morphism of schemes over a field `k`, and let `φ : 𝒪_X ⟶ f_*𝒪_Y` be the canonical
comparison map. If `H¹(X, coker φ) = 0`, if `H²(X, ker φ) = 0` and if `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)` is finite
dimensional over `k`, then the genus of `Y` is at most the genus of `X`, that is
`dim_k H¹(Y, 𝒪_Y) ≤ dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`.

The three hypotheses replace the properness of `X` over `k`, the bound on its dimension and the
hypothesis that `f` is a closed immersion over a dense open, which the source uses only to
produce them; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_le_of_isAffineHom_of_isZero (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsAffineHom f]
    (hcoker : IsZero (cohomologyOverField k g (cokernel (structureSheafToPushforward f)) 1))
    (hker : IsZero (cohomologyOverField k g (kernel (structureSheafToPushforward f)) 2))
    (hfin : FiniteDimensional k (cohomologyOverField k g (structureSheafModule X) 1)) :
    genus (f ≫ g) ≤ genus g
declarations.comment: with the two cohomology vanishings and the finiteness of H¹(X,𝒪_X) as hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genus_le_of_isFinite_of_isClosedImmersion_over_dense_open
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CE3].** Let `k` be a field, let `g : X ⟶ Spec k` be proper with
`dim X ≤ 1`, and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be finite and a closed immersion over a dense open `U ⊆ X`.
Then the genus of `Y` is at most the genus of `X`, that is
`dim_k H¹(Y, 𝒪_Y) ≤ dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.genus_le_of_isAffineHom_of_isZero` with its three cohomological
hypotheses discharged; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_le_of_isFinite_of_isClosedImmersion_over_dense_open
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1)
    (U : X.Opens) (hdense : Dense (U : Set X))
    (hclosed : IsClosedImmersion (pullback.snd f U.ι)) :
    genus (f ≫ g) ≤ genus g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.genus_le_and_isIso_of_isProper_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a proper scheme of dimension at most one over `k`. If
`f : X' ⟶ X` is a birational proper morphism, then

  `dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X) ≥ dim_k H¹(X', 𝒪_{X'})`,

and if moreover `X` is reduced, `H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ H⁰(X', 𝒪_{X'})` is surjective and equality holds,
then `X' = X`.

Here `dim_k H¹` is `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` of the structure morphism, and `X' = X` means that
`f` is an isomorphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_le_and_isIso_of_isProper_of_isBirational [IsProper g] (f : X' ⟶ X) [IsProper f]
    (hf : IsBirational f) (hX : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    genus (f ≫ g) ≤ genus g ∧
      (IsReduced X → Function.Surjective f.appTop → genus (f ≫ g) = genus g → IsIso f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_le_finSepDegree_mul_genus_toSpecΓ
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a proper integral scheme over `k` whose global regular
functions are exactly `k` and whose base change to an algebraic closure of `k` is irreducible,
reduced and of dimension one.  Writing `κ = Γ(X, ⊤)`, the geometric genus of `X` over `k` is at
most `[κ : k]_s · dim_κ H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricGenus_le_finSepDegree_mul_genus_toSpecΓ
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    [IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ g.appTop)]
    (hirr : IrreducibleSpace (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) g
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
    (hred : IsReduced (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) g
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) g
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))) = 1)
    (hcoker : IsZero (cohomologyOverField (AlgebraicClosure k)
      (pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))
      (cokernel (structureSheafToPushforward (normalizationOverField (AlgebraicClosure k)
        (pullback.snd g
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))))) 1))
    (hker : IsZero (cohomologyOverField (AlgebraicClosure k)
      (pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))
      (kernel (structureSheafToPushforward (normalizationOverField (AlgebraicClosure k)
        (pullback.snd g
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))))) 2))
    (hfin : FiniteDimensional (AlgebraicClosure k) (cohomologyOverField (AlgebraicClosure k)
      (pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))
      (structureSheafModule (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) g
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) 1)) :
    letI : Field Γ(X, ⊤) := (isField_of_universallyClosed k g).toField
    letI : Algebra k Γ(X, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ g.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    geometricGenus k g ≤ Field.finSepDegree k Γ(X, ⊤) * genus X.toSpecΓ
declarations.comment: κ = k, geometrically integral of dim 1, 0CE3's vanishings and H¹ finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_le_genus_of_irreducible
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and `g : X ⟶ Spec k` proper. If the base change `X_{k̄}` of `X` to an
algebraic closure `k̄` of `k` is irreducible, reduced and of dimension one, then
`g_geom(X/k) ≤ g(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricGenus_le_genus_of_irreducible
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (hirr : IrreducibleSpace (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) g
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
    (hred : IsReduced (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) g
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) g
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))) = 1) :
    geometricGenus k g ≤ genus g
declarations.comment: κ = k, geometrically irreducible of dimension one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_le_genus_of_dim_le_one
declarations.doc:
**The per-fibre bound of [Stacks, Tag 0CE5].**  Over an algebraically closed field `K`, the
geometric genus of a proper scheme of dimension at most one is at most its genus.  No hypothesis
is made on the irreducible components: the scheme may be reducible and non-reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricGenus_le_genus_of_dim_le_one (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (q : Z ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsProper q]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (Z : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    geometricGenus K q ≤ genus q
declarations.comment: the per-fibre bound, over an algebraically closed field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_le_finSepDegree_mul_genus_toSpecΓ_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CE5.**  Let `C` be a proper curve over a field `k` and let
`κ = Γ(C, ⊤)` be its field of global regular functions.  Then the geometric genus of `C` over `k`
is at most `[κ : k]_s · dim_κ H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`.

The sum over the `k`-embeddings `κ → k̄` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_eq_finsum_geometricGenus_pullback_snd_toSpecΓ`, and each of its
terms is bounded by the genus of the corresponding fibre by
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricGenus_le_genus_of_dim_le_one`, the fibre being a proper scheme of
dimension one over the algebraically closed field `k̄`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricGenus_le_finSepDegree_mul_genus_toSpecΓ_of_isCurve
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f] :
    letI : Field Γ(C, ⊤) := (isField_of_universallyClosed k f).toField
    letI : Algebra k Γ(C, ⊤) := ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    letI : IsProper C.toSpecΓ := isProper_toSpecΓ f
    geometricGenus k f ≤ Field.finSepDegree k Γ(C, ⊤) * genus C.toSpecΓ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_picardTorsion_le_genus_add_geometricGenus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CE6.**  Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme of dimension at
most one over `k` and let `ℓ` be a prime invertible in `k`.  Then the `ℓ`-torsion of `Pic(X)` is
finite-dimensional
over `F_ℓ` and

`dim_{F_ℓ} Pic(X)[ℓ] ≤ dim_k H¹(X, 𝒪_X) + g_geom(X/k)`.

The proof is the source's: extend the ground field to an algebraic closure and pass to the
reduction (`AlgebraicGeometry.picardTorsion_bound_of_reducedBaseChange`, which is Tag 0CC5, Tag
02KH, Tag 0CE2 (1) and Tag 0CE3), then decompose into connected components
(`AlgebraicGeometry.picardTorsion_bound_of_connectedComponents`) and apply Tag 0C20 to the
one-dimensional ones, the zero-dimensional ones having trivial Picard group.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_picardTorsion_le_genus_add_geometricGenus (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper g]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (hℓ : IsUnit (ℓ : k)) :
    FiniteDimensional (ZMod ℓ) (AddSubgroup.torsionBy (ofScheme X) (ℓ : ℤ)) ∧
      Module.finrank (ZMod ℓ) (AddSubgroup.torsionBy (ofScheme X) (ℓ : ℤ)) ≤
        genus g + geometricGenus k g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.NumericalType.picardGroup_embeds_intersectionCokernel
declarations.doc:
The Picard group of a numerical type embeds in the cokernel of its
integral intersection matrix.
declarations.statement:
public theorem picardGroup_embeds_intersectionCokernel (T : NumericalType) :
    ∃ f : picardGroup T →+ intersectionCokernel T, Function.Injective f

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.exists_isRationalPoint_smoothAt_specialFiber_and_genus_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CE8.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0C61] assume that the curve `C` has a
`K`-rational point. Then

1. the special fibre `X_k` has a `k`-rational point `x` at which `X_k ⟶ Spec(k)` is smooth;
2. every irreducible component `Cᵢ` of `X_k` through `x` has `H⁰(Cᵢ, 𝒪_{Cᵢ}) = k` and
   multiplicity `mᵢ = 1` in `X_k = Σ mᵢCᵢ`;
3. `H⁰(X_k, 𝒪_{X_k}) = k`, and the genus of `X_k` is the genus of `C`.

`H⁰(Y, 𝒪_Y) = k` is the assertion that the canonical map `k ⟶ Γ(Y, 𝒪_Y)` is an isomorphism, and
the genus is `AlgebraicGeometry.genus`, `dim H¹(𝒪)` over the base field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRationalPoint_smoothAt_specialFiber_and_genus_eq (p : Spec (.of S.K) ⟶ S.C)
    (hp : p ≫ S.C_to_K = 𝟙 _) :
    (∃ x : S.specialFiber, IsRationalPoint S.specialFiberToSpec x ∧
      InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt S.specialFiberToSpec x ∧
      ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber, x ∈ Z.1 →
        IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S.k)).inv ≫ (S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Z).appTop) ∧
          S.specialFiberMultiplicity Z = 1) ∧
    IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S.k)).inv ≫ S.specialFiberToSpec.appTop) ∧
      genus S.specialFiberToSpec = genus S.C_to_K
declarations.comment: the k-rational smooth point x of X_k, H⁰(Cᵢ) = k and mᵢ = 1 for the components through x, H⁰(X_k) = k and g(X_k) = g(C)

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.surjective_and_not_injective_of_isMinimalModel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CE9.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61] assume `X` is a minimal
model, `gcd(m₁, …, mₙ) = 1` and `H⁰((X_k)_red, 𝒪) = k`. Then the map
`H¹(X_k, 𝒪_{X_k}) ⟶ H¹((X_k)_red, 𝒪_{(X_k)_red})` induced by the reduction `(X_k)_red ⟶ X_k`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverFieldStructureSheafMap`) is surjective, and it has a nontrivial
kernel, that is it is not injective, as soon as `(X_k)_red ≠ X_k`, that is as soon as `X_k` is not
reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_and_not_injective_of_isMinimalModel
    (hmin : IsMinimalModel S.C_to_K S.X_to_R S.genericFiberIso)
    (hgcd : Finset.univ.gcd S.specialFiberMultiplicity = 1)
    (hred : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S.k)).inv ≫
      (S.specialFiber.reductionι ≫ S.specialFiberToSpec).appTop)) :
    Function.Surjective (cohomologyOverFieldStructureSheafMap S.k S.specialFiberToSpec
        S.specialFiber.reductionι 1) ∧
      (¬ IsReduced S.specialFiber →
        ¬ Function.Injective (cohomologyOverFieldStructureSheafMap S.k S.specialFiberToSpec
          S.specialFiber.reductionι 1))

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.topologicalGenus_add_geometricGenus_le_finrank_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CEA.** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61] suppose the special
fibre `X_k` has a `k`-rational point `x` which is a smooth point of `X_k ⟶ Spec(k)`. Then

`dim_k H¹((X_k)_red, 𝒪_{(X_k)_red}) ≥ g_top + g_geom(X_k/k)`,

where `g_top` is the topological genus ([Stacks, Tag 0C79]) of the numerical type associated to
`X` ([Stacks, Tag 0CA5]), for any enumeration `e` of the irreducible components of `X_k`, and
`g_geom(X_k/k)` is the geometric genus of [Stacks, Section 0CE0]. The cohomology of the reduction
`(X_k)_red` is taken over `k` through `(X_k)_red ⟶ X_k ⟶ Spec(k)`.

Only the rationality of `x` is used; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalGenus_add_geometricGenus_le_finrank_reduction
    (x : S.specialFiber) (hx : IsRationalPoint S.specialFiberToSpec x)
    (_hsm : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt S.specialFiberToSpec x)
    (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber) :
    (S.associatedNumericalType n e).topologicalGenus +
        (geometricGenus S.k S.specialFiberToSpec : ℤ) ≤
      Module.finrank S.k (cohomologyOverField S.k
        (S.specialFiber.reductionι ≫ S.specialFiberToSpec)
        (SheafOfModules.unit S.specialFiber.reduction.ringCatSheaf) 1)
declarations.comment: dim_k H^1((X_k)_red, O) >= g_top + g_geom(X_k/k) when X_k has a k-rational smooth point, g_top the topological genus of the numerical type associated to X

declarations.name: Stacks.Models.RegularProperModelSituation.smooth_of_topologicalGenus_add_geometricGenus_eq_finrank_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CEE**, in corrected form, with the
separability clause of part (2) asserted for the components of positive genus. In the
situation of [Stacks, Tag 0C61] let `x` be a `k`-rational point of `X_k` at which `X_k ⟶ Spec(k)`
is smooth, and suppose equality holds in [Stacks, Tag 0CEA]:
`dim_k H¹((X_k)_red, 𝒪) = g_top + g_geom(X_k/k)`. Then

1. `x` lies on a unique irreducible component of `X_k`, and that component is a smooth,
   H-projective, geometrically irreducible curve over `k`;
2. every other irreducible component `C` has `κ = H⁰(C, 𝒪_C)` finite over `k`, has a `κ`-rational
   point and is smooth over `κ`; and `κ/k` is separable as soon as `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≠ 0`.

**The correction.** The source asserts in (2) that `κ/k` is always separable. That is false: let
`R = 𝔽_p(t)[[π]]`, so `k = 𝔽_p(t)`, let `C = ℙ¹_K`, and let `X` be the blow-up of `ℙ¹_R` at the
closed point `c ∈ ℙ¹_k` with residue field `κ = k(t^{1/p})`, purely inseparable of degree `p` over
`k`. Then `X` is a regular proper model of `C`, `X_k = C₁ + E` is reduced with `C₁ ≅ ℙ¹_k` the
strict transform and `E ≅ ℙ¹_κ` the exceptional curve, the two meeting transversally in one
`κ`-point, so `(C₁ · E) = p`. A `k`-point of `C₁` away from `c` is a smooth rational point of
`X_k`. Here `dim_k H¹(X_k, 𝒪) = 0` (because `χ(X_k, 𝒪) = χ(ℙ¹_K, 𝒪) = 1` and `H⁰(X_k, 𝒪) = k`),
`g_top = 1 - 2 + 1 = 0` and `g_geom(X_k/k) = 0 + 0`, so equality holds; but `H⁰(E, 𝒪_E) = κ` is not
separable over `k`. The source's step "equality in `[κ_i : k] g_i ≥ [κ_i : k]_s g_i ≥ g_geom`
implies `κ_i/k` separable" needs `g_i > 0`; every other assertion of the tag survives.

**The proof.** Equality in the induction of [Stacks, Tag 0CEA] forces equality at each step
(`geometricGenus_eq_and_exists_componentIntersection_eq_weight`): `g_geom(C_Z/k) = [κ_Z : k] g_Z`
for every component, and each component `C_Z` not through `x` meets some `C_W` with
`(C_Z · C_W) = [κ_Z : k]`, which makes `C_Z ∩ C_W` a `κ_Z`-rational point at which `C_Z` is
smooth over `κ_Z`. A smooth rational point makes a curve geometrically integral over its field of
constants ([Stacks, Tag 0CDW]), and a geometrically integral curve whose geometric genus is its
genus is smooth, because its normalization over `k̄` does not change the genus and is therefore
an isomorphism ([Stacks, Tag 0CE4]). Projectivity of the integral proper curve through `x` is
[Stacks, Tag 0A25] for integral curves together with [Stacks, Tag 0BCL].
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_of_topologicalGenus_add_geometricGenus_eq_finrank_reduction
    (x : S.specialFiber) (hx : IsRationalPoint S.specialFiberToSpec x)
    (hsm : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt S.specialFiberToSpec x)
    (n : ℕ) (e : Fin n ≃ irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber)
    (heq : (S.associatedNumericalType n e).topologicalGenus +
        (geometricGenus S.k S.specialFiberToSpec : ℤ) =
      Module.finrank S.k (cohomologyOverField S.k
        (S.specialFiber.reductionι ≫ S.specialFiberToSpec)
        (SheafOfModules.unit S.specialFiber.reduction.ringCatSheaf) 1)) :
    (∃! Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber, x ∈ Z.1) ∧
    (∀ Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber, x ∈ Z.1 →
      Smooth (S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Z) ∧
        Stacks.HProjective.IsHProjective (S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Z) ∧
        GeometricallyIrreducible (S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Z) ∧
        IsCurve S.k (S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Z)) ∧
    (∀ Z : irreducibleComponents S.specialFiber, x ∉ Z.1 →
      letI : Field Γ((S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme, ⊤) :=
        (S.isField_and_finite_globalSections_specialFiberComponent Z).1.toField
      letI : Algebra S.k Γ((S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme, ⊤) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of S.k)).inv ≫ (S.specialFiberComponentToSpec Z).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
      FiniteDimensional S.k Γ((S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme, ⊤) ∧
        (genus (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme.toSpecΓ ≠ 0 →
          Algebra.IsSeparable S.k Γ((S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme, ⊤)) ∧
        (∃ c : (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme,
          IsRationalPoint (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme.toSpecΓ c) ∧
        Smooth (S.specialFiberComponentIdeal Z).subscheme.toSpecΓ)
declarations.comment: (1) in full, and (2) with kappa/k separable when H^1(C, O_C) is nonzero (the corrected form)

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.finite_flat_pushforward_coverMap
declarations.doc:
**`p : X ⟶ Z_R` is finite flat, with `p_* 𝒪_X = ⨁_{i < n} L_R^{⊗ i}`**, the direct sum of
the pullbacks to `Z_R` of the tensor powers of `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_flat_pushforward_coverMap (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    IsFinite (coverMap f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X) ∧
      Flat (coverMap f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X) ∧
      Nonempty ((⨁ fun i : Fin n => (Scheme.Modules.pullback (baseChangeFst f (PowerSeries k))).obj
          (tensorPow L i)) ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
          (coverMap f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit _))
declarations.comment: p : X → Z_R is finite and flat, and p_*O_X = Sym*(L_R)/(φ - π) = O ⊕ L_R ⊕ … ⊕ L_R^{⊗ n-1}; X is built from φ : L^{⊗ n} ≅ O_Z through Symⁿ L ≅ L^{⊗ n}

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.nonempty_coverMapArrowIso
declarations.doc:
**The local description of `p`**: over an affine open `U = Spec A` of `Z` on which `L` is
trivialized by `s`, with `f = φ(s^{⊗ n})` a unit of `A`,
`p⁻¹(U_R) = Spec (A ⊗_k R)[x]/(xⁿ - π f)` over `U_R = Spec (A ⊗_k R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_coverMapArrowIso (U : Z.affineOpens)
    (b : Module.Basis PUnit.{u + 1} Γ(Z, U.1) Γ(L, U.1)) :
    letI := (sectionsStructure f U.1).hom.toAlgebra
    let fU : Γ(Z, U.1) := φ.hom.app U.1 ((symPowIsoTensorPower f L n).hom.app U.1 (basisPow f U b))
    IsUnit fU ∧
      Nonempty (Arrow.mk (coverMap f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k)
          PowerSeries.X ∣_ baseChangeOpen f (PowerSeries k) U.1) ≅
        Arrow.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (Γ(Z, U.1) ⊗[k] PowerSeries k)
          (chartRing k n fU (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries k))))))
declarations.comment: p⁻¹(U_R) = Spec((A ⊗_k R)[x]/(xⁿ - π f)) for U = Spec A trivializing L by s, with f = φ(s^{⊗ n}) a unit

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.finite_etale_genericFibre
declarations.doc: **The morphism of generic fibres `X_K ⟶ Z_K` is finite étale.**
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_etale_genericFibre (hnk : IsUnit (n : k)) :
    IsFinite (coverMapBaseChange f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries k)
        (powerSeriesToLaurent k)) ∧

        (powerSeriesToLaurent k))

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.globalSections_cover
declarations.doc: **`H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = R` and `H⁰(X_K, 𝒪_{X_K}) = K`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem globalSections_cover (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hord : addOrderOf
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass Z.presheaf (structureIsSheaf Z.toRingedSpace) L ‹_›) = n) :
    Function.Bijective
        (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X).appTop ∧
      Function.Bijective (pullback.snd
        (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (powerSeriesToLaurent k).toRingHom))).appTop
declarations.comment: H^0(X, O_X) = R and H^0(X_K, O_{X_K}) = K

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.genus_genericFibre
declarations.doc: **The genus of `X_K` is `n(g - 1) + 1`**; in particular it is `1` when `Z` has genus `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem genus_genericFibre (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (hord : addOrderOf
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.picardClass Z.presheaf (structureIsSheaf Z.toRingedSpace) L ‹_›) = n) :
    (genus (pullback.snd
        (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (powerSeriesToLaurent k).toRingHom))) : ℤ) =
        n * (genus f - 1) + 1 ∧
      (genus f = 1 → genus (pullback.snd
        (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (powerSeriesToLaurent k).toRingHom))) = 1)
declarations.comment: the genus of X_K is n(g - 1) + 1, in particular 1 if Z has genus 1

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.isRegular_model
declarations.doc: **The scheme `X` is regular.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegular_model [Smooth f] (hnk : IsUnit (n : k)) :
    IsRegular (cover f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)
declarations.comment: the scheme X is regular

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.specialFibre_eq_pow
declarations.doc:
**The special fibre `X_k` is `n` times the reduced special fibre as an effective Cartier
divisor**: `π 𝒪_X` and its radical are invertible ideals, and `π 𝒪_X = (rad(π 𝒪_X))ⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialFibre_eq_pow [Smooth f] (hnk : IsUnit (n : k)) :
    Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (specialFibreIdeal f (symPowTrivialization f φ)) ∧
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor
        (specialFibreIdeal f (symPowTrivialization f φ)).radical ∧
      specialFibreIdeal f (symPowTrivialization f φ) =
        (specialFibreIdeal f (symPowTrivialization f φ)).radical ^ n
declarations.comment: the special fibre X_k is n times the reduced special fibre (X_k)_red as an effective Cartier divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.ramification_of_semistable
declarations.doc:
**Any finite extension `K'/K` over which `X_K` attains semistable reduction has ramification
index at least `n`**: the valuation `v_{R'}(π)` of `π` in the integral closure `R'` of `R` in
`K'` is a positive multiple of `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ramification_of_semistable [IsAlgClosed k] [IsProper f] [Nonempty Z] (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (K' : Type u) [Field K'] [Algebra (LaurentSeries k) K']
    [FiniteDimensional (LaurentSeries k) K'] [Algebra (PowerSeries k) K']
    [IsScalarTower (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k) K'] :
    haveI := isDiscreteValuationRing_integralClosure (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k) K'
    haveI := _root_.isFractionRing_integralClosure (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k) K'
    (∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (.of (integralClosure (PowerSeries k) K')))
      (e : pullback (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries k) K'))) ≅
        pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (integralClosure (PowerSeries k) K') K')))),
      Stacks.Models.IsModel (pullback.snd _ _) q e ∧ IsProper q ∧
        IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne q) →
    ∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal (integralClosure (PowerSeries k) K')
      (algebraMap (PowerSeries k) (integralClosure (PowerSeries k) K') PowerSeries.X) =
        (n * m : ℕ)
declarations.comment: any finite extension K'/K over which X_K attains semistable reduction has ramification index at least n: v_{R'}(π) is a positive multiple of n, for R' the integral closure of R in K'

declarations.name: Stacks.CyclicCover.no_universal_bound
declarations.doc:
**There is no universal bound on the degree of an extension over which a genus one curve
attains semistable reduction.** For every `B` there is a curve `X_K` over `K = k((π))` with
`H⁰(X_K, 𝒪) = K` and genus `1`, namely the generic fibre of the cyclic cover of a genus one curve
`Z` by an invertible module of prime order `ℓ > B`, such that every finite extension `K'/K` over
which `X_K` attains semistable reduction has `[K' : K] > B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem no_universal_bound (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (B : ℕ) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (_ : IsCurve k f) (_ : IsProjectiveVariety k f)
      (_ : Smooth f) (L : Z.Modules)
      (_ : SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Z.sheaf.obj Z.ringCatSheaf.property L) (n : ℕ)
      (φ : tensorPow L n ≅ SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf),
      genus (pullback.snd (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (powerSeriesToLaurent k).toRingHom))) = 1 ∧
      Function.Bijective (pullback.snd (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k)
        PowerSeries.X) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (powerSeriesToLaurent k).toRingHom))).appTop ∧
      ∀ (K' : Type u) [Field K'] [Algebra (LaurentSeries k) K']
        [FiniteDimensional (LaurentSeries k) K'] [Algebra (PowerSeries k) K']
        [IsScalarTower (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k) K'],
        haveI := isDiscreteValuationRing_integralClosure (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k) K'
        haveI := _root_.isFractionRing_integralClosure (PowerSeries k) (LaurentSeries k) K'
        (∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (.of (integralClosure (PowerSeries k) K')))
          (e : pullback (coverSnd f (symPowTrivialization f φ) (PowerSeries k) PowerSeries.X)
              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (PowerSeries k) K'))) ≅
            pullback q (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
              (algebraMap (integralClosure (PowerSeries k) K') K')))),
          Stacks.Models.IsModel (pullback.snd _ _) q e ∧ IsProper q ∧
            IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne q) →
        B < Module.finrank (LaurentSeries k) K'
declarations.comment: there is no universal bound for the degree of an extension over which a genus 1 curve attains semistable reduction: for every B there is a curve X_K over K = k((π)) with H⁰(X_K, O) = K and genus 1 such that every finite K'/K over which X_K attains semistable reduction has [K' : K] > B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.semistableReductionDegreeBound
declarations.doc:
The genus-dependent degree bound used in the semistable reduction theorem.
Here `ℓ` is the second prime strictly greater than `768 * g`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def semistableReductionDegreeBound (g : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: Module.flat_and_flat_localization_of_flat_quotient_of_locallyNilpotent
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S → S'` be ring maps with `R → S` of finite type and `R → S'` of finite
presentation, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal all of whose elements are nilpotent, and let `M` be a
finitely presented `S'`-module. If `M/IM` is flat over `S/IS` and `M` is flat over `R`, then `M` is
flat over `S`, and `S_q` is flat and essentially of finite presentation over `R` for every prime
`q ⊆ S` with `M ⊗_S κ(q)` nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.flat_and_flat_localization_of_flat_quotient_of_locallyNilpotent
    {R S S' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra S S']
    [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [Module S' M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [IsScalarTower S S' M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsNilpotent x)
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S'] [Module.FinitePresentation S' M]
    [Module.Flat (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S))
      (M ⧸ (I.map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S M)))]
    [Module.Flat R M] :
    Module.Flat S M ∧
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq]
        [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] [Algebra R Sq] [IsScalarTower R S Sq],
        Nontrivial (M ⊗[S] q.ResidueField) →
          Module.Flat R Sq ∧ (algebraMap R Sq).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.comment:
"Locally nilpotent" is `∀ x ∈ I, IsNilpotent x`. `IM` is written as `IS • ⊤`
over `S`, `S_q` is an abstract localization of `S` at `q`, and "essentially of finite
presentation" is `RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation`; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Koszul.quasiRegular_and_h1Regular_baseChange_of_quotient_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CEP.** Suppose that `B / (f₁, …, fᵣ)` is flat over `A`. If `f` is
quasi-regular, then its image in `B ⊗[A] A'` is quasi-regular; if `f` is H₁-regular, then its
image is H₁-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiRegular_and_h1Regular_baseChange_of_quotient_flat
    {A B A' : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A'] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → B)
    (hflat : Module.Flat A (B ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f))) :
    (IsQuasiRegular B (List.ofFn f) →
      IsQuasiRegular (B ⊗[A] A')
        (List.ofFn (KoszulH1.fp (A := A) (A' := A') f))) ∧
    (Koszul.IsH1Regular f →
      Koszul.IsH1Regular (KoszulH1.fp (A := A) (A' := A') f))

declarations.name: Koszul.flat_quotient_span_of_isQuasiRegular_of_locallyNilpotent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.largestOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CEY.** The largest open of the source of `f : X ⟶ Y` on which the
restriction of `f` has the property `P`, defined as the supremum of all opens `U` of `X` with
`P (U.ι ≫ f)`.

That this open is itself such a locus requires `P` to be local on the source for one of the
four topologies of the source lemma; see `largestOpen_isGreatest_fppf` and its variants.
declarations.statement:
def largestOpen (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) : X.Opens
declarations.comment: open locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.largestOpen_isGreatest_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CEY** for the fppf topology. For `P` local on the source in the fppf
topology, `largestOpen P f` is a locus for `P` and is the greatest open that is one.
declarations.statement:
theorem largestOpen_isGreatest_fppf (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.IsLocalAtSource Scheme.fppfPrecoverage] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsGreatest {U : X.Opens | P (U.ι ≫ f)} (largestOpen P f)
declarations.comment: fppf largest locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_largestOpen_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CEY** for the fppf topology: the largest locus of an fppf-local
property pulls back to the largest locus of the composite along a flat morphism locally of
finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem preimage_largestOpen_fppf (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_largestOpen_iff_of_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CEZ.** Étale morphisms on both sides of a commutative square preserve
membership in the largest open locus of a property étale local on the source and target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_largestOpen_iff_of_etaleAt
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hP : IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget P)
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hcomm : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g) (x' : X')
    (hg' : EtaleAt g' x')
    (hg : EtaleAt g (f'.base x')) :
    g'.base x' ∈ largestOpen P f ↔ x' ∈ largestOpen P f'

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.eq_univ_or_finite_compl_of_invariant_coordinateShear
declarations.doc:
A nonempty open subset of affine `n`-space, for `n ≥ 2`, invariant under
every elementary coordinate shear, is either all of affine space or has finite
complement consisting of closed points whose coordinates are algebraic over
the prime field (and in the latter case the field has positive characteristic).
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_univ_or_finite_compl_of_invariant_coordinateShear
    {k : Type*} [Field k] {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (W : Set (PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)))
    (hWopen : IsOpen W) (hWnonempty : W.Nonempty)
    (hWinv : ∀ (i j : Fin n) (hij : i ≠ j) (d : ℕ),
      PrimeSpectrum.comap (coordinateShear (R := k) i j hij d).toRingHom ⁻¹' W = W) :
    W = Set.univ ∨
      (0 < ringChar k ∧ Wᶜ.Finite ∧ ∀ q ∈ Wᶜ, q.asIdeal.IsMaximal ∧
        ∃ ι : ZMod (ringChar k) →+* q.asIdeal.ResidueField,
          ∀ i : Fin n, @IsIntegral (ZMod (ringChar k)) q.asIdeal.ResidueField _ _ ι.toAlgebra
            (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) q.asIdeal.ResidueField
            (MvPolynomial.X i)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_largestOpen_iff_of_smoothAt_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CF1.** If the right vertical morphism of a commutative square is
smooth at the relevant point and the comparison morphism to the fibre product is étale at the
chosen point, the two source points lie in their largest open loci simultaneously.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_largestOpen_iff_of_smoothAt_etaleAt
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.IsLocalAtSource Scheme.etalePrecoverage]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget
      (Scheme.precoverage (@Smooth : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))]
    [P.RespectsRight (@IsOpenImmersion : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})]
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hcomm : g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g) (x' : X')
    (hg : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt g (f'.base x'))
    (hg' : EtaleAt
      (pullback.lift g' f' hcomm) x') :
    g'.base x' ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.largestOpen P f ↔
      x' ∈ AlgebraicGeometry.largestOpen P f'

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.flat_of_flat_baseChange_thickening
declarations.doc:
**Flatness lifts across cartesian thickenings.** Let `iX : X ⟶ X'`, `iY : Y ⟶ Y'` and
`iS : S ⟶ S'` be thickenings, let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `f' : X' ⟶ Y'` be compatible morphisms over
`S` and `S'`, and let both `X` and `Y` be the base change of `S` along `X' ⟶ S'` and
`Y' ⟶ S'`. If `Y' ⟶ S'` is locally of finite type, `X' ⟶ S'` is flat and locally of finite
presentation and `f` is flat, then `f'` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_flat_baseChange_thickening
    {X X' Y Y' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (iX : X ⟶ X') (iY : Y ⟶ Y') (iS : S ⟶ S')
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (gX : X ⟶ S) (gX' : X' ⟶ S')
    (gY : Y ⟶ S) (gY' : Y' ⟶ S')
    (hiX : IsThickening iX)
    (hiY : IsThickening iY)
    (hiS : IsThickening iS)
    (hcomm : f ≫ iY = iX ≫ f')
    (hover : f ≫ gY = gX)
    (hover' : f' ≫ gY' = gX')
    (hX : IsPullback iX gX gX' iS)
    (hY : IsPullback iY gY gY' iS)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType gY'] [Flat gX'] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation gX']
    (hf : Flat f) : Flat f'
declarations.comment: flatness of the ambient morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.flat_stalkMap_of_flat_baseChange_thickening
declarations.doc:
**The local ring of the target is flat over the base.** In the situation of Stacks Tag 0CF3,
the local ring of `Y'` at the image of a point of `X'` is flat over the local ring of `S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_stalkMap_of_flat_baseChange_thickening
    {X X' Y Y' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (iX : X ⟶ X') (iY : Y ⟶ Y') (iS : S ⟶ S')
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (gX : X ⟶ S) (gX' : X' ⟶ S')
    (gY : Y ⟶ S) (gY' : Y' ⟶ S')
    (hiX : IsThickening iX)
    (hiY : IsThickening iY)
    (hiS : IsThickening iS)
    (hcomm : f ≫ iY = iX ≫ f')
    (hover : f ≫ gY = gX)
    (hover' : f' ≫ gY' = gX')
    (hX : IsPullback iX gX gX' iS)
    (hY : IsPullback iY gY gY' iS)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType gY'] [Flat gX'] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation gX']
    (hf : Flat f) (x' : X') : (gY'.stalkMap (f' x')).hom.Flat
declarations.comment: flatness of the target local ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.essentiallyOfFinitePresentation_stalkMap_of_flat_baseChange_thickening
declarations.doc:
**The local ring of the target is essentially of finite presentation over the base.** In the
situation of Stacks Tag 0CF3, the local ring of `Y'` at the image of a point of `X'` is
essentially of finite presentation over the local ring of `S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallyOfFinitePresentation_stalkMap_of_flat_baseChange_thickening
    {X X' Y Y' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (iX : X ⟶ X') (iY : Y ⟶ Y') (iS : S ⟶ S')
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (gX : X ⟶ S) (gX' : X' ⟶ S')
    (gY : Y ⟶ S) (gY' : Y' ⟶ S')
    (hiX : IsThickening iX)
    (hiY : IsThickening iY)
    (hiS : IsThickening iS)
    (hcomm : f ≫ iY = iX ≫ f')
    (hover : f ≫ gY = gX)
    (hover' : f' ≫ gY' = gX')
    (hX : IsPullback iX gX gX' iS)
    (hY : IsPullback iY gY gY' iS)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType gY'] [Flat gX'] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation gX']
    (hf : Flat f) (x' : X') :
    IsEssentiallyOfFinitePresentation
      (S'.presheaf.stalk (gY' (f' x')))
      (Y'.presheaf.stalk (f' x'))
      (gY'.stalkMap (f' x')).hom
declarations.comment: essential finite presentation of the target local ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Thickenings.FlatDeformationDiagram.finiteLocallyFree_iff
declarations.doc:
Being finite locally free, and being finite locally free of a given rank `d`, are each
invariant under a flat deformation diagram.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLocallyFree_iff (D : FlatDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    ((IsFinite D.f ∧ Flat D.f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f) ↔
      (IsFinite D.f' ∧ Flat D.f' ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f')) ∧
    ∀ d : ℕ, (IsFinite D.f ∧ Flat D.f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f ∧
        ∀ y : D.Y, D.f.finrank y = d) ↔
      (IsFinite D.f' ∧ Flat D.f' ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation D.f' ∧
        ∀ y' : D.Y', D.f'.finrank y' = d)
declarations.comment: finite_locally_free

declarations.statement:
theorem FlatDeformationDiagram.unramified_iff (D : FlatDeformationDiagram.{u}) :
    Unramified D.f ↔ Unramified D.f'
declarations.comment: unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_universallySubmersive_iff_universallySubmersive
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFQ.** A representable morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` is
universally submersive in the sense of Stacks 03HA — each of its represented base changes is a
universally submersive morphism of schemes — if and only if every base change of it by an
algebraic space over `S` is submersive on points, which is universal submersiveness in the
sense of Stacks 0412, part (2).

The implication from left to right chooses a scheme atlas `a : U ⟶ Z` of the base `Z`: the
chosen represented base change of `f` along `a ≫ g` is a quotient map of schemes, hence on
points, and it factors through the base change along `g` by a continuous map, so
`Topology.IsQuotientMap.of_comp` gives the conclusion.

The converse must upgrade quotient-map-ness of the base changes available inside the size
cutoff of the site to the unbounded `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.universally`. That is what
the affine-space test `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_of_affineSpace_tests` is for: the
base changes of a represented base change to the affine spaces over its target are inside the
cutoff once the index type is small, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_of_small_baseChange`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quotientMap_affineSpace_map_of_small` removes the smallness
restriction. No algebraicity hypothesis on `X` or `Y` is needed, only representability of
`f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_universallySubmersive_iff_universallySubmersive (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        ((topologically @Topology.IsQuotientMap : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).universally)
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f ↔
      UniversallySubmersive B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallySubmersive_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFR.** A base change of a universally submersive morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` is universally submersive.

Nothing is needed beyond unwinding the definition: a base change of `Z ×_Y X ⟶ Z` along
`k : W ⟶ Z` is a base change of `X ⟶ Y` along `k ≫ g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallySubmersive_pullback {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (_hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hf : UniversallySubmersive B S hS f) :
    UniversallySubmersive B S hS (pullback.fst g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSubmersive.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFS, submersive morphisms.** A composition of submersive morphisms of algebraic
spaces over `S` is submersive: the map on points of a composition is the composition of the
maps on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsSubmersive.comp {f : F ⟶ G} {g : G ⟶ H} (hg : IsSubmersive B S hS g)
    (hf : IsSubmersive B S hS f) :
    IsSubmersive B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: submersive

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallySubmersive_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFS, universally submersive morphisms.** A composition of universally submersive
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is universally submersive.

The base change `W ×_Z X ⟶ W` of the composite along `k : W ⟶ Z` is identified by the pasting
isomorphism `W ×_Z X ≅ (W ×_Z Y) ×_Y X` with the composition of a base change of `X ⟶ Y` and a
base change of `Y ⟶ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallySubmersive_comp {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : UniversallySubmersive B S hS f) (hg : UniversallySubmersive B S hS g) :
    UniversallySubmersive B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: universally submersive

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFT.** A base change of a universal homeomorphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
a universal homeomorphism.

Nothing is needed beyond unwinding the definition: a base change of `Z ×_Y X ⟶ Z` along
`k : W ⟶ Z` is a base change of `X ⟶ Y` along `k ≫ g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hf : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS (pullback.fst g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFT** for an arbitrary cartesian square: if `IsPullback a b g f` and `f` is a
universal homeomorphism, then so is `a`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_pullback` composed with the
identification of the given square with the canonical fibre product.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_of_isPullback (hC : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS C)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T) (f : C ⟶ T) (g : Z ⟶ T)
    (hf : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f) {a : A ⟶ Z} {b : A ⟶ C}
    (hpb : IsPullback a b g f) : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFU.** A composition of universal homeomorphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is
a universal homeomorphism.

The base change `W ×_Z X ⟶ W` of the composite along `k : W ⟶ Z` is identified by the pasting
isomorphism `W ×_Z X ≅ (W ×_Z Y) ×_Y X` with the composition of a base change of `X ⟶ Y` and a
base change of `Y ⟶ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_comp (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f) (hg : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS g) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEtaleCovering_refining_isSmoothCovering
declarations.doc:
A smooth covering of an algebraic space over `S` is refined by an étale covering of it: there
is an étale covering each of whose members factors through a member of the given smooth covering,
compatibly with the morphisms to the common target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEtaleCovering_refining_isSmoothCovering
    {I : Type v} {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {X : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ F}
    (hf : IsSmoothCovering B S hS X f) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (U : J → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (g : ∀ j, U j ⟶ F),
      IsEtaleCovering B S hS U g ∧
        ∀ j, ∃ (i : I) (h : U j ⟶ X i), h ≫ f i = g j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEtaleCovering_representable_refining_isSmoothCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFV.** Every smooth covering of an algebraic space over `S` is refined by an étale
covering: there are an étale covering of the same target, whose members are schemes of the site,
and, for each of its members, a member of the given covering together with a morphism to it over
the common target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEtaleCovering_representable_refining_isSmoothCovering
    {I : Type v} {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {X : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ F}
    (hsm : IsSmoothCovering B S hS X f) :
    ∃ (J : Type (u + 1)) (Y : J → BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : ∀ j, yoneda.obj (Y j) ⟶ F),
      IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun j => yoneda.obj (Y j)) g ∧
        ∀ j, ∃ (i : I) (h : yoneda.obj (Y j) ⟶ X i), h ≫ f i = g j
declarations.comment: the refinement with every member of it representable by a scheme of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallySubmersive_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
Universal submersiveness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is local on the base for the
fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
instance universallySubmersive_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (universallySubmersiveMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universalHomeomorphism_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFX.** Being a universal homeomorphism is, for morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S`, local on the base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH: such a morphism is a universal
homeomorphism exactly when its base change to every member of some fpqc covering family of its
target is a universal homeomorphism.

A morphism is a universal homeomorphism exactly when it is surjective, universally injective
and universally open, surjectivity is fpqc local on the base by **Stacks 041Q**, universal
injectivity by **Stacks 041R** and universal openness by **Stacks 041P**, so their conjunction
is.
declarations.statement:
instance universalHomeomorphism_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    (universalHomeomorphismMorphismProperty B S hS).IsLocalAtTarget
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CFZ.** A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is *étale-smooth local
on the source-and-target* when it is stable under étale precomposition and under smooth base
change, and holds exactly when it holds on an étale neighbourhood over a smooth target
neighbourhood of every point of the source.
declarations.statement:
structure IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.postcomp_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG0**, étale postcomposition. A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
which is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target is preserved by postcomposition with an
étale morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem postcomp_of_etale
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : P f) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) : P (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: etale_postcomposition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.of_comp_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG0**, cancelling an étale postcomposition. If a property of morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S` is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target and holds for `f ≫ g`
with `g` étale, then it holds for `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma of_comp_etale
    {P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)}
    (hP : IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom)
    (hfg : P (f ≫ g)) : P f
declarations.comment: etale_postcomposition_permanence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalAtSource_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG0**, étale locality on the source. A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target is local at the source for the
étale topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtSource_etale
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P) :
    P.IsLocalAtSource (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .etale B S hS)
declarations.comment: etale_local_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalAtTarget_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG0**, smooth locality on the target. A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target is local at the target for the
smooth topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtTarget_smooth
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P) :
    P.IsLocalAtTarget (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .smooth B S hS)
declarations.comment: smooth_local_target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG1.** Seven equivalent criteria for a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces
over `S` to have a property which is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target: the property
itself; an étale neighbourhood over a smooth target neighbourhood on which it holds above every
point of the source; one such neighbourhood surjective onto the source; every such
neighbourhood; a smooth covering of the target whose base changes have it; an étale covering of
the source whose composites have it; and a smooth covering of the target together with étale
coverings of the corresponding fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_tfae
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      P f,
      (∀ x : points B S hS X.1,
        ∃ (V U : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
          (b : V ⟶ Y)
          (e : U ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b)
          (v : points B S hS U.1),
          IsSmooth B S hS b.hom ∧
          IsEtale B S hS e.hom ∧
          pointsMap B S hS U.1
            (e ≫ (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom b.hom) :
              AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b ⟶ X)).hom v = x ∧
          P (e ≫ (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom b.hom) :
            AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b ⟶ V))),
      (∃ (V U : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
        (b : V ⟶ Y)
        (e : U ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b),
        IsSmooth B S hS b.hom ∧
        IsEtale B S hS e.hom ∧
        IsSurjective B S hS
          (e ≫ (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom b.hom) :
            AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b ⟶ X)).hom ∧
        P (e ≫ (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom b.hom) :
          AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b ⟶ V))),
      (∀ (V U : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
        (b : V ⟶ Y)
        (e : U ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b),
        IsSmooth B S hS b.hom →
        IsEtale B S hS e.hom →
        P (e ≫ (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom b.hom) :
          AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f b ⟶ V))),
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1))
        (V : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
        (b : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Y),
        IsSmoothCovering B S hS (fun i => (V i).1) (fun i => (b i).hom) ∧
        ∀ i, P (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom (b i).hom) :
          AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f (b i) ⟶ V i)),
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1))
        (U : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
        (a : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X),
        IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun i => (U i).1) (fun i => (a i).hom) ∧
        ∀ i, P ((a i) ≫ f)),
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1))
        (V : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
        (b : ∀ i, V i ⟶ Y)
        (J : I → Type (u + 1))
        (U : ∀ i, J i → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
        (e : ∀ i j, U i j ⟶ AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f (b i)),
        IsSmoothCovering B S hS (fun i => (V i).1) (fun i => (b i).hom) ∧
        ∀ i, IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun j => (U i j).1) (fun j => (e i j).hom) ∧
          ∀ j, P (e i j ≫
            (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom (b i).hom) :
              AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f (b i) ⟶ V i)))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_of_local
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG2.** A property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is étale local
on the source, smooth local on the target and stable under postcomposition with open immersions
is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget_of_local
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsLocalAtSource (Space.Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} .etale B S hS)]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.precoverage.{u, u + 1} .smooth B S hS)]
    [P.RespectsRight (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄
      (f : X ⟶ Y) => Space.IsOpenImmersion B S hS f.hom)] :
    Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtale_isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
Étaleness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is étale-smooth local on the
source-and-target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget :
    IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
declarations.comment: étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyQuasiFinite_isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
Local quasi-finiteness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is étale-smooth local on
the source-and-target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget :
    IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f.hom)
declarations.comment: locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUnramified_isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget
declarations.doc:
Unramifiedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is étale-smooth local on the
source-and-target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_isEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget :
    IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) => IsUnramified B S hS f.hom)
declarations.comment: unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_isFlat_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG5, flatness of the ambient morphism.** In a commuting diagram of thickenings
of algebraic spaces over `S` with the base thickening of finite order, the ambient source flat
over the ambient base and both unprimed spaces the base changes of their primed counterparts,
flatness of the morphism of special fibres implies flatness of its ambient deformation.

This is the forward implication of part 0CG8 of Tag 0CG6, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformation.isFlat_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_isFlat_restriction
    (hiX : IsThickening B S hS X' X) (hiY : IsThickening B S hS Y' Y)
    (hiB : IsFiniteOrderThickening B S hS B' B₀)
    (hcartX : IsPullback X.ι pX pX' B₀.ι) (hcartY : IsPullback Y.ι pY pY' B₀.ι)
    (hinner : f ≫ pY = pX) (houter : f' ≫ pY' = pX')
    (hrestrict : X.ι ≫ f' = f ≫ Y.ι)
    (hXflat : IsFlat B S hS pX') (hfflat : IsFlat B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS f'
declarations.comment: flatness of the upper morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatAt_base_of_isFlat_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG5, flatness of the ambient target along the image.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_isFlat_restriction` the ambient target is flat over the
ambient base at every point in the image of the ambient morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatAt_base_of_isFlat_restriction
    (hiX : IsThickening B S hS X' X) (hiY : IsThickening B S hS Y' Y)
    (hiB : IsFiniteOrderThickening B S hS B' B₀)
    (hcartX : IsPullback X.ι pX pX' B₀.ι) (hcartY : IsPullback Y.ι pY pY' B₀.ι)
    (hinner : f ≫ pY = pX) (houter : f' ≫ pY' = pX')
    (hrestrict : X.ι ≫ f' = f ≫ Y.ι)
    (hXflat : IsFlat B S hS pX') (hfflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (x' : points B S hS X'.1) :
    IsFlatAt B S hS pY' (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 f' x')
declarations.comment: flatness of the upper target at image points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformation.isFiniteLocallyFree_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG6, part 0CGV.** In a cartesian finite-order deformation of algebraic spaces the
morphism of special fibres is finite locally free if and only if its ambient deformation is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_iff :
    IsFiniteLocallyFree T S hS D.smallHom ↔ IsFiniteLocallyFree T S hS D.ambientHom
declarations.comment: 0CGV: finite locally free

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformation.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG6, part 0CGV, with the rank.** In a cartesian finite-order deformation of
algebraic spaces the morphism of special fibres is finite locally free of rank `d` if and only
if its ambient deformation is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff (d : ℕ) :
    IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank T S hS D.smallHom d ↔
      IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank T S hS D.ambientHom d
declarations.comment: 0CGV: finite locally free of rank d

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformation.isFlat_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG6, part 0CG8.** In a cartesian finite-order deformation of algebraic spaces the
morphism of special fibres is flat if and only if its ambient deformation is.
declarations.statement: theorem isFlat_iff : IsFlat T S hS D.f ↔ IsFlat T S hS D.f'
declarations.comment: 0CG8: flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformation.isSurjective_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG6, part 0CGF.** In a cartesian finite-order deformation of algebraic spaces the
morphism of special fibres is surjective if and only if its ambient deformation is.
declarations.statement: theorem isSurjective_iff : IsSurjective T S hS D.f ↔ IsSurjective T S hS D.f'
declarations.comment: 0CGF: surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformation.isLocallyOfFiniteType_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG6, part 0CGI.** In a cartesian finite-order deformation of algebraic spaces the
morphism of special fibres is locally of finite type if and only if its ambient deformation
is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_iff :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType T S hS D.f ↔ IsLocallyOfFiniteType T S hS D.f'
declarations.comment: 0CGI: locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CartesianFiniteOrderDeformation.isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CG6, part 0CGJ.** In a cartesian finite-order deformation of algebraic spaces the
morphism of special fibres is locally quasi-finite if and only if its ambient deformation
is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_iff :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite T S hS D.f ↔ IsLocallyQuasiFinite T S hS D.f'
declarations.comment: 0CGJ: locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isEtaleCovering_lift_of_isSmooth_of_isThickeningHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHJ.** Let `S` be a scheme and consider a commutative square of algebraic spaces
over `S`
```
X ←--a-- T
|        |
f        i
↓        ↓
Y ←--b-- T'
```
in which `f` is smooth and `i` is a thickening. Then there is an étale covering of `T'` by
affine schemes `T'ₚ` of the site such that over each member the square can be filled in: there
is a `ψ : T'ₚ ⟶ X` with `ψ` over `Y` equal to `T'ₚ ⟶ T' ⟶ Y` and with the restriction of `ψ` to
`T ×_{T'} T'ₚ` equal to the restriction of `a`.

The covering is indexed by the points of `T'`, and the member at a point contains that point.

The proof follows the source, with the three reductions performed in one step for each member of
the covering rather than globally. Write `Z = X ×_Y T'`; it is smooth over `T'` because `f` is,
and the given data provide a section `σ : T ⟶ Z` of `Z ⟶ T'` over `T`. Given a point of `T'`,
choose an affine étale chart `P` of `T'` through it (Stacks 03FX, in the pointwise form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_chart_at_point`) and let `J = T ×_{T'} P`, an affine
scheme and a thickening of `P`. Pulling an atlas of `Z` back along `J ⟶ Z` and intersecting with
the base change of `P` to that atlas produces an affine chart `U` of `Z` lying over `P` — so that
`U ⟶ P` is a *smooth morphism of affine schemes*, since smoothness of `Z ⟶ T'` is exactly the
condition on every square of étale charts — together with an étale `N ⟶ J` through the chosen
point and a morphism `N ⟶ U` over `Z`. Topological invariance of the étale site (Stacks 039R, in
the size-controlled cartesian form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleLift_isPullback_of_chart`) lifts `N ⟶ J` to an étale
`V ⟶ P` with `N = T ×_{T'} V`; shrinking `V` to an affine open through the point makes it affine,
and `Stacks.Smooth.exists_lift_of_isClosedImmersion_of_surjective` — the geometric form of
Algebra, Lemma 10.138.17 — then extends `T ×_{T'} V' ⟶ U` over the thickening to `V' ⟶ U`. The
member of the covering is `V'`, and `ψ` is `V' ⟶ U ⟶ Z ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEtaleCovering_lift_of_isSmooth_of_isThickeningHom
    {X Y T T' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f.hom)
    {i : T ⟶ T'} (hi : IsThickeningHom B S hS i) (a : T ⟶ X) (b : T' ⟶ Y)
    (hcomm : a ≫ f = i ≫ b) :
    ∃ (Z : points B S hS T'.obj → BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (q : ∀ p, yoneda.obj (Z p) ⟶ T'.obj),
      (∀ p, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (Z p))) ∧
      IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun p ↦ yoneda.obj (Z p)) q ∧
      ∀ p, ∃ ψ : yoneda.obj (Z p) ⟶ X.obj,
        ψ ≫ f.hom = q p ≫ b.hom ∧
        pullback.snd i.hom (q p) ≫ ψ = pullback.fst i.hom (q p) ≫ a.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_comp_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with `g` smooth.
If the composite `f ≫ g` is a local complete intersection morphism, then so is `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_comp_of_isSmooth
    {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hg : IsSmooth B S hS g)
    (hfg : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalCompleteIntersection_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHM.** The property of being a local complete intersection morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` is local on the base for the fpqc topology of Stacks 03YH: a morphism is Koszul
exactly when its base changes along the members of an fpqc covering of its target are.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget
      (fun ⦃X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y) =>
        IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .fpqc B S hS)

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHN.** The property of being a local complete intersection morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` is local on the source for the syntomic topology of Stacks 03YH.

The schemes case, Stacks 069P, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtSource_syntomic_isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism`; the étale
locality on source and target that the transfer also consumes needs only its étale restriction,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_isLocalAtSource_etale`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_isLocalAtSource_syntomic :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) =>
        IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f.hom)
      (Topology.precoverage.{u, v} .syntomic B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHQ.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *affine* when it is
representable by algebraic spaces and is affine in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAffineHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isAffineHom_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHR.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let
`g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be an affine 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, that is (Stacks 0CHQ) one which is
representable by algebraic spaces and affine in the sense of Stacks 04XB. If `P` is a 2-fibre
product of the cospan `(g, f)`, then the base change `P.snd : 𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is an affine
1-morphism of algebraic stacks: it is representable by algebraic spaces, and it is affine in the
sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_and_isAffineHom_snd
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hg_rep : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom.hom)
    (hg_aff : Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS g.hom) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS P.snd.hom.hom ∧
      Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS P.snd.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAffineHom_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHR.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, let
`g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be an affine 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, and let `P` be a 2-fibre product of the
cospan `(g, f)`. Then the base change `P.snd : 𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` of `g` along `f` is affine.

Both halves are base-change statements: representability by algebraic spaces is Stacks 0302 and
affineness in the sense of Stacks 04XB is Stacks 045C. The square is arbitrary, so this applies
to any square a consumer has already exhibited as a 2-fibre product rather than only to the
canonical one of Stacks 04T2.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hg : IsAffineHom B S hS g) :
    IsAffineHom B S hS P.snd

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isRepresentableMorphism_comp_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHS, for the definition of Stacks 0CHQ read literally.** Call a 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` affine when it is representable (by schemes, Stacks 02Y7) and affine in
the sense of Stacks 04XB. Then a composite of two affine 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks is
affine: representability composes by Stacks 02ZS, and affineness in the sense of Stacks 04XB
composes by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAffineHom_comp` (Stacks 045B with Stacks 03WH and the
implication (4) ⇒ (2) of Stacks 03WG), which applies because a representable 1-morphism is
representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableMorphism_comp_isAffineHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom) ∧ Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom)
    (hg : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒵.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor g.hom) ∧ Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS g.hom) :
    Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒵.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f ≫ g).hom) ∧
      Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS (f ≫ g).hom
declarations.comment: with 0CHQ read literally: representable by schemes and affine in the sense of 04XB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAffineHom_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHS.** A composite of two affine 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
affine: representability by algebraic spaces composes by Stacks 0301, and affineness in the sense
of Stacks 04XB composes by Stacks 045B, whose two ingredients at affineness are Stacks 03WH and
the implication (4) ⇒ (2) of Stacks 03WG.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f) (hg : IsAffineHom B S hS g) :
    IsAffineHom B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHU**, part (1). A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` *is integral* when it is
representable by algebraic spaces and is integral in the sense of Stacks 04XB: every algebraic
space representing its base change along a scheme-valued point of the target has integral
structural morphism, read as a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsIntegralHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1): integral morphisms

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsFinite
registrations.comment: part (2): finite morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIntegralHom_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHV**, the integral case. A base change of an integral 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks over `S` is integral: if `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` is integral and `P` is a 2-fibre product of the
cospan `(f, g)` for a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, then `P.fst : 𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is integral.

Representability by algebraic spaces base changes by **Stacks 0302** and the relative property
of Stacks 04XB by **Stacks 045C**, which applies because integrality of morphisms of algebraic
spaces is stable under base change and local at the target for the fppf precoverage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_baseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hg : IsIntegralHom B S hS g) :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS P.fst
declarations.comment: integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFinite_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHV**, the finite case. A base change of a finite 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
over `S` is finite: if `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` is finite and `P` is a 2-fibre product of the cospan
`(f, g)` for a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, then `P.fst : 𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is finite.

Representability by algebraic spaces base changes by **Stacks 0302** and the relative property
of Stacks 04XB by **Stacks 045C**, which applies because finiteness of morphisms of algebraic
spaces is stable under base change and local at the target for the fppf precoverage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_baseChange (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hg : IsFinite B S hS g) :
    IsFinite B S hS P.fst
declarations.comment: finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIntegralHom_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHW**, the integral case: a composite of integral 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
over `S` is integral.

Representability by algebraic spaces composes by **Stacks 0301** and the relative property of
Stacks 04XB by **Stacks 045B**, which applies because
integrality of morphisms of algebraic spaces is stable under base change and under composition
(**Stacks 03ZR**) and local at the target for the fppf precoverage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_comp (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f) (hg : IsIntegralHom B S hS g) :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFinite_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHW**, the finite case: a composite of finite 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S` is finite.

Representability by algebraic spaces composes by **Stacks 0301** and the relative property of
Stacks 04XB by **Stacks 045B**, which applies because finiteness of morphisms of algebraic
spaces is stable under base change and under composition (**Stacks 03ZR**) and local at the
target for the fppf precoverage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_comp (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsFinite B S hS f) (hg : IsFinite B S hS g) :
    IsFinite B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representable_universallySubmersive_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHX.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by
algebraic spaces is universally submersive in the relative sense of Tag 04XB — every algebraic
space representing a base change of `f` along a scheme-valued point of `𝒴` has universally
submersive structural morphism — exactly when, for every algebraic stack `𝒵` over `𝒴`, the map
`|𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳| → |𝒵|` of topological spaces is submersive.
declarations.statement:
theorem representable_universallySubmersive_iff
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (T : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 T),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom))
          (presheafOfCategories (T ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.UniversallySubmersive B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨T, hT⟩)).hom) ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsUniversallySubmersive B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isUniversallySubmersive_baseChange_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHY.** Universal submersiveness is stable under base change: let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
universally submersive 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let `R` be a 2-fibre product
square of the cospan `(g, f)` for some `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴`. Then the base change `R.fst : R.pt ⟶ 𝒴'` of
`f` along `g` is universally submersive.

The square is arbitrary, so this applies to any square a consumer has already exhibited as a
2-fibre product rather than only to the canonical one of Stacks 04T2.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallySubmersive_baseChange_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} {g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴}
    (R : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hR : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct R)
    (hf : IsUniversallySubmersive B S hS f) :
    IsUniversallySubmersive B S hS R.fst
