declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSubmersive_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHZ.** The composite of two submersive 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
submersive.
declarations.comment: composition_submersive

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isUniversallySubmersive_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CHZ.** The composite of two universally submersive 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
over `S` is universally submersive.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallySubmersive_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsUniversallySubmersive B S hS f) (hg : IsUniversallySubmersive B S hS g) :
    IsUniversallySubmersive B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: composition_universally_submersive

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representable_universallyInjective_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI1.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by
algebraic spaces is universally injective in the relative sense of Tag 04XB — every algebraic
space representing a base change of `f` along a scheme-valued point of `𝒴` has universally
injective structural morphism — exactly when, for every algebraic stack `𝒵` over `𝒴` and every
2-fibre product of the cospan, the map `|𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳| → |𝒵|` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem representable_universallyInjective_iff
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (T : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 T),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom))
          (presheafOfCategories (T ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.UniversallyInjective B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨T, hT⟩)).hom) ↔
      UniversallyInjective B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.UniversallyInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI2.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is *universally
injective* if for every 1-morphism `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` and every 2-fibre
product of `(g, f)` the map `|𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳| → |𝒵|` induced by the projection to `𝒵` is injective.
declarations.statement: abbrev UniversallyInjective {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI3.** The base change of a universally injective 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S` along any `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` is universally injective: in a 2-fibre-product
square over `(g, f)`, the projection to `𝒵` is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI4.** The composite of a pair of universally injective 1-morphisms of algebraic
stacks over `S` is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (hf : UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hg : UniversallyInjective B S hS g) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.representable_universalHomeomorphism_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI6.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by
algebraic spaces is a universal homeomorphism in the relative sense of Tag 04XB — every algebraic
space representing a base change of `f` along a scheme-valued point of `𝒴` has structural
morphism a universal homeomorphism — exactly when, for every algebraic stack `𝒵` over `𝒴`, the
map `|𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳| → |𝒵|` of topological spaces is a homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem representable_universalHomeomorphism_iff
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    (∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.val.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
        (T : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 T),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom))
          (presheafOfCategories (T ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨T, hT⟩)).hom) ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.UniversalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI7.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is a *universal
homeomorphism* if for every 1-morphism `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` and every
2-fibre product of `(g, f)` the map `|𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳| → |𝒵|` induced by the projection to `𝒵` is a
homeomorphism.
declarations.statement: abbrev UniversalHomeomorphism {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.UniversalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI7.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is a *universal
homeomorphism* when, for every 1-morphism `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the base
change `𝒵 ×_{g, 𝒴, f} 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` of `f` by `g` induces a homeomorphism `|𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳| → |𝒵|` on the
points of Stacks 04XG for the topology of Stacks 04XL.

For a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces this agrees with the relative notion of
Stacks 04XB, by **Stacks 0CI6**.
declarations.statement: abbrev UniversalHomeomorphism {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universalHomeomorphism_baseChange
declarations.doc:
The base change of a universal homeomorphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` along any
`g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` is a universal homeomorphism: in a 2-fibre-product square over `(g, f)`, the projection
to `𝒵` is a universal homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universalHomeomorphism_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CI9.** The composite of two universal homeomorphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`
is a universal homeomorphism.

A base change of `f ≫ g` along `k` is the outer rectangle of a base change of `g` along `k`
followed by a base change of `f` along the resulting projection, by the pasting law for 2-fibre
products; the two legs of that rectangle are homeomorphisms on points by hypothesis, so the
rectangle's own first leg is one too, and that condition depends only on the cospan.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS f) (hg : UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS g) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM_of_dm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIA, part (1).** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a DM 1-morphism of algebraic stacks. For every
DM algebraic stack `𝒵` and 1-morphism `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` there is a scheme with a surjective étale
1-morphism onto `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, g} 𝒵`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM_of_dm
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) (h𝒵 : IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS B.contains_terminal 𝒵) :
    Stack.IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt.val.val
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM_algebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIA, part (2).** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a DM 1-morphism of algebraic stacks. For every
algebraic space `Z` and 1-morphism `g : Z ⟶ 𝒴` there is a scheme with a surjective étale
1-morphism onto `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, g} Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM_algebraicSpace
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f)
    (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (g : Stack.algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒴) :
    Stack.IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt.val.val
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**A 2-fibre product of a Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism over a Deligne–Mumford algebraic stack
is Deligne–Mumford.** The projection of the canonical square of `(f, g)` to `𝒵` is a base change
of `f`, so it is Deligne–Mumford by Stacks 050F, and a stack Deligne–Mumford over a
Deligne–Mumford stack is Deligne–Mumford by Stacks 050L.

This is the first half of the argument for part (1) of Stacks 0CIA; the half left is the
structure theorem Stacks 06N3, which turns the conclusion into a surjective étale presentation
of the apex by a scheme and is applied in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) (h𝒵 : IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hT 𝒵) :
    IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hT (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt
declarations.comment:
part (1), the Deligne-Mumford condition on the 2-fibre product: the apex of the
  canonical square of a DM 1-morphism f and a 1-morphism out of a DM algebraic stack is itself a
  DM algebraic stack. This is the source's own argument for part (1) up to its closing appeal to
  Stacks 06N3; that appeal is made in
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM`, which
  states part (1) in the source's existence form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_algebraicSpaceStack
declarations.doc:
**A 2-fibre product of a Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism over an algebraic space is
Deligne–Mumford.** The source's reduction of part (2) of Stacks 0CIA to part (1): an algebraic
space is Deligne–Mumford when read as an algebraic stack, so no hypothesis beyond
Deligne–Mumfordness of `f` is needed.

As for `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM`, what is
left of Stacks 0CIA after this is one application of Stacks 06N3, made in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_algebraicSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_algebraicSpaceStack
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f)
    (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (g : Stack.algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hT (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt
declarations.comment:
part (2), the Deligne-Mumford condition on the 2-fibre product: the apex of the
  canonical square of a DM 1-morphism f and a 1-morphism out of an algebraic space is a DM
  algebraic stack, with no hypothesis on the algebraic space. This is the source's own reduction
  of part (2) to part (1), up to the closing appeal to Stacks 06N3; that appeal is made in
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_algebraicSpace`,
  which states part (2) in the source's existence form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIA, part (1).** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks. For every Deligne–Mumford algebraic stack `𝒵` over `𝒴` there is a scheme of the site
with a surjective étale 1-morphism onto `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, g} 𝒵`.

The apex is a Deligne–Mumford algebraic stack by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM`, and the
presentation comes from the structure theorem Stacks 06N3, carried here as the hypothesis
`hForward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM
    (hForward : Stack.ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hT)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) (h𝒵 : IsAbsolutelyDM B S hS hT 𝒵) :
    Stack.IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt.val.val
declarations.comment:
part (1), in the source's existence form: a scheme with a surjective etale
  1-morphism onto the 2-fibre product, with the substantial direction of Stacks 06N3 as the
  explicit hypothesis hForward (the structure theorem behind it, Stacks 06MD, 06N0, 06N2, 06G2,
  06G3, is absent from the library). The Deligne-Mumford condition on the apex, which is the
  whole of the source's argument apart from that appeal, is proved unconditionally in
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_algebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIA, part (2).** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks. For every algebraic space `Z` over `𝒴` there is a scheme of the site with a surjective
étale 1-morphism onto `𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, g} Z`, with no further hypothesis on `Z`.

This is part (1) applied to the algebraic space read as an algebraic stack, which is
Deligne–Mumford by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_algebraicSpaceStack`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_algebraicSpace
    (hForward : Stack.ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hT)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f)
    (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (g : Stack.algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒴) :
    Stack.IsDeligneMumfordStack.{u, w} B S hS
      (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f g).pt.val.val
declarations.comment:
part (2), in the source's existence form: a scheme with a surjective etale
  1-morphism onto the 2-fibre product with an algebraic space, with the substantial direction of
  Stacks 06N3 as the explicit hypothesis hForward (the structure theorem behind it, Stacks 06MD,
  06N0, 06N2, 06G2, 06G3, is absent from the library). The Deligne-Mumford condition on the apex
  is proved unconditionally in
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAbsolutelyDM_twoFibreProduct_algebraicSpaceStack`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_isFlatAt_iff_forall_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIC.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and let `x` be
a point of `|𝒳|`. The top horizontal morphism of *some* diagram of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.PointedFlatDiagram` is flat at its marked point if and
only if the top horizontal morphism of *every* such diagram is.

The forward implication is the iterated-2-fibre-product chase of the source; the backward one
holds because such a diagram exists through every point of `|𝒳|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFlatAt_iff_forall_isFlatAt {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳) :
    (∃ d : PointedFlatDiagram B S hS f x, Space.IsFlatAt B S hS d.h d.u) ↔
      ∀ d : PointedFlatDiagram B S hS f x, Space.IsFlatAt B S hS d.h d.u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CID.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is *flat at* a point
`x` of `|𝒳|` when the top horizontal morphism of some diagram of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.PointedFlatDiagram` is flat at its marked point.

**Stacks 0CIC** identifies this with the corresponding condition on every such diagram, so the
choice of the existential formulation is immaterial.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFlatAt {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x : points B S hS 𝒳) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnEveryEtaleSmoothDiagram_iff_some
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIF, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2).** Let `P` be a property of
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target, and
let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. Then the following
are equivalent:

1. for every 2-commutative square of algebraic spaces `h : U → V` over `f` with `V → 𝒴` smooth
   and `U → 𝒳 ×_𝒴 V` étale, the morphism `h` has `P`;
2. for some such square with `U → 𝒳` surjective, the morphism `h` has `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnEveryEtaleSmoothDiagram_iff_some
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsDM B S hS f) :
    HasPropertyOnEveryEtaleSmoothDiagram B S hS P f ↔
      HasPropertyOnSomeEtaleSmoothDiagram B S hS P f
declarations.comment: equivalence of parts (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeEtaleSmoothDiagram_iff_relative
declarations.doc:
**The third assertion of Stacks 0CIF.** For an étale-smooth local property `P` of morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is stable under base change and local at the target for the fppf
precoverage, and a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by algebraic
spaces, the existential étale-smooth diagram test for `P` is equivalent to the relative property
`P` of Stacks 03YK.

This is the covering set of the key `"representable morphism"` of Stacks 0CIF: the key names a
single asserted equivalence, and neither half of it alone asserts that equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnSomeEtaleSmoothDiagram_iff_relative
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, v} B S hS)]
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeEtaleSmoothDiagram B S hS P f ↔
      HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, v} B S hS P f.hom hf
declarations.comment: representable morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeEtaleSmoothDiagram_iff_represented
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIF, the assertion for representable source and target.** For a property `P` of
morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is étale-smooth local on the source-and-target, and
a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` whose source and target are representable
by algebraic spaces `F` and `G`, the existential étale-smooth diagram test holds for `f` exactly
when the induced morphism `F ⟶ G` of representing presheaves has `P`.

Forward: the given diagram becomes a square of morphisms of algebraic spaces whose comparison to
the fibre product is étale, and Stacks 0CG1 applies. Backward: test the condition on the diagram
given by the two representing equivalences.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnSomeEtaleSmoothDiagram_iff_represented :
    HasPropertyOnSomeEtaleSmoothDiagram B S hS P f ↔
      P (ObjectProperty.homMk (representingMap B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val F G eX eY f.hom) :
        (⟨F, hF⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨G, hG⟩)
declarations.comment: representable source and target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIG.** The property of Deligne–Mumford morphisms of algebraic stacks induced by an
étale-smooth local property `P` of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`: the morphism is
Deligne–Mumford and passes the universal étale-smooth diagram test at `P`.

For an étale-smooth local `P` — `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget`,
**Stacks 0CFZ** — Stacks 0CIF identifies that test with the existential one.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop
declarations.comment: the property of a DM morphism of algebraic stacks induced by an etale-smooth local property P of morphisms of algebraic spaces: IsDM f together with the universal etale-smooth diagram test at P, which is condition (1) of Stacks 0CIF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIH.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
étale-smooth local on the source-and-target and stable under composition. Then the property of
Deligne–Mumford 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` which **Stacks 0CIG** induces from `P`
is stable under composition.

The composite is Deligne–Mumford by **Stacks 050K**. For the diagram test, take a smooth chart
`W ⟶ 𝒵` surjective on objects, an étale chart `V ⟶ 𝒴 ×_𝒵 W` and an étale chart `U ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 V`,
the last two by **Stacks 0CIA**; the morphisms `V ⟶ W` and `U ⟶ V` have `P`, hence so does
`U ⟶ W`, and pasting the two 2-fibre products exhibits `U` as an étale chart of `𝒳 ×_𝒵 W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_comp
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    (hcomp : ∀ {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (p : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ Z), P p → P q → P (p ≫ q))
    (hT : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hForward : ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hT)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P f)
    (hg : HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P g) :
    HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment:
with the substantial direction of Stacks 06N3 as the explicit hypothesis hForward
  (the structure theorem behind it, Stacks 06MD, 06N0, 06N2, 06G2, 06G3, is absent from the
  library); it enters only through Stacks 0CIA, which supplies the surjective etale presentations
  of the two 2-fibre products the source's argument chooses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_comp_of_isEtaleSmoothLocal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIH.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
étale-smooth local on the source-and-target and stable under composition. Then the property of
Deligne–Mumford 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` which **Stacks 0CIG** induces from `P`
is stable under composition: if `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` are DM and have it, so does
`f ≫ g`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_comp` with its argument `hForward`
discharged by the unconditional forward direction of **Stacks 06N3**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM`, at
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.contains_terminal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_comp_of_isEtaleSmoothLocal
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    (hcomp : ∀ {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (p : X ⟶ Y) (q : Y ⟶ Z), P p → P q → P (p ≫ q))
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P f)
    (hg : HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P g) :
    HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct_of_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CII.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
étale-smooth local on the source-and-target and stable under base change. If a Deligne–Mumford
1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` has the property of Stacks 0CIG induced by
`P`, then so does its base change `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵` along any 1-morphism `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴`, the second
projection of any 2-fibre product square of `(f, g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct_of_isStableUnderBaseChange
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (R : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g) (hR : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct R)
    (hf : HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P f) :
    HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P R.snd

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CII.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
étale-smooth local on the source-and-target and stable under base change. Then the property of
Deligne–Mumford 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` that **Stacks 0CIG** induces from `P`
is inherited by the base change of a 1-morphism along the canonical 2-fibre product square.

The Deligne–Mumford condition on the base change is **Stacks 050F**, and the diagram of
condition (2) of **Stacks 0CIF** is the source's: its top-left corner is `V' ×_V U` for a smooth
presentation `V ⟶ 𝒴`, a surjective étale presentation `U ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 V` and a smooth presentation
`V' ⟶ 𝒵 ×_𝒴 V`, and its top horizontal morphism is the base change of `U ⟶ V` along
`V' ⟶ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_baseChange
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    (hP : Space.IsEtaleSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS P)
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hForward : ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P f) :
    HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P
      (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f g).snd
declarations.comment:
for the canonical 2-fibre product square of Stacks 003Q, which is the shape the
  library version of Stacks 050F is stated at, and with the substantial direction of Stacks 06N3 as the
  explicit hypothesis hForward (the structure theorem behind it, Stacks 06MD, 06N0, 06N2, 06G2,
  06G3, is absent from the library); it enters only through Stacks 0CIA, which supplies the
  surjective etale presentation the source's argument chooses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIJ.** An implication between properties of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
also holds for the properties of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks that Stacks 0CIG induces from
them. No étale-smooth locality hypothesis on either property is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty_mono
    {P P' : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)} (hPP' : P ≤ P')
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴}
    (hf : HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P f) :
    HasEtaleSmoothLocalProperty B S hS P' f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIL.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *étale* when it is
Deligne–Mumford and its universal étale-smooth diagram tests are étale morphisms of algebraic
spaces, in the sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale` (**Stacks 03FR**).
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEtale {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEtale_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIM.** The composite of two étale 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
étale, in the sense of **Stacks 0CIL**: it is Deligne–Mumford and passes the universal
étale-smooth diagram test at étaleness of morphisms of algebraic spaces.

This is **Stacks 0CIH** for the property `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale`, which is
étale-smooth local on the source-and-target (**Stacks 0CG3**) and stable under composition
(**Stacks 0465**).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_comp_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**The Deligne–Mumford conjunct of Stacks 0CIM.** A composite of two étale 1-morphisms of
algebraic stacks over `S` is Deligne–Mumford.

Étaleness of Stacks 0CIL contains the Deligne–Mumford condition of Stacks 04YW, and that
condition is stable under composition by **Stacks 050K**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_comp_of_isEtale {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : Stack.IsEtale B S hS f) (hg : Stack.IsEtale B S hS g) :
    Stack.IsDM B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the Deligne–Mumford conjunct of the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEtale_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIN.** A base change of an étale 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is étale:
if `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is étale and `Q` is any 2-fibre product of a cospan `(g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴, f)`, then
the projection `Q.fst : Q.pt ⟶ 𝒴'` is étale, both conjuncts of **Stacks 0CIL** included.

The diagram of condition (2) of **Stacks 0CIF** for the Deligne–Mumford `f` is cut out by the
surjective étale presentation of **Stacks 0CIA**, part (2), whose input, the substantial direction
of **Stacks 06N3**, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
    (hf : IsEtale B S hS f) :
    IsEtale B S hS Q.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_baseChange_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**The Deligne–Mumford conjunct of Stacks 0CIN.** The projection to `𝒴'` of any 2-fibre
product of a cospan `(g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴, f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)` of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
Deligne–Mumford as soon as `f` is étale.

Étaleness of Stacks 0CIL contains the Deligne–Mumford condition of Stacks 04YW, and that
condition is inherited by base changes by **Stacks 050F**; a 2-fibre product of `(g, f)` is one
of `(f, g)` with its two legs exchanged (**Stacks 003Q**), which turns the projection `Q.fst`
into the second projection that Stacks 050F speaks about.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_baseChange_of_isEtale {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
    (hf : Stack.IsEtale B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsDM B S hS Q.fst
declarations.comment: the Deligne–Mumford conjunct of the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEtale_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc: An open immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` is étale in the sense of Stacks 0CIL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_of_isOpenImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsOpenImmersion B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsEtale B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEtale_of_etaleOnEveryAlgebraicSpaceDiagram
declarations.doc:
A Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism of algebraic stacks whose every algebraic-space diagram with
étale comparisons has étale top horizontal morphism is étale.
declarations.comment: the implication (2) => (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_of_hasEtaleAlgebraicSpaceCoverAfterFppfBaseChange
declarations.doc:
If the big fppf site contains the terminal scheme, a 1-morphism `f` of algebraic stacks
satisfying `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasEtaleAlgebraicSpaceCoverAfterFppfBaseChange` is
Deligne–Mumford.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_of_hasEtaleAlgebraicSpaceCoverAfterFppfBaseChange
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴}
    (hf : HasEtaleAlgebraicSpaceCoverAfterFppfBaseChange B S hS f) : IsDM B S hS f
declarations.comment:
the Deligne-Mumford half of the implication (3) => (1), for a site
containing the terminal scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEtale_tfae_algebraicSpaceCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIQ.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following are
equivalent:

1. `f` is étale, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsEtale` (**Stacks 0CIL**);
2. `f` is Deligne–Mumford and for every `V ⟶ 𝒴` with `V` an algebraic space and every étale
   `U ⟶ V ×_𝒴 𝒳` with `U` an algebraic space, `U ⟶ V` is étale,
   `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.EtaleOnEveryAlgebraicSpaceDiagram`;
3. there are a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented `W ⟶ 𝒴` with `W` an algebraic space
   and a surjective étale `T ⟶ W ×_𝒴 𝒳` with `T` an algebraic space such that `T ⟶ W` is étale,
   `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasEtaleAlgebraicSpaceCoverAfterFppfBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_tfae_algebraicSpaceCharts
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE [IsEtale B S hS f, EtaleOnEveryAlgebraicSpaceDiagram B S hS f,
      HasEtaleAlgebraicSpaceCoverAfterFppfBaseChange B S hS f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEtale_of_isEtale_over_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIR.** Let `𝒳` and `𝒴` be algebraic stacks étale over an algebraic stack `𝒵`, with
structure 1-morphisms `p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` and `q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵`. Any 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` over `𝒵`, i.e.
with a 2-isomorphism `η : p ≅ f ≫ q`, is étale in the sense of Stacks 0CIL: Deligne–Mumford, and
étale on every diagram of its universal étale-smooth test.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEtale_of_isEtale_over_base_of_isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct`
with its étale charts supplied by **Stacks 0CIA**, part (2),
`Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDeligneMumfordStack_twoFibreProduct_of_isDM_algebraicSpace`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isDM_of_isEtale_over_base
declarations.doc:
**The Deligne–Mumford conjunct of Stacks 0CIR.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic
stacks over `𝒵` whose structural 1-morphism `p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` is étale is Deligne–Mumford.

Being over `𝒵` means `p ≅ f ≫ q`, so `f ≫ q` is Deligne–Mumford because `p` is étale, and
Stacks 050M, part (1), cancels the second factor.
declarations.comment: the Deligne-Mumford conjunct of the conclusion: a morphism between two stacks etale over a base is DM. The remaining conjunct of Tag 0CIL, the universal etale-smooth diagram condition, is not proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIT.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is *unramified* when it is
Deligne–Mumford and its universal étale-smooth diagram tests are unramified morphisms of
algebraic spaces, in the sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUnramified` (**Stacks 03ZH**,
part (1)).
declarations.statement: abbrev IsUnramified {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isUnramified_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIU.** The composition of unramified 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
unramified: for `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` unramified, so is `f ≫ g`.

This is **Stacks 0CIH** at unramifiedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces, which is étale-smooth
local on the source-and-target by **Stacks 0CG3** and stable under composition by
**Stacks 03ZI**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) (hg : IsUnramified B S hS g) :
    IsUnramified B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIU.** A composite of unramified 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
unramified.

This is **Stacks 0CIH** at unramifiedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces: that property is
étale-smooth local on the source-and-target by the unramified entry of **Stacks 0CG3** and stable
under composition by **Stacks 03ZI**, and unramifiedness of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is
exactly the property of Deligne–Mumford 1-morphisms that **Stacks 0CIG** induces from it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_comp
    (hT : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hForward : ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hT)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) (hg : IsUnramified B S hS g) :
    IsUnramified B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment:
with the substantial direction of Stacks 06N3 as the explicit hypothesis hForward
  (the structure theorem behind it, Stacks 06MD, 06N0, 06N2, 06G2, 06G3, is absent from the
  library); it is inherited from Stacks 0CIH, where it enters only through
  Stacks 0CIA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_baseChange_of_isUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram
declarations.doc:
A base change of an unramified 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is unramified: if
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is unramified, `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` is any 1-morphism and `R` is any 2-fibre product of
`(g, f)`, then the projection `R.fst : R.pt ⟶ 𝒴'` is unramified in the sense of Stacks 0CIT.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_baseChange_of_isUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴) (R : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hR : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct R)
    (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsUnramified B S hS R.fst
declarations.comment: unconditional: f is unramified in the sense of Stacks 0CIT and R is an arbitrary 2-fibre product of (g, f); the route through condition (2) of Stacks 0CIY is internal to the proof

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is unramified, `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` is any 1-morphism and `R` is any 2-fibre product
of `(f, g)`, then the projection `R.snd : R.pt ⟶ 𝒴'` is unramified in the sense of Stacks 0CIT.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_snd_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴) (R : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g) (hR : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct R)
    (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsUnramified B S hS R.snd
declarations.comment: unconditional, for a 2-fibre product of (f, g), the base change being its second projection R.snd

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIV.** The base change of an unramified 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`
along an arbitrary 1-morphism is unramified: for `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` unramified and `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴`
arbitrary, the second projection of the canonical 2-fibre product square of `(f, g)` — the base
change of `f` over `𝒵` — is unramified.

This is **Stacks 0CII** at unramifiedness of morphisms of algebraic spaces: that property is
étale-smooth local on the source-and-target by the unramified entry of **Stacks 0CG3** and stable
under base change by **Stacks 03ZJ**, and unramifiedness of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is
exactly the property of Deligne–Mumford 1-morphisms that **Stacks 0CIG** induces from it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_baseChange
    (hT : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hForward : ExistsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM.{u, w} B S hS hT)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsUnramified B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProductSquare B S hS f g).snd
declarations.comment:
for the canonical 2-fibre product square of Stacks 003Q, which is the shape the
  Stacks 0CII is stated at, and with the substantial direction of Stacks 06N3 as the
  explicit hypothesis hForward (the structure theorem behind it, Stacks 06MD, 06N0, 06N2, 06G2,
  06G3, is absent from the library); both are inherited from Stacks 0CII, where
  hForward enters only through Stacks 0CIA

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_of_isEtale
declarations.doc: An étale 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_of_isEtale {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴}
    (hf : IsEtale B S hS f) : IsUnramified B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isUnramified_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIX.** An immersion of algebraic stacks over `S`, in the sense of Stacks 04YL,
part (3), is unramified in the sense of Stacks 0CIT.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_of_isImmersion (j : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j) :
    Stack.IsUnramified B S hS j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIY.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following are
equivalent:
1. `f` is unramified (**Stacks 0CIT**);
2. `f` is DM, and for every algebraic space `V` with a 1-morphism `V ⟶ 𝒴` and every algebraic
   space `U` with an étale 1-morphism `U ⟶ V ×_𝒴 𝒳`, the morphism `U ⟶ V` is unramified;
3. there are an algebraic space `W` with a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented
   1-morphism `W ⟶ 𝒴` and an algebraic space `T` with a surjective étale 1-morphism
   `T ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 W` such that `T ⟶ W` is unramified.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_tfae {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    [IsUnramified B S hS f, IsUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram.{u, w} B S hS f,
      HasUnramifiedEtalePresentationOverFlatCover.{u, w} B S hS f].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_of_isUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIY, the implication (2) ⇒ (1).** A Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
over `S` whose every étale diagram of algebraic spaces has unramified top horizontal morphism is
unramified in the sense of Stacks 0CIT.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_of_isUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴}
    (hf : IsUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram.{u, w} B S hS f) :
    IsUnramified B S hS f
declarations.comment: the implication (2) => (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIY, the implication (1) ⇒ (2).** An unramified 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is
DM and every étale diagram of algebraic spaces over it has unramified top horizontal morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram_of_isUnramified
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} (hf : IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    IsUnramifiedOnEveryEtaleDiagram.{u, w} B S hS f
declarations.comment: the implication (1) => (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_of_surjectiveEtalePresentation_flatBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, let `W` be an algebraic space
with a surjective, flat, locally-of-finite-presentation 1-morphism `c : W ⟶ 𝒴`, and let the
2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_𝒴 W` admit a surjective étale 1-morphism from an algebraic space `T`. Then
`f` is Deligne–Mumford.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDM_of_surjectiveEtalePresentation_flatBaseChange
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (c : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS W hW ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hcSurj : IsSurjective B S hS c)
    (hcFlat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS c)
    (hcLfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS c)
    (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T)
    (t : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS T hT ⟶
      (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f c).pt)
    (htSurj : IsSurjective B S hS t)
    (htEt : IsRelativelyEtale B S hS t.hom) :
    IsDM B S hS f
declarations.comment: the Deligne-Mumford condition on f, which is the first conjunct of each of parts (1) and (2), from part (3); the unramifiedness of T -> W asserted by part (3) is not needed for it, and the easy direction of Stacks 06N3 that the source cites is taken in the form Stacks 06MB part (1), whose absolute Deligne-Mumford conclusion asks the big site to contain the terminal scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIZ.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S`. If `f ≫ g` is unramified, then `f` is unramified.

`f` is Deligne–Mumford by Stacks 050M part (1). For the étale-smooth diagram test, the nested
presentations supply a diagram over `f` extending to one over `f ≫ g`; the extended diagram's
top horizontal morphism is unramified, hence so is the one over `f` by **Stacks 06G6**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_of_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsUnramified B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hdata : HasSurjectiveEtaleSmoothDiagramOver.{u, w} B S hS f g) :
    IsUnramified B S hS f
declarations.comment: carrying as a hypothesis the two nested surjective etale presentations that the source obtains from Stacks 0CIA, which this library does not have because Stacks 06N3 is not proved; once they are given, the Deligne-Mumford hypothesis on the second factor is not used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isUnramified_of_comp_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CIZ.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S`. If `f ≫ g` is unramified and `g` is Deligne–Mumford, then `f` is unramified.

`f` is Deligne–Mumford by Stacks 050M. Choose a surjective smooth `W ⟶ 𝒵`, a surjective étale
`V ⟶ 𝒴 ×_𝒵 W` and a surjective étale `U ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 V`, the last two by Stacks 0CIA (the second
because `g` is Deligne–Mumford, the third because `f` is); then `U ⟶ W` is unramified, and
`U ⟶ V` is unramified by Stacks 06G6.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isUnramified_iff_isLocallyOfFiniteType_and_isEtale_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ0.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` admitting a diagram of algebraic
spaces as in `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasDiagonalDescentChart` is unramified exactly when it is
locally of finite type and its relative diagonal is étale.

Unramifiedness and local finite type are tested on the diagram's top morphism `h` of algebraic
spaces, and étaleness of the relative diagonal is tested on the relative diagonal of `h`; the
equivalence is then Stacks 05W1. Deligne–Mumfordness in the converse direction comes from
étaleness of the relative diagonal, étale morphisms of algebraic spaces being unramified by
Stacks 06CR.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_iff_isLocallyOfFiniteType_and_isEtale_relativeDiagonal
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hchart : Stack.HasDiagonalDescentChart.{u, w} B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsUnramified B S hS f ↔
      (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
        Stack.IsEtale B S hS (relativeDiagonal B S hS f))
declarations.comment: both implications: unramified iff locally of finite type with etale diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isUnramified_iff_isLocallyOfFiniteType_isEtale_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ0.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is unramified if and
only if it is locally of finite type and its relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is étale.

The implication (2) ⇒ (1) is
`isUnramified_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isEtale_relativeDiagonal`;
(1) ⇒ (2) is
`isLocallyOfFiniteType_and_isEtale_relativeDiagonal_of_isUnramified_of_etalePresentation`
at the structure theorem of Stacks 06N3,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsEtalePresentationOfIsAbsolutelyDM`, through which Stacks 0CIA is
available.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_iff_isLocallyOfFiniteType_isEtale_relativeDiagonal
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    Stack.IsUnramified B S hS f ↔
      (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧ Stack.IsEtale B S hS (relativeDiagonal B S hS f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEtale_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isFlat_of_isUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ1, (2) ⇒ (1).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is locally of
finite presentation, flat and unramified is étale. No diagram has to be supplied.

Deligne–Mumfordness is part of unramifiedness. For the universal étale-smooth test, take a
diagram it offers: its right leg is smooth, its left leg is smooth by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelySmooth_of_etaleSmoothDiagram` and its comparisons are smooth
because they are étale, so the universal *smooth* test of Stacks 06FM applies to it as well. That
gives local finite presentation of its top morphism directly, and flatness after Stacks 06FM
turns the existential test of Stacks 06PW into the universal one; unramifiedness is the
hypothesis at that diagram. Stacks 06LU concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isFlat_of_isUnramified
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) (hflat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hunr : Stack.IsUnramified B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsEtale B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isEtale_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ1.** For a 1-morphism `f` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following are
equivalent: `f` is étale; `f` is locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified; `f` is
locally of finite presentation, flat and has étale relative diagonal.

(2) ⇔ (3) is Stacks 0CJ0 together with Stacks 06Q5; (2) ⇒ (1) is Stacks 06LU on the top morphism
of an étale-smooth diagram; (1) ⇒ (2) uses the diagram Stacks 0CIA provides for the
Deligne–Mumford 1-morphism `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_tfae {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE
      [Stack.IsEtale B S hS f,
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f ∧ IsFlat B S hS f ∧ Stack.IsUnramified B S hS f,
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f ∧ IsFlat B S hS f ∧
          Stack.IsEtale B S hS (relativeDiagonal B S hS f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ3.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is a *local complete intersection
morphism*, or *Koszul*, when it passes the universal smooth-diagram test of Stacks 06FM at the
local complete intersection property of morphisms of algebraic spaces: every 2-commutative square
of algebraic spaces over `f` whose two vertical 1-morphisms are smooth and whose every comparison
1-morphism to a 2-fibre product is smooth has its top horizontal morphism a local complete
intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLocalCompleteIntersection {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocalCompleteIntersection.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ4.** The composition of local complete intersection 1-morphisms of algebraic
stacks over `S` is a local complete intersection 1-morphism: if `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` are
Koszul, so is `f ≫ g`.

This is the general composition remark **Stacks 06FP** at the Koszul property of morphisms of
algebraic spaces, which is stable under composition by **Stacks 06C8**, as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocalCompleteIntersection_comp`; the smooth locality
on the source-and-target that argument consumes is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalCompleteIntersection_isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalCompleteIntersection.comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴} {g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵}
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f)
    (hg : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS g) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocalCompleteIntersection_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ4.** A composition of local complete intersection 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
over `S` is a local complete intersection 1-morphism: if `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` are Koszul,
so is `f ≫ g`.

This is the general composition remark **Stacks 06FP**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_comp`, at the Koszul property of
morphisms of algebraic spaces, which is stable under composition by **Stacks 06C8**. Stacks 0CJ3
is the universal smooth-diagram criterion of **Stacks 06FM** where that remark speaks about the
existential one, so the hypotheses and the conclusion are moved across the equivalence of
conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 06FM.

One hypothesis beyond the source's is carried: `hlocal`, that the Koszul property of morphisms of
algebraic spaces is smooth local on the source-and-target (**Stacks 06FC** at that property),
which is what crosses that equivalence. It is not available in this library; see the
carried-hypothesis note in the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_comp
    (hlocal : Space.IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun _ _ k => Space.IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS k))
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f)
    (hg : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS g) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the composition argument in full, carrying one hypothesis this library does not prove: `hlocal`, Stacks 06FC at the Koszul property of morphisms of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocalCompleteIntersection_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ5.** A flat base change of a local complete intersection 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks over `S` is a local complete intersection 1-morphism: if `Q` is a 2-fibre product of the
cospan `(g, f)`, `g` is flat and `f` is Koszul, then the projection `Q.fst` is Koszul.

This is the flat base-change remark `hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_baseChange_of_isFlat` — the
form of **Stacks 06FQ** the source's hint names — at the Koszul property of morphisms of algebraic
spaces, which is invariant under isomorphism by **Stacks 03MJ** and stable under flat base change
by **Stacks 06C7**. Stacks 0CJ3 is the universal smooth-diagram criterion of **Stacks 06FM** where
that remark concludes about the existential one, so both hypothesis and conclusion are moved
across the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 06FM.

One hypothesis beyond the source's is carried: `hlocal`, that the Koszul property of morphisms of
algebraic spaces is smooth local on the source-and-target (**Stacks 06FC** at that property), which
is what crosses that equivalence. It is not available in this library; see the
carried-hypothesis note in the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_baseChange
    (hlocal : Space.IsSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget B S hS
      (fun _ _ k => Space.IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS k))
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS Q.fst
declarations.comment: the base-change argument in full, carrying one hypothesis this library does not prove: `hlocal`, Stacks 06FC at the Koszul property of morphisms of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocalCompleteIntersection_baseChange_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ5.** A flat base change of a local complete intersection 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks over `S` is a local complete intersection 1-morphism: if `Q` is a 2-fibre product of the
cospan `(g, f)` of algebraic stacks, `g` is flat and `f` is Koszul, then the projection
`Q.fst` to the source of `g` is Koszul.

This is the flat base-change argument
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocalCompleteIntersection_baseChange`, with the smooth
source-and-target locality of the Koszul property of morphisms of algebraic spaces (Stacks 06FC
at that property) supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalCompleteIntersection_isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_baseChange_of_isFlat
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
    (hf : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS Q.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection_comp_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ6.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` and `h : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of algebraic
stacks over `S` forming a 2-commutative triangle, `f ≫ g ≅ h`. If `g` is smooth and `h` is a
local complete intersection morphism, then `f` is a local complete intersection morphism.

Both the hypothesis on `h` and the conclusion are the universal smooth-diagram criterion of
Stacks 06FM (Definition Stacks 0CJ3), and they are moved to the existential one by smooth
locality on the source-and-target of the Koszul property of morphisms of algebraic spaces,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalCompleteIntersection_isSmoothLocalOnSourceAndTarget`. The
cancellation is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_of_comp_of_flatBaseChange`
at the pair (Koszul, smooth), whose space-level input is Stacks 0CHL,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_comp_of_isSmooth`, and which uses flat
base change of the Koszul property (Stacks 06C7) and base change of smoothness (Stacks 03ZE).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection_comp_of_isSmooth
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (h : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (e : f ≫ g ≅ h)
    (hg : IsSmooth B S hS g) (hh : IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS h) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersection B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_iff_isRelativeThickening
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is a thickening in the sense of **Stacks 0BPP** part
(1) if and only if it is representable by algebraic spaces and is a thickening in the relative sense
of §04XB, that is a closed immersion all of whose algebraic-space base changes are surjective.

The closed-immersion clause is the same on both sides; the surjectivity clause is surjectivity on
the points of Stacks 04XG on the left and the relative property of Stacks 03YK on the right, and
the two agree by **Stacks 04XI**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_iff_isRelativeThickening (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') :
    IsThickening i ↔ IsRelativeThickening B S hS i.hom
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedImmersion_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
A thickening of algebraic stacks over `S` is a closed immersion in the sense of **Stacks 04YL**
part (2).

In this library that is a clause of the definition of a thickening: **Stacks 0BPP** part (1)
realises the source as a *closed substack* of the target, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsThickening` records that closed immersion rather than recovering it
from a looser condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_isThickening (hi : IsThickening i) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS i
declarations.comment: closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universalHomeomorphism_of_isThickening
declarations.doc:
A thickening of algebraic stacks over `S` is a universal homeomorphism in the sense of
**Stacks 0CI7**: every base change of it induces a homeomorphism on the topological spaces of
points of Stacks 04XG and 04XL.

A base change of a thickening is a thickening (**Stacks 0BPR**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isThickening_fst_of_isTwoFibreProduct`), and a thickening is a
homeomorphism on points by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isHomeomorphOnPoints_of_isThickening`. The statement is at the
model-independent `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.UniversalHomeomorphism`, so it tests every 2-fibre
product square of the cospan and not only the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_of_isThickening (hi : IsThickening i) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism B S hS i
declarations.comment: universal homeomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAffineHom_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (1).** In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is affine (**Stacks 0CHQ**) if and only
if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is.

Representability by algebraic spaces is part (12) of the tag; affineness in the sense of Stacks
04XB is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_outer_of_inner` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_inner_of_outer` at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineMorphismProperty`, with the cancellation
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_of_comp_of_isClosedImmersion_of_isSurjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS m.inner ↔ AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (1): affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIntegralHom_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (5).** In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is integral (**Stacks 0CHU**) if and
only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is.

The argument is that of part (1) at `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.integralMorphismProperty`, with the
cancellation `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_of_comp_of_isClosedImmersion_of_isSurjective`
(Stacks 0415 splits integrality into affineness and universal closedness, which both cancel).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsIntegralHom B S hS m.inner ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsIntegralHom B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (5): integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (10), the quasi-separated half.** In a morphism of thickenings
`(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is
quasi-separated (**Stacks 04YW**) if and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is.

As in the source, this is a condition on the relative diagonals, which form a morphism of
thickenings (**Stacks 0BPU**), and it is clauses (d) and (g) of **Stacks 0BPV**:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_outer_of_inner` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_inner_of_outer`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS m.inner ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (10): quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (10), the separated half.** In a morphism of thickenings
`(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is
separated (**Stacks 04YW**) if and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is.

Separatedness is properness of the relative diagonal, and this is clause (q) of **Stacks 0BPV**:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_outer_of_inner` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_inner_of_outer`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS m.inner ↔ AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (10): separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.thickeningMorphism_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9.** Let `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` be a morphism of thickenings of
algebraic stacks over `S`, `f = m.inner` and `f' = m.outer`. Then
(1) `f` is affine if and only if `f'` is affine,
(2) `f` is surjective if and only if `f'` is surjective,
(3) `f` is quasi-compact if and only if `f'` is quasi-compact,
(4) `f` is universally closed if and only if `f'` is universally closed,
(5) `f` is integral if and only if `f'` is integral,
(6) `f` is universally injective if and only if `f'` is universally injective,
(7) `f` is universally open if and only if `f'` is universally open,
(8) `f` is quasi-DM if and only if `f'` is quasi-DM,
(9) `f` is DM if and only if `f'` is DM,
(10) `f` is quasi-separated if and only if `f'` is quasi-separated, and `f` is separated if and
only if `f'` is separated,
(11) `f` is representable if and only if `f'` is representable,
(12) `f` is representable by algebraic spaces if and only if `f'` is representable by algebraic
spaces.

The conjuncts are, in order, the twelve items of the source; item (13) ("add more here") states
nothing.
declarations.statement:
theorem thickeningMorphism_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    (AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS m.inner ↔ AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (IsSurjective B S hS m.inner ↔ IsSurjective B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS m.inner ↔ IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyClosed B S hS m.inner ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyClosed B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (AlgebraicStacks.IsIntegralHom B S hS m.inner ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsIntegralHom B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (UniversallyInjective B S hS m.inner ↔ UniversallyInjective B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyOpen B S hS m.inner ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyOpen B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS m.inner ↔ AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS m.outer) ∧
    (IsDM B S hS m.inner ↔ IsDM B S hS m.outer) ∧
    ((AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS m.inner ↔
        AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS m.outer) ∧
      (AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS m.inner ↔
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS m.outer)) ∧
    (Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor m.inner.hom) ↔
      Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳'.val.val.p 𝒴'.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor m.outer.hom)) ∧
    (IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS m.inner.hom.hom ↔
      IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS m.outer.hom.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableMorphism_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (11).** In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is representable (by schemes,
**Stacks 02Y7**) if and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableMorphism_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor m.inner.hom) ↔
      Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳'.val.val.p 𝒴'.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor m.outer.hom)
declarations.comment: part (11): representable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyClosed_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (4).** In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is universally closed (**Stacks 0513**)
if and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is.

The base changes of `f` and of `f'` are compared by the thickenings of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isThickening_baseChange_comp` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isThickening_baseChange_outer`, which are homeomorphisms on points
(**Stacks 0CJ7**).
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyClosed B S hS m.inner ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyClosed B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (4): universally closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyOpen_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (7).** In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is universally open (**Stacks 06U2**)
if and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is. The argument is that of part (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyOpen B S hS m.inner ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyOpen B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (7): universally open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactMorphism_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (3).** In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the restricted 1-morphism `f` is quasi-compact (**Stacks 050U**) if
and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is.

Quasi-compactness of an algebraic stack is compactness of its space of points (**Stacks 04YB**),
and the base changes of `f` and of `f'` are compared by the thickenings of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isThickening_baseChange_comp` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isThickening_baseChange_outer`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMorphism_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS m.inner ↔ IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (3): quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDM_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`,
the 1-morphism `f` is quasi-DM if and only if `f'` is quasi-DM.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiDM_inner_iff_outer :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS m.inner ↔ AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: item (8): quasi-DM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`,
the 1-morphism `f` is Deligne–Mumford if and only if `f'` is Deligne–Mumford.
declarations.statement: theorem isDM_inner_iff_outer : IsDM B S hS m.inner ↔ IsDM B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: item (9): DM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
In a morphism of thickenings `(f, f') : (𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳') → (𝒴 ⊂ 𝒴')` of algebraic stacks over `S`,
the 1-morphism `f` is representable by algebraic spaces if and only if `f'` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_inner_iff_outer :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS m.inner.hom.hom ↔
      IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS m.outer.hom.hom
declarations.comment: item (12): representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (2).** In a morphism of thickenings of algebraic stacks over `S`, the
restricted 1-morphism is surjective if and only if the ambient 1-morphism is surjective.

Surjectivity is a condition on the map of sets of points of **Stacks 04ZS**, the restriction
square induces a commutative square of those maps, and the two vertical maps of that square —
the thickenings — are bijective.
declarations.comment: part (2): surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_inner_iff_outer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJ9, part (6).** In a morphism of thickenings of algebraic stacks over `S`, the
restricted 1-morphism is universally injective if and only if the ambient 1-morphism is
universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_inner_iff_outer (m : ThickeningMorphism i j hi hj) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS m.inner ↔ UniversallyInjective B S hS m.outer
declarations.comment: part (6): universally injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_ambient_of_flatDeformation
declarations.doc:
For a commutative diagram of algebraic stacks over `S` over a thickening `iB : ℬ ⟶ ℬ'` of
bases, whose cube commutes (`hcoh`), with `𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'` locally of finite type, `𝒳' ⟶ ℬ'` flat and
locally of finite presentation, the restricted 1-morphism `f` flat, and the two restricted stacks
the base changes of the ambient ones along `iB`, the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_ambient_of_flatDeformation
    {iB : ℬ ⟶ ℬ'} {pX' : 𝒳' ⟶ ℬ'} {pY' : 𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'}
    {PX : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pX' iB} {PY : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pY' iB}
    {f : PX.pt ⟶ PY.pt} {f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'}
    (hiB : IsThickening iB)
    (hcartX : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PX) (hcartY : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PY)
    (houter : f' ≫ pY' ≅ pX')
    (hrestrict : f ≫ PY.fst ≅ PX.fst ≫ f')
    (hinner : f ≫ PY.snd ≅ PX.snd)
    (hcoh : Bicategory.whiskerLeft f PY.iso.hom ≫ Bicategory.whiskerRight hinner.hom iB =
      Bicategory.whiskerRight hrestrict.hom pY' ≫
        Bicategory.whiskerLeft PX.fst houter.hom ≫ PX.iso.hom)
    (hYft : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pY')
    (hXflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS pX')
    (hXfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS pX')
    (hfflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f'
declarations.comment: flatness of the ambient morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlatAt_target_of_flatDeformation
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_ambient_of_flatDeformation`, the
structure 1-morphism `𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'` is flat, in the sense of Stacks 0CID, at every point of `|𝒴'|` in
the image of `|f'|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatAt_target_of_flatDeformation
    {iB : ℬ ⟶ ℬ'} {pX' : 𝒳' ⟶ ℬ'} {pY' : 𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'}
    {PX : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pX' iB} {PY : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pY' iB}
    {f : PX.pt ⟶ PY.pt} {f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'}
    (hiB : IsThickening iB)
    (hcartX : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PX) (hcartY : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PY)
    (houter : f' ≫ pY' ≅ pX')
    (hrestrict : f ≫ PY.fst ≅ PX.fst ≫ f')
    (hinner : f ≫ PY.snd ≅ PX.snd)
    (hcoh : Bicategory.whiskerLeft f PY.iso.hom ≫ Bicategory.whiskerRight hinner.hom iB =
      Bicategory.whiskerRight hrestrict.hom pY' ≫
        Bicategory.whiskerLeft PX.fst houter.hom ≫ PX.iso.hom)
    (hYft : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pY')
    (hXflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS pX')
    (hXfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS pX')
    (hfflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (x' : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳') :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsFlatAt B S hS pY' (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f' x')
declarations.comment: flatness of the target over the base at image points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_of_flatDeformation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CJB.** Let `iB : ℬ ⟶ ℬ'` be a thickening of algebraic stacks over `S`, let
`pX' : 𝒳' ⟶ ℬ'` and `pY' : 𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'` be structure 1-morphisms, and let `f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'` be a
1-morphism over `ℬ'`, by `houter`. Let `PX` and `PY` present the restricted source and target as
the base changes of `𝒳'` and `𝒴'` along `iB`, and let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be the restricted 1-morphism
the universal property of the restricted target induces,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictedHom`. Assume

1. `pY'` is locally of finite type,
2. `pX'` is flat and locally of finite presentation,
3. `f` is flat,
4. `𝒳 = ℬ ×_{ℬ'} 𝒳'` and `𝒴 = ℬ ×_{ℬ'} 𝒴'`, i.e. `PX` and `PY` are 2-fibre products.

Then `f'` is flat, and `pY'` is flat — in the sense of **Stacks 0CID** — at every point of `|𝒴'|`
in the image of `|f'|`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlat_ambient_of_flatDeformation` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFlatAt_target_of_flatDeformation` with the two 2-cells of the
commutative diagram and its cube-coherence equation supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictedIsoFst`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictedIsoSnd` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictedHom_coherence` rather than assumed.

The two thickenings `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` and `𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴'` of the source's diagram are not hypotheses: they are
base changes of `iB` and so are thickenings by **Stacks 0BPR**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_flatDeformation
    {iB : ℬ ⟶ ℬ'} {pX' : 𝒳' ⟶ ℬ'} {pY' : 𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'}
    {PX : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pX' iB} {PY : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pY' iB} {f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'}
    (hiB : IsThickening iB)
    (hcartX : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PX) (hcartY : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PY)
    (houter : f' ≫ pY' ≅ pX')
    (hYft : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pY')
    (hXflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS pX')
    (hXfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS pX')
    (hfflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (restrictedHom B S hS PX PY houter hcartY)) :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f' ∧
      ∀ x' : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳',
        AlgebraicStacks.IsFlatAt B S hS pY' (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f' x')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_iff_isFlat_ambient
declarations.doc:
For a commutative diagram of thickenings of algebraic stacks over `S` over a thickening
`iB : ℬ ⟶ ℬ'` of bases, with `𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'` locally of finite type, `𝒳' ⟶ ℬ'` flat and locally of
finite presentation and the two restricted stacks the base changes of the ambient ones along `iB`,
the restricted 1-morphism `f` is flat if and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_iff_isFlat_ambient
    {iB : ℬ ⟶ ℬ'} {pX' : 𝒳' ⟶ ℬ'} {pY' : 𝒴' ⟶ ℬ'}
    {PX : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pX' iB} {PY : Bicategory.TwoCommSq pY' iB}
    {f : PX.pt ⟶ PY.pt} {f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'}
    (hiB : IsThickening iB)
    (hcartX : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PX) (hcartY : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct PY)
    (houter : f' ≫ pY' ≅ pX')
    (hrestrict : f ≫ PY.fst ≅ PX.fst ≫ f')
    (hinner : f ≫ PY.snd ≅ PX.snd)
    (hcoh : Bicategory.whiskerLeft f PY.iso.hom ≫ Bicategory.whiskerRight hinner.hom iB =
      Bicategory.whiskerRight hrestrict.hom pY' ≫
        Bicategory.whiskerLeft PX.fst houter.hom ≫ PX.iso.hom)
    (hYft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pY')
    (hXflat : IsFlat B S hS pX')
    (hXfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS pX') :
    IsFlat B S hS f ↔ IsFlat B S hS f'
declarations.comment: flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSmooth_iff_isSmooth_ambient
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_iff_isFlat_ambient`,
the restricted 1-morphism `f` is smooth if and only if the ambient 1-morphism `f'` is smooth.
declarations.statement:
