declarations.comment: the conormal map of an arrow of deformations is a conormal datum compatible with the base: its composite with the flat base change of the source deformation is the canonical map of Tag 01R4 for the square carrying the special fibre of the target over the closed point of the source's base. This is the factorisation through the total space of the source, not an identification of the map on the base with the map of maximal ideals

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.eq_of_isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalMap
declarations.doc:
**The conormal map of an arrow of deformations is the unique conormal datum compatible with
the base.** The special-fibre square of `P` is cartesian, so
`Stacks.Thickenings.eq_of_isBaseCompatibleConormalMap` applies: any map
`𝟙_X^* 𝒞_{X/P.scheme} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/Q.scheme}` whose composite with the flat base change of `P` is the
canonical map of the composite square is the conormal map of `φ`.

This is the sense in which the conormal map of an arrow of deformations "is" the map of the base
objects: it is determined by the square over `Spec A`, and
`Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalBaseChangeIso` exhibits that
square as the one the flat base change of `Q` and the conormal map of `φ.base` are read on.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalMap (φ : P ⟶ Q)
    {A : (modulePullback (Scheme.Hom.toLRSHom (𝟙 X.left)).toShHom).obj
        (immersionConormalSheaf P.specialMap) ⟶ immersionConormalSheaf Q.specialMap}
    (hA : IsBaseCompatibleConormalMap Q.specialMap P.specialMap (residueSpecMap P.base)
      X.hom P.toBase (φ.map ≫ P.toBase) (𝟙 X.left)
      P.specialCartesian.w (square_comp (specialMap_comp_map φ) P.specialCartesian.w) A) :
    A = immersionConormalSheafMap Q.specialMap P.specialMap (𝟙 X.left) φ.map
      (toShHom_square (specialMap_comp_map φ))
declarations.comment: the conormal map of an arrow of deformations is the UNIQUE conormal datum compatible with the base, the special-fibre square of the source being cartesian. This pins the map by the base object; it does not compute it on sections

declarations.name: Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_baseChangeDeformationHom
declarations.doc:
**The conormal map of the arrow of a deformation onto its base change is compatible with the
base.** This is `Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalMap` at
`Deformation.Examples.baseChangeDeformationHom`, the arrow the cofibered structure of the
deformation category produces, whose morphism of total spaces is the first projection of the
fibre product and whose base component is `g`.

Taken together with
`Deformation.Examples.isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalBaseChangeIso` and the
uniqueness `Deformation.Examples.eq_of_isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_deformationConormalMap`, this
says that the conormal map `𝒞_{X/P.scheme} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/(P ×_A B).scheme}` of the base change is
determined by `g` through the conormal map
`Deformation.Examples.residueConormalMap` of the base objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBaseCompatibleConormalMap_baseChangeDeformationHom :
    IsBaseCompatibleConormalMap (baseChangeDeformation P g).specialMap P.specialMap
      (residueSpecMap P.base) X.hom P.toBase
      ((baseChangeDeformationHom P g).map ≫ P.toBase) (𝟙 X.left)
      P.specialCartesian.w
      (square_comp (specialMap_comp_map (baseChangeDeformationHom P g)) P.specialCartesian.w)
      (immersionConormalSheafMap (baseChangeDeformation P g).specialMap P.specialMap
        (𝟙 X.left) (baseChangeDeformationHom P g).map
        (toShHom_square (specialMap_comp_map (baseChangeDeformationHom P g))))
declarations.comment: at the base change of a deformation: the conormal map of the arrow of a deformation onto its base change along a morphism of C_Lambda is a conormal datum compatible with the base. This is the general statement for an arrow of deformations instantiated at baseChangeDeformationHom, not a separate computation

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.cotangent_composition
declarations.doc:
At an identity of a groupoid scheme, the map `I/I² → J/J²` induced by composition is the
diagonal followed by the two maps induced by the projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem cotangent_composition :
    G.compositionCotangent x =
      ((G.firstCotangent x).coprod (G.secondCotangent x)).comp
        (LinearMap.id.prod LinearMap.id)
declarations.comment: composition on I/I²

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.cotangent_inverse
declarations.doc: At an identity of a groupoid scheme, inversion acts by `-1` on `I/I²`.
declarations.statement: theorem cotangent_inverse : G.inverseCotangent x = -LinearMap.id
declarations.comment: inversion on I/I²

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CK5, asking nothing beyond smoothness.** The sheaf of differentials `Ω_{X/Y}` of a
smooth morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` is finite locally free on the
small étale site of `X`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials`, the reduction
of Stacks 0CK5 to Stacks 02G1, applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafOfDifferentialsSchemeSiteComparison`, which proves the comparison
of Stacks 04CS that the reduction takes as its argument `hsite`.  The mathematics is that of the
reduction; only the argument is supplied.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials_of_isSmooth
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f.hom) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f)
declarations.comment:
the unconditional form, with the 04CS site transport of finite local freeness
  discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafOfDifferentialsSchemeSiteComparison`; smoothness of
  `f` is the only thing this asks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CK5.** The sheaf of differentials `Ω_{X/Y}` of a smooth morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` is finite locally free on the small étale site of `X`,
granted the comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SheafOfDifferentialsSchemeSiteComparison`.

An atlas of the target lifts along `f`, by Stacks 02X1, to a commuting square of étale charts
whose chart of the source is surjective on points.  Smoothness of `f` is the every-chart
condition of Stacks 03ZC(1), so the square's scheme morphism `ψ` is smooth; Stacks 02G1 makes
`Ω_{U/V}` finite locally free in the local-generators form of Stacks 01C6(2), and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_of_isFiniteLocallyFree` rewrites that in the
covering-family form of Stacks 03DL(2).  The hypothesis carries it to the small étale site,
Stacks 04CU — `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafOfDifferentialsEtaleChartComparison`, which is proved
and no longer assumed — to the restriction of `Ω_{X/Y}` to the chart, and the clause of
Stacks 03DN along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces descends it from that surjective chart
to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_sheafOfDifferentials {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f.hom)
    (hsite : SheafOfDifferentialsSchemeSiteComparison B S hS) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS f)
declarations.comment:
granted as `hsite` the comparison of 04CS transporting finite local freeness of
  the differentials of a morphism of schemes of the site from its small Zariski site to its small
  étale site.  The identification Ω_{X/Y}|_{U_étale} ≅ Ω_{U/V} of 04CU over a commuting square of
  étale charts is not granted: it is proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivationTranslate
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `θ · c`.**  For a morphism of thickenings `c` extending `e₀` and an
`𝒪_Z`-linear map `θ : e₀^*Ω_{W₀/Bas₀} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}`, the morphism of thickenings extending `e₀`
whose comorphism is that of `c` moved by the derivation attached to `θ` by Equation (0619).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivationTranslate
    (θ : (modulePullback B S hS e₀).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS b) ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS X Z)
    (c : ThickeningLiftOver B S hS Z W₀ e₀ r p) : ThickeningLiftOver B S hS Z W₀ e₀ r p
declarations.comment: the morphism theta . a' of thickenings over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.thickeningLiftSharp_sub_thickeningLiftSharp_derivationTranslate
declarations.doc:
**The comorphisms of `c` and of `θ · c` differ by the derivation related to `θ` by
Equation (0619).**  On every section `s` of `j^{-1}𝒪_W`,

`c^♯ s − (θ · c)^♯ s = ι (D (j^♯ s))`, where `D = d_{W₀/Bas₀} ∘ θ`.

That is, `(a')^♯ − (θ · a')^♯` factors as `𝒪_{Y'} ⟶ 𝒪_Y ⟶ a_*𝒞_{X/X'} ⟶ a_*𝒪_{X'}` through the
derivation `D` that Equation (0619) attaches to `θ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem thickeningLiftSharp_sub_thickeningLiftSharp_derivationTranslate
    (θ : (modulePullback B S hS e₀).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS b) ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS X Z)
    (c : ThickeningLiftOver B S hS Z W₀ e₀ r p)
    (V : (SmallEtale B S hS (⟨W₀.1.toFunctor, W₀.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS).1)ᵒᵖ)
    (x : (structureRingSheafInverseImage B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS W W₀)).obj.obj V) :
    (thickeningLiftSharp B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ c.1 c.2.1).hom.app V x -
        (thickeningLiftSharp B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀
          (derivationTranslate B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ b r ib hsq p θ c).1
          (derivationTranslate B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ b r ib hsq p θ c).2.1).hom.app V x =
      thickeningDerivationValue B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ b θ V x
declarations.comment: the comorphisms of a' and theta . a' differ by the derivation D = d o theta of Equation 0619

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_derivationTranslate_iff
declarations.doc:
**The notation `θ · c` means nothing else than that the comorphisms differ by the
derivation related to `θ` by Equation (0619).**  A morphism of thickenings `c'` over `Bas`
extending `e₀` equals `θ · c` if and only if `c^♯ s − c'^♯ s = ι (D (j^♯ s))` for every section
`s` of `j^{-1}𝒪_W`, where `D = d_{W₀/Bas₀} ∘ θ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_derivationTranslate_iff
    (θ : (modulePullback B S hS e₀).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS b) ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS X Z)
    (c c' : ThickeningLiftOver B S hS Z W₀ e₀ r p) :
    c' = derivationTranslate B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ b r ib hsq p θ c ↔
      ∀ (V : (SmallEtale B S hS (⟨W₀.1.toFunctor, W₀.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS).1)ᵒᵖ)
        (x : (structureRingSheafInverseImage B S hS
          (subspaceInclusion B S hS W W₀)).obj.obj V),
        (thickeningLiftSharp B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ c.1 c.2.1).hom.app V x -
            (thickeningLiftSharp B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ c'.1 c'.2.1).hom.app V x =
          thickeningDerivationValue B S hS Z hZ W₀ e₀ b θ V x
declarations.comment: that theta . a' is characterised by the comorphisms of a' and theta . a' differing by the derivation D = d o theta of Equation 0619

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivationAddAction
declarations.doc:
**The action `θ · c`.**  The group of `𝒪_Z`-linear maps `θ : e₀^*Ω_{W₀/Bas₀} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X}`
acts on the morphisms of thickenings over `Bas` extending `e₀` by `θ +ᵥ c = θ · c`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivationAddAction :
    AddAction ((modulePullback B S hS e₀).obj (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS b) ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS X Z) (ThickeningLiftOver B S hS Z W₀ e₀ r p)
declarations.comment: the action of theta on a', written theta . a'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivationMove_spec
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 0CK6].**  The action `θ · c` of a local section `θ` of
`SheafHom(e₀^*Ω_{W₀/T}, 𝒞_{Z/X})` on `c` means nothing else than this: `(e₀, θ · c)` is a
morphism of thickenings over `T` with the same map of conormal modules as `(e₀, c)`, and `c^♯`
and `(θ · c)^♯` differ by the derivation `D = d_{W₀/T} ∘ θ` of Equation
[Stacks Project, Tag 0619], read as maps `j^{-1}𝒪_W ⟶ (e₀)_*(i^{-1}𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivationMove_spec
    (θ : (modulePullback B S hS e₀).obj
        (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS W W₀ ≫ q)) ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS X Z)
    (p : X ⟶ T) (hcq : c ≫ q = p) :
    ∃ (hb : subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z ≫ derivationMove B S hS Z W₀ e₀ q hZ c hc θ p hcq =
        e₀ ≫ subspaceInclusion B S hS W W₀),
      derivationMove B S hS Z W₀ e₀ q hZ c hc θ p hcq ≫ q = p ∧
        conormalMap B S hS Z W₀ c e₀ hc =
          conormalMap B S hS Z W₀ (derivationMove B S hS Z W₀ e₀ q hZ c hc θ p hcq) e₀ hb ∧
        ∀ (V : (SmallEtale B S hS (⟨W₀.1.toFunctor, W₀.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS).1)ᵒᵖ)
          (x : ToType ((structureRingSheafInverseImage B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS W
              W₀)).obj.obj V)),
          (restrictedSquareZeroValues B S hS Z W₀ e₀ hZ).ι
              (derivationFamilyOfHom B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS W W₀ ≫ q) e₀
                (conormalModule B S hS X Z) θ V
                ((structureSharpRingInverseImage B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS W W₀)).hom.app V
                    x)) =
            (restrictedSharpThroughThickening B S hS Z W₀ c e₀ hc).hom.app V x -
              (restrictedSharpThroughThickening B S hS Z W₀
                (derivationMove B S hS Z W₀ e₀ q hZ c hc θ p hcq) e₀ hb).hom.app V x
declarations.comment: the action θ · a' of a local section θ: (a')^♯ and (θ · a')^♯ differ by the derivation D related to θ by Equation 0619

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_modulePullback_conormalMap
declarations.doc:
**The inverse image of the surjection of Stacks 0CK7 is surjective.**  Let `Z'` be a closed
subspace of an algebraic space `X'`, let `g : X ⟶ X'` be a morphism of algebraic spaces, and let
`a : W ⟶ g⁻¹(Z')` be a morphism of algebraic spaces.  The inverse image along `a` of the
canonical map of conormal modules `f^*𝒞_{Z'/X'} ⟶ 𝒞_{g⁻¹(Z')/X}` of the fibre product square is
an epimorphism of `𝒪_W`-modules.

In the situation of Stacks 0CK7 the base is a thickening `Z ⊆ Z'` and `Y = Z ×_{Z'} Y'`, so the
map `h^*𝒞_{Z/Z'} ⟶ 𝒞_{Y/Y'}` is the conormal map of a fibre product square and is surjective by
the surjectivity clause of Stacks 04CQ; this is the passage from that surjectivity to
surjectivity of `a^*h^*𝒞_{Z/Z'} ⟶ a^*𝒞_{Y/Y'}` along `a : X ⟶ Y`, which the source performs in
order to see that the map `A : a^*𝒞_{Y/Y'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` is determined by `a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_modulePullback_conormalMap {X X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : X ⟶ X')
    (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X'.1) {W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (a : W ⟶ (⟨(preimageSubspace B S hS g Z').1.toFunctor,
      (preimageSubspace B S hS g Z').2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)) :
    Epi ((modulePullback B S hS a).map
      (conormalMap B S hS (preimageSubspace B S hS g Z') Z' g
        (preimageProjection B S hS g Z')
        (conormalEtaleRestrictionSquare B S hS g Z')))
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the inverse image along `a` of the conormal surjection of a cartesian thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.liftSubfunctor_remark_of_cartesian
declarations.doc:
The special case of Lemmas 0618, 04D0, 061A and 061C in which the base `T = Z'` is itself a
thickening `Z ⊂ Z'` (any closed subspace `K`) and `Y = Z ×_{Z'} Y'` (the thickening `H` of `Y'` is
the inverse image of `Z`):
1. the map `A : a^*𝒞_{Y/Y'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` is determined by `a`: it is the only map whose composite
   with `a^*` of the surjection `h^*𝒞_{Z/Z'} ⟶ 𝒞_{Y/Y'}` is the canonical map
   `g^*𝒞_{Z/Z'} ⟶ 𝒞_{X/X'}` induced by `g'`
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCartesianConormalCompatible`, which also records `g = h ∘ a`);
2. for this `A` the sheaf of Lemma 061A is the rule
   `U' ↦ {a' : U' ⟶ Y' over Z' with a'|_U = a|_U}` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.liftSubfunctor`);
3. the sheaf `SheafHom_{𝒪_X}(a^*Ω_{Y/Z}, 𝒞_{X/X'})` acts on it
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.cartesianLiftSheafAddAction`, the action of Lemma 061C read through
   `Ω_{Y/Z'} = Ω_{Y/Z}`), simply transitively over every `U'` over which it has a section.

Here `X ⊂ X'` and `Y ⊂ Y'` are first order thickenings, as in Lemma 061C.
declarations.statement:
theorem liftSubfunctor_remark_of_cartesian
    (A : (modulePullback C S hS a).obj
        (conormalModule C S hS Y' ⟨(preimageSubspace C S hS pY' K).1, hH.1⟩) ⟶
      conormalModule C S hS X' ⟨G, hG.1⟩)
    (hA : IsCartesianConormalCompatible C S hS ⟨G, hG.1⟩ K pX' pY' a A) :
    (∀ A' : (modulePullback C S hS a).obj
        (conormalModule C S hS Y' ⟨(preimageSubspace C S hS pY' K).1, hH.1⟩) ⟶
      conormalModule C S hS X' ⟨G, hG.1⟩,
      IsCartesianConormalCompatible C S hS ⟨G, hG.1⟩ K pX' pY' a A' → A' = A) ∧
    conormalLiftSubfunctor C S hS hG hH pX' pY' a A = liftSubfunctor C S hS hG hH pX' pY' a ∧
    ∀ (U' : SpacesEtale C S hS X') (s : (liftSubfunctor C S hS hG hH pX' pY' a).obj (op U')),
      letI := cartesianLiftSheafAddAction C S hS K pX' pY' a hG₁ hH₁ A hA U'
      Function.Bijective (fun θ : cartesianLiftActionHom C S hS K hG pY' hH a U' => θ +ᵥ s)
declarations.comment: the special case B = Z' a thickening of Z and Y = Z ×_{Z'} Y': A is determined by a, the sheaf of 061A is the rule U' ↦ {a' : U' → Y' over Z' with a'|_U = a|_U}, and SheafHom_{O_X}(a^*Ω_{Y/Z}, C_{X/X'}) acts on it (the action of 061C), simply transitively

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivationMove_comp_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Acting by a derivation commutes with étale localization.**  For a commutative diagram of
first order thickenings `(h, h') : (T₂ ⊂ T₂') ⟶ (T₁ ⊂ T₁')`,
`(a_i, a_i') : (T_i ⊂ T_i') ⟶ (X_i ⊂ X_i')`, `(f, f') : (X₂ ⊂ X₂') ⟶ (X₁ ⊂ X₁')` and a commutative
square `f' ≫ q₁ = q₂ ≫ ε` with `X₂ ⟶ X₁` and `ε : B₂ ⟶ B₁` étale, and for
`θ₁ : a₁^*Ω_{X₁/B₁} ⟶ 𝒞_{T₁/T₁'}` with `θ₂` its étale localization
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleLocalizedDerivationDatum`, its last map the conormal map of
`(h, h')`): `(θ₂ · a₂') ≫ f' = h' ≫ (θ₁ · a₁')`, the actions being those of
[Stacks Project, Tag 0CK6] (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivationMove`, `T_i'` over `B_i` through
`a_i'`).
declarations.statement:
theorem derivationMove_comp_of_etale
    (hT₁ : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS T₁' Z₁.1) (hT₂ : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS T₂' Z₂.1)
    (hX₁ : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS X₁' W₁.1) (hX₂ : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS X₂' W₂.1)
    (ca' : a₂' ≫ f' = h' ≫ a₁') (ca : @CategoryStruct.comp (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) _ _ _ _ a₂ f =
      @CategoryStruct.comp (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) _ _ _ _ h a₁)
    (hfet : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) (hεet : IsEtale B S hS ε.hom)
    (θ₁ : (modulePullback B S hS a₁).obj
        (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₁' W₁ ≫ q₁)) ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS T₁' Z₁) :
    derivationMove B S hS Z₂ W₂ a₂ q₂ hT₂ a₂' ha₂
        (etaleLocalizedDerivationDatum B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₂' W₂ ≫ q₂)
          (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₁' W₁ ≫ q₁) f ε
          (comp_comp_eq_of_square_of_over B S hS W₁ W₂ f' f hf q₁ q₂ ε hq) a₂ h a₁ ca.symm
          (isIso_sheafOfDifferentialsMap_of_isEtale B S hS
            (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₁' W₁ ≫ q₁) f (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₂' W₂ ≫ q₂) ε
            hfet hεet (comp_comp_eq_of_square_of_over B S hS W₁ W₂ f' f hf q₁ q₂ ε hq))
          (conormalModule B S hS T₁' Z₁) (conormalModule B S hS T₂' Z₂) θ₁
          (conormalMap B S hS Z₂ Z₁ h' h hh)) (a₂' ≫ q₂) rfl ≫ f' =
      h' ≫ derivationMove B S hS Z₁ W₁ a₁ q₁ hT₁ a₁' ha₁ θ₁ (a₁' ≫ q₁) rfl
declarations.comment: the action of Remark 0CK6 is compatible with étale localization: (θ₂ · a₂') ≫ f' = h' ≫ (θ₁ · a₁') for θ₂ the composite a₂^*Ω_{X₂/B₂} = h^*a₁^*Ω_{X₁/B₁} → h^*C_{T₁/T₁'} → C_{T₂/T₂'}, the equality sign the identification of 04CU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictedLiftAction_comp_etaleLocalization
declarations.doc:
**The action of a derivation on lifts is compatible with étale localization.**  Let `S` be
a scheme and consider a commutative diagram of first order thickenings of algebraic spaces over
`S`
```
(T₂ ⊂ T₂') --(a₂, a₂')--> (X₂ ⊂ X₂')        X₂' --q₂--> B₂
   |                          |               |          |
 (h, h')                   (f, f')            f'         ε
   v                          v               v          v
(T₁ ⊂ T₁') --(a₁, a₁')--> (X₁ ⊂ X₁')        X₁' --q₁--> B₁
```
together with the commutative square on the right, with `f : X₂ ⟶ X₁` and `ε : B₂ ⟶ B₁` étale.
For an `𝒪_{T₁}`-linear map `θ₁ : a₁^*Ω_{X₁/B₁} ⟶ 𝒞_{T₁/T₁'}` let `θ₂` be the composite
```
a₂^*Ω_{X₂/B₂} = h^*a₁^*Ω_{X₁/B₁} --h^*θ₁--> h^*𝒞_{T₁/T₁'} ⟶ 𝒞_{T₂/T₂'},
```
whose equality sign is the inverse image along `a₂` of the identification
`f^*Ω_{X₁/B₁} ≅ Ω_{X₂/B₂}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 04CU]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localizationDifferentialsIso`) followed by the comparisons
`a₂^*f^* ≅ (a₂ ≫ f)^* = (h ≫ a₁)^* ≅ h^*a₁^*` of [Stacks Project, Tag 03LU], and whose last map
is the canonical map of conormal modules induced by the comorphism of `h'` on the defining ideals
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalComorphism`, transposed).  Then
```
(θ₂ · a₂') ≫ f' = h' ≫ (θ₁ · a₁'),
```
the actions being those of Remark [Stacks Project, Tag 0CK6],
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictedLiftAction`: `θ · a'` is the unique morphism of thickenings
over the base whose difference from `a'` ([Stacks Project, Tag 0618], Equation (0619)) is `θ`,
which exists by [Stacks Project, Tag 04D0].
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedLiftAction_comp_etaleLocalization
    (_hX₁ : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS X₁' X₁.1)
    (_hX₂ : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS X₂' X₂.1)
    (θ₁ : (modulePullback B S hS a₁).obj
        (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₁' X₁ ≫ q₁)) ⟶
      conormalModule B S hS T₁' T₁) :
    restrictedLiftAction B S hS T₂ X₂ hT₂ a₂ q₂ a₂' ha₂
        ((modulePullback B S hS a₂).map
            (localizationDifferentialsIso B S hS X₁ X₂ f' f hf q₁ q₂ ε hq hfet hεet).inv ≫
          (modulePullbackCompIso B S hS a₂ f).hom.app
            (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₁' X₁ ≫ q₁)) ≫
          (eqToHom (congrArg (modulePullback B S hS)
            (show @CategoryStruct.comp (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) _ _ _ _ a₂ f =
            @CategoryStruct.comp (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) _ _ _ _ h a₁ from hsq))).app
            (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₁' X₁ ≫ q₁)) ≫
          (modulePullbackCompIso B S hS h a₁).inv.app
            (sheafOfDifferentials B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X₁' X₁ ≫ q₁)) ≫
          (modulePullback B S hS h).map θ₁ ≫
          ((modulePullbackAdjunction B S hS h).homEquiv _ _).symm
            (conormalComorphism B S hS T₁ T₂ hT₁ hT₂ h' h hh)) ≫ f' =
      h' ≫ restrictedLiftAction B S hS T₁ X₁ hT₁ a₁ q₁ a₁' ha₁ θ₁

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.localStructure
declarations.statement:
theorem localStructure :
    (IsLocalRing (Space.etaleLocalRing C S hS G.objects.obj z) ∧
      IsLocalRing (Space.etaleLocalRing C S hS G.arrows.obj (identityArrowPoint G z)) ∧
      IsLocalRing (Space.etaleLocalRing C S hS (pullback G.source.hom G.target.hom)
        (identityPairPoint G z)) ∧
      IsLocalHom (sourceStalk G z) ∧ IsLocalHom (targetStalk G z) ∧
      IsLocalHom (identityPairComp G z) ∧ IsLocalHom (identityStalk G z) ∧
      IsLocalHom (inverseStalk G z) ∧ IsLocalHom (identityPairStalk G z)) ∧
    ((identityStalk G z).comp (targetStalk G z) = RingHom.id _ ∧
      (identityStalk G z).comp (sourceStalk G z) = RingHom.id _) ∧
    (IsCompl (sourceStalk G z).range.toAddSubgroup
        (RingHom.ker (identityStalk G z)).toAddSubgroup ∧
      IsCompl (targetStalk G z).range.toAddSubgroup
        (RingHom.ker (identityStalk G z)).toAddSubgroup) ∧
    ((pushoutMaximalIdeal (sourceStalk G z) (targetStalk G z)).IsMaximal ∧
      IsSepClosed (ResidueField
        (Localization.AtPrime (pushoutMaximalIdeal (sourceStalk G z) (targetStalk G z)))) ∧
      ∃ φ : Localization.AtPrime (pushoutMaximalIdeal (sourceStalk G z) (targetStalk G z)) →+*
          Space.etaleLocalRing C S hS (pullback G.source.hom G.target.hom)
            (identityPairPoint G z),
        φ.comp (algebraMap _ _) = identityPairTensorMap G z ∧ IsLocalHom φ ∧
        @IsLocalRing.IsHenselization
          (Localization.AtPrime (pushoutMaximalIdeal (sourceStalk G z) (targetStalk G z))) _ _
          (ResidueField
            (Localization.AtPrime (pushoutMaximalIdeal (sourceStalk G z) (targetStalk G z))))
          _ _ (Space.etaleLocalRing C S hS (pullback G.source.hom G.target.hom)
            (identityPairPoint G z)) _ _ φ.toAlgebra) ∧
    RingHom.ker (identityPairStalk G z) =
      ((RingHom.ker (identityStalk G z)).map (pushout.inl (CommRingCat.ofHom (sourceStalk G z))
          (CommRingCat.ofHom (targetStalk G z))).hom ⊔
        (RingHom.ker (identityStalk G z)).map (pushout.inr
          (CommRingCat.ofHom (sourceStalk G z)) (CommRingCat.ofHom (targetStalk G z))).hom).map
        (identityPairTensorMap G z) ∧
    (RingHom.ker (identityStalk G z)).map (identityPairComp G z) ≤
      ((RingHom.ker (identityStalk G z)).map (pushout.inl (CommRingCat.ofHom (sourceStalk G z))
          (CommRingCat.ofHom (targetStalk G z))).hom ⊔
        (RingHom.ker (identityStalk G z)).map (pushout.inr
          (CommRingCat.ofHom (sourceStalk G z)) (CommRingCat.ofHom (targetStalk G z))).hom).map
        (identityPairTensorMap G z)
declarations.comment: The whole section, for the etale local rings A = O_{U,u-bar}, B = O_{R,e(u-bar)} and C = O_{R x_{s,U,t} R,(e,e)(u-bar)} of a groupoid in algebraic spaces at a geometric point u-bar: (1) A, B, C are local and the maps s, t, c, e, i, (e,e) they induce are local homomorphisms; (2) e . t = 1 = e . s; (3) B = s(A) + I = t(A) + I as direct sums, I = ker e; (4) m_B (x) B + B (x) m_B is a maximal ideal of B (x)_{s,A,t} B (the pushout of s and t in CommRingCat), the localization at it has separably closed residue field, and C is the henselization of that localization through the map induced by b1 (x) b2 -> pr1(b1) pr2(b2); (5) the ideal J of C generated by I (x) B + B (x) I is the kernel of (e,e) : C -> A; (6) c : B -> C sends I into J.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.conormalMap_sectionTarget_eq_conormalMap_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKD.**  Let `G = (U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces, let
`U₀ ⊆ U` be a closed subspace whose inverse images along the source and the target agree — the
invariance of `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.IsInvariantClosed` — and let
`δ : U ⟶ R` be a section of the source agreeing with the unit on `U₀`, and let `s` be flat.
Then the conormal map of `𝒞_{U₀/U}` induced by `f = t ∘ δ` is the conormal map induced by
`id_U`, which is the canonical identification of `(id_{U₀})^*𝒞_{U₀/U}` with `𝒞_{U₀/U}`.  In the
language of the source, `f` acts as the identity on `𝒞_{U₀/U}`.

The source assumes `s` and `t` flat and `U` a first-order thickening of `U₀`; only flatness of
`s` is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalMap_sectionTarget_eq_conormalMap_id (δ : Section G)
    (hδ : subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ δ.1 =
      subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ identityArrow G)
    (hinv : U₀.1.preimage G.target.hom = U₀.1.preimage G.source.hom)
    (hs : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom)
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ (δ.1 ≫ G.target) =
      𝟙 _ ≫ subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀)
    (hsqId : subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ 𝟙 G.objects =
      𝟙 _ ≫ subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀) :
    conormalMap C S hS U₀ U₀ (δ.1 ≫ G.target) (𝟙 _) hsq =
      conormalMap C S hS U₀ U₀ (𝟙 G.objects) (𝟙 _) hsqId
declarations.comment: the conormal map induced by f = t ∘ δ equals the conormal map induced by the identity; only flatness of s is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.conormalMap_sectionTarget_comp_inv_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKD, read as the identity.**  Transported across the conormal map of the identity
square — the canonical identification of `(id_{U₀})^*𝒞_{U₀/U}` with `𝒞_{U₀/U}`, an isomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalMap_id` — the conormal map induced by `f = t ∘ δ` is the
identity: followed by the inverse of that identification it is the identity of
`(id_{U₀})^*𝒞_{U₀/U}`.  As in
`AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.conormalMap_sectionTarget_eq_conormalMap_id`, only
flatness of `s` is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalMap_sectionTarget_comp_inv_eq_id (δ : Section G)
    (hδ : subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ δ.1 =
      subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ identityArrow G)
    (hinv : U₀.1.preimage G.target.hom = U₀.1.preimage G.source.hom)
    (hs : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom)
    (hsq : subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ (δ.1 ≫ G.target) =
      𝟙 _ ≫ subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀)
    (hsqId : subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀ ≫ 𝟙 G.objects =
      𝟙 _ ≫ subspaceInclusion C S hS G.objects U₀) :
    conormalMap C S hS U₀ U₀ (δ.1 ≫ G.target) (𝟙 _) hsq ≫
        @inv _ _ _ _ (conormalMap C S hS U₀ U₀ (𝟙 G.objects) (𝟙 _) hsqId)
          (isIso_conormalMap_id C S hS U₀ hsqId) = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: f = t ∘ δ acts as the identity on the conormal module, read through the conormal map of the identity; only flatness of s is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.bijective_vadd_unitInfinitesimalSection
declarations.doc:
**The displayed bijection of Equation (0CKE).**  Translation of the unit is a bijection from
the `𝒪_{U₀}`-linear maps `θ : e₀^*Ω_{R₀/U₀} ⟶ 𝒞_{U₀/U}` onto the sections `Γ₀` of the source
which agree with the unit on `U₀`: every `δ ∈ Γ₀` is `θ · e` for exactly one `θ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_vadd_unitInfinitesimalSection :
    letI := (infinitesimalSectionDifference G U₀ hU₀).addAction
    Function.Bijective
      (fun θ : InfinitesimalSectionsHom G U₀ => θ +ᵥ unitInfinitesimalSection G U₀)
declarations.comment: the displayed bijection Hom_{O_{U_0}}(e_0^*Omega_{R_0/U_0}, C_{U_0/U}) -> Gamma_0, theta |-> theta . e, for a groupoid in algebraic spaces and a first order thickening U_0 of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.unitVAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Equation (0CKE) as a bijection.**  The map `θ ↦ θ · e` from the `𝒪_{U₀}`-linear maps
`e₀^*Ω_{R₀/U₀} ⟶ 𝒞_{U₀/U}` to the sections `Γ₀` infinitesimally close to the unit, bundled with
its inverse.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def unitVAddEquiv :
    InfinitesimalSectionsHom G U₀ ≃ InfinitesimalSections G U₀
declarations.comment: the displayed arrow Hom_{O_{U_0}}(e_0^*Omega_{R_0/U_0}, C_{U_0/U}) -> Gamma_0 bundled as a bijection, for a groupoid in algebraic spaces and a first order thickening U_0 of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.unitVAddEquiv_add
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 0CKF.**  Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces, `U₀ ⊆ U` an
`R`-invariant closed subspace such that `U` is a first order thickening of `U₀`.  The bijection
of Equation [Stacks Project, Tag 0CKE],
`θ ↦ θ · e` from `Hom_{𝒪_{U₀}}(e₀^*Ω_{R₀/U₀}, 𝒞_{U₀/U})` onto `Γ₀`, sends a sum of linear maps
to the composite of the corresponding sections:

`(θ₁ + θ₂) · e = (θ₁ · e) ∘ (θ₂ · e)`.

With `InfinitesimalSectionDifference.unitVAddEquiv_zero` (`0 · e = e`) this says that the
bijection is an isomorphism of groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem unitVAddEquiv_add (hinv : U₀.1.preimage G.target.hom = U₀.1.preimage G.source.hom)
    (θ₁ θ₂ : InfinitesimalSectionsHom G U₀) :
    unitVAddEquiv G U₀ hU₀ (θ₁ + θ₂) =
      infinitesimalSectionComp G U₀ (unitVAddEquiv G U₀ hU₀ θ₁) (unitVAddEquiv G U₀ hU₀ θ₂)
declarations.comment: the bijection theta |-> theta . e of (0CKE) carries the sum of two linear maps e_0^*Omega_{R_0/U_0} -> C_{U_0/U} to the composite of the two sections in Gamma_0, for an R-invariant first order thickening U_0 of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces.unitVAddMulEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 0CKF, bundled: the bijection (0CKE) is an isomorphism of groups.**  For an
`R`-invariant closed subspace `U₀ ⊆ U` of which `U` is a first order thickening, the bijection
`θ ↦ θ · e` of Equation [Stacks Project, Tag 0CKE] is a multiplicative equivalence from the
additive group of the `𝒪_{U₀}`-linear maps `e₀^*Ω_{R₀/U₀} ⟶ 𝒞_{U₀/U}` (written
multiplicatively) onto `Γ₀` with the composition of [Stacks Project, Tag 0CKC].
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def unitVAddMulEquiv
    (hinv : U₀.1.preimage G.target.hom = U₀.1.preimage G.source.hom) :
    Multiplicative (InfinitesimalSectionsHom G U₀) ≃* InfinitesimalSections G U₀
declarations.comment: the bijection Hom_{O_{U_0}}(e_0^*Omega_{R_0/U_0}, C_{U_0/U}) -> Gamma_0 of (0CKE) as an isomorphism from the additive group of linear maps onto Gamma_0 with its composition, for an R-invariant first order thickening U_0 of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.EtaleSmoothLift.fiber_endomorphisms_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKG, part (1).** Let `𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳'` be a first-order thickening of algebraic stacks, `W` an
algebraic space and `x : W ⟶ 𝒳` smooth, and consider the category `𝒞` of smooth lifts of the étale
opens of `W` along the thickening with its projection `p : 𝒞 ⟶ W_{spaces, étale}`
(Stacks 0CJP). Then the automorphism sheaves of the objects of `𝒞` are abelian: for every étale
open `U` of `W` and every object `ζ` of the fibre over `U`, the endomorphisms of `ζ` in that fibre
commute.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiber_endomorphisms_comm (hι₁ : AlgebraicStacks.IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS ι)
    (U : Space.SpacesEtale B S hS W)
    (ζ : (proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).Fiber U) (α β : ζ ⟶ ζ) :
    α ≫ β = β ≫ α
declarations.comment: part (1): the automorphism sheaves of objects of the category of smooth lifts are abelian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.EtaleSmoothLift.exists_band_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKG (2).** In Situation 0CJP, let `𝒳 ⊂ 𝒳'` be a first order thickening. Then the
sheaf of groups `𝒢` of Stacks 0CJY — the band of the gerbe `p : 𝒞 ⟶ W_{spaces,étale}` of smooth
lifts, with its banding `θ` and the three clauses of 0CJY — is a quasi-coherent `𝒪_W`-module: its
restriction to `W_étale` (Stacks 03G1) underlies a quasi-coherent `𝒪_W`-module `M`.

The gerbe inputs are proved (Stacks 0CJU, 0CJX) and so is the commutativity of the automorphism
groups (part (1)); nothing is assumed beyond Situation 0CJP and the first order thickening.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_band_isQuasicoherent (hι₁ : AlgebraicStacks.IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS ι) :
               haveI : (proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).IsFibered :=
        isFiberedInGroupoids_proj.isFibered
      haveI : ∀ U, IsGroupoid ((proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).Fiber U) :=
        isFiberedInGroupoids_proj.fiber_isGroupoid
      ∃ (𝒢 : Sheaf (Space.SpacesEtale.topology B S hS W) CommGrpCat.{u + 1})
        (θ : ∀ (U : Space.SpacesEtale B S hS W)
          (y : (proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).Fiber U),
          (Over.forget U).op ⋙ 𝒢.obj ⋙ forget CommGrpCat.{u + 1} ≅
            (proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).morPresheaf y y ⋙
              uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u + 1}),
        (∀ (U : Space.SpacesEtale B S hS W)
            (y : (proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).Fiber U) (g : Over U)
            (a b : 𝒢.obj.obj (op g.left)),
            ((θ U y).hom.app (op g) (a * b)).down =
              ((θ U y).hom.app (op g) a).down ≫ ((θ U y).hom.app (op g) b).down) ∧
          (∀ (U : Space.SpacesEtale B S hS W)
              (y z : (proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).Fiber U) (φ : y ⟶ z)
              (g : Over U) (a : 𝒢.obj.obj (op g.left)),
            ((θ U z).hom.app (op g) a).down =
              Functor.pullbackFiberHom (CategoryTheory.inv φ) g.hom ≫
                ((θ U y).hom.app (op g) a).down ≫ Functor.pullbackFiberHom φ g.hom) ∧
          (∀ (U : Space.SpacesEtale B S hS W)
            (y : (proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).Fiber U) (g : Over U)
            (a : 𝒢.obj.obj (op g.left)),
            ((θ U y).hom.app (op g) a).down =
              (Functor.pullbackFiberIdIso
                  ((proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).pullbackFiber y g.hom)).inv ≫
                ((θ g.left ((proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).pullbackFiber y
                    g.hom)).hom.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 g.left))) a).down ≫
                  (Functor.pullbackFiberIdIso
                    ((proj : EtaleSmoothLift B S hS ι hι W x hx ⥤ _).pullbackFiber y
                      g.hom)).hom) ∧
          ∃ M : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (Space.structureRingSheaf B S hS W),
            M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
              Nonempty ((Space.spacesEtaleAbelianRestriction B S hS W).obj
                ((sheafCompose _ commGroupAddCommGroupEquivalence.{u + 1}.functor).obj 𝒢) ≅
                (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj M)
declarations.comment: part (2): the sheaf of groups `𝒢` of Stacks 0CJY is a quasi-coherent `𝒪_W`-module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_smooth_affine_lift_of_isFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKI (Emerton).** Let `ι : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` be a first order thickening of algebraic stacks,
let `W` be affine and let `x : W ⟶ 𝒳` be smooth. Then there are an affine `W'`, a morphism
`i : W ⟶ W'` and a smooth `x' : W' ⟶ 𝒳'` such that the square `x ≫ ι ≅ i ≫ x'` is
2-cartesian, i.e. `W = 𝒳 ×_{𝒳'} W'`.

Here `W` and `W'` are algebraic spaces that are affine, that is, representable by affine schemes,
viewed as algebraic stacks through `algebraicSpaceStackFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_affine_lift_of_isFirstOrderThickening {𝒳 𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    {ι : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'} (hι₁ : IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS ι) (W : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hW : Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W.obj) (x : (algebraicSpaceStackFunctor B S hS).obj W ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hx : IsSmooth B S hS x) :
    ∃ (W' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (i : W ⟶ W')
      (x' : (algebraicSpaceStackFunctor B S hS).obj W' ⟶ 𝒳')
      (α : x ≫ ι ≅ (algebraicSpaceStackFunctor B S hS).map i ≫ x'),
      IsSmooth B S hS x' ∧
        Nonempty (IsTwoFibreProduct
          (⟨(algebraicSpaceStackFunctor B S hS).obj W, x,
            (algebraicSpaceStackFunctor B S hS).map i, α⟩ : TwoCommSq ι x')) ∧
        Space.IsAffineSpace B S hS W'.obj

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStack_of_faithful_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Descent along a faithful 1-morphism into a stack in groupoids.** Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site and
let `F : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒯` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over `𝒞`, that is a functor
with `F ⋙ q = p`. Assume that (1) `𝒯` is a stack in groupoids over `𝒞`, (2) for every object `U`
of `𝒞` the functor `𝒮_U ⥤ 𝒯_U` of fibre categories is faithful, and (3) for every object `y` of
`𝒯` over `U` the presheaf on `𝒞/U` sending `h : V ⟶ U` to the isomorphism classes of pairs
`(x, f)` with `x` an object of `𝒮_V` and `f : F(x) ⟶ h^* y` a morphism of `𝒯_V` is a sheaf. Then
`𝒮` is a stack in groupoids over `𝒞`.

Condition (3) is the two hypotheses `hsep` and `hglue`, in which a pair over `h` is a morphism
`f : F.obj x ⟶ y` lying over `h`, and the class of `(x₂, f₂)` is the restriction of the class of
`(x₁, f₁)` along `g : W ⟶ V` when `F.map c ≫ f₁ = f₂` for some lift `c : x₂ ⟶ x₁` of `g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStack_of_faithful_of_isSheaf {p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞} {q : 𝒯 ⥤ 𝒞} {F : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒯}
    {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hF : F ⋙ q = p) (hT : q.IsStack J)
    (hfaithful : ∀ U : 𝒞, (Fiber.fiberInclusion (p := p) (S := U) ⋙ F).Faithful)
    (hsep : ∀ (y : 𝒯) ⦃V : 𝒞⦄ (h : V ⟶ q.obj y) (R : Sieve V), R ∈ J V →
      ∀ ⦃x x' : 𝒮⦄ (f : F.obj x ⟶ y) (f' : F.obj x' ⟶ y),
        q.IsHomLift h f → q.IsHomLift h f' →
        (∀ ⦃W : 𝒞⦄ (g : W ⟶ V), R g → ∃ (z : 𝒮) (c : z ⟶ x) (c' : z ⟶ x'),
          p.IsHomLift g c ∧ p.IsHomLift g c' ∧ F.map c ≫ f = F.map c' ≫ f') →
        ∃ e : x ⟶ x', p.IsHomLift (𝟙 V) e ∧ F.map e ≫ f' = f)
    (hglue : ∀ (y : 𝒯) ⦃V : 𝒞⦄ (h : V ⟶ q.obj y) (R : Sieve V), R ∈ J V →
      ∀ (x : ∀ ⦃W : 𝒞⦄ (g : W ⟶ V), R g → 𝒮)
        (f : ∀ ⦃W : 𝒞⦄ (g : W ⟶ V) (hg : R g), F.obj (x g hg) ⟶ y),
        (∀ ⦃W : 𝒞⦄ (g : W ⟶ V) (hg : R g), q.IsHomLift (g ≫ h) (f g hg)) →
        (∀ ⦃W W' : 𝒞⦄ (g : W ⟶ V) (hg : R g) (k : W' ⟶ W),
          ∃ c : x (k ≫ g) (R.downward_closed hg k) ⟶ x g hg,
            p.IsHomLift k c ∧ F.map c ≫ f g hg = f (k ≫ g) (R.downward_closed hg k)) →
        ∃ (x₀ : 𝒮) (f₀ : F.obj x₀ ⟶ y), q.IsHomLift h f₀ ∧
          ∀ ⦃W : 𝒞⦄ (g : W ⟶ V) (hg : R g), ∃ c : x g hg ⟶ x₀,
            p.IsHomLift g c ∧ F.map c ≫ f₀ = f g hg) :
    p.IsStack J

declarations.name: Algebra.liftEmbeddingsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKN**.
For a finite separable extension `K/F` with `L` algebraically closed, the canonical
`L`-algebra map `L ⊗[F] K → (K →ₐ[F] L) → L` sending `x ⊗ₜ y` to `σ ↦ x * σ y` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def liftEmbeddingsEquiv (F K L : Type*)
    [Field F] [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra F L]
    [Module.Finite F K] [Algebra.IsSeparable F K] [IsAlgClosed L] :
    L ⊗[F] K ≃ₐ[L] ((K →ₐ[F] L) → L)

declarations.name: unramified_of_finiteType_and_etale_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
If the multiplication map `B ⊗[A] B → B` is flat, finite type implies unramified and
finite presentation together with flatness implies étale. In particular, every weakly étale
algebra of finite presentation is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramified_of_finiteType_and_etale_of_finitePresentation
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] :
    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B)).Flat →
      (Algebra.FiniteType A B → Algebra.Unramified A B) ∧
      (Algebra.FinitePresentation A B → Module.Flat A B → Algebra.Etale A B)) ∧
    (Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B →
      Algebra.FinitePresentation A B → Algebra.Etale A B)

declarations.name: structure_of_weaklyEtale_over_field
declarations.doc:
A weakly étale algebra `B` over a field `K` is reduced and integral. Every finitely
generated `K`-subalgebra is a finite product of finite separable extensions of `K`. Moreover,
`B` is a field or the zero ring exactly when it has no nontrivial idempotents; if it is a field,
then it is a separable algebraic extension. Subalgebras and quotient algebras of `B` are weakly
étale over `K`, as is the tensor product of `B` with any weakly étale `K`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem structure_of_weaklyEtale_over_field
    (K : Type u) (B : Type v) [Field K] [CommRing B] [Algebra K B]
    (hB : Algebra.WeaklyEtale K B) :
    IsReduced B ∧
      Algebra.IsIntegral K B ∧
      (∀ A : Subalgebra K B, A.FG →
        ∃ (ι : Type v) (_ : Finite ι) (L : ι → Type v) (_ : ∀ i, Field (L i))
          (_ : ∀ i, Algebra K (L i)) (_ : A ≃ₐ[K] ∀ i, L i),
          ∀ i, Module.Finite K (L i) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K (L i)) ∧
      (((Subsingleton B ∨ IsField B) ↔
          ∀ e : B, IsIdempotentElem e → e = 0 ∨ e = 1) ∧
        (IsField B → Algebra.IsSeparable K B ∧ Algebra.IsAlgebraic K B)) ∧
      ((∀ S : Subalgebra K B, Algebra.WeaklyEtale K S) ∧
        (∀ (Q : Type w) [CommRing Q] [Algebra K Q],
          (∃ f : B →ₐ[K] Q, Function.Surjective f) → Algebra.WeaklyEtale K Q)) ∧
      (∀ (B' : Type w) [CommRing B'] [Algebra K B'],
        Algebra.WeaklyEtale K B' → Algebra.WeaklyEtale K (B ⊗[K] B'))

declarations.name: exists_greatest_weaklyEtale_subalgebra
declarations.doc: An algebra over a field has a greatest weakly étale subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_greatest_weaklyEtale_subalgebra
    (K : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field K] [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] :
    ∃ Bmax : Subalgebra K A,
      Algebra.WeaklyEtale K Bmax ∧
        ∀ B : Subalgebra K A, Algebra.WeaklyEtale K B → B ≤ Bmax

declarations.name: exists_maximalWeaklyEtaleSubalgebraFunctor
declarations.doc:
The maximal weakly étale subalgebra over a field is functorial and commutes with filtered
colimits, reduction, and finite products. It pulls back along injective algebra maps, and over an
algebra without nontrivial idempotents it is either the zero ring or a separable algebraic field
extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_maximalWeaklyEtaleSubalgebraFunctor
    (K : Type u) [Field K] :
    ∃ (Bmax : CommAlgCat.{v} K ⥤ CommAlgCat.{v} K)
      (ι : Bmax ⟶ 𝟭 (CommAlgCat.{v} K)),
      (∀ A, Function.Injective (ι.app A)) ∧
      (∀ A, Algebra.WeaklyEtale K (Bmax.obj A)) ∧
      (∀ (A : CommAlgCat.{v} K) (S : Subalgebra K A),
        Algebra.WeaklyEtale K S →
          ∃ f : CommAlgCat.of K S ⟶ Bmax.obj A,
            f ≫ ι.app A = CommAlgCat.ofHom S.val) ∧
      (∀ (A' A : CommAlgCat.{v} K) (f : A' ⟶ A), Function.Injective f →
        ∀ x : A',
          (∃ b : Bmax.obj A', ι.app A' b = x) ↔
            ∃ b : Bmax.obj A, ι.app A b = f x) ∧
      PreservesFilteredColimits Bmax ∧
      (∀ A : CommAlgCat.{v} K,
        IsIso (Bmax.map (CommAlgCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K (nilradical A))))) ∧
      (∀ (J : Type v) [Finite J], PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) Bmax) ∧
      (∀ A : CommAlgCat.{v} K,
        (∀ e : A, IsIdempotentElem e → e = 0 ∨ e = 1) →
          Subsingleton A ∨
            (IsField (Bmax.obj A) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K (Bmax.obj A) ∧
              Algebra.IsAlgebraic K (Bmax.obj A)))

declarations.name: maximalWeaklyEtaleSubalgebra_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Extending the base field carries the maximal weakly étale subalgebra to the maximal
weakly étale subalgebra of the scalar extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem maximalWeaklyEtaleSubalgebra_baseChange
    (K : Type u) (L : Type v) (A : Type w)
    [Field K] [Field L] [CommRing A] [Algebra K L] [Algebra K A]
    (B : Subalgebra K A) (hB : Algebra.WeaklyEtale K B)
    (hBmax : ∀ C : Subalgebra K A, Algebra.WeaklyEtale K C → C ≤ B) :
    let f : L ⊗[K] B →ₐ[K] L ⊗[K] A :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id K L) B.val
    Function.Injective f ∧
      Algebra.WeaklyEtale L (L ⊗[K] B) ∧
      ∀ C : Subalgebra L (L ⊗[K] A), Algebra.WeaklyEtale L C →
        ∀ x : C, ∃ y : L ⊗[K] B, f y = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.separation_tfae_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CKV.** For a scheme of dimension zero, quasi-separatedness,
separatedness, Hausdorffness of the underlying space, and closedness of every affine open are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem separation_tfae_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X = 0) :
    List.TFAE [
      QuasiSeparatedSpace X,
      X.IsSeparated,
      T2Space X,
      ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → IsClosed (U : Set X)]
declarations.comment: separation_equivalences

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.connectedComponent_eq_singleton_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CKV.** The connected components of a quasi-separated zero-dimensional
scheme are its points.
declarations.comment: connected_components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_of_isCompact_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CKV.** Every quasi-compact open subset of a quasi-separated scheme of
dimension zero is affine.

theorem isAffine_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag0CKW.isIso_cohomologyBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Finite locally free base change.** For a cartesian square of schemes

```
Y --p--> X
|        |
k        iX
v        v
T --q--> S
```

with `S = Spec A` and `T = Spec B` affine and `q` finite locally free, and for every
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` and every `n`, the canonical map
`Hⁿ(X, F) ⊗_A B ⟶ Hⁿ(Y, p^* F)`, `x ⊗ b ↦ b • p^* x`, is an isomorphism of `B`-modules, for
an arbitrary scheme `X`.

The map is `cohomologyBaseChangeMap`, the `B`-linear extension of the pullback map
`cohomologyPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cohomologyBaseChangeMap [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree q]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (cohomologyBaseChangeMap H F n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag0CKW.isIso_cohomologyBaseChangeMap_of_isFiniteLocallyFree_module
declarations.doc:
**Finite locally free base change.** Let `φ : A ⟶ B` be a ring map making `B` a finite
locally free `A`-module, and consider a cartesian square of schemes

```
Y ------p-----> X
|               |
k               iX
v               v
Spec B --> Spec A
```

with bottom arrow `Spec φ`. For every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` and every `n`, the canonical
map `Hⁿ(X, F) ⊗_A B ⟶ Hⁿ(Y, p^* F)`, `x ⊗ b ↦ b • p^* x`, is an isomorphism of `B`-modules; here
`A` and `B` act through `Γ(Spec A, 𝒪)` and `Γ(Spec B, 𝒪)`, and `X` is an arbitrary scheme.
declarations.comment: as stated: B a finite locally free A-module

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.mem_radical_polynomialTIdeal_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The radical of `(t)` in `k[t^(ℚ≥0)]` is the ideal of polynomials with
vanishing constant coefficient: a positive exponent becomes at least one after enough
multiplications.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_radical_polynomialTIdeal_iff (k : Type*) [Field k] (p : rationalPolynomial k) :
    p ∈ (polynomialTIdeal k).radical ↔ p.coeff 0 = 0
declarations.comment: the radical of (t) in the monoid algebra

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.isMaximal_radical_polynomialTIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The radical of `(t)` is a maximal ideal of `k[t^(ℚ≥0)]`, being the
kernel of the constant-coefficient map onto the field `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMaximal_radical_polynomialTIdeal (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ((polynomialTIdeal k).radical).IsMaximal
declarations.comment: the radical of (t) is the maximal ideal

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.radicalQuotientEquiv
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0CKX.** The residue field of `k[t^(ℚ≥0)]` at the radical of `(t)` is `k`.
declarations.statement:
def radicalQuotientEquiv (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    rationalPolynomial k ⧸ (polynomialTIdeal k).radical ≃+* k
declarations.comment: the residue field at the radical of (t)

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.radical_polynomialTIdeal_sq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The radical of `(t)` is idempotent: a monomial of positive exponent is
the square of the monomial of half that exponent.
declarations.statement:
theorem radical_polynomialTIdeal_sq (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    (polynomialTIdeal k).radical ^ 2 = (polynomialTIdeal k).radical
declarations.comment: J ^ 2 = J for J the radical of (t)

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.radical_polynomialTIdeal_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** Every positive power of the radical of `(t)` equals it, so the tower
defining its adic completion is constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem radical_polynomialTIdeal_pow (k : Type*) [Field k] {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    (polynomialTIdeal k).radical ^ n = (polynomialTIdeal k).radical
declarations.comment: J ^ n = J for J the radical of (t)

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.radicalAdicCompletionEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The completion of `k[t^(ℚ≥0)]` at the radical of `(t)` is `k` itself,
because that radical is idempotent.
declarations.statement:
def radicalAdicCompletionEquiv (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    AdicCompletion (polynomialTIdeal k).radical (rationalPolynomial k) ≃+* k
declarations.comment: the radical-adic completion of the monoid algebra is k

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.injective_of_rationalPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The monoid algebra is contained in its `(t)`-adic completion: a
polynomial whose class vanishes modulo every power of `(t)` has all coefficients zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_of_rationalPolynomial (k : Type*) [CommRing k] :
    Function.Injective
      (AdicCompletion.of (polynomialTIdeal k) (rationalPolynomial k))
declarations.comment: the monoid algebra sits inside its (t)-adic completion

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.not_injective_compareAlgHom_radical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The comparison map from the `(t)`-adic completion of `k[t^(ℚ≥0)]` to the
completion at the radical of `(t)` is not injective: it kills the nonzero element `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_injective_compareAlgHom_radical (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ¬ Function.Injective
      (AdicCompletion.compareAlgHom k (polynomialTIdeal_pow_one_le_radical k))
declarations.comment: the comparison map is not injective

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.not_bijective_compareAlgHom_radical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The natural map from the `I`-adic completion to the `√I`-adic completion
of a ring can fail to be an isomorphism: for `I = (t)` in `k[t^(ℚ≥0)]` it is not bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_bijective_compareAlgHom_radical (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ¬ Function.Bijective
      (AdicCompletion.compareAlgHom k (polynomialTIdeal_pow_one_le_radical k))
declarations.comment: the comparison map is not a ring isomorphism

declarations.name: RationalPowerSeries.isEmpty_ringEquiv_adicCompletion_radical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKX.** The two completions are not isomorphic by any ring map at all: the
completion at the radical is the field `k`, while `t` is a nonzero non-unit of the `(t)`-adic
completion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_ringEquiv_adicCompletion_radical (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    IsEmpty (rationalPowerSeries k ≃+*
      AdicCompletion (polynomialTIdeal k).radical (rationalPolynomial k))
declarations.comment: the two completions are not isomorphic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_of_isTwoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CKY.** Let `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` and `𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids
over the big fppf site of `S`. If `𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` is representable by algebraic spaces and `𝒴` is a
stack in groupoids, then the 2-fibre product `𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴` is a stack in groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_of_isTwoFibreProduct
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (max (u + 1) w) v}
      (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f g)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
    (h𝒴 : 𝒴.val.p.IsStack (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) :
    P.pt.val.p.IsStack (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelyUnramified_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_isDM_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL0, part (4).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the
relative inertia projection `π : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` is unramified, in the relative sense of
Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, exactly when `f` is DM.

The direction (b) ⇒ (a) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelyUnramified_relativeInertiaProjection_of_isDM` and (a) ⇒ (b)
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDM_of_isRelativelyUnramified_relativeInertiaProjection`; neither
places any hypothesis on `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyUnramified_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_isDM_unconditional
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsRelativelyUnramified B S hS (relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f).hom ↔ IsDM B S hS f
declarations.comment:
part (4): the relative inertia projection is unramified iff f is DM, both
  directions and with no hypothesis. The direction (b) implies (a) is Stacks 0457 and 045C at the
  packaged unramified property; the converse needs no pseudo-torsor, being an instance of
  isUnramified_of_isUnramified_pullbackSnd, because the shear identifies the self-fibre-product
  of a fibre of the relative diagonal with the base change of the relative automorphism presheaf
  the inertia projection is tested on

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_isQuasiDM_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL0, part (5).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the
relative inertia projection `π : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` is locally quasi-finite, in the relative sense of
Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, exactly when `f` is quasi-DM.

The direction (b) ⇒ (a) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeInertiaProjection_of_isQuasiDM` and
(a) ⇒ (b) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiDM_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeInertiaProjection`; neither
places any hypothesis on `f`. This is the part the proof of **Stacks 0DSN** cites.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_isQuasiDM_unconditional
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f).hom ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f
declarations.comment:
part (5): the relative inertia projection is locally quasi-finite iff f is
  quasi-DM, both directions and with no hypothesis. The direction (b) implies (a) is Stacks 0457
  and 045C at the packaged locally-quasi-finite property; the converse is an instance of
  isLocallyQuasiFinite_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite_pullbackSnd, the generic half of Stacks 0DSK, fed
  by the shear identification rather than by a pseudo-torsor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallySeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the relative inertia projection
`π : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` is locally separated, in the relative sense of Properties of Stacks,
Section 04XB, exactly when the first relative diagonal `Δ_{f, 1} = Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳`
is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_relativeDiagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsLocallySeparated B S hS (relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f).hom ↔
      IsLocallySeparated B S hS
        (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom)
declarations.comment: part (3), conditions (a) and (b): the relative diagonal is locally separated exactly when the first projection of the relative inertia is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallySeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isImmersion_neutralSection
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S`, the relative diagonal
`Δ_{f, 1} = Δ_f` is locally separated in the sense of Stacks 04XB exactly when
`Δ_{f, 2} = e : 𝒳 ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`, the neutral section of the relative inertia, is an immersion of
algebraic stacks in the sense of part (3) of Stacks 04YL.

This is Stacks 04YU read at `Δ_f` instead of at `f` — whose representability hypothesis is
automatic there by part (1) of Stacks 04XS — composed with the identification of `Δ_{f, 2}` with
the neutral section, which is what the source means by "since `Δ_{f, 2}` is the diagonal of
`Δ_f` we have (b) ⇔ (c) by definition". The transports of the two conjuncts of part (3) of
Stacks 04YL are `isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_secondRelativeDiagonal_iff_neutralSection`
and `isImmersion_secondRelativeDiagonal_iff_neutralSection`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isImmersion_neutralSection (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsLocallySeparated B S hS
        (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom) ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsImmersion B S hS (relativeInertiaStackNeutralSection B S hS f)
declarations.comment: part (3), conditions (b) and (c): the relative diagonal is locally separated exactly when the neutral section of the relative inertia is an immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL0, part (1), conditions (a) and (b).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the relative inertia projection `π : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` is separated, in
the relative sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, exactly when the first relative
diagonal `Δ_{f, 1} = Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` is.

Both conditions are first read at the first projection `pr₁` of the 2-fibre product of `Δ_f`
with itself, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_twoFibreProductFst`. Then:

* (b) ⇒ (a) is Stacks 045C: `pr₁` is a base change of `Δ_f`, so it inherits separatedness, and
  no hypothesis on the property is needed.
* (a) ⇒ (b) is the section argument. `Δ_{f, 2} ≫ pr₁ = 𝟙 𝒳`, so `Δ_{f, 2}` is a section of
  `pr₁`, and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedImmersion_section_of_isSeparated` — Stacks 04YS at
  `pr₁`, which is representable by
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_twoFibreProductFst_relativeDiagonal`,
  followed by the three hypothesis-free transfers — makes `Δ_{f, 2}` a closed immersion.
  Stacks 04YS read at `Δ_f` instead of at `pr₁` turns that back into separatedness of `Δ_f`.

**Neither direction uses the group law of the relative inertia**, so Groupoids in Spaces,
Lemma 06P6 — the source's route, and Chapter 78 — is not needed; see the module docstring.

This theorem and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isClosedImmersion_neutralSection`,
which is (b) ⇔ (c), are together the covering set of part (1) of Stacks 0CL0, and both carry
it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_relativeDiagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsSeparated B S hS (relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f).hom ↔
      IsSeparated B S hS
        (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom)
declarations.comment: part (1), conditions (a) and (b): the relative inertia projection is separated exactly when the first relative diagonal is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL0, part (2), conditions (a) and (b).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the relative inertia projection `π : I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` is
quasi-separated, in the relative sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, exactly when the
first relative diagonal `Δ_{f, 1} = Δ_f` is.

The argument is that of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_relativeDiagonal` one step
down the scale: (b) ⇒ (a) is Stacks 045C at quasi-separatedness, and (a) ⇒ (b) is Stacks 04YT
at `pr₁` — making the section `Δ_{f, 2}` quasi-compact through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRelativelyQuasiCompact_section_of_isQuasiSeparated` — followed by
Stacks 04YT read at `Δ_f`.

This theorem and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isQuasiCompact_neutralSection`,
which is (b) ⇔ (c), are together the covering set of part (2) of Stacks 0CL0, and both carry
it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_relativeInertiaProjection_iff_relativeDiagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f).hom ↔
      IsQuasiSeparated B S hS
        (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom)
declarations.comment: part (2), conditions (a) and (b): the relative inertia projection is quasi-separated exactly when the first relative diagonal is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isClosedImmersion_neutralSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL0, part (1), conditions (b) and (c).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the relative diagonal `Δ_{f, 1} = Δ_f` is separated in the sense of
Stacks 04XB exactly when `Δ_{f, 2} = e : 𝒳 ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`, the neutral section of the relative
inertia, is a closed immersion of algebraic stacks in the sense of part (2) of Stacks 04YL.

This is part (1) of Stacks 04YZ — Stacks 04YS read at `Δ_f`, whose representability hypothesis
is automatic by part (1) of Stacks 04XS — composed with the identification of `Δ_{f, 2}` with
the neutral section, which is what the source means by "since `Δ_{f, 2}` is the diagonal of
`Δ_f` we have (b) ⇔ (c) by definition". The transports of the two conjuncts of part (2) of
Stacks 04YL are `Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_secondRelativeDiagonal_iff_neutralSection`
and `Stack.isClosedImmersion_secondRelativeDiagonal_iff_neutralSection`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isClosedImmersion_neutralSection (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsSeparated B S hS
        (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom) ↔
      AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (relativeInertiaStackNeutralSection B S hS f)
declarations.comment: part (1), conditions (b) and (c): the relative diagonal is separated exactly when the neutral section of the relative inertia is a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiSeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isQuasiCompact_neutralSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL0, part (2), conditions (b) and (c).** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks over `S`, the relative diagonal `Δ_{f, 1} = Δ_f` is quasi-separated in the
sense of Stacks 04XB exactly when `Δ_{f, 2} = e : 𝒳 ⟶ I_{𝒳/𝒴}`, the neutral section of the
relative inertia, is quasi-compact in that sense.

This is part (2) of Stacks 04YZ — Stacks 04YT read at `Δ_f` — composed with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompact_secondRelativeDiagonal_iff_neutralSection`. Being
quasi-compact is not one of the three parts of Stacks 04YL, so unlike condition (1)(c) there is
no representability conjunct to transport alongside.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_relativeDiagonal_iff_isQuasiCompact_neutralSection (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS
        (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom) ↔
      IsQuasiCompact B S hS (relativeInertiaStackNeutralSection B S hS f).hom
declarations.comment: part (2), conditions (b) and (c): the relative diagonal is quasi-separated exactly when the neutral section of the relative inertia is quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL1.** A closed immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-compact.

A closed immersion is representable by algebraic spaces (Stacks 04YL, part (2)), which is the
hypothesis of **Stacks 050T**; and its second conjunct `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsClosedImmersion`
differs from `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsQuasiCompact` only in the property demanded of the
structural morphism of each representing algebraic space, so **Stacks 04CG** transfers it
pointwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isClosedImmersion
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_valuationRing_of_mem_closure_range_pointsMap
declarations.doc:
A point in the closure of the image of a quasi-compact 1-morphism of algebraic stacks is
reached by the closed point of a valuative square. **Stacks 0CL2.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_valuationRing_of_mem_closure_range_pointsMap
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f)
    (y : points B S hS 𝒴.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒴.property))
    (hy : y ∈ @closure _
      (pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
      (Set.range
      (pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val (Classical.choose 𝒳.property)
        (Classical.choose 𝒴.property) f.hom.hom))) :
    ∃ (q : ValuativeSquare B S hS f)
      (hz : B.Contains
        (Spec (.of ((Spec (.of q.R)).residueField (IsLocalRing.closedPoint q.R))))),
      pointClass B S hS 𝒴.val.val
        (Classical.choose 𝒴.property)
        (fieldValuedPointMap B S hS
          (schemeFibredCategory B S hS
            (siteObject B S hS q.ring_mem q.base)).val
          q.y.hom
          (closedPointFieldValuedPoint B S hS
            (siteObject B S hS q.ring_mem q.base)
            (IsLocalRing.closedPoint q.R) hz)) = y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL3.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` the following are
equivalent: `f` is universally closed; every base change of `f` to a scheme of the site is closed
on points; every base change of `f` to an affine scheme of the site is closed on points; and
there is a smooth surjective 1-morphism from the algebraic stack of an algebraic space to `𝒴`
along which the base change of `f` is universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_tfae {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
        ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒴),
          IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst,
        ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) →
          ∀ (g : Stack.schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒴),
            IsClosed B S hS (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst,
        ∃ (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
            (g : Stack.algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS F hF ⟶ 𝒴),
          Stack.IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsSmooth B S hS g ∧
            UniversallyClosed B S hS
              (Stack.twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS g f).fst]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL5.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` *is proper* when it is separated
(**Stacks 04YW**), of finite type (**Stacks 06FS**, part (2)) and universally closed
(**Stacks 0513**, part (2)).

This is properness for an *arbitrary* 1-morphism of algebraic stacks; the Stacks 04XB relative
notion for a 1-morphism representable by algebraic spaces is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsProper`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsProper {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isProper_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL6.** A base change of a proper 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is proper:
if `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is proper and `P` is any 2-fibre product square of the cospan `(g, f)` for some
`g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴`, then the projection `P.fst` — the base change of `f` along `g` — is proper.

Properness is separatedness, finite type and universal closedness (Stacks 0CL5), and the three
conjuncts base change by **Stacks 050F**, **Stacks 06FU** and **Stacks 0514** respectively, which
is the source's own proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f) :
    IsProper B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isProper_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL7.** A composition of proper 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is proper:
if `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` are proper, then so is `f ≫ g`.

Properness is separatedness, finite type and universal closedness (Stacks 0CL5), and the three
conjuncts compose by **Stacks 050K**, **Stacks 06FT** and **Stacks 0515** respectively, which is
the source's own proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_comp {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f) (hg : IsProper B S hS g) :
    IsProper B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isProper_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CL8.** A closed immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` is a proper 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks.

Properness is the conjunction of **Stacks 0CL5**, and its three conjuncts are discharged in
turn: separatedness through monomorphy (**Stacks 0504** and **06MY**), local finite type by
**Stacks 06FV** for immersions, quasi-compactness by **Stacks 0CL1**, and universal closedness
from stability of closed immersions under base change (**Stacks 045C**) together with their
closedness on points (**Stacks 0H20**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_isClosedImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsProper B S hS f

registrations.comment: dotted arrows

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.Hom
registrations.comment: morphisms of dotted arrows

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSetoidCategory_dottedArrow_of_isSeparated_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLC, the setoid assertion.** If the relative diagonal `Δ_f` of a 1-morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is separated in the sense of Stacks 04XB, then the
category of dotted arrows of every valuative diagram for `f` is a setoid.

The category is a groupoid because the 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids is locally
groupoidal, so only the triviality of automorphisms is at issue. The two compatibility conditions
on an automorphism `θ` of a dotted arrow say that `θ` lies in the relative inertia of `f` and is
trivial at the generic point; separatedness of `Δ_f` makes the neutral section of the relative
inertia a closed immersion, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_id_of_isClosedImmersion_relativeInertiaNeutralSection` concludes,
the spectrum of a valuation ring being reduced and its generic point dominant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSetoidCategory_dottedArrow_of_isSeparated_relativeDiagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsSeparated B S hS (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom))
    (D : ValuativeDiagram B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f) :
    IsSetoidCategory (CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j f.hom D.y D.γ)
declarations.comment: setoid

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.instGroupoidDottedArrow
registrations.comment: groupoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_dottedArrow_equivalence_of_forall_exists_whiskerLeft
declarations.doc:
When the inertia `I_𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴` is proper, the category of
dotted arrows of a valuative diagram is independent, up to a noncanonical equivalence, of the
2-morphism witnessing the 2-commutativity.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_dottedArrow_equivalence_of_forall_exists_whiskerLeft
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hI : IsProper B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒴).hom)
    (D : ValuativeDiagram B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f)
    (γ γ' : (D.j ≫ D.y) ⟶ (D.x ≫ f.hom)) :
    Nonempty (CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j f.hom D.y γ ≌
      CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j f.hom D.y γ')
declarations.comment: 1 of 2: independence of the witness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_dottedArrow_iff_exists_diagonal
declarations.doc:
When the inertia `I_𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴` is proper, a dotted arrow of a valuative diagram exists — for
one and hence for every witnessing 2-morphism — exactly when there is a diagonal 1-morphism
`a : Spec R ⟶ 𝒳` with 2-morphisms `a ∘ j ⟶ x` and `y ⟶ f ∘ a`, with no condition relating
them to the witness.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_dottedArrow_iff_exists_diagonal
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hI : IsProper B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒴).hom)
    (D : ValuativeDiagram B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f)
    (γ : (D.j ≫ D.y) ⟶ (D.x ≫ f.hom)) :
    Nonempty (CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j f.hom D.y γ) ↔
      ∃ a : schemeFibredCategory B S hS D.whole ⟶ 𝒳.1,
        Nonempty ((D.j ≫ a) ⟶ D.x) ∧ Nonempty (D.y ⟶ (a ≫ f.hom))
declarations.comment: 2 of 2: existence for some and hence every witness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrowBaseChange.dottedArrows_baseChange_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLE.** The category of dotted arrows is invariant under base change along a
$2$-cartesian square.

Split a $2$-commutative rectangle into a left square, filled by `γ'`, and a right square,
filled by `φ` and assumed $2$-cartesian. Then the category of dotted arrows of the left square
is equivalent to the category of dotted arrows of the outer rectangle, whose filler is the
pasting of `γ'` and `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dottedArrows_baseChange_equivalence
    {S T X X' Y Y' : B}
    (j : S ⟶ T) (x' : S ⟶ X') (q : X' ⟶ X) (p : X' ⟶ Y')
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (y' : T ⟶ Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (φ : (p ≫ g) ≅ (q ≫ f)) (γ' : (j ≫ y') ≅ (x' ≫ p))
    (hcart : IsTwoCartesian q p f g φ) :
    Nonempty (CategoryTheory.DottedArrow x' j p y' γ'.hom ≌
      CategoryTheory.DottedArrow (x' ≫ q) j f (y' ≫ g)
          ((α_ j y' g).symm ≪≫ whiskerRightIso γ' g ≪≫ (α_ x' p g) ≪≫
            whiskerLeftIso x' φ ≪≫ (α_ x' q f).symm).hom)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.toWithFactorization_isEquivalence
declarations.doc: `toWithFactorization` is an equivalence of categories `𝒟 ≌ 𝒟''`.
declarations.statement:
instance toWithFactorization_isEquivalence {S T X Y Z : B} (x : S ⟶ X) (j : S ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (z : T ⟶ Z) (γ : (j ≫ z) ⟶ (x ≫ f ≫ g)) :
    (toWithFactorization x j f g z γ).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.fiber_categoryIso
declarations.doc:
The fibre of `compose` over an object `d'` of `𝒟'` is isomorphic, as a category (a
`CategoryIso`, not merely an equivalence), to the category of dotted arrows of the upper solid
square, whose bottom arrow is `d'.a` and whose witness is `d'.α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiber_categoryIso {S T X Y Z : B}
    (x : S ⟶ X) (j : S ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (z : T ⟶ Z)
    (γ : (j ≫ z) ⟶ (x ≫ f ≫ g))
    (d' : DottedArrow (x ≫ f) j g z (γ ≫ (α_ x f g).inv)) :
    Nonempty (CategoryIso ((compose x j f g z γ).Fiber d')
      (DottedArrow x j f d'.a d'.α))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.compose_isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.doc: `compose : 𝒟'' ⥤ 𝒟'` is fibred in groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem compose_isFiberedInGroupoids {S T X Y Z : B} (x : S ⟶ X) (j : S ⟶ T) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (z : T ⟶ Z) (γ : (j ≫ z) ⟶ (x ≫ f ≫ g)) :
    (compose x j f g z γ).IsFiberedInGroupoids

registrations.comment: equivalence with the intermediate category

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.DottedArrow.compose_isFiberedInGroupoids
registrations.comment: fibration over the lower dotted-arrow category

registrations.comment: fibre categories are upper dotted-arrow categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks satisfies the *uniqueness part of the
valuative criterion* when, for every valuative diagram for it, the category of dotted arrows
is either empty or a setoid with exactly one isomorphism class.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Uniqueness
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionUniqueness_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLH.** A base change of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks satisfying the uniqueness
part of the valuative criterion satisfies it as well.

The base change of `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` along `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` is the first projection of a 2-fibre product
`P` of the cospan `(g, f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionUniqueness_baseChange
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionUniqueness_comp
declarations.doc:
