The composition of two 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks satisfying the
uniqueness part of the valuative criterion satisfies it as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionUniqueness_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS f)
    (hg : ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS g) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionUniqueness_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLJ.** For a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks representable by algebraic spaces, the
uniqueness part of the valuative criterion holds exactly when it holds for every base change to
an algebraic space along a scheme-valued point of the target.

The base change is described exactly as in Stacks 02ZW: for an object `U` of the site and a
scheme-valued point `y` of `𝒴` over `U`, it is the first projection of the 2-fibre product
`U ×_𝒴 𝒳`, and the condition is imposed on the structure morphism of *any* algebraic space `F`
over `U` equivalent to it over the site of `U`. Quantifying over all such `F` rather than over a
chosen one spares a consumer the transport along a comparison equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionUniqueness_iff_baseChange
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS f ↔
      ∀ U : BigFppfOver B S hS,
        let 𝒰 := BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2
        let p𝒰 : 𝒰 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS := Over.map U.hom
        ∀ (y : 𝒰 ⥤ 𝒴.val.val.obj) (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p = p𝒰) (F : 𝒰ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F)
          (_e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
            (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒰 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p y f.hom.hom.toFunctor)
            (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
          (p : F ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj U.left.2)))),
          Space.ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ValuativeCriterion.Existence
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks satisfies the *existence part of the valuative criterion* when
every valuative square for it admits a dotted arrow after an extension of the fraction field and
passage to a dominating valuation ring.
declarations.statement: abbrev Existence (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionExistence_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLL.** A base change of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks satisfying the existence
part of the valuative criterion satisfies it as well.

The base change of `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` along `g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` is the first projection of a 2-fibre product
`P` of the cospan `(g, f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionExistence_baseChange
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f) (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionExistence_comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of two 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks satisfying the existence part of the
valuative criterion satisfies it as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionExistence_comp
    {𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS f)
    (hg : ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS g) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionExistence_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLN.** For a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks representable by algebraic spaces, the
existence part of the valuative criterion holds exactly when it holds for every base change to an
algebraic space along a scheme-valued point of the target.

The base change is described exactly as in Stacks 02ZW: for an object `U` of the site and a
scheme-valued point `y` of `𝒴` over `U`, it is the first projection of the 2-fibre product
`U ×_𝒴 𝒳`, and the condition is imposed on the structure morphism of *any* algebraic space `F`
over `U` equivalent to it over the site of `U`. Quantifying over all such `F` rather than over a
chosen one spares a consumer the transport along a comparison equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionExistence_iff_baseChange (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS f ↔
      ∀ U : BigFppfOver B S hS,
        let 𝒰 := BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2
        let p𝒰 : 𝒰 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS := Over.map U.hom
        ∀ (y : 𝒰 ⥤ 𝒴.val.val.obj) (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p = p𝒰) (F : 𝒰ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
          (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F)
          (_e : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
            (TwoFibreProductOver.fst p𝒰 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p y f.hom.hom.toFunctor)
            (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
          (p : F ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj U.left.2)))),
          Space.ValuativeCriterion.Existence p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionUniqueness_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLP, the uniqueness part.** A closed immersion of algebraic stacks over `S`
satisfies the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion (**Stacks 0CLG**).

By Stacks 0CLJ it is enough that every presheaf representing a base change of `f` along a
scheme-valued point of `𝒴` have structural morphism satisfying the uniqueness criterion for
presheaves; those presheaves have at most one section over every object by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.subsingleton_baseChange_of_isClosedImmersion`, so every morphism out of
them is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionUniqueness_of_isClosedImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS f
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionExistence_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLP, the existence part.** A closed immersion of algebraic stacks over `S` satisfies
the existence part of the valuative criterion (**Stacks 0CLK**).

By Stacks 0CLN it is enough that every presheaf representing a base change of `f` along a
scheme-valued point of `𝒴` have structural morphism satisfying the existence criterion for
presheaves. The closed immersion condition of Stacks 04YL is a condition on the structural
morphism of the lower-shriek extension of that presheaf, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.valuativeCriterionExistence_of_isClosedImmersion_relocalizeToYoneda`
turns it into the existence criterion for every morphism from the presheaf to the terminal
presheaf on the site of the point — which is the shape Stacks 0CLN asks for.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionExistence_of_isClosedImmersion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS f
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_of_isSetoidCategory_dottedArrow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLR.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. If the
relative diagonal `Δ_f` is quasi-separated, and if for every diagram (0CLB) and every choice of
`γ` as in Definition 0CLA the category of dotted arrows is a setoid, then `Δ_f` is separated.

Both conditions on `Δ_f` are read in the relative sense of Stacks 04XB. The setoid hypothesis
gives the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion for `Δ_f` through Stacks 0E8L, and
quasi-separatedness turns that into separatedness through Stacks 03KV. This is the converse of
the setoid assertion of Stacks 0CLC.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_relativeDiagonal_of_isSetoidCategory_dottedArrow (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS
      (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom))
    (hsetoid : ∀ D : ValuativeDiagram B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f,
      IsSetoidCategory (CategoryTheory.DottedArrow D.x D.j f.hom D.y D.γ)) :
    IsSeparated B S hS (relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_valuativeCriterionUniqueness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLT.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. Assume `f` is
quasi-separated. If `f` satisfies the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion, then `f` is
separated.

Separatedness of `f` is properness of `Δ_f` in the relative sense of Stacks 04XB. Its three
conjuncts are: separatedness of `Δ_f`, which is Stacks 0CLR fed with the setoid half of the
uniqueness criterion; finiteness of type, whose quasi-compactness half is the first conjunct of
quasi-separatedness and whose local half is part (2) of Stacks 04XS; and universal closedness,
which comes from the existence part of the valuative criterion for `Δ_f` through Stacks 0CLN and
Stacks 03KA.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_valuativeCriterionUniqueness (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hu : ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionUniqueness_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLU.** A separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks satisfies the uniqueness part of
the valuative criterion.

Separatedness is properness of the relative diagonal `Δ_f` in the sense of Stacks 04XB, so `Δ_f`
is in particular separated there and the category of dotted arrows of every valuative diagram is
a setoid by **Stacks 0CLC**. For the second half, two dotted arrows `a`, `b` of one valuative
diagram assemble into a scheme-valued point `(a, b, β_b ∘ β_a⁻¹)` of `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` whose valuative
diagram for `Δ_f` is filled by `(α_a, α_b)`; `Δ_f` is proper and representable by algebraic spaces
(**Stacks 04XS**), so that diagram has a dotted arrow by the valuative criterion of properness for
algebraic spaces (**Stacks 0A40**), and **Stacks 0E8L** turns that dotted arrow into a morphism
`a ⟶ b`, which the setoid property makes an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionUniqueness_of_isSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_valuativeCriterionExistence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLW.** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is quasi-compact
(**Stacks 050U**) and satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion (**Stacks 0CLK**)
is universally closed (**Stacks 0513**, part (2)).
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_valuativeCriterionExistence
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqc : Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    (hex : Stack.ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS f) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.valuativeCriterionExistence_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLX.** A quasi-separated, universally closed 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion.

Given a valuative square `q`, the specialisation step
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ValuativeSquare.exists_valuativeSquare_genericSection` produces a
valuative square `q₂` for the generic section of `q` whose closed point lies over the closed point
of `Spec q.R`. Its valuation ring and fraction field are the dominating extension; the two ring
maps come from 2-Yoneda and the full faithfulness of `Spec`; locality of the ring map is the
closed-point condition; and the dotted arrow is the special point of `q₂` followed by the
projection to `𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterionExistence_of_universallyClosed
    (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hclosed : AlgebraicStacks.UniversallyClosed B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isProper_iff_valuativeCriterion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CLZ.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is of
finite type (**Stacks 06FS**, part (2)) and quasi-separated (**Stacks 04YW**). Then `f` is proper
(**Stacks 0CL5**) if and only if it satisfies both the uniqueness part (**Stacks 0CLG**) and the
existence part (**Stacks 0CLK**) of the valuative criterion.

Properness is separatedness, finite type and universal closedness, and under the standing
hypotheses the equivalence is the conjunction of two equivalences: separatedness is the
uniqueness part, by **Stacks 0CLU** forwards and **Stacks 0CLT** backwards, and universal
closedness is the existence part, by **Stacks 0CLX** forwards and **Stacks 0CLW** backwards.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_iff_valuativeCriterion (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsProper B S hS f ↔
      ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness B S hS f ∧ ValuativeCriterion.Existence B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_affineLimit_surjective
declarations.doc:
If every map from a cofiltered limit of affine schemes over `S` to `X`
descends to a finite stage, then `X ⟶ S` is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_affineLimit_surjective
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hsurj : ∀ (I : Type u) [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
      (D : I ⥤ Over S) (c : Cone D), IsLimit c →
      (∀ i, IsAffine (D.obj i).left) →
      ∀ g : c.pt ⟶ Over.mk f,
        ∃ (i : I) (gᵢ : D.obj i ⟶ Over.mk f), c.π.app i ≫ gᵢ = g) :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_discreteValuationSpecialization
declarations.doc:
A point in the closure of the image of a finite-type morphism into a locally Noetherian
scheme is reached by a discrete valuation ring, with generic point on a generic component of the
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_discreteValuationSpecialization {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (y : Y)
    (y_mem_closure : y ∈ closure (Set.range f.base)) :
    Nonempty (DiscreteValuationSpecialization f y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_denseRange_of_exists_discreteLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CM3.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` and `h : U ⟶ X` be morphisms of schemes with
`S` locally Noetherian, `f` and `h` of finite type, `f` separated and `h(U)` dense in `X`. If
every commutative solid diagram with `Spec(K) ⟶ U ⟶ X` along the top and `Spec(A) ⟶ S` along the
bottom, where `A` is a discrete valuation ring with field of fractions `K`, admits a dotted arrow
`Spec(A) ⟶ X` making it commute, then `f` is proper.

This is `isProper_of_exists_discreteLift_of_denseRange` with its hypothesis `h0208` discharged by
`isProper_of_genericDiscreteValuativeCriterion'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_denseRange_of_exists_discreteLift
    {U X S : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType h] [QuasiCompact h] (hdense : DenseRange h)
    (hvaluative : ∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing D.R)
      (g : Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U), g ≫ h = D.i₁ → D.commSq.HasLift) :
    IsProper f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_denseRange_of_subsingleton_discreteLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CM4.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type with `S` locally
Noetherian, and let `h : U ⟶ X` be of finite type with `h(U)` dense in `X`. If every valuative
diagram for `f` over a discrete valuation ring whose generic arrow factors through `h` has at
most one dotted arrow, then `f` is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_denseRange_of_subsingleton_discreteLift
    {U X S : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType h] [QuasiCompact h] (hdense : DenseRange h)
    (hvaluative : ∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing D.R)
      (g : Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U), g ≫ h = D.i₁ → Subsingleton D.commSq.LiftStruct) :
    IsSeparated f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_denseRange_of_unique_discreteLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CM5.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` and `h : U ⟶ X` be of finite type with `S`
locally Noetherian and `h(U)` dense in `X`. If every valuative diagram for `f` over a discrete
valuation ring whose generic arrow factors through `h` has a unique dotted arrow, then `f` is
proper.

There is no separatedness hypothesis on `f`: separatedness is what the uniqueness of the dotted
arrow buys, through Stacks 0CM4.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_denseRange_of_unique_discreteLift
    {U X S : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType h] [QuasiCompact h] (hdense : DenseRange h)
    (hvaluative : ∀ (D : ValuativeCommSq f) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing D.R)
      (g : Spec (.of D.K) ⟶ U), g ≫ h = D.i₁ → Nonempty (Unique D.commSq.LiftStruct)) :
    IsProper f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_affineLimit_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM6.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite
presentation as soon as, for every cofiltered inverse limit of affine objects of the site,
the comparison map from the colimit of the sections of the source to the fibre product of
the sections over the limit with the colimit of the sections of the target is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_affineLimit_surjective
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : ∀ (I : Type u) [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
      (D : I ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (c : Cone D),
      IsLimit ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).mapCone c) →
      (∀ i, IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i))) →
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj c.pt) →
      ∀ (x : X.obj (Opposite.op c.pt)) (y : colimit (D.op ⋙ Y)),
        f.app (Opposite.op c.pt) x = colimit.desc (D.op ⋙ Y) (Y.mapCocone c.op) y →
        ∃ z : colimit (D.op ⋙ X),
          colimit.desc (D.op ⋙ X) (X.mapCocone c.op) z = x ∧
          colimMap (Functor.whiskerLeft D.op f) z = y) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM8, for `Y` quasi-separated.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` with `Y` quasi-separated.

1. For every morphism `g : Z ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces, point `z` of `|Z|` and closed subset `T`
   of `|X ×_Y Z|` whose image in `|Z|` misses `z`, there are an affine étale neighbourhood
   `(V, v)` of `z`, an affine `Z'` and a factorization `V ⟶ Z' ⟶ Y` of `V ⟶ Y` whose second leg
   `b` is locally of finite presentation, and a closed subset `T'` of `|X ×_Y Z'|` whose image in
   `|Z'|` misses the image of `v` and which receives the inverse image of `T` along the
   comparison morphisms `r` and `q` of the three fibre products.
2. If moreover `Z` is a scheme, represented by an object `Z₀` of the site, then `V` may be taken
   to be an affine open neighbourhood of `z`: the étale neighbourhood is an open immersion
   `V ⟶ Z₀` sending `v` to `z`, with all the conclusions of the first part.

The first part is `exists_affine_etale_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation`, which needs no
hypothesis on `Y`. The second part is
`exists_affineOpen_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation_of_factorization`, whose input — a
Zariski-local factorization of `Z₀ ⟶ Y` through an affine scheme locally of finite presentation
over `Y` — is supplied for quasi-separated `Y` by
`exists_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_factorization_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_etale_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    (∀ {Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
      (z : points B S hS Z) (T : Set (points B S hS (pullback f g))), IsClosed T →
      z ∉ pointsMap B S hS (pullback f g) (pullback.snd f g) '' T →
      ∃ (V Z' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Z)
        (v : points B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z')
        (b : yoneda.obj Z' ⟶ Y) (T' : Set (points B S hS (pullback f b)))
        (r : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g) (q : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f b),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z') ∧
        IsEtale B S hS p ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) p v = z ∧
        p ≫ g = a ≫ b ∧
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS b ∧
        IsClosed T' ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) a v ∉
          pointsMap B S hS (pullback f b) (pullback.snd f b) '' T' ∧
        r ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
        r ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ p ∧
        IsPullback r (pullback.snd f (p ≫ g)) (pullback.snd f g) p ∧
        q ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
        q ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ a ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) q ''
          (pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) r ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T') ∧
    (∀ {Z₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS} (g : yoneda.obj Z₀ ⟶ Y) (z : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Z₀))
      (T : Set (points B S hS (pullback f g))), IsClosed T →
      z ∉ pointsMap B S hS (pullback f g) (pullback.snd f g) '' T →
      ∃ (V Z' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z₀) (pV : V ⟶ Z₀)
        (v : points B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z')
        (b : yoneda.obj Z' ⟶ Y) (T' : Set (points B S hS (pullback f b)))
        (r : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g) (q : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f b),
        p = yoneda.map pV ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map pV) ∧
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map pV (pointsToScheme B S hS V v) =
          pointsToScheme B S hS Z₀ z ∧
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z') ∧
        IsEtale B S hS p ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) p v = z ∧
        p ≫ g = a ≫ b ∧
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS b ∧
        IsClosed T' ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) a v ∉
          pointsMap B S hS (pullback f b) (pullback.snd f b) '' T' ∧
        r ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
        r ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ p ∧
        IsPullback r (pullback.snd f (p ≫ g)) (pullback.snd f g) p ∧
        q ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
        q ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ a ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) q ''
          (pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) r ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T')
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, including the refinement for Z a scheme (V an affine open neighbourhood of z), under the extra hypothesis that Y is quasi-separated. For an arbitrary Y the refinement is open: it is equivalent to Z -> Y factoring Zariski locally through an affine scheme locally of finite presentation over Y, which is proved here only for Y quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_elementary_etale_separation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM8 for `Z` a scheme, with an elementary étale neighbourhood.** Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `Z` represented by
an object `Z₀` of the site, let `z` be a point of `|Z₀|`, and let `T` be a closed subset of
`|X ×_Y Z₀|` whose image in `|Z₀|` misses `z`. Then the conclusion of Tag 0CM8 holds with `V`
and `Z'` affine and with the étale neighbourhood `p : V ⟶ Z₀` *elementary*: the canonical
morphism `Spec κ(z) ⟶ Z₀` factors through it, so `v` and `z` have the same residue field.

The source asks only for an étale neighbourhood. The elementary refinement holds for an
arbitrary algebraic space `Y`, because the chart of `Y` can be chosen to receive the
field-valued point of `z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_elementary_etale_separation
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {Z₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : yoneda.obj Z₀ ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (z : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Z₀))
    (T : Set (points B S hS (pullback f g))) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hz : z ∉ pointsMap B S hS (pullback f g) (pullback.snd f g) '' T) :
    ∃ (V Z' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z₀) (pV : V ⟶ Z₀)
      (v : points B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z')
      (b : yoneda.obj Z' ⟶ Y) (T' : Set (points B S hS (pullback f b)))
      (r : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g) (q : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f b)
      (s : FieldValuedPoint.siteObject B S hS (yoneda.obj Z₀)
        (schemePointRepresentative B S hS Z₀ (pointsToScheme B S hS Z₀ z)) ⟶ V),
      p = yoneda.map pV ∧
      s ≫ pV = (schemePointRepresentative B S hS Z₀ (pointsToScheme B S hS Z₀ z)).siteHom ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z') ∧
      IsEtale B S hS p ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) p v = z ∧
      p ≫ g = a ≫ b ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS b ∧
      IsClosed T' ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) a v ∉
        pointsMap B S hS (pullback f b) (pullback.snd f b) '' T' ∧
      r ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      r ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ p ∧
      IsPullback r (pullback.snd f (p ≫ g)) (pullback.snd f g) p ∧
      q ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      q ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ a ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) q ''
        (pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) r ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T'
declarations.comment: the separation statement for Z a scheme, with V and Z' affine and the etale neighbourhood of z elementary -- the canonical morphism Spec kappa(z) -> Z factors through it -- and with clauses (1), (2) and (3) unchanged

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosed_separation_of_etale_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM8**, the étale-descent step of the proof. Let `f : X ⟶ Y`, `b : Z' ⟶ Y` and
`a : V ⟶ Z'` be morphisms of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`, and let `c : W ⟶ X` be a
morphism whose represented base changes are étale and which is surjective on points. There
are comparison morphisms `γ`, `α₁`, `α₂`, `κ` filling the square

```
W ×_Y V --α₁--> W ×_Y Z'
   |               |
   γ               κ
   ↓               ↓
X ×_Y V --α₂--> X ×_Y Z'
```

along which clauses (2) and (3) of Tag 0CM8 descend: given a closed subset `T₀` of
`|W ×_Y Z'|` receiving the inverse image of `T ⊆ |X ×_Y V|` and whose image in `|Z'|` misses
`r`, there is a closed `T' ⊆ |X ×_Y Z'|` receiving `T` and whose image in `|Z'|` misses `r`.
Clause (1), that `b` is locally of finite presentation, is a property of `b` alone and is
untouched by the descent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosed_separation_of_etale_cover
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (b : Z' ⟶ Y) (a : V ⟶ Z') (c : W ⟶ X)
    (hc : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf c)
    (hcsurj : Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS W c)) :
    ∃ (γ : pullback (c ≫ f) (a ≫ b) ⟶ pullback f (a ≫ b))
      (α₁ : pullback (c ≫ f) (a ≫ b) ⟶ pullback (c ≫ f) b)
      (α₂ : pullback f (a ≫ b) ⟶ pullback f b)
      (κ : pullback (c ≫ f) b ⟶ pullback f b),
      γ ≫ pullback.fst f (a ≫ b) = pullback.fst (c ≫ f) (a ≫ b) ≫ c ∧
        γ ≫ pullback.snd f (a ≫ b) = pullback.snd (c ≫ f) (a ≫ b) ∧
        α₁ ≫ pullback.fst (c ≫ f) b = pullback.fst (c ≫ f) (a ≫ b) ∧
        α₁ ≫ pullback.snd (c ≫ f) b = pullback.snd (c ≫ f) (a ≫ b) ≫ a ∧
        α₂ ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (a ≫ b) ∧
        α₂ ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (a ≫ b) ≫ a ∧
        κ ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst (c ≫ f) b ≫ c ∧
        κ ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd (c ≫ f) b ∧
        ∀ (T : Set (points B S hS (pullback f (a ≫ b))))
          (T₀ : Set (points B S hS (pullback (c ≫ f) b))),
          @IsClosed _ (pointTopology B S hS (pullback (c ≫ f) b)) T₀ →
          pointsMap B S hS _ α₁ '' (pointsMap B S hS _ γ ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T₀ →
          ∀ r : points B S hS Z',
            r ∉ pointsMap B S hS _ (pullback.snd (c ≫ f) b) '' T₀ →
            ∃ T' : Set (points B S hS (pullback f b)),
              @IsClosed _ (pointTopology B S hS (pullback f b)) T' ∧
                T ⊆ pointsMap B S hS _ α₂ ⁻¹' T' ∧
                  r ∉ pointsMap B S hS _ (pullback.snd f b) '' T'
declarations.comment: etale-descent step of the proof: clauses (2) and (3) descend along a cover of X whose represented base changes are etale and which is surjective on points; the reduction to the case of affine schemes and the appeal to Tag 05BD are not included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM8.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `g : Z ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces, let `z` be a point of `|Z|`, and let `T` be
a closed subset of `|X ×_Y Z|` whose image in `|Z|` misses `z`. Then there are an affine étale
neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `z`, an affine `Z'` and a factorization `V ⟶ Z' ⟶ Y` of `V ⟶ Y`
whose second leg `b` is locally of finite presentation, and a closed subset `T'` of
`|X ×_Y Z'|` whose image in `|Z'|` misses the image of `v` and which receives the inverse image
of `T` along the two comparison morphisms `r` and `q` of the three fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_etale_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation
    {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (z : points B S hS Z) (T : Set (points B S hS (pullback f g))) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hz : z ∉ pointsMap B S hS (pullback f g) (pullback.snd f g) '' T) :
    ∃ (V Z' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Z)
      (v : points B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z')
      (b : yoneda.obj Z' ⟶ Y) (T' : Set (points B S hS (pullback f b)))
      (r : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g) (q : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f b),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z') ∧
      IsEtale B S hS p ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) p v = z ∧
      p ≫ g = a ≫ b ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS b ∧
      IsClosed T' ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) a v ∉
        pointsMap B S hS (pullback f b) (pullback.snd f b) '' T' ∧
      r ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      r ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ p ∧
      IsPullback r (pullback.snd f (p ≫ g)) (pullback.snd f g) p ∧
      q ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      q ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ a ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) q ''
        (pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) r ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T'
declarations.comment: the separation statement, with V and Z' affine; the refinement for Z a scheme, where V may be taken to be an affine open neighbourhood of z, is not included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineOpen_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation_of_lfp_morphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM8, the refinement for `Z` a scheme and `Y` an arbitrary algebraic space**, for a
morphism `g : Z ⟶ Y` which is locally of finite presentation. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `Z` represented by an object `Z₀` of
the site, let `g : yoneda.obj Z₀ ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation, let `z` be a point of
`|Z₀|`, and let `T` be a closed subset of `|X ×_Y Z₀|` whose image in `|Z₀|` misses `z`. Then
the conclusion of Tag 0CM8 holds with the étale neighbourhood `p` an *open immersion* out of an
affine `V` sending `v` to `z`: that is, `V` is an affine open neighbourhood of `z`, `Z'` is
affine, and clauses (1), (2) and (3) — `b` locally of finite presentation, the image of `T'` in
`|Z'|` missing the image of `v`, and `T'` receiving the inverse image of `T` — all hold, as
does étaleness of `p`.

Nothing is assumed of `Y` beyond being an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation_of_lfp_morphism
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {Z₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : yoneda.obj Z₀ ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (z : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Z₀))
    (T : Set (points B S hS (pullback f g))) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hz : z ∉ pointsMap B S hS (pullback f g) (pullback.snd f g) '' T) :
    ∃ (V Z' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z₀) (pV : V ⟶ Z₀)
      (v : points B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z')
      (b : yoneda.obj Z' ⟶ Y) (T' : Set (points B S hS (pullback f b)))
      (r : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g) (q : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f b),
      p = yoneda.map pV ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map pV) ∧
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map pV (pointsToScheme B S hS V v) =
        pointsToScheme B S hS Z₀ z ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z') ∧
      IsEtale B S hS p ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) p v = z ∧
      p ≫ g = a ≫ b ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS b ∧
      IsClosed T' ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) a v ∉
        pointsMap B S hS (pullback f b) (pullback.snd f b) '' T' ∧
      r ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      r ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ p ∧
      IsPullback r (pullback.snd f (p ≫ g)) (pullback.snd f g) p ∧
      q ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      q ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ a ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) q ''
        (pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) r ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T'
declarations.comment: the refinement for Z a scheme with Y an arbitrary algebraic space over S, for g : Z -> Y locally of finite presentation: the etale neighbourhood p : V -> Z is an open immersion onto an affine open neighbourhood of z, Z' is affine, and clauses (1), (2) and (3) hold -- b locally of finite presentation, the image of T' in |Z'| missing a(v), and T' receiving the inverse image of T. An affine open neighbourhood of z is then itself an affine scheme locally of finite presentation over Y, which is the factorization the refinement amounts to

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineOpen_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM8, the refinement for `Z` a scheme**, with no hypothesis on `g`, in the
situation the source's own proof reduces to, where `Y` is represented by an object of the site
as well. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism with `X` an algebraic space over `S` and
`Y` and `Z` represented by objects `Y₀` and `Z₀` of the site, let `z` be a point of `|Z₀|`, and
let `T` be a closed subset of `|X ×_Y Z₀|` whose image in `|Z₀|` misses `z`. Then the
conclusion of Tag 0CM8 holds with `V` an affine *open* neighbourhood of `z`: the morphism
`p : V ⟶ Z₀` is an open immersion sending `v` to `z`, `V` and `Z'` are affine, and clauses
(1), (2) and (3) of the source hold unchanged.

For `Y` an arbitrary algebraic space the refinement holds whenever `g` is locally of finite
presentation, by
`exists_affineOpen_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation_of_lfp_morphism`, and in general
from a Zariski-local factorization, by
`exists_affineOpen_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation_of_factorization`,
which asks for the input in its sharpest form — an affine open neighbourhood of `z` whose
morphism to `Y` factors through an affine scheme *locally of finite presentation* over `Y`.
That input cannot be dispensed with: it is part of the refinement's own conclusion, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_factorization_of_separation`.
What `Y` being a scheme supplies is a Zariski-local factorization: for a general algebraic
space the affine opens of `Y` are replaced by affine étale charts, and pulling a chart back
along `Z₀ ⟶ Y` gives an étale morphism to `Z₀`, of which one needs a *section* near `z`. A
point above `z` with the same residue field as `z` is not enough for that and is in any case
always available, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_chart_of_fieldValuedPoint`, for an arbitrary
algebraic space and with no decency hypothesis; an étale morphism with trivial residue
extension at a point has a section near it exactly when the map of local rings there is an
isomorphism, by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_of_etale_of_isIso_stalkMap`, and that
is the Henselian property of `𝒪_{Z₀, z}` rather than anything about `Y`. What does supply the
factorization for an arbitrary `Y` and an arbitrary `g`, and which step of it this development
is missing, is recorded in the note opening this section.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineOpen_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_separation
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {Y₀ Z₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y₀) (g : yoneda.obj Z₀ ⟶ yoneda.obj Y₀)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (z : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Z₀))
    (T : Set (points B S hS (pullback f g))) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hz : z ∉ pointsMap B S hS (pullback f g) (pullback.snd f g) '' T) :
    ∃ (V Z' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z₀) (pV : V ⟶ Z₀)
      (v : points B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ yoneda.obj Z')
      (b : yoneda.obj Z' ⟶ yoneda.obj Y₀) (T' : Set (points B S hS (pullback f b)))
      (r : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f g) (q : pullback f (p ≫ g) ⟶ pullback f b),
      p = yoneda.map pV ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map pV) ∧
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map pV (pointsToScheme B S hS V v) =
        pointsToScheme B S hS Z₀ z ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z') ∧
      IsEtale B S hS p ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) p v = z ∧
      p ≫ g = a ≫ b ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS b ∧
      IsClosed T' ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) a v ∉
        pointsMap B S hS (pullback f b) (pullback.snd f b) '' T' ∧
      r ≫ pullback.fst f g = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      r ≫ pullback.snd f g = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ p ∧
      IsPullback r (pullback.snd f (p ≫ g)) (pullback.snd f g) p ∧
      q ≫ pullback.fst f b = pullback.fst f (p ≫ g) ∧
      q ≫ pullback.snd f b = pullback.snd f (p ≫ g) ≫ a ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) q ''
        (pointsMap B S hS (pullback f (p ≫ g)) r ⁻¹' T) ⊆ T'
declarations.comment: the refinement for Z a scheme with no hypothesis on g, for Y represented by an object of the site as well -- the situation the source's own proof reduces to before it produces the affine open neighbourhood: the etale neighbourhood p : V -> Z is an open immersion onto an affine open neighbourhood of z, Z' is affine, and clauses (1), (2) and (3) hold -- b locally of finite presentation, the image of T' in |Z'| missing a(v), and T' receiving the inverse image of T. The affine opens of Y supply the factorization of an affine open neighbourhood of z through an affine scheme locally of finite presentation over Y that the refinement amounts to

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst_of_affineSpaceTest
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM9, (3) implies (2).** If `f : X ⟶ Y` passes the affine-space test over one
surjective étale scheme atlas `V ⟶ Y` of the target, then the base change of `f` along every
morphism to `Y` which is locally of finite presentation is closed.

Closedness of `|Z ×_Y X| → |Z|` may be checked after the base change along the composite of an
étale atlas of `Z ×_Y V` with the projection to `Z`, which is open and surjective on points;
that composite exhibits the test object as a morphism of the site into `V` locally of finite
presentation, where the previous statement applies.

Quasi-compactness of `f` is not needed: it enters Tag 0CM9 only through the implication from
the finitely presented tests back to universal closedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst_of_affineSpaceTest
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y)
    (hgsurj : IsSurjective B S hS g) (hgetale : IsEtale B S hS g)
    (htest : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V), IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
      IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f))
    {Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (h : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hh : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h) :
    IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst h f)
declarations.comment: (3) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM9, (1) implies (2).** The base change of a universally closed morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` along a morphism which is locally of finite presentation is
closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst_of_universallyClosed (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f) {Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (h : Z ⟶ Y)
    (_hh : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h) :
    IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst h f)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineSpaceTest_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM9, (1) implies (3).** A universally closed morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` passes the affine-space test over every surjective étale scheme atlas of its target: each
affine space over the atlas is an object of the site mapping to the target, so the base change
of `f` along it is closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineSpaceTest_of_universallyClosed (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
      IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V), IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
          IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_of_isClosedMorphism_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM9, (2) implies (1).** A quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
whose base changes along the morphisms locally of finite presentation are closed is
universally closed.

Let `T ⊆ |X ×_Y Z|` be closed and let `z` be a point of `|Z|` outside the image of `T`. The
separation statement of Tag 0CM8 produces an étale neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `z`, a
factorization `V ⟶ Z' ⟶ Y` with `Z' ⟶ Y` locally of finite presentation, and a closed
`T' ⊆ |X ×_Y Z'|` receiving the inverse image of `T` and missing the image of `v`. Since
`|V| → |Z|` is open, `v` lies in the closure of the inverse image of the image of `T`, which
by Tag 03H4 is the image of the inverse image of `T` in `|X ×_Y V|`; that image lands in the
inverse image along `V ⟶ Z'` of the image of `T'`, a closed set by hypothesis. Hence the image
of `v` lies in the image of `T'` after all, so `z` is not in the closure of the image of
`T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_isClosedMorphism_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (htest : ∀ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z →
      ∀ h : Z ⟶ Y, IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h →
        IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst h f)) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CM9.** For a quasi-compact morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` the
following are equivalent: `f` is universally closed; the base change of `f` along every
morphism to `Y` which is locally of finite presentation is closed; and there is a surjective
étale morphism to `Y` from a presheaf represented by an object `V` of the site such that for
every `n` the base change of `f` along affine `n`-space over `V` is closed.

The implication from the second condition to the first is the one using quasi-compactness of
`f`, through the separation statement of Tag 0CM8.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompact (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
        ∀ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z →
          ∀ h : Z ⟶ Y, IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h →
            IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst h f),
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V),
              IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
                IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMA, (1) implies (2).** The base change of a proper morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` along a morphism which is locally of finite presentation is closed.

A proper morphism is universally closed, so this is the corresponding implication of Tag
0CM9.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst_of_isProper (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsProper B S hS f)
    {Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (h : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hh : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h) :
    IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst h f)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineSpaceTest_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMA, (1) implies (3).** A proper morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` passes the
affine-space test over a surjective étale scheme atlas of its target: for every `n` the base
change of `f` along affine `n`-space over the atlas is closed.

A proper morphism is universally closed, so this is the corresponding implication of Tag
0CM9.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineSpaceTest_of_isProper (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
      IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V), IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
          IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMA, (2) implies (1).** A separated morphism of finite type between algebraic
spaces over `S` whose base changes along the morphisms locally of finite presentation are
closed is proper.

Properness is separatedness, finite type and universal closedness; the first two are the
standing hypotheses and the third is supplied by Tag 0CM9, whose quasi-compactness hypothesis
is the second conjunct of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_isClosedMorphism_pullback_fst (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (htest : ∀ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z →
      ∀ h : Z ⟶ Y, IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h →
        IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst h f)) :
    IsProper B S hS f
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_affineSpaceTest
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMA, (3) implies (1).** A separated morphism of finite type between algebraic
spaces over `S` which passes the affine-space test over one surjective étale scheme atlas of
its target is proper.

The affine-space test gives closedness of the base changes along the morphisms locally of
finite presentation, by Tag 0CM9, and that in turn gives universal closedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_affineSpaceTest (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y)
    (hgsurj : IsSurjective B S hS g) (hgetale : IsEtale B S hS g)
    (htest : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V), IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
      IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f)) :
    IsProper B S hS f
declarations.comment: (3) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_tfae_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMA.** For a separated morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of finite type between algebraic
spaces over `S` the following are equivalent: `f` is proper; the base change of `f` along every
morphism to `Y` which is locally of finite presentation is closed; and there is a surjective
étale morphism to `Y` from a presheaf represented by an object `V` of the site such that for
every `n` the base change of `f` along affine `n`-space over `V` is closed.

This is the special case of Tag 0CM9 obtained by unfolding properness into separatedness,
finite type and universal closedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_tfae_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteType (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsProper B S hS f,
        ∀ (Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z →
          ∀ h : Z ⟶ Y, IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS h →
            IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst h f),
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (W : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : W ⟶ V),
              IsAffineSpaceOver B S hS V W n a ∧
                IsClosedMorphism B S hS (pullback.fst (yoneda.map a ≫ g) f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_discreteValuationSpecialization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMC.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of finite type of algebraic spaces over `S`,
with `Y` locally Noetherian, and let `y` be a point of `Y` in the closure of the image of the
points of `X`. Then there are a discrete valuation ring `A`, a field-valued point of `X` over its
fraction field `K`, a morphism `Spec K ⟶ Spec A` over `S` given by the inclusion `A → K`, and an
`A`-valued point of `Y` forming a commutative square with `f`, the closed point of `Spec A`
mapping to `y`. Moreover the point `x` of `X` given by `Spec K ⟶ X` is a codimension zero point;
it satisfies `f x ≠ y` as soon as `y` is in the closure of the set of `f x'` for the codimension
zero points `x'` of `X` with `f x' ≠ y`; and, when `f x ≠ y`, the morphism `Spec K ⟶ X` factors
as `Spec K ≅ Spec κ(u) ⟶ U ⟶ X` for a point `u` of a scheme `U` étale over `X`, so that `K` is
the residue field of `u`. The condition for `f x ≠ y` is also necessary: the square makes `y` a
specialization of `f x`, so an `x` with `f x ≠ y` is itself such an `x'`.

The residue-field clause is stated under `f x ≠ y` because the source's unconditional clause is
false. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_exists_discreteValuationSpecialization_residueField`
(in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.NoetherianValuativeCriterionCounterexample`), whose
statement is the conclusion of this theorem with the guard `f x ≠ y →` removed from the
residue-field clause (the clause guaranteeing `f x ≠ y` is left out, which only strengthens the
refutation):
```
¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : X ⟶ Y), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X →
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y → IsFiniteType B S hS f →
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) →
    ∀ y : points B S hS Y, y ∈ closure (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X f)) →
      ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing A)
        (K : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X) (_ : Algebra A K.carrier)
        (_ : IsFractionRing A K.carrier) (A_contained : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
        (s : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S) (j : K.siteObject ⟶ valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s)
        (g : yoneda.obj (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s) ⟶ Y),
        j.left.1 = Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K.carrier)).op ∧
        yoneda.map j ≫ g = yonedaEquiv.symm K.value ≫ f ∧
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s)) g
            ((schemePointRepresentative B S hS (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s)
                (⟨IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum A)).class B S hS
              (yoneda.obj (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s))) = y ∧
        localRingDimension B S hS (K.class B S hS X) = 0 ∧
        ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
          (u : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
          (e : K.carrier ≃+* ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).residueField u)
          (t : K.siteObject ⟶ U),
          IsEtale B S hS a ∧
            t.left.1 = Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom e.symm.toRingHom).op ≫
                ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).fromSpecResidueField u ∧
              a.app (Opposite.op K.siteObject) t = K.value
```
The witness is the identity of `X = Y = S = Spec k` for `k` the algebraic closure of `ℚ`: every
residue field of a scheme étale over `Spec k` is algebraically closed, being a separable
extension of `k`, while the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring is not, since a
uniformizer has no square root in it. The same proof gives the stronger
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_exists_etale_residueFieldEquiv`, in which `K` is only asked
to be abstractly isomorphic to such a residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_discreteValuationSpecialization {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (X_isAlgebraicSpace : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (Y_isAlgebraicSpace : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f_finiteType : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (Y_locallyNoetherian :
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (y : points B S hS Y) (y_mem_closure : y ∈ closure (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X f))) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing A)
      (K : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X) (_ : Algebra A K.carrier) (_ : IsFractionRing A K.carrier)
      (A_contained : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (s : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
      (j : K.siteObject ⟶ valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s)
      (g : yoneda.obj (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s) ⟶ Y),
      j.left.1 = Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K.carrier)).op ∧
      yoneda.map j ≫ g = yonedaEquiv.symm K.value ≫ f ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s)) g
          ((schemePointRepresentative B S hS (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s)
              (⟨IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum A)).class B S hS
            (yoneda.obj (valuationObject B S hS A A_contained s))) = y ∧
      localRingDimension B S hS (K.class B S hS X) = 0 ∧
      (y ∈ closure (pointsMap B S hS X f ''
          {x' | localRingDimension B S hS x' = 0 ∧ pointsMap B S hS X f x' ≠ y}) →
        pointsMap B S hS X f (K.class B S hS X) ≠ y) ∧
      (pointsMap B S hS X f (K.class B S hS X) ≠ y →
        ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X)
          (u : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
          (e : K.carrier ≃+* ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).residueField u)
          (t : K.siteObject ⟶ U),
          IsEtale B S hS a ∧
            t.left.1 = Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom e.symm.toRingHom).op ≫
                ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).fromSpecResidueField u ∧
              a.app (Opposite.op K.siteObject) t = K.value)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_denseRange_of_exists_discreteLift
registrations.comment:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `h : U ⟶ X` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, with
  `Y` locally Noetherian, `f` and `h` of finite type, `f` separated and the image of
  `|h| : |U| → |X|` dense in `|X|`. If every commutative valuative diagram for `f` over a discrete
  valuation ring whose generic arrow factors through `h` has a dotted arrow, then `f` is proper.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_denseRange_of_subsingleton_discreteLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CME.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `h : U ⟶ X` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
with `Y` locally Noetherian, `f` locally of finite type and quasi-separated, `h` of finite type
and the image of `|h| : |U| → |X|` dense in `|X|`. If every commutative valuative diagram for `f`
over a discrete valuation ring `A` with fraction field `K` whose generic arrow `Spec K ⟶ X`
factors through `h` has at most one dotted arrow `Spec A ⟶ X`, then `f` is separated.

The relative diagonal of `f` is representable, a monomorphism, separated, locally of finite type,
and quasi-compact because `f` is quasi-separated. Its base change `V ⟶ C` along an étale chart
`C` of the locally Noetherian algebraic space `X ×_Y X` (Stacks 04ZK) is therefore a
quasi-compact monomorphism of schemes locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian scheme,
and it satisfies condition (4) of Stacks 0208: at a generic point of `V` a dotted arrow exists by
`nonempty_liftStruct_of_denseRange`, and it is unique since `V ⟶ C` is a monomorphism. So
`V ⟶ C` is proper (Stacks 0208), hence a closed immersion (Stacks 04XV), and being a closed
immersion descends from the chart to the diagonal (Stacks 02L6, 02WZ).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_denseRange_of_subsingleton_discreteLift
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U) (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : U ⟶ X)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hh : IsFiniteType B S hS h)
    (hdense : @DenseRange _ (pointTopology B S hS X) _ (pointsMap B S hS U h))
    (hvaluative : ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
      ∀ g : yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.field_mem
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap q.R q.K)) ≫ q.base)) ⟶ U,
        g ≫ h = q.generic → Subsingleton q.Lift) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_of_denseRange_of_unique_discreteLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMF.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `h : U ⟶ X` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
with `Y` locally Noetherian, `f` and `h` of finite type, `f` quasi-separated and the image of
`|h| : |U| → |X|` dense in `|X|`. If every commutative valuative diagram for `f` over a discrete
valuation ring `A` with fraction field `K` whose generic arrow `Spec K ⟶ X` factors through `h`
has exactly one dotted arrow `Spec A ⟶ X`, then `f` is proper.

As in the source this combines Stacks 0CME, which gives separatedness of `f` from the uniqueness
of the dotted arrows, with Stacks 0CMD, which gives properness from their existence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_denseRange_of_unique_discreteLift
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U) (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : U ⟶ X)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hh : IsFiniteType B S hS h) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hdense : @DenseRange _ (pointTopology B S hS X) _ (pointsMap B S hS U h))
    (hvaluative : ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, IsDiscreteValuationRing q.R →
      ∀ g : yoneda.obj (siteObject B S hS q.field_mem
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap q.R q.K)) ≫ q.base)) ⟶ U,
        g ≫ h = q.generic → Nonempty q.Lift ∧ Subsingleton q.Lift) :
    IsProper B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMG, first assertion.** The relative diagonal of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks
over `S` which is locally of finite type is locally of finite presentation.

The first projection of the 2-fibre product undoes the diagonal, is a base change of `f` and is
therefore locally of finite type by Stacks 06FU, so Stacks 06Q6 cancels it against the identity
of `𝒳`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeDiagonal
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (relativeDiagonal B S hS f)
declarations.comment: locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFinitePresentation_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMG, second assertion.** The relative diagonal of a quasi-separated 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` which is locally of finite type is of finite presentation.

Local finite presentation is the first assertion; quasi-compactness of the diagonal is part (2)
of Stacks 04Z0 read off quasi-separatedness of `f`; and quasi-separatedness of the diagonal is
Section 04XB quasi-compactness of the second diagonal, which is part (2) of Stacks 04YZ at the
same hypothesis, together with Section 04XB quasi-separatedness of the second diagonal, which is
unconditional by part (4) of Stacks 04YQ and Stacks 03KK.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitePresentation_relativeDiagonal
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsFinitePresentation B S hS (relativeDiagonal B S hS f)
declarations.comment: finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsSchemeTheoreticImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMI.** A property of the objects of `𝒴` is *the scheme theoretic image* of a
1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` when it cuts out a closed substack of `𝒴`
through which `f` factors, and is contained in every closed substack of `𝒴` through which `f`
factors.
declarations.statement:
def IsSchemeTheoreticImage {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSchemeTheoreticImage_comp_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMJ**, the existence assertion. Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks over `S` and let `g : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳` be a surjective, flat 1-morphism locally of finite
presentation. Then the scheme theoretic image of `f` exists if and only if the scheme theoretic
image of `g ≫ f` exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSchemeTheoreticImage_comp_iff {𝒲 𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hlfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g) :
    HasSchemeTheoreticImage f ↔ HasSchemeTheoreticImage (g ≫ f)
declarations.comment: existence_iff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.eq_of_isSchemeTheoreticImage_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMJ**, the agreement of the two images. Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S` and let `g : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳` be a surjective, flat 1-morphism locally of finite
presentation. If `P` is the scheme theoretic image of `f` and `Q` is the scheme theoretic image of
`g ≫ f`, then `P = Q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_isSchemeTheoreticImage_comp {𝒲 𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒲 ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hlfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    {P Q : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f P)
    (hQ : IsSchemeTheoreticImage (g ≫ f) Q) : P = Q
declarations.comment: images_equal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_le_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**The easy containment of Stacks 0CMK, for any 2-commutative square.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and
`b : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` and let `sq` be a 2-commutative square
over them, with
apex `sq.pt` and legs `sq.fst : sq.pt ⟶ 𝒴'` and `sq.snd : sq.pt ⟶ 𝒳`. Then the intersection of
the closed substacks of `𝒴'` through which `sq.fst` factors is contained in the preimage under
`b` of the intersection of the closed substacks of `𝒴` through which `f` factors.

Let `Q` be a closed substack of `𝒴` through which `f` factors. Its preimage under `b` is a closed
substack of `𝒴'` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedSubstack_inverseImage`) through which `sq.fst`
factors (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorsThroughSubstack_inverseImage`, which is where the
2-commutativity of the square is used), so the candidate image of `sq.fst` is contained in it by
its own minimality. As `Q` ranges over the closed substacks of `𝒴` through which `f` factors this
says exactly that an object of the candidate image of `sq.fst` has its image under `b` in the
candidate image of `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_le_inverseImage (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (b : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (sq : Bicategory.TwoCommSq b f) :
    schemeTheoreticImageCandidate sq.fst ≤
      (schemeTheoreticImageCandidate f).inverseImage b.hom.hom.toFunctor
declarations.comment: containment

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_inverseImage_fullSubcategoryInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMK for the inclusion of a closed substack.** Let `P` cut out a closed substack of
`𝒴₂` and let `b : 𝒴₁ ⟶ 𝒴₂` be any 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. The base change of the
inclusion of that substack along `b` is the inclusion of the preimage of `P`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inverseImageSquare_fst`, and the square realising it is a 2-fibre product
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_inverseImageSquare`. Then the scheme theoretic image
of that base change is the preimage under `b` of the scheme theoretic image of the inclusion.

Both sides are computed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_fullSubcategoryInclusion`: a closed
substack is the scheme theoretic image of its own inclusion, and the preimage of a closed substack
is a closed substack. Neither flatness of `b` nor quasi-compactness of the inclusion is used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_inverseImage_fullSubcategoryInclusion
    {𝒴₁ 𝒴₂ : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (b : 𝒴₁ ⟶ 𝒴₂)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒴₂.val.val.obj} [P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
    (hP : IsClosedSubstack 𝒴₂ P)
    (hPalg : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased 𝒴₂ P)) :
    schemeTheoreticImageCandidate (inverseImageSquare b P hPalg).fst =
      (schemeTheoreticImageCandidate (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒴₂ P hPalg)).inverseImage
        b.hom.hom.toFunctor
declarations.comment: closed_substack_case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSchemeTheoreticImage_inverseImage_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMK.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`
and let `b : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` be a flat 1-morphism. Then formation of the scheme theoretic image commutes
with the base change along `b`: if `P` is the scheme theoretic image of `f`, then its inverse
image under `b` is the scheme theoretic image of the base change
`f' : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴'` (the first projection of the canonical 2-fibre product square).

The containment of the image of `f'` in the inverse image of `P` holds for any square
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_le_inverseImage`). For the converse, the
flat-local image of `f` — the closed substack of `𝒴` cut out by the scheme theoretic images of
the base changes of `f` to the smooth affine charts of `𝒴`, which descend by the invariance of
the proof of Stacks 0CMK
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.chartImageSubfunctor_le_chartSubfunctor_flatLocalImage`) — is a closed
substack through which `f` factors, so it contains `P`, and its inverse image under `b` lies in
the image of `f'` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inverseImage_flatLocalImage_le`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticImage_inverseImage_of_isFlat (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (b : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (hb : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS b)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f P) :
    IsSchemeTheoreticImage (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS b f).fst
      (P.inverseImage b.hom.hom.toFunctor)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.range_pointsMap_eq_closure_of_isSchemeTheoreticImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CML.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`
and let `P` cut out its scheme theoretic image `𝒵 ⊆ 𝒴` (Stacks 0CMI). Then the points of `𝒵` are
the closure in `|𝒴|` of the image of `|f|`.

The closure lies in `|𝒵|` for any `f`: `f` factors through `𝒵`, whose points are closed by
**Stacks 0H20**. Conversely, let `z` be a point of `𝒵`, and choose a smooth chart
`v : (Sch/V)_fppf ⟶ 𝒴` with `V` affine through its image, and a point `η` of `V` over it. The
point `(z, η)` lifts to `𝒵 ×_𝒴 V` (**Stacks 04XH**), so `η` comes from a field-valued point
`t : Spec K ⟶ V` at which `P` holds. As `f` is quasi-compact, `𝒳 ×_𝒴 V` is quasi-compact and has
a smooth surjective presentation by an affine `A`, with composite `g : A ⟶ V`. The scheme
theoretic image of `f` lies in the closed substack cut out by the scheme theoretic images of the
base changes of `f` to the smooth affine charts (the descent of the proof of **Stacks 0CMK**), and
that image along `v` lies in the scheme theoretic image of `g` (**Stacks 0CMJ**, in the form of
Stacks 06QA). So `t` factors through the scheme theoretic image of the quasi-compact `g`, and `η`
lies in the closure of the image of `g` (**Stacks 082Z**, read on schemes). The map
`|V| ⟶ |𝒴|` is continuous and carries the image of `g` into the image of `|f|`, the square
`A ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 V` commuting, so it carries `η` into the closure of the image of `|f|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_eq_closure_of_isSchemeTheoreticImage
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f P) :
    Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS
        (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒴 P hP.isAlgebraicStack)) =
      @closure _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
        (Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMR.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of categories fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf category of `S` is *limit preserving* when, for every cofiltered inverse system of affine
schemes over `S` whose image in schemes has a limiting cone, the canonical square

`colim 𝒳_{Uᵢ} ⟶ 𝒳_U`, `colim 𝒴_{Uᵢ} ⟶ 𝒴_U`

of fibre categories, with vertical maps induced by `f`, is a 2-fibre product.

The square is the determinate one: the vertical map out of the colimit is the colimit of the
componentwise maps `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.splitFiberMap` of strict split fibres, and the
filling 2-cell is, on every colimit generator, the canonical base-change comparison of the
fibred 1-morphism underlying `f`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLimitPreserving (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreservingOnObjects_of_isLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMS.** A limit preserving 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf category of `S` is limit preserving on objects: every object over an affine inverse limit,
with a cartesian comparison to an object at a finite stage, descends to a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreservingOnObjects_of_isLimitPreserving
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, vX, u + 1, uX}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS f) :
    BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, v, w, vX, uX}
      B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreserving_twoFibreProductSnd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMT.** The base change `p' : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵` of a limit preserving 1-morphism `p` of
categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of a scheme `S` is limit preserving.

Both conditions are properties of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.canonicalSquare` -- of `p'` for the
conclusion and of `p` for the hypothesis -- by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreserving_iff_isTwoFibreProduct_canonicalSquare`, and the two
squares are 2-cartesian together by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_squareComparison_canonicalSquare_twoFibreProductSnd`. The
input the source leaves implicit is that filtered colimits of categories commute with 2-fibre
products, which is what identifies `colim (𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵)_{Uᵢ}` with
`colim 𝒳_{Uᵢ} ×_{colim 𝒴_{Uᵢ}} colim 𝒵_{Uᵢ}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_twoFibreProductSnd
    (hp : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, max (u + 1) v w, max u v} B S hS p) :
    IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, max (u + 1) v w, max u v} B S hS
      (BigFppfOver.twoFibreProductSnd.{u, v, w} B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 p q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreservingOnObjects_twoFibreProductSnd
declarations.doc:
The base change along `q` of a limit preserving 1-morphism `p` of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of `S` is limit preserving on objects: every object of
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒵` over an affine inverse limit, with a cartesian comparison to an object of `𝒵` at a
finite stage, descends to a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreservingOnObjects_twoFibreProductSnd
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, max u v, u + 1, max (u + 1) v w}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (q : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hp : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, max (u + 1) v w, max u v} B S hS p) :
    BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, v, w} B S hS
      (BigFppfOver.twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 p q) 𝒵
      (BigFppfOver.twoFibreProductSnd B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 p q)
declarations.comment: limit preservation on objects of the base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreserving_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMU.** The composite of two limit preserving 1-morphisms of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of `S` is limit preserving: the square of Stacks 0CMR for
the composite is the horizontal pasting of the two given 2-cartesian squares.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, vX, u + 1, uX} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (p : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (q : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hp : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS p)
    (hq : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS q) :
    IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS (p ≫ q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreservingOnObjects_of_isLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMS.** A limit preserving 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf category of `S` is limit preserving on objects: every object over an affine inverse limit,
with a cartesian comparison to an object at a finite stage, descends to a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreservingOnObjects_of_isLimitPreserving
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, vX, u + 1, uX}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS)} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS f) :
    BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, v, w, vX, uX}
      B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f
declarations.comment: the implication (1) ⇒ (2), which holds here without the representability hypothesis that Tag 0CMV carries, and for index categories in any universe. The whole three-part equivalence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreserving_tfae`, for index categories in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreserving_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMV.** For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of categories fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf category of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces the following are equivalent:
`f` is limit preserving (Stacks 0CMR); `f` is limit preserving on objects (Stacks 06CU); and `f`
is locally of finite presentation in the sense of Stacks 03YK, that is, every algebraic space
representing a base change of `f` along a scheme-valued point of `𝒴` has locally finitely
presented structural morphism.

All three conditions are read for index categories in the universe of the schemes; see the
implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_tfae (hp : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS f,
       BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, u, u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f,
       ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
         (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ 𝒴.val.obj)
         (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒴.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
         (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
         (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
         Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
           (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒳.val.p 𝒴.val.p y
             (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f))
           (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
         Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
           (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
             ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj
