               ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom]
declarations.comment: index categories in the universe of the schemes

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreservingOnObjects_iff_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
registrations.comment: the equivalence of (2) and (3), which is Stacks 06CX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits_iff_isEquivalence_squareDiagonalComparison
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of Stacks 0CMW is the diagonal of the canonical square being an
equivalence.** The canonical functor `colim 𝒳_{Uᵢ} ⟶ 𝒳_U ×_{𝒴_U} colim 𝒴_{Uᵢ}` is fully faithful
at every directed limit of affine schemes over `S` exactly when, at every such limit, the
comparison of the square of relative diagonals of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.canonicalSquare` is an
equivalence.

This is the half of Stacks 0CMW that does not involve the diagonal 1-morphism
`Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳`: it is the category-theoretic criterion of the source's proof, applied to the
determinate square of Stacks 0CMR.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits_iff_isEquivalence_squareDiagonalComparison (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS f ↔
      ∀ (I : Type v) [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I]
        (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS) (c : Cone D),
        IsLimit ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).mapCone c) →
        (Cat.squareDiagonalComparison
          (canonicalSquare.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS f (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS)
            ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).mapCone c))).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: condition (2) as the diagonal of the canonical 0CMR square being an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits_of_isLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMW, condition (2) for a limit preserving 1-morphism.** If the square of
Stacks 0CMR is 2-cartesian then its comparison functor into the explicit 2-fibre product is an
equivalence, so the canonical functor `colim 𝒳_{Uᵢ} ⟶ 𝒳_U ×_{𝒴_U} colim 𝒴_{Uᵢ}` is fully
faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits_of_isLimitPreserving (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS f) :
    IsFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits.{u, v, w, uX, vX} B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (2) holds for a limit preserving 1-morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreserving_twoFibreProductDiagonal_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMW.** The relative diagonal `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_{f, 𝒴, f} 𝒳` of a 1-morphism of
categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of `S` is limit preserving if and only
if, at every directed limit `U = lim Uᵢ` of affine schemes over `S`, the canonical functor
`colim 𝒳_{Uᵢ} ⟶ 𝒳_U ×_{𝒴_U} colim 𝒴_{Uᵢ}` is fully faithful.

Both sides are properties of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.canonicalSquare` -- of `Δ` on the left, of
`f` on the right -- and the two squares are equivalent, so the source's criterion
`CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.fullyFaithful_squareComparison_iff` transfers between
them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_twoFibreProductDiagonal_iff :
    IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, max (u + 1) v w, max u v} B S hS
        (BigFppfOver.twoFibreProductDiagonal.{u, v, w} B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f) ↔
      IsFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits.{u, v, w, max (u + 1) v w, max u v} B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitPreserving_twoFibreProductDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMW, the "in particular" clause.** A limit preserving 1-morphism of categories
fibred in groupoids has a limit preserving relative diagonal: it satisfies the full faithfulness
condition by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isFullyFaithfulOnAffineLimits_of_isLimitPreserving`, and that condition
is limit preservation of the diagonal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_twoFibreProductDiagonal
    (hf : IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, max (u + 1) v w, max u v} B S hS f) :
    IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, max (u + 1) v w, max u v} B S hS
      (BigFppfOver.twoFibreProductDiagonal.{u, v, w} B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 f)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.CategoricalPullback.fullyFaithful_squareComparison_iff
declarations.doc:
**The category-theoretic core of Stacks 0CMW.** For a 2-commutative square of categories
whose corners `C` and `D'` are groupoids, the comparison functor `A : C' ⥤ C ×_D D'` is fully
faithful if and only if the comparison functor `B : C' ⥤ C ×_{Δ_p, C ×_D C} (C' ×_{D'} C')` of
the square of relative diagonals is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_squareComparison_iff [IsGroupoid C] [IsGroupoid D'] :
    ((squareComparison a u p b α).Full ∧ (squareComparison a u p b α).Faithful) ↔
      (diagonalComparison a u p b α).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the category-theoretic reduction of the equivalence (1) <=> (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLimitPreserving_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CMX.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` whose structure morphism `𝒳 → S` is
locally of finite presentation. Then `𝒳` is limit preserving in the sense of Artin's Axioms,
Definition 07XL: for every cofiltered system of affine schemes `Tᵢ` over `S` with limit `T`, the
comparison functor `colim 𝒳_{Tᵢ} ⥤ 𝒳_T` is an equivalence. Equivalently, the structure morphism
`𝒳 → S` is limit preserving in the sense of Stacks 0CMR. The index categories are taken in the
scheme universe, which is the smallness the source's directed sets have.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒳)) :
    Deformation.Artin.IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS 𝒳.val ∧
      Stack.IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒳).hom
declarations.comment: an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over S is limit preserving, and so is its structure morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_relativelyLimitPreserving_structure
declarations.doc:
**An algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over its base has a relatively limit
preserving smooth presentation.** This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_relativelyLimitPreserving` at the
structure morphism of Stacks 050D, and it is the algebraic-spaces input to the proof of
Stacks 0CMX: the presenting algebraic space of `𝒳` is relatively limit preserving over the
algebraic stack represented by `S`.

The attribute's clause string is deliberately narrow. This statement does **not** give the
conclusion of Stacks 0CMX, which is limit preservation of `𝒳` in the sense of Definition 07XL;
what it carries is the tag's first step, and it is the step that consumes the tag's hypothesis —
`Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation` on the structure morphism of Stacks 050D is
used, not merely stated. Anyone reading the tag as discharged by this declaration would be
misreading it: the conclusion here is about a smooth presentation by an algebraic space, in the
vocabulary of Stacks 049J, and the remaining step — limit preservation of the quotient stack — is
named with its three missing bridges in the implementation notes of this module.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram_relativelyLimitPreserving_structure
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒳)) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS
      (fun _ _ h => RelativelyLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} B S hS h)
      (structureMorphism B S hS 𝒳).hom
declarations.comment: only the smooth-diagram reduction; the conclusion is not 07XL

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLimitPreserving_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitPreserving_tfae {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    List.TFAE [Stack.IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS f.hom,
      BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, u, u} B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom,
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f]
declarations.comment: limit preserving, limit preserving on objects and locally of finite presentation are equivalent for a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isLimitPreservingOnObjects
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is limit preserving on objects, at index
categories in the universe `u` of the schemes, is locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isLimitPreservingOnObjects
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, u, u, u, u + 1}
      B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒴.val f.hom) :
    Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f
declarations.comment: the implication (2) => (3) only

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.isEquivalence_overPost
declarations.doc:
For `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` fibred in groupoids and `x` an object of `𝒳`, the functor
`Over.post p : 𝒳/x ⥤ 𝒞/p x` induced by `p` is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.isEquivalence_overPost (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (x : 𝒳) :
    (Over.post (X := x) p).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence of categories 𝒳/x ⥤ 𝒞/U

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsInheritedTopology.mem_over_iff_functorPushforward
declarations.doc:
For `p` fibred in groupoids and `J𝒳` inherited from `(𝒞, J)`, a sieve on an object of `𝒳/x` is
covering for the topology that `J𝒳` induces on `𝒳/x` exactly when its image under `Over.post p` is
covering for the topology that `J` induces on `𝒞/p x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsInheritedTopology.mem_over_iff_functorPushforward (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    {J : GrothendieckTopology 𝒞} {J𝒳 : GrothendieckTopology 𝒳}
    (hJ : _root_.CategoryTheory.Functor.IsInheritedTopology.{max u₂ v₂} p J J𝒳)
    {x : 𝒳} (Y : Over x) (S : Sieve Y) :
    S ∈ (J𝒳.over x) Y ↔
      Sieve.functorPushforward (Over.post p) S ∈
        (J.over (p.obj x)) ((Over.post (X := x) p).obj Y)
declarations.comment: coverings of x' in 𝒳/x correspond to coverings of p x' in 𝒞/U

declarations.statement:
instance {α : Type*} [Preorder α] :
    (toAntisymmetrization_mono (α := α)).functor.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
Every preorder is equivalent to its partial order quotient. In particular, they
  are equivalent for the purpose of computing limits and colimits.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.isDirected_antisymmetrization
declarations.doc: If `I` is directed, so is its antisymmetrization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDirected_antisymmetrization [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] :
    IsDirected (Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·)) (· ≤ ·)
declarations.comment: If `I` is directed, so is its partial order quotient.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.pullbackSystemFunctor
declarations.doc:
The pullback of systems over the antisymmetrization `Ī = Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·)` to
systems over `I`, along the quotient functor induced by `toAntisymmetrization`.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackSystemFunctor :
    (Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·) ⥤ C) ⥤ (I ⥤ C)
declarations.comment: The functor from systems over `Ī` to systems over `I`, `N ↦ (N_{π(i)})`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.systemEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between systems over the antisymmetrization of `I` and systems over `I`:
every system over `I` descends, uniquely up to canonical isomorphism, to a system over the
antisymmetrization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def systemEquivalence :
    (Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·) ⥤ C) ≌ (I ⥤ C)
declarations.comment: The functor from systems over `Ī` to systems over `I` is an equivalence.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.inverseSystemEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between inverse systems over the antisymmetrization of `I` and inverse
systems over `I`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseSystemEquivalence :
    ((Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·))ᵒᵖ ⥤ C) ≌ (Iᵒᵖ ⥤ C)
declarations.comment: The analogous equivalence for inverse systems.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasColimit_iff_hasColimit_of_systemEquivalence
declarations.doc: A system `N` over `Ī` has a colimit if and only if its pullback to `I` has a colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimit_iff_hasColimit_of_systemEquivalence
    (N : Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·) ⥤ C) :
    HasColimit N ↔ HasColimit ((pullbackSystemFunctor I C).obj N)
declarations.comment: Compatibility of the equivalence with colimits of systems.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.colimitPullbackSystemIso
declarations.doc: The colimit of the pullback of a system `N` over `Ī` to `I` is the colimit of `N`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colimitPullbackSystemIso (N : Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·) ⥤ C)
    [HasColimit N] :
    colimit ((toAntisymmetrization_mono (α := I)).functor ⋙ N) ≅ colimit N
declarations.comment: The colimits of related systems agree.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasLimit_iff_hasLimit_of_inverseSystemEquivalence
declarations.doc: An inverse system `N` over `Ī` has a limit if and only if its pullback to `I` has a limit.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLimit_iff_hasLimit_of_inverseSystemEquivalence
    (N : (Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·))ᵒᵖ ⥤ C) :
    HasLimit N ↔ HasLimit ((inverseSystemEquivalence I C).functor.obj N)
declarations.comment: Compatibility of the equivalence with limits of inverse systems.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.limitInverseSystemIso
declarations.doc: The limit of the pullback of an inverse system `N` over `Ī` to `I` is the limit of `N`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def limitInverseSystemIso (N : (Antisymmetrization I (· ≤ ·))ᵒᵖ ⥤ C)
    [HasLimit N] :
    limit ((toAntisymmetrization_mono (α := I)).functor.op ⋙ N) ≅ limit N
declarations.comment: The limits of related inverse systems agree.

registrations.name: Antisymmetrization
registrations.comment: The partial order quotient of a preorder.

registrations.name: preordToPartOrd
registrations.comment: The partial order quotient construction as a functor.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.exists_isSmooth_mapAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN2.** In the situation of Stacks 084W, if the base change `f` of `f₀` to the
limit `B` is smooth and `f₀` is locally of finite presentation, then the base change `f_i` of
`f₀` to some stage `B_i` is smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSmooth_mapAt (D : MorphismDescentSystem B S hS hZ I)
    (smooth : IsSmooth B S hS D.mapLimit) (fp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (i : I) (le : D.initial ≤ i), IsSmooth B S hS (D.mapAt i le)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.exists_isSmooth_mapAt_op
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN2 in the covariant indexing of Stacks 07SK.** In the situation of Stacks 084W, if
the base change `f` of `f₀` to the limit `B` is smooth and `f₀` is locally of finite presentation,
then there is a morphism `j ⟶ 0` of the cofiltered index category `Iᵒᵖ` along which the base
change of `f₀` is smooth.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.exists_isSmooth_mapAt` with its conclusion
read over a morphism of `Iᵒᵖ` instead of an inequality of `I`; the transition morphism is the same
one, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.MorphismDescentSystem.base_map_eq_baseAtToInitial`. It is the
shape in which the conclusions of Stacks 07SK are stated, so the two can be used together.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSmooth_mapAt_op (D : MorphismDescentSystem B S hS hZ I)
    (smooth : IsSmooth B S hS D.mapLimit) (fp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.map₀) :
    ∃ (j : Iᵒᵖ) (g : j ⟶ op D.initial),
      IsSmooth B S hS (D.mapAt j.unop (leOfHom g.unop))
declarations.comment: the cofiltered-covariant form: the conclusion ranges over a morphism of the cofiltered index category Iᵒᵖ carrying the covariant diagram `base`, which is the indexing the library's Stacks 07SK consumes, rather than over an inequality of the directed preorder I; the mathematical content is that of the inequality form beside it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.StackDescentSystem.exists_stage_model_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN4.** Let `(X_i)` be a directed inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated
algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms, and let `X = lim X_i`. If `𝒳` is an
algebraic stack of finite presentation over `X`, then there are a stage `i` and an algebraic
stack `𝒳_i` of finite presentation over `X_i` with `𝒳 ≅ 𝒳_i ×_{X_i} X` as algebraic stacks
over `X`.

Five inputs are carried as explicit hypotheses — `hPresentation`, `hDescent`,
`hStageStackModel`, `hModelFinitePresentation` and `hModelComparison`. None is a restatement of
this conclusion, and `hStageStackModel` is a universe-lifting datum rather than a mathematical
assumption. The module's implementation notes say what each one is, which declaration of the library it
would come from, and — for Stacks 0CN2 — exactly why the existing result falls short. What is
discharged here is Stacks 07SF for the limit with its quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness, the essential-surjectivity clause of Stacks 07SK for the object and arrow
spaces of the presenting groupoid, Stacks 04TK on the descended groupoid, and the assembly of the
conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_stage_model_of_isFinitePresentation
    (hPresentation : GroupoidPresentationOfAffineSmoothChart.{u, w} B S hS hZ)
    (hDescent : C.GroupoidStructureDescendsToStage)
    (hStageStackModel : C.StageStackModel.{u, w})
    (hModelFinitePresentation : C.ModelIsFinitePresentation.{u, w})
    (hModelComparison : C.ModelBaseChangeComparison.{u, w})
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ C.limitStack.{u, w})
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ (i : Iᵒᵖ) (𝒳ᵢ : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (fᵢ : 𝒳ᵢ ⟶ C.stageStack.{u, w} i),
      AlgebraicStacks.IsFinitePresentation B S hS fᵢ ∧
        ∃ e : Bicategory.Equivalence 𝒳
          (twoFibreProductAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS fᵢ
            (C.limitStackProjection.{u, w} i)),
          Nonempty (e.hom ≫ (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS fᵢ
            (C.limitStackProjection.{u, w} i)).snd ≅ f)
declarations.comment: a reduction, not a proof: inputs of the source's proof are carried as the explicit hypotheses hPresentation (Stacks 04T4 (4), (5), Stacks 04T5 (2) and the 050K/050H bookkeeping, with Stacks 04YC discharged), hDescent (what is left of Stacks 07SK and 0CN2 on a groupoid object once the essential-surjectivity clause is discharged: the descent of s, t, c, the pointwiseGroupoid field, the common stage, and Stacks 046Q), hStageStackModel (a universe-lifting datum, not a mathematical assumption: a quotient stack has hom universe one above that of AlgebraicStacks), hModelFinitePresentation (Stacks 06Q2 evaluated on a quotient stack) and hModelComparison (Stacks 044P, 044R, 046Q and 04Y1 for a base-changed groupoid); what is discharged here is Stacks 07SF for the limit with its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, the essential-surjectivity clause of Stacks 07SK for the object and arrow spaces of the presenting groupoid, Stacks 04TK on the descended groupoid, and the assembly of the conclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.StackDescentSystem.exists_stage_model_of_isFinitePresentation_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN4.** Let `(X_i)` be a directed inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated
algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms, and let `X = lim X_i`. If `𝒳` is an
algebraic stack of finite presentation over `X`, then there are a stage `i` and an algebraic
stack `𝒳_i` of finite presentation over `X_i` with `𝒳 ≅ 𝒳_i ×_{X_i} X` as algebraic stacks
over `X`.

This is the statement of `StackDescentSystem.exists_stage_model_of_isFinitePresentation` with
none of its hypotheses. The system satisfies the chapter's convention
(`StackDescentSystem.siteContainsBaseChangeLimits`), and under the convention the statement is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.finitePresentationStackDescendsStatement_holds`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_stage_model_of_isFinitePresentation_unconditional
    (C : StackDescentSystem B S hS hZ I)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ C.limitStack.{u, w})
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ (i : Iᵒᵖ) (𝒳ᵢ : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (fᵢ : 𝒳ᵢ ⟶ C.stageStack.{u, w} i),
      AlgebraicStacks.IsFinitePresentation B S hS fᵢ ∧
        ∃ e : Bicategory.Equivalence 𝒳
          (twoFibreProductAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS fᵢ
            (C.limitStackProjection.{u, w} i)),
          Nonempty (e.hom ≫ (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS fᵢ
            (C.limitStackProjection.{u, w} i)).snd ≅ f)
declarations.comment: The directed set `I` indexes the system as a covariant diagram on the cofiltered category `Iᵒᵖ`, and `StackDescentSystem` bounds the cardinality of `Iᵒᵖ` and of its hom types by the cofinality of the cutoff of the big fppf site, which is what keeps the limit `X` inside the site. The isomorphism `𝒳 ≅ 𝒳_i ×_{X_i} X` over `X` is an equivalence in the 2-category of algebraic stacks whose forward 1-morphism followed by the projection to `X` is 2-isomorphic to the structure 1-morphism of `𝒳`.

declarations.name: exists_mem_associatedPrimes_quotSMulTop_pow_of_mem_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**A minimal prime over `𝔭 + (x)` is an associated prime of `M/xⁿM`.** Let `R` be a
Noetherian ring, `M` a finite `R`-module and `x ∈ R`. If `𝔭` is an associated prime of `M` and
`𝔮` is a minimal prime over `𝔭 + (x)`, then `𝔮` is an associated prime of `M/xⁿM` for some
`n ≥ 1`.

The source states this for `x` in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring; neither
restriction is used, and `x ∉ 𝔪` makes `𝔭 + (x) = ⊤`, which has no minimal primes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mem_associatedPrimes_quotSMulTop_pow_of_mem_minimalPrimes {R : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] (x : R) {p q : Ideal R} (hp : p ∈ associatedPrimes R M)
    (hq : q ∈ (p + Ideal.span {x}).minimalPrimes) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ q ∈ associatedPrimes R (QuotSMulTop (x ^ n) M)
declarations.comment: Stated over an arbitrary Noetherian ring for an arbitrary `x`: the source's locality is unused, and `x ∈ 𝔪` is implied to the extent it matters by `𝔮` being a minimal prime over `𝔭 + (x)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_specMap_subalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN7.** If the morphism on spectra associated to an algebra is universally closed,
the same holds for the morphism associated to any subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyClosed_specMap_subalgebra
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (B' : Subalgebra A B)
    [UniversallyClosed (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)))] :
    UniversallyClosed (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B')))
declarations.comment: universally_closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_specMap_subalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN7.** Universal injectivity of the map on spectra passes from an algebra to any
of its subalgebras, provided the original map is universally closed and universally
injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyInjective_specMap_subalgebra
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [UniversallyClosed (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)]
    [UniversallyInjective (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)]
    (B' : Subalgebra A B) :
    UniversallyInjective (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B')).op)
declarations.comment: universally_closed_and_injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universalHomeomorphism_specMap_subalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN7.** If the map on spectra of an algebra is a universal homeomorphism, then so
is the map on spectra of any intermediate subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma universalHomeomorphism_specMap_subalgebra
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)]
    (B' : Subalgebra A B) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B')).op)
declarations.comment: universal_homeomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_residueFieldMap_specMap_subalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN7.** If a universal homeomorphism between affine spectra induces isomorphisms
on residue fields, then so does the map associated to any intermediate subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_residueFieldMap_specMap_subalgebra
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op)]
    (hres : ∀ x : Spec (.of B),
      IsIso ((Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op).residueFieldMap x))
    (B' : Subalgebra A B) :
    ∀ x : Spec (.of B'),
      IsIso ((Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B')).op).residueFieldMap x)
declarations.comment: universal_homeomorphism_residue_fields

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_specMap_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN8.** A filtered colimit of commutative `A`-algebras whose spectrum morphisms to
`Spec A` are universally closed again has universally closed spectrum morphism to `Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyClosed_specMap_of_isColimit
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J] [IsFiltered J]
    (F : Functor J (CommAlgCat.{u} A)) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (h : ∀ j, UniversallyClosed
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (F.obj j))).op)) :
    UniversallyClosed
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A c.pt)).op)
declarations.comment: universally_closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_specMap_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN8.** A filtered colimit of commutative `A`-algebras whose spectrum morphisms to
`Spec A` are universally injective again has universally injective spectrum morphism to
`Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyInjective_specMap_of_isColimit
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J] [IsFiltered J]
    (F : Functor J (CommAlgCat.{u} A)) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (h : ∀ j, UniversallyInjective
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (F.obj j))).op)) :
    UniversallyInjective
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A c.pt)).op)
declarations.comment: closed_injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universalHomeomorphism_specMap_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN8.** A filtered colimit of commutative `A`-algebras whose spectrum morphisms to
`Spec A` are universal homeomorphisms again has universal-homeomorphic spectrum morphism to
`Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma universalHomeomorphism_specMap_of_isColimit
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J] [IsFiltered J]
    (F : Functor J (CommAlgCat.{u} A)) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (h : ∀ j, UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (F.obj j))).op)) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A c.pt)).op)
declarations.comment: universal_homeomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_residueFieldMap_specMap_of_colimitPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN8.** A filtered colimit of affine maps which induce isomorphisms on residue
fields still induces an isomorphism on the residue field at every point.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_residueFieldMap_specMap_of_colimitPresentation
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J] [IsFiltered J]
    {B : CommAlgCat.{u} A} (pres : ColimitPresentation J B)
    (hresidue : ∀ i x, IsIso
      ((Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap A ↥(pres.diag.obj i))).op).residueFieldMap x)) :
    ∀ x, IsIso
      ((Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A ↥B)).op).residueFieldMap x)
declarations.comment: homeomorphism_equal_residue_fields

declarations.name: IsLocalization.exists_numerator_not_mem_of_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CN9.** Special-element conditions over a localization can be witnessed by a
numerator before localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_numerator_not_mem_of_localization
    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] (A : Subring B) (S : Submonoid A)
    {n : ℕ} (b : Fin n → B) (x : Localization (S.map A.subtype))
    (hx : x ∉ Set.range
      (IsLocalization.map (M := S) (S := Localization S) (T := S.map A.subtype)
        (Localization (S.map A.subtype)) A.subtype S.le_comap_map))
    (hbx : ∀ i, algebraMap B (Localization (S.map A.subtype)) (b i) *
      x ^ (i.val + 1) ∈ Set.range
        (IsLocalization.map (M := S) (S := Localization S) (T := S.map A.subtype)
          (Localization (S.map A.subtype)) A.subtype S.le_comap_map)) :
    ∃ (s : S) (y : B),
      x = IsLocalization.mk' (Localization (S.map A.subtype)) y
          ⟨A.subtype s.1, Submonoid.mem_map_of_mem A.subtype s.2⟩ ∧
        y ∉ A ∧ ∀ i, b i * y ^ (i.val + 1) ∈ A

declarations.name: Subring.exists_not_mem_and_sq_mem_and_cube_mem_of_pow_mem_of_succ_pow_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CNA.** If an element outside a subring has two consecutive powers,
with the first exponent at least two, in the subring, then some element outside the subring has
its square and cube in the subring.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_not_mem_and_sq_mem_and_cube_mem_of_pow_mem_of_succ_pow_mem
    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] (A : Subring B) {b : B} {n : ℕ} (hb : b ∉ A) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (hpow : b ^ n ∈ A) (hpow_succ : b ^ (n + 1) ∈ A) :
    ∃ b' : B, b' ∉ A ∧ b' ^ 2 ∈ A ∧ b' ^ 3 ∈ A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_not_mem_and_sq_mem_and_cube_mem_of_universalHomeomorphism_of_residueFieldMap_isIso
declarations.doc:
A proper subring extension which is a universal homeomorphism on spectra
and induces isomorphisms on residue fields contains an element outside the
subring whose square and cube are in the subring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_mem_and_sq_mem_and_cube_mem_of_universalHomeomorphism_of_residueFieldMap_isIso
    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] (A : Subring B)
    [UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom A.subtype).op)]
    (hres : ∀ x : Spec (CommRingCat.of B),
      IsIso ((Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom A.subtype).op).residueFieldMap x))
    (hA : A ≠ ⊤) :
    ∃ b : B, b ∉ A ∧ b ^ 2 ∈ A ∧ b ^ 3 ∈ A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_special_element_of_universalHomeomorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNC.** A proper extension inducing a universal homeomorphism on
spectra contains either a square-and-cube special element or a prime-power special element.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_special_element_of_universalHomeomorphism
    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] (A : Subring B)
    [UniversalHomeomorphism
      (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom A.subtype).op)]
    (hA : A ≠ ⊤) :
    (∃ b : B, b ∉ A ∧ b ^ 2 ∈ A ∧ b ^ 3 ∈ A) ∨
      (∃ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧
        ∃ b : B, b ∉ A ∧ (p : B) * b ∈ A ∧ b ^ p ∈ A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universalHomeomorphism_and_residueFieldIso_iff_finite_adjoin_square_cube
declarations.doc:
An injective extension induces a universal homeomorphism with unchanged residue fields
if and only if each finite subset is contained in an algebra generated by a sequence whose
successive elements have square and cube in the algebra generated by their predecessors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universalHomeomorphism_and_residueFieldIso_iff_finite_adjoin_square_cube
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hAB : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B)) :
    let f := Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op
    (UniversalHomeomorphism f ∧ (∀ x, IsIso (f.residueFieldMap x))) ↔
      ∀ E : Finset B, ∃ (n : ℕ) (b : Fin n → B),
        (↑E : Set B) ⊆ Algebra.adjoin A (Set.range b) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n,
        b i ^ 2 ∈ Algebra.adjoin A
            (Set.range (fun j : Fin i ↦ b (Fin.castLE i.isLt.le j))) ∧
          b i ^ 3 ∈ Algebra.adjoin A
              (Set.range (fun j : Fin i ↦ b (Fin.castLE i.isLt.le j)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universalHomeomorphism_spec_iff_finite_adjoin_tower
declarations.doc:
An inclusion of rings induces a universal homeomorphism on spectra exactly when every finite
set is contained in a finite, successively elementary extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_spec_iff_finite_adjoin_tower
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hAB : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B)) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism
        (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op) ↔
      ∀ E : Finset B, ∃ (n : ℕ) (b : Fin n → B),
        ((E : Set B) ⊆ Algebra.adjoin A (Set.range b)) ∧
          ∀ i : Fin n,
            (((b i) ^ 2 ∈ Algebra.adjoin A
                (Set.range fun j : { j : Fin n // j < i } ↦ b j)) ∧
              ((b i) ^ 3 ∈ Algebra.adjoin A
                (Set.range fun j : { j : Fin n // j < i } ↦ b j))) ∨
            (∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧
              (((p : B) * b i ∈ Algebra.adjoin A
                  (Set.range fun j : { j : Fin n // j < i } ↦ b j)) ∧
                ((b i) ^ p ∈ Algebra.adjoin A
                  (Set.range fun j : { j : Fin n // j < i } ↦ b j))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universalHomeomorphism_iff_locallyNilpotent_ker_and_pow_mem_range
declarations.doc:
A ring map that is an isomorphism after inverting a prime induces a universal
homeomorphism on spectra precisely when its kernel is locally nilpotent and
every target element has a prime-power multiple and prime-power power in its
image.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalHomeomorphism_iff_locallyNilpotent_ker_and_pow_mem_range
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
    (p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p)
    (hφ : Function.Bijective
      (IsLocalization.Away.map (Localization.Away (p : A))
        (Localization.Away (φ (p : A))) φ (p : A))) :
    UniversalHomeomorphism
        (Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ).op) ↔
      (RingHom.ker φ).LocallyNilpotent ∧
        ∀ b : B, ∃ n : ℕ,
          (p : B) ^ n * b ∈ Set.range φ ∧ b ^ (p ^ n) ∈ Set.range φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullback_snd_imageι_comp_of_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CNG.** The scheme-theoretic image of a section over a retrocompact open subset of
the target of a separated morphism is isomorphic to that open subset after base change.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_pullback_snd_imageι_comp_of_section {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsSeparated f] (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsRetrocompact (V : Set Y))
    (s : V.toScheme ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = V.ι) :
    IsIso (pullback.snd (s.imageι ≫ f) V.ι)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.ProductsFromFiniteCofiltered.finiteSubproductsConeIsLimit
declarations.doc: A product is canonically the inverse limit of its finite subproducts.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteSubproductsConeIsLimit [HasProduct X] :
    IsLimit (finiteSubproductsCone X)
declarations.comment: limit of finite subproducts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasProduct_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
An arbitrary family of schemes affine over `S` has a product in the category of schemes
over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProduct_of_isAffineHom {I : Type u} (S : Scheme.{u})
    (T : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, T i ⟶ S) [∀ i, IsAffineHom (f i)] :
    HasProduct (fun i => Over.mk (f i))
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_finiteSubproductsCone_π_app
declarations.doc:
The canonical projection from the infinite product of a family of schemes affine over `S`
onto any of its finite subproducts is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_finiteSubproductsCone_π_app {I : Type u} (S : Scheme.{u})
    (T : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, T i ⟶ S) [∀ i, IsAffineHom (f i)]
    [HasProduct (fun i => Over.mk (f i))] (J : (Finset (Discrete I))ᵒᵖ) :
    IsAffineHom ((finiteSubproductsCone (fun i => Over.mk (f i))).π.app J).left
declarations.comment: affine projections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_product_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNJ.** The structure morphism of the product over `S` of surjective
affine morphisms is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_product_hom {I : Type u} (S : Scheme.{u})
    (T : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, T i ⟶ S) [∀ i, IsAffineHom (f i)]
    [∀ i, Surjective (f i)] :
    letI := hasProduct_of_isAffineHom S T f
    Surjective (∏ᶜ (fun i ↦ Over.mk (f i))).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegralHom_product
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNK.** The product over a scheme of an arbitrary family of integral
morphisms is integral over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_product {I : Type u} (S : Scheme.{u})
    (T : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, T i ⟶ S) [∀ i, IsIntegralHom (f i)] :
    letI : HasProduct (fun i ↦ Over.mk (f i)) := hasProduct_of_isAffineHom S T f
    IsIntegralHom (∏ᶜ (fun i ↦ Over.mk (f i))).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNM.** A directed inverse system of Noetherian schemes with affine
transition morphisms, equipped with a chosen limiting cone.
declarations.statement:
structure LimitNoetherianSituation (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.nonempty_goodDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNN.** In the limit situation `S = lim S_i` of a directed inverse
system of Noetherian schemes with affine transition morphisms, a quasi-separated morphism
`X ⟶ S` of finite type fits into a diagram over some stage `S_i` with a model `W` of finite type
over `S_i` whose base change receives `X` as a closed subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_goodDiagram {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{u, u} I) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ D.limitScheme)
    [QuasiSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    Nonempty (GoodDiagram D f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.GoodDiagram.isLimit_imageCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNQ.** The scheme-theoretic images of a good diagram at
all later stages form an inverse system with canonical limit `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isLimit_imageCone {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ D.limitScheme) [QuasiSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (G : GoodDiagram D f) :
    IsLimit (imageCone G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.exists_morphismAt_of_dominant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNR, existence.** A morphism of schemes over the limit is realized by
a morphism of the systems of scheme-theoretic images on a sufficiently late common tail.

No hypothesis beyond the source's: in particular no smallness of the index type, and none of the
quasi-separatedness, finite-type or quasi-compactness hypotheses the source carries, all three
of which are consequences of the good diagrams.
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.exists_morphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNR, existence.** A morphism of schemes over the limit is
realized by a morphism of the systems of images on a sufficiently late common tail.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_morphismAt (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme} {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    [QuasiSeparated pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX]
    [QuasiSeparated pY] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [QuasiCompact pY]
    (GX : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY : GoodDiagram D pY) :
    ∃ (i₀ : I) (hX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hY : GY.index ≤ i₀),
      Nonempty (MorphismAt D f GX GY i₀ hX hY)
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_eq_morphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNR, eventual uniqueness.** Two system morphisms inducing the same
limit morphism agree at every sufficiently late stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_eq_morphismAt (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme} {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (GX : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY : GoodDiagram D pY)
    (i₀ : I) (hX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hY : GY.index ≤ i₀)
    (F G : MorphismAt D f GX GY i₀ hX hY) :
    ∃ (i₃ : I) (_hi : i₀ ≤ i₃),
      ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)) (_hj : i₃ ≤ unop j.left),
        F.maps.app j = G.maps.app j
declarations.comment: eventual uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.MorphismAt.eventually_eq_morphismAt_of_dominant
declarations.doc:
Two morphisms of the image systems inducing the same morphism on the limits agree at every
sufficiently late stage.
declarations.comment: eventual uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.exists_eventual_iso_imageSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNS.** The systems associated to two good diagrams for the same
scheme over the limit become isomorphic on a common tail, by an isomorphism of systems inducing
the identity of `X` and lying over the base system.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eventual_iso_imageSystem [FinallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ D.limitScheme)
    [QuasiSeparated p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p]
    (G₁ G₂ : GoodDiagram D p) :
    ∃ (i₀ : I) (h₁ : G₁.index ≤ i₀) (h₂ : G₂.index ≤ i₀)
      (F : MorphismAt D (𝟙 X) G₁ G₂ i₀ h₁ h₂)
      (G : MorphismAt D (𝟙 X) G₂ G₁ i₀ h₂ h₁),
      ∀ j : Over (op i₀),
        (F.maps.app j ≫ G.maps.app j = 𝟙 _) ∧
        (G.maps.app j ≫ F.maps.app j = 𝟙 _)
declarations.comment: eventual isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_natural_imageSystem_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNS, naturality.** The comparison between the systems of two choices
of good diagrams commutes, eventually, with any morphism of schemes over the limit.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_natural_imageSystem_comparison [FinallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [QuasiSeparated pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX]
    (GX₁ GX₂ : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY₁ GY₂ : GoodDiagram D pY)
    (i₀ : I) (hX₁ : GX₁.index ≤ i₀) (hX₂ : GX₂.index ≤ i₀)
    (hY₁ : GY₁.index ≤ i₀) (hY₂ : GY₂.index ≤ i₀)
    (FX : MorphismAt D (𝟙 X) GX₁ GX₂ i₀ hX₁ hX₂)
    (FY : MorphismAt D (𝟙 Y) GY₁ GY₂ i₀ hY₁ hY₂)
    (H₁ : MorphismAt D f GX₁ GY₁ i₀ hX₁ hY₁)
    (H₂ : MorphismAt D f GX₂ GY₂ i₀ hX₂ hY₂) :
    ∃ (i₃ : I) (_ : i₀ ≤ i₃),
      ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)) (_ : i₃ ≤ unop j.left),
        H₁.maps.app j ≫ FY.maps.app j =
          FX.maps.app j ≫ H₂.maps.app j
declarations.comment: naturality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_flat_morphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNT, eventual flatness.**

The morphisms of the image systems of a flat morphism of finite presentation are flat at every
sufficiently late stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eventually_flat_morphismAt
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme} {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    [QuasiSeparated pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX]
    [QuasiSeparated pY] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [QuasiCompact pY]
    [Flat f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (GX : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY : GoodDiagram D pY)
    (i₀ : I) (hX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hY : GY.index ≤ i₀)
    (F : MorphismAt D f GX GY i₀ hX hY) :
    ∃ (i₃ : I) (_ : i₀ ≤ i₃),
      ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)), i₃ ≤ unop j.left → Flat (F.maps.app j)
declarations.comment: eventual flatness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_isPullback_morphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNT, cartesian transition squares.**

On a sufficiently late tail every transition square of the morphism of image systems of a flat
morphism of finite presentation is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eventually_isPullback_morphismAt
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme} {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    [QuasiSeparated pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX]
    [QuasiSeparated pY] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [QuasiCompact pY]
    [Flat f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (GX : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY : GoodDiagram D pY)
    (i₀ : I) (hX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hY : GY.index ≤ i₀)
    (F : MorphismAt D f GX GY i₀ hX hY) :
    ∃ (i₃ : I) (_ : i₀ ≤ i₃),
      ∀ {j k : Over (op i₀)} (a : j ⟶ k),
        i₃ ≤ unop j.left → i₃ ≤ unop k.left →
          IsPullback (F.maps.app j)
            ((Over.map ((homOfLE hX).op) ⋙ GoodDiagram.imageSystem GX).map a)
            ((Over.map ((homOfLE hY).op) ⋙ GoodDiagram.imageSystem GY).map a)
            (F.maps.app k)
declarations.comment: cartesian transition squares

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_isPullback_limit_morphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNT, cartesian limit square.**

The square relating a flat morphism of finite presentation to each sufficiently late morphism of
the image systems is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eventually_isPullback_limit_morphismAt
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme} {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    [QuasiSeparated pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX]
    [QuasiSeparated pY] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [QuasiCompact pY]
    [Flat f] (hfp : FinitePresentation f)
    (GX : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY : GoodDiagram D pY)
    (i₀ : I) (hX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hY : GY.index ≤ i₀)
    (F : MorphismAt D f GX GY i₀ hX hY) :
    ∃ (i₃ : I) (_ : i₀ ≤ i₃),
      ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)), i₃ ≤ unop j.left →
        IsPullback f
          ((GoodDiagram.imageCone GX).π.app ((Over.map ((homOfLE hX).op)).obj j))
          ((GoodDiagram.imageCone GY).π.app ((Over.map ((homOfLE hY).op)).obj j))
          (F.maps.app j)
declarations.comment: cartesian limit square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_smooth_morphismAt
declarations.doc:
The morphisms on the image systems of a smooth map become smooth at every
sufficiently late stage.

`Nonempty I` is not a weakening. The conclusion names a specific cofinal stage `i₃ ≥ i₀`,
which is exactly how Stacks 0CNU states it ("there exists an `i₃ ≥ i₀` such that for `i ≥ i₃`"),
and that phrasing presupposes the index `i₀`. The hypothesis is the source's own.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_smooth_morphismAt {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Small.{u} I] [FinallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme} {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    [QuasiSeparated pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX]
    [QuasiSeparated pY] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [QuasiCompact pY]
    [Smooth f]
    (GX : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY : GoodDiagram D pY)
    (i₀ : I) (hX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hY : GY.index ≤ i₀)
    (F : MorphismAt D f GX GY i₀ hX hY) :
    ∃ (i₃ : I) (_ : i₀ ≤ i₃),
      ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)), i₃ ≤ unop j.left → Smooth (F.maps.app j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_isProper_morphismAt'
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CNV].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CNM], the components of a morphism of the
image systems of two good diagrams which induces a proper morphism on the limits are proper from
some stage onwards.

The limit of the system is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because its stages are Noetherian
and its transition morphisms affine, so no hypothesis on its underlying space is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isProper_morphismAt' {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{u, u} I)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {pX : X ⟶ D.limitScheme} {pY : Y ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX)
    [QuasiSeparated pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX]
    [QuasiSeparated pY] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [QuasiCompact pY] [IsProper f]
    (GX : GoodDiagram D pX) (GY : GoodDiagram D pY)
    (i₀ : I) (hX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hY : GY.index ≤ i₀)
    (F : MorphismAt D f GX GY i₀ hX hY) :
    ∃ (i₃ : I) (_ : i₀ ≤ i₃),
      ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)), i₃ ≤ unop j.left → IsProper (F.maps.app j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.eventually_comp_eq_comp_morphismAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNW, the eventual commutation.** Given a commuting square of schemes
quasi-separated and of finite type over the limit `S`, good diagrams for its four corners and
morphisms `p_i`, `q_i`, `a_i`, `b_i` of the resulting image systems realizing the four morphisms
of the square on a common tail, the two composites `a_i ∘ p_i` and `b_i ∘ q_i` agree at every
sufficiently late stage.
declarations.comment: eventual commutation of the two composites of systems

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.isClosedImmersion_fibreProductComparison
declarations.doc:
For the model `W² ×_{W⁴} W³` of the first corner of a cartesian square, the comparison
`(q_j, p_j) : X¹_j ⟶ X²_j ×_{X⁴_j} X³_j` is a closed immersion at every stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_fibreProductComparison (j : Over (op i₀)) :
    IsClosedImmersion (MorphismAt.fibreComparisonApp
      (fibreProductProjTrd G₄ M₂ M₃ hsq hq hb ha i₀ h)
      (fibreProductProjSnd G₄ M₂ M₃ hsq hq hb ha i₀ h)
      (fibreProductBaseTrd G₄ M₃ ha i₀ h) (fibreProductBaseSnd G₄ M₂ hb i₀ h) j
      (fibreProduct_comp_eq_comp G₄ M₂ M₃ hsq hq hb ha i₀ h j))
declarations.comment: closed immersion of the comparison, for the model `W² ×_{W⁴} W³` of the first corner

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.exists_eventually_isClosedImmersion_fibreComparison_of_goodDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNW, the closed immersion, for four independently chosen good
diagrams.** Given a cartesian square of schemes over `S`, a good diagram for each of its four
corners chosen separately, and morphisms `p_i`, `q_i`, `a_i`, `b_i` of the resulting image
systems realizing the four morphisms of the square over a common index `i₀`, the comparison
`(q_i, p_i) : X¹_i ⟶ X²_i ×_{X⁴_i} X³_i` is a closed immersion at every sufficiently late stage.

The compatible models the restricted statement needs are *produced* from the data: replacing
`G₂`, `G₃` and `G₄` by the good diagrams whose models are their own scheme-theoretic images at
the stage `i₀`, the components of `B` and of `A` at that stage are morphisms of models over one
stage, by `AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.MorphismAt.stageModelOver`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eventually_isClosedImmersion_fibreComparison_of_goodDiagram
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X₁ X₂ X₃ X₄ : Scheme.{u}} {s₁ : X₁ ⟶ D.limitScheme} {s₂ : X₂ ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    {s₃ : X₃ ⟶ D.limitScheme} {s₄ : X₄ ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    [QuasiSeparated s₂] [LocallyOfFiniteType s₂] [QuasiCompact s₂]
    [QuasiSeparated s₃] [LocallyOfFiniteType s₃] [QuasiCompact s₃]
    [QuasiSeparated s₄] [LocallyOfFiniteType s₄] [QuasiCompact s₄]
    {p : X₁ ⟶ X₃} {q : X₁ ⟶ X₂} {a : X₃ ⟶ X₄} {b : X₂ ⟶ X₄}
    (hsq : IsPullback q p b a) (hq : q ≫ s₂ = s₁) (hb : b ≫ s₄ = s₂) (ha : a ≫ s₄ = s₃)
    (G₁ : GoodDiagram D s₁) (G₂ : GoodDiagram D s₂) (G₃ : GoodDiagram D s₃)
    (G₄ : GoodDiagram D s₄) (i₀ : I) (h₁ : G₁.index ≤ i₀) (h₂ : G₂.index ≤ i₀)
    (h₃ : G₃.index ≤ i₀) (h₄ : G₄.index ≤ i₀)
    (P : MorphismAt D p G₁ G₃ i₀ h₁ h₃) (Q : MorphismAt D q G₁ G₂ i₀ h₁ h₂)
    (A : MorphismAt D a G₃ G₄ i₀ h₃ h₄) (B : MorphismAt D b G₂ G₄ i₀ h₂ h₄) :
    ∃ (i₇ : I) (_ : i₀ ≤ i₇), ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)) (_ : i₇ ≤ unop j.left)
      (hj : P.maps.app j ≫ A.maps.app j = Q.maps.app j ≫ B.maps.app j),
      IsClosedImmersion (MorphismAt.fibreComparisonApp P Q A B j hj)
declarations.comment: closed immersion of the comparison, for four independently chosen good diagrams

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.exists_eventually_isClosedImmersion_and_isIso_fibreComparison_of_fourIndices
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNW.** In the limit situation `S = lim S_i` of a directed inverse
system of Noetherian schemes with affine transition morphisms, let

```
X¹ ⟶ X³
↓     ↓
X² ⟶ X⁴
```

be a cartesian square of schemes quasi-separated and of finite type over `S`. For each corner
choose, independently of the others, a good diagram, take the resulting limit descriptions
`X^n = lim X^n_i` of their systems of scheme-theoretic images, and morphisms of those systems
`(a_i)_{i ≥ i₅}`, `(b_i)_{i ≥ i₆}`, `(p_i)_{i ≥ i₇}` and `(q_i)_{i ≥ i₈}` realizing the four
morphisms of the square, each starting at its own index. Then there exists
`i₉ ≥ max(i₅, i₆, i₇, i₈)` such that at every stage `i ≥ i₉` the square of systems commutes,
`a_i ∘ p_i = b_i ∘ q_i`, and the induced morphism

```
(q_i, p_i) : X¹_i ⟶ X²_i ×_{b_i, X⁴_i, a_i} X³_i
```

is a closed immersion; and if moreover `a` and `b` are flat and of finite presentation, there
exists `i₁₀ ≥ i₉` such that at every stage above `i₁₀` that same morphism is an isomorphism.

The four morphisms of systems are read on the stages above `i₉` by restriction,
`AlgebraicGeometry.LimitNoetherianSituation.MorphismAt.restrict'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eventually_isClosedImmersion_and_isIso_fibreComparison_of_fourIndices
    (D : LimitNoetherianSituation.{v, u} I)
    {X₁ X₂ X₃ X₄ : Scheme.{u}} {s₁ : X₁ ⟶ D.limitScheme} {s₂ : X₂ ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    {s₃ : X₃ ⟶ D.limitScheme} {s₄ : X₄ ⟶ D.limitScheme}
    [QuasiSeparated s₂] [LocallyOfFiniteType s₂] [QuasiCompact s₂]
    [QuasiSeparated s₃] [LocallyOfFiniteType s₃] [QuasiCompact s₃]
    [QuasiSeparated s₄] [LocallyOfFiniteType s₄] [QuasiCompact s₄]
    {p : X₁ ⟶ X₃} {q : X₁ ⟶ X₂} {a : X₃ ⟶ X₄} {b : X₂ ⟶ X₄}
    (hsq : IsPullback q p b a) (hq : q ≫ s₂ = s₁) (hb : b ≫ s₄ = s₂) (ha : a ≫ s₄ = s₃)
    (G₁ : GoodDiagram D s₁) (G₂ : GoodDiagram D s₂) (G₃ : GoodDiagram D s₃)
    (G₄ : GoodDiagram D s₄) (i₅ i₆ i₇ i₈ : I)
    (h₃₅ : G₃.index ≤ i₅) (h₄₅ : G₄.index ≤ i₅) (h₂₆ : G₂.index ≤ i₆) (h₄₆ : G₄.index ≤ i₆)
    (h₁₇ : G₁.index ≤ i₇) (h₃₇ : G₃.index ≤ i₇) (h₁₈ : G₁.index ≤ i₈) (h₂₈ : G₂.index ≤ i₈)
    (A : MorphismAt D a G₃ G₄ i₅ h₃₅ h₄₅) (B : MorphismAt D b G₂ G₄ i₆ h₂₆ h₄₆)
    (P : MorphismAt D p G₁ G₃ i₇ h₁₇ h₃₇) (Q : MorphismAt D q G₁ G₂ i₈ h₁₈ h₂₈) :
    ∃ (i₉ : I) (k₅ : i₅ ≤ i₉) (k₆ : i₆ ≤ i₉) (k₇ : i₇ ≤ i₉) (k₈ : i₈ ≤ i₉)
      (hcomm : ∀ j : Over (op i₉),
        (P.restrict' k₇).maps.app j ≫ (A.restrict' k₅).maps.app j =
          (Q.restrict' k₈).maps.app j ≫ (B.restrict' k₆).maps.app j),
      (∀ j : Over (op i₉), IsClosedImmersion (MorphismAt.fibreComparisonApp
          (P.restrict' k₇) (Q.restrict' k₈) (A.restrict' k₅) (B.restrict' k₆) j (hcomm j))) ∧
        (Flat a → Flat b → FinitePresentation a → FinitePresentation b →
          ∃ (i₁₀ : I) (_ : i₉ ≤ i₁₀), ∀ j : Over (op i₉), i₁₀ ≤ unop j.left →
            IsIso (MorphismAt.fibreComparisonApp
              (P.restrict' k₇) (Q.restrict' k₈) (A.restrict' k₅) (B.restrict' k₆) j
              (hcomm j)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_integral_surjective_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNX**, in corrected form, with `U` retrocompact in `S`: a surjective
integral morphism over a retrocompact open subscheme extends to a surjective integral morphism
over the whole scheme, without changing its restriction to the open subscheme. The general
statement of [Stacks, Tag 0CNX] is false;
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_integral_surjective_extension_and_not_forall` pairs this theorem with
the failure of the statement for an arbitrary open subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_integral_surjective_extension
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (U : S.Opens) [QuasiCompact U.ι]
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsIntegralHom f] [Surjective f] :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (g : W ⟶ S),
      IsIntegralHom g ∧ Surjective g ∧
        Nonempty (Over.mk f ≅ (Over.pullback U.ι).obj (Over.mk g))
declarations.comment: a surjective integral morphism over a retrocompact open of S extends to a surjective integral morphism over S with the same restriction to the open

declarations.name: Stacks.FiniteFactorization.exists_finite_surjective_extension
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and let `U ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open.
A finite surjective morphism `f : V ⟶ U` extends to a finite surjective morphism `g : V̄ ⟶ S`:
there is an isomorphism `e : V̄ ×_S U ≅ V` identifying the projection `V̄ ×_S U ⟶ U` with `f`, so
that `e` is an isomorphism of schemes over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_surjective_extension {S V : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S))
    (f : V ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsFinite f] [Surjective f] :
    ∃ (Vbar : Scheme.{u}) (g : Vbar ⟶ S),
      IsFinite g ∧ Surjective g ∧
        ∃ e : pullback g U.ι ≅ V,
          e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd g U.ι

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_integral_surjective_openCover_factorization_of_mem_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CNZ.** For every fppf covering `{X i ⟶ S}` of a scheme `S` there
are a surjective integral morphism `g : S' ⟶ S` and an open covering of `S'` such that each
member `U c` of the covering maps to `S` through some member `X i` of the given covering.

No hypothesis is imposed on `S`, as none is imposed in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_integral_surjective_openCover_factorization_of_mem_fppfPrecoverage
    {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage S) :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S), IsIntegralHom g ∧ Surjective g ∧
      ∃ (J : Type u) (U : J → S'.Opens), (⨆ c, U c) = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ c, ∃ i, ∃ t : (U c).toScheme ⟶ X i, (U c).ι ≫ g = t ≫ f i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_surjective_openCover_factorization_of_mem_fppfPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CP0].** For every fppf covering `{X i ⟶ S}` of a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme `S` there are a surjective finite morphism `g : S' ⟶ S` of finite
presentation and an open covering of `S'` such that each member `U c` of the covering maps to
`S` through some member `X i` of the given covering.

The second input of the source proof, [Stacks, Tag 09YZ], is supplied by
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817PartTwo.nonempty_integralLimitPresentation`, which proves it
at exactly the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness assumed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_surjective_openCover_factorization_of_mem_fppfPrecoverage
    {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage S) :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S), IsFinite g ∧ Surjective g ∧ FinitePresentation g ∧
      ∃ (J : Type u) (U : J → S'.Opens), (⨆ c, U c) = ⊤ ∧
        ∀ c, ∃ i, ∃ t : (U c).toScheme ⟶ X i, (U c).ι ≫ g = t ≫ f i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_extending_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CP1.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`W ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open subscheme and let `U ⊆ W` be a quasi-compact open subscheme.
Let `f : X ⟶ W` be proper and let `s : U ⟶ X` satisfy `s ≫ f = U.ι`. Then there is a
`U`-admissible blowup `b : S' ⟶ S` and a morphism `s' : b⁻¹(W) ⟶ X` with `s' ≫ f = b|_{b⁻¹(W)}`
extending `s`, the extension being witnessed by a morphism `t : U ⟶ b⁻¹(W)` over `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_extending_section [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (W : S.Opens) (U : W.toScheme.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set S))
    (hU : IsCompact (U : Set W.toScheme)) (f : X ⟶ W.toScheme) [IsProper f]
    (s : U.toScheme ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = U.ι)
    (h080Y : CartierBoundaryReduction W.toScheme U)
    (h081S : StrictTransformOpenImmersion (s.imageι ≫ f) U) :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (b : S' ⟶ S),
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup (W.ι ''ᵁ U) b ∧
        ∃ s' : (b ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ⟶ X,
          s' ≫ f = b ∣_ W ∧
            ∃ t : U.toScheme ⟶ (b ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme, t ≫ b ∣_ W = U.ι ∧ t ≫ s' = s
declarations.comment: with Stacks 080Y and 081S as hypotheses, in the shape Stacks 081T consumes them

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_extending_section_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CP1.** Let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`W ⊆ S` be a quasi-compact open subscheme and let `U ⊆ W` be a quasi-compact open subscheme.
Let `f : X ⟶ W` be proper and let `s : U ⟶ X` satisfy `s ≫ f = U.ι`. Then there is a
`U`-admissible blowup `b : S' ⟶ S` and a morphism `s' : b⁻¹(W) ⟶ X` with `s' ≫ f = b|_{b⁻¹(W)}`
extending `s`, the extension being witnessed by a morphism `t : U ⟶ b⁻¹(W)` over `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_extending_section_of_qcqs [CompactSpace S]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (W : S.Opens) (U : W.toScheme.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set S))
    (hU : IsCompact (U : Set W.toScheme)) (f : X ⟶ W.toScheme) [IsProper f]
    (s : U.toScheme ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = U.ι) :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (b : S' ⟶ S),
      Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup (W.ι ''ᵁ U) b ∧
        ∃ s' : (b ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme ⟶ X,
          s' ≫ f = b ∣_ W ∧
            ∃ t : U.toScheme ⟶ (b ⁻¹ᵁ W).toScheme, t ≫ b ∣_ W = U.ι ∧ t ≫ s' = s
declarations.comment: the conclusion in full, under exactly the source's hypotheses (1)-(3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP2.** The morphism of scheme-theoretic images induced by a commutative square
of algebraic spaces over `S`.
declarations.statement:
def schemeTheoreticImageMap (hY₁ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y₁)
    (hY₂ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y₂) (hsq : f₁ ≫ q = p ≫ f₂) :
    (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₁).toFunctor ⟶
      (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₂).toFunctor
declarations.comment: the induced morphism of scheme-theoretic images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticImageMap_ι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP2**, the right square: the induced morphism of scheme-theoretic images is
compatible with their inclusions into the targets.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageMap_ι (hY₁ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y₁)
    (hY₂ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y₂) (hsq : f₁ ≫ q = p ≫ f₂) :
    schemeTheoreticImageMap B S hS hY₁ hY₂ hsq ≫
        (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₂).ι =
      (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₁).ι ≫ q
declarations.comment: the right square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.toSchemeTheoreticImage_comp_schemeTheoreticImageMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP2**, the left square: a morphism of scheme-theoretic images compatible with the
inclusions into the targets is also compatible with the factorizations of the horizontal
morphisms through their images.
declarations.statement:
theorem toSchemeTheoreticImage_comp_schemeTheoreticImageMap (hsq : f₁ ≫ q = p ≫ f₂)
    (h : (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₁).toFunctor ⟶
      (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₂).toFunctor)
    (hh : h ≫ (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₂).ι =
      (schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS f₁).ι ≫ q) :
    toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS f₁ ≫ h = p ≫ toSchemeTheoreticImage B S hS f₂
declarations.comment: the left square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_pullback_snd_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_comp_of_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP3.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`V ⊆ Y` be an open subspace whose inclusion into `Y` is quasi-compact, and let `s : V ⟶ X`
satisfy `s ≫ f = 𝟙 V`.  Let `Y'` be the scheme-theoretic image of `s`, a closed subspace of
`X`, and let `Y' ⟶ Y` be its inclusion followed by `f`.  Then **`Y' ⟶ Y` is an isomorphism
over `V`**: the projection `Y' ×_Y V ⟶ V` of its base change along `V ⟶ Y` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullback_snd_schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor_comp_of_section
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS V.ι)
    (s : V.toFunctor ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = V.ι) :
    IsIso (pullback.snd ((schemeTheoreticImageSubfunctor B S hS s).ι ≫ f) V.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineLimitSquare_iff_qcqsLimitSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP4.** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, the affine-limit
comparison square is cartesian for every sufficiently small cofiltered inverse system of
affine objects exactly when the comparison square of morphism sets is cartesian for every
sufficiently small cofiltered inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
spaces with affine transition morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineLimitSquare_iff_qcqsLimitSquare (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    AffineLimitSquare B S hS f ↔ QcqsLimitSquare B S hS hZ f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.qcqsLimitSquare_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP4.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
presentation satisfies the comparison condition for cofiltered limits of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transition morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem qcqsLimitSquare_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    QcqsLimitSquare B S hS hZ f
declarations.comment: the implication from locally of finite presentation
