declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NoetherianSpaceSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP6.** A directed inverse system `(B_i)_{i ∈ I}` of Noetherian algebraic spaces
over a scheme `S` with affine transition morphisms `B_{i'} ⟶ B_i` for `i ≤ i'`. Its limit
`B = lim_i B_i` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NoetherianSpaceSystem.limit`, an algebraic space by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NoetherianSpaceSystem.isAlgebraicSpace_limit` (Stacks 07SF).

The field `indexSize` is the chapter's standing convention (Stacks 07SD) that the rings it
considers have their spectra in the site, stated for the fixed size cutoff of the site.
declarations.statement:
structure NoetherianSpaceSystem (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NoetherianLimitSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP6.** A directed inverse system of Noetherian algebraic spaces
over a scheme `S` with affine transition morphisms, equipped with a chosen limiting cone whose
point is again an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
structure NoetherianLimitSystem (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NoetherianLimitSystem.nonempty_goodDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP7.** In Situation 0CP6, let `f : X ⟶ B` be a quasi-separated morphism of finite
type of algebraic spaces over `S`. Then there are a stage `i`, an algebraic space `W` with a
morphism `W ⟶ B_i` of finite type, and a morphism `X ⟶ W` over `B ⟶ B_i`, such that the induced
morphism `X ⟶ B ×_{B_i} W` is a closed immersion: a diagram as in Stacks 0CP8.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_goodDiagram (D : NoetherianLimitSystem B S hS hZ I)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ D.limitCone.pt)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hfft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    Nonempty (GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D f)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram
registrations.comment:
the diagram: X ⟶ W over B ⟶ B_i, W ⟶ B_i of finite type and
  X ⟶ B ×_{B_i} W a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.mono_lift_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**The monomorphism half of Stacks 0CP9.** In Situation 0CP6, for a diagram as in Stacks 0CP8,
the space `X` is a *subspace* of the limit of the inverse system of the scheme-theoretic images
`X_{i'}` of `X ⟶ B_{i'} ×_{B_i} W`: the comparison morphism from `X` to the vertex of any limiting
cone on that system is a monomorphism.

The remaining half, that the comparison morphism is an isomorphism, is not proved; by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.nonempty_isLimit_imageCone_iff` it is equivalent to the
inclusion `imageInter G ≤ Subfunctor.range G.induced` of subfunctors of `B ×_{B_i} W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_lift_of_isLimit (G : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D f) {c : Cone (imageSystem G)}
    (hc : IsLimit c) : Mono (hc.lift (imageCone G))
declarations.comment: X is a subspace of the limit: the cone to the images is jointly monic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.isLimit_imageCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CP9.** In Situation 0CP6, for a diagram as in Stacks 0CP8, the canonical cone
from `X` to the inverse system of the scheme-theoretic images `X_{i'}` of
`X ⟶ B_{i'} ×_{B_i} W` is a limit cone: `X = lim_{i' ≥ i} X_{i'}`.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.nonempty_isLimit_imageCone_iff` this is the single
inclusion `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.imageInter_le_range_induced` of subfunctors of
`B ×_{B_i} W`. The hypothesis that the index type of the system be small for the site is what
produces the limit of the system of affine charts used there; it is not a hypothesis of the
source.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isLimit_imageCone (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hSize : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof) : IsLimit (imageCone G)
declarations.comment: X = lim X_{i'}, for an index type small for the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.exists_systemMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPA, existence.** In Situation 0CP6, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `B` with `X` quasi-separated over `B`, and let `GX` and `GY` be diagrams as in
Stacks 0CP8 for `X` and for `Y`. Then some stage `i₀` above the indices of both diagrams
carries a morphism of the inverse systems of scheme-theoretic images on the tail above `i₀`,
over the system `(B_i)_{i ≥ i₀}`, whose limit is `f`.

The model `V ⟶ B_{i₂}` of `GY` is locally of finite presentation, so the composite
`X ⟶ Y ⟶ V` is defined over a stage `X_{i₀} ⟶ V` by the surjectivity half of the limit
criterion for morphisms out of an inverse limit; the components of the system morphism are the
factorizations through the scheme-theoretic images `Y_i` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.exists_comp_stageImage_ι`. The two hypotheses `hX` and
`hSize` are those of the library's Stacks 0CP9.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_systemMorphism (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX) (hSize : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (GX : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pX)
    (GY : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pY) :
    ∃ (i₀ : I) (hiX : GX.index ≤ i₀) (hiY : GY.index ≤ i₀),
      Nonempty (SystemMorphism GX GY f i₀ hiX hiY)
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.eventually_eq_systemMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPA, eventual uniqueness.** Two morphisms of the inverse systems of
scheme-theoretic images on the tail above a stage `i₀`, both inducing the same morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` in the limit, have the same component at every sufficiently late stage.

Their components at the initial stage agree after composing with the projection `X ⟶ X_{i₀}`,
by the two compatibilities with the canonical cones, and after composing with the model
`V ⟶ B_{i₂}`, by the two equations over the base; so the injectivity half of the limit
criterion for morphisms out of an inverse limit makes them agree after one transition
morphism, and naturality propagates that to all later stages. The source's equalizer argument
is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_eq_systemMorphism (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX) (hSize : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    {GX : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pX} {GY : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pY} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {i₀ : I} {hiX : GX.index ≤ i₀} {hiY : GY.index ≤ i₀}
    (F G : SystemMorphism GX GY f i₀ hiX hiY) :
    ∃ i₃ : I, i₀ ≤ i₃ ∧ ∀ j : Over (op i₀), i₃ ≤ j.left.unop →
      F.maps.app j = G.maps.app j
declarations.comment: eventual uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NoetherianLimitSystem.isEquivalence_limitFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPB.** In Situation 0CP6, the category of algebraic spaces quasi-separated and of
finite type over `B = lim B_i` is equivalent to the category of the inverse systems of algebraic
spaces over `(B_i)` produced by Stacks 0CP9 from a diagram as in Stacks 0CP8, whose morphisms are
the morphisms of inverse systems over `(B_i)` on a tail of the index set, up to shrinking the
index set. The equivalence takes a system to its limit: it is essentially surjective by
Stacks 0CP7, full by the existence half and faithful by the uniqueness half of Stacks 0CPA.
declarations.statement: theorem isEquivalence_limitFunctor : (limitFunctor D).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
the category of algebraic spaces quasi-separated and of finite type over B is
  equivalent to the category of the inverse systems over (B_i) that 0CP9 produces from the
  diagrams (0CP8), up to shrinking the index set

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NoetherianLimitSystem.exists_iso_imageSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPB, the example.** Let `X` be an algebraic space quasi-separated and of finite type
over `B`, and let `X ⟶ W₁ ⟶ B_{i₁}` and `X ⟶ W₂ ⟶ B_{i₂}` be two diagrams as in Stacks 0CP8. Then,
up to shrinking the index set to the stages above some `i₀`, the corresponding limit descriptions
`X = lim X_{1,i}` and `X = lim X_{2,i}` of Stacks 0CP9 are isomorphic: there is an isomorphism of
inverse systems `(X_{1,i})_{i ≥ i₀} ≅ (X_{2,i})_{i ≥ i₀}` over `(B_i)_{i ≥ i₀}`, compatible in both
directions with the maps from `X`, that is, with limit `id_X`. The isomorphism is canonical: every
morphism of the two systems over `(B_i)` on any tail whose limit is `id_X` agrees with it at all
sufficiently late stages.

It is obtained by applying Stacks 0CPA to `id_X` in both directions: existence gives the two
morphisms of systems, and uniqueness shows that their composites agree with the identities at
late stages.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_imageSystem (U : FiniteTypeSpaces D)
    (G₁ G₂ : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D U.obj.hom) :
    ∃ (i₀ : I) (h₁ : G₁.index ≤ i₀) (h₂ : G₂.index ≤ i₀)
      (e : Over.map (homOfLE h₁).op ⋙ GoodDiagram.imageSystem G₁ ≅
        Over.map (homOfLE h₂).op ⋙ GoodDiagram.imageSystem G₂),
      (∀ j : Over (op i₀),
        e.hom.app j ≫ (GoodDiagram.stageImage G₂ ((Over.map (homOfLE h₂).op).obj j)).ι ≫
            pullback.fst _ _ =
          (GoodDiagram.stageImage G₁ ((Over.map (homOfLE h₁).op).obj j)).ι ≫ pullback.fst _ _) ∧
      (∀ j : Over (op i₀),
        e.inv.app j ≫ (GoodDiagram.stageImage G₁ ((Over.map (homOfLE h₁).op).obj j)).ι ≫
            pullback.fst _ _ =
          (GoodDiagram.stageImage G₂ ((Over.map (homOfLE h₂).op).obj j)).ι ≫ pullback.fst _ _) ∧
      (∀ j : Over (op i₀),
        (GoodDiagram.imageCone G₁).π.app ((Over.map (homOfLE h₁).op).obj j) ≫ e.hom.app j =
          (GoodDiagram.imageCone G₂).π.app ((Over.map (homOfLE h₂).op).obj j)) ∧
      (∀ j : Over (op i₀),
        (GoodDiagram.imageCone G₂).π.app ((Over.map (homOfLE h₂).op).obj j) ≫ e.inv.app j =
          (GoodDiagram.imageCone G₁).π.app ((Over.map (homOfLE h₁).op).obj j)) ∧
      ∀ (i₁ : I) (k₁ : G₁.index ≤ i₁) (k₂ : G₂.index ≤ i₁)
        (F : GoodDiagram.SystemMorphism G₁ G₂ (𝟙 U.obj.left) i₁ k₁ k₂),
        ∃ (i₃ : I) (hi₀ : i₀ ≤ i₃) (hi₁ : i₁ ≤ i₃), ∀ (i : I) (hi : i₃ ≤ i),
          F.maps.app (Over.mk (homOfLE (hi₁.trans hi)).op) =
            e.hom.app (Over.mk (homOfLE (hi₀.trans hi)).op)
declarations.comment:
the example: two limit descriptions of X are canonically isomorphic, after
  shrinking the index set

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.SystemMorphism.exists_isFlat_isPullback
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0CP6, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces quasi-separated over `B`,
let `GX` and `GY` be diagrams as in Stacks 0CP8 for `X` and `Y`, and let `(f_i)_{i ≥ i₀}` be a
morphism of the inverse systems of scheme-theoretic images `X = lim X_i` and `Y = lim Y_i` whose
limit is `f`, as in Stacks 0CPA. If `f` is flat and of finite presentation, then there is a stage
`i₃ ≥ i₀` such that for every `k ≥ i₃` the morphism `f_k` is flat, `X = Y ×_{Y_k} X_k`, and
`X_i = Y_i ×_{Y_k} X_k` for every `i ≥ k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFlat_isPullback (algX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (algY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (qsX : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX)
    (qsY : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pY) (small : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    {GX : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pX} {GY : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pY} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {i₀ : I} {leX : GX.index ≤ i₀} {leY : GY.index ≤ i₀}
    (F : SystemMorphism GX GY f i₀ leX leY)
    (flat : IsFlat B S hS f) (fp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ i₃ : I, i₀ ≤ i₃ ∧ ∀ k : Over (op i₀), i₃ ≤ k.left.unop →
      IsFlat B S hS (F.maps.app k) ∧
      IsPullback ((imageCone GX).π.app ((Over.map (homOfLE leX).op).obj k)) f
        (F.maps.app k) ((imageCone GY).π.app ((Over.map (homOfLE leY).op).obj k)) ∧
      ∀ (j : Over (op i₀)) (a : j ⟶ k),
        IsPullback ((imageSystem GX).map ((Over.map (homOfLE leX).op).map a)) (F.maps.app j)
          (F.maps.app k) ((imageSystem GY).map ((Over.map (homOfLE leY).op).map a))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.SystemMorphism.exists_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPD.** In Situation 0CP6, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
quasi-separated over `B`, let `GX` and `GY` be diagrams as in Stacks 0CP8 for `X` and `Y`, and
let `(f_i)_{i ≥ i₀}` be a morphism of the inverse systems of scheme-theoretic images
`X = lim X_i` and `Y = lim Y_i` whose limit is `f`, as in Stacks 0CPA. If `f` is smooth, then
there is a stage `i₃ ≥ i₀` such that `f_i` is smooth for every `i ≥ i₃`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSmooth (algX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (algY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (qsX : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX)
    (qsY : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pY) (small : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    {GX : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pX} {GY : GoodDiagram B S hS hZ D pY} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {i₀ : I} {leX : GX.index ≤ i₀} {leY : GY.index ≤ i₀}
    (F : SystemMorphism GX GY f i₀ leX leY) (smooth : IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    ∃ i₃ : I, i₀ ≤ i₃ ∧ ∀ k : Over (op i₀), i₃ ≤ k.left.unop →
      IsSmooth B S hS (F.maps.app k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.SystemMorphism.exists_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPE.** In Situation 0CP6, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
quasi-separated over `B`, let `GX` and `GY` be diagrams as in Stacks 0CP8 for `X` and `Y`, and
let `(f_i)_{i ≥ i₀}` be a morphism of the inverse systems of scheme-theoretic images
`X = lim X_i` and `Y = lim Y_i` whose limit is `f`, as in Stacks 0CPA. If `f` is proper, then
there is a stage `i₃ ≥ i₀` such that `f_i` is proper for every `i ≥ i₃`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper (algX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (algY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (qsX : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX)
    (qsY : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pY) (small : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (F : SystemMorphism GX GY f i₀ leX leY) (proper : IsProper B S hS f) :
    ∃ i₃ : I, i₀ ≤ i₃ ∧ ∀ k : Over (op i₀), i₃ ≤ k.left.unop →
      IsProper B S hS (F.maps.app k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.GoodDiagram.exists_isClosedImmersion_lift_and_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPF.** In Situation 0CP6, let
```
X₁ --p--> X₃
|q        |a
X₂ --b--> X₄
```
be a cartesian diagram of algebraic spaces over `B`, quasi-separated over `B`. For each
`j = 1, 2, 3, 4` let `G_j` be a diagram `X_j ⟶ W_j ⟶ B_{i_j}` as in Stacks 0CP8, with limit
description `X_j = lim_{i ≥ i_j} X^j_i` (Stacks 0CP9), and let `(a_i)_{i ≥ i₅}`, `(b_i)_{i ≥ i₆}`,
`(p_i)_{i ≥ i₇}`, `(q_i)_{i ≥ i₈}` be morphisms of these inverse systems inducing `a`, `b`, `p`,
`q`, as in Stacks 0CPA. Then there is an `i₉ ≥ i₅, i₆, i₇, i₈` such that for `i ≥ i₉` we have
`a_i ∘ p_i = b_i ∘ q_i` and `(q_i, p_i) : X¹_i ⟶ X²_i ×_{b_i, X⁴_i, a_i} X³_i` is a closed
immersion. If `a` is flat and of finite presentation (the source asks this of `a` and of `b`),
there is an `i₁₀ ≥ i₉` such that for `i ≥ i₁₀` this morphism is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isClosedImmersion_lift_and_isIso (alg₁ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁)
    (alg₂ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₂) (alg₃ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₃)
    (alg₄ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₄) (qs₁ : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX₁)
    (qs₃ : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX₃) (qs₄ : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS pX₄)
    (small : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (cart : IsPullback p q a b) (overA : a ≫ pX₄ = pX₃) (overB : b ≫ pX₄ = pX₂)
    (overQ : q ≫ pX₂ = pX₁)
    (Fa : SystemMorphism G₃ G₄ a i₅ h₃₅ h₄₅) (Fb : SystemMorphism G₂ G₄ b i₆ h₂₆ h₄₆)
    (Fp : SystemMorphism G₁ G₃ p i₇ h₁₇ h₃₇) (Fq : SystemMorphism G₁ G₂ q i₈ h₁₈ h₂₈) :
    ∃ (i₉ : I) (le₅ : i₅ ≤ i₉) (le₆ : i₆ ≤ i₉) (le₇ : i₇ ≤ i₉) (le₈ : i₈ ≤ i₉)
      (comm : ∀ (i : I) (le : i₉ ≤ i),
        Fp.app i (le₇.trans le) ≫ Fa.app i (le₅.trans le) =
          Fq.app i (le₈.trans le) ≫ Fb.app i (le₆.trans le)),
      (∀ (i : I) (le : i₉ ≤ i),
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.lift _ _ (comm i le).symm)) ∧
      (IsFlat B S hS a → IsFinitePresentation B S hS a →
        ∃ i₁₀ : I, ∃ le₁₀ : i₉ ≤ i₁₀, ∀ (i : I) (le : i₁₀ ≤ i),
          IsIso (pullback.lift _ _ (comm i (le₁₀.trans le)).symm))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_extending_section_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPI.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X`, `Y` be algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`U ⊆ W ⊆ Y` be open subspaces, and let `f : X ⟶ W` and `s : U ⟶ X` be morphisms with
`f ∘ s = id_U`. Assume that `f` is proper, that `Y` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and that
`U` and `W` are quasi-compact. Then there are a `U`-admissible blowup `b : Y' ⟶ Y` and a morphism
`s' : b⁻¹(W) ⟶ X` extending `s` with `f ∘ s' = b|_{b⁻¹(W)}`.

Here `W` is the algebraic space `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.openSubspace B S hS Y W`, so
`f ∘ s = id_U` reads `s ≫ f = U ↪ W`; quasi-separatedness of `Y` is absolute quasi-separatedness;
being a `U`-admissible blowup is Stacks 086B, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAdmissibleBlowup`;
`b⁻¹(W)` is the inverse image subfunctor `W.1.preimage b.hom`, and `b|_{b⁻¹(W)}` is
`W.1.fromPreimage b.hom`; and `s'` *extends* `s` in that its restriction to `b⁻¹(U) ⊆ b⁻¹(W)` is
`s ∘ b|_{b⁻¹(U)}` (the morphism `b⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` being an isomorphism, as `b` is `U`-admissible).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleBlowup_extending_section_of_isProper {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y.1)
    (U W : OpenSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hUW : U.1 ≤ W.1)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.1.toFunctor)
    (f : X ⟶ openSubspace B S hS Y W) (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (s : U.1.toFunctor ⟶ X.1) (hs : s ≫ f.hom = Subfunctor.homOfLe hUW) :
    ∃ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : Y' ⟶ Y), IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U b ∧
      ∃ s' : (W.1.preimage b.hom).toFunctor ⟶ X.1, s' ≫ f.hom = W.1.fromPreimage b.hom ∧
        Subfunctor.homOfLe (fun T _ hx => hUW T hx :
          U.1.preimage b.hom ≤ W.1.preimage b.hom) ≫ s' = U.1.fromPreimage b.hom ≫ s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceMap
declarations.doc:
The map `Isom_𝒳(x, y) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f(x), f(y))` of sheaves on the big fppf site of `U` induced
by a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`: it applies `f` to a local isomorphism and compares the chosen
pullbacks of `x` and `y` with those of their images.
declarations.statement:
def isomSpaceMap (x y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    isomSpace B S hS 𝒳 U x y ⟶
      isomSpace B S hS 𝒴 U (imageFiberObj B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x)
        (imageFiberObj B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U y)
declarations.comment: the map Isom_𝒳(x, x) → Isom_𝒴(y, y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
The relative automorphism sheaf `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)`, as a subsheaf of `Isom_𝒳(x, x)`: its
sections over `V` are the local automorphisms `α` of `x` with `f(α) = id`.
declarations.statement:
def relativeIsomSubfunctor (x : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    Subfunctor (isomSpace B S hS 𝒳 U x x)
declarations.comment: the sheaf Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSpaceGrpObj
declarations.doc: The group structure on `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)`, restricted from that of `Isom_𝒳(x, x)`.
declarations.statement:
def relativeIsomSpaceGrpObj (x : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    GrpObj (relativeIsomSpace B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x)
declarations.comment: the group structure on Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isMonHom_relativeIsomSpaceι
declarations.doc: The inclusion `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒳(x, x)` is a homomorphism of sheaves of groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMonHom_relativeIsomSpaceι (x : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    letI : 𝒳.val.p.IsPreFibered := 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids.isFibered.toIsPreFibered
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpace B S hS 𝒳 U x x) := isomSpaceGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 U x
    letI : GrpObj (relativeIsomSpace B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x) :=
      relativeIsomSpaceGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x
    IsMonHom (relativeIsomSubfunctor B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x).ι
declarations.comment: the first map is a homomorphism of sheaves of groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isMonHom_isomSpaceMap
declarations.doc: The map `Isom_𝒳(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f(x), f(x))` is a homomorphism of sheaves of groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMonHom_isomSpaceMap (x : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    letI : 𝒳.val.p.IsPreFibered := 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids.isFibered.toIsPreFibered
    letI : 𝒴.val.p.IsPreFibered := 𝒴.isFiberedInGroupoids.isFibered.toIsPreFibered
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpace B S hS 𝒳 U x x) := isomSpaceGrpObj B S hS 𝒳 U x
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpace B S hS 𝒴 U (imageFiberObj B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x)
        (imageFiberObj B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x)) :=
      isomSpaceGrpObj B S hS 𝒴 U (imageFiberObj B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x)
    IsMonHom (isomSpaceMap B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x x)
declarations.comment: the second map is a homomorphism of sheaves of groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSpaceι_app_injective
declarations.doc: The inclusion `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒳(x, x)` is injective on sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeIsomSpaceι_app_injective (x : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U)
    (V : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ)
    (a b : (relativeIsomSpace B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x).obj V)
    (h : (relativeIsomSubfunctor B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x).ι.app V a =
      (relativeIsomSubfunctor B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x).ι.app V b) : a = b
declarations.comment: injectivity of the first map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsom_exact
declarations.doc:
The sequence `0 → Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) → Isom_𝒳(x, x) → Isom_𝒴(y, y)` is exact at the middle
term: a local automorphism of `x` has identity image in `Isom_𝒴(y, y)` exactly when it comes from
a relative automorphism of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeIsom_exact (x : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U)
    (V : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ)
    (m : (isomSpace B S hS 𝒳 U x x).obj V) :
    ((isomSpaceMap B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x x).app V m).1 = 𝟙 _ ↔
      ∃ n : (relativeIsomSpace B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x).obj V,
        (relativeIsomSubfunctor B S hS 𝒳 𝒴 F U x).ι.app V n = m
declarations.comment: exactness at Isom_𝒳(x, x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverSpaceMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPK, part (3): the map on isomorphism sheaves.** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks carries `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` into `Isom_𝒴(x₁ ≫ f, x₂ ≫ f)`: it keeps the point of `Z`
and applies `f` to the isomorphism of the fibre.

The source calls this a map *of algebraic spaces*; that the source and target are algebraic
spaces over `Z` is asserted by Stacks 06PP and is not proved here, so this is the map of the
underlying sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isomSpaceOverSpaceMap (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    isomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂ ⟶
      isomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)
declarations.comment: part (3): the map on isomorphism sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isPullback_relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPK, part (3): the cartesian square.** The isomorphisms of `x₁` and `x₂` lifting the
2-morphism `α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f` are the fibre product of `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` and `Z` over
`Isom_𝒴(x₁ ≫ f, x₂ ≫ f)`, along the map induced by `f` and the section determined by `α`.

The square is cartesian pointwise and for an elementary reason: a section of `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` over
`W` together with a point of `Z` over `W` having the same image in `Isom_𝒴(x₁ ≫ f, x₂ ≫ f)` is the
same thing as a section of `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)` whose image under `f` is the component of `α`, because
the two images have the same point of `Z` as their first component.

The square is the one Stacks 0CPK part (3) draws, as a square of sheaves on the big fppf site of
`S`; that its four corners are algebraic spaces is asserted by Stacks 06PP and is not proved
here. Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace` it also identifies the
explicit sub-presheaf with the fibre product of Stacks 06PP part (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) (α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f) :
    IsPullback (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpaceι B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
      (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
      (isomSpaceOverSpaceMap B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂)
      (twistedSection B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (3): the cartesian square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj
declarations.doc:
The group structure over `Z` on the sheaf `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)` of automorphisms of an
algebraic-space-valued point `x` of `𝒳` whose image under `f` is the identity: the law is
composition of automorphisms, the unit is the identity and the inverse is the inverse
automorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj :
    GrpObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x)
declarations.comment: part (1): the relative automorphism sheaf is a group over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutGroupAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
The relative automorphism sheaf `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x)` as a group algebraic space over `Z`, with
the group structure `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeAutGroupAlgebraicSpace :
    Space.GroupAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z hZ
declarations.comment: part (1): the relative automorphisms are a group algebraic space over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSpaceSliceModObj
declarations.doc:
The action of `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₂, x₂)` on `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` over `Z`, by
postcomposition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeIsomSpaceSliceModObj :
    letI : GrpObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂) :=
      relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x₂
    ModObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)
      (relativeIsomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (4): the action by postcomposition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isPseudoTorsor_relativeIsomSpaceSlice
declarations.doc:
The isomorphisms lifting `α` are a pseudo-torsor under the relative automorphisms of the
target point, over `Z`: `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` is a pseudo-torsor under `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₂, x₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoTorsor_relativeIsomSpaceSlice :
    letI : GrpObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂) :=
      relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x₂
    letI : ModObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)
        (relativeIsomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α) :=
      relativeIsomSpaceSliceModObj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α
    IsPseudoTorsor (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)
      (relativeIsomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (4): the relative isomorphisms are a pseudo-torsor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_isPseudoTorsor_relativeIsomSpaceSlice
declarations.doc:
For every 2-morphism `α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f` the sheaf `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` and the relative
automorphism sheaf `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₂, x₂)` are algebraic spaces over `Z`, and the first is a
pseudo-torsor under the second over `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_isPseudoTorsor_relativeIsomSpaceSlice :
    letI : GrpObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂) :=
      relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x₂
    letI : ModObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)
        (relativeIsomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α) :=
      relativeIsomSpaceSliceModObj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₂ x₂ (𝟙 (x₂ ≫ f))) ∧
      IsPseudoTorsor (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)
        (relativeIsomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (4): the relative isomorphisms are an algebraic space and a pseudo-torsor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicSpace_isPullback_relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace
declarations.doc:
The sheaves `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂)`, `Isom_𝒴(f x₁, f x₂)` and `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` are algebraic
spaces over `Z`, and the square cutting out `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isomSpaceOverSpaceMap` is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_isPullback_relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (isomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (isomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α) ∧
      IsPullback (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpaceι B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
        (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
        (isomSpaceOverSpaceMap B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂)
        (twistedSection B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
declarations.comment: part (3): the cartesian square of algebraic spaces over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isMonHom_relativeAutSpaceSliceι
declarations.doc: The inclusion `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒳(x, x)` is a homomorphism of groups over `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMonHom_relativeAutSpaceSliceι :
    letI : GrpObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x) :=
      relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ x x) := isomSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ x
    IsMonHom (relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x f)
declarations.comment: part (2): the first map is a homomorphism of groups over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isMonHom_isomSpaceSliceMap
declarations.doc:
The map `Isom_𝒳(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f x, f x)` induced by `f` is a homomorphism of groups over
`Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMonHom_isomSpaceSliceMap :
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ x x) := isomSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ x
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ (x ≫ f) (x ≫ f)) :=
      isomSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ (x ≫ f)
    IsMonHom (isomSpaceSliceMap B S hS Z hZ x f)
declarations.comment: part (2): the second map is a homomorphism of groups over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutSpaceSliceι_injective
declarations.doc: The inclusion `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒳(x, x)` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeAutSpaceSliceι_injective (Q : Over Z)
    (g h : Q ⟶ relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x)
    (hgh : g ≫ relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x f =
      h ≫ relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x f) : g = h
declarations.comment: part (2): injectivity of the first map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeAutSpaceSlice_exact
declarations.doc:
The sequence `0 ⟶ Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒳(x, x) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f x, f x)` of groups over `Z` is
exact at the middle term: a point of `Isom_𝒳(x, x)` is killed by the second map exactly when it
comes from a relative automorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeAutSpaceSlice_exact (Q : Over Z) (p : Q ⟶ isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ x x) :
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ (x ≫ f) (x ≫ f)) :=
      isomSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ (x ≫ f)
    p ≫ isomSpaceSliceMap B S hS Z hZ x f = 1 ↔
      ∃ g : Q ⟶ relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x,
        g ≫ relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x f = p
declarations.comment: part (2): exactness at Isom_𝒳(x, x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeIsomSpaceSlice_properties
declarations.doc:
For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks, an algebraic space `Z` and two points
`x₁, x₂ : Z ⟶ 𝒳`, the isomorphism sheaves attached to these data, read in the slice over `Z`,
satisfy:

* the relative automorphism sheaf `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₂, x₂)` is an algebraic space over `Z` and
  carries a group structure over `Z`, i.e. is a group algebraic space over `Z`;
* the sequence `0 ⟶ Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₂, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒳(x₂, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f x₂, f x₂)` is a sequence of
  homomorphisms of groups over `Z`, injective at the first map and exact at the middle term;
* the two isomorphism sheaves are algebraic spaces over `Z` and there is a map
  `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(f x₁, f x₂)` for which the square cutting out
  `Isom^α_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₁, x₂)` is cartesian for every 2-morphism `α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f`;
* that sheaf is an algebraic space over `Z` and a pseudo-torsor under `Isom_{𝒳/𝒴}(x₂, x₂)` over
  `Z` for every such `α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeIsomSpaceSlice_properties (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Z hZ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    letI : GrpObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂) :=
      relativeAutSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ f x₂
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ x₂ x₂) := isomSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ x₂
    letI : GrpObj (isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ (x₂ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)) :=
      isomSpaceSliceGrpObj B S hS Z hZ (x₂ ≫ f)
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₂ x₂ (𝟙 (x₂ ≫ f))) ∧
      Nonempty (GrpObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)) ∧
      IsMonHom (relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x₂ f) ∧
      IsMonHom (isomSpaceSliceMap B S hS Z hZ x₂ f) ∧
      (∀ (Q : Over Z) (g h : Q ⟶ relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂),
        g ≫ relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x₂ f =
          h ≫ relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x₂ f → g = h) ∧
      (∀ (Q : Over Z) (p : Q ⟶ isomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ x₂ x₂),
        p ≫ isomSpaceSliceMap B S hS Z hZ x₂ f = 1 ↔
          ∃ g : Q ⟶ relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂,
            g ≫ relativeAutSpaceSliceι B S hS Z hZ x₂ f = p) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (isomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ x₁ x₂) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (isomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)) ∧
      (∀ α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f,
        IsPullback (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpaceι B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
          (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpaceProj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)
          (isomSpaceOverSpaceMap B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂)
          (twistedSection B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)) ∧
      (∀ α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f,
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (relativeIsomSpaceOverSpace B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α)) ∧
      (∀ α : x₁ ≫ f ⟶ x₂ ≫ f,
        letI : ModObj (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)
            (relativeIsomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α) :=
          relativeIsomSpaceSliceModObj B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α
        IsPseudoTorsor (relativeAutSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₂)
          (relativeIsomSpaceSlice B S hS Z hZ f x₁ x₂ α))
declarations.comment: the whole statement: parts (1), (2), (3) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isProper_mapBase_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (1), the separated case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is separated then the
comparison `T₁ ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} T₂ ⟶ T₁ ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} T₂` of algebraic-space-valued points of `𝒳`
is proper, in the sense of Stacks 04XB.

This is Stacks 050H part (6) at a cospan whose two sources are algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_mapBase_of_isSeparated (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsProper.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.mapBase B S hS x₁ x₂ f).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isQuasiCompactAndQuasiSeparated_mapBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (1), the quasi-separated case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-separated then
the comparison `T₁ ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} T₂ ⟶ T₁ ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} T₂` of algebraic-space-valued points of
`𝒳` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, in the sense of Stacks 04XB.

This is Stacks 050H part (7) at a cospan whose two sources are algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactAndQuasiSeparated_mapBase
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsQuasiCompact.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
        (AlgebraicStacks.mapBase B S hS x₁ x₂ f).hom ∧
      Stack.IsQuasiSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
        (AlgebraicStacks.mapBase B S hS x₁ x₂ f).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isLocallyQuasiFinite_mapBase_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (1), the quasi-DM case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-DM then the comparison
`T₁ ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} T₂ ⟶ T₁ ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} T₂` of algebraic-space-valued points of `𝒳` is locally
quasi-finite, in the sense of Stacks 04XB.

This is Stacks 050H part (5) at a cospan whose two sources are algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_mapBase_of_isQuasiDM
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsLocallyQuasiFinite.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (AlgebraicStacks.mapBase B S hS x₁ x₂ f).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isUnramified_mapBase_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (1), the Deligne–Mumford case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is Deligne–Mumford then
the comparison `T₁ ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} T₂ ⟶ T₁ ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} T₂` of algebraic-space-valued points of
`𝒳` is unramified, in the sense of Stacks 04XB.

This is Stacks 050H part (4) at a cospan whose two sources are algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_mapBase_of_isDM (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) :
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
        (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.val.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.val.p =
        Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS x₁ x₂).val.val.p
            (AlgebraicStacks.twoFibreProduct B S hS (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.val.p z
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (AlgebraicStacks.mapBase B S hS x₁ x₂ f).hom))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isProper_isomMap_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (2), the separated case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is separated then the induced
map `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(y₁, y₂)` is proper, in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_isomMap_of_isSeparated (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsProper.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (isomMap B S hS f T hT x₁ x₂)
declarations.comment: part (2): proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isQuasiCompactAndQuasiSeparated_isomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (2), the quasi-separated case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-separated then
the induced map `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(y₁, y₂)` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, in the
sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactAndQuasiSeparated_isomMap
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsQuasiCompact.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (isomMap B S hS f T hT x₁ x₂) ∧
      Stack.IsQuasiSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (isomMap B S hS f T hT x₁ x₂)
declarations.comment: part (2): quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isLocallyQuasiFinite_isomMap_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (2), the quasi-DM case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-DM then the induced
map `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(y₁, y₂)` is locally quasi-finite, in the sense of Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiFinite_isomMap_of_isQuasiDM
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiDM B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsLocallyQuasiFinite.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS (isomMap B S hS f T hT x₁ x₂)
declarations.comment: part (2): locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isUnramified_isomMap_of_isDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPL, part (2), the Deligne–Mumford case.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is Deligne–Mumford then
the induced map `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(y₁, y₂)` is unramified, in the sense of
Stacks 04XB.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnramified_isomMap_of_isDM (hf : Stack.IsDM B S hS f) :
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
        (isomStack B S hS T hT (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ (isomStack B S hS T hT (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (G : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 G),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (isomStack B S hS T hT x₁ x₂).val.p
            (isomStack B S hS T hT (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.p z
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (isomMap B S hS f T hT x₁ x₂)))
          (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsUnramified B S hS
          (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨G, hG⟩)).hom
declarations.comment: part (2): unramified

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPM, part (1), first half**, verbatim: *"Let `j : 𝒳 → 𝒴` be an immersion of
algebraic stacks. If `𝒴` is locally Noetherian, then `𝒳` is locally Noetherian [and `j` is
quasi-compact]."* Local Noetherianity of an algebraic stack over `S` is the smooth-scheme-atlas
criterion of **Stacks 04YG** at `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian`.

The 2-fibre product `𝒫 = V ×_𝒴 𝒳` of a locally Noetherian smooth surjective scheme chart
`g : V ⟶ 𝒴` with `j` has first projection a base change of `j`, so `𝒫` is representable by an
algebraic space `F` and the induced morphism `F ⟶ V` is locally of finite type; `F` is then
locally Noetherian by Stacks 04ZK, and an étale scheme chart of `F` composed with the second
projection — a base change of `g`, hence smooth and surjective — is a locally Noetherian scheme
atlas of `𝒳`.

Quasi-compactness of `j`, the other half of part (1), and part (2) are in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/QuasiCompactImmersion.lean`, which consumes this
statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_of_isImmersion
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j)
    (hY : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (1): the source is locally Noetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.hasRelativeProperty_quasiCompact_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be an immersion of algebraic stacks, where `𝒴` has a smooth surjective
scheme atlas with locally Noetherian source. Then `j` is quasi-compact: it has the relative
property of Stacks 03YK at quasi-compactness of morphisms of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeProperty_quasiCompact_of_isImmersion
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j)
    (hY : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴) :
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
      (Space.quasiCompactProperty B S hS) j.hom hj.1
declarations.comment: part (1): the 1-morphism is quasi-compact, in the sense of Stacks 03YK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isNoetherianStack_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be an immersion of algebraic stacks. If `𝒴` is Noetherian, then `𝒳` is
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherianStack_of_isImmersion
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (j : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j)
    (hY : IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒴) :
    IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (2): the source is Noetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_iff_isSurjective_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPN, parts (1) and (2).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` is
universally injective if and only if its relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_iff_isSurjective_relativeDiagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS f ↔
      IsSurjective B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS f)
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSurjective_relativeDiagonal_of_liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPN, the implication (3) `⟹` (2).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks
over `S` which lifts 2-arrows at geometric points has surjective relative diagonal
`Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳`.

A point of `|𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳|` is represented over an algebraically closed field, where it is a triple
`(x₁, x₂, β)`; condition (3) writes `β` as `f(α)`, and then `(𝟙, α)` is an arrow from
`Δ_f(x₁) = (x₁, x₁, id)` to that triple, so the two represent the same point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_relativeDiagonal_of_liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h₃ : LiftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints B S hS f) :
    IsSurjective B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS f)
declarations.comment: part (3) implies part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_of_liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPN, the implication (3) `⟹` (1).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`
which lifts 2-arrows at geometric points is universally injective: its relative diagonal is
surjective, and parts (1) and (2) of Stacks 0CPN
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_iff_isSurjective_relativeDiagonal`) conclude.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h₃ : LiftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints B S hS f) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (3) implies part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints_of_isSurjective_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPN, the implication (2) `⟹` (3).** A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks
over `S` whose relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is surjective lifts 2-arrows at geometric
points: for every algebraically closed field `k`, all `x₁, x₂ : Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` and every 2-arrow
`β : f ∘ x₁ ⟶ f ∘ x₂` there is a 2-arrow `α : x₁ ⟶ x₂` with `β = id_f ⋆ α`.

The triple `t = (x₁, x₂, β)` is a point of `𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` over `Spec k`, and the fibre
`T = 𝒳 ×_{Δ_f, 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳, t} Spec k` is an algebraic space locally of finite type over `Spec k` by
**Stacks 04XS**. Surjectivity of `Δ_f` makes `T` nonempty, and since `k` is algebraically closed
`T` then has a `k`-point
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_obj_base_of_nonempty_points`), which is exactly the
2-arrow `α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints_of_isSurjective_relativeDiagonal (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h₂ : IsSurjective B S hS (AlgebraicStacks.relativeDiagonal B S hS f)) :
    LiftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_iff_liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPN, parts (1) and (3).** A 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` is universally
injective if and only if it lifts 2-arrows at geometric points.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_iff_liftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS f ↔ LiftsTwoArrowsAtGeometricPoints B S hS f
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasRelativeProperty_iff_of_fppfCoverStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPP.** Let `P` be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
stable under base change and local on the target for the fppf precoverage, let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` representable by algebraic spaces, and let `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be
surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Then `f` has the relative property `P` of
Stacks 03YK if and only if the projection to `𝒵` of a 2-fibre product of the cospan `(g, f)` has
it.

Unlike **Stacks 06TY** the cover `g` is not assumed representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeProperty_iff_of_fppfCoverStack
    (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget (Space.Topology.fppf.precoverage.{u, u} B S hS)]
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom)
    (hSurj : IsSurjective B S hS g)
    (hFlat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hLfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS g)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q) :
    HasRelativeProperty B S hS P f.hom hf ↔
      ∃ hfst : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS Q.fst.hom.hom,
        HasRelativeProperty B S hS P Q.fst.hom hfst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPQ, with universal closedness of `Δ_f` assumed.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and
`g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`. If `f` is surjective, flat, locally of
finite presentation and universally injective, if the relative diagonal of `f` is universally
closed, and if `f ≫ g` is separated, then `g` is separated.

The relative diagonal of `f` is surjective by Stacks 0CPN, so properness of `Δ_{f ≫ g} = Δ_f ≫ i`
gives properness of the comparison 1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒳`; and `i` is a base change
of `Δ_g` along `f × f`, so properness of `Δ_g` descends by Stacks 0CPP.

Given the other hypotheses, universal closedness of `Δ_f` is also a consequence of the
conclusion, so the implication below is in fact an equivalence; and local finite type of a
relative diagonal (part (2) of Stacks 04XS) and the three properties of `f × f` are assumed. See
the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfSurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hfFlat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hfLfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hfUI : Stack.UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hh : IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hdiagUC : Stack.UniversallyClosed B S hS (relativeDiagonal B S hS f).hom)
    (hdiagLFT : ∀ {𝒰 𝒱 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (k : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒱)
      (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (y : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤ (twoFibreProduct B S hS k k).val.val.obj)
      (_hy : y ⋙ (twoFibreProduct B S hS k k).val.val.p = Over.map U.hom)
      (F : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom) 𝒰.val.val.p
            (twoFibreProduct B S hS k k).val.val.p y
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (relativeDiagonal B S hS k).hom))
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom)
    (hCospan : ∀ {𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (k : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒱) (l : 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒲),
      Stack.IsSurjective B S hS k → IsFlat B S hS k →
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS k →
      Stack.IsSurjective B S hS (mapCospan B S hS k k l) ∧
        IsFlat B S hS (mapCospan B S hS k k l) ∧
        IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (mapCospan B S hS k k l)) :
    IsSeparated B S hS g
declarations.comment: universal closedness of Δ_f is added: the published statement is false without it, a section of a 1-morphism of stacks being a monomorphism only when the 1-morphism is faithful; 04XS (2) and the permanence of the three properties under forming f × f are assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective_of_isSeparated_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPQ, corrected: `g` with separated diagonal.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵` be
1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`. If `f` is surjective, flat, locally of finite
presentation and universally injective, if `f ≫ g` is separated, and if the relative diagonal
`Δ_g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴 ×_𝒵 𝒴` is separated in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, then `g`
is separated.

The added hypothesis is on `g`, not on `f`, and it is strictly weaker than the conclusion, which
asks `Δ_g` to be proper. It is exactly what the published statement is missing: the comparison
1-morphism `i : 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒳` is a base change of `Δ_g` (Stacks 050H), so it is separated,
and then part (3) of Stacks 050M cancels it out of the proper `Δ_{f ≫ g} = Δ_f ≫ i`, making `Δ_f`
proper, in particular universally closed; the published route through Stacks 0CPN, Stacks 08AJ
and Stacks 0CPP then goes through
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks`
`.isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective_of_universallyClosed_relativeDiagonal`).
Without it the statement fails, the obstruction being separatedness of `i`:
`Stacks.Examples.not_forall_isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective`. It holds
whenever `g` is representable by algebraic spaces,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks`
`.isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective_of_isSeparated_diagonal
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfSurj : Stack.IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hfFlat : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hfLfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hfUI : Stack.UniversallyInjective B S hS f)
    (hh : IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hΔg : Stack.IsSeparated.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS
      (Stack.relativeDiagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒵.val g.hom)) :
    IsSeparated B S hS g
declarations.comment: corrected form: the relative diagonal of g is assumed separated, which holds when g is representable by algebraic spaces and is strictly weaker than the conclusion; the published statement fails, see Stacks.Examples.not_forall_isSeparated_of_isSeparated_comp_of_universallyInjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSurjective_and_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeDiagonal_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPR, part (2).** If a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` makes
`𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`, then its relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation.

Surjectivity is Stacks 06P1 (2)(b) read at a field-valued point
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSurjective_relativeDiagonal_of_isGerbeOver`);
flatness and local finite presentation hold because `Δ_f` is a section of the gerbe
`𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳`
(`isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeDiagonal`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_and_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeDiagonal_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsGerbeOver B S hS f) :
    Stack.IsSurjective B S hS (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f) ∧
      IsFlat B S hS (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f)
declarations.comment: part (2): the relative diagonal is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeInertiaProjection_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPR, part (1).** If a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` makes
`𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`, then the forgetful 1-morphism `I_{𝒳/𝒴} ⟶ 𝒳` of the relative inertia is
flat and locally of finite presentation.

The relative inertia is equivalent over the site to `𝒳 ×_{Δ_f, 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳, Δ_f} 𝒳` in such a way
that the forgetful 1-morphism becomes the first projection
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.relativeInertiaProjection_eq_comp_fst`), which is a base
change of `Δ_f`; so part (2) together with **Stacks 06PY** and **Stacks 06Q4** gives the two
properties for the projection, and they are unchanged by the comparison.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_relativeInertiaProjection_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsGerbeOver B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS (Stack.relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (Stack.relativeInertiaProjection B S hS f)
declarations.comment: part (1): the relative inertia is flat and locally of finite presentation over the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isSurjective_and_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comparison_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPR, part (3).** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`
making `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`, let `T₁` and `T₂` be algebraic spaces over `S` and let
`x_i : T_i ⟶ 𝒳` be 1-morphisms, with `y_i = x_i ≫ f`. Then the comparison 1-morphism

    T₁ ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} T₂ ⟶ T₁ ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} T₂

is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation.

By **Stacks 04Z1** that comparison is a base change of the relative diagonal `Δ_f`, which has the
three properties by part (2), and they base change by **Stacks 04ZU**, **Stacks 06PY** and
**Stacks 06Q4**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_and_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_comparison_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsGerbeOver B S hS f) (T₁ T₂ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (x₁ : ofAlgebraicSpace.{u, w} B S hS T₁ ⟶ 𝒳)
    (x₂ : ofAlgebraicSpace.{u, w} B S hS T₂ ⟶ 𝒳) :
    Stack.IsSurjective B S hS (Stack.comparison B S hS x₁ x₂ f) ∧
      IsFlat B S hS (Stack.comparison B S hS x₁ x₂ f) ∧
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (Stack.comparison B S hS x₁ x₂ f)
declarations.comment: part (3): the comparison of the two fibre products of a pair of algebraic spaces over the stacks is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isomMap_isSurjective_and_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPR, part (4).** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`
making `𝒳` a gerbe over `𝒴`, let `T` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `x₁, x₂ : T ⟶ 𝒳` be
1-morphisms, with `y_i = x_i ≫ f`. Then the morphism

    Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(y₁, y₂)

which applies `f` to an isomorphism `x₁(t) ≅ x₂(t)` is representable by algebraic spaces, and
it is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation: for every scheme `U` over `S` and
every object of `Isom_𝒴(y₁, y₂)` over `U`, the morphism to `U` from the algebraic space
representing the base change is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation
(**Stacks 04XB**).

As in the source, `Isom_𝒳(x₁, x₂) ⟶ Isom_𝒴(y₁, y₂)` is a base change of the comparison
`T ×_{x₁, 𝒳, x₂} T ⟶ T ×_{y₁, 𝒴, y₂} T` of part (3)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HigherDiagonal.isTwoFibreProduct_isomSquare`), which is a base change of
`Δ_f` (**Stacks 050H**). The relative diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, so its three
properties of part (2) are its relative properties in the sense of Stacks 04XB, by **Stacks 04XI**
for surjectivity and by **Stacks 06FM**, the assertion for representable morphisms, for flatness
and local finite presentation; and these pass along the two base changes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isomMap_isSurjective_and_isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : IsGerbeOver B S hS f)
    (T : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T)
    (x₁ x₂ : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS T hT ⟶ 𝒳) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (HigherDiagonal.isomMap B S hS f T hT x₁ x₂).hom ∧
    ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (z : BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2 ⥤
        (HigherDiagonal.isomStack B S hS T hT (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.obj)
      (_hz : z ⋙ (HigherDiagonal.isomStack B S hS T hT (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.p =
        Over.map U.hom)
      (G : (BigFppfOver B U.left.1 U.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B U.left.1 U.left.2 G),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map U.hom)
            (HigherDiagonal.isomStack B S hS T hT x₁ x₂).val.p
            (HigherDiagonal.isomStack B S hS T hT (x₁ ≫ f) (x₂ ≫ f)).val.p z
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (HigherDiagonal.isomMap B S hS f T hT x₁ x₂)))
          (presheafOfCategories (G ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        Space.IsSurjective B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨G, hG⟩)).hom ∧
          Space.IsFlat B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨G, hG⟩)).hom ∧
          Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS U
            ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B U.left.1 S U.left.2 hS U.hom).obj ⟨G, hG⟩)).hom
declarations.comment: part (4): the morphism of isomorphism spaces is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isGerbeOver_iff_isSurjective_isFlat_isLfp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPS.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. Then `𝒳` is
a gerbe over `𝒴` if and only if `f` and its relative diagonal `Δ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒴 𝒳` are both
surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation.

The implication from the gerbe condition is **Stacks 06QI** and **Stacks 0CPR**, part (2)
(`isSurjective_isFlat_isLfp_of_isGerbeOver`); the converse reads both clauses of the gerbe
condition off **Stacks 06QA** applied to `f` and to `Δ_f`
(`isGerbeOver_of_isSurjective_isFlat_isLfp`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isGerbeOver_iff_isSurjective_isFlat_isLfp
    {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    IsGerbeOver B S hS f ↔
      (Stack.IsSurjective B S hS f ∧ IsFlat B S hS f ∧
          IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) ∧
        (Stack.IsSurjective B S hS (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f) ∧
          IsFlat B S hS (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f) ∧
          IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
            (Stack.relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPT, part (1).** If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
universally closed and its second factor is separated, then its first factor is universally
closed.

`f` is 2-isomorphic to its graph over `𝒵` followed by the second projection of the canonical
2-fibre product of the cospan `(f ≫ g, g)`. The graph is universally closed because `g` is
separated, the projection is the base change of `f ≫ g` along `g` and so is universally closed
by **Stacks 0514**, and **Stacks 0515** composes them.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_of_comp_of_isSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : UniversallyClosed B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (1): universal closedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isClosed_range_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPT, part (1).** Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.universallyClosed_of_comp_of_isSeparated` the image of
`|𝒳|` in `|𝒴|` is closed for the topology of Stacks 04XL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_range_of_comp_of_isSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : UniversallyClosed B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    @_root_.IsClosed _ (Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)
      (Set.range (Stack.pointsMap B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property 𝒴.val.property f.hom.hom))
declarations.comment: part (1): closed image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isProper_of_comp_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPT, part (2).** If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
proper and its second factor is separated, then its first factor is proper.

Properness of **Stacks 0CL5** is separatedness, finite type and universal closedness. The first
is **Stacks 050M** part (3), whose hypothesis on `Δ_g` is separatedness in the sense of
Stacks 04XB and follows from the properness of `Δ_g` that separatedness of `g` asserts. Finite
type is local finite type, which cancels outright by **Stacks 06U9**, together with
quasi-compactness, which cancels against the quasi-separatedness of `g` by **Stacks 050Y**.
Universal closedness is part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_comp_of_isSeparated (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsProper B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsSeparated B S hS g) :
    IsProper B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2): properness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_le
declarations.doc:
Minimality of the candidate image: the intersection of the closed substacks through which `f`
factors is contained in each of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticImageCandidate_le {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    {Q : ObjectProperty 𝒴.val.val.obj} (hQ : IsClosedSubstack 𝒴 Q)
    (hfac : FactorsThroughSubstack f Q) : schemeTheoreticImageCandidate f ≤ Q
declarations.comment: minimality of the candidate image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorsThroughSubstack_schemeTheoreticImageCandidate
declarations.doc:
The factorization through the candidate image: `f` factors through the intersection of the
closed substacks of `𝒴` through which it factors, because factoring through a strictly full
subcategory is a condition on the objects in the image of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThroughSubstack_schemeTheoreticImageCandidate
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    FactorsThroughSubstack f (schemeTheoreticImageCandidate f)
declarations.comment: the candidate image factors f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSchemeTheoreticImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPU.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. Then the
scheme theoretic image of `f` exists: there is a smallest closed substack of `𝒴` through which
`f` factors, namely `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageCandidate f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSchemeTheoreticImage {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) :
    HasSchemeTheoreticImage f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.le_inverseImage_of_isSchemeTheoreticImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPV**, the containment that induces the morphism. Let a commutative square of
algebraic stacks over `S` be given, with horizontal 1-morphisms `f₁ : 𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒴₁`, `f₂ : 𝒳₂ ⟶ 𝒴₂`
and vertical ones `a : 𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒳₂`, `b : 𝒴₁ ⟶ 𝒴₂`, and let `Pᵢ` be the scheme theoretic image of
`fᵢ`. Then `P₁` is contained in the preimage of `P₂` under `b`.

The preimage of `P₂` cuts out a closed substack of `𝒴₁`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedSubstack_inverseImage`) through which `f₁` factors
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.factorsThroughSubstack_inverseImage`), so the minimality of the scheme
theoretic image applies to it.
declarations.comment: containment

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPV**, the induced 1-morphism. The 1-morphism `b : 𝒴₁ ⟶ 𝒴₂` of a commutative
square of algebraic stacks carries the scheme theoretic image of `f₁` into the scheme theoretic
image of `f₂`, and therefore induces a 1-morphism `𝒵₁ ⟶ 𝒵₂` between them.
declarations.comment: induced_morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageMap_comp_inclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPV**, the right-hand square of the induced diagram: the induced 1-morphism
`𝒵₁ ⟶ 𝒵₂` composed with the inclusion `𝒵₂ ⟶ 𝒴₂` is the inclusion `𝒵₁ ⟶ 𝒴₁` followed by `b`.
declarations.comment: inclusion_square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.schemeTheoreticImageMapFactorizationSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPV**, the left-hand square of the induced diagram. Let `kᵢ : 𝒳ᵢ ⟶ 𝒵ᵢ` be
factorizations of `fᵢ` through the scheme theoretic images. Then the induced 1-morphism
`𝒵₁ ⟶ 𝒵₂` makes the square with `a : 𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒳₂` 2-commute.

Both composites `𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒵₂ ⟶ 𝒴₂` are 2-isomorphic, by the given square and the two
factorizations, and the inclusion of `𝒵₂` is fully faithful, so the 2-isomorphism descends to
`𝒵₂`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def schemeTheoreticImageMapFactorizationSquare {f₁ : 𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒴₁} {f₂ : 𝒳₂ ⟶ 𝒴₂}
    {a : 𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒳₂} {b : 𝒴₁ ⟶ 𝒴₂} (sq : f₁ ≫ b ≅ a ≫ f₂)
    {P₁ : ObjectProperty 𝒴₁.val.val.obj} {P₂ : ObjectProperty 𝒴₂.val.val.obj}
    (h₁ : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f₁ P₁) (h₂ : IsSchemeTheoreticImage f₂ P₂)
    (k₁ : 𝒳₁ ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒴₁ P₁ h₁.isAlgebraicStack)
    (k₂ : 𝒳₂ ⟶ fullSubcategoryAlgebraicStack 𝒴₂ P₂ h₂.isAlgebraicStack)
    (e₁ : k₁ ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒴₁ P₁ h₁.isAlgebraicStack ≅ f₁)
    (e₂ : k₂ ≫ fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒴₂ P₂ h₂.isAlgebraicStack ≅ f₂) :
    k₁ ≫ schemeTheoreticImageMap sq h₁ h₂ ≅ a ≫ k₂
declarations.comment: factorization_square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isEquivalence_fst_of_isSchemeTheoreticImage_partialSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CPW.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces and separated, let `𝒱 ⊆ 𝒴` be an open substack such that
`𝒱 ⟶ 𝒴` is quasi-compact, and let `s : 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒳` be a 1-morphism with `f ∘ s ≅ id_𝒱`, i.e. with a
2-isomorphism `s ≫ f ≅ (𝒱 ⟶ 𝒴)`. Let `P` cut out the scheme theoretic image `𝒴'` of `s`
(Stacks 0CMI). Then `𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴` is an isomorphism over `𝒱`: the projection `𝒴' ×_𝒴 𝒱 ⟶ 𝒱` is an
equivalence of categories.

`s` is quasi-compact by **Stacks 050Y**, as `s ≫ f` is 2-isomorphic to the quasi-compact
`𝒱 ⟶ 𝒴` and `f` is quasi-separated. The projection has a section, so it is essentially surjective
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.essSurj_fst_partialSectionImageSquare`). It is faithful because `f` is,
being representable by algebraic spaces. It is full because every object of `𝒴' ×_𝒴 𝒱`, read in
`𝒱 ×_𝒴 𝒳`, is isomorphic to the image of an object of `𝒱` under the graph of `s`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_iso_partialSectionGraph_obj`, which is where **Stacks 0CMK** and
the separatedness of `f` enter), and the graph is a section of the projection to `𝒱`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_fst_of_isSchemeTheoreticImage_partialSection
    (hrep : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS ι[V]) (hsec : s ≫ f ≅ ι[V])
    {P : ObjectProperty 𝒳.val.val.obj} (hP : IsSchemeTheoreticImage s P) :
    Functor.IsEquivalence (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS ι[V]
      (fullSubcategoryInclusion 𝒳 P hP.isAlgebraicStack ≫ f)).fst.hom.hom.toFunctor
