declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_isFinitePresentation_isClosedImmersion_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQ1.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack over a scheme `S`
to an algebraic space over `S`, with `f` of finite type and quasi-separated and `Y` quasi-compact
and quasi-separated. Then there are a 1-morphism of finite presentation `f' : 𝒳' ⟶ Y` and a
closed immersion `i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` of algebraic stacks over `Y`, that is, with `i ≫ f' ≅ f`.

The source's proof, which approximates `Y` by Noetherian algebraic spaces (Stacks 07SU), takes
place over `Spec ℤ`, where it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_finitePresentation_closedImmersion_overIntegers` with Stacks 07SU
supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasNoetherianApproximation_of_isQuasiCompactSpace`.
Construction A of Stacks 04X5 carries `f` to a quasi-separated 1-morphism, locally of finite
type, from a quasi-compact algebraic stack to the view `Λ Y` of `Y` over `Spec ℤ`, which is again
quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the factorization obtained there descends to `S`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_descent_changeBase`), and finite presentation and being a closed
immersion descend along Construction A.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinitePresentation_isClosedImmersion_of_isFiniteType (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Y hY)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hYqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y) :
    ∃ (𝒳' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
      (f' : 𝒳' ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Y hY) (i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'),
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS f' ∧ IsClosedImmersion B S hS i ∧ Nonempty (i ≫ f' ≅ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.closedImmersionIntoFinitePresentationStatement_holds_overScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQ2.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack over a scheme `S`
to an algebraic space over `S`, with `f` of finite type and separated and `Y` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Then there are a separated 1-morphism of finite presentation `f' : 𝒳' ⟶ Y` and a
closed immersion `i : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'` of algebraic stacks over `Y`, that is, with `i ≫ f' ≅ f`.

The source's proof, which approximates `Y` by Noetherian algebraic spaces (Stacks 07SU), takes
place over `Spec ℤ`, where it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_separated_finitePresentation_closedImmersion_overIntegers`.
Construction A of Stacks 04X5 carries `f` to a separated 1-morphism, locally of finite type,
from a quasi-compact algebraic stack to the view `Λ Y` of `Y` over `Spec ℤ`, which is again
quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the factorization obtained there descends to `S`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_descent_changeBase`), and separatedness, finite presentation
and being a closed immersion descend along Construction A.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedImmersionIntoFinitePresentationStatement_holds_overScheme (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    ClosedImmersionIntoFinitePresentationStatement.{u, w} B S hS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_admissibleBlowup_flat_finitePresentation_closedSubstack
declarations.doc:
**Flattening by blowing up.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack to an
algebraic space and `V ⊆ Y` an open subspace, with (1) `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, (2)
`f` of finite type and quasi-separated, (3) `V` quasi-compact and (4) `𝒳_V ⟶ V` flat and locally
of finite presentation. Then there are a `V`-admissible blowup `b : Y' ⟶ Y` and a closed substack
`𝒳' ⊆ 𝒳_{Y'}` containing every object of `𝒳_{Y'}` over `b⁻¹V` (so `𝒳'_V = 𝒳_V`, `b` being an
isomorphism over `V`) such that `𝒳' ⟶ Y'` is flat and of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_admissibleBlowup_flat_finitePresentation_closedSubstack
    {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Y hY)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.toFunctor)
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS
      (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS hV.1 hY V.ι) f).fst)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS
      (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS hV.1 hY V.ι) f).fst) :
    ∃ (Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : Y' ⟶ ⟨Y, hY⟩),
      Space.IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS ⟨V, hV⟩ b ∧
        ∃ P : ObjectProperty (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS
            (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS Y'.2 hY b.hom) f).pt.val.val.obj,
          IsClosedSubstack _ P ∧
          (∀ x, ((twoFibreProductSquare B S hS
              (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS Y'.2 hY b.hom) f).fst.hom.hom.obj
                x).fiber.as ∈ (V.preimage b.hom).obj (Opposite.op ((twoFibreProductSquare B S hS
                  (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS Y'.2 hY b.hom) f).fst.hom.hom.obj
                    x).base) →
            P x) ∧
          ∀ hP : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS (fullSubcategoryBased _ P),
            IsFlat B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion _ P hP ≫ (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS
              (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS Y'.2 hY b.hom) f).fst) ∧
            IsFinitePresentation B S hS (fullSubcategoryInclusion _ P hP ≫
              (twoFibreProductSquare B S hS
                (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS Y'.2 hY b.hom) f).fst)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_finite_surjective_zariskiLocal_factorization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQ6].** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over
`S`, let `V ⊆ Y` be a quasi-compact open subspace and let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ V` be a surjective and flat
1-morphism of algebraic stacks which is locally of finite presentation. Then there is a finite
surjective morphism `g : Y' ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces such that `V' = g⁻¹(V) ⟶ V` factors Zariski
locally through `f`: there are open immersions `ι j : W j ⟶ Y'` contained in `g⁻¹(V)` (they
factor through `V` over `g`, by `q j`) whose images cover `g⁻¹(V)`, and 1-morphisms
`x j : W j ⟶ 𝒳` with `x j ≫ f` 2-isomorphic to `q j`.

The proof is the source's second paragraph: [Stacks, Proposition 09YC] (in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsFiniteSurjectiveSchemeCover_of_isQuasiCompactSpace`) gives a finite
surjective `π : h_{Y₁} ⟶ Y` from a scheme of the site; `Y₁` is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, `π⁻¹(V)` is a quasi-compact open of `h_{Y₁}`, and the base change of `f` to it is
again surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. The scheme case,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_finite_surjective_zariskiLocal_factorization_of_yoneda`
([Stacks, Tag 0CP0] and [Stacks, Tag 0CNY]), then gives a finite surjective `Y' ⟶ h_{Y₁}`, and
its composite with `π` is the required `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_surjective_zariskiLocal_factorization
    {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.toFunctor)
    {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS V.toFunctor hV.1)
    (hfs : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hff : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hfl : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f) :
    ∃ (Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') (g : Y' ⟶ Y),
      Space.IsFinite B S hS g ∧ Space.IsSurjective B S hS g ∧
      ∃ (J : Type u) (W : J → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hW : ∀ j, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (W j)) (ι : ∀ j, W j ⟶ Y')
        (q : ∀ j, W j ⟶ V.toFunctor)
        (x : ∀ j, algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS (W j) (hW j) ⟶ 𝒳),
        (∀ j, Space.IsOpenImmersion B S hS (ι j)) ∧ (∀ j, ι j ≫ g = q j ≫ V.ι) ∧
        (∀ y : Space.points B S hS Y',
          Space.pointsMap B S hS Y' g y ∈ Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) →
            ∃ j, y ∈ Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS (W j) (ι j))) ∧
        ∀ j, Nonempty (x j ≫ f ≅ algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS (hW j) hV.1 (q j))
declarations.comment: Chow's lemma for algebraic stacks: a flat surjection locally of finite presentation onto a quasi-compact open of a qcqs algebraic space splits Zariski locally after a finite surjective base change.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.hasProperCompactifiableCover_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQ7].** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism from an algebraic stack to an
algebraic space and `V ⊆ Y` an open subspace. Assume that `f` is separated and of finite type,
that `Y` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, that `V` is quasi-compact, and that `𝒳_V` is a
gerbe over `V`. Then there are algebraic spaces `Z`, `Z̄`, an open immersion `j : Z ⟶ Z̄`, a proper
`ḡ : Z̄ ⟶ Y` and a proper `h : Z ⟶ 𝒳` with `h ≫ f` 2-isomorphic to `g = j ≫ ḡ`, such that `|V|`
is contained in the image of `|g|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperCompactifiableCover_of_isGerbeOver {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Y hY)
    (hfs : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.toFunctor)
    (hG : IsGerbeOver B S hS (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS
      (algebraicSpaceStackMap.{u, w} B S hS hV.1 hY V.ι) f).fst) :
    HasProperCompactifiableCover.{u, w} B S hS hY f V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.hasChowCover
declarations.doc:
**Chow's lemma for algebraic stacks (Stacks 0CQ8).** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ Y` be a 1-morphism from an
algebraic stack to an algebraic space over `S`, with `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `f`
separated of finite type. Then there are an algebraic space `X` with a proper surjective
1-morphism `a : X ⟶ 𝒳`, an open immersion `i : X ⟶ X̄` and a proper morphism `p : X̄ ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces such that `a ≫ f` is 2-isomorphic to the 1-morphism induced by `i ≫ p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasChowCover (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : B.Contains S}
    {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS Y hY)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    HasChowCover.{u, w} B S hS hY f
declarations.comment: Chow's lemma for algebraic stacks: the commutative diagram is a 2-isomorphism `a ≫ f ≅ i ≫ p` in the 2-category of algebraic stacks over S, with X and X̄ algebraic spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.InverseSystem.AbelianGroupDerivedLift.exists_lift_of_inverseSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0CQ9 / Lemma 15.88.11.**
Every inverse system `K : Nᵒᵖ ⥤ D(Ab)` of objects of the derived category `D(Ab)`
lifts to an object `M` of `D(Ab(N))`: there exist an object `M` of `D(Ab(N))` and,
for every index `n`, an isomorphism `ψ n : ev_n(M) ≅ K_n` in `D(Ab)`, such that for
every morphism `f : a ⟶ b` of `Nᵒᵖ` the square
`ev_a(M) → ev_b(M) → K_b` and `ev_a(M) → K_a → K_b` commutes, i.e. the isomorphisms
`ψ` are compatible with the transition maps (the induced transition maps `evTrans f`
of `M` on the source, the given transition maps `K.map f` of the system on the
target).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_of_inverseSystem (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory Ab.{u}) :
    ∃ (M : DerivedCategory AbN.{u}) (ψ : ∀ n, (evD n).obj M ≅ K.obj n),
      ∀ ⦃a b : ℕᵒᵖ⦄ (f : a ⟶ b),
        (evTrans f).app M ≫ (ψ b).hom = (ψ a).hom ≫ K.map f

declarations.name: Rlim.isMittagLeffler_iff_isZero_rightDerivedLim_one_and_countable_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQA (Emmanouil).** An inverse system of abelian groups is Mittag--Leffler if and
only if the first derived inverse limit vanishes for it and for the countable direct sum of
copies of it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMittagLeffler_iff_isZero_rightDerivedLim_one_and_countable_coproduct
    (A : Rlim.InvSystemAb.{v}) :
    let F : Rlim.InvSystemAb.{v} ⥤ Ab.{v} := lim
    ∀ (RF : DerivedCategory Rlim.InvSystemAb.{v} ⥤ DerivedCategory Ab.{v})
      (α : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF),
      RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
          (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso Rlim.InvSystemAb.{v} (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) →
        ((A ⋙ forget Ab).IsMittagLeffler ↔
          (IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{v} 1).obj
            (RF.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Rlim.InvSystemAb.{v} 0).obj A))) ∧
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{v} 1).obj
            (RF.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Rlim.InvSystemAb.{v} 0).obj
              (∐ fun _ : Discrete ℕ => A))))))

registrations.name: isMittagLeffler_of_shortExact
registrations.comment:
In a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by the
  natural numbers, if the outer two systems are Mittag-Leffler, then the middle system is
  Mittag-Leffler.

declarations.name: ModuleRightDerivedLimit.rightDerivedInverseLimit_isDerivedLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQD.** The right-derived inverse-limit functor for compatible modules over an
inverse system of rings is, on every object, a derived limit of the associated inverse system in
the derived category of modules over the inverse-limit ring. Equivalently, its value fits in the
canonical distinguished triangle
`R lim K ⟶ ∏ Kₙ ⟶ ∏ Kₙ ⟶ (R lim K)⟦1⟧`, whose middle map is `1 - shift`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rightDerivedInverseLimit_isDerivedLimit
    (A : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}) :
    let B := limit A
    let F : PresheafOfModules.{v} A ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} B := ModuleInverseLimit.inverseLimit A
    ∀ (hF : F.Additive),
      letI := hF
      ∀ (RF : DerivedCategory (PresheafOfModules.{v} A) ⥤
            DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B))
          (α : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
            DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF),
        RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
            (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (PresheafOfModules.{v} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) →
        ∀ K : DerivedCategory (PresheafOfModules.{v} A),
          ∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => (derivedModuleDiagram A K).obj (Opposite.op n),
            Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit (derivedModuleDiagram A K) (RF.obj K)

declarations.name: ModuleRightDerivedLimit.inverseLimit_hasRightDerivedFunctor_and_homology_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQE.** For a complex of compatible modules over an inverse system of rings, the
long exact cohomology sequence of its canonical derived-limit triangle breaks into short exact
sequences
`0 ⟶ R¹ lim H^(p-1)(Kₙ) ⟶ H^p(R lim K) ⟶ lim H^p(Kₙ) ⟶ 0`.

The displayed maps are the cokernel descent of the connecting morphism and the kernel lift of
the following morphism in the long exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem inverseLimit_hasRightDerivedFunctor_and_homology_shortExact
    (A : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{u}) :
    let B := limit A
    let F : PresheafOfModules.{v} A ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} B := ModuleInverseLimit.inverseLimit A
    ∃ (hF : F.Additive),
      letI := hF
      ∃ (RF : DerivedCategory (PresheafOfModules.{v} A) ⥤
            DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B))
          (α : F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
            DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF),
        RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
            (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (PresheafOfModules.{v} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
        ∀ K : DerivedCategory (PresheafOfModules.{v} A),
          ∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
              (ModuleRightDerivedLimit.derivedModuleDiagram A K).obj (Opposite.op n),
            let E := ModuleRightDerivedLimit.derivedModuleDiagram A K
            let P := ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ E.obj (Opposite.op n)
            let d : P ⟶ P := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
              Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ E.obj (Opposite.op n)) n -
                Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ E.obj (Opposite.op n)) (n + 1) ≫
                  E.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
            ∃ (a : RF.obj K ⟶ P) (b : P ⟶ (RF.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
              Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk a d b ∈
                  distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B)) ∧
              ∀ p : ℤ,
                let H : ℤ → PresheafOfModules.{v} A := fun q ↦
                  (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{v} A) q).obj K
                let EH : ℤ → (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} B) := fun q ↦
                  E ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) q
                let MH : ℤ → (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} B) := fun q ↦
                  ModuleInverseLimit.moduleDiagram A (H q)
                let HP : ℤ → ModuleCat.{v} B := fun q ↦
                  (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) q).obj P
                let PH : ℤ → ModuleCat.{v} B := fun q ↦
                  ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (MH q).obj (Opposite.op n)
                let δH : (q : ℤ) → (PH q ⟶ PH q) := fun q ↦ Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
                  Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (MH q).obj (Opposite.op n)) n -
                    Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (MH q).obj (Opposite.op n)) (n + 1) ≫
                      (MH q).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
                let R1lim := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) 1).obj
                  (RF.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (PresheafOfModules.{v} A) 0).obj
                    (H (p - 1))))
                let HpRlim :=
                  (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) p).obj (RF.obj K)
                let limHp := F.obj (H p)
                let T := Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk a d b
                let connecting : HP (p - 1) ⟶ HpRlim :=
                  (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) 0).homologySequenceδ
                    T (p - 1) p (by omega)
                ∃ (eHPrev : EH (p - 1) ≅ MH (p - 1)) (eHCurr : EH p ≅ MH p)
                    (ePrev : HP (p - 1) ≅ PH (p - 1)) (eCurr : HP p ≅ PH p),
                  (∀ n : ℕ, ePrev.hom ≫
                      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (MH (p - 1)).obj (Opposite.op n)) n =
                    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) (p - 1)).map
                        (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ E.obj (Opposite.op n)) n) ≫
                      eHPrev.hom.app (Opposite.op n)) ∧
                  (∀ n : ℕ, eCurr.hom ≫
                      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (MH p).obj (Opposite.op n)) n =
                    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) p).map
                        (Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ E.obj (Opposite.op n)) n) ≫
                      eHCurr.hom.app (Opposite.op n)) ∧
                  (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) (p - 1)).map d ≫
                      ePrev.hom = ePrev.hom ≫ δH (p - 1) ∧
                  (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) p).map d ≫
                      eCurr.hom = eCurr.hom ≫ δH p ∧
                  ∃ (eR1 : R1lim ≅ cokernel (δH (p - 1)))
                    (eLim : limHp ≅ kernel (δH p))
                    (hConnecting : δH (p - 1) ≫ ePrev.inv ≫ connecting = 0)
                    (hKernel : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) p).map a ≫
                      eCurr.hom ≫ δH p = 0),
                    (∀ n : ℕ, eLim.hom ≫ kernel.ι (δH p) ≫
                        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ (MH p).obj (Opposite.op n)) n =
                      limit.π (MH p) (Opposite.op n)) ∧
                    let i : R1lim ⟶ HpRlim := eR1.hom ≫
                      cokernel.desc (δH (p - 1)) (ePrev.inv ≫ connecting) hConnecting
                    let q : HpRlim ⟶ limHp :=
                      kernel.lift (δH p)
                        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) p).map a ≫
                          eCurr.hom)
                        hKernel ≫ eLim.inv
                    ∃ w : i ≫ q = 0, (ShortComplex.mk i q w).ShortExact

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedLimit_isPseudoCoherent_and_baseChange_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQF.** Suppose a tower of rings has surjective transition maps with locally
nilpotent kernels, and its derived module objects are preserved by the base-change maps induced
by their transitions. If all terms are pseudo-coherent, or one term is pseudo-coherent and all
subsequent kernels are nilpotent, then every derived inverse limit is pseudo-coherent and its
canonical base-change map to each term is an isomorphism.

The limit ring is the vertex of the arbitrary limit cone `c`. The distinguished triangle has
the prescribed product difference map for the transitions restricted to that vertex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedLimit_isPseudoCoherent_and_baseChange_iso
    (A : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cone A) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (Kₙ : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A.obj (op n))))
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, Kₙ (n + 1) ⟶
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (Kₙ n))
    (hSurjective : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom)
    (hLocallyNilpotent : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (RingHom.ker (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom).IsLocallyNilpotent)
    (hPseudoCoherent : (∀ n : ℕ, PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (Kₙ n)) ∨
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (Kₙ n₀) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
          IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom))
    (hBaseChange : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsIso (derivedBaseChangeComparison (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom (φ n))) :
    let X : ℕ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} c.pt) := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (c.π.app (op n)).hom).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Kₙ n)
    let t : ∀ n : ℕ, X (n + 1) ⟶ X n := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (c.π.app (op (n + 1))).hom).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (φ n) ≫
        (derivedRestrictScalarsComp (c.π.app (op (n + 1))).hom
          (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom (c.π.app (op n)).hom
          (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (c.w (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)).symm).hom.app (Kₙ n)
    ∀ [HasProduct X] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} c.pt))
      (p : K ⟶ ∏ᶜ X) (δ : ∏ᶜ X ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk p
        (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ Pi.π X n - Pi.π X (n + 1) ≫ t n) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} c.pt)) →
      PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
        IsIso (derivedBaseChangeComparison (c.π.app (op n)).hom (p ≫ Pi.π X n))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedLimit_isPerfect_and_baseChange_iso
declarations.doc:
Suppose a tower of rings has surjective transition maps with locally nilpotent kernels, and
its derived module objects are preserved by the base-change maps induced by their transitions.
If all terms are perfect, or one term is perfect and every subsequent transition kernel is
nilpotent, then every derived inverse limit over the vertex of the limit cone `c` is perfect and
its canonical base-change map to each term is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedLimit_isPerfect_and_baseChange_iso
    (A : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cone A) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (Kₙ : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A.obj (op n))))
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, Kₙ (n + 1) ⟶
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (Kₙ n))
    (hSurjective : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom)
    (hLocallyNilpotent : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (RingHom.ker (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom).IsLocallyNilpotent)
    (hPerfect : (∀ n : ℕ, StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (Kₙ n)) ∨
      ∃ n₀ : ℕ, StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (Kₙ n₀) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
          IsNilpotent (RingHom.ker (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom))
    (hBaseChange : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsIso (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedBaseChangeComparison
        (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom (φ n))) :
    let X : ℕ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} c.pt) := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (c.π.app (op n)).hom).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Kₙ n)
    let t : ∀ n : ℕ, X (n + 1) ⟶ X n := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (c.π.app (op (n + 1))).hom).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (φ n) ≫
        (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedRestrictScalarsComp (c.π.app (op (n + 1))).hom
          (A.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom (c.π.app (op n)).hom
          (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (c.w (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)).symm).hom.app (Kₙ n)
    ∀ [HasProduct X] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} c.pt))
      (p : K ⟶ ∏ᶜ X) (δ : ∏ᶜ X ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk p
        (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ Pi.π X n - Pi.π X (n + 1) ≫ t n) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} c.pt)) →
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
        IsIso (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedBaseChangeComparison
          (c.π.app (op n)).hom (p ≫ Pi.π X n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_derivedTensor_adicQuotient_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQH], the derived completeness of the reductions.** For `ℐ` of finite type,
`K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/ℐⁿ` is derived complete along `ℐ`: multiplication by `fⁿ`, for a local section `f`
of `ℐ` over `U`, is zero on its restriction to `U`. The source states this for `n ≥ 1`; it holds
for every `n`, `𝒪/ℐ⁰` being zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_derivedTensor_adicQuotient_of_isFiniteType
    [I.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (n : ℕ) :
    IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj
        (adicQuotientObj X I n))
declarations.comment: first assertion: `K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/ℐⁿ` is derived complete for `n ≥ 1`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_not_isIso_derivedCompletionComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQH], the comparison map is not an isomorphism in general.** There are a
ringed site `(𝒞, 𝒪)`, a sheaf of ideals `ℐ` of finite type and `K ∈ D(𝒪)` such that no
comparison map `K^∧ ⟶ R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/ℐⁿ)` — no map `c` into a derived limit `L` of the
reduction tower whose composites with the projections are the factorizations — is an
isomorphism. The witness is the one-point ringed site of `k[X] ⋉ k[X, X⁻¹]/k[X]` for `k = ℤ`,
with `ℐ = (X)` and `K = (𝒪/ℐ)[0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_isIso_derivedCompletionComparison :
    ∃ (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
      (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
        (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
      (_ : I.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType)
      (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))),
      ∀ (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
        (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩)
        (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
        (c : (derivedCompletion X I).obj K ⟶ L),
        Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ =>
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              (adicReductionTower X I K).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
          distTriang
            (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) →
        (∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
          derivedCompletionAdicFactor X I K (n + 1)) →
        ¬ IsIso c
declarations.comment: fifth assertion: in general the comparison map is not an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.existsUnique_derivedCompletion_factorization_adicQuotient
declarations.doc:
**The canonical factorization.** The derived reduction `K ⟶ K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/ℐⁿ` factors uniquely
as `K ⟶ K^∧ ⟶ K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/ℐⁿ` through the derived completion, for an arbitrary sheaf of ideals
and an arbitrary reflector.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_derivedCompletion_factorization_adicQuotient
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! g : (derivedCompletion X I).obj K ⟶
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj
          (adicQuotientObj X I n),
      (derivedCompletionUnit X I).app K ≫ g = adicQuotientReduction X I K n
declarations.comment:
second assertion: the canonical factorization `K → K^∧ → K ⊗^L O/I^n` of the
  canonical map, for the derived completion functor of Tag 099F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionAdicFactor_comp_map
declarations.doc:
**The factorizations are compatible for varying `n`.** The factorization through `K^∧` of
the reduction modulo `ℐⁿ`, followed by the transition map `𝒪/ℐⁿ ⟶ 𝒪/ℐᵐ`, is the factorization
of the reduction modulo `ℐᵐ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCompletionAdicFactor_comp_map
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) :
    derivedCompletionAdicFactor X I K n ≫
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).map
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) 0).map
            (Stacks.Sites.adicQuotientModuleMap (X := X) I h)) =
      derivedCompletionAdicFactor X I K m
declarations.comment: third assertion: the factorizations are compatible for varying `n`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_derivedCompletionComparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map `K^∧ ⟶ R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/ℐⁿ)`.** The compatible factorizations
`K^∧ ⟶ K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/ℐⁿ⁺¹` lift through the Milnor triangle of the reduction tower to a map into its
derived limit, whose composite with each projection is the corresponding factorization.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedCompletionComparison
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) :
    ∃ (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
      (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩)
      (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (c : (derivedCompletion X I).obj K ⟶ L),
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ =>
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              (adicReductionTower X I K).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
          distTriang
            (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (adicReductionTower X I K).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
          derivedCompletionAdicFactor X I K (n + 1)
declarations.comment:
fourth assertion: the comparison map `K^∧ → R lim (K ⊗^L O/I^n)` induced by the
  compatible factorizations; `R lim` is presented by its Milnor triangle

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_derivedSectionsOverObject
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQI], the left hand side, for a sheaf of ideals with nilpotent sections.**
The canonical map `RΓ(U, K) ⟶ RΓ(U, K^∧)` is invertible.

Together with `isDerivedComplete_derivedSectionsOverObject`, whose content is that the right hand
side `RΓ(U, K)^∧` is `RΓ(U, K)` as well, this is the equality `RΓ(U, K^∧) = RΓ(U, K)^∧` of the
source in this regime, compatibly with the canonical maps on both sides.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_derivedSectionsOverObject
    [𝓘.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    [(ObjectProperty.ι (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X 𝓘)).IsRightAdjoint]
    (hgen : IsGeneratedAsIdealSheafBySectionsOver X 𝓘 U f)
    (hnil : ∀ (V : X.C) (g : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).obj.obj (op V)),
      g ∈ 𝓘.toSubmodule.obj (op V) → IsNilpotent g)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) :
    IsIso ((derivedSectionsOverObject X U).map ((derivedCompletionUnit X 𝓘).app K))
declarations.comment:
the left hand side: the canonical map `RΓ(U, K) ⟶ RΓ(U, K^∧)` is invertible, for a
  sheaf of ideals of finite type all of whose local sections are nilpotent — the hypothesis under
  which this library has the derived completion functor of [Stacks, Tag 099F]. The equality with
  `RΓ(U, K)^∧` is this together with `isDerivedComplete_derivedSectionsOverObject`. The general
  case needs [Stacks, Tags 0A0F, 0BLX]; the first is `derivedCompletion_restrict`, the second is
  not available as an identity here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_derivedSectionsOverObject_of_forall_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQI], the left hand side, for a sheaf of ideals with nilpotent sections, with
the derived completion functor produced rather than assumed.** This is
`isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_derivedSectionsOverObject` without its `IsRightAdjoint` instance
argument: the left adjoint of the inclusion of derived complete objects is discharged inside the
statement from the nilpotence hypothesis, by
`isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_isFiniteType_of_forall_isNilpotent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_derivedSectionsOverObject_of_forall_isNilpotent
    [𝓘.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (hgen : IsGeneratedAsIdealSheafBySectionsOver X 𝓘 U f)
    (hnil : ∀ (V : X.C) (g : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).obj.obj (op V)),
      g ∈ 𝓘.toSubmodule.obj (op V) → IsNilpotent g)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) :
    letI : (ObjectProperty.ι (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X 𝓘)).IsRightAdjoint :=
      isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_isFiniteType_of_forall_isNilpotent X 𝓘 hnil
    IsIso ((derivedSectionsOverObject X U).map ((derivedCompletionUnit X 𝓘).app K))
declarations.comment:
the left hand side: the canonical map `RΓ(U, K) ⟶ RΓ(U, K^∧)` is invertible, for a
  sheaf of ideals of finite type all of whose local sections are nilpotent — the hypothesis under
  which this library has the derived completion functor of [Stacks, Tag 099F]. That functor is
  *produced* from the nilpotence hypothesis rather than assumed: the `IsRightAdjoint` instance is
  discharged inside the statement. The equality with `RΓ(U, K)^∧` is this together with
  `isDerivedComplete_derivedSectionsOverObject`. The general case needs
  [Stacks, Tags 0A0F, 0BLX]; the first is `derivedCompletion_restrict`, the second is not
  available as an identity here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_derivedSectionsOverObject
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQI], the right hand side, for a sheaf of ideals with nilpotent sections.**
`RΓ(U, K)` is derived complete along `I = (f_1, …, f_r) ⊂ A = 𝒪(U)`, so its derived completion is
itself.

Together with `isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_derivedSectionsOverObject` this is the equality
`RΓ(U, K^∧) = RΓ(U, K)^∧` of the source in this regime. The completion is along the ideal
generated by the chosen sections, not along `𝓘(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_derivedSectionsOverObject
    (hgen : IsGeneratedAsIdealSheafBySectionsOver X 𝓘 U f)
    (hnil : ∀ (V : X.C) (g : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).obj.obj (op V)),
      g ∈ 𝓘.toSubmodule.obj (op V) → IsNilpotent g)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) :
    _root_.IsDerivedComplete (localIdeal X U f)
      ((derivedSectionsOverObject X U).obj K)
declarations.comment:
the right hand side `RΓ(U, K)^∧`, identified with `RΓ(U, K)` by its being already
  derived complete along `I = (f_1, …, f_r) ⊂ 𝒪(U)`, for a sheaf of ideals all of whose local
  sections are nilpotent. The completion is along the ideal the chosen sections generate and not
  along `𝓘(U)`, which the source warns need not be the same ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.nonempty_iso_derivedSectionsOverObject_derivedCompletion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CQI].** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` be a sheaf of ideals of
finite type and let `K ↦ K^∧` be the derived completion of [Stacks, Tag 099F]. Let `U` be an
object of `𝒞` such that `ℐ` is generated as an ideal sheaf by `f_1, …, f_r ∈ ℐ(U)`, and set
`A = 𝒪(U)` and `I = (f_1, …, f_r) ⊂ A`. Then, for every `K ∈ D(𝒪)`,
```
RΓ(U, K^∧) = RΓ(U, K)^∧   in D(A),
```
the right hand side being the derived completion of `RΓ(U, K)` along `I`.

`I` is the ideal of `A` generated by the chosen sections and is not `ℐ(U)`: the source warns
that the two may differ, and neither side of the statement mentions `ℐ(U)`.

Derived completion commutes with localization
([Stacks, Tag 0A0F], `derivedCompletionRestrictIso`), so `K^∧|_U` is the derived completion of
`K|_U` along `ℐ|_U`; on the localized ringed site `(𝒞/U, 𝒪_U)` the sections `f_i` are global
sections generating `ℐ|_U`, so [Stacks, Tag 0BLX] gives
`RΓ(𝒞/U, (K|_U)^∧) = RΓ(𝒞/U, K|_U)^∧`; and `RΓ(U, -)` is `RΓ(𝒞/U, (-)|_U)` by
[Stacks, Tag 0D6F] in its `A`-linear functor-level form,
`derivedSectionsOverObjectIsoSliceModule`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_derivedSectionsOverObject_derivedCompletion
    (_hf : ∀ i, f i ∈ 𝓘.toSubmodule.obj (op U))
    (hgen : idealOfGlobalSections (X.over U)
      (fun i => globalSectionOfTerminalSection (X := X.over U) Over.mkIdTerminal (f i)) =
        overIdeal 𝓘 U)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    Nonempty ((derivedSectionsOverObject X U).obj ((derivedCompletion X 𝓘).obj K) ≅
      (DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionFunctor (sectionRing X U) f).obj
        ((derivedSectionsOverObject X U).obj K))
declarations.comment: the whole remark, at the source's own hypotheses — `(𝒞, 𝒪)` a ringed site, `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` a sheaf of ideals of finite type, `K ↦ K^∧` the derived completion of [Stacks, Tag 099F], `U` an object over which `ℐ` is generated as an ideal sheaf by `f_1, …, f_r ∈ ℐ(U)`, `A = 𝒪(U)` and `I = (f_1, …, f_r) ⊂ A`: the displayed identity `RΓ(U, K^∧) = RΓ(U, K)^∧` in `D(A)` for every `K` of `D(𝒪)`, the right hand side being the derived completion of `RΓ(U, K)` along `I`. Both completion functors are produced: the one on `D(𝒪)` is the reflector of [Stacks, Tag 099F] at a finite-type ideal sheaf and the one on `D(A)` is the reflector of [Stacks, Tag 0G3E] along `I`. The proof is the source's, by [Stacks, Tag 0A0F] and [Stacks, Tag 0BLX], and `I` is the ideal the chosen sections generate rather than `ℐ(U)`, which the source warns need not be the same ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.classifyingQuotientStackEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQJ**, the leg `[B/G] ≌ [[B/G]]`.  The quotient stack `[B/G]` of the trivial
action of `G` on `B` (Stacks 044Q part (2), the quotient stack of the action groupoid of
Stacks 0444) is equivalent over the big fppf site of `S` to `[[B/G]]`, the stack of fppf
`G`-torsors with an equivariant morphism to `B`.  This is Stacks 04WM at `X = B`.
declarations.statement:
def classifyingQuotientStackEquivalence :
    StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (Stack.quotientStackOfAction ⟨B, hB⟩ G.obj.X (𝟙_ (Over B)) G.property hB).p
      (TorsorWithMap.projection hB G (𝟙_ (Over B)))
declarations.comment: the leg [B/G] ≌ [[B/G]] over the big fppf site, Stacks 04WM at X = B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.classifyingStackEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQJ.** Let `S` be a scheme, `B` an algebraic space over `S` and `G` a group
algebraic space over `B`.  Then the stacks in groupoids over `(Sch/S)_fppf`
`[B/G]`, `[[B/G]]`, `G-Torsors` and `𝒢/ℬ-Torsors` are all canonically equivalent: this gives
equivalences over the site
`[B/G] ≌ [[B/G]]`, `[[B/G]] ≌ G-Torsors` and `G-Torsors ≌ 𝒢/ℬ-Torsors`, and, if `G ⟶ B` is flat
and locally of finite presentation, `G-Torsors ≌ G-Principal`.

Each is the canonical one:
* the forward functor of `[B/G] ≌ [[B/G]]` extends the pointwise comparison `F_p`
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.actionPointwiseComparison`) sending a point `b : U ⟶ B` to the
  trivial torsor, by a natural isomorphism lying over identities (Stacks 04WM at `X = B`);
* the forward functor of `[[B/G]] ≌ G-Torsors` forgets the equivariant map to `B`;
* the forward functor of `G-Torsors ≌ 𝒢/ℬ-Torsors` is the comparison functor of Stacks 04UT;
* the forward functor of `G-Torsors ≌ G-Principal` is the canonical inclusion
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FppfTorsors.toPrincipal`.
declarations.statement:
def classifyingStackEquivalences :
    { c : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (Stack.quotientStackOfAction ⟨B, hB⟩ G.obj.X (𝟙_ (Over B)) G.property hB).p
          (TorsorWithMap.projection hB G (𝟙_ (Over B))) ×
        StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver (TorsorWithMap.projection hB G (𝟙_ (Over B)))
          (FppfTorsors.projection hB G) ×
        StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver (FppfTorsors.projection hB G)
          (SheafTorsors.projection G.obj) ×
        (IsFlat 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom → IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom →
          StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver (FppfTorsors.projection hB G)
            (PrincipalHomogeneousSpaces.projection hB G)) //
      (∃ α : Stack.pointwiseToQuotientStack
            (groupoidOfAction ⟨B, hB⟩ G.obj.X (𝟙_ (Over B)) G.property hB).groupoid ⋙
              c.1.hom.functor ≅
            actionPointwiseComparison hB G (𝟙_ (Over B)) hB,
          ∀ A : (actionPointwiseCategory hB G (𝟙_ (Over B)) hB).obj,
            (TorsorWithMap.projection hB G (𝟙_ (Over B))).IsHomLift (𝟙 A.base) (α.hom.app A)) ∧
        c.2.1.hom.functor =
          TorsorWithMap.forget hB G (𝟙_ (Over B)) ⋙ torsorObjComparisonInverse hB G ∧
        c.2.2.1.hom.functor = FppfTorsors.comparison hB G ∧
        ∀ hflat hlfp, (c.2.2.2 hflat hlfp).hom.functor = FppfTorsors.toPrincipal hB G }
declarations.comment: the whole lemma: [B/G] ≌ [[B/G]] ≌ G-Torsors ≌ 𝒢/ℬ-Torsors over the big fppf site, and G-Torsors ≌ G-Principal for G ⟶ B flat and locally of finite presentation, each with its canonical forward functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fppfTorsorsEquivPrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQJ.** For `G ⟶ B` flat and locally of finite presentation the canonical functor
`G-Torsors ⥤ G-Principal` is an equivalence of categories, with quasi-inverse the functor
reading a principal homogeneous space as an fppf torsor and with identity unit and counit.
declarations.statement:
def fppfTorsorsEquivPrincipal (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B)
    (G : GroupAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B hB) (hflat : IsFlat 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation 𝒞 S hS G.obj.X.hom) :
    FppfTorsors hB G ≌ PrincipalHomogeneousSpaces hB G
declarations.comment: G-Torsors ≌ G-Principal, for G ⟶ B flat and locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FppfTorsors.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 04UT**, with nothing carried, and with it the `𝒢/ℬ-Torsors` leg of **Stacks
0CQJ**: the comparison functor `G-Torsors ⥤ 𝒢/ℬ-Torsors` is an equivalence of stacks in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`.

The hypothesis every earlier rendering carried is the object half of Stacks 04U1, equivalently
Stacks 04S6 part (3), which is now the theorem
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBootstrapAlgebraicSpaceAlongFlatSurjection`.

theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_comparison (hB : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS B)

      (comparison hB G))

theorem universallyClosed_of_surjective_comp

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isProper_of_discreteExistenceAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CQM.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` and `h : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over
`S`. Assume that `𝒴` is locally Noetherian, that `f` and `h` are of finite type, that `f` is
separated, and that the image of `|h| : |𝒰| → |𝒳|` is dense in `|𝒳|`. If for every
2-commutative diagram `Spec K ⟶ 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴`, `Spec A ⟶ 𝒴`, with `A` a discrete valuation ring
with field of fractions `K` and a 2-arrow `γ : y ∘ j → f ∘ h ∘ u`, there are an extension
`K'/K` of fields and a valuation ring `A' ⊂ K'` dominating `A` such that the category of dotted
arrows of the induced diagram for `f` is nonempty, then `f` is proper.

`𝒴` locally Noetherian is the existence of a smooth surjective atlas by a locally Noetherian
scheme (`HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas`). The valuative hypothesis is
`ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistenceAlong B S hS h f`: a diagram of the statement is a valuative
square for `f` (Stacks 0CLK) over a discrete valuation ring whose generic point `x` is `u ≫ h`,
its 2-arrow being the square's `γ`; the induced diagram over `A'` with its 2-arrow `γ'` is the
square's restriction along the dominating extension (`e.inducedGamma`), and its category of
dotted arrows is that of Stacks 0CLA (`CategoryTheory.DottedArrow`).

The proof is the source's: the reduction to an affine locally Noetherian base and an affine
source (`isProper_of_discreteExistenceAlong_of_affineCore`), and the affine case
(`universallyClosed_of_discreteExistenceAlong_affineCore`), which uses
Chow's lemma for algebraic stacks over a Noetherian base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_discreteExistenceAlong
    {𝒰 𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (h : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒴 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hh : IsFiniteType B S hS h) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hdense : @Dense _ (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val) (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS h)))
    (hlift : ValuativeCriterion.DiscreteExistenceAlong B S hS h f) :
    IsProper B S hS f

declarations.name: Stacks.Triangulated.RightOrthogonal.inRightOrthogonal_iff_postcomp_bijective
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 0CQQ / Lemma 13.40.2.

Let `A ⊆ D` (described by `P`) be a full subcategory invariant under all shifts
(up to isomorphism), and let `X --f--> Y --g--> Z --h--> X[1]` be a distinguished
triangle. Then `Z` is in the right orthogonal `Aᗮ` if and only if, for every
object `A` of `A`, the map `f_* : Hom(A, X) → Hom(A, Y)`, `g ↦ g ≫ f`, is an
isomorphism of abelian groups (here expressed as a bijection).

Proof outline (as in the source), applying the homological functor `Hom(A,-)`:
* `(1) ⇒ (2)`: injectivity of `f_*` uses the inverse-rotated triangle
  `Z⟦-1⟧ → X → Y` and `coyoneda_exact₂`: a kernel element factors through
  `Z⟦-1⟧`, which vanishes by `hom_to_shift_eq_zero`; surjectivity uses
  `coyoneda_exact₂` on `T` since `u ≫ g = 0` for any `u : A ⟶ Y` (as `Z ∈ Aᗮ`).
* `(2) ⇒ (1)`: for `u : A ⟶ Z`, first `u ≫ h = 0` by injectivity of `· ≫ f⟦1⟧`
  (Helper 3 and `bijective_postcomp_shift` transport bijectivity to `Hom(A, X⟦1⟧)`) together with
  `comp_distTriang_mor_zero₂₃` on the rotated triangle; then `coyoneda_exact₂` on
  the rotated triangle factors `u = v ≫ g`, surjectivity of `f_*` gives `v = w ≫ f`,
  and `f ≫ g = 0` yields `u = w ≫ (f ≫ g) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inRightOrthogonal_iff_postcomp_bijective
    (P : C → Prop) (hP : InvariantUnderAllShifts P)
    (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles) :
    InRightOrthogonal P T.obj₃ ↔
      ∀ (A : C), P A → Function.Bijective (fun g : A ⟶ T.obj₁ => g ≫ T.mor₁)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isTriangulated_extensionProduct_of_le_rightOrthogonal
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a triangulated category, let `A` and `B` be triangulated subcategories of `C`
with `B` contained in the right orthogonal of `A`. Then the objects `X` of `C` that fit in a
distinguished triangle `A' ⟶ X ⟶ B' ⟶ A'⟦1⟧` with `A'` in `A` and `B'` in `B` form a
triangulated subcategory of `C`: they are stable under shifts, two out of three of them in a
distinguished triangle forces the third, and they are stable under direct sums. For
`B = A.rightOrthogonal` this is the property `P` of [Stacks, Tag 0CQR].
declarations.statement:
theorem isTriangulated_extensionProduct_of_le_rightOrthogonal
    (A B : ObjectProperty C) [A.IsTriangulated] [B.IsTriangulated]
    (hB : B ≤ A.rightOrthogonal) :
    (A.extensionProduct B).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isLeftAdjoint_ι_iff_extensionProduct_rightOrthogonal_eq_top_and_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a pretriangulated category and let `A : ObjectProperty C` be invariant under all
shifts, for instance a triangulated subcategory of `C`. Then the inclusion
`A.ι : A.FullSubcategory ⥤ C` has a right adjoint if and only if every object `X` of `C` fits in
a distinguished triangle `A' ⟶ X ⟶ B ⟶ A'⟦1⟧` with `A'` satisfying `A` and `B` in the right
orthogonal of `A`, i.e. if and only if `A.extensionProduct A.rightOrthogonal = ⊤`; and in that
case `A` is saturated, i.e. thick ([Stacks, Tag 05RB]), and the objects isomorphic to an object
satisfying `A` are exactly the objects of the left orthogonal of `A.rightOrthogonal`, so a
strictly full such `A` satisfies `A = ᗮ(Aᗮ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_ι_iff_extensionProduct_rightOrthogonal_eq_top_and_isSaturated
    (A : ObjectProperty C) [A.IsStableUnderShift ℤ] :
    (A.ι.IsLeftAdjoint ↔ A.extensionProduct A.rightOrthogonal = ⊤) ∧
      (A.extensionProduct A.rightOrthogonal = ⊤ →
        A.IsSaturated ∧ A.isoClosure = A.rightOrthogonal.leftOrthogonal)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isRightAdjoint_ι_iff_extensionProduct_leftOrthogonal_self_eq_top_and_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a pretriangulated category and let `B : ObjectProperty C` be invariant under all
shifts, for instance a triangulated subcategory of `C`. Then the inclusion
`B.ι : B.FullSubcategory ⥤ C` has a left adjoint if and only if every object `X` of `C` fits in a
distinguished triangle `A ⟶ X ⟶ B' ⟶ A⟦1⟧` with `A` in the left orthogonal of `B` and `B'`
satisfying `B`, i.e. if and only if `B.leftOrthogonal.extensionProduct B = ⊤`; and in that case
`B` is saturated, i.e. thick ([Stacks, Tag 05RB]), and the objects isomorphic to an object
satisfying `B` are exactly the objects of the right orthogonal of `B.leftOrthogonal`, so a
strictly full such `B` satisfies `B = (ᗮB)ᗮ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightAdjoint_ι_iff_extensionProduct_leftOrthogonal_self_eq_top_and_isSaturated
    (B : ObjectProperty C) [B.IsStableUnderShift ℤ] :
    (B.ι.IsRightAdjoint ↔ B.leftOrthogonal.extensionProduct B = ⊤) ∧
      (B.leftOrthogonal.extensionProduct B = ⊤ →
        B.IsSaturated ∧ B.isoClosure = B.leftOrthogonal.rightOrthogonal)

declarations.name: open_mapping_lemma
declarations.doc:
Let `u : N → M` be a continuous homomorphism of topological abelian groups. Assume that `M`
is separated, and that `N` is complete (which, by `IsGroupComplete`, includes separatedness of
`N`), linearly topologized, and has a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of `0`. Then
exactly one of the following two statements holds:

1. `u` is open; or
2. there exists an open subgroup `N' ⊆ N` such that the image `u(N')` is nowhere dense in `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem open_mapping_lemma
    {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [TopologicalSpace N] [IsTopologicalAddGroup N]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [TopologicalSpace M] [IsTopologicalAddGroup M]
    [T2Space M]
    (u : N →+ M) (hu : Continuous u)
    (hNcomplete : IsGroupComplete N)
    (hNlin : IsLinearlyTopologized N)
    (hNcount : HasCountableFundamentalSystem N) :
    Xor (IsOpenMap u)
      (∃ N' : AddSubgroup N, IsOpen (N' : Set N) ∧ IsNowhereDense (u '' (N' : Set N)))

declarations.name: Rlim.Hom.exists_shortExact_map_from_isHomotopyColimit
declarations.doc:
Let `F : ℕ ⥤ D` be a system in a pretriangulated category and let `K` be a derived colimit
of `F`. For every `L`, there is a short exact sequence
`0 → R¹ lim Hom(F n, L[-1]) → Hom(K, L) → lim Hom(F n, L) → 0`.

Here `R¹ lim` is written as the cokernel of `1 - shift` on the product of the inverse system
`Hom(F n, L[-1])`, using the explicit description of derived inverse limits from Tag 07KW.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_shortExact_map_from_isHomotopyColimit
    {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] [Preadditive D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    (F : ℕ ⥤ D) [HasCoproduct F.obj] (K L : D) (hK : IsHomotopyColimit F K) :
    let A₀ : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v} := F.op ⋙ preadditiveYoneda.obj L
    let A₁ : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v} := F.op ⋙ preadditiveYoneda.obj (L⟦(-1 : ℤ)⟧)
    let P₁ : AddCommGrpCat.{v} := ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ A₁.obj (Opposite.op n)
    let shift₁ : P₁ ⟶ P₁ := Pi.lift fun n ↦
      Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ A₁.obj (Opposite.op n)) (n + 1) ≫
        A₁.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    let δ₁ : P₁ ⟶ P₁ := 𝟙 P₁ - shift₁
    let H : AddCommGrpCat.{v} := (preadditiveYoneda.obj L).obj (Opposite.op K)
    ∃ (i : cokernel δ₁ ⟶ H) (p : H ⟶ limit A₀) (z : i ≫ p = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk i p z).ShortExact

declarations.name: DerivedCompleteTorsion.exists_pow_smul_top_eq_bot_of_isDerivedCompleteModule_of_isIPowerTorsion
declarations.doc:
If `I` is finitely generated and `M` is both derived complete and `I`-power torsion, then a
single power of `I` annihilates all of `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_smul_top_eq_bot_of_isDerivedCompleteModule_of_isIPowerTorsion
    (I : Ideal A) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A) (hI : I.FG)
    (hM : IsDerivedCompleteModule I M)
    (htors : IsIPowerTorsion A M I) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M) = ⊥

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentι
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. The inclusion functor
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` has a right adjoint `DQ_X`.
declarations.statement: theorem isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentι : (quasiCoherentι X).IsLeftAdjoint

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_quasiCoherentι
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `X` the inclusion `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` has a
right adjoint `DQ_X` together with a `Functor.CommShift ℤ` structure making the adjunction
triangulated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_quasiCoherentι :
    ∃ (DQ : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
      (adj : quasiCoherentι X ⊣ DQ) (_ : DQ.CommShift ℤ), adj.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the coherator is exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.coheratorDerivedPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Derived direct image commutes with the coherator.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
schemes along which `Rf_*` preserves quasi-coherence of cohomology — as it does whenever `f` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, by [Stacks, Tag 08D5] part (1) — and suppose the inclusions
`D_QCoh ⥤ D` admit right adjoints `DQ_X` and `DQ_Y` on `X` and on `Y`. Then the two functors
`D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` given by `Rf_* ∘ DQ_X` and by `DQ_Y ∘ Rf_*` are canonically isomorphic.

Both are right adjoint to `Lf^* : D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`, which lands in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` by
[Stacks, Tag 08DW] part (1), so they are identified by uniqueness of right adjoints.
declarations.statement:
def coheratorDerivedPushforwardIso :
    DQX ⋙ quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f hpush ≅ derivedPushforward f ⋙ DQY

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.coheratorDerivedPushforwardIsoOfQcqs
declarations.doc:
Derived direct image commutes with the coherator. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes and suppose the inclusions `D_QCoh ⥤ D` admit right adjoints
`DQ_X` and `DQ_Y` on `X` and on `Y`. Then

`Rf_* ∘ DQ_X ≅ DQ_Y ∘ Rf_*`

as functors `D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`.

This is `Stacks.Duality.coheratorDerivedPushforwardIso` with its preservation hypothesis
discharged: for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism `Rf_*` sends `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into
`D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, which is part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 08D5] in the form
`Stacks.Duality.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.mayerVietorisTriangle
declarations.doc:
The canonical triangle

`DQ_X(K) ⟶ Rj_{U,*}DQ_U(K|_U) ⊕ Rj_{V,*}DQ_V(K|_V) ⟶ Rj_{U ∩ V,*}DQ_{U ∩ V}(K|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶`

attached to a scheme `X`, two opens `U`, `V` of `X`, coherators `DQ_X`, `DQ_U`, `DQ_V`,
`DQ_{U ∩ V}` with `DQ_X` commuting with the shift, an object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)`, and the last two maps
`mor₂`, `mor₃` of the Mayer--Vietoris triangle of [Stacks, Tag 08BV] for the cover `X = U ∪ V`.

It is the image under `DQ_X` of that Mayer--Vietoris triangle, conjugated by
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.mayerVietorisMiddleIso` and
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.mayerVietorisThirdIso`: the first map is `DQ_X` of the canonical
`biprod.lift` of the two units of `j_W^* ⊣ Rj_{W,*}` followed by the middle identification, the
second is `DQ_X(mor₂)` read through both identifications, and the third is `DQ_X(mor₃)` read
through the third identification and the commutation of `DQ_X` with the shift.
declarations.statement:
def mayerVietorisTriangle [DQX.CommShift ℤ]
    (mor₂ : restrictPushforward U K ⊞ restrictPushforward V K ⟶ restrictPushforward (U ⊓ V) K)
    (mor₃ : restrictPushforward (U ⊓ V) K ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) :
    Triangle (quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
declarations.comment: the canonical triangle, as data

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.mayerVietorisTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `X = U ∪ V` with `U` and `V`
quasi-compact open, and let `DQ_X`, `DQ_U`, `DQ_V`, `DQ_{U ∩ V}` be coherators — right adjoints of
the inclusions `D_QCoh ⥤ D`. Then for every object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` there is a distinguished
triangle

`DQ_X(K) ⟶ Rj_{U,*}DQ_U(K|_U) ⊕ Rj_{V,*}DQ_V(K|_V) ⟶ Rj_{U ∩ V,*}DQ_{U ∩ V}(K|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶`

in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mayerVietorisTriangle_distinguished (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    ∃ (f : DQX.obj K ⟶
          coheratorPushforwardOpens U DQU K ⊞ coheratorPushforwardOpens V DQV K)
      (g : coheratorPushforwardOpens U DQU K ⊞ coheratorPushforwardOpens V DQV K ⟶
          coheratorPushforwardOpens (U ⊓ V) DQUV K)
      (h : coheratorPushforwardOpens (U ⊓ V) DQUV K ⟶ (DQX.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang (quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
declarations.comment: the distinguished triangle of the tag, over arbitrary coherators

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_distTriang_rightAdjoint_quasiCoherentι
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CR2].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme covered by two
quasi-compact opens, `X = U ∪ V`, and write `DQ_Z` for the coherator of `Z`, the right adjoint of
the inclusion `D_QCoh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ D(𝒪_Z)` whose existence for `Z` quasi-compact and quasi-separated is
[Stacks, Tag 0CR0] (`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentι`). Then for every
object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` there is a distinguished triangle

`DQ_X(K) ⟶ Rj_{U,*}DQ_U(K|_U) ⊕ Rj_{V,*}DQ_V(K|_V) ⟶ Rj_{U ∩ V,*}DQ_{U ∩ V}(K|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶`

in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

The four coherators are the ones [Stacks, Tag 0CR0] produces at `X`, `U`, `V` and `U ∩ V`: the
three opens are quasi-compact — `U ∩ V` because `X` is quasi-separated — and quasi-separated,
being opens of a quasi-separated scheme. The triangle is then
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.mayerVietorisTriangle_distinguished` at those coherators.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distTriang_rightAdjoint_quasiCoherentι (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    letI := isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentι X
    letI := isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentι U.toScheme
    letI := isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentι V.toScheme
    letI := isLeftAdjoint_quasiCoherentι (U ⊓ V).toScheme
    ∃ (f : (quasiCoherentι X).rightAdjoint.obj K ⟶
          coheratorPushforwardOpens U (quasiCoherentι U.toScheme).rightAdjoint K ⊞
            coheratorPushforwardOpens V (quasiCoherentι V.toScheme).rightAdjoint K)
      (g : coheratorPushforwardOpens U (quasiCoherentι U.toScheme).rightAdjoint K ⊞
            coheratorPushforwardOpens V (quasiCoherentι V.toScheme).rightAdjoint K ⟶
          coheratorPushforwardOpens (U ⊓ V) (quasiCoherentι (U ⊓ V).toScheme).rightAdjoint K)
      (h : coheratorPushforwardOpens (U ⊓ V) (quasiCoherentι (U ⊓ V).toScheme).rightAdjoint K ⟶
          ((quasiCoherentι X).rightAdjoint.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang (quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
declarations.comment: the distinguished triangle at the coherators of `X`, `U`, `V` and `U ∩ V` supplied by Tag 0CR0

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_coherator_distTriang
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CR2], in existential form.** For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `X`
covered by two quasi-compact opens, `X = U ∪ V`, there are coherators `DQ_X`, `DQ_U`, `DQ_V`,
`DQ_{U ∩ V}` of `X`, `U`, `V` and `U ∩ V` — right adjoints of the inclusions
`D_QCoh(𝒪_Z) ⥤ D(𝒪_Z)`, [Stacks, Tag 0CR0] — such that every object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` sits in a
distinguished triangle

`DQ_X(K) ⟶ Rj_{U,*}DQ_U(K|_U) ⊕ Rj_{V,*}DQ_V(K|_V) ⟶ Rj_{U ∩ V,*}DQ_{U ∩ V}(K|_{U ∩ V}) ⟶`

in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. A coherator is unique up to a canonical isomorphism, so this is the same
assertion as `Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_distTriang_rightAdjoint_quasiCoherentι`, read
without naming the right adjoints.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coherator_distTriang (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    ∃ (DQX : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
      (DQU : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory U.toScheme)
      (DQV : DerivedCategory V.toScheme.Modules ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory V.toScheme)
      (DQUV : DerivedCategory (U ⊓ V).toScheme.Modules ⥤
        quasiCoherentDerivedCategory (U ⊓ V).toScheme)
      (_ : quasiCoherentι X ⊣ DQX) (_ : quasiCoherentι U.toScheme ⊣ DQU)
      (_ : quasiCoherentι V.toScheme ⊣ DQV) (_ : quasiCoherentι (U ⊓ V).toScheme ⊣ DQUV),
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
        ∃ (f : DQX.obj K ⟶
              coheratorPushforwardOpens U DQU K ⊞ coheratorPushforwardOpens V DQV K)
          (g : coheratorPushforwardOpens U DQU K ⊞ coheratorPushforwardOpens V DQV K ⟶
              coheratorPushforwardOpens (U ⊓ V) DQUV K)
          (h : coheratorPushforwardOpens (U ⊓ V) DQUV K ⟶ (DQX.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang (quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
declarations.comment: coherators of the four schemes exist and the triangle of the tag is distinguished for them

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLeftAdjoint_ι_derivedCategoryB_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CR4.**  Let `S` be a scheme and `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over `S`.  The inclusion functor `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` has a right adjoint, the coherator
`DQ_X`.

This is the source's first proof: the induction principle of Stacks 08GP
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLeftAdjoint_ι_of_forall_isAffineSpace`) from the affine case
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLeftAdjoint_ι_of_isAffineSpace`).  The statement holds at every model
of the derived category `D(𝒪_X)`, by the model comparison
`StacksDraft.DerivedModel.isLeftAdjoint_ι_derivedCategoryB_of_model`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_ι_derivedCategoryB_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (h : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) :
    (@DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB _ _ _ h
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O))).ι.IsLeftAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentDerivedInclusion_isLeftAdjoint_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CR4.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S`.  The inclusion functor `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` has a right adjoint.

The proof is the source's first one; see the module documentation.  The conclusion is
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsLeftAdjoint`, the existence of a right adjoint, which is what the tag
asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentDerivedInclusion_isLeftAdjoint_of_qcqs
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hFqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS F) (hFqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F) :
    (qcohDerivedProp B S hS ⟨F, hF⟩).ι.IsLeftAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coherator_edsMayerVietoris_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CR6.**  Let `S` be a scheme and `(U ⊆ X, j_V : V ⟶ X)` an elementary distinguished
square of algebraic spaces over `S` (here `X = W`, `U = Uo`, `j_V = fV`) with `X`, `U` and `V`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let `P = U ×_X V`.

1. *The functors `DQ_X`, `DQ_U`, `DQ_V`, `DQ_P` exist*: the four inclusions
   `D_QCoh ⥤ D` have right adjoints (Stacks 0CR4, at the four spaces; `P` is quasi-compact and
   quasi-separated by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_edsInterHom` and
   `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparated_edsInterHom`).
2. *The canonical triangle*: for every choice of these right adjoints, with their adjunctions,
   and every `K` in `D(𝒪_X)` there is a distinguished triangle

   `DQ_X(K) ⟶ Rj_{U,*}DQ_U(K|_U) ⊕ Rj_{V,*}DQ_V(K|_V) ⟶ Rj_{P,*}DQ_P(K|_P) ⟶ DQ_X(K)[1]`

   **whose two maps are the canonical ones**: the exact functor `DQ_X` applied to the two maps of
   the Mayer–Vietoris triangle of Stacks 08GW
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mem_distTriang_edsDerivedRestrictPushMayerVietorisLowerShriek`,
   whose maps are written out here verbatim: the derived units `K ⟶ R(j_{Y,*}(K|_Y))` and the
   difference of the derived comparisons `R(j_{U,*}(K|_U)) ⟶ R(j_{P,*}(K|_P))`,
   `R(j_{V,*}(K|_V)) ⟶ R(j_{P,*}(K|_P))`), conjugated by the three isomorphisms
   `DQ_X(R(j_{Y,*}(K|_Y))) ≅ Rj_{Y,*}DQ_Y(K|_Y)`
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coheratorRestrictPushObjIso`), which are Stacks 0CR5 for the étale
   morphism `j_Y` composed with `DQ_X` of the canonical identification
   `R(j_{Y,*}((-)|_Y)) ≅ Rj_{Y,*}((-)|_Y)`.  Only the connecting map is existentially
   quantified, as in Stacks 08GW.

`Rj_{Y,*}` is the chosen total right derived functor of the direct image along `j_Y`, and the
derived categories are the standard model `HasDerivedCategory.standard`, in which Stacks 08GW is
stated.  The hypotheses are the source's: `hWqc`, `hWqs` say that `X` is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, `hUqc`, `hUqs` that `U` is, and `hVqc`, `hVqs` that `V` is (quasi-separated in
the absolute sense, over `Spec ℤ`, as in Stacks 0CR4).
declarations.statement:
theorem coherator_edsMayerVietoris_triangle
    (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.1)
    (hWqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal W.1)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Uo.toFunctor)
    (hUqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Uo.toFunctor)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V)
    (hVqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal V) :
    ((qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS W).ι.IsLeftAdjoint ∧
      (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsOpen B S hS hsq)).ι.IsLeftAdjoint ∧
      (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq)).ι.IsLeftAdjoint ∧
      (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsInter B S hS hsq)).ι.IsLeftAdjoint) ∧
    ∀ (DQX : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) ⥤
        (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS W).FullSubcategory)
      (adjX : (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS W).ι ⊣ DQX)
      (DQU : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (edsOpen B S hS hsq).1
          (edsOpen B S hS hsq).2) ⥤
        (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsOpen B S hS hsq)).FullSubcategory)
      (adjU : (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsOpen B S hS hsq)).ι ⊣ DQU)
      (DQV : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq).1
          (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2) ⥤
        (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq)).FullSubcategory)
      (adjV : (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsEtale B S hS hsq)).ι ⊣ DQV)
      (DQP : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (edsInter B S hS hsq).1
          (edsInter B S hS hsq).2) ⥤
        (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsInter B S hS hsq)).FullSubcategory)
      (adjP : (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS (edsInter B S hS hsq)).ι ⊣ DQP)
      (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2)),
      ∃ δ, Triangle.mk
        (biprod.lift
          ((qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS W).ι.map (DQX.map
            ((derivedUnitOfNatTrans (edsAdjOpen B S hS hsq).unit
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushOpen B S hS hsq)
              (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitOpen B S hS hsq)).app K)) ≫
            (coheratorRestrictPushObjIso B S hS (edsOpenHom B S hS hsq)
              (isEtale_edsOpenHom B S hS hsq)
              (isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiCompactSpace B S hS B.contains_terminal W.2 hWqs hUqc _)
              (isQuasiSeparated_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_source B S hS B.contains_terminal
                (edsOpen B S hS hsq).2 hUqs _)
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushOpen B S hS hsq) (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitOpen B S hS hsq)
              DQX adjX DQU adjU K).hom)
          ((qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS W).ι.map (DQX.map
            ((derivedUnitOfNatTrans (edsAdjEtale B S hS hsq).unit
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushEtale B S hS hsq)
              (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitEtale B S hS hsq)).app K)) ≫
            (coheratorRestrictPushObjIso B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
              (isEtale_edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
              (isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiCompactSpace B S hS B.contains_terminal W.2 hWqs hVqc _)
              (isQuasiSeparated_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_source B S hS B.contains_terminal
                (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2 hVqs _)
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushEtale B S hS hsq) (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitEtale B S hS hsq)
              DQX adjX DQV adjV K).hom))
        (biprod.desc
          ((coheratorRestrictPushObjIso B S hS (edsOpenHom B S hS hsq)
              (isEtale_edsOpenHom B S hS hsq)
              (isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiCompactSpace B S hS B.contains_terminal W.2 hWqs hUqc _)
              (isQuasiSeparated_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_source B S hS B.contains_terminal
                (edsOpen B S hS hsq).2 hUqs _)
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushOpen B S hS hsq) (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitOpen B S hS hsq)
              DQX adjX DQU adjU K).inv ≫
            (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS W).ι.map (DQX.map
            ((Functor.rightDerivedNatTrans (edsDerivedRestrictPushOpen B S hS hsq)
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushInter B S hS hsq)
              (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitOpen B S hS hsq)
              (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitInter B S hS hsq)
              (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
              (Functor.whiskerRight (NatTrans.mapHomotopyCategory
                (conjugateEquiv ((edsAdjOpen B S hS hsq).comp
                    (edsLowerShriekAdjOpen B S hS hsq))
                  ((edsAdjInter B S hS hsq).comp (edsLowerShriekAdjInter B S hS hsq))
                  (edsShriekOpenComparison B S hS hsq (edsLowerShriekAdjOpen B S hS hsq)
                    (edsLowerShriekAdjInter B S hS hsq)))
                (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) DerivedCategory.Qh)).app K)) ≫
            (coheratorRestrictPushObjIso B S hS (edsInterHom B S hS hsq)
              (isEtale_edsInterHom B S hS hsq)
              (isQuasiCompact_edsInterHom B S hS hsq hWqs hUqc hVqc)
              (isQuasiSeparated_edsInterHom B S hS hsq hUqs hVqs)
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushInter B S hS hsq) (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitInter B S hS hsq)
              DQX adjX DQP adjP K).hom)
          ((coheratorRestrictPushObjIso B S hS (edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
              (isEtale_edsEtaleHom B S hS hsq)
              (isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiCompactSpace B S hS B.contains_terminal W.2 hWqs hVqc _)
              (isQuasiSeparated_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_source B S hS B.contains_terminal
                (edsEtale B S hS hsq).2 hVqs _)
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushEtale B S hS hsq) (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitEtale B S hS hsq)
              DQX adjX DQV adjV K).inv ≫
            (qcohDerivedCategoryB B S hS W).ι.map (DQX.map
            (-((Functor.rightDerivedNatTrans (edsDerivedRestrictPushEtale B S hS hsq)
              (edsDerivedRestrictPushInter B S hS hsq)
              (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitEtale B S hS hsq)
              (edsTotalRightDerivedUnitInter B S hS hsq)
              (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (Modules.{u, u} B S hS W.1 W.2) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
              (Functor.whiskerRight (NatTrans.mapHomotopyCategory
                (conjugateEquiv ((edsAdjEtale B S hS hsq).comp
                    (edsLowerShriekAdjEtale B S hS hsq))
                  ((edsAdjInter B S hS hsq).comp (edsLowerShriekAdjInter B S hS hsq))

                (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) DerivedCategory.Qh)).app K))) ≫
