declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.shiftFunctor_preservesProductsCoproducts_and_productCoproductTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a pre-triangulated category and `I` an index type.
(1)(a) The shift functors preserve `I`-indexed products, i.e. if `∏ Xᵢ` exists then
`(∏ Xᵢ)⟦n⟧` together with the shifted projections is a product of the `Xᵢ⟦n⟧`;
(1)(b) dually, they preserve `I`-indexed coproducts.
(2)(a) If `Xᵢ → Yᵢ → Zᵢ → Xᵢ⟦1⟧` is a family of distinguished triangles whose products
exist, then `∏ Xᵢ → ∏ Yᵢ → ∏ Zᵢ → (∏ Xᵢ)⟦1⟧` is distinguished;
(2)(b) if their coproducts exist, then `∐ Xᵢ → ∐ Yᵢ → ∐ Zᵢ → (∐ Xᵢ)⟦1⟧` is distinguished.
declarations.statement:
theorem
    shiftFunctor_preservesProductsCoproducts_and_productCoproductTriangle_distinguished
    (I : Type w) :
    (∀ n : ℤ, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor C n)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℤ, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor C n)) ∧
    (∀ T : I → Triangle C, (∀ i, T i ∈ distTriang C) →
      ∀ [HasProduct fun i => (T i).obj₁] [HasProduct fun i => (T i).obj₂]
        [HasProduct fun i => (T i).obj₃] [HasProduct fun i => (T i).obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧],
        productTriangle T ∈ distTriang C) ∧
    (∀ T : I → Triangle C, (∀ i, T i ∈ distTriang C) →
      ∀ [HasCoproduct fun i => (T i).obj₁] [HasCoproduct fun i => (T i).obj₂]
        [HasCoproduct fun i => (T i).obj₃],
        Triangle.mk (Limits.Sigma.map fun i => (T i).mor₁)
            (Limits.Sigma.map fun i => (T i).mor₂)
            (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
              (T i).mor₃ ≫ (Limits.Sigma.ι (fun i => (T i).obj₁) i)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧') ∈
          distTriang C)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_iso_of_isHomotopyColimitWithCoprojections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CRH]: a derived colimit datum is unique up to a compatible isomorphism.**
Let `(Kₙ, fₙ)` be a system of objects of a pre-triangulated category whose direct sum exists, and
let `(K, iₙ, c)` and `(K', i'ₙ, c')` be two derived colimit data for it: objects endowed with
coprojections satisfying `iₙ₊₁ ∘ fₙ = iₙ` and with a morphism to `(∐ Kₙ)⟦1⟧` completing
`∐ Kₙ --(1 - fₙ)--> ∐ Kₙ --(iₙ)--> · --c-->` to a distinguished triangle. Then there is an
isomorphism `φ : K ≅ K'` with `φ ∘ iₙ = i'ₙ` for every `n` and `c' ∘ φ = c`.

The existence of a morphism `φ` completing the identity of the first two terms to a morphism of
the two triangles is TR3, and that it is invertible is the five lemma for distinguished triangles
(Lemma 13.4.3). The isomorphism is not unique: nothing pins the completion TR3 produces.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_hom_of_isHomotopyColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRI.** A morphism of sequential systems induces a morphism between chosen
homotopy colimits. It commutes with every canonical coprojection and completes the morphism of
the two defining distinguished triangles.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_hom_of_isHomotopyColimit {F G : ℕ ⥤ D} [HasCoproduct F.obj]
    [HasCoproduct G.obj] (a : F ⟶ G) {K L : D}
    (p : ∐ F.obj ⟶ K) (q : K ⟶ (∐ F.obj)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hK : Triangle.mk (Stacks.CountableCoproducts.oneSubShift F) p q ∈ distTriang D)
    (p' : ∐ G.obj ⟶ L) (q' : L ⟶ (∐ G.obj)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hL : Triangle.mk (Stacks.CountableCoproducts.oneSubShift G) p' q' ∈ distTriang D) :
    ∃ b : K ⟶ L,
      (∀ n : ℕ, Sigma.ι F.obj n ≫ p ≫ b = a.app n ≫ Sigma.ι G.obj n ≫ p') ∧
      b ≫ q' = q ≫ (Limits.Sigma.map (fun n ↦ a.app n))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_iso_of_isHomotopyColimit_of_strictMono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRJ**. Let `F : ℕ ⥤ D` be a system of objects `K m = F.obj m` of a
pre-triangulated category, let `n : ℕ → ℕ` be strictly increasing, and assume the direct sums
`∐ K m` and `∐ K (n i)` exist. If `K` is a derived colimit of the system with structure map `p`
and `K'` is a derived colimit of the subsystem `(K (n i))` with structure map `p'` (Definition
090Z), then there is an isomorphism `e : K' ≅ K`, i.e. `hocolim K (n i) ⟶ hocolim K m`, such
that for every `i` the composition `K (n i) ⟶ K' ⟶ K` of the coprojection with `e` is the
coprojection `K (n i) ⟶ K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_of_isHomotopyColimit_of_strictMono
    (F : ℕ ⥤ D) [HasCoproduct F.obj] {n : ℕ → ℕ} (hn : StrictMono n)
    [HasCoproduct (hn.monotone.functor ⋙ F).obj]
    {K : D} (p : ∐ F.obj ⟶ K) (q : K ⟶ (∐ F.obj)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hK : Triangle.mk (Limits.Sigma.desc fun m ↦ Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj m -
        F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ m)) ≫ Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj (m + 1)) p q ∈ distTriang D)
    {K' : D} (p' : ∐ (hn.monotone.functor ⋙ F).obj ⟶ K')
    (q' : K' ⟶ (∐ (hn.monotone.functor ⋙ F).obj)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hK' : Triangle.mk (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i ↦
      Limits.Sigma.ι (hn.monotone.functor ⋙ F).obj i -
        (hn.monotone.functor ⋙ F).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ i)) ≫
          Limits.Sigma.ι (hn.monotone.functor ⋙ F).obj (i + 1)) p' q' ∈ distTriang D) :
    ∃ e : K' ≅ K, ∀ i : ℕ,
      Limits.Sigma.ι (hn.monotone.functor ⋙ F).obj i ≫ p' ≫ e.hom =
        Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj (n i) ≫ p

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_iso_colimit_of_isHomotopyColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRK**. Let `F : ℕ ⥤ D` be a system of objects `K n = F.obj n` of a pre-triangulated
category whose direct sum `∐ K n` exists, let `A` be an abelian category in which colimits over
`ℕ` exist and are exact, and let `H : D ⥤ A` be a homological functor commuting with countable
direct sums. If `K` is a derived colimit of the system with structure map `p : ∐ K n ⟶ K`
(Definition 090Z), then `H K = colim H (K n)`: there is an isomorphism
`e : colim H (K n) ≅ H K` such that for every `n` the `n`-th coprojection of the colimit followed
by `e` is `H` applied to the coprojection `K n ⟶ K` of the derived colimit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_colimit_of_isHomotopyColimit
    (F : ℕ ⥤ D) [HasCoproduct F.obj] (H : D ⥤ A) [H.IsHomological]
    [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) H]
    {K : D} (p : ∐ F.obj ⟶ K) (q : K ⟶ (∐ F.obj)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hK : Triangle.mk (Limits.Sigma.desc fun n ↦ Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj n -
        F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)) ≫ Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj (n + 1)) p q ∈ distTriang D) :
    ∃ e : colimit (F ⋙ H) ≅ H.obj K, ∀ n : ℕ,
      colimit.ι (F ⋙ H) n ≫ e.hom = H.map (Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj n ≫ p)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isHomotopyColimit_toDerivedCategory_obj_colimit
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra and `Mₙ` a system of differential graded
modules. Then the derived colimit `hocolim Mₙ` in `D(A, d)` is represented by the differential
graded module `colim Mₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomotopyColimit_toDerivedCategory_obj_colimit
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) (F : ℕ ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) :
    IsHomotopyColimit (F ⋙ toDerivedCategory A) ((toDerivedCategory A).obj (colimit F))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.countable_cohomology_of_isHomotopyColimit_of_isCompactObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRM, the implication (1) ⇒ (2).** *"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra
such that `H^i(A)` is countable for every `i`. Let `M` be an object of `D(A, d)`. If
`M = hocolim Eₙ` with each `Eₙ` compact, then `H^i(M)` is countable for every `i`."*

Cohomology commutes with the derived colimit in the weak sense that the long exact sequence of the
triangle `⊕ Eₙ → ⊕ Eₙ → M → (⊕ Eₙ)[1]` places `H^i(M)` between two cohomology modules of `⊕ Eₙ`,
and those are countable because each `Eₙ` is compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem countable_cohomology_of_isHomotopyColimit_of_isCompactObject
    (hA : ∀ k : ℤ, Countable (A.Cohomology k)) (M : derivedCategory.{u, u, u} A)
    (F : ℕ ⥤ derivedCategory.{u, u, u} A) (hF : ∀ j, IsCompactObject.{u} (F.obj j))
    (hM : IsHomotopyColimit F M) (i : ℤ) :
    Countable ((cohomologyFunctor A i).obj M)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isHomotopyColimit_isCompactObject_of_countable_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRM, the implication (2) ⇒ (1).** *"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra
such that `H^i(A)` is countable for every `i`. Let `M` be an object of `D(A, d)`. If `H^i(M)` is
countable for every `i` then `M = hocolim Eₙ` with each `Eₙ` compact."*

The system is the diagonally refined cell tower described in the implementation notes of this
file: at the `n`-th step the `n`-th cell of `M` is attached and the dead cells in the window
`4 ^ n` of the current enumeration are killed, finitely many at a time, so that every term stays
compact; the two hypotheses of the gluing criterion
`CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.isHomotopyColimit_of_forall_fac_of_forall_eventually_eq_zero`
are `DifferentialGradedModule.exists_comp_eq_of_surjective` and
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_comp_map_eq_zero`.

Compactness is concluded in the universe-restricted spelling `IsCompactObject.{u}`, which makes
this statement stronger than the source's; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHomotopyColimit_isCompactObject_of_countable_cohomology
    (hA : ∀ k : ℤ, Countable (A.Cohomology k)) (M : derivedCategory.{u, u, u} A)
    (hM : ∀ i : ℤ, Countable ((cohomologyFunctor A i).obj M)) :
    ∃ F : ℕ ⥤ derivedCategory.{u, u, u} A,
      (∀ n : ℕ, IsCompactObject.{u} (F.obj n)) ∧ IsHomotopyColimit F M
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isHomotopyColimit_isCompactObject_iff_countable_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRM.** *"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra with `H^i(A)` countable for
each `i`. Let `M` be an object of `D(A, d)`. Then the following are equivalent: (1)
`M = hocolim Eₙ` with `Eₙ` compact in `D(A, d)`, and (2) `H^i(M)` is countable for each `i`."*

The implication (1) ⇒ (2) is
`DifferentialGradedModule.countable_cohomology_of_isHomotopyColimit_of_isCompactObject` and the
implication (2) ⇒ (1) is
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isHomotopyColimit_isCompactObject_of_countable_cohomology`.
Compactness is read in the universe-restricted spelling `IsCompactObject.{u}` on both sides; see
the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHomotopyColimit_isCompactObject_iff_countable_cohomology
    (hA : ∀ k : ℤ, Countable (A.Cohomology k)) (M : derivedCategory.{u, u, u} A) :
    (∃ F : ℕ ⥤ derivedCategory.{u, u, u} A,
        (∀ n : ℕ, IsCompactObject.{u} (F.obj n)) ∧ IsHomotopyColimit F M) ↔
      ∀ i : ℤ, Countable ((cohomologyFunctor A i).obj M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CountableSections.countable_cohomology_derivedTensor_and_ext_of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CRP].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let `K` be an
object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` such that the cohomology sheaves `H^i(K)` have countable sets of
sections over affine opens. Then for any quasi-compact open `U ⊆ X` and any perfect object `E`
of `D(𝒪_X)` the sets `H^i(U, K ⊗^L E)` and `Ext^i(E|_U, K|_U)` are countable.

Quasi-compactness of `X` is not used, so it is not assumed: the statement holds on every
quasi-separated scheme. `H^i(U, -)` is the cohomology of the right derived functor of sections
over `U` (`derivedSectionsOpen`), `⊗^L` is the derived tensor product of `D(𝒪_X)`, perfectness
is that of [Stacks, Tag 08CM], `E|_U` and `K|_U` are the restrictions along the open immersion
`U ⟶ X`, and `Ext^i` is the group of degree-`i` morphisms in `D(𝒪_U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem countable_cohomology_derivedTensor_and_ext_of_isCompact [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hKc : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → ∀ i : ℤ,
      Countable Γ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K, V))
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) (i : ℤ) :
    Countable ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
        ((derivedSectionsOpen X.toRingedSpace U).obj
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj K).obj E))) ∧
      Countable (ShiftedHom ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CountableSections.countable_cohomology_derivedTensor_of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-separated scheme and let `K` and `E` be objects of `D(𝒪_X)`. Suppose the
cohomology sheaves of `K ⊗^L E` have countable sets of sections over affine opens, and that over
an affine open the cohomology of `K ⊗^L E` is computed by those sections. Then for every
quasi-compact open `U` the set `H^i(U, K ⊗^L E)` is countable.
declarations.statement:
theorem countable_cohomology_derivedTensor_of_isCompact (X : Scheme.{u}) [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K E : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaves X.toRingedSpace))
    (hsections : ∀ (V : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen V → ∀ i : ℤ,
      Countable ((cohomologySheafSectionsOpen X.toRingedSpace V i).obj
        (((Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.derTensor X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj K).obj E)))
    (hcomparison : ∀ (V : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen V → ∀ i : ℤ,
      Nonempty ((cohomologyOpen X.toRingedSpace V i).obj
          (((Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.derTensor X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj K).obj E) ≅
        (cohomologySheafSectionsOpen X.toRingedSpace V i).obj
          (((Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.derTensor X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj K).obj E)))
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (i : ℤ) :
    Countable ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
      ((derivedSectionsOpen X.toRingedSpace U).obj
        (((Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.derTensor X.toRingedSpace).tensor.obj K).obj E)))
declarations.comment: countability of H^i(U, K ⊗^L E) over every quasi-compact open, from countable sections of the cohomology sheaves of K ⊗^L E over affine opens. Two inputs are hypotheses rather than proved. First, that the cohomology of an affine open is the sections of the cohomology sheaves there: the library has this only at another model of the derived category. Second, that the cohomology sheaves of K ⊗^L E inherit countable sections over affine opens from those of K when E is perfect, which is why perfectness of E does not appear. The Ext^i(E|_U, K|_U) half is not covered: it needs the isomorphism K ⊗^L E^∨ ≅ RHom(E, K) for perfect E, which is unproved here

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CountableSections.exists_isHomotopyColimit_isPerfect_iff_countable
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CRQ].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme such that the
sets of sections of `𝒪_X` over affine opens are countable. Let `K` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. The following are equivalent:

1. `K = hocolim Eₙ` with `Eₙ` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, and
2. the cohomology sheaves `H^i(K)` have countable sets of sections over affine opens.

`hocolim` is the derived colimit of [Stacks, Tag 090Z], perfectness is that of
[Stacks, Tag 08CM], and the derived category is an arbitrary model of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHomotopyColimit_isPerfect_iff_countable {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [h : HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules]
    (hO : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → Countable Γ(X, V))
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) :
    (∃ F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules,
      (∀ n, @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect X.toRingedSpace h (F.obj n)) ∧
        IsHomotopyColimit F K) ↔
      ∀ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → ∀ i : ℤ,
        Countable Γ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K, V)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CountableSections.exists_isHomotopyColimitWith_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_derivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a ring, `X` a scheme of finite presentation over `A` (`p : X ⟶ Spec A`) and
`f : U ⟶ X` flat of finite presentation. There are an inverse system `L : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` of perfect
objects and maps

`dₙ : RΓ(X, R𝓗om(Lₙ, -)) ⟶ RΓ(U, Lf^* -)`

of functors `D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(A)`, compatible with the transition maps, such that for every `K` in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the maps `dₙ` at `K` exhibit

`RΓ(U, Lf^* K) = hocolim RΓ(X, R𝓗om(Lₙ, K)) = hocolim R Hom_X(Lₙ, K)`

in `D(A)`. The system `L` and the maps `dₙ` do not depend on `K`, and `dₙ` is natural in `K`:
this is the source's "functorially in `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`". Here `RΓ(X, -)` is the derived
global sections functor into `D(A)`, `R𝓗om` the derived internal Hom, `Lf^*` the derived pullback
of [Stacks, Tag 06YJ], and `hocolim` the derived colimit of [Stacks, Tag 090Z].

Stated at `HasDerivedCategory.standard`, scoped to this declaration: part (2), biduality and
[Stacks, Tag 08DQ] exist only at that model.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHomotopyColimitWith_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_derivedSheafHom
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] :
    ∃ (L : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules)
      (d : ∀ n, (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op (L.obj (op n))) ⋙
          derivedGlobalSectionsOver p ⟶
        Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom ⋙
          derivedGlobalSectionsOver (f ≫ p)),
      (∀ n, Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) (L.obj (op n))) ∧
      (∀ n, Functor.whiskerRight ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).map
          (L.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).op) (derivedGlobalSectionsOver p) ≫ d (n + 1) =
          d n) ∧
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
        (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        IsHomotopyColimitWith
          (L.rightOp ⋙ (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).flip.obj K ⋙
            derivedGlobalSectionsOver p)
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver (f ≫ p)).obj
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
              f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K))
          (fun n => (d n).app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CountableSections.exists_isHomotopyColimitWith_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CRR] (2).** Let `A` be a ring, `X` a scheme of finite presentation over `A`
and `f : U ⟶ X` a flat morphism of finite presentation. Then there is a system `E : ℕ ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`
of perfect objects such that

`RΓ(U, Lf^* K) = hocolim RΓ(X, K ⊗^𝐋 Eₙ)`

in `D(A)`, functorially in `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`: there are maps
`cₙ : RΓ(X, - ⊗^𝐋 Eₙ) ⟶ RΓ(U, Lf^* -)`, natural in `K` and compatible with the transitions of the
system, which for every `K` with quasi-coherent cohomology are the coprojections of a derived
colimit. One system `E` serves every `K`.

`RΓ(X, -)` and `RΓ(U, -)` are the `A`-linear derived global sections along `X ⟶ Spec A` and
`U ⟶ X ⟶ Spec A`, `⊗^𝐋` is the derived tensor product of [Stacks, Tag 06YU], `Lf^*` the derived
pullback of [Stacks, Tag 06YJ], and `hocolim` the derived colimit of [Stacks, Tag 090Z].

Stated at `HasDerivedCategory.standard`, scoped to this declaration: the projection formula
([Stacks, Tag 08EU]), Tor independent base change ([Stacks, Tag 08IB]) and the Leray isomorphism
exist only at that model.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHomotopyColimitWith_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_derivedTensor
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] :
    ∃ (E : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory X.Modules)
      (c : ∀ n, (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).flip.obj (E.obj n) ⋙ derivedGlobalSectionsOver p ⟶
        Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom ⋙
          derivedGlobalSectionsOver (f ≫ p)),
      (∀ n, Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) (E.obj n)) ∧
      (∀ n, Functor.whiskerRight ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).flip.map (E.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n))))
          (derivedGlobalSectionsOver p) ≫ c (n + 1) = c n) ∧
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
        (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        IsHomotopyColimitWith
          (E ⋙ (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor
            X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj K ⋙ derivedGlobalSectionsOver p)
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver (f ≫ p)).obj
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
              f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K))
          (fun n => (c n).app K)

**Stacks 0CRS, functoriality in `E`, with nothing granted.**

Let `(U ⊆ X, j_V : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary distinguished square of algebraic spaces over a
scheme `S` and let `P = U ×_X V`.  Write `Γ(X, -)` for global sections of `𝒪_X`-modules on the
small étale ringed site, `Φ_Y = j_{Y,*}((-)|_Y)` for the three restrict-then-push composites of
the square, and let `RΓ(X, -)`, `RΓ(U, -)`, `RΓ(V, -)`, `RΓ(P, -)` be right derived functors of
`Γ(X, -)`, `Γ(X, -) ∘ Φ_U`, `Γ(X, -) ∘ Φ_V` and `Γ(X, -) ∘ Φ_P`.  Then the five maps of the
Mayer–Vietoris triangle

`RΓ(X, E) ⟶ RΓ(U, E) ⊕ RΓ(V, E) ⟶ RΓ(U ×_X V, E) ⟶ RΓ(X, E)[1]`

Let `(U ⊆ X, j_V : V ⟶ X)` be an elementary distinguished square of algebraic spaces over a
scheme `S` and let `P = U ×_X V`.  Write `Γ(X, -)` for global sections of `𝒪_X`-modules on the
small étale ringed site, `Φ_Y = j_{Y,*}((-)|_Y)` for the three restrict-then-push composites of
the square, and let `RΓ(X, -)`, `RΓ(U, -)`, `RΓ(V, -)`, `RΓ(P, -)` be right derived functors of

**The four maps are the restriction maps, written out in the statement and not existentially
quantified.**  The two out of `RΓ(X, -)` are `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedNatTrans` of
`Γ(X, -)` applied to the units `F ⟶ j_{U,*}F|_U` and `F ⟶ j_{V,*}F|_V` of the adjunctions
`(-)|_Y ⊣ j_{Y,*}` of Stacks 03LU — that is, of the restriction maps
`Γ(X, F) ⟶ Γ(X, j_{U,*}F|_U) = Γ(U, F|_U)` and `Γ(X, F) ⟶ Γ(V, F|_V)` — and the two into
`RΓ(U ×_X V, -)` are `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedNatTrans` of `Γ(X, -)` applied to the
two comparisons `j_{U,*}F|_U ⟶ j_{P,*}F|_P` and `j_{V,*}F|_V ⟶ j_{P,*}F|_P` of Stacks 08GW
part (1): the conjugates, under the adjunctions `j_{Y!}((-)|_Y) ⊣ j_{Y,*}((-)|_Y)`, of the
extension-by-zero comparisons `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.edsShriekOpenComparison` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.edsShriekEtaleComparison` of Stacks 08GV, at the extension by zero the
library constructs (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.edsLowerShriekAdjOpen` and its two companions).
They are the same four maps as in Stacks 08GW part (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mem_distTriang_edsDerivedRestrictPushMayerVietorisLowerShriek`.

Only the connecting transformation `δ : RΓ(P, -) ⟶ RΓ(X, -) ⋙ (-)[1]` is existentially
quantified: the library attaches no canonical such map to an object of `D(𝒪_X)`, and the source
likewise asserts only that a triangle with these three terms and these four maps is
distinguished, as Stacks 08GV part (2) and Stacks 08GW part (2) do.

its hypothesis `hMV` — part (1) of Stacks 08GW — discharged and its four maps named.  The

K-injective resolution of `E` (Stacks 079P,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_quasiIso_isKInjective_injective_modules`), and at an *injective*
module it is proved outright from part (1) of Stacks 08GV:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.shortExact_edsRestrictPushMayerVietoris_of_injective`.  So the
surjectivity on the right, which at a general module is the étale-local vanishing of an
obstruction in `Ext¹(𝒪_X, F) = H¹(X, F)` (Stacks 01FW) and is still the hypothesis `hepi` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.shortExact_edsRestrictPushMayerVietoris`, is not needed here at all.

`Γ(X, -) ∘ j_{Y,*} ∘ (-)|_Y` in that factored form; that this is `RΓ(Y, E|_Y)` is the
adjunction of Stacks 03LU, `Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.globalSectionsPushforwardIso`, and is
not transported here.

**Stacks 0CRS, the long exact cohomology sequence, with nothing granted.**

The distinguished triangle of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_delta_mem_distTriang_edsSectionsMayerVietoris_unconditional` has an
exact homology sequence, which at each `n` is the six-term exact sequence

`H^n(X,E) ⟶ H^n(U,E) ⊕ H^n(V,E) ⟶ H^n(U ×_X V,E) ⟶ H^{n+1}(X,E) ⟶ H^{n+1}(U,E) ⊕ H^{n+1}(V,E)
⟶ H^{n+1}(U ×_X V,E)`

— the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence of the source, since the homology functor is additive
and so carries the biproduct `RΓ(U,E) ⊕ RΓ(V,E)` to `H^n(U,E) ⊕ H^n(V,E)`.

**Its maps are the restriction maps on cohomology**, because the triangle whose homology
sequence this is carries its four maps written out: they are the right derived transformations
of `Γ(X, -)` applied to the units `F ⟶ j_{U,*}F|_U`, `F ⟶ j_{V,*}F|_V` of Stacks 03LU and to
the two comparisons `j_{U,*}F|_U ⟶ j_{P,*}F|_P`, `j_{V,*}F|_V ⟶ j_{P,*}F|_P` of Stacks 08GW
part (1), so the maps of the long exact sequence are `H^n` of them.  Only the connecting map
`δ`, and with it `H^n(U ×_X V,E) ⟶ H^{n+1}(X,E)`, is existentially quantified, as in the
source.

its hypothesis `hMV` — part (1) of Stacks 08GW — discharged and its four maps named.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.countable_cohomology_derivedTensor_and_ext_of_qcqs_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRU.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `K`
be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` such that the cohomology sheaves `H^q(K)` have countable sets of
sections over the affine schemes étale over `X`, and let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.
Then for every quasi-compact quasi-separated étale `U ⟶ X` and every `i : ℤ` the sets
`H^i(U, K ⊗^𝐋 E)` and `Ext^i(E|_U, K|_U)` are countable.

Here `U` is an object of the spaces-étale site of `X`, and quasi-compactness and
quasi-separatedness are those of `U` itself; since `X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated these
are equivalent to quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the morphism `U ⟶ X`.
`H^i(U, K ⊗^𝐋 E)` is the `i`-th cohomology of the derived global sections over `U` of the
restriction of `K ⊗^𝐋 E` to `U`, and `(-)|_U` is restriction of modules along the étale
`U ⟶ X`, read on derived categories.

The cohomology clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCountableCohomology_derivedTensor_restrict_of_isPerfect` at the
canonical derived tensor product of the small étale site, and the `Ext` clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.countable_ext_of_qcqs_etale_of_countable_sections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem countable_cohomology_derivedTensor_and_ext_of_qcqs_etale
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (∀ v : SmallEtale B S hS X.1, IsAffineChart B S hS X.1 v → ∀ q : ℤ,
      Countable (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) q).obj K.obj).val.obj (op v))) →
    ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2),
      RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) E →
    ∀ U : SpacesEtale B S hS X, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.left.1 →
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal U.1.left.1 → ∀ i : ℤ,
      letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (Modules.{u, u} B S hS U.1.left.1 U.1.left.2)
      letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
      Countable ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} i).obj
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsAb B S hS U.1.left).obj
            ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS U.1.hom U.2).mapDerivedCategory.obj
              (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B S hS X).obj K.obj).obj E)))) ∧
        Countable (DerivedCategory.Ext
          ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS U.1.hom U.2).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
          ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS U.1.hom U.2).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCountableCohomology_derivedTensor_restrict_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `K` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology sheaves have countable sets of sections over the affine schemes
étale over `X`, and let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.  Then `H^i(U, (K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} E)|_U)`
is countable for every quasi-compact quasi-separated `U` étale over `X` and every `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCountableCohomology_derivedTensor_restrict_of_isPerfect
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, u, u + 1}
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hqcK : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) q).obj K).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hcountK : ∀ v : SmallEtale B S hS X.1, IsAffineChart B S hS X.1 v → ∀ q : ℤ,
      Countable (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) q).obj K).val.obj (op v)))
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect.{u + 1, u, u, u, u + 1} E)
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.left.1)
    (hUqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ U.1.left.1) :
    HasCountableCohomology ((derivedGlobalSectionsAb B S hS U.1.left).obj
      ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS U.1.hom U.2).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((T.tensor.obj K).obj E)))
declarations.comment: the sets H^i(U, K ⊗^𝐋 E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.countable_ext_of_qcqs_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRU, the clause on `Ext^i(E|_U, K|_U)`.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `K` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and let `E` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then for every quasi-compact quasi-separated étale `U ⟶ X` the set
`Ext^i(E|_U, K|_U)` is countable.

The three hypotheses are the three inputs the source proof takes from elsewhere, and they are the
three this library does not supply:

* `hExt` identifies `Ext^i(E|_Y, K|_Y)` with the `i`-th cohomology of a derived-sections object
  `RΓ Y`. This is the content of Stacks 08JJ that the library lacks: the carrier of 08JJ in this
  repository, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_tensorDualToSheafHom_of_localSummand`, proves only the
  undergived sheaf isomorphism `F ⊗ E^∨ ≅ SheafHom(E, F)`, not the derived identity
  `K ⊗^𝐋 E^∨ ≅ RSheafHom(E, K)` that turns `Ext` into cohomology.
* `haff` is the affine case, i.e. Stacks 0CRP transported to the spaces-étale site. The 0CRP
  carrier in this repository is about quasi-compact opens of a *scheme* and assumes its own
  affine case, so it does not supply this.
* `hMV` is the Mayer–Vietoris triangle of an elementary distinguished square, i.e. Stacks 0CRS.
  The 0CRS carrier here is conditional on part (1) of Stacks 08GW, which is itself unproved.

Granted those, the devissage is `hasCountableCohomology_of_qcqs_etale`.

Perfectness of `E` is part of the statement of Stacks 0CRU and is kept here, but it is not
consumed by this proof: in the source argument perfectness is used exactly inside the affine case
and inside the reduction of `Ext` to cohomology, and both of those are the hypotheses `haff` and
`hExt`. The binder is therefore written `_hE`.
declarations.statement:
theorem countable_ext_of_qcqs_etale (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.obj)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.obj)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.obj X.property)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.obj X.property))
    (_hE : RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.obj X.property) E)
    (RΓ : (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) → (Y ⟶ X.obj) →
      DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (hExt : ∀ (Y : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (hY : IsEtale B S hS Y.obj.hom.hom) (j : ℤ),
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Ext
        ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (Y := X) ⟨Y.obj.hom.hom⟩ hY).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
        ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (Y := X) ⟨Y.obj.hom.hom⟩ hY).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          K.obj) j ≃
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} j).obj
          (RΓ Y.obj.left.obj Y.obj.hom.hom)))
    (haff : ∀ V : SpacesEtale B S hS X, IsAffineSpace B S hS V.obj.left.obj →
      HasCountableCohomology (RΓ V.obj.left.obj V.obj.hom.hom))
    (hMV : ∀ (W V : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (U : Subfunctor W.obj.left.obj)
      (f : V.obj.left.obj ⟶ W.obj.left.obj), f ≫ W.obj.hom.hom = V.obj.hom.hom →
      IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS W.obj.left.property U f →
      ∃ (fU : RΓ W.obj.left.obj W.obj.hom.hom ⟶ RΓ U.toFunctor (U.ι ≫ W.obj.hom.hom))
        (fV : RΓ W.obj.left.obj W.obj.hom.hom ⟶ RΓ V.obj.left.obj V.obj.hom.hom)
        (gU : RΓ U.toFunctor (U.ι ≫ W.obj.hom.hom) ⟶
          RΓ (pullback U.ι f) (pullback.fst U.ι f ≫ U.ι ≫ W.obj.hom.hom))
        (gV : RΓ V.obj.left.obj V.obj.hom.hom ⟶
          RΓ (pullback U.ι f) (pullback.fst U.ι f ≫ U.ι ≫ W.obj.hom.hom))
        (δ : RΓ (pullback U.ι f) (pullback.fst U.ι f ≫ U.ι ≫ W.obj.hom.hom) ⟶
          (RΓ W.obj.left.obj W.obj.hom.hom)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
        Triangle.mk (biprod.lift fU fV) (biprod.desc gU (-gV)) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u}))
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (hU : IsEtale B S hS U.obj.hom.hom)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.obj.left.obj)
    (hUqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ U.obj.left.obj) (i : ℤ) :
    Countable (DerivedCategory.Ext
      ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (Y := X) ⟨U.obj.hom.hom⟩ hU).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
      ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (Y := X) ⟨U.obj.hom.hom⟩ hU).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj)
      i)
declarations.comment: the sets Ext^i(E|_U, K|_U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.countable_ext_etaleRestrict_of_countable_sections_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**The `Ext` clause of [Stacks, Tag 0CRU].**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact absolutely
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `K` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology
sheaves have countable sets of sections over the affine schemes étale over `X`, and let `E` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.  Then `Ext^i_{𝒪_U}(E|_U, K|_U)` is countable for every quasi-compact
absolutely quasi-separated object `U` of the spaces-étale site of `X`.

Every hypothesis is the tag's own.  This is
`countable_ext_etaleRestrict_of_countable_sections_derivedDualTensor_of_qcohDerived`, in this
namespace, with its remaining input — countability of the sections of the cohomology sheaves of
`E^∨ ⊗^𝐋 K` — supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.countable_sections_homology_derivedDualTensor_of_isPerfect`.

This is one half of the tag's covering set; the other is the `H^i(U, K ⊗^𝐋 E)` clause,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCountableCohomology_derivedTensor_restrict_of_isPerfect`.
declarations.statement:
theorem countable_ext_etaleRestrict_of_countable_sections_of_isPerfect
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hqcK : ∀ q : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) q).obj
      K).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hcountK : ∀ v : SmallEtale B S hS X.1, IsAffineChart B S hS X.1 v → ∀ q : ℤ,
      Countable (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) q).obj
        K).val.obj (op v)))
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) E)
    (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.left.1)
    (hUqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ U.1.left.1) (i : ℤ) :
    Countable (DerivedCategory.Ext
      ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS U.1.hom U.2).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
      ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS U.1.hom U.2).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) i)
declarations.comment: the sets Ext^i(E|_U, K|_U), at the tag's own hypotheses; the H^i(U, K ⊗^𝐋 E) clause is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasCountableCohomology_derivedTensor_restrict_of_isPerfect`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isHomotopyColimitCocone_derivedSections_tensor_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRW (2).** Let `A` be a ring and `f : U ⟶ X` a flat morphism of algebraic spaces
of finite presentation over `A`. There is a system `(Eₙ)` of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` with
`RΓ(U, Lf^*K) = hocolim RΓ(X, Eₙ ⊗^L K)` in `D(A)` functorially in `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`: natural
maps `RΓ(X, Eₙ ⊗^L -) ⟶ RΓ(U, Lf^* -)` exhibit the homotopy colimit at every such `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHomotopyColimitCocone_derivedSections_tensor_of_isFlat
    {U X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA} (f : U ⟶ X)
    (hX : IsFinitePresentation B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA X).hom)
    (hU : IsFinitePresentation B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA U).hom)
    (hf : IsFlat B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) :
    ∃ E : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2),
      (∀ n, (smallEtaleRingedSite B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2).IsPerfect (E.obj n)) ∧
      ∃ ι : ∀ n, (smallEtaleDerivedTensor B (Spec (.of A)) hA X).obj (E.obj n) ⋙
          derivedModulePushforward B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA X) ⋙
            representedAffineDerivedSections B (Spec (.of A)) hA
              (baseSiteObj B (Spec (.of A)) hA) ⟶
          smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B (Spec (.of A)) hA f ⋙
            derivedModulePushforward B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA U) ⋙
              representedAffineDerivedSections B (Spec (.of A)) hA
                (baseSiteObj B (Spec (.of A)) hA),
        ∀ K, QcohDerived B (Spec (.of A)) hA X K →
          IsHomotopyColimitCocone
            (E ⋙ (smallEtaleDerivedTensor B (Spec (.of A)) hA X).flip.obj K ⋙
              derivedModulePushforward B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA X) ⋙
                representedAffineDerivedSections B (Spec (.of A)) hA
                  (baseSiteObj B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
            fun n ↦ (ι n).app K
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isHomotopyColimitCocone_derivedHom_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CRW (1).** Let `A` be a ring and `f : U ⟶ X` a flat morphism of algebraic spaces
of finite presentation over `A`. There is an inverse system `(Lₙ)` of perfect objects of
`D(𝒪_X)` with `RΓ(U, Lf^*K) = hocolim RHom_X(Lₙ, K)` in `D(A)` functorially in
`K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, where `RHom_X(L, K) = RΓ(X, R𝓗om(L, K))`: natural maps
`RHom_X(Lₙ, -) ⟶ RΓ(U, Lf^* -)` exhibit the homotopy colimit at every such `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isHomotopyColimitCocone_derivedHom_of_isFlat
    {U X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA} (f : U ⟶ X)
    (hX : IsFinitePresentation B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA X).hom)
    (hU : IsFinitePresentation B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA U).hom)
    (hf : IsFlat B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom) :
    ∃ L : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2),
      (∀ n, (smallEtaleRingedSite B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2).IsPerfect (L.obj n)) ∧
      ∃ ι : ∀ n, (smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B (Spec (.of A)) hA X).obj (op (L.obj (op n))) ⋙
          derivedModulePushforward B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA X) ⋙
            representedAffineDerivedSections B (Spec (.of A)) hA
              (baseSiteObj B (Spec (.of A)) hA) ⟶
          smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B (Spec (.of A)) hA f ⋙
            derivedModulePushforward B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA U) ⋙
              representedAffineDerivedSections B (Spec (.of A)) hA
                (baseSiteObj B (Spec (.of A)) hA),
        ∀ K, QcohDerived B (Spec (.of A)) hA X K →
          IsHomotopyColimitCocone
            (L.rightOp ⋙ (smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B (Spec (.of A)) hA X).flip.obj K ⋙
              derivedModulePushforward B (Spec (.of A)) hA (toBase B (Spec (.of A)) hA X) ⋙
                representedAffineDerivedSections B (Spec (.of A)) hA
                  (baseSiteObj B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
            fun n ↦ (ι n).app K
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_derivedPushforwardComparison
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `Φ(K) ⟶ Rf_*(K)` is an isomorphism for every `K`.** This is the content
of [Stacks, Tag 0CRX]. Both functors are triangulated — `Φ` and `Rf_*` because they are right
derived functors on Grothendieck abelian categories
(`Stacks.DerivedAcyclic.isTriangulated_of_isRightDerivedFunctor`), and the derived inclusions
because the inclusions are exact — so the dévissage
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.isIso_natTrans_of_isIso_app_quasicoherentPushforward` reduces the claim to
complexes pushed forward from an affine open, where it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_derivedPushforwardComparison_app_quasicoherentPushforward`.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_derivedPushforwardComparison : IsIso (derivedPushforwardComparison f Φ ηΦ)
declarations.comment: the canonical map Φ(K) ⟶ Rf_*(K) is an isomorphism for every K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentComparisonSquareOfAffineDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**The square for quasi-compact schemes with affine diagonal.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of schemes, with `X` and `Y` quasi-compact with affine diagonal, and let `Φ`, with derivation unit
`ηΦ`, be a total right derived functor of `f_* : QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then the square

```
D(QCoh(𝒪_X)) --i_X--> D_QCoh(𝒪_X)
     | Φ                  | Rf_*
     v                     v
D(QCoh(𝒪_Y)) --i_Y--> D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)
```

commutes, the horizontal arrows being the comparison functors of [Stacks, Tag 06VT] and the right
edge the restriction `AlgebraicGeometry.affineDiagonalDerivedQuasicoherentPushforward` of the
unbounded derived direct image.

The isomorphism is the canonical one: after the fully faithful inclusion of `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardComparison`, the map `Φ(K) ⟶ Rf_*(K)` induced by
`f_* ⟶ Rf_*`, which is invertible by `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_derivedPushforwardComparison`.
declarations.comment: the commuting square, for any right derived functor (Φ, ηΦ) of f_*

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_injective_quasicoherentSections_rightDerived_ne_cohomology
declarations.doc:
On an affine scheme the comparison from derived sections computed inside `QCoh(𝒪_X)` to sheaf
cohomology is not an isomorphism. There are a ring `A`, an injective object `ℱ` of
`QCoh(𝒪_{Spec A})` and a quasi-compact open `U ⊆ Spec A` with `R^1_{QCoh}Γ(U, ℱ) = 0` and
`H^1(U, ℱ) ≠ 0`; in particular no morphism from the first group to the second is an isomorphism,
so the canonical `t^1` is not one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_quasicoherentSections_rightDerived_ne_cohomology :
    ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{u})
      (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec A).ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
      (U : (Spec A).Opens),
      Injective F ∧ IsCompact (U : Set (Spec A)) ∧
        IsZero (((quasicoherentSections (Spec A) U).rightDerived 1).obj F) ∧
        ¬ IsZero (Hgroup (Spec A).ringCatSheaf U 1
            ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec A).ringCatSheaf).ι.obj F)) ∧
        ∀ t : ((quasicoherentSections (Spec A) U).rightDerived 1).obj F ⟶
            Hgroup (Spec A).ringCatSheaf U 1
              ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec A).ringCatSheaf).ι.obj F),
          ¬ IsIso t
declarations.comment: R^1_QCoh Γ(U, ℱ) = 0 while H^1(U, ℱ) ≠ 0, for ℱ injective in QCoh(𝒪_{Spec A})

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.InjectiveTilde.exists_injective_tilde_nonzero_firstCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CRZ.** An injective module on an affine scheme with Noetherian
underlying space can have nonzero first cohomology on a quasi-compact open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_injective_tilde_nonzero_firstCohomology :
    ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (I : ModuleCat.{u} A) (U : (Spec A).Opens),
      NoetherianSpace (Spec A) ∧ Injective I ∧
        IsCompact (U : Set (Spec A)) ∧
          ¬ IsZero (Hgroup (Spec A).ringCatSheaf U 1 (tilde I))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.extIso
declarations.doc:
Degree-`n` cohomology of derived Hom out of `N` is
`Ext^n_{D(B,d)}(N, -) = Hom_{D(B,d)}(N, (-)[n])`, as functors on `D(B, d)`.
declarations.statement:
def extIso (D : DerivedHomData A B N L) (n : ℤ) :
    D.functor ⋙ extCohomologyFunctor A n ≅ extFunctor B N n
declarations.comment: the identification of the cohomology of derived Hom with Ext

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.extLinearEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
The identification `DifferentialGradedModule.extLinearEquiv` is natural in the target: a
cohomology class of derived Hom pushed forward along `g` is sent to the `Ext`-class followed by
the `n`-shift of `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extLinearEquiv_naturality (D : DerivedHomData A B N L) (n : ℤ)
    {M M' : derivedCategory' B} (g : M ⟶ M')
    (x : (degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization' A).obj ((D.functor.obj M)⟦n⟧)) :
    extLinearEquiv A B N L D n M'
        ((degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization' A).map ((D.functor.map g)⟦n⟧') x) =
      extLinearEquiv A B N L D n M x ≫ g⟦n⟧'
declarations.comment: the identification is natural in the target

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.extLinearEquiv_derivedPrecomp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CS5, the clause asserting compatibility with Tag 0BYV.** For a homomorphism
`f : M ⟶ N` of differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodules, the identification of Tag 0CS5 carries the
pullback along `f` of a degree-`n` cohomology class of derived Hom out of `N` — the transformation
of Tag 0BYV, `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedPrecomp` — to the `Ext`-class of `N` composed
with the image of `f` in `D(B, d)`.

Together with `DifferentialGradedModule.extIso` and
`DifferentialGradedModule.extLinearEquiv_naturality` this completes Tag 0CS5.
declarations.statement:
theorem extLinearEquiv_derivedPrecomp (DN : DerivedHomData A B N.rightModule N.leftAction)
    (DM : DerivedHomData A B M.rightModule M.leftAction) (f : M ⟶ N) (n : ℤ)
    (P : derivedCategory' B)
    (x : (degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization' A).obj ((DN.functor.obj P)⟦n⟧)) :
    extLinearEquiv A B M.rightModule M.leftAction DM n P
        ((degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization' A).map
          (((derivedPrecomp DN DM f).app P)⟦n⟧') x) =
      (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q.map ((toHomotopyCategory B).map f.rightHom) ≫
        extLinearEquiv A B N.rightModule N.leftAction DN n P x
declarations.comment: the identification is natural in the bimodule, with respect to Tag 0BYV

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.General.homComplexExtEquiv
declarations.doc:
**`H^n(Hom^•_{(A, d)}(L, M)) = Ext^n_{D(A, d)}(L, M)`**, at independent universes, for `L`
orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules.

This is the content that Tag 0CS5 and Tag 0BYW together provide, in the form Tag 0CS6 asks for:
Tag 09LC identifies the cohomology of the Hom complex with the morphism groups of `K(A, d)`
(`DifferentialGradedModule.General.homComplexHomologyEquiv`), and the localization functor is
bijective on the morphisms out of a left-orthogonal object
(`DifferentialGradedModule.General.bijective_q_map_of_leftOrthogonal`), which is the mechanism of
Tag 09KY; the shift is moved across the localization by its commutation with the translation.

With `Ext^n_{D(A, d)}(L, M) = Hom_{D(A, d)}(L, M[n])`, as everywhere in Tag 0CS6, the right-hand
side is that `Ext`-group.
declarations.statement:
def homComplexExtEquiv (n : ℤ)
    (hL : (acyclic.{u, v, w} A).leftOrthogonal ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L)) :
    ↥((homComplex A L M).homology n) ≃+
      ((quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, w} A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L) ⟶
        ((quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, w} A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M))⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: the cohomology of ordinary differential graded Hom is Ext out of a module orthogonal to the acyclics, at independent universes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedExtMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CS6.** *The maps
`Ext^n_{D(E, d)}(M, N) → Ext^n_{D(𝒪)}(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•, N ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•)` induced by the functor
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•`.* With `Ext^n_{D(C)}(X, Y) = Hom_{D(C)}(X, Y[n])`, the map induced by a functor
is its action on morphisms followed by its commutation with the translation, here that of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedCommShift`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorWithComplexDerivedExtMap
    {M N : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).algebra} (n : ℤ)
    (f : M ⟶ N⟦n⟧) :
    (tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).obj M ⟶
      ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).obj N)⟦n⟧
declarations.comment: the induced maps on Ext

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedExtMap_q
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CS6, the maps on `Ext` are those induced by tensoring with `K`.** On a class coming
from `K(Mod_(E, d))`, the map induced by `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` agrees, through the comparison
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K → - ⊗_E K` of Tag 09LX, with the map induced by the differential graded tensor
functor of Tag 09LV read on homotopy categories. This is the compatibility of that comparison
with the translation.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorWithComplexDerivedExtMap_q
    {P Y : DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.{o, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}
      (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).algebra} (n : ℤ) (f : P ⟶ Y⟦n⟧) :
    (tensorWithComplexDerivedCounit.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).app P ≫
        tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategoryExtMap.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K n f =
      tensorWithComplexDerivedExtMap.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K n
          ((quasiIsomorphisms (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).algebra).Q.map f ≫
            (((quasiIsomorphisms (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).algebra).Q).commShiftIso n).hom.app
              Y) ≫
        ((tensorWithComplexDerivedCounit.{u, v, w, t, s, o} X R K).app Y)⟦n⟧'
declarations.comment: the maps on Ext are those induced by tensoring with K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomSourceExtEquivOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CS6, the source of the canonical map in `D(R)`**, read on cohomology and *for
every* `M`, `N` *in* `D(E, d)`. The degree-`n` cohomology of the source of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver` is the
`Ext`-group

`Ext^n_{D(E, d)}(M, N) = Hom_{D(E, d)}(M, N[n])`,

so that source really is `RHom(M, N)` read on cohomology. It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomSourceExtEquiv` read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.homologyForgetEquiv` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.dgHomComplexModulesDerivedForgetIso`, which say that forgetting the
`R`-action changes neither the cohomology group nor the complex it is taken of. There is no
hypothesis on `M` or `N`.
declarations.comment: the source of the canonical map in D(R) is RHom(M, N), read on cohomology, for every M, N in D(E, d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomTargetExtEquivOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CS6, the target of the canonical map in `D(R)`**, read on cohomology and *for
every* `M`, `N` *in* `D(E, d)`. The degree-`n` cohomology of the target of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver` is the
`Ext`-group

`Ext^n_{D(O)}(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•, N ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•) = Hom_{D(O)}(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•, (N ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•)[n])`.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomTargetExtEquiv` read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.homologyForgetEquiv` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.globalDerivedHomForgetAppOver`. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomSourceExtEquivOver` it exhibits both
cohomology modules of the clause as the `Ext`-groups the clause compares; that the *map* between
them is the one induced by `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver_homology`.

There is no hypothesis on `M` or `N`, and none on the site.
declarations.statement:
def tensorWithComplexDerivedHomTargetExtEquivOver
    (M N : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra)
    (n : ℤ) :
    ↥((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj
        ((scalarRestriction X R).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (((globalDerivedHomModules X).obj
              (op ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).obj M))).obj
            ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).obj N)))) ≃+
      ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).obj M ⟶
        ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).obj N)⟦n⟧)
declarations.comment: the target of the canonical map in D(R) read on cohomology: its degree-n cohomology is Ext^n_{D(O)}(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K, N ⊗_E^𝐋 K), for every M, N in D(E, d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CS6, the central clause, in the source's `D(R)`.** The degree-`n` cohomology of
the canonical map

`RHom(M, N) ⟶ RHom_O(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•, N ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•)`

of `D(R)` is the map on `Ext` induced by the derived tensor product with `K`, for every `M`, `N`
in `D(E, d)` and every `n`, with both sides read as the `Ext`-groups they are by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomSourceExtEquivOver` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomTargetExtEquivOver`.

There is no hypothesis on `M` or `N`: the statement is quantified over every object of
`D(E, d)`, as the source's is, and the property-(P) reduction of the source's proof is performed
by the choice of representative `DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPModel`. Nor is anything
assumed about the site.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerived_homology` read over
the source's base ring: the canonical map in `D(R)` forgets to the `D(ℤ)`-valued one by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver_forget`, and
forgetting the scalars changes neither the cohomology groups nor the map between them.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver_homology
    (M N : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra)
    (n : ℤ)
    (η : ↥((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).obj
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((DifferentialGradedModule.dgCategory.{_, _, u}
          (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra).homComplexModules
        (DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPModel.{o, u, 0}
          (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra M)
        (DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPModel.{o, u, 0}
          (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra N))))) :
    tensorWithComplexDerivedHomTargetExtEquivOver X R K M N n
        (ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) n).map
          (tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver X R K M N)) η) =
      tensorWithComplexDerivedExtMap.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K n
        (tensorWithComplexDerivedHomSourceExtEquivOver X R K M N n η)
declarations.comment: H^n of the canonical map is the Ext map induced by - ⊗_E^𝐋 K, for every M, N in D(E, d) and every n, in the source's D(R)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapModulesOver
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map in `D(R)`.** The differential graded functor of Tag 09LV acts on the
`R`-module-valued differential graded Hom complexes, and the Hom complex of two complexes of
`O`-modules over `R` maps canonically to their global derived hom of Tag 0B6E read over `R`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.homComplexToGlobalDerivedHomModulesOver`); the composite is this
morphism of `D(R)`.

Its source is the differential graded Hom complex of two differential graded modules, and its
target is the global derived hom of the ordinary tensor products.
declarations.statement:
def tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapModulesOver
    (M N : (DifferentialGradedModule.dgCategory.{_, _, u}
      (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra).Obj) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((DifferentialGradedModule.dgCategory.{_, _, u}
        (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra).homComplexModules M N) ⟶
      (scalarRestriction X R).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (((globalDerivedHomModules X).obj (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              ((tensorWithComplexDG.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).functor.obj M)))).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            ((tensorWithComplexDG.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).functor.obj N)))
declarations.comment: the canonical map out of the differential graded Hom complex, into RHom_O(M ⊗_E K, N ⊗_E K), in the source's D(R)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `RHom(M, N) ⟶ RHom_O(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•, N ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•)` in `D(R)`**, *for every*
`M`, `N` *in* `D(E, d)`. The canonical map of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapModulesOver`, taken at the chosen
property-(P) representatives of `M` and `N`, is read into the global derived hom of the *derived*
tensor products,

`RHom(M, N) ⟶ RHom_O(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•, N ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•)`,

by transporting both arguments along
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerivedRepIso`: in the contravariant argument the
isomorphism is used as it stands, and in the covariant one it is inverted.

There is no hypothesis on `M` or `N`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorWithComplexDerivedHomMapDerivedModulesOver
    (M N : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((DifferentialGradedModule.dgCategory.{_, _, u}
            (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra).homComplexModules
          (DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPModel.{o, u, 0}
            (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra M)
          (DifferentialGradedModule.propertyPModel.{o, u, 0}
            (Rep.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).algebra N)) ⟶
      (scalarRestriction X R).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (((globalDerivedHomModules X).obj
            (op ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).obj M))).obj
          ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, u, u, u, u, o} X R K).obj N))
declarations.comment: the canonical map RHom(M, N) ⟶ RHom_O(M ⊗_E^𝐋 K, N ⊗_E^𝐋 K) in the source's D(R), for every M, N in D(E, d)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveGenerator.twistSum
declarations.doc:
The direct sum `𝒪_X ⊕ 𝒪_X(-1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝒪_X(-n)` of the `n + 1` nonpositive twists of the
structure sheaf of `X = ℙⁿ_A`.
declarations.statement: public def twistSum : (projectiveSpaceOverRing n (.of A)).Modules

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveGenerator.matrixRingEquivEnd
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CS9]: `R = Hom_{𝒪_X}(P, P)`.** On `X = ℙⁿ_A = Proj A[X₀, …, Xₙ]`, the ring
of upper triangular `(n + 1) × (n + 1)` matrices whose `(i, j)` entry is homogeneous of degree
`j - i` — `S₀` on the diagonal, `S₁` above it, and so on — is the endomorphism ring of
`P = 𝒪_X ⊕ 𝒪_X(-1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝒪_X(-n)`, the `(i, j)` entry acting as the component
`𝒪_X(-j) ⟶ 𝒪_X(-i)` by multiplication.
declarations.statement: public def matrixRingEquivEnd : endomorphismMatrices A n ≃+* End (projTwistSum A n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_isGE_isLE_coherator_obj_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSA].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let
`DQ_X : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` be a coherator of `X`, i.e. a right adjoint of the inclusion
`ι : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` with the adjunction triangulated — the exact functor `DQ_X` of
[Stacks, Tag 0CR0]. Then there is an integer `N`, depending only on `X` and on `DQ_X` and in
particular not on `K`, `a` or `b`, such that for every object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` and all integers
`a`, `b`, if `H^i(U, K) = 0` for every affine open `U ⊆ X` and every `i ∉ [a, b]`, then the
cohomology sheaves `H^i(DQ_X(K))` vanish for `i ∉ [a, b + N]`.

This is `Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_isGE_isLE_coherator_obj`, the source's induction over the
quasi-compact opens of `X` ([Stacks, Tag 08DR]), with its three inputs supplied: the two
Mayer–Vietoris triangles of [Stacks, Tag 08BV] are
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.isMayerVietorisApex_restrictPushforward_sup` and
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.isMayerVietorisApex_self`, and the affine base case is
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.hasCoheratorBoundAt_of_isAffineOpen`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGE_isLE_coherator_obj_of_qcqs (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (DQ : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (adj : quasiCoherentι X ⊣ DQ) [DQ.CommShift ℤ] [adj.IsTriangulated] :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ (a b : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules), AffineAmplitudeIn X a b K →
      ((quasiCoherentι X).obj (DQ.obj K)).IsGE a ∧
        ((quasiCoherentι X).obj (DQ.obj K)).IsLE (b + N)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cohomology_of_isDerivedLimit_single_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSB].** Let `X` be a scheme, let `(𝓕ₙ)` be an inverse system of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules and let `L` be a derived limit in `D(𝒪_X)` of the system `(𝓕ₙ)`
placed in degree zero. Then `H^i(U, L) = 0` for every affine open `U ⊆ X` and every `i` outside
`[0, 1]`.

Sections over `U` commute with derived limits, so `RΓ(U, L) = R lim RΓ(U, 𝓕ₙ)`, and each
`RΓ(U, 𝓕ₙ)` is concentrated in degree zero because `𝓕ₙ` is quasi-coherent and `U` is affine. In
the Milnor short exact sequence `0 → lim¹ H^{i-1}(U, 𝓕ₙ) → H^i(U, L) → lim H^i(U, 𝓕ₙ) → 0` both
outer terms then vanish as soon as `i ≠ 0` and `i ≠ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_cohomology_of_isDerivedLimit_single_of_isAffineOpen (X : Scheme.{u})
    (𝓕 : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules) (hqc : ∀ n : ℕ, (𝓕.obj ⟨n⟩).IsQuasicoherent)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓕 ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory.{u + 1} X.Modules)
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit (𝓕 ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0) L)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (i : ℤ) (hi0 : i ≠ 0) (hi1 : i ≠ 1) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
      ((derivedSectionsOverObject (schemeOpensRingedSite X) U).obj L))
declarations.comment: the cohomology computation on an affine open: H^i(U, R lim 𝓕ₙ) = 0 for i outside [0, 1]

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_isGE_isLE_coherator_obj_of_isDerivedLimit_single
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSB].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `DQ` be a
coherator of `X` and let `L` be a derived limit in `D(𝒪_X)` of an inverse system `(𝓕ₙ)` of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules placed in degree zero. Then `DQ L` lies in `D^b_QCoh(𝒪_X)`: its
cohomology sheaves vanish below degree `0` and above degree `1 + N` for some `N` depending only
on `X` and `DQ`.

The affine amplitude of `L` is `[0, 1]`, so this is the boundedness property of the coherator,
[Stacks, Tag 0CSA] in the form
`Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_isGE_isLE_coherator_obj_of_qcqs`, applied with `a = 0` and
`b = 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGE_isLE_coherator_obj_of_isDerivedLimit_single (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (DQ : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (adj : quasiCoherentι X ⊣ DQ) [DQ.CommShift ℤ] [adj.IsTriangulated]
    (𝓕 : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules) (hqc : ∀ n : ℕ, (𝓕.obj ⟨n⟩).IsQuasicoherent)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝓕 ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit (𝓕 ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0) L) :
    ∃ N : ℤ, ((quasiCoherentι X).obj (DQ.obj L)).IsGE 0 ∧
      ((quasiCoherentι X).obj (DQ.obj L)).IsLE (1 + N)
declarations.comment: the conclusion that the R lim in D_QCoh(𝒪_X), i.e. DQ_X(R lim 𝓕ₙ), lies in D^b_QCoh(𝒪_X), for every coherator DQ of X

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Coherator.isDerivedLimit_coherator_obj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSB].** Let `X` be a scheme and let `DQ` be a right adjoint of the inclusion
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` which makes the adjunction triangulated. If `L` is a derived limit in
`D(𝒪_X)` of an inverse system `F` of objects of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, then `DQ L` is a derived limit of
`F` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

Right adjoints preserve products, so `DQ` preserves the product of the system; it is exact, so it
carries the triangle witnessing the derived limit to one of the same shape. The inclusion is fully
faithful, so the unit of the adjunction identifies `F ⋙ ι ⋙ DQ` with `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_coherator_obj
    (DQ : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) ⥤
      (derivedQuasiCoherent X).FullSubcategory)
    (adj : (derivedQuasiCoherent X).ι ⊣ DQ) [DQ.CommShift ℤ] [adj.IsTriangulated]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ (derivedQuasiCoherent X).FullSubcategory)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (F ⋙ (derivedQuasiCoherent X).ι).obj (op n)]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit (F ⋙ (derivedQuasiCoherent X).ι) L) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ F.obj (op n),
      letI := h
      IsDerivedLimit F (DQ.obj L)
declarations.comment: the identification DQ_X(R lim 𝓕ₙ) = (R lim in D_QCoh(𝒪_X))(𝓕ₙ), for every coherator DQ of X, i.e. every exact right adjoint of the inclusion; one exists on any quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme by Stacks 0CR0, `Stacks.Duality.Coherator.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_quasiCoherentι`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPseudoCoherent_derivedPushforward_tensor_and_isIso_tensorFlatBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSC].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes of finite presentation, let
`E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `𝒢^•` be a bounded above complex of finitely
presented `𝒪_X`-modules, flat over `S`, with support proper over `S`. Then
`K = Rf_*(E ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} 𝒢^•)` is a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_S)`, and its formation commutes
with arbitrary base change: for every cartesian square the canonical map
`Lg^*Rf_*(E ⊗^L 𝒢^•) ⟶ Rf'_*(L(g')^*E ⊗^L (g')^*𝒢^•)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.tensorFlatBaseChangeMap` is an isomorphism.

Support proper over `S` means that a single closed subset of `X` proper over `S` contains the
support of every term of `𝒢^•`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedPushforward_tensor_and_isIso_tensorFlatBaseChangeMap
    (hf : FinitePresentation f)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (G : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (hGminus : CochainComplex.minus X.Modules G)
    (hfp : ∀ i : ℤ, (G.X i).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom (G.X i))
    (hsupp : letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation f := hf.locallyOfFinitePresentation
      ∃ Z : Closeds X, IsProperOver f Z ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.supp (G.X i) ⊆ (Z : Set X)) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S.toRingedSpace)
        ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj E).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj G))) ∧
      ∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
        (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g),
        IsIso (tensorFlatBaseChangeMap f g f' g' (comp_toShHom_of_comm hsq.w) E G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPseudoCoherent_derivedPushforward_and_isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSD].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a flat proper morphism of schemes of finite
presentation and let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be pseudo-coherent. Then `Rf_*E` is a pseudo-coherent object of
`D(𝒪_S)` and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change: for every cartesian square
`X' = X ×_S S'` the base change map `Lg^*Rf_*E ⟶ Rf'_*L(g')^*E` of [Stacks, Tag 08HY] is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedPushforward_and_isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap [Flat f] [IsProper f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S.toRingedSpace)
        ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) ∧
      ∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : X' ⟶ X)
        (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g),
        IsIso (derivedBaseChangeMap g'.toLRSHom.toShHom f'.toLRSHom.toShHom f.toLRSHom.toShHom
          g.toLRSHom.toShHom (comp_toShHom_of_comm sq.w) E)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.exists_boundedAboveFiniteFree_of_isPseudoCoherent_restrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CSF.** If a derived right `R`-module is pseudo-coherent over `A`, where `R` is a
possibly noncommutative `A`-algebra which is finite free over `A`, then it is represented by a
bounded-above complex of finite free right `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedAboveFiniteFree_of_isPseudoCoherent_restrictScalars
    (A : Type uA) (R : Type uR) [CommRing A] [Ring R] [Algebra A R]
    (M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uA uR v} Rᵐᵒᵖ))
    (hR : Module.Finite A R ∧ Module.Free A R)
    (hM : ∀ m : ℤ, IsPseudoCoherentFrom
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max uA uR v} (algebraMap A Rᵐᵒᵖ)).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)
      m) :
    ∃ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max uA uR v} Rᵐᵒᵖ) ℤ,
      IsBoundedAboveFiniteFree E ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpacePseudoCoherent.isPseudoCoherent_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_tfae :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (Proj (polyGrading A n)).Modules := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod (Proj (polyGrading A n)).toRingedSpace) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory
        (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.Modules (Proj (polyGrading A n)).sheaf) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) := HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory (Proj (polyGrading A n)).Modules, quasicoherentObject A n K →
      List.TFAE
        [RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := (Proj (polyGrading A n)).toRingedSpace) K,
          ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Proj (polyGrading A n)).Modules,
            RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := (Proj (polyGrading A n)).toRingedSpace) E →
              StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
                ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver (projToSpecCoeff A n)).obj
                  (((derivedTensorProductFunctor (Proj (polyGrading A n)).sheaf).obj E).obj K)),
          ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Proj (polyGrading A n)).Modules,
            Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect
                (X := (Proj (polyGrading A n)).toRingedSpace) E →
              StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
                ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver (projToSpecCoeff A n)).obj
                  (((derivedTensorProductFunctor (Proj (polyGrading A n)).sheaf).obj E).obj K)),
          ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Proj (polyGrading A n)).Modules,
            Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect
                (X := (Proj (polyGrading A n)).toRingedSpace) E →
              StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
                ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver (projToSpecCoeff A n)).obj
                  (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Proj (polyGrading A n)).sheaf).obj
                    (Opposite.op E)).obj K)),
          ∀ d : Fin (n + 1), StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
            ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver (projToSpecCoeff A n)).obj
              (((derivedTensorProductFunctor (Proj (polyGrading A n)).sheaf).obj K).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Proj (polyGrading A n)).Modules 0).obj
                  (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistingSheaf (polyGrading A n) d))))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPseudoCoherent_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_tensor_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSH].** Let `A` be a ring, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme over `A` (the structure morphism being `f : X ⟶ Spec A`), and let `K ∈ D^-_QCoh(𝒪_X)`,
i.e. `K` has quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves vanishing in all sufficiently large degrees. If
`RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K)` is pseudo-coherent in `D(A)` for every perfect `E` in `D(𝒪_X)`, then
`RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K)` is pseudo-coherent in `D(A)` for every pseudo-coherent `E` in `D(𝒪_X)`.

The proof is the source's: by [Stacks, Tag 08ES] a pseudo-coherent `E` is approximated, in any
given degree, by a perfect `P ⟶ E` whose cone `C` has no cohomology from that degree on; tensoring
with `K` raises the vanishing bound by an upper bound `b` of the cohomology of `K` and keeps it in
`D_QCoh` ([Stacks, Tag 08DX]); `RΓ(X, -)` raises it by its cohomological dimension `N`
([Stacks, Tag 08D5]); so `RΓ(X, P ⊗^𝐋 K) ⟶ RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K)` is an isomorphism in high degrees and
the pseudo-coherence of its source passes to its target degree by degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_tensor_of_isPseudoCoherent
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj
      K).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hKb : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K))
    (hpc : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E →
        StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj K)))
    (E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_derivedChowDatum
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedChowDatum {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (x : X) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (m : ℕ) (V : (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A))).Opens) (Z : Scheme.{u})
      (iZ : Z ⟶ pullback f (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))) (z : Z)
      (E : DerivedCategory
        (pullback f (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))).Modules),
      x ∈ U ∧ IsClosedImmersion iZ ∧ FinitePresentation iZ ∧
        IsIso ((iZ ≫ pullback.fst f
          (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))) ∣_ U) ∧
        (iZ ≫ pullback.fst f
          (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))).base z = x ∧
        IsClosedImmersion ((iZ ≫ pullback.snd f
          (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))) ∣_ V) ∧
        (iZ ≫ pullback.fst f
            (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))) ⁻¹ᵁ U =
          (iZ ≫ pullback.snd f
            (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))) ⁻¹ᵁ V ∧
        (iZ ≫ pullback.snd f
          (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))).base z ∈ V ∧
        Nonempty ((derivedPullback (ofScheme (pullback.snd f
            (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A)) ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι)).obj E ≅
          (derivedPullback (ofScheme (pullback.snd f
            (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A)) ⁻¹ᵁ V).ι)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (pullback f (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))).Modules 0).obj
              ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward iZ).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)))) ∧
        RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := (pullback f
          (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))).toRingedSpace) E ∧
        CohomologySupportedOn (pullback f
            (projectiveSpaceOver m (Spec (.of A)) ↘ Spec (.of A))).ringCatSheaf
          (Set.range iZ.base) E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_chowDatumMorphism
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSK], first assertion: `U ⟶ V` is a closed immersion.**  It is the inverse of
an isomorphism, a transport along an equality of opens, and the closed immersion `c|_V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_chowDatumMorphism (hb : IsIso ((iZ ≫ p) ∣_ U))
    (hc : IsClosedImmersion ((iZ ≫ q) ∣_ V))
    (hW : (iZ ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ U = (iZ ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V) :
    IsClosedImmersion (chowDatumMorphism p q iZ U V hb hW)
declarations.comment: the morphism U ⟶ V of the statement is a closed immersion; the derived comparison is chowDatum_derivedPushforward_tensor_restrict_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentation_chowDatumMorphism
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSK], first assertion: `U ⟶ V` is of finite presentation.**  The two
factorization identities show that `U ⟶ V` is a morphism over the base `S`, and
[Stacks, Tag 02FV] then deduces finite presentation of `U ⟶ V` from finite presentation of
`U ⟶ S` and of `V ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_chowDatumMorphism {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : P ⟶ S)
    (hpq : p ≫ f = q ≫ g) (hb : IsIso ((iZ ≫ p) ∣_ U))
    (hW : (iZ ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ U = (iZ ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (hU : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (U.ι ≫ f))
    (hV : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (V.ι ≫ g)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (chowDatumMorphism p q iZ U V hb hW)
declarations.comment: the morphism U ⟶ V of the statement is of finite presentation, given that U and V are of finite presentation over the base; the derived comparison is chowDatum_derivedPushforward_tensor_restrict_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.chowDatum_derivedPushforward_tensor_restrict_iso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CSK], the derived comparison.**  In the situation of Chow's lemma in the
derived category — `p : T ⟶ X` and `q : T ⟶ P` the two projections of `T = X ×_A P`,
`iZ : Z ⟶ T` the closed subscheme, `b = iZ ≫ p` an isomorphism over the open `U ⊆ X`,
`c = iZ ≫ q` a closed immersion over the open `V ⊆ P`, and `b ⁻¹ᵁ U = c ⁻¹ᵁ V` — for every
`E ∈ D(𝒪_T)` and every `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)`

`Rq_*(Lp^*K ⊗^𝐋 E)|_V ≅ R(c ∘ (b|_U)⁻¹)_*(K|_U)`.

The two hypotheses are the inputs the source cites and this library does not carry: `hE` is
clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0CSJ], that the restriction of `E` to `q ⁻¹ᵁ V` is the direct image of
the structure sheaf of `W = c ⁻¹ᵁ V` along the closed immersion `i = iZ ∣_ (q ⁻¹ᵁ V)`; and
`hproj` is [Stacks, Tag 08EU] at `i` and at the target complex `Lp^*K` restricted, which is the
projection formula at a *general* complex, the case the library's [Stacks, Tag 08EU] excludes.

Everything else is proved: the localization of the direct image is [Stacks, Tag 08FE], here
`AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedChow.derivedPushforwardRestrictOpenIso`; the monoidality of derived
pullback is [Stacks, Tag 079U]; the two composition isomorphisms are [Stacks, Tag 0D5S] and
