Noetherianity of the fibre of `f` over the residue field of a point of an étale scheme chart of
`Y` above `y` holds for some such chart exactly when it holds for every such chart, and exactly
when the base change of `f` along some field-valued representative of `y` is locally
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherianFiber_tfae
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : points B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      (∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y)
          (v : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V),
        IsEtale B S hS g ∧
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) g
            ((schemePointRepresentative B S hS V v).class B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) = y ∧
          IsLocallyNoetherianFiberAt B S hS f
            (FieldValuedPoint.map B S hS (yoneda.obj V) g
              (schemePointRepresentative B S hS V v))),
      (∀ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y)
          (v : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V),
        IsEtale B S hS g →
          pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj V) g
            ((schemePointRepresentative B S hS V v).class B S hS (yoneda.obj V)) = y →
          IsLocallyNoetherianFiberAt B S hS f
            (FieldValuedPoint.map B S hS (yoneda.obj V) g
              (schemePointRepresentative B S hS V v))),
      (∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y,
        p.class B S hS Y = y ∧ IsLocallyNoetherianFiberAt B S hS f p)
    ]
declarations.comment: conditions (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyNoetherianFiberAt_iff_exists
declarations.doc:
If a point `y` of `Y` has a field-valued representative presenting it by a monomorphism,
then the fibre of `f` over that representative is locally Noetherian exactly when the fibre over
some field-valued representative of `y` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherianFiberAt_iff_exists
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : points B S hS Y) (p₀ : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    [Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS Y p₀)] (hp₀ : p₀.class B S hS Y = y) :
    IsLocallyNoetherianFiberAt B S hS f p₀ ↔
      ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y,
        p.class B S hS Y = y ∧ IsLocallyNoetherianFiberAt B S hS f p
declarations.comment: condition (4): a monomorphic representative

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyNoetherianFiber
declarations.doc:
The fibre of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` above a point `y` of `Y`
is *locally Noetherian* when the base change of `f` along some field-valued representative of
`y` is locally Noetherian.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyNoetherianFiber_tfae` this is equivalent to the fibre
over the residue field of a point above `y` of some, equivalently of every, étale scheme chart
of `Y` being locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLocallyNoetherianFiber {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (y : points B S hS Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: the fibre over a point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasLocallyNoetherianFibersAtPoints
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` has *locally Noetherian fibres* when its fibre
above every point of its target is locally Noetherian.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasLocallyNoetherianFibers` is the every-chart reading of the same
condition, quantifying instead over the points of the étale scheme charts of the target; by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyNoetherianFiber_tfae` the two agree pointwise.
declarations.statement:
abbrev HasLocallyNoetherianFibersAtPoints {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: all fibres

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyNoetherianFibersAtPoints_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type has locally
Noetherian fibres: the spectrum of a field is Noetherian, so Stacks 04ZK applies to the base
change of `f` along any field-valued representative of a point of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocallyNoetherianFibersAtPoints_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    HasLocallyNoetherianFibersAtPoints B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeWeakAssassin_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeWeakAssassin_tfae (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (x : points B S hS X.1) :
    List.TFAE [IsWeaklyAssociatedOnSomeSchemeChartFibre B S hS f F x,
      IsWeaklyAssociatedOnEverySchemeChartFibre B S hS f F x,
      IsWeaklyAssociatedOnSomeEtaleChartSquare B S hS f F x,
      IsWeaklyAssociatedOnEveryEtaleChartSquare B S hS f F x,
      IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x]
declarations.comment: conditions (1) to (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_iff_of_mono
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S`, let `𝓕` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `x ∈ |X|` and let `Spec(k₀) ⟶ Y` be a
monomorphism representing `f(x)`. Then there is a unique point `x₀ ∈ |X_{k₀}|` mapping to `x`,
and the equivalent conditions of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeWeakAssassin_tfae` hold
exactly when `x₀` is a weakly associated point of `𝓕|_{X_{k₀}}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_iff_of_mono (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (p₀ : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y.1) [Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS Y.1 p₀)]
    {x : points B S hS X.1} (rep : p₀.class B S hS Y.1 = pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x) :
    (∃! x₀ : points B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀).1,
      pointsMap B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀).1
        (fibreAtFieldValuedPointProjection B S hS f p₀).hom x₀ = x) ∧
    ∀ x₀ : points B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀).1,
      pointsMap B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀).1
          (fibreAtFieldValuedPointProjection B S hS f p₀).hom x₀ = x →
        (IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x ↔
          IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀)
            ((modulePullback B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPointProjection B S hS f p₀)).obj F)
            x₀)
declarations.comment: condition (6), at a monomorphism from the spectrum of a field representing the image point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_iff_associated
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S`, let `𝓕` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x ∈ |X|` be such that the
fibre of `f` over `f(x)` is locally Noetherian. Then in conditions (1), (2), (3), (4) and (6) of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeWeakAssassin_tfae` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_iff_of_mono` "weakly associated" may
be replaced by "associated": each of the resulting conditions is equivalent to `x` lying in the
relative weak assassin `WeakAss_{X/Y}(𝓕)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_iff_associated (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (x : points B S hS X.1)
    (noeth : IsLocallyNoetherianFiber B S hS f.hom (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x)) :
    (IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x ↔
        IsAssociatedOnSomeSchemeChartFibre B S hS f F x) ∧
      (IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x ↔
        IsAssociatedOnEverySchemeChartFibre B S hS f F x) ∧
      (IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x ↔
        IsAssociatedOnSomeEtaleChartSquare B S hS f F x) ∧
      (IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x ↔
        IsAssociatedOnEveryEtaleChartSquare B S hS f F x) ∧
      ∀ (p₀ : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y.1) [Mono (fieldMorphism B S hS Y.1 p₀)],
        p₀.class B S hS Y.1 = pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x →
        ∀ x₀ : points B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀).1,
          pointsMap B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀).1
              (fibreAtFieldValuedPointProjection B S hS f p₀).hom x₀ = x →
            (IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x ↔
              IsAssociatedPoint B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p₀)
                ((modulePullback B S hS (fibreAtFieldValuedPointProjection B S hS f p₀)).obj F)
                x₀)
declarations.comment: the locally Noetherian case: weakly associated replaced by associated in conditions (1), (2), (3), (4) and (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint
declarations.doc:
A point `x` of `X` lies in the relative weak assassin `WeakAss_{X/Y}(F)` of an `𝒪_X`-module
`F` along a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces: for some field-valued representative of
the image of `x` in `Y`, the fibre of `f` over that representative carries a point above `x`
which is weakly associated to the restriction of `F` to the fibre.

This is condition (5) of Stacks 0CUZ, the field-valued one. When the fibres of `f` are locally
Noetherian — for instance when `f` is locally of finite type, by Stacks 0CUY — this set is
also written `Ass_{X/Y}(F)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (x : points B S hS X.1) : Prop
declarations.comment:
the membership predicate, via condition (5) of 0CUZ; stated for every module,
not only a quasi-coherent one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
The relative weak assassin `WeakAss_{X/Y}(F) ⊆ |X|` of an `𝒪_X`-module along a morphism of
algebraic spaces. When the fibres of `f` are locally Noetherian this is the set written
`Ass_{X/Y}(F)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) : Set (points B S hS X.1)
declarations.comment: the set WeakAss_{X/Y}(F), which under locally Noetherian fibres is Ass_{X/Y}(F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weaklyAssociatedPoints_tensor_modulePullback_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let `𝓕` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and `𝓖` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module. Assume `𝓕` is flat over `Y`,
that `X` and `Y` are locally Noetherian and that the fibres of `f` are locally Noetherian. Then

`Ass_X(𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*𝓖) = {x ∈ Ass_{X/Y}(𝓕) such that f(x) ∈ Ass_Y(𝓖)}`,

where `Ass` and `Ass_{X/Y}` are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weaklyAssociatedPoints` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPoints_tensor_modulePullback_eq (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    [hFqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hF : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F)
    (hLNX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hLNY : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hfib : HasLocallyNoetherianFibersAtPoints B S hS f.hom) :
    weaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS X (F ⊗ (modulePullback B S hS f).obj G) =
      {x | x ∈ relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS f F ∧
        pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x ∈ weaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS Y G}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` with vertical morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`f' : X' ⟶ Y'` and horizontal morphisms `g : Y' ⟶ Y` and `g' : X' ⟶ X`, and for an
`𝒪_X`-module `F` with `F' = (g')^*F`, the image under `g'` of a point of `WeakAss_{X'/Y'}(F')`
lies in `WeakAss_{X/Y}(F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_of_baseChange
    (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    {x' : points B S hS X'.1}
    (hx' : IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f' ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) x') :
    IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom x')
declarations.comment: part (1), for the relative weak assassin of Stacks 0CV0 and with no finiteness hypothesis on f, which part (1) does not use: the two fibres are identified outright by pasting the cartesian squares

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_baseChange_of_pointsMap_eq
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` with vertical morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`f' : X' ⟶ Y'` and horizontal morphisms `g : Y' ⟶ Y` and `g' : X' ⟶ X`, and for a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` with `F' = (g')^*F`: for every point `x` of `WeakAss_{X/Y}(F)`
and every point `y'` of `Y'` whose image in `Y` is the image of `x`, there is a point of
`WeakAss_{X'/Y'}(F')` whose image under `g'` is `x` and whose image under `f'` is `y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint_baseChange_of_pointsMap_eq
    (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) {x : points B S hS X.1} {y' : points B S hS Y'.1}
    (hx : IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x)
    (hy' : pointsMap B S hS Y'.1 g.hom y' = pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x) :
    ∃ x' : points B S hS X'.1,
      IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f' ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) x' ∧
        pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom x' = x ∧
          pointsMap B S hS X'.1 f'.hom x' = y'
declarations.comment: part (2), for the relative weak assassin of Stacks 0CV0 and with no finiteness hypothesis on f, which the proof does not use: in place of the source's appeal to Stacks 05DC the witness is carried to a representative coming from y' by the ascent of weak association along the flat surjective base change identifying the two fibres

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints_modulePullback_eq_preimage
declarations.doc:
Let

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
Y' --g---> Y
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and
put `F' = (g')^*F`. Assume that `f` is locally of finite type and that for every `y' ∈ |Y'|` the
transcendence degree of `y'/g(y')` is `0` (Stacks 04NM). Then the relative weak assassin
`WeakAss_{X'/Y'}(F')` of Stacks 0CV0 is the inverse image of `WeakAss_{X/Y}(F)` under `|g'|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints_modulePullback_eq_preimage
    (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (f_lft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (g_trdeg : ∀ y' : points B S hS Y'.1, HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS g.hom y' 0) :
    relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS f' ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) =
      pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom ⁻¹' relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS f F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints_modulePushforward_eq_image_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**The relative weak assassin of a finite direct image.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a finite morphism and let `G` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module. Then the relative weak assassin `WeakAss_{X/Y}(i_*G)` is the image
under `i` of `WeakAss_{Z/Y}(G)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints_modulePushforward_eq_image_of_isFinite
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsFinite B S hS i.hom) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS f ((modulePushforward B S hS i).obj G) =
      pointsMap B S hS Z.1 i.hom '' relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS (i ≫ f) G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PrePureSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CV6.** The standing situation for impurities: a finite type, decent morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`, a finite type quasi-coherent module `F` on the
source, and a point `y` of the target.
declarations.statement: structure PrePureSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ImpurityDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CV7.** The diagram from which an impurity is defined: a scheme `T` with a
morphism `g : T ⟶ Y` to the target, a specialization `t' ⤳ t` in `T` whose specialized point
lies over the chosen point `y`, and a point `ξ` of the base change `X_T = T ×_Y X` lying over
the generalization `t'`.
declarations.statement: structure ImpurityDiagram (P : PrePureSituation.{u, m} B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ImpurityDiagram.IsImpurity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CV8.** The diagram defines an *impurity of `F` above `y`* when the distinguished
point `ξ` of the base change `X_T` lies in the relative assassin `Ass_{X_T/T}(F_T)` and the
point `t` of `T` does not lie in the image under `f_T` of the closure of `{ξ}`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def IsImpurity : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.AffineLimitPresentation.exists_isImpurity_stageDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CV9.** In Situation 0CV6, let `(g : T ⟶ Y, t' ⤳ t, ξ)` be an impurity of `ℱ`
above `y` and let `T = lim_{i} Tᵢ` be a directed limit of affine schemes over `Y`. Then for
some stage `i` the triple `(Tᵢ ⟶ Y, t'ᵢ ⤳ tᵢ, ξᵢ)` is an impurity of `ℱ` above `y`, where the
three points are the images of `t'`, `t` and `ξ` under the canonical projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_stageDiagram (hD : D.IsImpurity) :
    ∃ i : A.J, (A.stageDiagram i).IsImpurity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImpurity_baseChange_etale_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVA.** Let `(Y', y') ⟶ (Y, y)` be a morphism of pointed algebraic spaces over `S`
with `Y' ⟶ Y` flat at `y'`. An impurity `(T ⟶ Y, t' ⤳ t, ξ)` of `F` above `y` gives an
impurity `(T₁ ⟶ Y', t₁' ⤳ t₁, ξ₁)` of the pullback `F'` of `F` to `X' = Y' ×_Y X` above `y'`
such that `T₁` is étale over `Y' ×_Y T`: the structure morphism `T₁ ⟶ Y'` is an étale morphism
`T₁ ⟶ Y' ×_Y T` followed by the projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_baseChange_etale_of_isFlatAt (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (c : PointedOver P) (hflat : IsFlatAt B S hS c.g c.y')
    (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (hD : D.IsImpurity) :
    ∃ (E : ImpurityDiagram c.baseChange) (e : yoneda.obj E.T ⟶ pullback c.g D.g),
      IsEtale B S hS e ∧ e ≫ pullback.fst c.g D.g = E.g ∧ E.IsImpurity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImpurity_pointedBaseChange_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVA**, with the field-valued representative of Stacks 05DC as a hypothesis. That
hypothesis always holds, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ImpurityDiagram.hasFibreWitnessAboveGeneralization`, and is not used:
the statement is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImpurity_baseChange_etale_of_isFlatAt`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_pointedBaseChange_of_isFlatAt (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (c : PointedOver P) (hflat : IsFlatAt B S hS c.g c.y')
    (D : ImpurityDiagram P) (hD : D.IsImpurity)
    (hwitness : D.HasFibreWitnessAboveGeneralization) :
    ∃ (E : ImpurityDiagram c.baseChange) (e : yoneda.obj E.T ⟶ pullback c.g D.g),
      IsEtale B S hS e ∧ e ≫ pullback.fst c.g D.g = E.g ∧ E.IsImpurity
declarations.comment: granting hwitness, the choice of field-valued representative that Stacks 05DC supplies; the binder is unused, that representative always existing by ImpurityDiagram.hasFibreWitnessAboveGeneralization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImpurity_isQuasiFiniteAt_of_exists_isImpurity_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVB, condition (3) implies condition (4).** An impurity of `F` above `y` whose
structure morphism `T ⟶ Y` is étale, so that `(T, t) ⟶ (Y, y)` is an étale neighbourhood, is an
impurity whose structure morphism is quasi-finite at `t`: an étale morphism of algebraic spaces
is locally quasi-finite by Stacks 03XU.

The implications (1) ⟹ (3) and (1) ⟹ (4) are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImpurity_isEtale_of_isImpurity_strictHenselization` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isImpurity_isQuasiFiniteAt_of_isImpurity_strictHenselization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImpurity_isQuasiFiniteAt_of_exists_isImpurity_isEtale
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (h : ∃ D : ImpurityDiagram P, IsEtale B S hS D.g ∧ D.IsImpurity) :
    ∃ D : ImpurityDiagram P, IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS D.g D.t ∧ D.IsImpurity
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasImpurityOverStrictHenselization_iff_hasRelativeAssociatedPointAvoidingClosedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVB, (1) ⟺ (2).** For a geometric point `ȳ` of `Y` lying over `y`, there is an
impurity of `ℱ` above `y` over the strict henselization `Y^{sh}` exactly when some point of the
relative assassin of `ℱ^{sh}` does not specialize to a point of the closed fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasImpurityOverStrictHenselization_iff_hasRelativeAssociatedPointAvoidingClosedFibre
    (hybar : ybar.LiesOver P.y) :
    HasImpurityOverStrictHenselization P ybar ↔
      HasRelativeAssociatedPointAvoidingClosedFibre P ybar
declarations.comment:
(1) ⟺ (2), with (2) corrected as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasRelativeAssociatedPointAvoidingClosedFibre`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_hasImpurityOverStrictHenselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVB.** In Situation 0CV6, for a geometric point `ȳ` of `Y` lying over `y`, the four
conditions of the source are equivalent: an impurity of `ℱ` above `y` over `Y^{sh}` with
specialized point `ȳ`; a point of `Ass_{X^{sh}/Y^{sh}}(ℱ^{sh})` not specializing into the closed
fibre; an impurity over an étale neighbourhood of `y`; an impurity whose structure morphism is
quasi-finite at its specialized point.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_hasImpurityOverStrictHenselization (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (ybar : GeometricPoint B S hS P.Y) (hybar : ybar.LiesOver P.y) :
    [HasImpurityOverStrictHenselization P ybar,
      HasRelativeAssociatedPointAvoidingClosedFibre P ybar,
      HasImpurityOverEtaleNeighborhood P,
      HasImpurityQuasiFiniteAtPoint P].TFAE
declarations.comment: condition (2) in the corrected reading recorded in the note of StrictHenselizationConditions: some associated point does not specialize into the closed fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSpacePureAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVD, part (3).** The algebraic space `X` is *pure above `y`* when its structure
sheaf `𝒪_X` is pure above `y`.

The module of the situation plays no role: the condition is part (1) for the situation with the
same morphism and the same chosen point whose module is `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement: def IsSpacePureAbove (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSpacePureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVD, part (6).** The algebraic space `X` is *`Y`-pure*, or *pure relative to
`Y`*, when its structure sheaf `𝒪_X` is pure relative to `Y`.

This is part (5) for the situation whose module is `𝒪_X`; neither the module nor the chosen
point of the situation plays a role, the latter because purity relative to `Y` varies it over
all of `|Y|`.
declarations.statement: def IsSpacePureRelative (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPureAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVD, part (1).** The module is *pure above `y`* when no impurity of `F` above `y`
has its structure morphism `T ⟶ Y` quasi-finite at `t`.

This is the failure of condition (4) of Stacks 0CVB, which is the condition the proof of
Stacks 0CVF works with.
declarations.statement: def IsPureAbove (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1), as the failure of condition (4) of Stacks 0CVB

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversallyPureAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVD, part (2).** The module is *universally pure above `y`* when there is no
impurity of `F` above `y` at all.
declarations.statement: def IsUniversallyPureAbove (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsUniversallyPureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVD, part (4).** The module is *universally pure relative to `Y`* when it is
universally pure above every point of `Y`.

The chosen point of the situation is irrelevant: the condition varies it over all of `|Y|`.
declarations.statement: def IsUniversallyPureRelative (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVD, part (5).** The module is *pure relative to `Y`* when it is pure above every
point of `Y`.

The chosen point of the situation is irrelevant: the condition varies it over all of `|Y|`.
declarations.statement: def IsPureRelative (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVE.** A finite type quasi-coherent module is universally pure above `y` exactly
when, for every morphism `(Y', y') ⟶ (Y, y)` of pointed algebraic spaces, its base change
`F_{Y'}` is pure above `y'`.

The source lists the two conditions without the connective; they are equivalent, as the
statement of the analogous Stacks 05J6 for schemes makes explicit. The consequence the source
draws for purity relative to the whole base is
`isUniversallyPureRelative_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureRelative`.

Both directions are formal, as the source says: an impurity of a base change is an impurity of
`F` by `isImpurity_alongBaseChange_iff`, and conversely an impurity diagram `(T, t' ⤳ t, ξ)` of
`F` is an impurity of the base change along `(T, t) ⟶ (Y, y)` itself, whose structure morphism
is the identity and hence quasi-finite at `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureAbove_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureAbove
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) :
    IsUniversallyPureAbove P ↔ ∀ c : PointedOver P, IsPureAbove c.baseChange
declarations.comment: the equivalence left implicit by the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureRelative_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVE, the closing clause.** The module is universally pure relative to `Y` exactly
when, for every morphism `Y' ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces, its base change `F_{Y'}` is pure
relative to `Y'`.

This is formal, as the source says, and is the pointwise equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureAbove` read at every
point of the base at once: a pointed morphism `(Y', y') ⟶ (Y, y)` is a morphism `Y' ⟶ Y`
together with a point `y'` of `Y'` whose image is `y`, and the two sides quantify over all `y`
and all such `y'` in the two possible orders.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureRelative_iff_forall_baseChange_isPureRelative
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS) :
    IsUniversallyPureRelative P ↔
      ∀ (Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y')
        (g : Y' ⟶ P.Y), P.IsPureRelativeAlong hY' g
declarations.comment: the 'in particular' clause: universally pure relative to Y iff every base change is pure relative to Y'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPureAbove_baseChange_of_isQuasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVF.** If `(Y', y') ⟶ (Y, y)` is a morphism of pointed algebraic spaces with
`Y' ⟶ Y` quasi-finite at `y'`, and the module is pure above `y`, then its base change `F_{Y'}`
is pure above `y'`.

An impurity of `F_{Y'}` above `y'` whose structure morphism is quasi-finite at `t` is an
impurity of `F` above `y` whose structure morphism is quasi-finite at `t`, by
`isQuasiFiniteAt_comp`, the pointwise form of Stacks 03XK that the source appeals to.

Purity above `y` is written out in the hypothesis rather than named: the condition stated there
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsPureAbove` of Stacks 0CVD part (1), definitionally and on the
nose, so a consumer holding that predicate may pass it directly.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPureAbove_baseChange_of_isQuasiFiniteAt (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (c : PointedOver P)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS c.g c.y')
    (hP : ∀ D : ImpurityDiagram P, IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS D.g D.t → ¬ D.IsImpurity) :
    IsPureAbove c.baseChange

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPureAbove_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVG, part (1).** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, let `(Y₁, y₁) ⟶ (Y, y)` be a
morphism of pointed algebraic spaces with `Y₁ ⟶ Y` flat at `y₁`. If the base change `F_{Y₁}`
is pure above `y₁`, then `F` is pure above `y`. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPureAbove_of_isPureAbove_baseChange_of_isFlatAt`.
declarations.statement: alias isPureAbove_of_isFlatAt
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVG, part (2).** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, let `(Y₁, y₁) ⟶ (Y, y)` be a
morphism of pointed algebraic spaces with `Y₁ ⟶ Y` flat at `y₁`. If the base change `F_{Y₁}`
is universally pure above `y₁`, then `F` is universally pure above `y`. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isUniversallyPureAbove_baseChange_of_isFlatAt`.
declarations.statement: alias isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isFlatAt
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPureAbove_of_isPureAbove_baseChange_of_isFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVG, part (1).** If `(Y₁, y₁) ⟶ (Y, y)` is a morphism of pointed algebraic
spaces with `Y₁ ⟶ Y` flat at `y₁` and the base change `F_{Y₁}` is pure above `y₁`, then `F` is
pure above `y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPureAbove_of_isPureAbove_baseChange_of_isFlatAt (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (c : PointedOver P) (hflat : IsFlatAt B S hS c.g c.y')
    (hpure : IsPureAbove c.baseChange) :
    IsPureAbove P
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.isPureAbove_situation_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVH, purity above `y`.** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a
closed immersion and suppose `ℱ = i_*𝒢` for a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`.
Then `𝒢` is pure above `y` exactly when `ℱ` is.

An impurity of `𝒢` above `y` whose structure morphism is quasi-finite at `t` is such an impurity
of `ℱ` above `y`, and conversely; this is Stacks 0CV4 on the base changes, together with the
fact that `Z_T ⟶ X_T` is a closed embedding on points.

The inputs of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.BaseChangeInput` — affine base
change on the base changes — are hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPureAbove_situation_iff
    (hin : c.BaseChangeInput) :
    IsPureAbove c.situation ↔ IsPureAbove P
declarations.comment: pure above y, granting as hin affine base change (Stacks 02KG) on the base changes of the situation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.isUniversallyPureAbove_situation_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVH, universal purity above `y`.** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion and suppose `ℱ = i_*𝒢` for a finite type quasi-coherent
`𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`. Then `𝒢` is universally pure above `y` exactly when `ℱ` is.

An impurity of `𝒢` above `y` is an impurity of `ℱ` above `y`, and conversely.

The inputs of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.BaseChangeInput` — affine base
change on the base changes — are hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureAbove_situation_iff
    (hin : c.BaseChangeInput) :
    IsUniversallyPureAbove c.situation ↔ IsUniversallyPureAbove P
declarations.comment: universally pure above y, granting as hin affine base change (Stacks 02KG) on the base changes of the situation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.isPureAbove_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVH, purity above `y`.** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a
closed immersion and suppose `ℱ = i_*𝒢` for a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`.
Then `𝒢` is pure above `y` if and only if `ℱ` is pure above `y`.
declarations.statement: theorem isPureAbove_iff : IsPureAbove c.situation ↔ IsPureAbove P
declarations.comment: pure above y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.isUniversallyPureAbove_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVH, universal purity above `y`.** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion and suppose `ℱ = i_*𝒢` for a finite type quasi-coherent
`𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`.  Then `𝒢` is universally pure above `y` if and only if `ℱ` is universally
pure above `y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureAbove_iff :
    IsUniversallyPureAbove c.situation ↔ IsUniversallyPureAbove P
declarations.comment: universally pure above y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVI, part (2).** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, if `f : X ⟶ Y` is proper then
the module `ℱ` is universally pure above `y`.

A proper morphism is universally closed, and a universally closed morphism admits no impurity
diagram. Since the point `y` of the situation is arbitrary, this is purity of `ℱ` relative
to `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS P.f) : IsUniversallyPureAbove P
declarations.comment: part (2): a finite type quasi-coherent module on the source of a proper morphism is universally pure above every point of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVI, part (1), in general form.** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion and suppose `ℱ = i_*𝒢` for a finite type quasi-coherent
`𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`. If the composite `Z ⟶ Y` is proper, then `ℱ` is universally pure above `y`.

This is part (2) applied to the situation on `Z`, transferred to `ℱ` by Stacks 0CVH. The
source states the hypothesis as properness of the support of `ℱ` over `Y` and then reduces to
part (2) exactly this way, at the scheme-theoretic support; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport`.

The input of Stacks 0CVH, affine base change on the base changes of the situation, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.baseChangeInput`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ClosedSubspaceModule.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper
    {P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS} (c : ClosedSubspaceModule P)
    (hZY : IsProper B S hS (c.i.hom ≫ P.f)) :
    IsUniversallyPureAbove P
declarations.comment: part (1) in general form, taking the closed-immersion presentation of the module as data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVI, part (1).** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, if the scheme-theoretic
support of `ℱ` is proper over `Y`, then `ℱ` is universally pure above `y`.

This is the general form above at the closed-immersion presentation of `ℱ` furnished by its
scheme-theoretic support, Stacks 07U1, and the module on it of Stacks 07U0.

The two arguments `hZ` and `hid` are not assumptions about the geometry but the closed-subspace data of the scheme-theoretic support, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedSubspace_schemeTheoreticSupport` produces from
quasi-coherence of the module together with its finite type in the sectionwise sense of
Stacks 03DL(5); they are taken as arguments because every other hypothesis here, the
properness assumption included, is stated about the closed subspace they exhibit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hZ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS P.sourceSpace P.F))
    (hid : definingIdealSheaf B S hS P.sourceSpace
        ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS P.sourceSpace P.F, hZ⟩ =
      annihilatorIdealSheaf B S hS P.sourceSpace P.F)
    (hZY : IsProper B S hS ((closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS P.sourceSpace
      ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS P.sourceSpace P.F, hZ⟩).hom ≫ P.f)) :
    IsUniversallyPureAbove P
declarations.comment: part (1) at the scheme-theoretic support, naming the support's closed-subspace data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_structure_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVI, part (3).** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a proper decent morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S`, then `X` is universally pure above every point of `Y`, that is, universally pure
relative to `Y`.

This is part (2) for the situation whose module is the structure sheaf of `X`.
declarations.comment: part (3): the source of a proper decent morphism is universally pure above every point of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVI, part (1), for a closed-immersion presentation of the module.** In the
situation of Stacks 0CV6, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion and suppose `ℱ = i_*𝒢` for a
finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`. If the composite `Z ⟶ Y` is proper, then `ℱ` is
universally pure above `y`.

This is part (2) applied to the situation on `Z`, transferred to `ℱ` by Stacks 0CVH; it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ClosedSubspaceModule.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper`.
declarations.statement: alias ClosedSubspaceModule.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper_comp
declarations.comment: part (1), for any presentation of the module as the direct image along a closed immersion whose composite to the target is proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper_supportSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVI, part (1).** In the situation of Stacks 0CV6, if the support of `ℱ` is proper
over `Y`, then `ℱ` is universally pure above `y`; the point `y` being arbitrary, `ℱ` is
universally pure relative to `Y`.

The support is the scheme-theoretic support `Z` of Stacks 07U1, and properness over `Y` is
properness of the composite `Z ⟶ X ⟶ Y`. The proof is the source's: by Stacks 07U0 the module
is `i_*𝒢` for a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢`, and the closed-immersion form
above applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyPureAbove_of_isProper_supportSubspace
    (P : PrePureSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hZY : IsProper B S hS
      ((closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS P.sourceSpace P.supportSubspace).hom ≫ P.f)) :
    IsUniversallyPureAbove P
declarations.comment: part (1): a finite type quasi-coherent module whose scheme-theoretic support is proper over the target is universally pure above every point of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_tensor_modulePullback_iff_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite type, let `x` be a point of `|X|`, let `𝓕` be a finite type quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module and let `𝓖` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module.  If `𝓕` is flat at `x` over `Y`, then
`x` is weakly associated to `𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*𝓖` if and only if the image of `x` is weakly associated
to `𝓖` and `x` lies in the relative weak assassin `WeakAss_{X/Y}(𝓕)` of Stacks 0CV0 — which, the
fibres of `f` being locally Noetherian by Stacks 0CUY, is the set the source writes
`Ass_{X/Y}(𝓕)`.

This is the source's proof.  A commuting square of étale scheme charts over `f` through `x`
exists by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chartDiagram_chartSchemeToPoints_eq`; on it the two
sides of the formula become the Zariski conditions of the scheme case by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_tensor_modulePullback_iff_of_chartDiagram`,
whose comparison of `(𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*𝓖)|_U` with `𝓕|_U ⊗_{𝒪_U} q^*(𝓖|_V)` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_restrictToChart_tensor_modulePullback_chartDiagram` and whose
identification of the relative assassins is the two chart-diagram comparisons of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Divisors.MorphismWeaklyAssociated.ChartDiagramRelativeAssassin`
joined by Stacks 05F2, available because the chart morphism inherits local finite type from `f`.
The chart restrictions are quasi-coherent and, on the source, of finite type, the chart morphism
is locally of finite type, and the chart restriction of `𝓕` is flat over the target chart at the
chart point by Stacks 05VU; so the scheme case,
`Stacks.Divisors.isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_tensorPullback_iff_of_finiteType`, applies with no
further hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_tensor_modulePullback_iff_of_finiteType (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [F.IsFiniteType] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (x : points B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F x) :
    IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS X (F ⊗ (modulePullback B S hS f).obj G) x ↔
      (IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS Y G (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x) ∧
        x ∈ relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS f F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.weaklyAssociatedPoints_tensor_modulePullback_eq_inter_preimage
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` which is locally of
finite type, let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module which is flat over `Y`, and let
`G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module. Then the weakly associated points of `F ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*G` are
exactly the points of `Ass_{X/Y}(F)` lying over weakly associated points of `G`.

This is the source's own proof, which is that the statement is an immediate consequence of its
pointwise form, Stacks 0CVK, available here as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBourbakiFormulaAtFlatPoints_of_finiteType`. The tag's flatness
hypothesis is what makes the pointwise flatness side condition hold at every point, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_forall_of_isFlatOver`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyAssociatedPoints_tensor_modulePullback_eq_inter_preimage (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [F.IsFiniteType] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hF : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    weaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS X (F ⊗ (modulePullback B S hS f).obj G) =
      relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS f F ∩
        pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom ⁻¹' weaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS Y G
declarations.comment: the full set equality, in the intersection-with-a-preimage form the tag writes, under the tag's own assumptions and with the source's own proof: the statement is an immediate consequence of its pointwise form, Stacks 0CVK, proved in its own generality as Space.isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_tensor_modulePullback_iff_of_finiteType and is applied here through Space.isBourbakiFormulaAtFlatPoints_of_finiteType, the two differing by and_comm. The sets are Space.relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints of Stacks 0CV0, the Ass_{X/Y}(F) of the tag once the fibres of f are locally Noetherian as they are here by Stacks 0CUY, and Space.weaklyAssociatedPoints of Stacks 0CTX. The tag's flatness assumption hF is used, through Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_forall_of_isFlatOver, to discharge the pointwise flatness side condition of Stacks 0CVK at every point. Nothing beyond the tag's own assumptions is used: every binder of this theorem is one of them, namely f locally of finite type, F quasi-coherent of finite type, G quasi-coherent, and F flat over Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isIsoAt_secondMap_iff_isZeroAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVM**, pointwise.  For an exact sequence `F ⟶ G ⟶ H ⟶ 0` of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules and a scheme `T` over `Y`, the base change of `v : G ⟶ H` to `X ×_Y T` is an
isomorphism exactly when the base change of `u : F ⟶ G` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIsoAt_secondMap_iff_isZeroAt (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (H : Modules.{u, u} B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2) (hH : H.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (v : D.G ⟶ H) (hcomp : D.u ≫ v = 0)
    (hexact : (ShortComplex.mk D.u v hcomp).Exact) [Epi v] (T : D.SchemesOver) :
    (D.secondMap H hH v).IsIsoAt (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) T ↔
      D.IsZeroAt (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) T
declarations.comment: pointwise

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoFunctor_secondMap_eq_zeroFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVM.**  For an exact sequence `F ⟶ G ⟶ H ⟶ 0` of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules,
the locus of schemes over `Y` where the base change of `v : G ⟶ H` is an isomorphism coincides
with the locus where the base change of `u : F ⟶ G` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoFunctor_secondMap_eq_zeroFunctor (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (H : Modules.{u, u} B S hS D.X.1 D.X.2) (hH : H.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (v : D.G ⟶ H) (hcomp : D.u ≫ v = 0)
    (hexact : (ShortComplex.mk D.u v hcomp).Exact) [Epi v] :
    (D.secondMap H hH v).isoFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS) =
      D.zeroFunctor (modulePullbackSystem B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_of_isFlatOver_of_supp_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVT.** A morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation admitting
a finite type quasi-coherent module of full support which is flat over the target is universally
open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universallyOpen_of_isFlatOver_of_supp_eq_univ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hsupp : SheafOfModules.supp F = Set.univ)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) : UniversallyOpen f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyOpen_of_isFlatOver_of_fullSupport
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
presentation and let `𝓕` be an `𝒪_X`-module which, on charts, is quasi-coherent, of finite type,
of full support and flat over `Y`. Then `f` is universally open.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyOpen_of_isFlatOver_of_fullSupport
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : IsQuasicoherentOnCharts B S hS hX F) (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS hX F)
    (hsupp : HasFullSupportOnCharts B S hS hX F) (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS hX f F) :
    UniversallyOpen B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyConstructible_relativeAssassinContainmentLocus
declarations.doc:
Let `V` be a scheme of the site, let `f : X ⟶ schemeSpace V` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces which is locally of finite presentation, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let
`U` be an open subset of `|X|`. Let `φ : schemeSpace W ⟶ X` be a surjective étale scheme chart
and `α : W ⟶ V` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of the site with
`φ ≫ f = schemeSpaceMap α`, such that the chart restriction of `F` is of finite presentation
and `φ⁻¹(U)` is quasi-compact over `V`. Then the set of points `y` of `V` over which every point
of the relative assassin of `F` above `y` lies in `U` is locally constructible in `V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstructible_relativeAssassinContainmentLocus
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (V W : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace V) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (U : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hUopen : @IsOpen _ (pointTopology B S hS X.1) U)
    (φ : schemeSpace W ⟶ X)
    (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS (schemeSpace W).1 φ.hom))
    (α : W ⟶ V) (hα : φ ≫ f = schemeSpaceMap α)
    (hfX : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hαqc : QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map α))
    (hαqs : QuasiSeparated ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map α))
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hGfp : (baseChangeModule B S hS F W φ.hom).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hUqc : QuasiCompact ((chartOpenOfOpenPoints B S hS W φ U hUopen).ι ≫
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map α)) :
    IsLocallyConstructible (relativeAssassinContainmentLocus B S hS V f F U)
declarations.comment: the surjective etale scheme chart of X is a hypothesis rather than a construction, and so are the transfers along it of quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of alpha, of finite presentation of the chart restriction of F, and of quasi-compactness of U over V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyConstructible_relativeAssassinContainmentLocus_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `V` be a scheme of the site, let `X` be an algebraic space of finite presentation over `V`,
let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation and let `U` be an open subset of
`|X|` whose map to `|V|` is quasi-compact. Then the set of points of `V` over which every point of
the relative assassin of `F` above that point lies in `U` is locally constructible.

Here `hUqc` is the point-level reading of "`U → V` is quasi-compact": the part of `U` lying over
a quasi-compact open of `|V|` is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstructible_relativeAssassinContainmentLocus_of_isFinitePresentation
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace V) (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F)
    (U : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hUopen : IsOpen U)
    (hUqc : ∀ A : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V).Opens,
      IsCompact (A : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)) →
      IsCompact (U ∩ (fun x =>
          schemeSpacePointToScheme B S hS V (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x)) ⁻¹'
        (A : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)))) :
    IsLocallyConstructible (relativeAssassinContainmentLocus B S hS V f F U)
declarations.comment: with `U → V` quasi-compact read on the point sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyConstructible_relativeAssassinContainmentLocus_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
Let `V` be a scheme of the site, let `X` be an algebraic space of finite presentation over `V`,
let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation and let `U ⊆ X` be an open subspace
whose morphism to `V` is quasi-compact. Then the set of points of `V` over which every point of the
relative assassin of `F` above that point lies in `U` is locally constructible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstructible_relativeAssassinContainmentLocus_of_isQuasiCompact
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace V) (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F)
    (U : Subfunctor X.1) (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS (U.ι ≫ f.hom)) :
    IsLocallyConstructible (relativeAssassinContainmentLocus B S hS V f F
      (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineChart_hasFreeSectionsAlongFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVW**, reduced to the affine étale chart of the target at the
prescribed point.

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose restriction to every étale chart of `X` is quasi-coherent of
finite type, and let `y` be a point of `|Y|` at which `F` is flat over `Y` along the whole
set-theoretic fibre `f^{-1}({y})`. Then there are

* an object `Y₁` of the site whose scheme is affine, an étale morphism `q : Y₁ ⟶ Y` and a
  point `w` of `Y₁` above `y` — the source's `(Y', y') ⟶ (Y, y)` before the passage to an
  elementary étale neighbourhood;
* an étale chart `U` of `X` whose scheme is affine, and a morphism `ĝ : U ⟶ Y₁` of the site
  making the square over `q` commute, such that the induced morphism from `U` to the base
  change `X ×_Y Y₁` is surjective on points — the source's affine surjective étale cover `X'`
  of `X ×_Y Y'`;
* the morphism of schemes underlying `ĝ` is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, and the
  conclusion of Stacks 05L1 holds for it, for the restriction of `F` to `U`, and for the point
  of the scheme of `Y₁` determined by `w` — with the covering clause of that conclusion read
  on the point space of `X`, where it says that the set-theoretic fibre `f^{-1}({y})` is the
  image of the fibre of the affine scheme Stacks 05L1 produces.

The hypothesis `hFt` is the source's "`F` of finite type", on the small étale site of `X`.
The chartwise finite type it gives is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnCharts_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite`, and chartwise
quasi-coherence follows from `SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_restrictToChart`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineChart_hasFreeSectionsAlongFibre {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hFt : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (y : points B S hS Y.1)
    (hflat : ∀ x : points B S hS X.1, pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x = y →
      x ∈ flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    ∃ (Y₁ : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj Y₁ ⟶ Y.1) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
      (ĝ : U.obj.left ⟶ Y₁) (hsq : yoneda.map ĝ ≫ q = U.obj.hom ≫ f.hom)
      (w : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Y₁)),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y₁) ∧
      IsAffine (etaleChartScheme B S hS U) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj Y₁) q w = y ∧
      IsSurjective B S hS (pullback.lift (yoneda.map ĝ) U.obj.hom hsq) ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ĝ) ∧
      QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ĝ) ∧
      HasFreeSectionsAlongFibreOver ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ĝ)
        (chartModule B S hS X.2 F U) (pointsToScheme B S hS Y₁ w)
        (pointOfEtaleChart B S hS U) (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom ⁻¹' {y})
declarations.comment: the etale neighbourhood, the affine scheme and its free sections are delivered; reduced to the affine etale chart of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineChart_hasFreeSectionsAlongFibre_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CVW**, at the source's own hypotheses.  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `y`
be a point of `|Y|` at which `F` is flat along the fibre.  Then there is an affine étale
neighbourhood of `y` in `Y` and an affine étale chart of `X` over it, surjective onto the
fibre, over which `F` has free sections along the fibre.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineChart_hasFreeSectionsAlongFibre`, which takes `F`
of finite type on the small étale site of `X` and derives the finite type of each chart
restriction by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnCharts_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite`.
declarations.statement: alias exists_affineChart_hasFreeSectionsAlongFibre_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.comment: the etale neighbourhood, the affine scheme and its free sections are delivered, reduced to the affine etale chart of the target. At the source's own hypotheses: `F` of finite type on the small etale site of `X`, from which the finite type of each chart restriction follows by isFiniteTypeOnCharts_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite, which is proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etale_affine_free_sections_along_fibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVW.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`𝓕` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `y ∈ |Y|`, with fibre `F = f^{-1}({y}) ⊆ |X|`.
Assume

1. `f` is of finite type (`hf`),
2. `𝓕` is of finite type (`hFt`), and
3. `𝓕` is flat over `Y` at every point of `F` (`hflat`).

Then there are a scheme `Y'` with a point `y'` and an étale morphism `e : Y' ⟶ Y` sending `y'`
to `y`, an affine scheme `X'` with morphisms `g : X' ⟶ X` and `k : X' ⟶ Spec 𝒪_{Y', y'}` making
the square over `f` commute, such that the induced `X' ⟶ X ×_Y Spec 𝒪_{Y', y'}` is étale, `F`
is the image under `g` of the fibre `X'_{y'}` of `X'` over the closed point of
`Spec 𝒪_{Y', y'}` (so `|X'_{y'}| ⟶ F` is surjective), and `Γ(X', g^*𝓕)` is a free
`𝒪_{Y', y'}`-module, the module structure coming from `k`.

The schemes `Y'`, `Spec 𝒪_{Y', y'}` (`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.specStalk`) and `X'` are
objects of the big fppf site of `S`, morphisms of algebraic spaces out of them are morphisms out
of the presheaves they represent, and `Γ(X', g^*𝓕)` is the module of global sections of the
restriction of `g^*𝓕` to the scheme `X'`, its identity chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_affine_free_sections_along_fibre {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hFt : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (y : points B S hS Y.1)
    (hflat : ∀ x : points B S hS X.1, pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x = y →
      x ∈ flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    ∃ (Y' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y')
      (e : yoneda.obj Y' ⟶ Y.1) (X' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj X' ⟶ X.1)
      (k : X' ⟶ BigFppfOver.specStalk B S hS Y' y')
      (hcomm : yoneda.map k ≫ yoneda.map (BigFppfOver.specStalkTo B S hS Y' y') ≫ e =
        g ≫ f.hom),
      IsEtale B S hS e ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj Y') e ((pointsEquivScheme B S hS Y').symm y') = y ∧
      IsEtale B S hS (pullback.lift (yoneda.map k) g hcomm) ∧
      pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom ⁻¹' {y} =
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X') g ''
          (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X') (yoneda.map k) ⁻¹'
            {BigFppfOver.specStalkClosedPoint B S hS Y' y'}) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X') ∧
      (let M := restrictToChart B S hS (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X')
          ((modulePullback B S hS (X := ⟨yoneda.obj X', isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X'⟩)
            (Y := X) (ObjectProperty.homMk g)).obj F)
          (idEtaleChart B S hS X')
       letI : Module (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y').presheaf.stalk y') Γ(M, ⊤) :=
         globalSectionsModuleOfSpecBase ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map k) M
       Module.Free (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y').presheaf.stalk y') Γ(M, ⊤))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_chart_square_at_point
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVY: the diagram of the conclusion.** Every point `x` of the source
of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` lies in the image of a commuting square
of étale scheme charts

```
(X, x) ←—— (U, x')
  |          |
  ↓          ↓
(Y, f x) ←— (V, y')
```

whose two charts `U` and `V` are **affine**, through a point `x'` of `U` lying over `x`; the
point `y'` of `V` it induces then lies over the image of `x`.

This is the diagram of pointed schemes which Tag 0CVY asserts, and it is produced here with
none of the tag's three hypotheses: neither `f` nor any module on `X` enters. What Tag 0CVY
adds to it is the projectivity of `Γ(U, 𝓕|_U)` over `Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` after a further shrinking,
which is the case of schemes, Tag 05ID; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections`.

The three conclusions after affineness are, in order: the square of charts commutes over `f`;
the chart point lies over `x`; and the image of the chart point in the target chart lies over
the image of `x` in `|Y|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_etale_chart_square_at_point
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : points B S hS X) :
    ∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (g : (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V)
      (x' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U))),
      IsAffine (chartScheme U) ∧ IsAffine (chartScheme V) ∧
        U.obj.hom ≫ f = yoneda.map g ≫ V.obj.hom ∧
        pointsMap B S hS _ U.obj.hom x' = x ∧
        pointsMap B S hS _ V.obj.hom (pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map g) x') =
          pointsMap B S hS X f x
declarations.comment: the commutative diagram of pointed schemes of the conclusion — affine étale charts of the source and of the target, through the given point and through its image, with a morphism between them over f — and nothing of the projectivity of the sections, which is the case of schemes, Tag 05ID

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVY.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module and let `x` be a point of `|X|`. Assume

1. `f` is locally of finite presentation (`hfp`, Stacks 03XP part (1));
2. `F` is quasi-coherent and of finite presentation (`hqc`, `hFfp`), chartwise: its
   restriction to every étale scheme chart of `X` is;
3. `F` is flat at `x` over `Y` (`hflat`), chartwise: on every commuting square of étale charts
   and at every point of the source chart over `x`, the restriction of `F` to the source chart
   is flat over the target chart there.

Then there are an étale chart `U` of `X`, an étale chart `V` of `Y`, affine objects `X'`, `Y'`
of the site with étale morphisms `p : X' ⟶ U` and `q : Y' ⟶ V`, a morphism `k : X' ⟶ Y'` and a
point `x''` of `|X'|` such that the composites `X' → X` and `Y' → Y` are étale, the square
commutes over `f`, `x''` lies over `x`, its image in `|Y'|` lies over the image of `x`, and the
sections `Γ(X', p^*(F|_U))` form a projective `Γ(Y', 𝒪_{Y'})`-module.

The conclusion is the conclusion of Tag 0CVY, with no clause dropped, and nothing is assumed
beyond the tag's own hypotheses. The source's proof of Tag 0CVY is the remark that the
statement reduces to the case of schemes, Tag 05ID; that case, read inside the big fppf site,
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_hom_projective_sections`. See the module
docstring on this, and on why the module of the conclusion is named as a pullback of a chart
restriction.

The hypotheses (2) and (3) are stated chartwise, which is how this development states these
conditions for a module on an algebraic space: compare
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOver`, the definition of Stacks 05VV, which is the chartwise
condition on every commuting square of étale charts. They are not weakenings: the chartwise
form is one of the equivalent conditions of Stacks 05VU, which the source's definition
Stacks 05VV names.

Everything in the conclusion except the projectivity comes from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_chart_square_at_point`, which is unconditional;
the hypotheses are used only to feed the case of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFfp : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (g : (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V)
      (x' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U))),
      U.obj.hom ≫ f = yoneda.map g ≫ V.obj.hom →
      pointsMap B S hS _ U.obj.hom x' = x →
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt
        (LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToSheafedSpace.map
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g).toLRSHom)
        (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U) (pointsToScheme B S hS _ x')) :
    ∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (U' E' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (p : U' ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U)
      (q : E' ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V) (k : U' ⟶ E')
      (x'' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj U')),
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U') ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj E') ∧
      (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) ≫ f = yoneda.map k ≫ yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom ∧
      pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) x'' = x ∧
      pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom)
          (pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map k) x'') = pointsMap B S hS X f x ∧
      (let M := (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p)).obj
           (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U)
       letI : Module Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj E', ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤) :=
         Module.compHom Γ(M, ⊤) ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map k).appTop.hom
       Module.Projective Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj E', ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤))
declarations.comment: the full conclusion — the pointed affine étale diagram and the projectivity of the sections — with the case of schemes, Tag 05ID, supplied by exists_isAffine_etale_hom_projective_sections, and with the tag's conditions (2) and (3) on the module in their étale-chartwise form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_of_isFlatOverAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVY.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
which is locally of finite presentation, let `𝓕` be an `𝒪_X`-module which is quasi-coherent and
of finite presentation on every étale chart, and let `x` be a point of `X` at which `𝓕` is flat
over `Y`. Then `x` lies in the image of a commuting square of étale charts, refined by affine
objects `U'` of `X` and `E'` of `Y` of the site, through a point of `U'`, such that
`Γ(U', 𝓕|_{U'})` is a projective `Γ(E', 𝒪_{E'})`-module.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections`, whose
proof feeds the case of schemes, Tag 05ID, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_hom_projective_sections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_of_isFlatOverAt
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hFfp : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (g : (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V)
      (x' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U))),
      U.obj.hom ≫ f = yoneda.map g ≫ V.obj.hom →
      pointsMap B S hS _ U.obj.hom x' = x →
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt
        (LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToSheafedSpace.map
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g).toLRSHom)
        (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U) (pointsToScheme B S hS _ x')) :
    ∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (U' E' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (p : U' ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U)
      (q : E' ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V) (k : U' ⟶ E')
      (x'' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj U')),
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U') ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj E') ∧
      (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) ≫ f = yoneda.map k ≫ yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom ∧
      pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) x'' = x ∧
      pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom)
          (pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map k) x'') = pointsMap B S hS X f x ∧
      (let M := (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p)).obj
           (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U)
       letI : Module Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj E', ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤) :=
         Module.compHom Γ(M, ⊤) ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map k).appTop.hom
       Module.Projective Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj E', ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_chart_square_along_fibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVZ: the diagram of the conclusion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `y` be a point of `|Y|`. Then there
is a commuting square of étale scheme charts

```
X ←—— U
|     |
↓     ↓
Y ←—— V
```

whose two charts `U` and `V` are **affine**, together with a point `y'` of `|V|` lying over `y`,
such that the fibre `F = f^{-1}({y})` is contained in the image of `|U| → |X|`. Moreover every
point of `F` is the image of a point of `|U|` lying over `y'`.

This is the diagram of Tag 0CVZ, produced with none of the tag's hypotheses on the module and
with only quasi-compactness of `f`, which is part of the tag's hypothesis (1) and is what makes
`F` quasi-compact. What Tag 0CVZ adds to it is the projectivity of `Γ(U, 𝓕|_U)` over
`Γ(V, 𝒪_V)` after a further shrinking, which is the case of schemes, Tag 05KW; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_along_fibre`.

The clauses after affineness are, in order: the square of charts commutes over `f`; the chart
point lies over `y`; the fibre is contained in the image of the source chart; and the sharpened
form of that containment, by points of the source chart lying over `y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_etale_chart_square_along_fibre
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) (y : points B S hS Y) :
    ∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (k : (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V)
      (y' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V))),
      IsAffine (chartScheme U) ∧ IsAffine (chartScheme V) ∧
        U.obj.hom ≫ f = yoneda.map k ≫ V.obj.hom ∧
        pointsMap B S hS _ V.obj.hom y' = y ∧
        {x : points B S hS X | pointsMap B S hS X f x = y} ⊆
          Set.range (pointsMap B S hS _ U.obj.hom) ∧
        ∀ x : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x = y →
          ∃ x' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U)),
            pointsMap B S hS _ U.obj.hom x' = x ∧
            pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map k) x' = y'
declarations.comment: the affine étale diagram covering the fibre — affine étale charts of the source and of the target with a morphism between them over f, through a point of the target chart over y and with the source chart covering the fibre — and nothing of the projectivity of the sections, which is the case of schemes, Tag 05KW

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_along_fibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVZ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `𝓕` be an `𝒪_X`-module and let `y` be a point of `|Y|`. Assume

1. `f` is of finite presentation (`hfp`, Stacks 03XP part (3));
2. `𝓕` is quasi-coherent and of finite presentation (`hqc`, `h𝓕fp`), chartwise: its restriction
   to every étale scheme chart of `X` is;
3. `𝓕` is flat over `Y` at every point of the fibre `F = f^{-1}({y})` (`hflat`), chartwise: on
   every commuting square of étale charts and at every point of the source chart lying over a
   point of `F`, the restriction of `𝓕` to the source chart is flat over the target chart there.

Then there are an étale chart `Z` of `X`, an étale chart `V` of `Y`, affine objects `X'`, `Y'`
of the site with étale morphisms `p : X' ⟶ Z` and `q : Y' ⟶ V`, a morphism `k : X' ⟶ Y'` and a
point `y'` of `|Y'|` such that the composites `X' → X` and `Y' → Y` are étale, the square
commutes over `f`, `y'` lies over `y`, the fibre `F` is contained in the image of `|X'| → |X|`,
and the sections `Γ(X', p^*(𝓕|_Z))` form a projective `Γ(Y', 𝒪_{Y'})`-module.

The conclusion is the conclusion of Tag 0CVZ, with no clause dropped, and nothing is granted as
a hypothesis: everything except the projectivity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_chart_square_along_fibre`, and the projectivity
is the case of schemes, Tag 05KW, read inside the site by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_hom_projective_sections_along_fibre`.

Quasi-coherence and the hypotheses (2) and (3) are stated chartwise here; compare
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOver`, the definition of Stacks 05VV. This is **not** the
source's reading of them, and it is not comparable to it: chartwise quasi-coherence and
chartwise finite presentation are weaker than the source's conditions on `X` itself, while the
chartwise flatness asked here is the every-chart-square form, which is strictly more than
Stacks 05VV asks at a point. The statement at the source's own three hypotheses, with no
chartwise condition on the module anywhere, is
`exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_along_fibre_of_isFlatOverAtPoint`, which is
proved from this one. See the module docstring for the three transfers between the readings.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_along_fibre
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝓕 : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) (y : points B S hS Y)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hqc : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, (restrictToChart B S hS hX 𝓕 U).IsQuasicoherent)
    (h𝓕fp : ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X, (restrictToChart B S hS hX 𝓕 U).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hflat : ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (g : (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V)
      (x' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U))),
      U.obj.hom ≫ f = yoneda.map g ≫ V.obj.hom →
      pointsMap B S hS X f (pointsMap B S hS _ U.obj.hom x') = y →
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt
        (LocallyRingedSpace.forgetToSheafedSpace.map
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map g).toLRSHom)
        (restrictToChart B S hS hX 𝓕 U) (pointsToScheme B S hS _ x')) :
    ∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y)
      (X' Y' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (p : X' ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X).obj U)
      (q : Y' ⟶ (SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y).obj V) (k : X' ⟶ Y')
      (y' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Y')),
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom) ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X') ∧
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y') ∧
      (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom) ≫ f = yoneda.map k ≫ yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom ∧
      pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map q ≫ V.obj.hom) y' = y ∧
      {x : points B S hS X | pointsMap B S hS X f x = y} ⊆
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS _ (yoneda.map p ≫ U.obj.hom)) ∧
      (let M := (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p)).obj
           (restrictToChart B S hS hX 𝓕 U)
       letI : Module Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y', ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤) :=
         Module.compHom Γ(M, ⊤) ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map k).appTop.hom
       Module.Projective Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y', ⊤) Γ(M, ⊤))
declarations.comment: the full conclusion — the affine étale diagram covering the fibre and the projectivity of the sections — with quasi-coherence and the tag's conditions (2) and (3) on the module in their étale-chartwise form, for a consumer holding chart data; the case of schemes, Tag 05KW, is discharged inside the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_along_fibre_of_isFlatOverAtPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CVZ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `𝓕` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `y` be a point of `|Y|` with fibre
`F = f^{-1}({y}) ⊆ |X|`. Assume

1. `f` is of finite presentation (`hfp`, Stacks 03XP part (3));
2. `𝓕` is of finite presentation (`h𝓕fp`), on the small étale site of `X`, which is the
   property Stacks 05VR item (l) names;
3. `𝓕` is flat over `Y` at every point of `F` (`hflat`), in the some-chart sense of
   Stacks 05VV, which is condition (1) of Stacks 05VU.

Then there are an étale chart `Z` of `X`, an étale chart `V` of `Y`, affine objects `X'`, `Y'`
of the site with étale morphisms `p : X' ⟶ Z` and `q : Y' ⟶ V`, a morphism `k : X' ⟶ Y'` and a
point `y'` of `|Y'|` such that the composites `X' → X` and `Y' → Y` are étale, the square
commutes over `f`, `y'` lies over `y`, the fibre `F` is contained in the image of `|X'| → |X|`,
and the sections `Γ(X', p^*(𝓕|_Z))` form a projective `Γ(Y', 𝒪_{Y'})`-module.

**Every hypothesis here is the source's own, and no chartwise condition on the module appears.**
This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_along_fibre`
with its three chartwise hypotheses on the module discharged: quasi-coherence on the small étale
site gives chartwise quasi-coherence by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_restrictToChart`, finite presentation on the small
étale site gives chartwise finite presentation by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinitePresentationOnCharts_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite`, and the
some-chart form of condition (3) gives the every-chart form by Stacks 05VU,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtOnChartDiagram_of_isFlatOverAtPoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_etale_charts_projective_sections_along_fibre_of_isFlatOverAtPoint
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
