declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModuleMapSituation.isoLocusRepresentation_of_isPureRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWD.**  In Situation 083F, assume (1) `f` is of finite presentation, (2) `ℱ` is of
finite presentation, flat over `B` and pure relative to `B`, and (3) `u` is surjective.  Then
`F_iso` is representable by a closed immersion `Z ⟶ B`: there is a closed subspace `Z` of `B`
such that a scheme `T` over `B` lies in `F_iso` — the base change `u_T` is an isomorphism —
exactly when its structure morphism factors through `Z`.  Moreover `Z ⟶ B` is of finite
presentation if `𝒢` is of finite presentation.

The source writes `Z ⟶ S` in the last sentence, which is false as written; its proof gives
`Z ⟶ B`, and that is what is stated.  See the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoLocusRepresentation_of_isPureRelative
    (D : ModuleMapSituation.{u, u} B S hS)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hFfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F)
    (hFflat : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOver B S hS D.X.2 D.f.hom D.F)
    (hpure : ∀ y : points B S hS D.Y.1, IsPureRelative (D.fpSourcePrePureSituation hf hFfp y))
    [Epi D.u] :
    D.IsoLocusRepresentation
declarations.comment: F_iso is represented by a closed subspace Z of the base, and Z → B is of finite presentation when 𝒢 is of finite presentation (the source's 'Z → S' is a misprint for Z → B, see the module notes)

declarations.name: Algebra.IsPushout.height_fiber_add_height_eq_and_add_trdeg_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWE.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a finite type `k`-algebra, let `K/k` be a
field extension and let `T = K ⊗_k S` be the base change, presented as a pushout square. Then for
every prime `q` of `S` and every prime `Q` of `T` lying over `q`, the dimension of the fibre ring
`(T ⊗_S κ(q))_Q` — the height of the image of `Q` in `T ⧸ q T` — added to `dim S_q` gives
`dim T_Q`, and added to `trdeg_K κ(Q)` gives `trdeg_k κ(q)`. Moreover, given `q` there is a prime
`Q` over `q` for which this dimension is zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem height_fiber_add_height_eq_and_add_trdeg_eq (k K S T : Type*) [Field k] [Field K]
    [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k S] [Algebra k T] [Algebra K T]
    [Algebra S T] [IsScalarTower k K T] [IsScalarTower k S T] [Algebra.IsPushout k K S T]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] :
    (∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (Q : Ideal T) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver q],
        (Q.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (q.map (algebraMap S T)))).height + q.height = Q.height ∧
        (Q.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (q.map (algebraMap S T)))).height
            + Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg K Q.ResidueField)
          = Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg k q.ResidueField)) ∧
      ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], ∃ (Q : Ideal T) (_ : Q.IsPrime) (_ : Q.LiesOver q),
        (Q.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (q.map (algebraMap S T)))).height = 0
declarations.comment:
The dimension of the fibre `(S_K ⊗_S κ(𝔮))_{𝔮_K}` is the height of the image of
`𝔮_K` in `S_K ⧸ 𝔮 S_K`, Mathlib's spelling in the going-down height formula (Lemma 00ON); the two
equalities are stated additively rather than with a truncated subtraction in `ℕ∞`; the base change
`K ⊗_k S` is an arbitrary pushout square of `k`-algebras, as in the siblings 00P3 and 00P4; and
transcendence degrees are compared through `Cardinal.toENat`, as in 00P1. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_not_isFlatOverAt_fiber_lt_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWF.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `n` be a natural number. The closed subset of
each fibre where `F` is not flat over `S` has dimension less than `n` if and only if
`trdeg_{κ(f x)} κ(x) < n` at every point `x` where `F` is not flat over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_not_isFlatOverAt_fiber_lt_iff {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (n : ℕ) :
    (∀ s : S, topologicalKrullDim
        ↥{y : f.fiber s | ¬ IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (f.fiberι s y)} <
          (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) ↔
      ∀ x : X, ¬ IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x →
        letI : Algebra (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) :=
          (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
        (Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) :
          WithBot ℕ∞) < (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: the dimension criterion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_not_isFlatOverAt_fiber_lt_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWF.** The dimension criterion is stable under base change: if the
non-flat locus has dimension less than `n` in every fibre of `f`, then the same holds for the
pullback of `F` along any base change of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_not_isFlatOverAt_fiber_lt_of_isPullback {X S S' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'} (hsq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ s : S, topologicalKrullDim
        ↥{y : f.fiber s | ¬ IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (f.fiberι s y)} <
          (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) (s' : S') :
    topologicalKrullDim
        ↥{y : f'.fiber s' | ¬ IsFlatOverAt f'.toLRSHom.toShHom
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F) (f'.fiberι s' y)} < (n : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: stability under base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverInDimensionsGE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWG.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type and let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type. Then `F` is *flat over `S` in dimensions `≥ n`* if
for every point `s` of `S` the closed subset of the fibre `X_s` of points at which `F` is not
flat over `S` has dimension less than `n`.

This is the first of the two equivalent conditions of Stacks 0CWF; the second one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverInDimensionsGE_iff_forall_toENat_trdeg_lt`.
declarations.statement:
def IsFlatOverInDimensionsGE {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (n : ℕ) : Prop

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isClosedSubspace_isProper_of_henselianPair
registrations.comment: the whole tag, on the theorem proved in ClopenLiftOverHenselianPair

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_completeDevissage_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWJ.** Let `X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S`, let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `y` be a point of `Y`. There
are an étale morphism `q : (Y', y') ⟶ (Y, y)` with `Y'` an affine scheme, and étale morphisms
`hᵢ : Wᵢ ⟶ X_{Y'} = Y' ×_Y X`, `i = 1, …, n`, from schemes `Wᵢ`, such that for each `i` the
pullback `Fᵢ` of `F` to `Wᵢ` (its restriction to the étale chart `Wᵢ ⟶ X_{Y'} ⟶ X`) has a
complete dévissage `Fᵢ/Wᵢ/Y'` over `y'`, the morphism `Wᵢ ⟶ Y'` being the `aᵢ` with
`hᵢ ≫ pr₁ = aᵢ`, and such that every point of `X_{Y'}` lying over `y'` is in the image of some
`hᵢ`, that is, `|(X_{Y'})_{y'}| ⊆ ⋃ hᵢ(Wᵢ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_etale_completeDevissage_cover (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hFq : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hFt : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (y : points B S hS Y) :
    ∃ (Y' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj Y' ⟶ Y) (y' : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Y')),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y') ∧ IsEtale B S hS q ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj Y') q y' = y ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (W : Fin n → BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (h : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (W i) ⟶ pullback q f) (_ : ∀ i, IsEtale B S hS (h i))
        (hW : ∀ i, IsEtaleChart B S hS X (CostructuredArrow.mk (h i ≫ pullback.snd q f)))
        (a : ∀ i, W i ⟶ Y') (_ : ∀ i, h i ≫ pullback.fst q f = yoneda.map (a i))
        (hl : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (a i)))
        (hq : ∀ i, (restrictToChart B S hS hX F ⟨_, hW i⟩).IsQuasicoherent)
        (ht : ∀ i, (restrictToChart B S hS hX F ⟨_, hW i⟩).IsFiniteType),
        (∀ i, Nonempty (@CompleteDevissage _ _ ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (a i))
          (restrictToChart B S hS hX F ⟨_, hW i⟩) (pointsToScheme B S hS Y' y')
          (hl i) (hq i) (ht i))) ∧
        ∀ x : points B S hS (pullback q f),
          pointsMap B S hS _ (pullback.fst q f) x = y' →
            ∃ (i : Fin n) (z : points B S hS (yoneda.obj (W i))),
              pointsMap B S hS _ (h i) z = x
declarations.comment: the full statement, proved from the source's hypotheses; nothing is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affineChart_hasCompleteDevissageCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWJ**, delivered at an affine étale chart of the base change.

Let `X ⟶ Y` be a finite type morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a finite type
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, and let `y` be a point of `Y`. Then there are

* an object `Y₁` of the site whose scheme is affine, an étale morphism `q : Y₁ ⟶ Y`, and a
  point `w` of `Y₁` above `y` — the source's `(Y', y') ⟶ (Y, y)` before the passage to an
  elementary étale neighbourhood;
* an étale chart `U` of `X` whose scheme is affine, and a morphism `ĝ : U ⟶ Y₁` of the site
  making the square over `q` commute, such that the induced morphism from `U` to the base
  change `X ×_Y Y₁` is surjective on points — the source's affine surjective étale cover `X'`
  of `X`, after the reduction to an affine base;
* the morphism of schemes underlying `ĝ` is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, and the
  conclusion of Stacks 05HU holds for it, for the restriction of `F` to `U`, and for the
  point of the scheme of `Y₁` determined by `w`.

The finitely many étale morphisms `hᵢ : Wᵢ ⟶ X_{Y'}` of the source's conclusion, their
complete dévissages and the inclusion of the fibre in the union of their images are bound
inside `AlgebraicGeometry.HasCompleteDevissageCover`. See the implementation notes of this
file for why they are delivered at the chart `U` rather than at `X_{Y'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineChart_hasCompleteDevissageCover (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)
    (hFq : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hFt : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (y : points B S hS Y) :
    ∃ (Y₁ : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : yoneda.obj Y₁ ⟶ Y) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X)
      (ĝ : U.obj.left ⟶ Y₁) (hsq : yoneda.map ĝ ≫ q = U.obj.hom ≫ f)
      (w : points B S hS (yoneda.obj Y₁)),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y₁) ∧
      IsAffine (etaleChartScheme B S hS U) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf q ∧
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj Y₁) q w = y ∧
      IsSurjective B S hS (Limits.pullback.lift (yoneda.map ĝ) U.obj.hom hsq) ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ĝ) ∧
      QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ĝ) ∧
      HasCompleteDevissageCover ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ĝ)
        (restrictToChart B S hS hX F U) (pointsToScheme B S hS Y₁ w)
declarations.comment: the elementary étale neighbourhood of the point, the covering family and its dévissages are delivered for the affine étale chart of the base change rather than for the base change as an algebraic space: the sources of the covering étale morphisms carry no size bound, so they are not objects of the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_setFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWK.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite type, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `y` be
a point of `|Y|` with a quasi-compact field-valued representative. In the set-theoretic fibre
`f^{-1}({y}) ⊆ |X|`, with its subspace topology, the points at which `F` is flat over `Y` form
an open subset.

The hypothesis on `y` is condition (5) of Stacks 03JV; by Stacks 0AC8 it provides an étale
scheme chart of `Y` with exactly one point above `y`, which is what makes the fibre of a chart
of `X` map openly onto the set-theoretic fibre. It holds at every point of a decent algebraic
space, which is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_flatLocus_setFibre_of_isDecentSpace`.

The hypothesis on `y` corrects Stacks 0CWK, which as published asks nothing of `y`; the corrected
statement adds condition (5) of Stacks 03JV at `y`. The published form is false:
`Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusSpace.not_isOpen_flatLocus_setFibre_of_free_shift` takes no
hypotheses and produces a big fppf site, an algebraic space `Y = Spec A/ℤ` for
`A = ℚ[t, u_i]/((t - i)u_i)`, the étale quotient morphism `f : Spec A ⟶ Y`, the cyclic module
`A ⧸ (u_i : i ≥ 1)` on its source and a point `y` of `|Y|`, satisfying every hypothesis of this
theorem except the one on `y`, and for which the conclusion below is false. Its companion
`Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusSpace.not_hasQuasiCompactFieldRepresentative_ybase` deduces from
that failure that the point it produces has no quasi-compact field-valued representative, so the
hypothesis on `y` is exactly what the source is missing.

Flatness at a point is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocus`, the some-chart form of Stacks 05VV
part (1), which Stacks 05VU shows is independent of the chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_flatLocus_setFibre (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (Fm : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [Fm.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (hft : IsFiniteTypeOnCharts B S hS X.2 Fm)
    (y : points B S hS Y.1) (hy : HasQuasiCompactFieldRepresentative B S hS Y.1 y) :
    IsOpen {x : (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom ⁻¹' {y} : Set (points B S hS X.1)) |
      (x : points B S hS X.1) ∈ flatLocus B S hS X.2 f.hom Fm}
declarations.comment: the statement in full, at the Stacks erratum: the point y of the target has a quasi-compact field-valued representative, condition (5) of Stacks 03JV, which holds at every point of a decent algebraic space. The tag as published asks nothing of y and is false that way, refuted by the theorem Stacks.Examples.NonOpenFlatLocusSpace.not_isOpen_flatLocus_setFibre_of_free_shift of StacksFrontier/Examples/Flatness/NonOpenFlatLocusSpace.lean

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_of_forall_isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWL, the implication (2) ⟹ (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type, let `𝓕` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of
finite type and let `x` be a point of `|X|` with image `y` under `|f|`. If `𝓕` is flat over `Y`
at every point `x'` of `|X|` which lies over `y`, lies in the relative weak assassin
`WeakAss_{X/Y}(𝓕)` of Stacks 0CV0 — which is `Ass_{X/Y}(𝓕)` here, the fibres of `f` being
locally Noetherian — and specializes to `x`, then `𝓕` is flat over `Y` at `x`.

No decency is required, as the source records. Nothing is carried: the case of schemes is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_of_forall_mem_relativeAssassin_specializes`, More on Flatness
Theorem 05UA (2) ⟹ (1) in relative-assassin form, and the reduction to a commuting square of
étale scheme charts of `f` is what is proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtPoint_of_forall_isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (x : points B S hS X.1)
    (h2 : ∀ x' : points B S hS X.1,
      pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x' = pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x →
      IsRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint B S hS f F x' → x' ⤳ x →
        IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F x') :
    IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F x
declarations.comment: the implication (2) => (1), which the tag asserts holds with no decency hypothesis: for f locally of finite type and F a finite type quasi-coherent module, flatness of F over Y at every point of the fibre over y which lies in Ass_{X/Y}(F) and specializes to x gives flatness of F over Y at x. UNCONDITIONAL -- nothing is carried: the case of schemes is More on Flatness Theorem 05UA (2) => (1), proved in this library as AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_of_forall_mem_relativeAssassin_specializes, and the reduction to a commuting square of etale scheme charts is proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_of_specializes_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWL, the implication (1) ⟹ (2), for decent `X`.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` decent and let `𝓕` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module which
is flat over `Y` at a point `x` of `|X|`. Then `𝓕` is flat over `Y` at every point `x'` of `|X|`
which specializes to `x`.

This is clause (2) of the tag and more, in four ways: the relative-assassin condition on `x'` is
not needed; `x'` is not required to lie in the set-theoretic fibre of `f` through `x`; decency
of `Y` is not needed; and neither local finiteness of the type of `f` nor finiteness of the type
of `𝓕` is a hypothesis. Decency of `X` lifts the specialization to an étale scheme chart
(Stacks 03IL), and the case of schemes is then
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFlatOverAt_of_specializes_acrossFibres`, which propagates relative flatness
to an arbitrary generalization and so asks nothing about the images of the two lifted points in the
target chart scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtPoint_of_specializes_of_isDecentSpace (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X.1)
    {x x' : points B S hS X.1} (hflat : IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F x)
    (hspec : x' ⤳ x) :
    IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F x'
declarations.comment: the implication (1) => (2) for decent X, UNCONDITIONALLY -- nothing is carried: flatness of F over Y at x gives flatness of F over Y at every point of |X| which specializes to x. This is stronger than the tag's clause (2) in four ways: the point is not required to lie in Ass_{X/Y}(F), it is not required to lie in the set-theoretic fibre through x, decency of Y is not needed, and f locally of finite type and F of finite type are not needed and are not hypotheses; quasi-coherence of F and decency of X are

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_of_forall_specializes_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWM.** Let `S` be a local scheme with closed point `s`, read as the
target `Y` of a morphism of algebraic spaces: the target is represented by a scheme of the site
isomorphic to the spectrum of a local ring, and `s` is a closed point of `|Y|`. Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite type and let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module. Assume

1. every point of `Ass_{X/S}(F)` specializes to a point of the closed fibre `X_s` (`hass`),
   and
2. `F` is flat over `S` at every point of `X_s` (`hflat`).

Then `F` is flat over `S`.

The conclusion is the tag's, with no clause dropped and nothing carried. The representability
of the target in `hlocal` is consumed: a representable algebraic space is decent, which is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOver_of_forall_specializes_fibre` asks of the target. The
closedness of `s` is a hypothesis of the tag that the implication does not use.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOver_of_forall_specializes_closedFibre {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (s : points B S hS Y.1)
    (hlocal : ∃ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (A : CommRingCat.{u}), IsLocalRing A ∧
      Nonempty (Spec A ≅ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) ∧ Nonempty (yoneda.obj T ≅ Y.1))
    (_hs : IsClosed ({s} : Set (points B S hS Y.1)))
    (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom) (hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (hass : ∀ x' ∈ relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS f F,
      ∃ θ : points B S hS X.1, x' ⤳ θ ∧ pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom θ = s)
    (hflat : ∀ θ : points B S hS X.1, pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom θ = s →
      IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F θ) :
    IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F
declarations.comment: the lemma's implication: from its hypotheses (1) and (2) to flatness of ℱ over the local base. UNCONDITIONAL -- nothing is carried and no decency of X is assumed: the step the source's proof invokes, the implication (2) => (1) of Stacks 0CWL, is proved here for arbitrary X and Y as isFlatOverAtPoint_of_forall_isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint, and the passage of flatness from a point of the closed fibre to a point of Ass_{X/S}(F) specializing to it is proved here as isFlatOverAtPoint_of_specializes_of_isRelativeWeaklyAssociatedPoint, using only that the local base is a decent space. The closedness of s is a hypothesis of the statement that the implication does not use

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_idealSheafData_isFlatOverAtPoint_iff_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWP.** Let `S = Spec A` be the spectrum of a henselian local ring with
closed point `s`, let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite
type, let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type and let `E ⊆ |X_s|` be a subset.
There is a closed subscheme `Z ⊆ S` such that for every morphism of pointed schemes
`(T, t) ⟶ (S, s)` the following are equivalent:

1. `F_T` is flat over `T` at all points of `|X_t|` which map to a point of `E ⊆ |X_s|`;
2. `Spec 𝒪_{T,t} ⟶ S` factors through `Z`.

Here `X` is an algebraic space over `S`, `f` its structure morphism to the terminal algebraic
space `S`, and `X_T = X ×_S T` the fibre product of algebraic spaces; the points of `|X_t|` are
the points of `|X_T|` over `t ∈ |T|`, and the closed fibre `|X_s|` is the set of points of `|X|`
over `s`, through which a point of `|X_t|` maps to `|X_s|` by its image in `|X|`. Flatness of
`F_T` over `T` at a point is Stacks 05VV at a point, and `Z` is given by its ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_idealSheafData_isFlatOverAtPoint_iff_factors [HenselianLocalRing A]
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA))))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2) (hFq : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFt : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (E : Set {x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 //
      pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 f.hom x = closedBasePoint A B hA}) :
    ∃ Z : (Spec (.of A)).IdealSheafData,
      ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA) (g : T ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA)))
        (t : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).obj T),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).map g t = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A →
        ((∀ x' : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA (pullback f (schemeSpaceMap g)).1,
            pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA _ (pullback.snd f (schemeSpaceMap g)).hom x' =
              (pointsEquivScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA T).symm t →
            ∀ hx : pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 f.hom
                (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA _ (pullback.fst f (schemeSpaceMap g)).hom x') =
                closedBasePoint A B hA,
              (⟨_, hx⟩ : {x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 //
                pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 f.hom x = closedBasePoint A B hA}) ∈ E →
              IsFlatOverAtPoint B (Spec (.of A)) hA (pullback f (schemeSpaceMap g)).2
                (pullback.snd f (schemeSpaceMap g)).hom
                ((modulePullback B (Spec (.of A)) hA (pullback.fst f (schemeSpaceMap g))).obj F)
                x') ↔
          ∃ h : Spec (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).obj T).presheaf.stalk t) ⟶
              Z.subscheme,
            h ≫ Z.subschemeι = ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).obj T).fromSpecStalk t ≫
              (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).map g)
declarations.comment: the closed flattening subscheme, for an arbitrary subset E of the closed fibre: nothing is assumed beyond the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finitePresentation_idealSheafData_isFlatOverAtPoint_iff_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CWP, the final assertion.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_idealSheafData_isFlatOverAtPoint_iff_factors`, if moreover
`X ⟶ S` is locally of finite presentation, `F` is of finite presentation and `E ⊆ |X_s|` is
closed and quasi-compact, then the closed subscheme `Z` may be chosen with `Z ⟶ S` of finite
presentation. The topology on `|X_s|` is the subspace topology of the closed fibre in `|X|`
(Stacks 03BY).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_idealSheafData_isFlatOverAtPoint_iff_factors
    [HenselianLocalRing A]
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA))))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom)
    (hfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B (Spec (.of A)) hA f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 X.2) (hFq : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFt : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) (hFp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F)
    (E : Set {x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 //
      pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 f.hom x = closedBasePoint A B hA})
    (hEc : IsClosed E) (hEk : IsCompact E) :
    ∃ Z : (Spec (.of A)).IdealSheafData,
      AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation Z.subschemeι ∧
      ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA) (g : T ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hA)))
        (t : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).obj T),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).map g t = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A →
        ((∀ x' : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA (pullback f (schemeSpaceMap g)).1,
            pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA _ (pullback.snd f (schemeSpaceMap g)).hom x' =
              (pointsEquivScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA T).symm t →
            ∀ hx : pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 f.hom
                (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA _ (pullback.fst f (schemeSpaceMap g)).hom x') =
                closedBasePoint A B hA,
              (⟨_, hx⟩ : {x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 //
                pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X.1 f.hom x = closedBasePoint A B hA}) ∈ E →
              IsFlatOverAtPoint B (Spec (.of A)) hA (pullback f (schemeSpaceMap g)).2
                (pullback.snd f (schemeSpaceMap g)).hom
                ((modulePullback B (Spec (.of A)) hA (pullback.fst f (schemeSpaceMap g))).obj F)
                x') ↔
          ∃ h : Spec (((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).obj T).presheaf.stalk t) ⟶
              Z.subscheme,
            h ≫ Z.subschemeι = ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).obj T).fromSpecStalk t ≫
              (BigFppfOver.toScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA).map g)
declarations.comment: the finite-presentation assertion, for E closed and quasi-compact in |X_s|: nothing is assumed beyond the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.HasUniversalFlattening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWR.** The universal flattening of `F` exists when the flatness condition of
Stacks 0CWX is stable under base change and the functor `F_flat` it cuts out of `Y` is an
algebraic space.
declarations.statement: def HasUniversalFlattening (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: the universal flattening of a module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasUniversalFlattening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWR.** The universal flattening of an algebraic space `X` over `Y` exists when the
universal flattening of its structure sheaf `𝒪_X` does.
declarations.statement: def HasUniversalFlattening {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: the universal flattening of the space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnSomeChartDiagram_iff_hasTrdegLt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWS, conditions (1) and (3).** Flatness in dimensions `≥ n` on some commuting
square of surjective étale scheme charts is the bound `trdeg < n` at every point at which `F`
is not flat over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnSomeChartDiagram_iff_hasTrdegLt (n : ℕ) :
    IsFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnSomeChartDiagram B S hS Xs.2 f.hom F n ↔
      HasTrdegLtAtNonflatPoints B S hS Xs.2 f.hom F n
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnEveryChartDiagram_iff_hasTrdegLt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWS, conditions (2) and (3).** Flatness in dimensions `≥ n` on every commuting
square of étale scheme charts is the bound `trdeg < n` at every point at which `F` is not flat
over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnEveryChartDiagram_iff_hasTrdegLt (n : ℕ) :
    IsFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnEveryChartDiagram B S hS Xs.2 f.hom F n ↔
      HasTrdegLtAtNonflatPoints B S hS Xs.2 f.hom F n
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnSomeChartDiagram_iff_onEveryChartDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWS, conditions (1) and (2).** Flatness in dimensions `≥ n` can be tested on one
commuting square of surjective étale scheme charts, and then holds on every commuting square of
étale scheme charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnSomeChartDiagram_iff_onEveryChartDiagram (n : ℕ) :
    IsFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnSomeChartDiagram B S hS Xs.2 f.hom F n ↔
      IsFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnEveryChartDiagram B S hS Xs.2 f.hom F n
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverInDimensionsGE_modulePullback_of_hasTrdegLt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWS, the base-change clause.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite type, let `F`
be quasi-coherent of finite type, and let the square be cartesian over a morphism `Y' ⟶ Y`.
If the transcendence degree over its image of every point of `|X|` at which `F` is not flat
over `Y` is less than `n`, then the inverse image `(g')^*F` of `F` on `X' = X ×_Y Y'` is flat
over `Y'` in dimensions `≥ n`.

The hypothesis is condition (3) of Stacks 0CWS written out: the flat locus is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flatLocus` of Stacks 0DLR and the transcendence degree is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasTranscendenceDegreeAt` of Stacks 04NM, and by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverInDimensionsGE_iff_hasTrdegLt` it is exactly flatness over
`Y` in dimensions `≥ n` in the sense of Stacks 0CWT, which is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverInDimensionsGE_modulePullback_of_isPullback` below states it
as.  Writing it out is what keeps the registered form of the clause free of the abbreviations
introduced in this file, so that no hypothesis of it is read as standing in for an input.

The clause is that condition on the two sides together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTrdegLtAtNonflatPoints_modulePullback_of_isPullback`, which is where
Stacks 05VW at a point enters.

The hypotheses on `F` are the source's, read on the small étale site: quasi-coherence and finite
type there, which the inverse image inherits by Stacks 03GA and by Stacks 03DO for the clause
03DL (5), `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_modulePullback`.  The chartwise forms of
the two, which the equivalence of Stacks 0CWS consumes, follow for both modules by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnCharts_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnCharts_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite`, so neither is assumed of
the inverse image.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverInDimensionsGE_modulePullback_of_hasTrdegLt
    (hftS : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) {g' : X' ⟶ Xs} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {g : Y' ⟶ Ys} (sq : IsPullback g'.hom f'.hom f.hom g.hom) (n : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ x : points B S hS Xs.1, x ∉ flatLocus B S hS Xs.2 f.hom F →
      ∃ r : ℕ∞, HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f.hom x r ∧ r < (n : ℕ∞)) :
    IsFlatOverInDimensionsGE B S hS f' ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) n
declarations.comment: the base-change clause: if the transcendence degree over its image of every point at which the module is not flat over the target is < n -- condition (3) of the tag, written out -- then the inverse image of the module is flat over the new target in dimensions >= n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatOverInDimensionsGE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWT.** `F` is *flat over `Y` in dimensions `≥ n`*. The source defines this by the
equivalent conditions of Stacks 0CWS; condition (2) is taken as the definition, and the three
conditions are interchangeable by the theorems above.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFlatOverInDimensionsGE (n : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition, taken in the form of condition (2) of Stacks 0CWS; conditions (1) and (3) are interchangeable with it by `isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnSomeChartDiagram_iff_onEveryChartDiagram` and `isFlatOverInDimensionsGEOnEveryChartDiagram_iff_hasTrdegLt`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation
declarations.doc:
**Situation 0CWU.** The standing data of Situation 0CWU: the flatness situation of
Stacks 0CWX — a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` and a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F` — in which moreover `f` is locally of finite type and `F` is of finite type.
declarations.statement: structure FlatDimensionSituation extends FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS
declarations.comment: standing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.isLocallyOfFiniteType_baseChangeInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Situation 0CWU, the first observation.** The base change `f_T : X_T ⟶ T` of a locally
finite type morphism to a test scheme is again locally of finite type. This is **Stacks 03XH**,
stability of the property under base change, at the fibre product square defining `X_T`.

The source says `f_T` is *of* finite type, which does not follow from its own hypotheses: `f` is
assumed only locally of finite type, and base change preserves exactly that. The half of
Stacks 03XH the source cites is the locally-of-finite-type one, and it is also what
Definition 0CWT consumes, so the corrected statement is the one that is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_baseChangeInclusion (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u} B S hS)
    (T : SchemesOver D.Y) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (baseChangeInclusion D.f T).hom
declarations.comment: the base-changed morphism is locally of finite type; corrected from the source's "of finite type", which does not follow from its hypothesis that f is only locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.isFiniteTypeOnSite_baseChangeModule
declarations.doc:
**Situation 0CWU, the second observation.** The base change `F_T` of a finite type module to
a test scheme is again of finite type. This is **Stacks 03DO** for the inverse image of
Stacks 03LU along the projection `X_T ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeOnSite_baseChangeModule (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u} B S hS)
    (T : SchemesOver D.Y) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite (D.toFlatnessSituation.baseChangeModule T)
declarations.comment: the base-changed module is of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.flatDimensionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Equation 0CWV, the functor `F_n` of Situation 0CWU**: the functor on the test schemes
over `Y` whose value at `T` is a one-point set when `F_T` is flat over `T` in dimensions `≥ n`,
and is empty otherwise.

That the condition is inherited along a morphism of test schemes, which is what makes the
assignment a functor, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.isFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange_of_hom`.
declarations.statement:
def flatDimensionFunctor (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u} B S hS) (n : ℕ) :
    (SchemesOver D.Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the functor F_n of equation 0CWV

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.flatDimensionFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWW, clause (1).** In Situation 0CWU the functor `F_n` of equation 0CWV satisfies
the sheaf property for the fpqc topology on the test schemes over `Y`.

`F_n` is subterminal, so its sheaf property is exactly fpqc locality of the condition of
Stacks 0CWT on the base change, which is
`isFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange_of_mem_fpqcTopology` of this namespace.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatDimensionFunctor_isSheaf_fpqc (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{u} B S hS) (n : ℕ) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology D.Y) (D.flatDimensionFunctor n)
declarations.comment: clause (1): in Situation 0CWU the functor F_n of equation 0CWV is a sheaf for the fpqc topology on the test schemes over Y. Proved for every situation of the tag, from nothing but the data of Situation 0CWU: the functor is subterminal, so its sheaf property is fpqc locality of the condition of Stacks 0CWT on the base change, and that locality is the pointwise descent of condition (3) of Stacks 0CWS along the jointly surjective flat family a covering sieve contains

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.flatDimensionFunctor_limitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWW, clause (2).** In Situation 0CWU, if `f` is quasi-compact and locally of
finite presentation and `ℱ` is of finite presentation, then the functor `F_n` of equation 0CWV
is limit preserving.

The proof is the source's, with the chart presentation constructed rather than assumed.  Since
`F_n` is subterminal, limit preservation is descent of the condition of Stacks 0CWT along a
cofiltered inverse system of affine test schemes with affine limit
(`limitPreserving_flatDimensionFunctor_iff`), so a system `T = lim T_i` of affine test schemes
may be fixed first.  The presentation is then taken at one of its stages: for an index `i₀`, the
base change `X_{T_{i₀}}` is quasi-compact over the affine scheme underlying `T_{i₀}`, hence has
a surjective étale scheme chart `U` with affine scheme
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_isSurjective_chart_baseChangeSpace`, Stacks 03H6), and
`U ⟶ T_{i₀}` together with the restriction of `F_{T_{i₀}}` to `U` is a scheme-level situation
`E` of Stacks 05MT (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.stageSituation`).  That is
the chart presentation of the source read over a stage instead of over `Y`: because `T_{i₀}` is
represented, the target chart of the presenting square is the identity chart, so no base change
of a chart of `Y` and no affine open of one is needed, and the value of the presentation at a
test scheme `T'` over `T_{i₀}` is `T'` itself.

The identification of the two conditions at every test scheme over `T_{i₀}` is the theorem
`isFlatInDimensionsGEAfterBaseChange_iff_stageSituation` of that same namespace,
the chart clause of Stacks 0CWS at the square whose source chart is the base change of `U` and
whose target chart is the identity chart.  The system `K` of affine schemes over the scheme
underlying `T_{i₀}` is the given system restricted to the indices over `i₀`,
`CategoryTheory.Over.post` of `T ↦ T` on `CategoryTheory.Over i₀`; its limit is the given one
because `CategoryTheory.Over.forget i₀` is initial for a cofiltered index category.  Limit
preservation of the scheme-level `F'_n` is part (2) of **Stacks 05MV**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FlatDimensionSituation.flatDimensionFunctor_limitPreserving`, applied to `E`
and to `K`; the three hypotheses it asks of `E` are the hypotheses on `f` and `ℱ` read on the
presentation, and are where they enter.

The schemes live in the maximum of the two index universes of the tested inverse system and a
third parameter.  That is the universe signature every limit-preservation statement in this
library carries: Stacks 05MY and part (2) of Stacks 05MV both have it, and it is the signature
at which the limit of a cofiltered system of affine schemes indexed by a category of those
universes exists in the first place.  It is also the signature of the statement of
Stacks 0CWW (limit preserving).
declarations.statement:
theorem flatDimensionFunctor_limitPreserving
    (D : FlatDimensionSituation.{max u w w'} B₁ S₁ hS₁) (n : ℕ)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B₁ S₁ hS₁ D.f.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B₁ S₁ hS₁ D.f.hom)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F) :
    LimitPreserving.{max u w w', max u w w', w, w'}
      (testSchemeFunctor D.Y) (D.flatDimensionFunctor n)
declarations.comment: clause (2), limit preservation of F_n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWX.** The standing data of Stacks 0CWX: a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces over `S` and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`, whose base changes to the schemes over
`Y` are tested for flatness.
declarations.statement: structure FlatnessSituation
declarations.comment: standing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.baseChangeModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWX.** The base change `F_T` of the module to a test scheme `T` over `Y`: the
pullback of `F` along the projection `X_T = X ×_Y T ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
def baseChangeModule (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS) (T : SchemesOver D.Y) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS (baseChangeSpace D.f T).1 (baseChangeSpace D.f T).2
declarations.comment: the base change F_T of the module to a test scheme over the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWX.**  The flattening functor

`F_flat : (Sch/Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets`, `T ↦ {*}` if `F_T` is flat over `T` and `∅` otherwise.

Its value at a test scheme is a subtype of a one-element type, cut out by flatness of the base
change there; that this is stable under a morphism of test schemes, which is what makes the
assignment a functor, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.isFlatAfterBaseChange_of_hom`.
declarations.statement: def flatFunctor (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS) : (SchemesOver D.Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u
declarations.comment: the functor F_flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_limitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWZ, part (2).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is locally of finite presentation and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of
finite presentation.  Then the functor `F_flat` of equation 0CWY is limit preserving in the sense
of Stacks 049J: it carries a cofiltered inverse limit of affine test schemes over `Y` to a
filtered colimit of sets.

`F_flat` is subterminal, so limit preservation is, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_limitPreserving_iff`, the assertion that
flatness of `F_T` over a cofiltered limit `T` of affine test schemes already holds over one of
the stages.  Pick a stage, read the condition over it on an affine surjective étale scheme chart
of `X_{T_i}` of finite presentation over `T_i`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.exists_affine_testChart`), and the condition at every
test scheme over that stage becomes flatness of the Zariski inverse image of the chart
restriction over the base-changed chart scheme
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.TestChart.isFlatAfterBaseChange_baseChange_iff`).
That is the statement the scheme-level descent theorem Stacks 05LY,
`AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isFlatOver_modulePullback`, descends to a stage; its hypotheses on
the chart are finite presentation of its structure morphism and finite presentation of the
restricted module, which are the two preceding results.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatFunctor_limitPreserving (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hFfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u} D.testScheme D.flatFunctor
declarations.comment: part (2), at the tag's own hypotheses; the index universe of the cofiltered system is the universe of the schemes, which is the largest Stacks 05LY admits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_isSeparatedFor_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWZ, part (1), the separatedness half of the fpqc sheaf property.** Two sections
of `F_flat` over a test scheme which agree on the members of an fpqc covering presieve of that
test scheme are equal.

Every value of `F_flat` has at most one element, so this holds for an arbitrary presieve; the
fpqc hypothesis is carried only so that the statement is the one the source makes.  The
existence half of the sheaf condition is fpqc descent of flatness of the base-changed module; it
is proved separately, so that part (1) holds in full, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_isSheafFor_fpqc` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_isSheaf_fpqcTopology`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatFunctor_isSeparatedFor_fpqc (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS)
    {T : SchemesOver D.Y} (R : Presieve T)
    (_hR : R ∈ D.testFpqcPrecoverage T) :
    Presieve.IsSeparatedFor D.flatFunctor R
declarations.comment: part (1), separatedness half only; gluing half not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_isSheaf_fpqcTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWZ, part (1).**  The functor `F_flat` satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc
topology on the test schemes over `Y`.

`F_flat` is subterminal, so the sheaf condition for a covering sieve is the implication from
flatness of the base-changed module at every member of the sieve to flatness at its target.  A
covering sieve of the fpqc topology contains a flat family which is jointly surjective on points
— `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFpqcCovering_jointlySurjective_family_of_mem_fpqcTopology` —
and flatness of the base-changed module descends along such a family by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.isFlatAfterBaseChange_of_jointlySurjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatFunctor_isSheaf_fpqcTopology (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (fpqcTopology D.Y) D.flatFunctor
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_isSheafFor_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWZ, part (1)**, in the presieve form: `F_flat` satisfies the sheaf condition for
every fpqc covering presieve of a test scheme over `Y`.

The sieve a covering presieve generates is a covering sieve of the fpqc topology, and every
member of that sieve factors through a member of the presieve, along which flatness of the
base-changed module is inherited by the final assertion of Stacks 05VW.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatFunctor_isSheafFor_fpqc (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS)
    {T : SchemesOver D.Y} (R : Presieve T) (hR : R ∈ D.testFpqcPrecoverage T) :
    Presieve.IsSheafFor D.flatFunctor R
declarations.comment: part (1), the sheaf condition for a covering presieve

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.subsingleton_colimitType_flatFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CWZ, part (2), the uniqueness half of limit preservation.** Along a cofiltered
system of test schemes over `Y`, the filtered colimit of the values of `F_flat` has at most one
element.

Limit preservation asserts that the canonical map from that colimit to the value of `F_flat` at
the limit test scheme is a bijection.  This is its injectivity half: the target also has at most
one element (`flatFunctor_obj_subsingleton`), so no two classes in the colimit can be separated.
It needs none of the hypotheses of part (2) — not quasi-compactness or local finite presentation
of `f`, not finite presentation of `F` — and no restriction on the index universes.  The
surjectivity half does need them and is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.flatFunctor_limitPreserving` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/FlatteningFunctorLimitPreserving.lean`, which is part (2)
in full.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_colimitType_flatFunctor (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS)
    {I : Type w} [Category.{w'} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (E : I ⥤ SchemesOver D.Y) :
    Subsingleton ((E.op ⋙ D.flatFunctor).ColimitType)
declarations.comment: part (2), injectivity half only; surjectivity not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.mono_etalePullbackComparison_and_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CX0.** In Situation 0CWU, let `h : X' ⟶ X` be an étale morphism, set `F' = h^* F`
and `f' = f ∘ h`, and let `F'_n` be the functor of equation 0CWV for `(f' : X' ⟶ Y, F')`. Then
`F_n` is a subfunctor of `F'_n` — the canonical natural transformation `F_n ⟶ F'_n` is a
monomorphism — and if `h(|X'|) ⊇ Ass_{X/Y}(F)` then `F_n = F'_n` — that monomorphism is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_etalePullbackComparison_and_isIso (n : ℕ) :
    Mono (D.etalePullbackComparison h hh n) ∧
      (relativeWeaklyAssociatedPoints B S hS D.f D.F ⊆
          Set.range (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 h.hom) →
        IsIso (D.etalePullbackComparison h hh n))
declarations.comment: the full statement at the source's hypotheses, nothing granted or assumed: Situation 0CWU (f locally of finite type, F quasi-coherent of finite type) and h etale only. 'F_n is a subfunctor of F'_n' is that the canonical natural transformation F_n -> F'_n between these subterminal functors is a monomorphism, and 'F_n = F'_n' is that it is an isomorphism. Ass_{X/Y}(F) is the relative weak assassin of Stacks 0CV0, which the source writes Ass_{X/Y}(F) as the fibres of f are locally Noetherian, and h(X') is the image of |X'| -> |X|

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.isAlgebraicSpace_flatDimensionSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CX1.** In Situation 0CWU, assume moreover that `f` is of finite
presentation, that `F` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, and that `F` is pure relative
to `Y`. Then `F_n` is an algebraic space and `F_n ⟶ Y` is a monomorphism of finite presentation.

`F_n` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatDimensionSituation.flatDimensionSubfunctor`, the functor of
equation 0CWV read on the big fppf site of `S` as a subfunctor of `Y`. Purity of `F` relative to
`Y` is purity above every point of `Y`, Stacks 0CVD part (5), for the situation of Stacks 0CV6
which `f` and `F` determine; that situation is formed from the hypotheses of the theorem, since a
morphism of finite presentation is of finite type and decent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_flatDimensionSubfunctor (n : ℕ)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F)
    (hpure : ∀ y, IsPureAbove (D.fpPrePureSituation hf y)) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.flatDimensionSubfunctor n).toFunctor ∧
      Mono (D.flatDimensionSubfunctor n).ι ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS (D.flatDimensionSubfunctor n).ι
declarations.comment: the full statement under exactly the source's hypotheses, nothing granted or assumed: F_n is the subfunctor of Y of the maps T ⟶ Y along which F_T is flat in dimensions ≥ n (equation 0CWV); purity relative to Y is purity above every point of Y (Stacks 0CVD (5)); finite presentation of f is local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness (Stacks 03XP (3))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.hasUniversalFlattening_of_isPureAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CX2, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces of finite
presentation and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation which is pure
relative to `Y`, that is, pure above every point `y ∈ |Y|`. Then the universal flattening
`Y' ⟶ Y` of `F` exists, and `Y' ⟶ Y` is a monomorphism of finite presentation.

Here `Y'` is the subfunctor `F_flat` of `Y` and `Y' ⟶ Y` is its inclusion. This is Theorem 0CX1
at `n = 0`, where `F_0 = F_flat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasUniversalFlattening_of_isPureAbove (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS)
    (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F)
    (hpure : ∀ y : points B S hS D.Y.1,
      IsPureAbove ((D.toFlatDimensionSituation hf hF).fpPrePureSituation hf y)) :
    D.HasUniversalFlattening ∧ Mono (D.flatSubfunctor D.isFlatStableUnderBaseChange).ι ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS (D.flatSubfunctor D.isFlatStableUnderBaseChange).ι
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatnessSituation.hasUniversalFlattening_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CX2, part (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces of finite
presentation and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation. Then the
universal flattening `Y' ⟶ Y` of `F` exists, and `Y' ⟶ Y` is a monomorphism of finite
presentation.

Over a proper morphism `F` is universally pure above every point of `Y`, by Stacks 0CVI, part (2).
So it is pure relative to `Y`, and part (1) applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasUniversalFlattening_of_isProper (D : FlatnessSituation.{u} B S hS)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS D.f.hom) (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS D.f.hom)
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite D.F) :
    D.HasUniversalFlattening ∧ Mono (D.flatSubfunctor D.isFlatStableUnderBaseChange).ι ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS (D.flatSubfunctor D.isFlatStableUnderBaseChange).ι
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasUniversalFlattening_of_isPureAbove_structure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CX2, part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces of finite
presentation such that `X` is pure relative to `Y`, that is, `𝒪_X` is pure above every point
`y ∈ |Y|`. Then the universal flattening `Y' ⟶ Y` of `X` exists, and `Y' ⟶ Y` is a monomorphism
of finite presentation.

This is part (1) for the module `𝒪_X`, which is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasUniversalFlattening_of_isPureAbove_structure {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hpure : ∀ y : points B S hS Y.1, IsPureAbove (structurePrePureSituation X.2 Y.2 f.hom
      (isFiniteType_of_isFinitePresentation B S hS hf)
      (isDecent_of_isFinitePresentation B S hS f hf) y)) :
    HasUniversalFlattening f ∧
      Mono ((structureSheafFlatnessSituation f).flatSubfunctor
        (structureSheafFlatnessSituation f).isFlatStableUnderBaseChange).ι ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS ((structureSheafFlatnessSituation f).flatSubfunctor
        (structureSheafFlatnessSituation f).isFlatStableUnderBaseChange).ι
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasUniversalFlattening_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CX2, part (4).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces of finite
presentation. Then the universal flattening of `X` exists.

This is part (3) for the module `𝒪_X`, which is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasUniversalFlattening_of_isProper {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hf : IsFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom) :
    HasUniversalFlattening f
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.InverseSystemExistenceSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CX4.** The standing data of Grothendieck's existence theorem for algebraic spaces:
an inverse system of rings with surjective, locally nilpotent transitions, a separated algebraic
space of finite presentation over the inverse-limit ring, and a compatible system of finitely
presented quasi-coherent modules on its infinitesimal base changes which are flat over, and have
support proper over, the affine base at their level.
declarations.statement: structure InverseSystemExistenceSituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation
declarations.doc:
**Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CX4].** An inverse system of rings `(Aₙ)` with surjective
transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent; an algebraic space `X` separated and of finite
presentation over `A = lim Aₙ`; and a system `(Fₙ, φₙ)` of finitely presented `𝒪_{Xₙ}`-modules on
the infinitesimal base changes `Xₙ = X ×_{Spec A} Spec Aₙ`, each flat over `Aₙ` with support proper
over `Aₙ`, together with isomorphisms `φₙ` from the restriction of `Fₙ₊₁` to `Xₙ` to `Fₙ`.
declarations.statement: structure FlatSheafExistenceSituation
declarations.comment: the situation as stated: nothing is granted or assumed beyond the source's data and hypotheses; the two containment fields only say that Spec A and Spec Aₙ are schemes of the chosen big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.derivedLimit_bounded
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CX5].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CX4] consider
`K = R lim_{D_QCoh(𝒪_X)}(Fₙ) = DQ_X(R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Fₙ)`. Then `K` is in `D^b_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and in fact
`K` has nonzero cohomology sheaves only in degrees `≥ 0`.

Formally: the coherator `DQ_X`, the right adjoint of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)`, exists; the system
`(Fₙ)` (that is, `(iₙ,* Fₙ)` placed in degree `0`) has a derived limit `L = R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Fₙ`; and
for every coherator `DQ_X` and every such `L`, `K = DQ_X(L)` is a derived limit of `(Fₙ)` in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, its cohomology sheaves vanish in negative degrees, and they vanish above some
degree; and every derived limit `K` of `(Fₙ)` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` has the same two properties.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedLimit_bounded :
    (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.IsLeftAdjoint ∧
    (∃ L, IsDerivedLimit D.derivedSystem L) ∧
    (∀ (DQ : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left ⥤
        (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).FullSubcategory)
      (_ : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι ⊣ DQ)
      (L : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left),
      IsDerivedLimit D.derivedSystem L →
        (∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => D.quasicoherentSystem.obj ⟨n⟩,
          IsDerivedLimit D.quasicoherentSystem (DQ.obj L)) ∧
        SpaceCohomologyVanishesBelow D.X.left 0
          ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj (DQ.obj L)) ∧
        ∃ c : ℤ, SpaceCohomologyVanishesAbove D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left c
          ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj (DQ.obj L))) ∧
    ∀ (_ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => D.quasicoherentSystem.obj ⟨n⟩)
      (K : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).FullSubcategory),
      IsDerivedLimit D.quasicoherentSystem K →
        SpaceCohomologyVanishesBelow D.X.left 0
          ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj K) ∧
        ∃ c : ℤ, SpaceCohomologyVanishesAbove D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left c
          ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj K)
declarations.comment: the full statement: DQ_X exists and R lim F_n exists in D(O_X); for every coherator DQ_X and every such derived limit L, K = DQ_X(L) is a derived limit of (F_n) in D_QCoh(O_X), and every derived limit K of (F_n) in D_QCoh(O_X) lies in D^b with cohomology sheaves only in degrees at least 0; nothing is granted or assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.perfectSections_of_derivedLimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CX6].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CX4] let `K = DQ_X(L)` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0CX5] (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.derivedLimit_bounded`):
`DQ_X` is a coherator (`adj : ι ⊣ DQ_X`) and `p : L ⟶ ∏ (iₙ,* Fₙ)[0]` is the first map of a
distinguished triangle `L ⟶ ∏ Fₙ ⟶ ∏ Fₙ ⟶ L[1]` whose middle map is `1 - transition`
(`hp` is exactly the triangle of `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit` with `p` bound),
so `L = R lim Fₙ`. Then for every perfect `E` on `X` and every `n`:

1. `RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K)` is a perfect object of `D(A)` and the canonical map
   `RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K) ⊗^𝐋_A Aₙ ⟶ RΓ(Xₙ, E|_{Xₙ} ⊗^𝐋 Fₙ)` is an isomorphism in `D(Aₙ)`;
2. `RHom_X(E, K)` is a perfect object of `D(A)` and the canonical map
   `RHom_X(E, K) ⊗^𝐋_A Aₙ ⟶ RHom_{Xₙ}(E|_{Xₙ}, Fₙ)` is an isomorphism in `D(Aₙ)`; this map is
   the one induced from (1) at `E^∨` by Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.48.4 (Stacks 08JJ).

Here `E|_{Xₙ}` is the derived pullback of `E` along `iₙ : Xₙ ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectSections_of_derivedLimit
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hp : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ => Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          D.derivedSystem.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left))
    (E : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left)
    (hE : spaceIsPerfect D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left E) (n : ℕ) :
    (StacksDraft.ringIsPerfect (D.limitTensorSections DQ L E) ∧
      IsIso (D.limitTensorSectionsBaseChangeMap adj L E p n)) ∧
    (StacksDraft.ringIsPerfect (D.limitSheafHomSections DQ L E) ∧
      IsIso (D.limitSheafHomSectionsBaseChangeMap adj L E hE p n))
declarations.comment: both parts in full, for every perfect E on X and every n, with K = DQ_X(L) for every coherator DQ_X and every L presented as R lim (i_n,* F_n) by the IsDerivedLimit triangle hp (as in derivedLimit_bounded, 0CX5): (1) RΓ(X, E ⊗^L K) is perfect in D(A) and the canonical map RΓ(X, E ⊗^L K) ⊗^L_A A_n → RΓ(X_n, E|_{X_n} ⊗^L F_n) is an isomorphism; (2) RHom_X(E, K) is perfect in D(A) and the canonical map RHom_X(E, K) ⊗^L_A A_n → RHom_{X_n}(E|_{X_n}, F_n), the map induced from (1) at E^∨ by 08JJ / 21.48.4, is an isomorphism; nothing is granted or assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_coheratorObj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CX7].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CX4] let `K = DQ_X(L)` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0CX5]: `DQ_X` is a coherator (`adj : ι ⊣ DQ_X`, the right adjoint of the inclusion
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⟶ D(𝒪_X)`) and `L` is a derived limit `R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Fₙ` of the system `(iₙ,* Fₙ)`.
Then `K` is pseudo-coherent relative to `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_coheratorObj
    {DQ : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left ⥤
      (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).FullSubcategory}
