declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.isIso_etaleStageBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CX8].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CX4] let `K = DQ_X(L)` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0CX5]: `DQ_X` is a coherator (`adj : ι ⊣ DQ_X`) and
`L ⟶ ∏ Fₙ ⟶ ∏ Fₙ ⟶ L[1]` (first map `p`) presents `L` as `R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Fₙ`, with
canonical maps `φₙ : K ⟶ Fₙ` the counit followed by the projections. For every `n` and every
étale morphism `j : U ⟶ X` with `U` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical map
`RΓ(U, K) ⊗^𝐋_A Aₙ ⟶ RΓ(Uₙ, Fₙ)` of `D(Aₙ)` induced by `φₙ`, `Uₙ = U ×_X Xₙ`, is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etaleStageBaseChangeMap
    {DQ : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left ⥤
      (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).FullSubcategory}
    (adj : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι ⊣ DQ)
    {L : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left}
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hp : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ => Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          D.derivedSystem.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left))
    (n : ℕ) {U : AlgebraicSpaces D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase} (j : U ⟶ D.X.left)
    (hj : IsEtale D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase j.hom)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase U.1)
    (hUqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.B.contains_terminal U.1) :
    IsIso (D.etaleStageBaseChangeMap n j
      (D.isQuasiCompact_isQuasiSeparated_of_isEtale j hj hUqc hUqs).1
      (D.isQuasiCompact_isQuasiSeparated_of_isEtale j hj hUqc hUqs).2 adj p)
declarations.comment: the full statement: for every coherator DQ_X and every presentation of L = R lim F_n in D(O_X), every n and every etale U → X with U quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical map RΓ(U, K) ⊗^L_A A_n → RΓ(U_n, F_n) in D(A_n) induced by K = DQ_X(L) → F_n is an isomorphism, U_n = U ×_X X_n; nothing is granted or assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.exists_isExistenceNeighbourhood
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CX4] let `K = DQ_X(L)` be as in [Stacks, Tag 0CX5]: `DQ_X` is a
coherator (`adj : ι ⊣ DQ_X`) and `L ⟶ ∏ Fₙ ⟶ ∏ Fₙ ⟶ L[1]` (first map `p`) presents `L` as
`R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Fₙ`, with canonical maps `K ⟶ Fₙ` the counit followed by the projections. Then
there is an open subspace `W ⊂ X` containing the points `X₀` lying over `Spec(A₁)` such that
`Hⁱ(K)|_W = 0` for `i ≠ 0`, `H⁰(K)|_W` is of finite presentation, and
`H⁰(K)|_W ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_{Xₙ} ⟶ Fₙ` induced by `K ⟶ Fₙ` is an isomorphism on `W ×_X Xₙ` for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isExistenceNeighbourhood
    {DQ : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left ⥤
      (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).FullSubcategory}
    (adj : (spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι ⊣ DQ)
    {L : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left}
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hp : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ => Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => D.derivedSystem.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
          D.derivedSystem.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left)) :
    ∃ (W : Subfunctor D.X.left.1) (hW : IsOpenSubspace D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase W),
      D.IsExistenceNeighbourhood
        ((spaceQuasicoherentProp D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left).ι.obj (DQ.obj L))
        (D.derivedLimitProjection adj p) W hW
declarations.comment: the full statement: for every coherator DQ_X and every presentation of L = R lim F_n in D(O_X), K = DQ_X(L) has an open subspace W containing X_0 with H^i(K)|_W = 0 for i ≠ 0, H^0(K)|_W of finite presentation, and F_n = H^0(K)|_W ⊗ O_{X_n} through the canonical maps K → F_n; nothing is granted or assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.exists_isExistenceNeighbourhood_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXA.** In Situation 0CX4 let `K` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` with maps
`πₙ : K ⟶ Fₙ`, and let `W ⊆ X` be an open subspace with the conclusions of Stacks 0CX9
(`D.IsExistenceNeighbourhood K π W hW`). Then, after shrinking `W` to an open subspace `W'` which
still has the conclusions of Stacks 0CX9, the support of `F = H⁰(K)|_{W'}` is proper over `A`.

This covers the source's statement as written: its `K` is that of Stacks 0CX5,
`K = DQ_X(R lim Fₙ)`, here `(spaceQuasicoherentProp _ _ _ _).ι.obj (DQ.obj L)` with the maps
`D.derivedLimitProjection adj p` for a coherator `adj : ι ⊣ DQ` and a triangle `p` presenting
`L = R lim_{D(𝒪_X)} Fₙ`, and its `W` is any open subspace with the conclusions of Stacks 0CX9
for that `K`, which is what `D.IsExistenceNeighbourhood K π W hW` says; the statement below is
the special case of the one for every `K` and every such `W`.

The source's proof, at the first level: `F` restricted to `X₁` is `F₁` by part (3) of
Stacks 0CX9, since `W` contains `X₀ = |X₁|`; so the support of `F` meets `X₁` in the support of
`F₁`, proper over `A₁`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.exists_isOpenSubspace_hasProperSupport`
(the henselian pair `(A, Ker(A → A₁))` and Stacks 0CWI) shrinks `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isExistenceNeighbourhood_hasProperSupport
    {K : spaceDerivedCategory D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left}
    {π : ∀ n : ℕ, K ⟶ D.derivedSystem.obj (op n)} {W : Subfunctor D.X.left.1}
    {hW : IsOpenSubspace D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase W}
    (hN : D.IsExistenceNeighbourhood K π W hW) :
    ∃ (W' : Subfunctor D.X.left.1) (hW' : IsOpenSubspace D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase W')
      (_ : W' ≤ W), D.IsExistenceNeighbourhood K π W' hW' ∧
      ∃ hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase (W'.ι ≫ D.X.hom.hom),
        HasProperSupport D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase hW'.1
          (schemeSpace (limitBaseObject D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase)).2
          (W'.ι ≫ D.X.hom.hom) hlft
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
            ((modulePullback D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase
              (openSubspaceHom D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase W' hW')).obj
                ((spaceDerivedHomology D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left 0).obj K)))
declarations.comment: the full statement: for every K with maps to the Fₙ (in particular the K of 0CX5 with its canonical maps) and every W with the three conclusions of 0CX9, a smaller open W', still with those conclusions, on which the support of H⁰(K)|_W' is proper over A; nothing is granted or assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FlatSheafExistenceSituation.exists_algebraization
declarations.doc:
**Grothendieck's existence theorem, [Stacks, Tag 0CXB].** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0CX4]
there exists a finitely presented `𝒪_X`-module `F`, flat over `A`, whose support is closed and
proper over `A`, with identifications `αₙ : F ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_{Xₙ} = iₙ^* F ≅ Fₙ` for all `n`,
compatible with the maps `φₙ : Fₙ₊₁ ⊗ 𝒪_{Xₙ} ≅ Fₙ` through `tₙ^* iₙ₊₁^* = iₙ^*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algebraization :
    ∃ F : Modules.{u, u} D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1 D.X.left.2,
      F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite ∧
        IsFlatOver D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.2 D.X.hom.hom F ∧
        ∃ hcl : IsClosed (supportOfSheaf D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)),
          IsProperOver D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.2
            (schemeSpace (limitBaseObject D.system D.B D.containsLimitBase)).2 D.X.hom.hom
            (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation D.B D.S
              D.containsLimitBase D.finitePresentation.1)
            (supportOfSheaf D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase D.X.left.1
              ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)) hcl ∧
          ∃ α : ∀ n : ℕ, (modulePullback D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase
              (D.closedImmersion n)).obj F ≅ D.F n,
            ∀ n : ℕ,
              (modulePullback D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase (D.transition n)).map
                  (α (n + 1)).hom ≫ (D.φ n).hom =
                (modulePullbackCompIso D.B D.S D.containsLimitBase (D.transition n)
                    (D.closedImmersion (n + 1))).hom.app F ≫
                  eqToHom (congrArg (fun g => (modulePullback D.B D.S
                    D.containsLimitBase g).obj F) (D.transition_closedImmersion n)) ≫
                  (α n).hom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_tfae_leftResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXC.** Let `X` be an object of an abelian category which admits a projective
resolution, and let `d : ℕ`. The following are equivalent: (1) `X` has projective dimension
at most `d`; (2) there is a resolution `0 → P_d → ⋯ → P₀ → X → 0` by projectives, that is, a
left resolution `F` of `X` by projective objects with `F.complex.X i = 0` for `i > d`; (3) for
some resolution `⋯ → P₁ → P₀ → X → 0` by projectives the `d`-th syzygy of `X`, the `d`-th cycles
object of the augmented complex, is projective; (4) for every such resolution the `d`-th syzygy
is projective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem CategoryTheory.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_tfae_leftResolution {C : Type u}
    [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (X : C) [HasProjectiveResolution X] (d : ℕ) :
    List.TFAE
      [HasProjectiveDimensionLE X d,
        ∃ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution (isProjective C) X,
          ∀ i, d < i → Limits.IsZero (F.complex.X i),
        ∃ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution (isProjective C) X,
          Projective ((F.complex.toSingle₀AsComplex X F.π).cycles d),
        ∀ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution (isProjective C) X,
          Projective ((F.complex.toSingle₀AsComplex X F.π).cycles d)]
declarations.comment:
A resolution `⋯ → P₁ → P₀ → M → 0` is an `ObjectProperty.LeftResolution` by the
class of projective objects (00LQ), the notion 00O7 uses; the source's `M`, `Ker(P₀ → M)` and
`Ker(P_{d-1} → P_{d-2})` are the single syzygy `(F.complex.toSingle₀AsComplex X F.π).cycles d`,
the `d`-th cycles of the augmentation `F.π` read as a complex; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_exists_leftResolution_free
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXD.** Let `R` be a commutative local ring, let `M` be an `R`-module and let
`d : ℕ`. Then `M` has projective dimension at most `d` — equivalently, by Stacks 0CXC, `M` has a
resolution of length `d` by projectives — if and only if `M` has a resolution
`0 → P_d → ⋯ → P₀ → M → 0` by *free* modules, that is, a left resolution `F` of `M` by free
modules with `F.complex.X i = 0` for `i > d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_exists_leftResolution_free {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) (d : ℕ) :
    HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d ↔
      ∃ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution (fun N : ModuleCat.{v} R => Module.Free R N) M,
        ∀ i, d < i → IsZero (F.complex.X i)
declarations.comment:
Condition (5) is added to Lemma 0CXC by stating its equivalence with item 1 of
that lemma's `TFAE`. A resolution `0 → P_d → ⋯ → P₀ → M → 0` by frees is an
`ObjectProperty.LeftResolution` for the class of free modules (00LQ), the notion 0CXC and 00O7
use, vanishing in degrees `> d`; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_exists_leftResolution_projective_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXE.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, let `M` be a finite `R`-module and let `d : ℕ`.
Then `M` has projective dimension at most `d` — equivalently, by Stacks 0CXC, `M` has a resolution
of length `d` by projectives — if and only if `M` has a resolution `0 → P_d → ⋯ → P₀ → M → 0` by
*finite projective* modules, that is, a left resolution `F` of `M` by projective modules that are
finite over `R`, with `F.complex.X i = 0` for `i > d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_exists_leftResolution_projective_finite
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v} R] (M : ModuleCat.{v} R)
    [Module.Finite R M] (d : ℕ) :
    HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d ↔
      ∃ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution
          (fun N : ModuleCat.{v} R => Projective N ∧ Module.Finite R N) M,
        ∀ i, d < i → IsZero (F.complex.X i)
declarations.comment:
Condition (6) is added to Lemma 0CXC by stating its equivalence with item 1 of
that lemma's `TFAE`. A resolution `0 → P_d → ⋯ → P₀ → M → 0` by finite projectives is an
`ObjectProperty.LeftResolution` for the class of finite projective modules (00LQ), the notion
0CXC, 0CXD and 00O7 use, vanishing in degrees `> d`; stated for a not necessarily commutative
ring. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_exists_leftResolution_free_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXF.** Let `R` be a local Noetherian ring, let `M` be a finite `R`-module and let
`d : ℕ`. Then `M` has projective dimension at most `d` — equivalently, by Stacks 0CXC, 0CXD and
0CXE, `M` has a resolution of length `d` by projectives, by frees, or by finite projectives — if
and only if `M` has a resolution `0 → F_d → ⋯ → F₀ → M → 0` by *finite free* modules, that is, a
left resolution `F` of `M` by free modules that are finite over `R`, with `F.complex.X i = 0` for
`i > d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ModuleCat.hasProjectiveDimensionLE_iff_exists_leftResolution_free_finite
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) [Module.Finite R M] (d : ℕ) :
    HasProjectiveDimensionLE M d ↔
      ∃ F : ObjectProperty.LeftResolution
          (fun N : ModuleCat.{v} R => Module.Free R N ∧ Module.Finite R N) M,
        ∀ i, d < i → IsZero (F.complex.X i)
declarations.comment:
Condition (7) is added to Lemmas 0CXC, 0CXD and 0CXE by stating its equivalence
with item 1 of 0CXC's `TFAE`. A resolution `0 → F_d → ⋯ → F₀ → M → 0` by finite frees is an
`ObjectProperty.LeftResolution` for the class of finite free modules (00LQ), the notion 00O7 uses,
vanishing in degrees `> d`; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_infinite_subset_pairwise_not_specializes
declarations.doc:
An infinite set of points on a Noetherian scheme contains an infinite subset with no
nontrivial specializations among its points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_infinite_subset_pairwise_not_specializes (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S]
    {T : Set S} (hT : T.Infinite) :
    ∃ T' : Set S, T' ⊆ T ∧ T'.Infinite ∧
      ∀ ⦃x y : S⦄, x ∈ T' → y ∈ T' → x ≠ y → ¬ x ⤳ y

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.FormalObject.exists_predeformationFormalObject
declarations.doc:
A formal object of a category over the big fppf site of `S` gives a formal object of
the predeformation category of its closed fibre, with the same levels, the same transition
maps and the same complete local base.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormalObject.exists_predeformationFormalObject
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F : Type v} [Category.{w} F]
    (p : F ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (ξ : FormalObject B S hS p)
    (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra Λ ξ.base.R]
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S)
    (hR : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ ξ.base.R)) ≫ iΛ =
      ξ.base.toS) :
    let R := ξ.base.R
    letI : CommRing R := ξ.base.commRing
    letI : IsLocalRing R := ξ.base.localRing
    let k := ResidueField R
    letI : Field k := ResidueField.field R
    letI : Algebra Λ k := ResidueField.algebra R
    let q : F ⥤ Over S := p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion
    ∃ hx₀ : q.obj (ξ.level 0) = Over.mk
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ),
      let C := predeformationCategory iΛ q (ξ.level 0) hx₀
      letI : Category C.carrier := C.category
      ∃ η : Deformation.FormalObject C.projection,
        η.base = ξ.completeLocalBase Λ ∧
          (∀ n, (C.objects (η.level n)).point = ξ.level n) ∧
          (∀ n, HEq (C.objects (η.level n)).arrow
            (FormalObject.closedPointArrow ξ n)) ∧
          (∀ n, HEq (C.morphisms (η.level (n + 1)) (η.level n)
            (η.transition n)).arrow (ξ.transition n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyOfFiniteType_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXI.** Let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of a scheme
`S` whose diagonal `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 × 𝒳` is representable by algebraic spaces. If `𝒳` is limit
preserving then `Δ` is locally of finite type.

The base change of `Δ` along a scheme-valued point of `𝒳 × 𝒳` over `U` is the presheaf of
vertical morphisms between the two components of that point, so a section of the representing
algebraic space over an affine inverse limit is a vertical morphism there, and limit preservation
of `𝒳` makes it the restriction of one at a finite stage. The surjectivity criterion of Stacks
0CM6 turns that into local finite presentation of the representing space over `U`, and Stacks
0464 into local finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_diagonal
    (hΔ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳).hom)
    (h𝒳 : Deformation.Artin.IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS 𝒳) :
    HasRelativeProperty.{u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS (Space.locallyOfFiniteTypeProperty B S hS)
      (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳) hΔ

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.FormalObject.IsVersal
declarations.doc:
A formal object `ξ` of a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` is
versal, relative to a ring `Λ` through which the structure morphism of its complete local base
factors, when the formal object of the predeformation category of its closed fibre determined
by `ξ` is versal.

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isVersalAt_iff_isVersal
declarations.doc:
With the notation of **Stacks 07XF**, let `R` be the completed local ring of `U` at a finite
type point `u₀`, presented by a ring equivalence `e`, and let `ξ` be the formal object attached
by the approximation functor of **Stacks 07X6** to a Cartesian restriction `x_R` of `x` over
`Spec R`. Then `x` is versal at `u₀` exactly when `ξ` is versal in the sense of
**Stacks 0CXJ**.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVersalAt_iff_isVersal
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F : Type v} [Category.{w} F]
    (p : F ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (U : Over S) (x : F)
    (hx : (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x = U)
    (u₀ : U.left)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom]
    (_hu₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u₀)
    (xR : Deformation.Artin.CompleteLocalObjects B S hS p)
    (ξ : Deformation.Artin.FormalObject B S hS p)
    (hξ : ξ = (Deformation.Artin.approximationFunctor B S hS p hp).obj xR)
    (e : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.completedLocalRing U.left u₀ ≃+* ξ.base.R)
    (g : Spec (.of ξ.base.R) ⟶ U.left)
    (hg : g = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom e.toRingHom) ≫
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap (U.left.presheaf.stalk u₀)
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.completedLocalRing U.left u₀))) ≫
      U.left.fromSpecStalk u₀)
    (hbase : ξ.base.toS = g ≫ U.hom)
    (r : xR.obj.1 ⟶ x)
    (_hr : p.IsCartesian (p.map r) r)
    (hrbase : HEq
      ((eqToHom (Deformation.Artin.chosenBase_eq B S hS p xR.obj).symm ≫
        p.map r).left.hom ≫ eqToHom (congrArg Over.left hx)) g)
    (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra Λ ξ.base.R]
    (hΛstalk : CommRingCat.of Λ = S.presheaf.stalk (Deformation.Artin.basePoint U u₀))
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S)
    (hiΛ : HEq iΛ (S.fromSpecStalk (Deformation.Artin.basePoint U u₀)))
    (hΛ : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ ξ.base.R)) ≫ iΛ =
      ξ.base.toS) :
    Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt U (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ x hx ↔
      Deformation.Artin.FormalObject.IsVersal B S hS p hp ξ Λ iΛ hΛ

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.smoothAt_iff_isVersalAt
declarations.doc:
Smoothness at a finite-type point is equivalent to versality of the
corresponding object of the slice fibred over schemes over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smoothAt_iff_isVersalAt
    {U V S : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V) (g : V ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ g)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (u₀ : U)
    (hu₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u₀) :
    InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f u₀ ↔
      Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt (Over.mk (f ≫ g))
        (Over.forget (Over.mk g)) u₀
        (Over.mk (Over.homMk f (by simp))) rfl

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.BaseChange.isSmoothAt_baseChange_of_isVersalAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXM.** Let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of a
locally Noetherian scheme `S`, let `x` be an object of `𝒳` over a scheme `U` locally of finite
type over `S`, and let `u₀` be a finite type point of `U`.  Assume the diagonal of `𝒳` is
representable by algebraic spaces and locally of finite type, and that `𝒳` satisfies (RS).
Let `V` be a scheme locally of finite type over `S`, let `y` be an object of `𝒳` over `V`, let
`F` be the algebraic space representing the 2-fibre product
`𝒵 = (Sch/V)_{fppf} ×_𝒳 (Sch/U)_{fppf}` over `V`, and let `z₀` be a finite type point of `F`
lying over `u₀`.  If `x` is versal at `u₀`, then `F ⟶ V` is smooth at `z₀`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSmoothAt_baseChange_of_isVersalAt
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (hΔ : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS 𝒳)
    (hΔlft :
      letI : 𝒳.val.p.IsFibered := 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids.isFibered
      ∀ (T : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (a b : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber T)
        (G : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u),
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B T.left.1 T.left.2 G →
        Nonempty (G ⋙ uliftFunctor.{v, u} ≅
          ((Over.iteratedSliceBackward T).op ⋙ 𝒳.val.p.isomPresheaf a b) ⋙
            uliftFunctor.{u, v}) →
        AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B T.left.1 T.left.2
          (terminal.from G : G ⟶
            ⊤_ ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B T.left.1 T.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)))
    (hRS : Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRS B S hS 𝒳.val.p
      𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (U V : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (B.inclusion.map U.hom)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (B.inclusion.map V.hom)]
    (x : 𝒳.val.obj) (hx : 𝒳.val.p.obj x = U)
    (u₀ : U.left.1)
    (hu₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u₀)
    (y : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B V.left.1 V.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.val.obj)
    (hy : y ⋙ 𝒳.val.p = Over.map V.hom)
    (F : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B V.left.1 V.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B V.left.1 V.left.2 F)
    (e : BaseChangeEquivalence B S hS 𝒳 U V x hx y F)
    (z₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FieldValuedPoint B V.left.1 V.left.2 F)
    (hz₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFiniteTypePoint B V.left.1 V.left.2 F
      (z₀.class B V.left.1 V.left.2 F))
    (hzu :
      letI : Category (TwoFibreProductOver (Over.map V.hom)
        (Over.forget U) 𝒳.val.p y
        (Functor.TwoYoneda.liftBased 𝒳.val.p
          𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids U ⟨x, hx⟩).toFunctor) :=
            TwoFibreProductOver.instCategory
      let P := e.inv.functor.obj ⟨z₀.siteObject, Discrete.mk z₀.value⟩
      ∃ hP : P.x = z₀.siteObject,
        (B.inclusion.map
          ((eqToHom (P.hx.trans P.hy.symm) ≫ P.y.hom).left))
          ((B.inclusion.map (eqToHom (congrArg Over.left hP).symm))
            (IsLocalRing.closedPoint z₀.carrier)) = u₀)
    (hversal : Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt (Over.mk (B.inclusion.map U.hom))
      (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ x
      (by simpa using congrArg (Over.post B.inclusion).obj hx)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmoothAt B V.left.1 V.left.2
      (terminal.from F : F ⟶
        ⊤_ ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B V.left.1 V.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
      (z₀.class B V.left.1 V.left.2 F)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.locallyOfFiniteType_and_quasiCompact_of_isPullback_appTop
declarations.doc:
**Observation (3) of the section on condition (RS\*).** Let `S` be locally Noetherian, and
let `U = Spec B`, `V = Spec A`, `W = Spec B'`, `Z = Spec A'` be affine schemes with morphisms
`f : U ⟶ V`, `g : U ⟶ W`, `i : V ⟶ Z`, `j : W ⟶ Z` whose square of global sections exhibits
`A' = A ×_B B'`, with `B' → B` surjective, and let `t : Z ⟶ S` give the `S`-algebra structures.
If `A` and `B'` are of finite type over `S` and `B` is finite over `A`, then `A'` is of finite
type over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyOfFiniteType_and_quasiCompact_of_isPullback_appTop
    {S U V W Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    [IsAffine U] [IsAffine V] [IsAffine W] [IsAffine Z]
    (f : U ⟶ V) (g : U ⟶ W) (i : V ⟶ Z) (j : W ⟶ Z) (t : Z ⟶ S)
    (hsq : IsPullback i.appTop j.appTop f.appTop g.appTop)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective g.appTop.hom) (hfin : f.appTop.hom.Finite)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (i ≫ t)] [LocallyOfFiniteType (j ≫ t)] :
    LocallyOfFiniteType t ∧ QuasiCompact t
declarations.comment: observation (3): if S is locally Noetherian, A, B, B' are of finite type over S and B is finite over A, then A' = A ×_B B' is of finite type over S

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isPushout_of_isPullback_appTop
declarations.doc:
A cartesian square of global sections of four affine schemes, one of whose maps is surjective
on global sections, is a cocartesian square of schemes. This is [Stacks Project, Tag 0ET0]
transported along `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isoSpec`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPushout_of_isPullback_appTop {U V W Z : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine U] [IsAffine V] [IsAffine W] [IsAffine Z]
    (f : U ⟶ V) (g : U ⟶ W) (i : V ⟶ Z) (j : W ⟶ Z)
    (hsq : IsPullback i.appTop j.appTop f.appTop g.appTop)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective g.appTop.hom) : IsPushout f g i j
declarations.comment: observation (1): Spec(A') = Spec(A) ⨿_{Spec(B)} Spec(B') in the category of schemes, for A' = A ×_B B' with B' → B surjective (the square-zero kernel is not needed)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.satisfiesRS_of_satisfiesRSStar
declarations.doc:
**The remark following Stacks 07Y8: condition (RS\*) implies condition (RS).**

Given a pushout square of finite-type local Artinian objects of the site along a closed
immersion, the closed immersion is a surjection of Artinian local rings, so its kernel is
nilpotent; the surjection therefore factors as a tower of square-zero surjections, each of
which (RS\*) covers, and the resulting squares of fibres paste to the given one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem satisfiesRS_of_satisfiesRSStar
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒵 : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} 𝒵] (p : 𝒵 ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp) :
    SatisfiesRS B S hS p hp
declarations.comment: observation (4): if 𝒳 satisfies (RS*), then 𝒳 satisfies (RS); the base need not be locally Noetherian

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.satisfiesRSStar_of_isAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXP.** Every algebraic stack over `S` satisfies condition (RS*) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 07Y8].

The atlas of the stack is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and smooth; smooth
morphisms of algebraic spaces are formally smooth
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_of_isSmooth_unconditional`, the implication (1) ⟹ (2) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04AM]), so the atlas is formally smooth on objects
([Stacks Project, Tag 06D3]), and `Deformation.Artin.satisfiesRSStar_of_atlas` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesRSStar_of_isAlgebraicStack
    (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : Stack.IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∀ hp : 𝒳.p.IsFiberedInGroupoids, SatisfiesRSStar B S hS 𝒳.p hp

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar
declarations.doc:
The two-fibre product of categories fibred in groupoids satisfying condition (RS*) again
satisfies (RS*).
declarations.statement:
public theorem twoFibreProductOver_satisfiesRSStar
    {X : Type uX} [Category X]
    {Y : Type uY} [Category Y]
    {Z : Type uZ} [Category Z]
    (pX : X ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (pY : Y ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (pZ : Z ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (F : X ⥤ Y) (G : Z ⥤ Y)
    (hX : pX.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hY : pY.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hZ : pZ.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hF : F ⋙ pY = pX) (hG : G ⋙ pY = pZ)
    (rsX : Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRSStar B S hS pX hX)
    (rsY : Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRSStar B S hS pY hY)
    (rsZ : Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRSStar B S hS pZ hZ) :
    Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRSStar B S hS
      (TwoFibreProductOver.structureFunctor pX pZ pY F G)
      (TwoFibreProductOver.isFiberedInGroupoids pX pZ pY F G
        hX hZ hY hF hG)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.IsEffectiveSystem
declarations.doc:
A diagram in a category over a base is effective over a specified base cocone when
that cocone comes from a cocone of the objects. In a category fibred in groupoids, the
lifted maps exhibit the diagram objects as the restrictions of the vertex object.
declarations.comment: effectivity_of_a_system_of_objects

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.IsStronglyFormallyEffective
declarations.doc:
Strong formal effectiveness for a category fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf site of a locally Noetherian scheme.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsStronglyFormallyEffective
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {X : Type v} [Category.{w} X]
    (p : X ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (_hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) : Prop
declarations.comment: strong_formal_effectiveness

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isOpenVersality_of_isSquareZeroEffective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CXU.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `𝒳` a category fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` such that

1. the diagonal of `𝒳` is representable by algebraic spaces,
2. `𝒳` has (RS*),
3. `𝒳` is limit preserving,
4. systems of objects as in Stacks 0CXT, over inverse systems of algebras whose transition maps
   are surjective with square-zero kernels, are effective.

Then `𝒳` satisfies openness of versality: if `x` is an object of `𝒳` over a scheme `U` locally of
finite type over `S`, versal at a finite type point `u₀` of `U`, then `x` is versal at every finite
type point of an open neighbourhood of `u₀`.

The conclusion is the body of `Deformation.Artin.IsOpenVersality` (Stacks 07XQ), written out; see
the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenVersality_of_isSquareZeroEffective [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (hΔ : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS 𝒳)
    (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS 𝒳.val.p 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hlim : IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, w, v} B S hS 𝒳)
    (heff : IsSquareZeroEffective B S hS 𝒳.val.p 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (U : Over S) (hUft : LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (x : 𝒳.val.obj)
    (hx : (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x = U) (u₀ : U.left)
    (hu₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u₀)
    (hversal : IsVersalAt U (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ x hx) :
    ∃ V : U.left.Opens, u₀ ∈ V.1 ∧
      ∀ u ∈ V.1, AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u →
        IsVersalAt U (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u x hx

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isOpenVersality_diagonal_of_isFullyFaithfulOnSquareZeroTowers
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `𝒳` a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf
site of `S` whose second diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, which satisfies (RS*),
which is limit preserving, and for which the restriction functors
`𝒳_{Spec lim Rₙ} ⟶ lim 𝒳_{Spec Rₙ}` of square-zero towers are fully faithful. Then the diagonal
`Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 × 𝒳` satisfies openness of versality: for every scheme `V` locally of finite type over
`S` and every object `y` of `𝒳 × 𝒳` over `V`, the 2-fibre product
`(Sch/V)_{fppf} ×_{y, 𝒳 × 𝒳, Δ} 𝒳` satisfies openness of versality — an object over a scheme `U`
locally of finite type over `V` which is versal at a finite type point `u₀` is versal at every
finite type point of an open neighbourhood of `u₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenVersality_diagonal_of_isFullyFaithfulOnSquareZeroTowers
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h1 : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.relativeDiagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product 𝒳 𝒳)
        (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.diagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳)))
    (h2 : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS 𝒳.val.p 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (h3 : IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS 𝒳)
    (h4 : IsFullyFaithfulOnSquareZeroTowers B S hS 𝒳.val.p) :
    ∀ (V : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS), LocallyOfFiniteType (B.inclusion.map V.hom) →
      ∀ (y : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B V.left.1 V.left.2 ⥤
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product 𝒳 𝒳).val.obj),
        y ⋙ (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product 𝒳 𝒳).val.p = Over.map V.hom →
        let q := TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map V.hom) 𝒳.val.p
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product 𝒳 𝒳).val.p y
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.diagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳).toFunctor ⋙
            Over.post B.inclusion
        ∀ (U : Over V.left.1), LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom →
          ∀ (x : TwoFibreProductOver (Over.map V.hom) 𝒳.val.p
              (CatFiberedInGroupoids.product 𝒳 𝒳).val.p y
              (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.diagonalBasedFunctor B S hS 𝒳).toFunctor)
            (hx : q.obj x = U) (u₀ : U.left),
            IsFiniteTypePoint u₀ →
            IsVersalAt U q u₀ x hx →
            ∃ W : U.left.Opens, u₀ ∈ W.1 ∧
              ∀ u ∈ W.1, IsFiniteTypePoint u → IsVersalAt U q u x hx

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.exists_nonEffectiveSystem_quotientStack_trivialAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CXX.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field which is not the
algebraic closure of a finite field, let `A` be an abelian variety over `k` and let
`𝒳 = [Spec(k)/A]`. There is an inverse system of `k`-algebras whose transition maps are
surjective with locally nilpotent kernels — the thickenings of the triangle of three affine
lines — and a system of objects of `𝒳` over the spectra of its levels, which is not effective
in the sense of Tag 0CXT.

The mathematical inputs the library does not have are hypotheses: `h0AFB` is the lifting of an
object along a nilpotent thickening of the triangle, the method of Tag 0AFB; `h0AF9` is the
finiteness of the order of the class of every object over the limit, Tag 0AF9 together with
Tag 0AFA; `ξ₀` together with `hnontorsion` is the object over the reduced triangle whose class
has infinite order, which the source builds from a non-torsion rational point of `A` and
Tag 0AEN; `H`, `cls` and `hcls` are the first cohomology class of an object of `𝒳`, that is,
the description of the fibre categories of a classifying stack as groupoids of torsors; and
`U`, `cU`, `e`, `eL`, `he`, `heL`, `hchart` realize the spectra of the levels of the inverse
system and of its limit as objects of the chosen big fppf site. Non-effectivity is nowhere
assumed, and the system of objects is constructed rather than supposed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_nonEffectiveSystem_quotientStack_trivialAction
    [IsAlgClosed k]
    (_hkinf : ∀ F : Subfield k, Finite F → ¬ Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k)
    (U : ℕ ⥤ fppfOverField k C hk) (cU : Cocone U)
    (cR : Cone (triangleThickenings k)) (hcR : IsLimit cR)
    (e : ∀ n : ℕ, (schemeOverField k C hk).obj (U.obj n) ≅
      Spec (.of ((triangleThickenings k).obj (.op n))))
    (eL : (schemeOverField k C hk).obj cU.pt ≅ Spec (.of cR.pt))
    (he : ∀ {i j : ℕ} (g : i ⟶ j), (schemeOverField k C hk).map (U.map g) ≫ (e j).hom =
      (e i).hom ≫ Scheme.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom ((triangleThickenings k).map g.op).hom.toRingHom).op)
    (heL : ∀ n : ℕ, (schemeOverField k C hk).map (cU.ι.app n) ≫ eL.hom =
      (e n).hom ≫ Scheme.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (cR.π.app (.op n)).hom.toRingHom).op)
    (hchart : eL.inv ≫ C.inclusion.map cU.pt.hom =
      Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k cR.pt)).op)
    (H : (fppfOverField k C hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (cls : (x : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).obj) →
      H.obj (.op ((Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p.obj x)))
    (hcls : ∀ {x y : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).obj} (φ : x ⟶ y),
      cls x = H.map ((Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p.map φ).op (cls y))
    (ξ₀ : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).obj)
    (hξ₀ : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p.obj ξ₀ ≅ U.obj 0)
    (hnontorsion : ¬ IsOfFinAddOrder (cls ξ₀))
    (h0AF9 : ∀ x : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).obj,
      (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p.obj x = cU.pt → IsOfFinAddOrder (cls x))
    (h0AFB : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).obj)
      (a : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p.obj x ≅ U.obj n),
      ∃ (y : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).obj)
        (b : (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p.obj y ≅ U.obj (n + 1))
        (φ : x ⟶ y), (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p.map φ ≫ b.hom =
          a.hom ≫ U.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n))) :
    ∃ (R : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u} k) (cS : Cone R)
      (ξ : ℕ ⥤ (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).obj)
      (c : Cocone (ξ ⋙ (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p))
      (f : ∀ n : ℕ, (schemeOverField k C hk).obj
        ((ξ ⋙ (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p).obj n) ≅ Spec (.of (R.obj (.op n))))
      (fL : (schemeOverField k C hk).obj c.pt ≅ Spec (.of cS.pt)),
      Nonempty (IsLimit cS) ∧
      (∀ {i j : ℕᵒᵖ} (g : i ⟶ j), Function.Surjective (R.map g).hom) ∧
      (∀ {i j : ℕᵒᵖ} (g : i ⟶ j),
        (RingHom.ker (R.map g).hom.toRingHom).LocallyNilpotent) ∧
      (∀ {i j : ℕ} (g : i ⟶ j), (schemeOverField k C hk).map
          ((ξ ⋙ (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p).map g) ≫ (f j).hom =
        (f i).hom ≫ Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (R.map g.op).hom.toRingHom).op) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, (schemeOverField k C hk).map (c.ι.app n) ≫ fL.hom =
        (f n).hom ≫ Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (cS.π.app (.op n)).hom.toRingHom).op) ∧
      (fL.inv ≫ C.inclusion.map c.pt.hom =
        Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k cS.pt)).op) ∧
      ¬ IsEffectiveSystem (Stack.quotientStack Q.groupoid).p ξ c
declarations.comment: RESTRICTED: Tag 0AFB (lifting an object along a thickening) is the hypothesis h0AFB, Tags 0AF9 and 0AFA (finite order of the class over the limit) are h0AF9, the non-torsion rational point of the abelian variety with Tag 0AEN is ξ₀ with hnontorsion, and the class of a torsor is the data H, cls, hcls; the site realization is U, cU, e, eL, he, heL, hchart

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.exists_isOpen_refinement_of_isCompact_of_pairwiseSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CY5.** Let `Z` be a quasi-compact subset of a topological space `X` whose
distinct points can be separated by disjoint opens of `X`, let `U : I → Set X` be an open
cover of `Z`, and for each `(p+1)`-tuple `σ` of indices let `W σ` be an open set contained in
`⋂ k, U (σ k)` and agreeing with it on `Z`. Then `Z` has an open cover `V : I → Set X` with
`V i ⊆ U i`, with `closure (V i) ∩ Z ⊆ U i`, and with `⋂ k, V (σ k) ⊆ W σ` for every `σ`.

The reduction to the finite case is by extracting a finite subcover of `Z` and extending the
resulting family by `∅` outside it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpen_refinement_of_isCompact_of_pairwiseSeparated
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsCompact Z)
    (hSep : ∀ x ∈ Z, ∀ y ∈ Z, x ≠ y →
      ∃ A B : Set X, IsOpen A ∧ IsOpen B ∧ x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ B ∧ Disjoint A B)
    (p : ℕ) (I : Type*)
    (U : I → Set X) (hU : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (W : (Fin (p + 1) → I) → Set X) (hW : ∀ σ, IsOpen (W σ))
    (hCover : Z ⊆ ⋃ i, U i)
    (hWinter : ∀ σ, W σ ∩ Z = (⋂ k, U (σ k)) ∩ Z) :
    ∃ V : I → Set X,
      (∀ i, IsOpen (V i)) ∧
      (Z ⊆ ⋃ i, V i) ∧
      (∀ i, V i ⊆ U i) ∧
      (∀ i, closure (V i) ∩ Z ⊆ U i) ∧
      (∀ σ : Fin (p + 1) → I, ⋂ k, V (σ k) ⊆ W σ)

declarations.name: noetherian_base_change_finite_type
declarations.doc:
If `R → R'` is of finite type and `S` is a Noetherian `R`-algebra, then
the base change `R' ⊗[R] S` is a Noetherian ring.

The proof transports the result along the commutativity isomorphism
`S ⊗[R] R' ≃ R' ⊗[R] S`, after observing that base change preserves
finite type and applying the Hilbert basis theorem.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherian_base_change_finite_type
    (R R' S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R R'] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R R'] [IsNoetherianRing S] :
    IsNoetherianRing (TensorProduct R R' S)

declarations.name: Algebra.ker_algebraMap_isMaximal_of_finiteType_of_isJacobsonRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CY7.** Let `R` be a Jacobson ring and let `K` be a field which is of finite type
as an `R`-algebra. Then `RingHom.ker (algebraMap R K)` is a maximal ideal of `R`. In particular,
if `R` is a subring of `K` then `R` is a field; that `K` is then finite over `R` is
`finite_of_finite_type_of_isJacobsonRing`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.ker_algebraMap_isMaximal_of_finiteType_of_isJacobsonRing
    (R K : Type*) [CommRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsJacobsonRing R]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R K] :
    (RingHom.ker (algebraMap R K)).IsMaximal

declarations.name: isIntegral_pi_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0CY8 (finite product integral).**
Let `ι` be a finite index type and let `φ_i : R_i → S_i` be ring maps (recorded as the
`Algebra (R i) (S i)` instances). For the product rings `∏ R_i = ∀ i, R i` and
`∏ S_i = ∀ i, S i` with the product algebra structure, an element `s = (s_i)_i` of
`∏ S_i` is integral over `∏ R_i` if and only if each component `s_i` is integral over
`R_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_pi_iff (ι : Type*) [Finite ι] (R : ι → Type*) (S : ι → Type*)
    [∀ i, CommRing (R i)] [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra (R i) (S i)]
    (s : ∀ i, S i) :
    IsIntegral (∀ i, R i) s ↔ ∀ i, IsIntegral (R i) (s i)

declarations.name: IsIntegralClosure.pi_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CY9.** Let `R i → S i` be a finite family of ring maps and let `S' i` be an algebra
whose canonical map to `S i` identifies it with the integral closure of `R i` in `S i`. Then
`∏ i, S' i` is the integral closure of `∏ i, R i` in `∏ i, S i`, and conversely. Taking
`S' = R` this says that `∏ i, R i → ∏ i, S i` is integrally closed if and only if each
`R i → S i` is.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsIntegralClosure.pi_iff {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] {R S S' : ι → Type*}
    [∀ i, CommRing (R i)] [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, CommSemiring (S' i)]
    [∀ i, Algebra (R i) (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra (S' i) (S i)] :
    IsIntegralClosure (∀ i, S' i) (∀ i, R i) (∀ i, S i) ↔
      ∀ i, IsIntegralClosure (S' i) (R i) (S i)

declarations.name: isNormalRing_pi
declarations.doc:
A finite product of normal rings is normal.
(Stacks Lemma 10.37.16, tag `0CYA`.)
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalRing_pi

    (h : ∀ i, IsNormalRing (R i)) :
    IsNormalRing (∀ i, R i)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.pseudoCoherent_iff_derivedTensor_preserves_products
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYB.** Pseudo-coherence of a bounded-above complex is equivalent to derived
tensor product commuting with arbitrary products; the degreewise variants characterize
`m`-pseudo-coherence.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_iff_derivedTensor_preserves_products
    (T : DerivedTensorProduct.{u, v, w} R) (P : DerivedProducts.{u, v, w} R)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Minus (ModuleCat.{max v w} (SmallRing.{u, v, w} R))) (m : ℤ) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsPseudoCoherent K.obj,
      ∀ (A : Type (max v w)) (Q : A → ModuleCat.{max v w} (SmallRing.{u, v, w} R)),
        IsIso (tensorProductComparison T P K.obj A Q),
      ∀ (A : Type (max v w)) (Q : ModuleCat.{max v w} (SmallRing.{u, v, w} R)),
        IsIso (tensorPowerComparison T P K.obj A Q),
      ∀ A : Type (max v w), IsIso (tensorRingPowerComparison T P K.obj A)] ∧
    List.TFAE [
      IsPseudoCoherentFrom K.obj m,
      ∀ (A : Type (max v w)) (Q : A → ModuleCat.{max v w} (SmallRing.{u, v, w} R)),
        (∀ i : ℤ, m < i → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).map
          (tensorProductComparison T P K.obj A Q))) ∧
        Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).map
          (tensorProductComparison T P K.obj A Q)),
      ∀ (A : Type (max v w)) (Q : ModuleCat.{max v w} (SmallRing.{u, v, w} R)),
        (∀ i : ℤ, m < i → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).map
          (tensorPowerComparison T P K.obj A Q))) ∧
        Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).map
          (tensorPowerComparison T P K.obj A Q)),
      ∀ A : Type (max v w),
        (∀ i : ℤ, m < i → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).map
          (tensorRingPowerComparison T P K.obj A))) ∧
        Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).map
          (tensorRingPowerComparison T P K.obj A))]

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.MorphismOfFirstOrderThickenings.existenceObstructionClass_first
declarations.doc:
The obstruction classes of the two thickenings are compatible: the map
`Ext²_O(F, K₂) ⟶ Ext²_O(F, K₁)` induced by `κ` carries `o(F, K₂, c₂)` to `o(F, K₁, c₁)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existenceObstructionClass_first
    [HasExt.{e} (SheafOfModules.{w₂} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf D.O₂))]
    (F K₁ K₂ : SheafOfModules.{w₂} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (baseRing i)))
    (c₁ : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).obj D.first.I).obj F ⟶ K₁)
    (c₂ : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).obj D.second.I).obj F ⟶ K₂)
    (κ : K₂ ⟶ K₁)
    (hκ : c₂ ≫ κ =
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).map D.idealMap).app F ≫ c₁) :
    existenceObstructionClass D.first F K₁ c₁ =
      (existenceObstructionClass D.second F K₂ c₂).comp (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ κ) (add_zero 2)

structure FlatThickeningMorphismSituation

declarations.name: Deformation.ToposThickening.MorphismOfFirstOrderThickenings.existenceObstructionClass_first_tensorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYE.** In the situation of Stacks 0CYD the canonical map
`Ext²_O(ℱ, f^*J₂ ⊗_O ℱ) ⟶ Ext²_O(ℱ, f^*J₁ ⊗_O ℱ)` carries the obstruction class
`o(ℱ, f^*J₂ ⊗_O ℱ, 1)` of the second column to the obstruction class `o(ℱ, f^*J₁ ⊗_O ℱ, 1)` of
the first.

The coefficient module of the `k`-th column is written `Iₖ ⊗_O ℱ` and the map on `Ext²` is the
one induced by the map `I₂ ⟶ I₁` of square-zero ideals of the upper row; under the hypotheses of
Stacks 0CYD the comparison `f^*Jₖ ⟶ Iₖ` is an isomorphism, which is the reading under which
`Deformation.ToposThickening.hasFlatLift_iff_obstruction_eq_zero` states Stacks 08VW. See the
implementation notes.

This is Stacks 0CYC at `Kₖ = Iₖ ⊗_O ℱ` and `cₖ = 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existenceObstructionClass_first_tensorIdeal :
    existenceObstructionClass D.first F
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).obj D.first.I).obj F)
        (𝟙 (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).obj D.first.I).obj F)) =
      (existenceObstructionClass D.second F
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).obj D.second.I).obj F)
          (𝟙 (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).obj D.second.I).obj F))).comp
        (Abelian.Ext.mk₀
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (baseRing i)).map D.idealMap).app F))
        (add_zero 2)
declarations.comment: coefficients and Ext map written through the ideals Iₖ, which are f^*Jₖ by 08MQ

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isOpenVersality_of_obstructionTheory
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and let `𝒳` be a category fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`. Assume

1. the diagonal `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 × 𝒳` is representable by algebraic spaces,
2. `𝒳` has (RS*),
3. `𝒳` is limit preserving,
4. there exists an obstruction theory `O`,
5. for an object `x` of `𝒳` over `Spec A` and `A`-modules `Mₙ`, `n ≥ 1`,
   (a) `T_x(∏ Mₙ) = ∏ T_x(Mₙ)`, and
   (b) `𝒪_x(∏ Mₙ) ⟶ ∏ 𝒪_x(Mₙ)` is injective.

Then `𝒳` satisfies openness of versality: if `x` over a scheme `U` locally of finite type over
`S` is versal at a finite type point `u₀`, it is versal at every finite type point of an open
neighbourhood of `u₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenVersality_of_obstructionTheory [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h1 : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS 𝒳)
    (h2 : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS 𝒳.val.p 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (h3 : IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u + 1, u} B S hS 𝒳)
    (O : ObstructionTheory B S hS 𝒳.val.p 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (h5a : TangentPreservesCountableProducts B S hS 𝒳.val.p 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids h2)
    (h5b : O.InjectiveOnCountableProducts) :
    ∀ (U : Over S), LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom →
      ∀ (x : 𝒳.val.obj) (hx : (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x = U) (u₀ : U.left),
        IsFiniteTypePoint u₀ →
        IsVersalAt U (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ x hx →
        ∃ W : U.left.Opens, u₀ ∈ W.1 ∧
          ∀ u ∈ W.1, IsFiniteTypePoint u →
            IsVersalAt U (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u x hx

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_sigmaDesc

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_iff_exists_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYL, parts (1) and (2).** The reduced closed subscheme on `Z` is proper over `S`
exactly when some closed subscheme structure on `Z` is proper over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProperOver_iff_exists_isProper :
    IsProperOver f Z ↔ ∃ I : X.IdealSheafData, I.support = Z ∧ IsProper (I.subschemeι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isProper_iff_forall_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYL, parts (2) and (3).** If one closed subscheme structure on `Z` is proper over
`S`, then every closed subscheme structure on `Z` is proper over `S`.
declarations.comment: parts (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYM.** A closed subset `Z` of `X` is proper over `S` if its reduced induced closed
subscheme is proper over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsProperOver {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (Z : Closeds X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_of_le
declarations.doc:

base.

public theorem isProperOver_of_le {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    {Y Z : Closeds X} (hYZ : Y ≤ Z) (hZ : IsProperOver f Z) : IsProperOver f Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_preimage_baseChange
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0CYP.** A closed subset proper over the base remains proper after base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProperOver_preimage_baseChange {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}}
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (h : IsPullback g' f' f g) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (Z : Closeds X) (hZ : IsProperOver f Z) :
    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback h inferInstance
    IsProperOver f' (Z.preimage g'.continuous)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosed_image_of_isProperOver
declarations.doc:
The image of a closed subset proper over the base is closed in a separated
scheme locally of finite type over that base.
declarations.statement:
lemma isClosed_image_of_isProperOver {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfg : f ≫ g = p)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [IsSeparated g]
    (Z : Closeds X) (hZ : IsProperOver p Z) :
    IsClosed (f.base '' (Z : Set X))
declarations.comment: image_separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_image
declarations.doc:
The image of a closed subset proper over the base is itself proper over the
base, when the target is separated and locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
lemma isProperOver_image {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hfg : f ≫ g = p)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [IsSeparated g]
    (Z : Closeds X) (hZ : IsProperOver p Z) :
    IsProperOver g
      ⟨f.base '' (Z : Set X), isClosed_image_of_isProperOver p g f hfg Z hZ⟩
declarations.comment: image_separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_preimage
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of a closed subset proper over the base along a proper
morphism is proper over the base.

    [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (Z : Closeds Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_closedImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_sup
