declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isProperOver_supp_iff_isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
The support of a quasi-coherent module of finite type is proper over the base if and only if
its scheme-theoretic support is proper over the base.
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport_iff_exists_pushforward
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic support of a quasi-coherent module `F` of finite type is proper over the
base if and only if there is a closed subscheme of `X` proper over the base carrying a
quasi-coherent module of finite type whose direct image is `F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProper_schemeTheoreticSupport_iff_exists_pushforward :
    IsProper ((schemeTheoreticSupport F).subschemeι ≫ f) ↔
      ∃ (J : X.IdealSheafData) (G : J.subscheme.Modules),
        G.IsFiniteType ∧ G.IsQuasicoherent ∧ IsProper (J.subschemeι ≫ f) ∧
          Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward J.subschemeι).obj G ≅ F)
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_supp_pullback
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square, base change preserves properness of the support
of a finite type module over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_supp_pullback {X' X S' S : Scheme.{u}}
    (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    (h : IsPullback g' f' f g) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hF : IsProperOver f ⟨SheafOfModules.supp F, SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp F⟩) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f' := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback h inferInstance
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F).IsFiniteType :=
      SheafOfModules.pullback_isFiniteType g'.toLRSHom.toShHom F
    IsProperOver f'
      ⟨SheafOfModules.supp ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F),
        SheafOfModules.isClosed_supp _⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSerreClass_hasProperSupport_coherentModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CYU, part (2).** For `f : X ⟶ S` locally of finite type with `S`
locally Noetherian, the coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose support is proper over `S` form a Serre
subcategory of the abelian category of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.

The zero module has empty support, which is proper over `S`; and the support of the middle term
of an exact sequence of coherent modules is contained in the union of the supports of the outer
two, a union of two closed subsets proper over `S` being proper over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSerreClass_hasProperSupport_coherentModules [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass
      (C := SheafOfModules.CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf)
      (fun F => Stacks.Algebraization.HasProperSupport f F.obj)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_biprod_support
declarations.doc:
The direct sum of two sheaves with proper support
has proper support.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_biprod_support {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F G : X.Modules)
    (b : BinaryBicone F G) (hb : b.IsBilimit)
    (hF : ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp F ∧
      IsProperOver f Z))
    (hG : ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp G ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)) :
    ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp b.pt ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)
declarations.comment: sheaf_operations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_extension_support
declarations.doc:
A short exact extension of sheaves with proper
support has proper support.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_extension_support {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (E : ShortComplex X.Modules) (hE : E.ShortExact)
    (hF : ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp E.X₁ ∧
      IsProperOver f Z))
    (hG : ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp E.X₃ ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)) :
    ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp E.X₂ ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)
declarations.comment: sheaf_operations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_image_support
declarations.doc:
The image of a morphism from a finite type sheaf with proper
support to an arbitrary sheaf of modules has proper support.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_image_support {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F G : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType]
    (u : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp F ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)) :
    ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp (Abelian.image u) ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)
declarations.comment: sheaf_operations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_cokernel_support
declarations.doc:
The cokernel of a morphism from an arbitrary sheaf of modules to a finite type
sheaf with proper support has proper support.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_cokernel_support {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F G : X.Modules)
    [G.IsFiniteType]
    (u : F ⟶ G)
    (hG : ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp G ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)) :
    ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp (cokernel u) ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)
declarations.comment: sheaf_operations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProperOver_quotient_support
declarations.doc:
A quotient of a finite type sheaf with proper
support has proper support.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_quotient_support {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F Q : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFiniteType]
    (q : F ⟶ Q) [Epi q]
    (hF : ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp F ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)) :
    ∃ Z : Closeds X, ((Z : Set X) = SheafOfModules.supp Q ∧
      IsProperOver f Z)
declarations.comment: sheaf_operations

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.isSerreClass_hasProperSupport
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CYV], part (1).** The coherent adic systems along `ℐ` whose first term has
support proper over `S` form a Serre subcategory of `Coh(X, ℐ)`.

All terms of a coherent adic system have the same support, and the support of the middle term of a
short exact sequence is the union of the supports of the outer two, which is proper over `S`
because a finite union of closed subsets proper over the base is proper over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSerreClass_hasProperSupport {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    letI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
    letI : IsNoetherian X := AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian.mk
    ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass (C := CoherentAdicSystems I)
      (fun F => Stacks.Algebraization.HasProperSupport f (F.obj.obj (op 0)))
declarations.comment: proper support

declarations.name: Stacks.Coherent.isSerreClass_hasProperAnnihilator
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CYV], part (2).** The coherent adic systems along `ℐ` admitting a closed
subscheme of `X` proper over `S` whose ideal sheaf annihilates every term form a Serre subcategory
of `Coh(X, ℐ)`.

An ideal sheaf annihilating every term of a system annihilates every term of a subobject and of a
quotient; for an extension the product of the two ideal sheaves works, and the closed subset it
cuts out is the union of the two, which is again proper over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSerreClass_hasProperAnnihilator {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S] (f : X ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (I : X.IdealSheafData) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    letI : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
    letI : IsNoetherian X := AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian.mk
    (HasProperAnnihilator f I).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: common proper annihilator

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fittingIdeal_zero_le_annihilatorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CYX, part (1).** The scheme-theoretic support of a finite type
quasi-coherent module is a closed subscheme of the one cut out by its zeroth Fitting ideal:
over every affine open the zeroth Fitting ideal is contained in the annihilator.
declarations.statement: theorem fittingIdeal_zero_le_annihilatorIdeal : fittingIdeal F 0 ≤ annihilatorIdeal' F
declarations.comment: scheme_theoretic_inclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fittingIdeal_zero_support_eq_supp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CYX, part (2).** The closed subscheme cut out by the zeroth Fitting
ideal of a finite type quasi-coherent module has the support of the module as its underlying
closed set, so it agrees there with the scheme-theoretic support.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_zero_support_eq_supp :
    (fittingIdeal F 0).support = SheafOfModules.supp F
declarations.comment: underlying_support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_module_on_fittingSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CYX, part (3).** A finite type quasi-coherent module is the direct
image of a finite type quasi-coherent module on the closed subscheme cut out by its zeroth
Fitting ideal, namely of its own pullback there.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_module_on_fittingSubscheme :
    ∃ (G : (fittingIdeal F 0).subscheme.Modules)
      (_ : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (fittingIdeal F 0).subschemeι).obj G ≅ F),
      G.IsFiniteType ∧ G.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: module_on_fitting_subscheme

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supp_eq_annihilatorIdeal_support
registrations.comment: underlying_support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.induced_locallyOfFiniteType_iff
declarations.doc:
In the situation of two closed immersions `i : Z ⟶ X` and `j : Z ⟶ Y`, morphisms
`f : X' ⟶ X` and `g : Y' ⟶ Y`, and an isomorphism over `Z` between the two inverse images of `Z`,
the induced morphism from the glued scheme `X' ⨿_{X' ×_X Z} Y'` to the pushout `Y ⨿_Z X` is
locally of finite type if and only if `f` and `g` are locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem induced_locallyOfFiniteType_iff (S : CompatiblePushoutMorphismSituation.{u}) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType S.induced ↔
      LocallyOfFiniteType S.f ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType S.g
declarations.comment: locally_of_finite_type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_induced_iff
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `AlgebraicGeometry.CompatiblePushoutMorphismSituation`, the induced
morphism between the two pushouts is flat if and only if both morphisms on the pieces are flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_induced_iff (S : CompatiblePushoutMorphismSituation.{u}) :
    Flat S.induced ↔ Flat S.f ∧ Flat S.g
declarations.comment: flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation_induced_iff
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `AlgebraicGeometry.CompatiblePushoutMorphismSituation`, the induced
morphism between the two pushouts is flat and locally of finite presentation if and only if both
morphisms on the pieces are flat and locally of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation_induced_iff
    (S : CompatiblePushoutMorphismSituation.{u}) :
    (Flat S.induced ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation S.induced) ↔
      ((Flat S.f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation S.f) ∧
        (Flat S.g ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation S.g))
declarations.comment: flat_locally_of_finite_presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_induced_iff
declarations.doc:
In a compatible morphism of pushouts along closed immersions, the induced morphism is étale if
and only if the morphisms on both pieces are étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_induced_iff (S : CompatiblePushoutMorphismSituation.{u}) :
    Etale S.induced ↔ (Etale S.f ∧ Etale S.g)
declarations.comment: etale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_induced_iff
declarations.doc:
In a compatible morphism of pushouts along closed immersions, the induced morphism is smooth
if and only if the morphisms on both pieces are smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_induced_iff (S : CompatiblePushoutMorphismSituation.{u}) :
    Smooth S.induced ↔ (Smooth S.f ∧ Smooth S.g)
declarations.comment: smooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealSheaf_schemeTheoreticUnion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYZ.** The defining ideal sheaf of the scheme-theoretic union of two closed
subspaces is the meet of their defining ideal sheaves.

One containment is inclusion-reversal.  For the other, the meet of the two ideal sheaves is
quasi-coherent, hence by Stacks 03MB cuts out a closed subspace `W`; that `W` contains both `Y`
and `Z` because its ideal is contained in each of theirs, so the scheme-theoretic union, being
the smallest closed subspace containing both, is contained in `W`, and inclusion-reversal gives
the containment of ideals back.
declarations.statement:
theorem definingIdealSheaf_schemeTheoreticUnion :
    definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (schemeTheoreticUnion B S hS X.1 X.2 Y Z) =
      definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Y ⊓ definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z
declarations.comment: the defining ideal of the scheme-theoretic union is the meet of the two defining ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.definingIdealSheaf_schemeTheoreticIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYZ.** The defining ideal sheaf of the scheme-theoretic intersection of two closed
subspaces is the sum of their defining ideal sheaves.

One containment is inclusion-reversal.  For the other, the sum of the two ideal sheaves is
quasi-coherent, hence by Stacks 03MB cuts out a closed subspace `W`; that `W` is contained in
both `Y` and `Z` because its ideal contains each of theirs, hence in their intersection, and
inclusion-reversal gives the containment of ideals back.
declarations.statement:
theorem definingIdealSheaf_schemeTheoreticIntersection :
    definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (schemeTheoreticIntersection B S hS X.1 X.2 Y Z) =
      definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Y ⊔ definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z
declarations.comment: the defining ideal of the scheme-theoretic intersection is the sum of the two defining ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYZ.** The closed subspace cut out by the sum of the defining quasi-coherent
ideal sheaves.
declarations.comment: scheme-theoretic intersection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticUnion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CYZ.** The closed subspace cut out by the intersection of the defining
quasi-coherent ideal sheaves.
declarations.comment: scheme-theoretic union

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_schemeTheoreticIntersection
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic intersection of two closed subspaces of an algebraic
space over `S` is the fibre product of the two over the ambient space: the square formed by the
four inclusions is Cartesian in the category of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_schemeTheoreticIntersection (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (Z Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS F) :
    IsPullback
      (Subfunctor.homOfLe (show (schemeTheoreticIntersection B S hS F hF Z Y).1 ≤ Z.1 from
        inf_le_left))
      (Subfunctor.homOfLe (show (schemeTheoreticIntersection B S hS F hF Z Y).1 ≤ Y.1 from
        inf_le_right))
      Z.1.ι Y.1.ι
declarations.comment: the intersection square is cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_schemeTheoreticIntersection_le_left
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic intersection of two closed subspaces of an algebraic
space over `S` is a closed subspace of the first of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_schemeTheoreticIntersection_le_left
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (Z Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS F) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS
      (Subfunctor.homOfLe (show (schemeTheoreticIntersection B S hS F hF Z Y).1 ≤ Z.1 from
        inf_le_left))
declarations.comment: closed immersion into the first factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_schemeTheoreticIntersection_le_right
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic intersection of two closed subspaces of an algebraic
space over `S` is a closed subspace of the second of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_schemeTheoreticIntersection_le_right
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (Z Y : ClosedSubspaces B S hS F) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS
      (Subfunctor.homOfLe (show (schemeTheoreticIntersection B S hS F hF Z Y).1 ≤ Y.1 from
        inf_le_right))
declarations.comment: closed immersion into the second factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.unionIntersectionShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ1, second assertion.**  For two closed subspaces `Y, Z` of an algebraic space
`X` over `S`, with `Y ∪ Z` and `Y ∩ Z` their scheme-theoretic union and intersection,

`0 ⟶ 𝒪_{Y ∪ Z} ⟶ 𝒪_Y × 𝒪_Z ⟶ 𝒪_{Y ∩ Z} ⟶ 0`

is a short exact sequence of `𝒪_X`-modules, the four structure sheaves being taken as modules
on `X` under Stacks 04CJ, the first map built from the two canonical maps `𝒪_{Y ∪ Z} ⟶ 𝒪_Y` and
`𝒪_{Y ∪ Z} ⟶ 𝒪_Z` and the second from the canonical map `𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_{Y ∩ Z}` and the negative of
the canonical map `𝒪_Z ⟶ 𝒪_{Y ∩ Z}`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.shortExact_biprod_of_ker_eq_inf_sup` applied to the four
structure projections of `𝒪_X`, which are epimorphisms by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_structureProjection` and whose kernels are the four defining
ideals; the two identifications of Stacks 0CYZ say that the kernels for the union and the
intersection are the meet and the join of the kernels for `Y` and `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem unionIntersectionShortComplex_shortExact :
    (unionIntersectionShortComplex B S hS X Y Z).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the short exact sequence of the structure sheaves of the union, the two subspaces and the intersection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPushout_schemeTheoreticUnion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0CZ1], third assertion.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and
let `Y, Z ⊆ X` be closed subspaces, with `Y ∪ Z` and `Y ∩ Z` the scheme-theoretic union and
intersection of [Stacks Project, Tag 0CYZ].  Then the square

```
Y ∩ Z ⟶ Y
  ↓        ↓
  Z   ⟶ Y ∪ Z
```

of the four closed subspaces and the four inclusions is cocartesian in the category of algebraic
spaces over `S`, that is, `Y ∪ Z = Y ⨿_{Y ∩ Z} Z`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_desc_schemeTheoreticUnion` packaged as a colimit;
the square commutes because both composites are the inclusion of `Y ∩ Z` into `Y ∪ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_schemeTheoreticUnion (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (Y Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    IsPushout
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (Subfunctor.homOfLe (inf_le_left : Y.1 ⊓ Z.1 ≤ Y.1)) :
        closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (schemeTheoreticIntersection B S hS X.1 X.2 Y Z) ⟶
          closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Y)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (Subfunctor.homOfLe (inf_le_right : Y.1 ⊓ Z.1 ≤ Z.1)) :
        closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (schemeTheoreticIntersection B S hS X.1 X.2 Y Z) ⟶
          closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z)
      (ObjectProperty.homMk
          (Subfunctor.homOfLe (le_schemeTheoreticUnion_left B S hS X.2 Y Z)) :
        closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Y ⟶
          closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (schemeTheoreticUnion B S hS X.1 X.2 Y Z))
      (ObjectProperty.homMk
          (Subfunctor.homOfLe (le_schemeTheoreticUnion_right B S hS X.2 Y Z)) :
        closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z ⟶
          closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (schemeTheoreticUnion B S hS X.1 X.2 Y Z))
declarations.comment: the square of the two subspaces, their scheme-theoretic intersection and their scheme-theoretic union is cocartesian in the category of algebraic spaces over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_le_schemeTheoreticUnion_left
declarations.doc:
The first of two closed subspaces of an algebraic space over `S` is a
closed subspace of their scheme-theoretic union.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_le_schemeTheoreticUnion_left (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (Y Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS F) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS
      (Subfunctor.homOfLe (le_schemeTheoreticUnion_left B S hS hF Y Z))
declarations.comment: closed immersion of the first subspace into the union

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_le_schemeTheoreticUnion_right
declarations.doc:
The second of two closed subspaces of an algebraic space over `S` is a
closed subspace of their scheme-theoretic union.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_le_schemeTheoreticUnion_right (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (Y Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS F) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS
      (Subfunctor.homOfLe (le_schemeTheoreticUnion_right B S hS hF Y Z))
declarations.comment: closed immersion of the second subspace into the union

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_coproduct
declarations.doc:
Let `F i ⟶ Y`, for `i` in a finite index type, be finite morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S`, and let `G` be their coproduct as a sheaf of sets on the big fppf site of `S`, given by a
colimit cofan. Then the induced morphism `G ⟶ Y` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_coproduct {I : Type v} [Finite I]
    (F : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (F i)) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (G : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (ι : ∀ i, (⟨F i, (hF i).isSheaf⟩ :
      Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)) ⟶ G)
    (hG : IsColimit (Cofan.mk G ι))
    (fᵢ : ∀ i, F i ⟶ Y) (f : G.obj ⟶ Y) (hf : ∀ i, (ι i).hom ≫ f = fᵢ i)
    (hfin : ∀ i, IsFinite B S hS (fᵢ i)) :
    IsFinite B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdealInt
declarations.doc:
**The `k`-th Fitting ideal sheaf of an `𝒪_F`-module, for `k : ℤ`**: the smallest sheaf of
ideals of `𝒪_F` whose sections over every affine étale chart contain the module-theoretic `k`-th
Fitting ideal of the sections of the module there.

For `k < 0` the chartwise ideal is zero, so `Fit₋₁(G) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fittingIdealInt (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) (k : ℤ) :
    (SheafOfModules.unit
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))).Submodule
declarations.comment: the chain Fit_k, k : ℤ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdealInt_obj_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ3: over an affine étale chart the sections of `Fit_k(G)` are exactly the
module-theoretic `k`-th Fitting ideal of the sections of `G` over the chart ring.**

One inclusion is the defining property of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdealInt`; the other
holds because the sections restricting into the chartwise Fitting ideals already form a sheaf of
ideals containing them, so the infimum is below it.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdealInt_obj_eq (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF)
    (hG : IsCartesianOnAffineCharts G)
    (hfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS F,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS F hF W) (G.val.obj (op W)))
    (k : ℤ) {U : SmallEtale B S hS F}
    (hU : IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) :
    (fittingIdealInt B S hS F hF G k).toSubmodule.obj (op U) =
      @_root_.fittingIdeal (chartRing B S hS F hF U) _ (G.val.obj (op U)) _ _ (hfin U hU) k
declarations.comment: the chartwise characterisation of the sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdeal_obj_eq_fittingIdealOnChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ3 for the `ℕ`-indexed Fitting ideal sheaf**: over an affine étale chart the
sections of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdeal` are exactly the chartwise Fitting ideal of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdealOnChart`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_obj_eq_fittingIdealOnChart (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF)
    (hG : IsCartesianOnAffineCharts G)
    (hfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS F,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS F hF W) (G.val.obj (op W)))
    (r : ℕ) {U : SmallEtale B S hS F}
    (hU : IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)) :
    (fittingIdeal B S hS F hF G r).toSubmodule.obj (op U) =
      @fittingIdealOnChart B S hS F hF G r U (hfin U hU)
declarations.comment: the chartwise characterisation, in nonnegative degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdealInt_eq_bot_of_lt_zero
declarations.doc:
**`Fit₋₁(G) = 0`, and more generally the Fitting ideal sheaves vanish in negative degree**: in
negative degree the chartwise Fitting ideal is zero, so every sheaf of ideals belongs to the
family whose infimum defines `Fit_k(G)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdealInt_eq_bot_of_lt_zero (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) {k : ℤ} (hk : k < 0) :
    fittingIdealInt B S hS F hF G k = ⊥

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.monotone_fittingIdealInt
declarations.doc:
**The chain of Fitting ideal sheaves increases.**  A sheaf of ideals whose sections over every
affine étale chart contain the chartwise `Fit_l` contains the chartwise `Fit_k` there too, for
`k ≤ l`, so the family whose infimum is `Fit_l(G)` is contained in the family for `Fit_k(G)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem monotone_fittingIdealInt (G : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) :
    Monotone fun k : ℤ => fittingIdealInt B S hS F hF G k
declarations.comment: the chain increases

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdealInt_chain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ3.**  For a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `G` on an algebraic space `X`
the Fitting ideals form an increasing chain `0 = Fit₋₁(G) ⊆ Fit₀(G) ⊆ … ⊆ 𝒪_X` of sheaves of
ideals, characterised by: over every affine étale chart `U` the sections of `Fit_k(G)` are the
module-theoretic `k`-th Fitting ideal of the sections `G(U)` over the chart ring `𝒪_X(U)`.

The finiteness of the sections over every affine chart is the étale-local reading of finite type
used by the conventions of Stacks 0CZ3, under which the Fitting ideals are defined chartwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdealInt_chain (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS X.1 X.2 W) (G.val.obj (op W))) :
    fittingIdealInt B S hS X.1 X.2 G (-1) = ⊥ ∧
      Monotone (fun k : ℤ => fittingIdealInt B S hS X.1 X.2 G k) ∧
      (∀ k : ℤ, fittingIdealInt B S hS X.1 X.2 G k ≤ ⊤) ∧
      ∀ (k : ℤ) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
        (hU : IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)),
        (fittingIdealInt B S hS X.1 X.2 G k).toSubmodule.obj (op U) =
          @_root_.fittingIdeal (chartRing B S hS X.1 X.2 U) _ (G.val.obj (op U)) _ _
            (hfin U hU) k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdealPullback_eq_fittingIdeal
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces and let `G` be a finite type
quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module.  Then the ideal sheaf on `X` generated by the inverse image of the
`r`-th Fitting ideal sheaf of `G` is the `r`-th Fitting ideal sheaf of `f^*G`:
`f^{-1}Fit_r(G) · 𝒪_X = Fit_r(f^*G)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdealPullback_eq_fittingIdeal {f : X ⟶ Y} {G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2}
    (hqc : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hft : PresheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).J G.val)
    (r : ℕ) :
    fittingIdealPullback B S hS f G r =
      fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj G) r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal_fittingIdeal_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.doc:
For a finitely presented quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` on an algebraic space `X`, the `r`-th
Fitting ideal `Fit_r(ℱ)` is a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal_fittingIdeal_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite G) (r : ℕ) :
    IsFiniteTypeQuasicoherentIdeal B S hS X (fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_le_fittingClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ6, part (1).**  Let `G` be a finite type, quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `Z₀`
be the closed subspace of `X` cut out by `Fit_0(G)` and let `Z` be the scheme-theoretic support
of `G`.  Then `Z ⊆ Z₀ ⊆ X` as closed subspaces.

The scheme-theoretic support of Stacks 07U1 is a closed subspace by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedSubspace_schemeTheoreticSupport`.  It is the infimum of
the closed subspaces whose defining ideal sheaf annihilates `G`, and `Z₀` is one of them because
`Fit_0(G)` annihilates `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_le_fittingClosedSubspace
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G] (Z₀ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (cutOut : definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z₀ = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G 0) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X G) ∧
      schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X G ≤ Z₀.1
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_schemeTheoreticSupport_eq_supportOfSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ6, part (2).**  Let `G` be a finite type, quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `Z₀`
be the closed subspace of `X` cut out by `Fit_0(G)` and let `Z` be the scheme-theoretic support
of `G`.  Then `|Z| = |Z₀| = Supp(G)` as closed subsets of `|X|`.

The point set of a closed subspace is the zero locus of its defining ideal sheaf
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.range_pointsMap_ι_eq_idealZeroLocus`); the defining ideal sheaves of
`Z` and `Z₀` are the annihilator and `Fit_0(G)`.  The support lies in the zero locus of the
annihilator, which lies in the zero locus of `Fit_0(G)` because `Fit_0(G) ⊆ Ann(G)`, and the
latter is the support by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealZeroLocus_fittingIdeal_zero_eq_supportOfSheaf`.  The support is
closed by Stacks 07TZ.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_schemeTheoreticSupport_eq_supportOfSheaf
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G] (Z₀ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (cutOut : definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z₀ = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G 0) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X G).toFunctor
        (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X G).ι) =
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z₀.1.toFunctor Z₀.1.ι) ∧
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z₀.1.toFunctor Z₀.1.ι) =
        supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj G) ∧
      IsClosed (supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj G))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_module_on_fittingClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ6, part (3).**  Let `G` be a finite type, quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let
`Z₀` be the closed subspace of `X` cut out by `Fit_0(G)`.  Then there is a finite type,
quasi-coherent `𝒪_{Z₀}`-module `G₀` with `(Z₀ → X)_* G₀ ≅ G`.

The ideal cutting out `Z₀` is `Fit_0(G)`, which annihilates `G`, so the essential-image assertion
of Stacks 04CJ part (3) for the closed immersion `Z₀ → X`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentEssImagePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion`, produces the
quasi-coherent module; it is of finite type by Stacks 07U0 part (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_module_on_fittingClosedSubspace
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G] (Z₀ : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (cutOut : definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z₀ = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G 0) :
    ∃ G₀ : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z₀).1
        (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z₀).2,
      G₀.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧ SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G₀ ∧
        Nonempty ((modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z₀)).obj G₀ ≅
          G)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_fin_span_iff_fittingIdealGeometricStalk_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ7.**  Let `G` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module on an algebraic space
`X` and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X`.  Then `G` can be generated by `r` elements on an
affine étale neighbourhood of `x̄` if and only if the stalk `Fit_r(G)_{x̄}` of its `r`-th Fitting
ideal is the whole étale local ring `𝒪_{X, x̄}`.

The finiteness of the sections over every affine étale chart is the étale-local reading of
finite type used by the conventions of Stacks 0CZ3, under which the Fitting ideals are defined
chartwise; `hG` is the cartesian property of Stacks 03DX, which a quasi-coherent module has by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCartesianOnAffineCharts_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_span_iff_fittingIdealGeometricStalk_eq_top
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (hG : IsCartesianOnAffineCharts G)
    (hfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS F,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS F hF W) (G.val.obj (op W)))
    (r : ℕ) (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) :
    (∃ U : SmallEtaleNeighborhood x,
        IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U.chart) ∧
          ∃ s : Fin r → G.val.obj (op U.chart),
            Submodule.span (chartRing B S hS F hF U.chart) (Set.range s) = ⊤) ↔
      fittingIdealGeometricStalk G r x = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_tfae_fittingIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CZ8.**  Let `F` be an algebraic space and let `G` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_F`-module on its small étale site.  For every `r`, the following are equivalent: `G` is
finite locally free of rank `r`; its `(r-1)`-st Fitting ideal sheaf vanishes and its `r`-th is
the unit ideal sheaf; its Fitting ideal sheaves vanish below `r` and are the unit ideal sheaf
from `r` onward.

The condition at index `r - 1` is read with truncated subtraction and is therefore guarded by the
disjunct `r = 0`, under which it is vacuous.  No finite type hypothesis is needed; see the
implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_tfae_fittingIdeal
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (r : ℕ) :
    List.TFAE [
      RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF) G r,
      (r = 0 ∨ fittingIdeal B S hS F hF G (r - 1) = ⊥) ∧
        fittingIdeal B S hS F hF G r = ⊤,
      (∀ k < r, fittingIdeal B S hS F hF G k = ⊥) ∧
        (∀ k, r ≤ k → fittingIdeal B S hS F hF G k = ⊤)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_fittingClosedSubspaces
declarations.doc:
**The closed subspaces cut out by the Fitting ideals of an `𝒪_X`-module.**  If every Fitting
ideal sheaf of `G` is quasi-coherent, there is a decreasing chain of closed subspaces of `X` whose
defining ideal sheaves are the Fitting ideals of `G`.  This is the chain
`X ⊇ Z_0 ⊇ Z_1 ⊇ …` of Stacks 0CZ9.

Each subspace comes from the surjectivity half of Stacks 03MB,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_definingIdealSheaf_eq_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, and the chain
decreases because the Fitting ideals increase and the correspondence of Stacks 03MB reverses
inclusions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fittingClosedSubspaces (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hqc : ∀ r : ℕ,
      (fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ∃ Z : ℕ → ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      (∀ r, definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (Z r) = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r) ∧
        Antitone fun r ↦ (Z r).1
declarations.comment: the decreasing chain of closed subspaces cut out by the Fitting ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iInf_fittingClosedSubspace_eq_sheafify_bot
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 0CZ9: the intersection of the Fitting closed subspaces is the empty
algebraic space.**  For a chain of closed subspaces of `X` whose defining ideal sheaves are the
Fitting ideals of `G`, the intersection of the chain is the sheafification of the bottom
subfunctor, as soon as the sections of `G` over every affine étale chart form a finite module.

The intersection has no points, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iInter_range_pointsMap_ι_fittingClosedSubspace_eq_empty`, and an
inclusion into the empty open subspace is detected on points by Stacks 03BZ; the reverse inclusion
holds for any family of subsheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem iInf_fittingClosedSubspace_eq_sheafify_bot
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (Z : ℕ → ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hZ : ∀ r, definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (Z r) = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r)
    (hfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS X.1 X.2 W) (G.val.obj (op W))) :
    (⨅ r : ℕ, (Z r).1) = (⊥ : Subfunctor X.1).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: (1) the intersection is empty; (2), (3) and finite presentation not covered

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_fittingClosedSubspaces_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZ9.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf
site `B` and let `G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type.  The Fitting ideal sheaves
of `G` cut out a decreasing chain of closed subspaces `X = Z_{-1} ⊇ Z_0 ⊇ Z_1 ⊇ …` such that

1. the intersection of the `Z_r` is empty;
2. for every algebraic space `T ⟶ X` the module `G_T` is locally generated by at most `r`
   sections exactly when `T ⟶ X` factors, necessarily uniquely, through `X ∖ Z_r`;
3. for every algebraic space `T ⟶ X` the module `G_T` is finite locally free of rank `r`
   exactly when `T ⟶ X` factors, necessarily uniquely, through `Z_{r-1} ∖ Z_r`;

and, if `G` is moreover of finite presentation, the three morphisms `Z_r ⟶ X`, `X ∖ Z_r ⟶ X` and
`Z_{r-1} ∖ Z_r ⟶ X` are of finite presentation.

The chain is the one cut out by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingIdeal`, the test objects of
clauses (2) and (3) are arbitrary algebraic spaces rather than only schemes over `X`, and
`Z_{r-1} ∖ Z_r` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fittingRankStratum`, which for `r = 0` is
`X ∖ Z_0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fittingClosedSubspaces_spec (hGqc : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hGft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G) :
    ∃ Z : ℕ → ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      (∀ r, definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (Z r) = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r) ∧
      (Antitone fun r ↦ (Z r).1) ∧
      (⨅ r : ℕ, (Z r).1) = (⊥ : Subfunctor X.1).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
      (∀ (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (r : ℕ) (f : T ⟶ X),
        (∀ x : points B S hS T.1, ∃ (U : SmallEtale B S hS T.1)
            (s : Fin r → ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj G).val.obj (op U)),
            IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS T.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
              Submodule.span (chartRing B S hS T.1 T.2 U) (Set.range s) = ⊤ ∧
                x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS
                  (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS T.1).obj U)) U.1.hom)) ↔
          ∃! g : T.1 ⟶ (openComplement B S hS (Z r).1).toFunctor,
            g ≫ (openComplement B S hS (Z r).1).ι = f.hom) ∧
      (∀ (T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (r : ℕ) (f : T ⟶ X),
        RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS T.1 T.2)
            ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj G) r ↔
          ∃! g : T.1 ⟶ (fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r).toFunctor,
            g ≫ (fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r).ι = f.hom) ∧
      (SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite G → ∀ r : ℕ,
        IsFinitePresentation B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X (Z r)).hom ∧
          IsFinitePresentation B S hS (openComplement B S hS (Z r).1).ι ∧
            IsFinitePresentation B S hS (fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r).ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyClosedSubspace_and_disjoint_fittingRankStratum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZA, the Fitting rank strata.**  Let `G` be an `𝒪_X`-module and let
`X ⊇ Z_0 ⊇ Z_1 ⊇ …` be closed subspaces of `X` whose defining ideal sheaves are the Fitting
ideals of `G`, as in Stacks 0CZ9.  Then the strata `X_r = Z_{r-1} \ Z_r`, with the convention
`Z_{-1} = X`, are locally closed subspaces of `X`, and distinct strata are disjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyClosedSubspace_and_disjoint_fittingRankStratum
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (Z : ℕ → ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hZ : ∀ r, definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (Z r) = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r) :
    (∀ r : ℕ, IsLocallyClosedSubspace B S hS (fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r)) ∧
      ∀ r s : ℕ, r ≠ s →
        fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r ⊓ fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z s ≤
          (⊥ : Subfunctor X.1).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: the strata X_r = Z_{r-1} \ Z_r are disjoint locally closed subspaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_fittingRankStratum_index
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZA, the Fitting rank strata cover `X`.**  Every point of `X` lies in exactly one
Fitting rank stratum `X_r = Z_{r-1} \ Z_r`: there is a unique `r` with the point outside `Z_r`
and inside every earlier member of the chain.

The input is clause (1) of Stacks 0CZ9,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iInter_range_pointsMap_ι_fittingClosedSubspace_eq_empty`: the point
sets of the Fitting closed subspaces have empty intersection, so every point leaves the chain,
and it does so at a unique index because the chain decreases.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_fittingRankStratum_index (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (Z : ℕ → ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hZ : ∀ r, definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (Z r) = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r)
    (hfin : ∀ W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
      IsAffine ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1 ⋙ BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj W) →
        Module.Finite (chartRing B S hS X.1 X.2 W) (G.val.obj (op W)))
    (x : points B S hS X.1) :
    ∃! r : ℕ, x ∉ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (Z r).1.toFunctor (Z r).1.ι) ∧
      ∀ k < r, x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (Z k).1.toFunctor (Z k).1.ι)
declarations.comment: every point of X lies in exactly one stratum X_r = Z_{r-1} \ Z_r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_fittingRankStratification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZA, the disjoint union of the Fitting rank strata.**  The disjoint union
`X' = ∐_{r ≥ 0} X_r` of the strata `X_r = Z_{r-1} \ Z_r` of a chain `X ⊇ Z_0 ⊇ Z_1 ⊇ …` of closed
subspaces of `X` is an algebraic space over `S`, and its structural morphism restricts on the
`r`-th summand to the inclusion of `X_r` in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_fittingRankStratification (Z : ℕ → ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (fittingRankStratification B S hS X Z).obj ∧
      ∀ r : ℕ, Sigma.ι (fun k : ℕ ↦ fittingRankStratumSpace B S hS X Z k) r ≫
          fittingRankStratificationHom B S hS X Z = fittingRankStratumHom B S hS X Z r
declarations.comment: X' = ∐_{r ≥ 0} X_r is an algebraic space, with its morphism to X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_fittingRankStratification_flat_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZA.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf
site `B` and let `G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.  Then the Fitting
ideal sheaves of `G` cut out a decreasing chain of closed subspaces
`X = Z_{-1} ⊇ Z_0 ⊇ Z_1 ⊇ …` with empty intersection, the strata `X_r = Z_{r-1} ∖ Z_r` are
pairwise disjoint locally closed subspaces of `X` and every point of `X` lies in exactly one of
them, the disjoint union `X' = ∐_{r ≥ 0} X_r` is an algebraic space over `S` whose structural
morphism restricts on the `r`-th summand to the inclusion of `X_r`, and

1. `X'` **represents the functor** sending a test object `f : h_T ⟶ X` of the site to a
   one-point set when `G_T` is flat over `T` in the sense of Stacks 05VV and to the empty set
   otherwise;
2. the pullback of `G` to `X_r` is finite locally free of rank `r`;
3. both `X_r ⟶ X` and `X' ⟶ X` are of finite presentation.

The hypotheses are exactly the ones Stacks 0CZA makes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fittingRankStratification_flat_spec (hGqc : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hGfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite G) :
    ∃ Z : ℕ → ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      (∀ r, definingIdealSheaf B S hS X (Z r) = fittingIdeal B S hS X.1 X.2 G r) ∧
      (Antitone fun r ↦ (Z r).1) ∧
      (⨅ r : ℕ, (Z r).1) = (⊥ : Subfunctor X.1).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, IsLocallyClosedSubspace B S hS (fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r)) ∧
      (∀ r s : ℕ, r ≠ s →
        fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r ⊓ fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z s ≤
          (⊥ : Subfunctor X.1).sheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) ∧
      (∀ x : points B S hS X.1, ∃! r : ℕ,
        x ∉ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (Z r).1.toFunctor (Z r).1.ι) ∧
          ∀ k < r, x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (Z k).1.toFunctor (Z k).1.ι)) ∧
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (fittingRankStratification B S hS X Z).obj ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, Sigma.ι (fun k : ℕ ↦ fittingRankStratumSpace B S hS X Z k) r ≫
          fittingRankStratificationHom B S hS X Z = fittingRankStratumHom B S hS X Z r) ∧
      (∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : schemeSpace T ⟶ X),
        IsFlatOver B S hS (schemeSpace T).2
            (𝟙 (schemeSpace T) : schemeSpace T ⟶ schemeSpace T).hom
            ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj G) ↔
          ∃! h : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (fittingRankStratification B S hS X Z).1,
            h ≫ (fittingRankStratificationHom B S hS X Z).hom = f.hom) ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (fittingRankStratumSpace B S hS X Z r).1
          (fittingRankStratumSpace B S hS X Z r).2)
        ((modulePullback B S hS (fittingRankStratumHom B S hS X Z r)).obj G) r) ∧
      (∀ r : ℕ, IsFinitePresentation B S hS (fittingRankStratum B S hS X Z r).ι) ∧
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS (fittingRankStratificationHom B S hS X Z).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_tfae_isProper_closedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 0CZC fails without local finite type** (the remark after Definition 0CZD, Section
0CZB). Over every big fppf site there are a scheme `S`, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces
over `S` which is not locally of finite type, and a closed subset `T ⊆ |X|` for which the three
conditions of Lemma 0CZC are not equivalent: (1) the reduced induced closed subspace on `T` is
proper over `Y`, (2) some closed subspace with points `T` is, (3) every one is.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_tfae_isProper_closedSubspace (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) :
    ∃ (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
      (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T),
      ¬ IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∧
      ¬ [IsProper B S hS ((reducedClosedSubspace B S hS X hX T hT).ι ≫ f),
          ∃ (Z : Subfunctor X) (_ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z),
            Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.toFunctor Z.ι) = T ∧ IsProper B S hS (Z.ι ≫ f),
          ∀ (Z : Subfunctor X) (_ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z),
            Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.toFunctor Z.ι) = T →
              IsProper B S hS (Z.ι ≫ f)].TFAE
declarations.comment: the remark after Definition 0CZD: Lemma 0CZC is false if f is not locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_reducedClosedSubspace_iff_exists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZC, conditions (1) and (2).** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` locally
of finite type and a closed set `T` of points of the source, the reduced induced closed subspace
on `T` is proper over the target exactly when some closed subspace with set of points `T` is
proper over the target.

The forward implication must exhibit a closed subspace with set of points `T`, which is the
existence clause of Stacks 03IQ. That clause is now available unconditionally: the reduced
induced subspace *is* a closed subspace by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedSubspace_reducedClosedSubspace_of_closedImmersionDescent`
applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isClosedImmersion`, which is
Stacks 02W8 at the closed immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_reducedClosedSubspace_iff_exists (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T) :
    IsProperOver B S hS hX hY f hf T hT ↔
      ∃ (Z : Subfunctor X) (_ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z),
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.toFunctor Z.ι) = T ∧ IsProper B S hS (Z.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isProper_closedSubspace_iff_forall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZC, conditions (2) and (3).** If one closed subspace with a given closed set of
points is proper over the target, then every closed subspace with that set of points is.

The implication from (3) to (2) must exhibit a closed subspace with set of points `T`, which is
the existence clause of Stacks 03IQ. That clause is now available unconditionally: the reduced
induced subspace *is* a closed subspace by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedSubspace_reducedClosedSubspace_of_closedImmersionDescent`
applied to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isClosedImmersion`, which is
Stacks 02W8 at the closed immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_closedSubspace_iff_forall (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T) :
    (∃ (Z : Subfunctor X) (_ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z),
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.toFunctor Z.ι) = T ∧ IsProper B S hS (Z.ι ≫ f)) ↔
      ∀ (Z : Subfunctor X) (_ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z),
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.toFunctor Z.ι) = T → IsProper B S hS (Z.ι ≫ f)
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZD.** A closed subset of the points of an algebraic space `X` is *proper over
`Y`* when the reduced induced closed subspace of `X` supported on it is proper over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsProperOver (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (_hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (_hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (T : Set (points B S hS X))
    (hT : IsClosed T) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperOver_of_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZE.** A closed subset of a closed subset proper over the base is proper over the
base.

The reduced closed subspace on the smaller set is a subfunctor of the one on the larger set, so
the inclusion between them is a closed immersion and hence proper; composing with properness
over `Y` of the larger one gives the result.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_of_subset (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (T' T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT' : _root_.IsClosed T') (hT : _root_.IsClosed T)
    (hsub : T' ⊆ T) (hproper : IsProperOver B S hS hX hY f hf T hT) :
    IsProperOver B S hS hX hY f hf T' hT'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperOver_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZF, properness.** In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right
vertical morphism is locally of finite type, the inverse image of a closed subset proper over
the base is proper over the new base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_preimage {X' X Y' Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hproper : IsProperOver B S hS X.property Y.property f.hom hf T hT) :
    IsProperOver B S hS X'.property Y'.property f'.hom
      ((isLocallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS).of_isPullback sq hf)
      (pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom ⁻¹' T)
      (isClosed_preimage_pointsMap B S hS X'.property X.property g'.hom hT)
declarations.comment: properness

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_preimage_pointsMap
registrations.comment: closedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_image_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZG, closedness of the image under a universally closed morphism.** A universally
closed morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` carries closed subsets of its space of points to
closed subsets: it is closed, by Stacks 03HI.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_image_of_universallyClosed (_hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T) :
    IsClosed (pointsMap B S hS X f '' T)
declarations.comment: image_universally_closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperOver_image_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZG, properness of the image under a universally closed morphism.** The image of a
closed subset proper over the base under a universally closed morphism is proper over the base.

The restriction of a universally closed morphism to the reduced induced subspace is universally
closed, the inclusion of that subspace being universally closed, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_ι_comp_of_universallyClosed_ι_comp` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_image_of_universallyClosed (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hA : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS A)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ A) (hf : UniversallyClosed B S hS f)
    (hXft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hYft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTproper : IsProperOver B S hS hX hA (f ≫ g) hXft T hT) :
    IsProperOver B S hS hY hA g hYft (pointsMap B S hS X f '' T)
      (isClosed_image_of_universallyClosed B S hS hX hY f hf T hT)
declarations.comment: image_universally_closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_image_of_isProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZG, closedness of the image in a separated target.** If the structure morphism of
`Y` is separated and the closed subset `T` of the points of `X` is proper over the base, then the
image of `T` in the points of `Y` is closed.

The reduced induced subspace on `T` is universally closed over the base, so its morphism to `Y`
is universally closed by Stacks 04NX, the structure morphism of `Y` being separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_image_of_isProperOver (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hA : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS A)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (pX : X ⟶ A) (pY : Y ⟶ A) (hcomm : f ≫ pY = pX)
    (hpX : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pX) (_hpY : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pY)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS pY)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hproper : IsProperOver B S hS hX hA pX hpX T hT) :
    IsClosed (pointsMap B S hS X f '' T)
declarations.comment: image_separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperOver_image_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZG, properness of the image in a separated target.** The image in `Y` of a closed
subset of `X` proper over the base is proper over the base when the structure morphism of `Y` is
separated.

As for closedness, the reduced induced subspace on `T` is universally closed over `Y` by
Stacks 04NX, so `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_ι_comp_of_universallyClosed_ι_comp` applies. The
closedness of the image is an explicit hypothesis, as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsProperOver` is a
predicate on closed subsets.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_image_of_isSeparated (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hA : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS A)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (pX : X ⟶ A) (pY : Y ⟶ A) (hcomm : f ≫ pY = pX)
    (hpX : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pX) (hpY : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS pY)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS pY)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hproper : IsProperOver B S hS hX hA pX hpX T hT)
    (hImage : IsClosed (pointsMap B S hS X f '' T)) :
    IsProperOver B S hS hY hA pY hpY (pointsMap B S hS X f '' T) hImage
declarations.comment: image_separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperOver_preimage_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZG, properness of the inverse image.** The inverse image of a closed subset
proper over the base under a proper morphism is proper over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_preimage_of_isProper (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hA : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS A)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ A) (hf : IsProper B S hS f)
    (hXft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hYft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (T : Set (points B S hS Y)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTproper : IsProperOver B S hS hY hA g hYft T hT) :
    IsProperOver B S hS hX hA (f ≫ g) hXft (pointsMap B S hS X f ⁻¹' T)
      (isClosed_preimage_pointsMap B S hS hX hY f hT)
declarations.comment: inverse_image_proper

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperOver_iUnion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZH.** A finite union of closed subsets of the points of `X`, each proper over
`Y`, is proper over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_iUnion {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (T : ι → Set (points B S hS X))
    (hT : ∀ i, IsClosed (T i))
    (hproper : ∀ i, IsProperOver B S hS hX hY f hf (T i) (hT i)) :
    IsProperOver B S hS hX hY f hf (⋃ i, T i) (isClosed_iUnion_of_finite hT)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZI.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite type and let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  The following
are equivalent:

1. the support of `F` is proper over `Y`;
2. the scheme-theoretic support of `F`, Stacks 07U1, is proper over `Y`;
3. there are a closed subspace `Z ⊆ X` and a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `G` with
   `Z → Y` proper and `(Z → X)_* G = F`.

The support of `F` is closed by Stacks 07TZ, so Definition 0CZD applies to it; the
scheme-theoretic support is a closed subspace whose set of points is that support by Stacks 07U0
part (4), so (1) and (2) agree by Stacks 0CZC, which says that properness over the base of a
closed subspace depends only on its set of points.  (2) implies (3) by the existence clause of
Stacks 07U0, together with part (3) of the same lemma for finite type of the module.  (3)
implies (1) because the support of `F` is contained in the set of points of `Z`, which is proper
over `Y` by Stacks 0CZC, so Stacks 0CZE applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperSupport_tfae (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (hft : PresheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).J F.val) :
    List.TFAE
      [HasProperSupport B S hS X.2 Y.2 f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F),
        IsProper B S hS ((schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).ι ≫ f),
        ∃ (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
          (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).1
            (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).2),
          G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧ SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G ∧
            IsProper B S hS (Z.1.ι ≫ f) ∧
            Nonempty ((modulePushforward B S hS
              (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj G ≅ F)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProperOver_supportOfSheaf_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` whose right vertical morphism `f` is
locally of finite type, the support of the pullback along the upper horizontal morphism of a
finite type, quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose support is proper over `Y` is proper over `Y'`.
It takes the quasi-coherence of `F` (`_hqc`), its finite type (`hft`) and the properness of its
support over `Y` (`hproper`) as hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperOver_supportOfSheaf_modulePullback {X' X Y' Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (_hqc : SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite F)
    (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (hproper : IsProperOver B S hS X.property Y.property f.hom hf
      (supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F))
      (letI := hft; isClosed_supportOfSheaf_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite B S hS X.1 X.property F)) :
    IsProperOver B S hS X'.property Y'.property f'.hom
      ((isLocallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange B S hS).of_isPullback sq hf)
      (supportOfSheaf B S hS X'.1
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F)))
      (isClosed_supportOfSheaf_modulePullback B S hS g' F hft)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZK, part (1), the quotient clause.** A quotient of an `𝒪_X`-module of finite
type whose support is proper over `Y` again has support proper over `Y`.

The quotient is of finite type by Stacks 03DL(5), so its support is closed by Stacks 07TZ; an
epimorphism of sheaves of modules is a local surjection, so that support is contained in the
support of the source by Stacks 04KB(5); and a closed subset of a closed subset proper over the
base is proper over the base by Stacks 0CZE.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperSupport_of_epi (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX} (p : M ⟶ N) [Epi p]
    (hMft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite M)
    (hM : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj M)) :
    HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj N)
declarations.comment: part (1), quotients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_toSheaf_of_sectionwiseSplit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZK, part (1), the direct sum clause.** A direct sum of two `𝒪_X`-modules whose
supports are proper over `Y` again has support proper over `Y`.

The support of a module is the support of its underlying abelian sheaf, and the two inclusions,
the two projections and the three identities they satisfy on sections carry over to the
underlying abelian sheaves unchanged, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_of_sectionwiseSplit` read off the sections of the
modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperSupport_toSheaf_of_sectionwiseSplit (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    {P M N : Modules.{u, v} B S hS X hX}
    (i₁ : M ⟶ P) (i₂ : N ⟶ P) (p₁ : P ⟶ M) (p₂ : P ⟶ N)
    (hi₁ : ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (σ : M.val.obj (op U)),
      p₁.val.app (op U) (i₁.val.app (op U) σ) = σ)
    (hi₂ : ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (σ : N.val.obj (op U)),
      p₂.val.app (op U) (i₂.val.app (op U) σ) = σ)
    (htotal : ∀ (U : SmallEtale B S hS X) (τ : P.val.obj (op U)),
      i₁.val.app (op U) (p₁.val.app (op U) τ) +
        i₂.val.app (op U) (p₂.val.app (op U) τ) = τ)
    (hM : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj M))
    (hN : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj N)) :
    HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj P)
declarations.comment: part (1), direct sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_X₂_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZK, part (1), the extension clause.**  An extension of `𝒪_X`-modules whose
supports are proper over `Y` again has support proper over `Y`: the middle term of a short exact
sequence of `𝒪_X`-modules whose outer terms have support proper over `Y` has support proper
over `Y`.

The support of the middle term is *exactly* the union of the supports of the outer two.  It is
contained in that union by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_middle_subset_union`; it contains the support of the
first term because the first map is a monomorphism and the support of the third because the
second map is an epimorphism, hence a local surjection, which are the two halves of Stacks
04KB.  So the support is closed, being a union of two closed supports, and a finite union of
closed subsets proper over `Y` is proper over `Y` by Stacks 0CZH.

No finiteness hypothesis appears: as for a direct sum, the containment of supports is an
equality, so closedness of the support of the extension comes from the two given supports and
not from the finite type closure of Stacks 05VR.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperSupport_X₂_of_shortExact (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    {T : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)} (hT : T.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj T.X₁))
    (h₃ : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj T.X₃)) :
    HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj T.X₂)
declarations.comment: part (1), extensions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZK, part (1), the cokernel clause.**  The cokernel of a map `u : M ⟶ N` of
`𝒪_X`-modules whose target is of finite type and has support proper over `Y` again has support
proper over `Y`.

The cokernel is a quotient of `N`, so this is the quotient clause
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_of_epi`.  Stacks 0CZK assumes proper support of both
`M` and `N`; the source of `u` plays no part.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperSupport_cokernel (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX} (u : M ⟶ N)
    (hNft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite N)
    (hN : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj N)) :
    HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
      (cokernel (C := Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) u))
declarations.comment: part (1), cokernels

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_abelianImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZK, part (1), the image clause.**  The image of a map `u : M ⟶ N` of
`𝒪_X`-modules whose source is of finite type and has support proper over `Y` again has support
proper over `Y`.

`CategoryTheory.Abelian.coimage u` is by definition `cokernel (kernel.ι u)`, hence a quotient of
`M`, so it has support proper over `Y` by the quotient clause
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_of_epi`; and
`CategoryTheory.Abelian.coimageIsoImage` identifies it with the image, whose support is
therefore the same by Stacks 04KB.  Stacks 0CZK assumes proper support of both `M` and `N`; the
target of `u` plays no part.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProperSupport_abelianImage (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX} (u : M ⟶ N)
    (hMft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite M)
    (hM : HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj M)) :
    HasProperSupport B S hS hX hY f hf ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
      (Abelian.image (C := Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) u))
declarations.comment: part (1), images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSerreClass_isCoherentProperOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZK, part (2).**  The coherent `𝒪_X`-modules whose support is proper over `Y`
form a Serre subcategory of the abelian category `Coh(𝒪_X)` of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules.

The property is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentProperOver`, the one cutting out the source
of equation 76.42.5.1, and the abelian structure on `Coh(𝒪_X)` is Stacks 07UC in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coherentModules_abelian_of_closure`, which needs no locally Noetherian
hypothesis in this tree; the hypothesis of the source is therefore absent.

By Stacks 02MP it is enough to exhibit one object with the property and to show that the middle
term of an exact sequence whose outer terms have the property has it.  The zero module has
empty support.  For the exactness condition: the kernel `K` of `T.X₂ ⟶ T.X₃`, formed in the
ambient category of all `𝒪_X`-modules, is a quotient of `T.X₁` because the sequence is exact,
so it has support proper over `Y` by the quotient clause of part (1); the support of `T.X₂` is
contained in the union of the support of `K` and the support of `T.X₃`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_subset_union_kernel`; and the support of `T.X₂` is
closed because a coherent module is of finite type, by Stacks 07TZ.  Stacks 0CZH and 0CZE then
finish, in the form `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasProperSupport_of_subset_union`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSerreClass_isCoherentProperOver (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    letI : Abelian (CoherentModules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) :=
      coherentModules_abelian_of_closure B S hS X hX
    (isCoherentProperOver B S hS hX hY f hf).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: part (2), the Serre subcategory; the locally Noetherian hypothesis on Y is absent because the abelian structure on Coh(O_X) is Stacks 07UC in the hypothesis-free form `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coherentModules_abelian_of_closure`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor
declarations.doc:
The finite-presentation subfunctor `Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y} : (Sch/Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Sets` of the functor of
quotients: its value at a test scheme `T` is the subset of `Q_{F/X/Y}(T)` of those quotients that
are of finite presentation as `𝒪_{X_T}`-modules, and its action on a morphism of test schemes is
pullback of quotients.
declarations.statement: def finitePresentationQuotientsFunctor : (SchemesOver D.Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the finite-presentation subfunctor Q^{fp}_{F/X/Y} of the functor of quotients

declarations.name: fittingIdeal_strictTransform_affineBlowup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0CZM.** Let `M` be a finite module over a commutative ring `R`, and let `I` be
its `k`th Fitting ideal.  On the affine blowup chart `R[I/a]` associated to any `a ∈ I`, the
`k`th Fitting ideal of the strict transform of `M` — the quotient of `R[I/a] ⊗[R] M` by its
`a`-power torsion — is the unit ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_strictTransform_affineBlowup_eq_top
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (k : ℕ) (a : R) (ha : a ∈ fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ))
    (S : Type w) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization.Away a S] :
    let I := fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ)
    let R' := affineBlowupAlgebra I a S
    let M' := (R' ⊗[R] M) ⧸
      Ideal.primaryComponent (R' ⊗[R] M)
        (Ideal.span {algebraMap R R' a})
    fittingIdeal (R := R') (M := M') (k : ℤ) = ⊤

declarations.name: isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_strictTransform_affineBlowup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0CZN.** Let `M` be a finite module over a commutative ring `R`, and let `I` be
its `k`th Fitting ideal.  Suppose that the localization of `M` at every prime outside `V(I)` is
free of rank `k`.  Then the strict transform of `M` on the affine blowup chart `R[I/a]`, for any
`a ∈ I`, is finite locally free of rank `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_strictTransform_affineBlowup
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (k : ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
      ¬ fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ) ≤ p →
        Nonempty ((Fin k → Localization.AtPrime p) ≃ₗ[Localization.AtPrime p]
          LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M))
    (a : R) (ha : a ∈ fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ))
    (S : Type w) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization.Away a S] :
    let I := fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ)
    let R' := affineBlowupAlgebra I a S
    let M' := (R' ⊗[R] M) ⧸
      Ideal.primaryComponent (R' ⊗[R] M)
        (Ideal.span {algebraMap R R' a})
    Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank R' M' k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransformSheaf_isGeneratedByNear
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CZP.** The strict transform of a finite type quasi-coherent module on
the blowup of its `k`-th Fitting ideal is locally generated by at most `k` sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictTransformSheaf_isGeneratedByNear
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (k : ℕ) (s : Stacks.StrictTransform.baseChange (𝟙 S)
      (blowUpToBase (fittingIdeal F (k : ℤ)))) :
    IsGeneratedByNear
      (Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf (𝟙 S) (blowUpToBase (fittingIdeal F (k : ℤ)))
        (exceptionalIdeal (fittingIdeal F (k : ℤ))) F)
      k s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_strictTransform_fittingBlowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CZQ.** Blowing up the `k`-th Fitting ideal and taking the strict
transform makes a generically rank-`k` module finite locally free of rank `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_strictTransform_fittingBlowUp
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (k : ℕ)
    (h : let I := fittingIdeal F (k : ℤ)
      let U : S.Opens := ⟨I.supportᶜ, I.support.isClosed.isOpen_compl⟩
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj F) k) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
      (Stacks.StrictTransform.sheaf (𝟙 S) (blowUpToBase (fittingIdeal F (k : ℤ)))
        (exceptionalIdeal (fittingIdeal F (k : ℤ))) F) k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isOpen_freeLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CZR (openness).** The locus of points at which a sheaf of modules on
a scheme is free of finite rank on a neighbourhood is open: the trivialising neighbourhood of a
point of the locus is contained in the locus.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_freeLocus {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) :
    IsOpen (freeLocus F)
declarations.comment: openness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.freeLocus_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0CZR (base change).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite presentation
and let `F` be a finitely presented `𝒪_X`-module flat over `S`. The formation of the locus of
points at which `F` is free of finite rank on a neighbourhood commutes with an arbitrary base
change `g : S' ⟶ S`: the locus of the pulled-back module is the preimage of the original locus
under the projection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem freeLocus_pullback {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver f.toLRSHom.toShHom F) (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    freeLocus ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F) =
      pullback.fst f g ⁻¹' freeLocus F
declarations.comment: base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Clause (4) of Stacks 0CZS in the small-étale-site reading of Stacks 0CZT.**  If a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `M` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of a geometric point `x̄`
of `X` in the Zariski-chart sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint` —
the source's own reading — then the image point of `x̄` lies in the finite-free étale locus
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleFiniteFreeLocus`, the locus of Stacks 0CZT.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (h : IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS xbar M) :
    xbar.image ∈ etaleFiniteFreeLocus B S hS M
declarations.comment: clause (4) in the SMALL-ETALE-SITE reading: the source's Zariski-chart reading of clause (4) at a geometric point xbar implies that the image point of xbar lies in the locus of points of |X| admitting an etale morphism of algebraic spaces a : V -> X through them along which the inverse image of F is finite free in the sense of 03DE(2), which is the locus of Stacks 0CZT

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) implies clause (4), in the small-étale-site reading of Stacks 0CZT.**  Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation, let `M` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite
presentation on charts and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X`.  If `M` is flat at `x` over `Y`
and the geometric fibre stalk `(M_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a flat `𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module, then the image point
of `x̄` lies in the finite-free étale locus of Stacks 0CZT.  The fibre stalk and its base ring are
in the quotient form `M_{x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} M_{x̄}` over `𝒪_{X, x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} 𝒪_{X, x̄}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 M)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f M xbar)
    (hfibre : Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f M xbar)) :
    xbar.image ∈ etaleFiniteFreeLocus B S hS M
declarations.comment: (1) implies (4) with clause (4) in the SMALL-ETALE-SITE reading, i.e. membership in the locus of Stacks 0CZT; the fibre stalk and its base ring are in the QUOTIENT FORM M_xbar / m_ybar M_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar}, whose identification with the stalk on the geometric fibre X_ybar is condition (2) of Stacks 05WY and is not available

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_geometricFibre_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint
