declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (4) implies (3).**  If a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `M` is finite free in an
étale neighbourhood of a geometric point `x̄` of `X` — clause (4), in the source's Zariski-chart
reading — then the inverse image of `M` to the geometric fibre `X_ȳ` through `x̄` is finite free in
an étale neighbourhood of the lift of `x̄` to that fibre, which is clause (3).

The source calls this implication immediate, and so it is: clause (4) puts `x` in the finite-free
étale locus of `M` on `|X|`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint`), and that
locus only grows under an inverse image, the lift of `x̄` lying over `x̄` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap_geometricFibreToSource_geometricFibrePoint`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_geometricFibre_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (h : IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS xbar M) :
    (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar).image ∈
      etaleFiniteFreeLocus B S hS ((modulePullback B S hS
        (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj M)
declarations.comment: (4) implies (3), with the geometric fibre X_ybar formed as the fibre product of f with the geometric point ybar = f o xbar in the category of algebraic spaces over S (02X2), the etale neighbourhood of xbar inside X_ybar read as in the locus of 0CZT, and clause (4) in the source's Zariski-chart reading

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_geometricFibre_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (1) implies (3).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation, let `M`
be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on charts and let `x̄` be a geometric point
of `X`.  If `M` is flat at `x` over `Y` and the geometric fibre stalk `(M_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a flat
`𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module, then the inverse image of `M` to the geometric fibre is finite free in an
étale neighbourhood of the lift of `x̄`.

This is `(1) ⟹ (4)` followed by `(4) ⟹ (3)`.  The fibre stalk and its base ring are in the
quotient form `M_{x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} M_{x̄}` over `𝒪_{X, x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} 𝒪_{X, x̄}`, as they are throughout
this development; the identification of that quotient with the étale local ring of the geometric
fibre constructed here is condition (2) of Stacks 05WY and is not available.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_geometricFibre_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 M)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f M xbar)
    (hfibre : Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f M xbar)) :
    (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar).image ∈
      etaleFiniteFreeLocus B S hS ((modulePullback B S hS
        (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj M)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3), with the geometric fibre X_ybar formed as the fibre product of f with ybar = f o xbar (02X2) and the fibre stalk of clause (1) in the QUOTIENT FORM M_xbar / m_ybar M_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar}, whose identification with the etale local ring of that fibre is condition (2) of Stacks 05WY and is not available

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricFibrePoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (3) implies (1).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`,
let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X` with image `ȳ`.
If the inverse image of `F` to the geometric fibre `X_ȳ` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood
of the lift of `x̄` — clause (3) — then the fibre stalk `(F_ȳ)_x̄` is a flat
`𝒪_{X_ȳ, x̄}`-module, which is clause (1).

The defining square of `X_ȳ` is cartesian, so clause (1) for `f` at `x̄` and clause (1) for the
structure morphism `X_ȳ ⟶ Spec(κ(ȳ))` at the lift are the same condition
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_modulePullback_iff`).
Clause (3) is clause (4) for the inverse image on the fibre, so `(4) ⟹ (2) ⟹ (1)` on the fibre
gives clause (1) at the lift, and the comparison carries it down.  Condition (2) of Stacks 05WY —
the identification of the fibre stalk with the stalk on `X_ȳ` — is not used: both sides of the
comparison are taken in the quotient form.

Neither flatness of `F` over `Y`, nor local finite presentation of `f`, nor finite presentation of
`F` is assumed, which generalises the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricFibrePoint
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (h : IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar)
      ((modulePullback B S hS
        (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj F)) :
    Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)
declarations.comment: (3) implies (1), with the geometric fibre X_ybar formed as the fibre product of f with ybar = f o xbar in the category of algebraic spaces over S (02X2), clause (3) read as finite freeness of the inverse image of F to X_ybar on a Zariski open of an etale SCHEME chart of X_ybar around a point above the canonical lift of xbar, and the fibre stalk of clause (1) in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar}; flatness of F over Y, local finite presentation of f and finite presentation of F are not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteFreeNearGeometricFibrePoint_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (1) implies (3).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation, let `F`
be a finitely presented quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X` with
image `ȳ`.  If `F` is flat at `x` over `Y` and the fibre stalk `(F_ȳ)_x̄` is a flat
`𝒪_{X_ȳ, x̄}`-module, then the inverse image of `F` to the geometric fibre `X_ȳ` is finite free in
an étale neighbourhood of the lift of `x̄`, which is clause (3).

Clause (1) at `x̄` is clause (1) for the structure morphism `X_ȳ ⟶ Spec(κ(ȳ))` at the lift, by the
comparison across the cartesian defining square of `X_ȳ`, and `(1) ⟹ (4)` applied on the fibre is
clause (3).  Its hypotheses there are the base changes of the hypotheses here: Stacks 03XR for
local finite presentation of the structure morphism, the inverse image of a finitely presented
module for finite presentation on charts, and Stacks 05VW (1) for flatness at the lift.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteFreeNearGeometricFibrePoint_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F]
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
    (hfibre : Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)) :
    IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar)
      ((modulePullback B S hS
        (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj F)
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3), with the geometric fibre X_ybar formed as the fibre product of f with ybar = f o xbar in the category of algebraic spaces over S (02X2), the fibre stalk of clause (1) in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar}, and clause (3) read as finite freeness of the inverse image of F to X_ybar on a Zariski open of an etale SCHEME chart of X_ybar around a point above the canonical lift of xbar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_geometricFibre_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, the equivalence of all four clauses.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation, let `F` be a finitely presented
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X` with image `ȳ`.  If `F` is
flat at `x` over `Y`, then

1. `(F_ȳ)_x̄` is a flat `𝒪_{X_ȳ, x̄}`-module,
2. `(F_ȳ)_x̄` is a free `𝒪_{X_ȳ, x̄}`-module,
3. `F_ȳ` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of `x̄` in `X_ȳ`,
4. `F` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of `x` in `X`

are equivalent.  Clauses (1) and (2) appear twice: in the quotient form
`F_x̄ / 𝔪_ȳ F_x̄` over `𝒪_{X, x̄} / 𝔪_ȳ 𝒪_{X, x̄}` in which this development carries them, and in
the literal form on the geometric fibre `X_ȳ` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/GeometricFibreEtaleFreeLocus.lean` — the honest geometric
stalk of the inverse image of `F` at the canonical lift of `x̄`, over the honest étale local ring
of `X_ȳ` there.  The entries are, in order: clause (1) in the quotient form, clause (2) in the
quotient form, clause (1) in the literal form, clause (2) in the literal form, clause (3), and
clause (4).

The equivalence of the two forms of clauses (1) and (2) is *not* condition (2) of Stacks 05WY, and
does not supply it: no identification of the quotient with the stalk on `X_ȳ` is produced, only
the agreement of the flatness and freeness conditions, which clause (3) mediates.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_geometricFibre_tfae
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F]
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar) :
    [Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
        (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar),
      Module.Free (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
        (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar),
      Module.Flat
        ↥(etaleLocalRing B S hS (geometricFibre B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar)).1
          (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar))
        ↥(geometricModuleStalk B S hS (geometricFibre B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))
          (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar)
          ((modulePullback B S hS
            (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj F)),
      Module.Free
        ↥(etaleLocalRing B S hS (geometricFibre B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar)).1
          (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar))
        ↥(geometricModuleStalk B S hS (geometricFibre B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))
          (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar)
          ((modulePullback B S hS
            (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj F)),
      IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar)
        ((modulePullback B S hS
          (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj F),
      IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS xbar F].TFAE
declarations.comment: clauses (1), (2), (3) and (4) are equivalent, under the source's own hypotheses; the geometric fibre X_ybar is formed as the fibre product of f with ybar = f o xbar in the category of algebraic spaces over S (02X2), clauses (3) and (4) are read as finite freeness on a Zariski open of an etale SCHEME chart around a point above the relevant geometric point, and clauses (1) and (2) appear BOTH in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar} and in the LITERAL FORM on X_ybar, i.e. the geometric stalk of the inverse image of F at the canonical lift of xbar over the etale local ring of X_ybar there; the agreement of the two forms is a consequence of the equivalence and is NOT condition (2) of Stacks 05WY, which stays unavailable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_geometricFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (3) implies (4), both clauses in the small-étale-site reading of the locus of
Stacks 0CZT.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation, let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on charts which is flat over `Y`, and let `x̄` be a geometric
point of `X` with image `ȳ`.  If the image of the canonical lift of `x̄` lies in the finite-free
étale locus of the inverse image of `F` to the geometric fibre `X_ȳ`, then the image of `x̄` lies
in the finite-free étale locus of `F`.

This is the reverse inclusion of the base-change clause of Stacks 0CZT —
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint_modulePullback`
— at the cartesian defining square of `X_ȳ`, with the Zariski-chart reading upstairs supplied at a
*chosen* geometric point over the image of the lift
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint_of_mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus`);
only the image point of the chosen point enters the conclusion, and it is the image of the lift,
which is the image of `x̄`.

Because the chosen point need not be `x̄`, the source's hypothesis of flatness of `F` over `Y` *at
`x`* is strengthened here to flatness over `Y` everywhere.  The equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_geometricFibre_tfae` carries the source's
own hypothesis, at the Zariski-chart reading of clause (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_geometricFibre
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F)
    (hF : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (h : (geometricFibrePoint B S hS f xbar).image ∈ etaleFiniteFreeLocus B S hS
      ((modulePullback B S hS
        (geometricFibreToSource B S hS f (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar))).obj F)) :
    xbar.image ∈ etaleFiniteFreeLocus B S hS F
declarations.comment: (3) implies (4) with BOTH clauses in the SMALL-ETALE-SITE reading, i.e. membership in the locus of Stacks 0CZT on the geometric fibre X_ybar and on X respectively, X_ybar being the fibre product of f with ybar = f o xbar in the category of algebraic spaces over S (02X2); the source's flatness of F over Y at x is STRENGTHENED to flatness of F over Y everywhere, because the Zariski-chart reading upstairs is recovered only at a geometric point chosen over the image of the lift of xbar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (1) implies (4).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation, let `F`
be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on charts and let `x̄` be a geometric
point of `X`.  If `F` is flat at `x` over `Y` and the fibre stalk `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a flat
`𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module, then `F` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of `x` in `X`.

The route is the source's: clause (1) together with the standing flatness makes the geometric
stalk `F_{x̄}` free over `𝒪_{X, x̄}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.free_geometricModuleStalk_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk`, which is
Stacks 05X0 at `𝟙 X` over `f`); freeness descends to the Zariski stalk of an étale scheme chart;
and Stacks 0B8J trivialises the chart restriction on a Zariski open of the chart.  The fibre
stalk and its base ring are taken in the quotient form `F_{x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} F_{x̄}` over
`𝒪_{X, x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} 𝒪_{X, x̄}`, as in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/GeometricFibreStalkFreeness.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
    (hfibre : Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)) :
    IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS xbar F
declarations.comment: (1) implies (4), with the etale neighbourhood of x taken to be a Zariski open of an etale SCHEME chart of X around a point above x and finite freeness read on the Zariski site of that chart (the source's own route through More on Morphisms 080Q); the fibre stalk and its base ring are in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar}, whose identification with the stalk on the geometric fibre X_ybar is condition (2) of Stacks 05WY and is not available

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.free_geometricFibreModuleStalk_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (4) implies (2).**  If `F` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of `x` in
`X`, then the fibre stalk `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a free `𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module.

The trivialization makes the Zariski stalk of the chart restriction free, freeness ascends to the
geometric stalk by Stacks 05VP, and the fibre stalk is the reduction of the geometric stalk
modulo `𝔪_{ȳ} 𝒪_{X, x̄}`.  Neither flatness of `F` over `Y`, nor local finite presentation of
`f`, nor finite presentation of `F` is used, which generalises the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_geometricFibreModuleStalk_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (h : IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS xbar F) :
    Module.Free (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)
declarations.comment: (4) implies (2), with the etale neighbourhood of x a Zariski open of an etale SCHEME chart of X and the fibre stalk in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar}; flatness of F over Y, local finite presentation of f and finite presentation of F are not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, the equivalence of clauses (1), (2) and (4).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation, let `F` be a finitely
presented quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X` with image `ȳ`.
If `F` is flat at `x` over `Y`, then

1. `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a flat `𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module,
2. `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a free `𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module,
4. `F` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of `x` in `X`

are equivalent.  The fibre stalk and its base ring are taken in the quotient form
`F_{x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} F_{x̄}` over `𝒪_{X, x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} 𝒪_{X, x̄}`, which is how the source's own proof
reads clause (1), and clause (4) is read on a Zariski open of an étale scheme chart.  Clause (3)
is not among the entries *here*: it is proved from clause (4) in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/GeometricFibreEtaleFreeLocus.lean`, and it is added to the
equivalence — in its Zariski-chart reading on the geometric fibre, together with clauses (1) and
(2) in their literal form on that fibre — by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_geometricFibre_tfae` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/GeometricFibreStalkClauseThree.lean`.  The source's reverse
implication `(3) ⟹ (2)` goes through the identification of the stalk on the geometric fibre with
the quotient, which is condition (2) of Stacks 05WY and is still not available; the equivalence
does not need it, only the agreement of the two flatness conditions across the cartesian defining
square of the fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_tfae
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F]
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar) :
    [Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
        (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar),
      Module.Free (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
        (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar),
      IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS xbar F].TFAE
declarations.comment: clauses (1), (2) and (4) are equivalent, under the source's own hypotheses, with the fibre stalk and its base ring in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar} and clause (4) read as finite freeness on a Zariski open of an etale SCHEME chart of X around a point above x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_of_free
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (2) implies (1).** A free fibre stalk `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a flat
`𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module.

The fibre stalk and its base ring are taken in the quotient form `F_{x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} F_{x̄}` over
`𝒪_{X, x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} 𝒪_{X, x̄}`, which is condition (1) of Stacks 05WY for `X ⟶ X ⟶ Y` and is how
the source's own proof reads clause (1); their identification with the étale local ring and the
geometric stalk on a geometric fibre `X_{ȳ}` is not available, the fibre of a morphism of
algebraic spaces over a point of the target not being constructed in this library.  Neither
flatness of `F` at `x` over `Y`, nor local finite presentation of `f`, nor finite presentation
of `F` is assumed, which generalises the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_of_free {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, m} B S hS X.1 X.2) (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hfree : Module.Free (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)) :
    Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1), with the fibre stalk and its base ring in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar} (the geometric fibre X_ybar is not constructed in this library); flatness of F over Y and finite presentation are not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_iff_free_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, (1) is equivalent to (2).** For a finitely presented `𝒪_X`-module `F`,
flatness and freeness of the fibre stalk `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` over the local ring `𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}` of the
geometric fibre agree.

The fibre stalk and its base ring are taken in the quotient form `F_{x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} F_{x̄}` over
`𝒪_{X, x̄} / 𝔪_{ȳ} 𝒪_{X, x̄}`, which is condition (1) of Stacks 05WY for `X ⟶ X ⟶ Y` and is how
the source's own proof reads clause (1); the geometric fibre `X_{ȳ}` itself is not constructed in
this library.  Neither flatness of `F` at `x` over `Y` nor local finite presentation of `f` is
assumed, which generalises the source: both clauses are conditions on the fibre stalk alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_iff_free_of_isFinitePresentation
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite] (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
        (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar) ↔
      Module.Free (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
        (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)
declarations.comment: (1) iff (2) under the source's own hypotheses, with the fibre stalk and base ring in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar} (the geometric fibre X_ybar is not constructed in this library)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chartOpen_over_iso_free_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, clause (4).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite presentation, let `F` be
a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on charts and let `x̄` be a geometric point
of `X`.  If `F` is flat at `x` over `Y` and the fibre stalk `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a flat
`𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module — clause (1) — then `F` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of `x` in
`X`: there are an étale scheme chart `φ : (U, u) → (X, x̄)`, a Zariski open `W ⊆ U` containing
`u` and a rank `r` such that `(φ^* F)|_W` is free on `r` generators.

This is the source's own `(1) ⟹ (4)`, in the reading its proof produces.  Clause (1) makes the
geometric stalk `F_{x̄}` free over `𝒪_{X, x̄}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.free_geometricModuleStalk_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk`, which is
Stacks 05X0 at `𝟙 X` over `f`); that descends along the faithfully flat comparison of
Stacks 05VP to freeness of the Zariski stalk `(φ^* F)_u` over `𝒪_{U, u}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.free_chartZariskiModuleStalk_of_free_geometricModuleStalk`); and the
chart restriction is of finite presentation on the Zariski site of `U`, which is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinitePresentationOnCharts` says, so Stacks 0B8J spreads a basis of
that stalk to a trivialization on a Zariski open neighbourhood of `u`.  0B8J is used through
`Stacks.StalkFiniteType.exists_over_iso_free_of_stalk_basis`, which takes the basis over the
local ring `𝒪_{U, u}` rather than over the `RingCat`-valued stalk.  The open `W` is itself an
étale neighbourhood of `x̄` in `X`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartOpenNeighborhood`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chartOpen_over_iso_free_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
    (hfibre : Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
      (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)) :
    ∃ (N : SmallEtaleNeighborhood xbar) (W : (chartScheme N.chart).Opens)
        (_ : chartPoint B S hS X.1 N ∈ W) (r : ℕ),
      Nonempty ((restrictToChart B S hS X.2 F N.chart).over W ≅
        SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))
declarations.comment: (1) implies (4) under the source's own hypotheses, with clause (1) in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar} (the geometric fibre X_ybar is not constructed in this library) and clause (4) in the reading the source's proof produces: an etale SCHEME chart (U, u) over (X, xbar) together with a Zariski open W of U containing u on which the chart restriction phi^* F becomes free on finitely many generators. That W is an etale neighbourhood of xbar in X by chartOpenNeighborhood. The finite freeness is read as freeness of (phi^* F)|_W on the slice of the Zariski site of U at W; identifying that with the chart restriction of F to W read on the Zariski site of W itself is an equivalence of sites and is NOT claimed. Clause (3) is not statable: it needs the geometric fibre X_ybar as an algebraic space.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_chartOpen_over_iso_free_iff_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZS, clause (1) if and only if clause (4).**  For `f : X ⟶ Y` locally of finite
presentation, `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on charts flat at `x`
over `Y`, and `x̄` a geometric point of `X`: the fibre stalk `(F_{ȳ})_{x̄}` is a flat
`𝒪_{X_{ȳ}, x̄}`-module exactly when `F` becomes free on finitely many generators on a Zariski
open neighbourhood of `u` in some étale scheme chart `(U, u)` of `x̄`.

Clause (4) is read as the source's own proof produces it, on the slice of the Zariski site of
the chart at the open; identifying that with the chart restriction of `F` read on the Zariski
site of the open itself is an equivalence of sites and is not claimed.  The reverse implication
uses only quasi-coherence of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chartOpen_over_iso_free_iff_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F)
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar) :
    (∃ (N : SmallEtaleNeighborhood xbar) (W : (chartScheme N.chart).Opens)
        (_ : chartPoint B S hS X.1 N ∈ W) (r : ℕ),
      Nonempty ((restrictToChart B S hS X.2 F N.chart).over W ≅
        SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))) ↔
      Module.Flat (geometricFibreLocalRing B S hS f xbar)
        (geometricFibreModuleStalk B S hS f F xbar)
declarations.comment: (1) iff (4), clause (1) in the QUOTIENT FORM F_xbar / m_ybar F_xbar over O_{X, xbar} / m_ybar O_{X, xbar} (the geometric fibre X_ybar is not constructed in this library) and clause (4) in the reading the source's proof produces: an etale SCHEME chart (U, u) over (X, xbar) with a Zariski open W of U containing u on which phi^* F becomes free on finitely many generators, the finite freeness read on the slice of the Zariski site of U at W. Identifying that slice reading with the chart restriction of F to W read on the Zariski site of W itself is an equivalence of sites and is NOT claimed; neither is the identification of clause (4) with the small-etale reading of the locus of Tag 0CZT. The (4) => (1) direction needs NONE of the source's hypotheses except quasi-coherence of F. Clause (3) is not statable: it needs the geometric fibre X_ybar as an algebraic space.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_etaleFreeLocus
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
presentation and let `F` be a finitely presented `𝒪_X`-module which is flat over `Y`.  Then the
set of points of `|X|` at which `F` is free in an étale neighbourhood is open in `|X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_etaleFreeLocus {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (_hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F]
    (_hF : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    @IsOpen _ (pointTopology B S hS X.1) (etaleFreeLocus B S hS F)
declarations.comment: openness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleFreeLocus_modulePullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZT, the base-change clause.**  Let

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `f` be locally of finite presentation and
let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on the small étale site which is
flat over `Y`.  Then the étale free locus of the inverse image of `F` on `X'` is the inverse
image of the étale free locus of `F`:

```
W((g')^* F) = |g'|⁻¹(W(F)).
```

The hypotheses are asked of `f` and `F` only, which is what the source asks; nothing is required
of `f'` or of `(g')^* F`, so no stability of the hypotheses under base change is used.

The inclusion `⊇` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preimage_etaleFreeLocus_subset` and holds for an
arbitrary morphism with no hypothesis.  The inclusion `⊆` is the source's argument, transporting
clause (1) of Stacks 0CZS across the square by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_modulePullback_iff`, between the two ends
`exists_geometricPoint_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk_of_mem_etaleFreeLocus` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFreeLocus_of_flat_geometricFibreModuleStalk`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFreeLocus_modulePullback_eq
    {X Y X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    etaleFreeLocus B S hS ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) =
      pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom ⁻¹' etaleFreeLocus B S hS F
declarations.comment: the base-change clause: the formation of the locus W commutes with arbitrary base change, as the EQUALITY W((g')^* F) = |g'|^(-1)(W(F)) of subsets of |X'|, at an arbitrary cartesian square of algebraic spaces over S. The openness clause is isOpen_etaleFreeLocus of Spaces/EtaleFreeLocus.lean; the two together are the whole tag. Hypotheses are the source's own and are asked DOWNSTAIRS only, of f and F: f locally of finite presentation, F quasi-coherent, F of finite presentation on the small etale site, and F flat over Y. Nothing is asked of f' or of the inverse image of F, so no stability of the hypotheses under base change is used. The test scheme T of the source is not named: the statement is at a cartesian square, of which the square of a morphism of test schemes is an instance by isPullback_baseChangeMap. Freeness is IsFreeModule, the universal-property reading on the small etale site, at an arbitrary index type.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**The reverse inclusion of the base-change clause.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation, let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on charts which is flat over `Y`, and let

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

be a cartesian square.  If the inverse image `(g')^*F` is finite free in an étale neighbourhood of
a geometric point `x̄'` of `X'` — clause (4) of Stacks 0CZS in the source's Zariski-chart reading —
then the image of `x̄'` in `|X|` lies in the finite-free étale locus of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_etaleFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint_modulePullback
    {X Y X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentationOnCharts B S hS X.2 F)
    (hF : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) (xbar' : GeometricPoint B S hS X'.1)
    (h : IsFiniteFreeNearGeometricPoint B S hS xbar' ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F)) :
    pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom xbar'.image ∈ etaleFiniteFreeLocus B S hS F
declarations.comment: the reverse inclusion W' ⊆ |g'|^{-1}(W) of the base-change clause, with membership in W' read at a geometric point xbar' of X' in the source's own Zariski-chart reading of clause (4) of Stacks 0CZS -- a Zariski open of an etale SCHEME chart of X' on which the chart restriction of (g')^*F is finite free -- and W the locus of points of |X| admitting an etale morphism of algebraic spaces through them along which the inverse image of F is finite free in the sense of 03DE(2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleFreeLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**The base-change clause for the étale free locus.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite presentation, let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation on charts which is flat over `Y`, and let

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

be a cartesian square.  Then the étale free locus of the inverse image `(g')^*F` on `|X'|` is the
inverse image under `|g'|` of the étale free locus of `F` on `|X|`.

The locus is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleFreeLocus`, the plain-freeness locus by which the
source defines it, and finite presentation of `F` is taken on the small étale site.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleFreeLocus_modulePullback_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
    {X Y X' Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (hpb : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentationOnSite F]
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (hF : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    etaleFreeLocus B S hS ((modulePullback B S hS g').obj F) =
      pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g'.hom ⁻¹' etaleFreeLocus B S hS F
declarations.comment: the base-change clause: the etale free locus of (g')^*F on |X'| is the preimage under |g'| of the etale free locus of F on |X|, at the PLAIN-FREENESS locus the source defines and the openness clause carries, with finite presentation of F read on the small etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientObstruction_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU: the obstruction vanishes exactly when the quotient lifts.** For `x ∈ Q(T)`
given by `K ⊂ F_T`, `o_x(T') = 0` if and only if there is `x' ∈ Q(T')` restricting to `x`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.mem_finitePresentationQuotients_of_quotientPullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU, finite presentation (Stacks 08VU).** If `x ∈ Q^{fp}(T)`, every lift
`x' ∈ Q(T')` of `x` lies in `Q^{fp}(T')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_finitePresentationQuotients_of_quotientPullback_eq
    {K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)} (hK : K ∈ D.finitePresentationQuotients T)
    {K' : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T')} (hK' : K' ∈ D.quotients T')
    (hpb : D.quotientPullback h K' = K) :
    K' ∈ D.finitePresentationQuotients T'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.reductionShortComplex_relativeSquare_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU: `0 ⟶ f_T^*𝒥 ⊗ F_T ⟶ F_{T'} ⟶ F_T ⟶ 0` is exact.** Since `F_{T'}` is flat
over `T'`, the reduction `π : F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` (read on `X_{T'}`) has kernel `f_T^*𝒥 ⊗ F_T`, embedded
by `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reductionShortComplex_relativeSquare_shortExact :
    (reductionShortComplex (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.relativeMap h))
      (D.relativeSquareThickening h) (D.relativeSquareLeft h)
      (relBaseRight (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.projection T')))
      (D.relativeMapFirstOrderThickening h hh) (D.relativeSquareThickeningFirstOrderThickening h hh)
      (D.relativeSquare_comm h) (D.baseChangeModule T') (D.isStrict_relativeSquare h hh)
      (D.isFlat_baseChangeModule_relBaseRight hF T')).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.isIso_baseIdealTensorToIdealTensor_relativeSquare
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU: `f_T^*𝒥 ⊗ F_T = I ⊗ F_T` (Stacks 08MQ).** The canonical comparison of
`f_T^*𝒥 ⊗ F_T` with `I ⊗ F_T`, for `F_T = F_{T'}|_{X_T}`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_baseIdealTensorToIdealTensor_relativeSquare :
    IsIso (baseIdealTensorToIdealTensor (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.relativeMap h))
      (D.relativeSquareThickening h) (D.relativeSquareLeft h)
      (relBaseRight (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.projection T')))
      (D.relativeMapFirstOrderThickening h hh) (D.relativeSquareThickeningFirstOrderThickening h hh)
      (D.relativeSquare_comm h)
      ((modulePullback B S hS (D.relativeMap h)).obj (D.baseChangeModule T')))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.obstructionKernel_baseIdealTensor_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU: `0 ⟶ K ⊗_{𝒪_T} 𝒥 ⟶ F_T ⊗_{𝒪_T} 𝒥 ⟶ Q ⊗_{𝒪_T} 𝒥 ⟶ 0` is exact**, `Q` being
flat over `T`. Here `G ⊗_{𝒪_T} 𝒥 = f_T^*𝒥 ⊗ G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem obstructionKernel_baseIdealTensor_shortExact {K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)}
    (hK : K ∈ D.quotients T) :
    ((ShortComplex.mk (C := SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS (D.space T)).O)) (D.obstructionKernel h K).arrow
        (cokernel.π (D.obstructionKernel h K).arrow)
      (cokernel.condition _)).map (baseIdealTensor.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u}
        (D.relativeSquareThickening h) (D.relativeSquareLeft h)
        (D.relativeSquareThickeningFirstOrderThickening h hh))).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientObstructionExtension_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU: the canonical extension
`0 ⟶ Q ⊗_{𝒪_T} 𝒥 ⟶ π⁻¹(K)/i(K ⊗_{𝒪_T} 𝒥) ⟶ K ⟶ 0` of `𝒪_{X_T}`-modules is short exact.** Its
class is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.quotientObstruction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientObstructionExtension_shortExact (K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)) :
    (quotientLiftExtension (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.relativeMap h))
      (D.relativeSquareThickening h) (D.relativeSquareLeft h)
      (relBaseRight (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.projection T')))
      (D.relativeMapFirstOrderThickening h hh) (D.relativeSquareThickeningFirstOrderThickening h hh)
      (D.relativeSquare_comm h) (D.baseChangeModule T') (D.isStrict_relativeSquare h hh)
      (D.isFlat_baseChangeModule_relBaseRight hF T') (D.obstructionKernel h K)).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.isStrict_relativeSquare
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU: the ideal `I` of `X_T ⊂ X_{T'}` is a quotient of `f_T^*𝒥`.** The relative
square is strict (Stacks 08M9): the map of ideals `f̃'^*(f'⁻¹𝒥) ⟶ I` of the morphism of
thickenings of Stacks 08M7, built from the first order thickenings `X_T ⊂ X_{T'}` and
`t̃ = (id, f'⁻¹t^♯)` and the commutative square `f̃' ∘ i = t̃ ∘ f̃`, is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrict_relativeSquare :
    MorphismOfThickenings.IsStrict.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u}
      (MorphismOfThickenings.ofFirstOrderThickenings.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u, u + 1, u, u,
          u + 1, u}
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.relativeMap h)) (D.relativeSquareThickening h)
        (D.relativeSquareLeft h) (relBaseRight (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (D.projection T')))
        (D.relativeMapFirstOrderThickening h hh)
        (D.relativeSquareThickeningFirstOrderThickening h hh) (D.relativeSquare_comm h))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.isFirstOrderThickening_range_relativeMap
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0CZU, `X_T ⊂ X_{T'}` is a first order thickening**: the image of `X_T` in `X_{T'}`,
which is the inverse image of the first order thickening `T ⊂ T'`, is a first order thickening of
`X_{T'}` (Stacks 09ZX).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFirstOrderThickening_range_relativeMap :
    IsFirstOrderThickening B S hS (D.space T') (Subfunctor.range (D.relativeMap h).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuotientSituation.exists_addTorsor_quotientLifts
declarations.doc:
In Situation 082M with `F` flat over `B`, let
`T ⊂ T'` be a first order thickening of schemes over `B` with ideal sheaf `𝒥`, and let
`x ∈ Q_{F/X/B}(T)` be given by `0 ⟶ 𝒦 ⟶ F_T ⟶ 𝒬 ⟶ 0` (`K ∈ D.quotients T`). If the obstruction
`o_x(T')` of Remark 0CZU vanishes (`D.quotientObstruction hF h hh K = 0`), the set of lifts
`x' ∈ Q_{F/X/B}(T')` of `x` (`D.quotientLifts h K`: the `K' ∈ D.quotients T'` with
`D.quotientPullback h K' = K`) is a principal homogeneous space under
`Hom_{𝒪_{X_T}}(𝒦, 𝒬 ⊗_{𝒪_T} 𝒥)` (`D.deformationGroup h hh K`), with the action of the remark:
`φ` sends `𝒦'` to `𝒦'_φ` (`D.quotientLiftAction hF h hh hK φ K'`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_addTorsor_quotientLifts {K : Subobject (D.baseChangeModule T)}
    (hK : K ∈ D.quotients T) (ho : D.quotientObstruction.{e} hF h hh K = 0) :
    ∃ Tor : AddTorsor (D.deformationGroup h hh K) (D.quotientLifts h K),
      ∀ (φ : D.deformationGroup h hh K) (K' : D.quotientLifts h K),
        (Tor.vadd φ K').val = D.quotientLiftAction hF h hh hK φ K'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**`Quot_{F/X/S}` is an algebraic space locally of finite presentation over `S`.** Let `S` be
Noetherian with all local rings G-rings, `f : X ⟶ S` separated and of finite presentation, and `F`
a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation, flat over `S`. Then every model of
`Quot_{F/X/S}` in the universe of the site is an algebraic space whose morphism to `S` is locally
of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_and_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_quotOverBase
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] (hG : ∀ s : S, IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hFfp : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    ∀ N : QuotSitePresheafModel (quotOverBase X f hf F hF),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS N.presheaf ∧ IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS N.toBase
declarations.comment: Quot_{F/X/S} is an algebraic space locally of finite presentation over S, by Artin's axioms (Stacks 07Y1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_diag_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZW, the diagonal.** In the situation of the remark, the diagonal
`Quot_{F/X/S} ⟶ Quot_{F/X/S} × Quot_{F/X/S}` is representable (by closed immersions of
schemes, hence by algebraic spaces): for two quotients `F_T ⟶ 𝒬ᵢ`, the locus of `T` over which
they agree is a closed subscheme of `T`, by Stacks 083M (the remark's own argument, through the
vanishing of `𝒦₁ ⟶ 𝒬₂` and of `𝒦₂ ⟶ 𝒬₁`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_diag_quotOverBase :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (diag (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF))
declarations.comment: the diagonal of Quot_{F/X/S} is representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheaf_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZW, axiom [0].** In the situation of the remark, `Quot_{F/X/S}` is a sheaf for
the étale topology (indeed for the fppf topology), by Stacks 09TT.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_quotOverBase :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF) ∧
      Presheaf.IsSheaf ((AlgebraicGeometry.etaleTopology B).over (B.obj hS))
        (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)
declarations.comment: axiom [0]: Quot_{F/X/S} is a sheaf, for the fppf and hence for the étale topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.satisfiesRS_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZW, axiom [2].** In the situation of the remark, `Quot_{F/X/S}` satisfies the
Rim–Schlessinger condition: for a pushout `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` of spectra of Artinian local rings of
finite type over `S` along a closed immersion `X ⟶ X'`, the map
`Quot(Y') ⟶ Quot(Y) ×_{Quot(X)} Quot(X')` is bijective; equivalently the category fibred in sets
`𝒮_{Quot}` satisfies (RS) of Stacks 07WP. This is Stacks 08IW together with the descent of the
properness of the support across the thickening `Y ⟶ Y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesRS_quotOverBase :
    Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRSFunctor B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF) ∧
      Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRS B S hS
        (Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).val.p
        (Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).isFiberedInGroupoids
declarations.comment: axiom [2]: Quot_{F/X/S} satisfies the Rim-Schlessinger condition (RS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffective_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZW, axiom [4]: formal objects of `Quot_{F/X/S}` are effective.** For `f`
separated and `F` of finite presentation, every formal object of `𝒮_{Quot_{F/X/S}}` over a
Noetherian complete local ring is effective. This is Grothendieck's existence theorem (Stacks
08BE) applied to the quotient modules, together with the algebraization of the quotient maps
(representability of `Hom` sheaves, Stacks 08K6) and their surjectivity, checked on the closed
fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_quotOverBase (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hFfp : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite)
    (ξ : FormalObject B S hS
      (Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).val.p) :
    FormalObject.IsEffective B S hS
      (Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).val.p
      (Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).property ξ
declarations.comment: axiom [4]: formal objects of Quot_{F/X/S} are effective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.limitPreserving_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZW, axiom [1].** In the situation of the remark (`F` of finite presentation),
`Quot_{F/X/S}` is limit preserving: for every cofiltered system of affine schemes `Tᵢ` of the site
with limit `T` in schemes, the map `colim Quot(Tᵢ) ⟶ Quot(T)` is bijective. A quotient over the
limit descends to a stage (Stacks 082Q, with the descent of flatness and of proper support), and
two quotients over a stage agreeing over the limit agree at a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_quotOverBase (hFfp : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u} (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)
      (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)
declarations.comment: axiom [1]: Quot_{F/X/S} is limit preserving

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteDimensionalTangentSpaces_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZW, axiom [3].** In the situation of the remark, with `F` of finite presentation
and flat over `S`, the tangent spaces of `Quot_{F/X/S}` at the points over fields of finite type
over `S` are finite-dimensional, for their canonical vector space structure.

A lift over `k[V]` of a point `F_k ⟶ F_k/𝒦₀` is a quotient of `F_{k[V]}` flat over `k[V]`; its
difference with the trivial lift is a morphism `𝒦₀ ⟶ (F_k/𝒦₀) ⊗ V`, natural in `V` and
determining the lift, so the tangent space embeds `k`-linearly into `Hom(𝒦₀, F_k/𝒦₀)`
(the deformation theory of quotients of Stacks 0CZV). That space is finite-dimensional because
`𝒦₀` is coherent and `F_k/𝒦₀` is coherent with support proper over `k` (Stacks 0D0T).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteDimensionalTangentSpaces_quotOverBase (hFfp : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite)
    (hflat : IsFlatOver B S hS X.2 f.hom F) :
    Stack.HasFiniteDimensionalTangentSpaces B S hS
      (Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF))
declarations.comment: axiom [3]: the tangent spaces of Quot_{F/X/S} at finite type points are finite dimensional

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenVersality_quotOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZW, axiom [5]: openness of versality for `Quot_{F/X/S}`.** For `S` locally
Noetherian, `f` separated and `F` of finite presentation, a finite type point of a scheme locally
of finite type over `S` at which an object of `Quot_{F/X/S}` is versal has an open neighbourhood
of finite type points at which it is versal. This is Stacks 0CXU: the diagonal is representable,
(RS*) holds, `Quot_{F/X/S}` is limit preserving (axiom [1]), and towers of square-zero thickenings
of affine schemes are effective, by Grothendieck existence for such towers (Stacks 0CXB),
representability of `Hom` sheaves (Stacks 08K6) and Nakayama.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenVersality_quotOverBase [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f.hom) (hFfp : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) :
    ∀ U : Over S, LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom →
      ∀ (y : (Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).val.obj)
        (hy : ((Stack.fibredCategory B S hS (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).val.p ⋙
          Over.post B.inclusion).obj y = U)
        (u : U.left),
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u →
        Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt U ((Stack.fibredCategory B S hS
          (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u y hy →
        ∃ V : U.left.Opens, u ∈ V.1 ∧
          ∀ u' ∈ V.1, AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u' →
            Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt U ((Stack.fibredCategory B S hS
              (quotOverBasePresheaf X f hf F hF)).val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u' y hy
declarations.comment: axiom [5]: openness of versality for Quot_{F/X/S}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZY.** A family classified by the Hilbert functor of `f : X ⟶ Y` over a scheme `T`
over `Y`: a closed subspace of the base change `X_T` which is of finite presentation, flat and
proper over `T`.
declarations.statement: structure HilbertFamily (f : X ⟶ Y) (T : SchemesOverPresheaf B S hS Y)
declarations.comment: families classified by the functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZY.** The *Hilbert functor* of `f : X ⟶ Y`: it sends a scheme `T` over `Y` to the
set of closed subspaces of `X_T` which are of finite presentation, flat and proper over `T`, and a
morphism of schemes over `Y` to base change of those subspaces.
declarations.statement: def hilbertFunctor (f : X ⟶ Y) : (SchemesOverPresheaf B S hS Y)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the Hilbert functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertFunctor_map_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZY.** The Hilbert functor acts by inverse image of closed subspaces along the
transition maps of base changes.
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertFunctor_map_obj (f : X ⟶ Y) {T T' : SchemesOverPresheaf B S hS Y} (g : T' ⟶ T)
    (z : HilbertFamily f T) :
    ((hilbertFunctor f).map g.op z).Z = z.Z.preimage (schemeBaseChangeMap f g)
declarations.comment: base change in the Hilbert functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HilbertFamilyOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZY.** A family classified by the Hilbert functor, over a scheme of the big fppf site
rather than over a scheme of `Y`: the morphism to `Y` it lies over, together with a family over the
resulting scheme over `Y`.
declarations.statement: structure HilbertFamilyOver (f : X ⟶ Y) (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
declarations.comment: families over the schemes of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZY.** The Hilbert functor read as a presheaf on the schemes of the big fppf site: a
section over `T` is a morphism `T ⟶ Y` together with a family over `T` for the resulting scheme
over `Y`, and restriction pulls back both.
declarations.statement: def hilbertPresheaf (f : X ⟶ Y) : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the presheaf on the schemes of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hilbertPresheafToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0CZY.** The canonical morphism from the Hilbert presheaf to the base algebraic space
`Y`, sending a family to the morphism to `Y` it lies over. Its target is the universe lift of `Y`
because subfunctors of a presheaf on the site live one universe up.
declarations.statement: def hilbertPresheafToBase (f : X ⟶ Y) : hilbertPresheaf f ⟶ Y.obj ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism to the base
